stories.title: IAEA says strikes near Iran nuclear power plant ‘must stop’
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency called for an end to strikes near an Iranian nuclear power plant, which has been targeted four times since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began. The IAEA warned that continued attacks near the facility pose serious safety risks.

stories.title: Trump says Iran could be ‘taken out’ on April 7, Hegseth says major strikes to come
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran could be "taken out" on April 7 and described a weekend operation to recover a downed U.S. airman from Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth indicated that major strikes were forthcoming if Trump's deadline passed without a deal.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills at least 10 near Gaza school as ceasefire strains
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike near a school housing displaced Palestinians in Gaza killed at least 10 people and wounded several others on Monday. The attack is the latest violence threatening the fragile U.S.-backed Gaza ceasefire deal, according to health officials.

stories.title: Nigeria Christian group disputes army rescue claim in Kaduna church attack
stories.summary: A Nigerian Christian group in Kaduna state disputed the army's claim that it had rescued 31 people abducted by armed men in northern Kaduna. The group maintained that the victims remained in captivity despite the military's assertions.

stories.title: Rules of war must be respected in words and action, ICRC president says
stories.summary: The president of the International Committee of the Red Cross urged governments to respect the rules of war in both words and actions. The statement followed U.S. President Donald Trump's escalating rhetoric against Iran, including threats to rain "hell" on Tehran.

stories.title: Trump says April 7 deadline to make a deal with Iran is final
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared his April 7 deadline for a deal with Iran is final. He acknowledged an Iranian peace proposal as significant but stated it was not sufficient to meet his demands.

stories.title: North Korea leader’s sister says Seoul’s regret sending drones ‘wise behaviour’
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret to Pyongyang over drones that were sent into North Korea earlier this year, calling the actions "irresponsible." North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's sister responded by characterizing Seoul's expression of regret as "wise behaviour."

stories.title: Kuwait says six injured after Iranian attack on residential area
stories.summary: Kuwait reported six people were injured after Iranian retaliatory strikes hit a residential area. Gulf nations including Kuwait have sustained damage from Iran's strikes since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks in late February, sparking a regional war.

stories.title: Iran conveys to Pakistan its rejection of US ceasefire proposal: report
stories.summary: Iran has communicated its rejection of a U.S. ceasefire proposal to Pakistan, which is serving as an intermediary. Tehran's response included 10 clauses demanding a permanent end to the war, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions relief, and reconstruction. U.S. President Trump had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal.

stories.title: ‘New’ Bangladesh-India ties will avoid ‘mistakes of the past’: Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir
stories.summary: Bangladesh Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kobir stated that renewed Bangladesh-India relations should avoid past mistakes. He recommended more frequent exchanges at the level of political parties and officials to address difficult issues and prevent misunderstandings between the two countries.

stories.title: Russia says Ukraine damaged CPC terminal on the Black Sea with drones
stories.summary: Russia accused Ukraine of using drones to attack the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's Black Sea terminal, which handles approximately 1.5% of global oil supply. Moscow reported damage to the single point mooring, loading infrastructure, and four large storage tanks.

stories.title: Israel rescuers say four bodies recovered from Iran strike site
stories.summary: Israeli rescue teams recovered four bodies from an Iranian strike site. The victims were identified as two men and two women, all Israeli civilians from the same family, according to the military.

stories.title: Russian grain ship believed sunk in Ukrainian drone attack is found and towed to shore, TASS says
stories.summary: A Russian grain ship carrying wheat, previously believed sunk in the Sea of Azov after a Ukrainian drone attack, was found and towed to shore, according to TASS. The death toll from the attack rose to three.

stories.title: Iraq could restore oil exports to pre-war level within a week if Hormuz reopens, Basra Oil chief says
stories.summary: The head of Iraq's state-run Basra Oil Company said Iraq could restore crude oil exports to approximately 3.4 million barrels per day within a week if the Iran war ends and the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

stories.title: Ukraine drones spark blaze at Russia’s Sheskharis oil terminal, sources say
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal, sparking a fire. The attack is part of Ukraine's intensified aerial campaign targeting Russian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Air Chief Marshal visits the U.S. to boost defence ties
stories.summary: India's Air Chief Marshal visited the United States to strengthen defence ties between the two countries. The visit is part of a series of high-level exchanges reflecting growing strategic convergence between India and the U.S.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu ousts top aide after he allegedly made racist remarks
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed his chief of staff, Ziv Agmon, after leaked comments in which Agmon allegedly referred to Jews of Moroccan descent as "baboons" and disparaged members of Netanyahu's Likud party. Ido Norden has been named as Agmon's successor.

stories.title: Watch: Israel confirms U.S.-Israeli strikes kill Iran Guards intelligence chief
stories.summary: Israel's Defence Minister confirmed that a joint U.S.-Israeli strike in Tehran killed Majid Khademi, the intelligence chief of Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps. Iran condemned the attack as a "terrorist attack" and blamed both Israel and the United States. The killing is the latest in a series of strikes targeting senior Iranian leadership since late February.

stories.title: Iran rejects latest ceasefire proposal as Trump deadline approaches
stories.summary: Iran rejected the latest U.S. ceasefire proposal as President Donald Trump's deadline approaches. Trump's deadline centers on Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately one-fifth of the world's oil is shipped during peacetime.

stories.title: Russia provided Iran with list of Israeli energy targets, Ukrainian intelligence finds - exclusive
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reportedly found that Russia provided Iran with a categorized list of Israeli energy targets, divided into three tiers based on strategic importance.

stories.title: Former Russian governor gets 14-year prison sentence for taking bribes tied to border fortifications
stories.summary: A court in Kursk sentenced former regional Governor Alexei Smirnov to 14 years in a maximum-security prison and fined him 400 million rubles for accepting bribes connected to border fortification contracts.

stories.title: Government simplifies modernization of aviation to combat Shahed-type drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has simplified procedures for modernizing aircraft to counter Iranian-designed Shahed-type drones, streamlining the re-equipping process for the country's aviation forces.

stories.title: Ogra, PSO come under fire for poor monitoring of oil stocks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority and Pakistan State Oil faced criticism in Islamabad for inadequate online monitoring and automation of petroleum stock and supply data. The cabinet committee responded by deciding to activate law enforcement and investigation agencies to monitor retail petroleum outlets and counter hoarding.

stories.title: Hormuz closure divides the fortunes of Middle Eastern oil states
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected Middle Eastern oil-producing states differently depending on their geographic positions. Countries with alternative export routes have fared better than those dependent on transit through the strait.

stories.title: F-15s assassinated Khamenei, now hunting Iran ballistic missiles, Air Force base chief tells 'Post'
stories.summary: The chief of Israel's Hatzerim Air Force Base revealed that F-15 fighter jets were used in the operation that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei and are now being deployed to hunt Iranian ballistic missile crews despite ongoing air defense threats.

stories.title: Murmansk governor confirms Russian general killed in An-26 crash in Crimea
stories.summary: Murmansk Governor Andrei Chibis confirmed that Lieutenant General Alexander Otroshchenko was among those killed when an An-26 military transport plane crashed in Russian-occupied Crimea on March 31. There were no survivors.

stories.title: 2 dead, including pregnant woman, in Russia flooding
stories.summary: Two people, including a pregnant woman, died in flooding in the Derbent district of Dagestan, Russia, according to the TASS news agency citing the republic's emergency medicine center.

stories.title: Russian shelling of Dnipropetrovsk region leaves ten people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched more than fifty attacks on the Nikopol, Synelnykove, and Kryvyi Rih districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring ten people.

stories.title: Hermitage director says ritual significance now outweighs artistic value in Russian society, defends transfer of relics to Orthodox Church
stories.summary: Hermitage Museum director Mikhail Piotrovsky commented on the transfer of religious relics from Russian museums to the Russian Orthodox Church, stating that ritual significance now outweighs artistic value in Russian society, and defending the museum's decision.

stories.title: IAEA Director General Grossi shares fears over potential for renewed nuclear arms race
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi expressed concern about the potential for a renewed nuclear arms race, noting that Iran's lack of cooperation has caused the agency to lose the continuity of knowledge needed to confirm Iran's nuclear program is entirely peaceful.

stories.title: IDF Home Front Command extends siren warning times for Hezbollah rockets in North
stories.summary: Israel's IDF Home Front Command extended siren warning times for Hezbollah rocket threats in 22 locations across the Golan Heights, increasing the alert window from 'immediate' to 15–30 seconds depending on the specific town.

stories.title: Israel rescuers say four bodies recovered from Iran strike site
stories.summary: Israeli rescue teams recovered four bodies from a site in Israel struck by Iranian forces. Dozens of firefighters and medical personnel had been deployed to the scene on the evening of April 5.

stories.title: PDMA issues flood advisory for several KP districts
stories.summary: The Provincial Disaster Management Authority in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, issued a flood advisory for multiple districts from April 7 to 8. The Kabul River at Nowshera was expected to reach low to medium flood levels, with flash flooding also anticipated along associated tributaries and other rivers in the region.

stories.title: Russia to grade school students’ behavior as ‘exemplary,’ ‘acceptable,’ or ‘unacceptable,’ Kommersant reports
stories.summary: Russia's Education Ministry announced that schools nationwide will adopt a three-tier behavior grading system for students, with ratings of "exemplary," "acceptable," or "unacceptable," according to the Russian business daily Kommersant.

stories.title: RBC reports Russia orders police not to identify themselves as law enforcement on social media
stories.summary: Russian police officers have been ordered not to identify themselves as law enforcement on social media or messaging apps, according to reports by Russian outlets RBC and Ura.ru citing unnamed sources.

stories.title: Russian army strikes Sloviansk, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled a residential area in Sloviansk, Donetsk region, killing at least one person and injuring five others.

stories.title: Miners escape from attacked coal mine in Russian-controlled Ukraine, official says
stories.summary: All 41 miners trapped underground after Ukraine struck the Bilorechenska coal mine in the Russian-controlled Luhansk region have been safely evacuated. A Russian-installed official confirmed on Monday that all personnel were accounted for.

stories.title: Russia’s internet regulator says DDoS attacks hit record levels in February and March, surging after reports of Telegram ban
stories.summary: Russia's internet regulator Roskomnadzor reported record levels of DDoS attacks in February and March, with the surge occurring after reports of a potential Telegram ban in the country.

stories.title: Iran’s ‘lost the key’ post offers comic relief amid global tension
stories.summary: Iran posted a sarcastic social media message in response to US President Donald Trump's threats to attack Iranian infrastructure, including power installations and bridges, if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened before his deadline. The post provided a moment of dark humor amid escalating tensions.

stories.title: Drone strikes occupation administration building in Starobilsk, Luhansk region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike significantly damaged the building of a former district administration in Starobilsk, located in the Russian-occupied part of Luhansk region.

stories.title: Israel strikes Iran’s largest petrochemical complex, defence minister says
stories.summary: Israel struck the South Pars Petrochemical complex in Asaluyeh, described as Iran's largest petrochemical facility. Several explosions were reportedly heard at the site, according to Israel's defense minister.

stories.title: Moscow university tightens expulsion rules as students allege military recruitment drive
stories.summary: Moscow's MIREA university tightened its expulsion rules, now requiring students to clear all outstanding academic debts by April 15 or face removal. Students allege the policy change is connected to a military recruitment drive, as previously students were not expelled until accumulating five or more unresolved course failures.

stories.title: Younger Hungarian voters spurn Orban, some say they will leave if he is re-elected
stories.summary: Younger Hungarian voters are increasingly turning against Prime Minister Viktor Orbán ahead of a pivotal election. Some who grew up under his government say they will leave Hungary if the longtime leader wins another term, emerging as a key bloc driving opposition support.

stories.title: RBC: Russia’s digital ministry sends companies guide to detecting VPNs on user devices, notes iPhones pose challenge
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry sent major internet companies a guide for detecting VPN services on user devices, according to RBC. The document, confirmed by IT industry sources, noted that iPhones pose a particular challenge for detection.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video does not show Iranian soldiers capturing US pilot after shooting down jet
stories.summary: A viral video falsely claimed to show Iranian forces capturing a US pilot after downing an F-15 fighter jet. Fact-checkers determined the footage is old and actually depicts a Libyan soldier performing a parachute jump, unrelated to the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: US regulator ends probe into Tesla's 'actually smart summon' feature after software fixes
stories.summary: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration closed its investigation into Tesla's "actually smart summon" feature after the company implemented software fixes. The probe had focused on low-speed incidents, with no injuries or fatalities reported.

stories.title: Iranian dissident to ‘Post’: Someone had been sent by Iran’s regime to kill me
stories.summary: An Iranian dissident told the Jerusalem Post that someone sent by Iran's regime attempted to kill him at his home in Malmö, Sweden, on the evening of September 2, when he and his wife were not expecting visitors.

stories.title: Russian attacks in Kherson region leave one killed, injure ten
stories.summary: One person was killed and ten others were injured in Russian attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region on April 6.

stories.title: Austerity delusion
stories.summary: A commentary criticizes Pakistan's government for announcing superficial austerity measures, including declining a single oil price hike, while continuing lavish spending such as purchasing a multibillion-rupee Gulfstream jet. The piece argues these steps fail to deliver meaningful financial reform or address structural inequality.

stories.title: Ukraine missile maker targets 'game changer' air defence system by 2027
stories.summary: Ukrainian missile manufacturer Fire Point is in talks with European companies to develop a new low-cost air defence system by 2027. The system would serve as an alternative to the Patriot system, which has become increasingly difficult to obtain.

stories.title: Propagandist Margarita Simonyan’s Telegram channel loses more than half its views after Russia blocks app
stories.summary: Views on Russian state media figure Margarita Simonyan's Telegram channel dropped 52.3 percent in late March compared to late February, according to analysis by the Telegram channel ChTD, following Russia's reported blocking of the Telegram app.

stories.title: Israeli doctor arrested on suspicion of involvement in stabbing
stories.summary: An Israeli doctor was arrested on suspicion of involvement in a stabbing incident in which a 34-year-old man from Petah Tikva was wounded during a violent altercation.

stories.title: Judicial magistrate grants bail to PTI protesters arrested for demonstrating near Karachi Press Club
stories.summary: A judicial magistrate in Karachi granted bail to 24 PTI workers and leaders arrested for protesting near Karachi Press Club against fuel price increases linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Four other PTI leaders were sent to an anti-terrorism court.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on Novorossiysk oil terminal and Be-12 amphibious aircraft
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its defense forces struck the Sheskharis oil terminal in Krasnodar Krai, Russia, on the night of April 6. The military also confirmed a strike on a Be-12 amphibious aircraft.

stories.title: Moscow concert hall attacker dies by suicide in jail, Russian authorities say
stories.summary: A man sentenced to life in prison for his role in the March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack died by suicide at a Moscow pretrial detention center, according to RBC citing Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service.

stories.title: Senate panel rejects bill seeking to enhance women’s participation in politcal process
stories.summary: A Pakistani Senate committee rejected a PTI lawmaker's bill to amend the Elections Act to require political parties to ensure at least 33 percent of office-bearers at all levels are women. Nearly all other parties opposed the measure.

stories.title: SSU, Defense Forces hit oil terminal at Novorossiysk port – source
stories.summary: Ukraine's SSU Special Operations Center "Alpha" and other defense force components, including military intelligence and special operations units, carried out a drone strike on the Sheskharis oil terminal at Russia's Novorossiysk seaport in Krasnodar region.

stories.title: Kremlin says 'highly likely' that Ukraine planted explosives near Hungary-bound gas pipeline
stories.summary: The Kremlin stated it is highly likely that evidence will emerge showing Ukraine planted explosives discovered near a gas pipeline in Serbia that carries Russian gas to Hungary. Moscow said conclusive proof had not yet been established.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Christian party official in Lebanon, widening divisions over Hezbollah
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on an apartment east of Beirut in Ain Saadeh, Lebanon, killed a local official from a Christian political party. The attack has sharpened internal Lebanese divisions over Hezbollah as Israeli strikes expand to new areas of the country.

stories.title: Crocus Attack Accomplice Found Dead in Prison Cell in Apparent Suicide
stories.summary: Yakubdzhoni Davlatkhon Yusufzoda, who was sentenced to life in prison last month for aiding and abetting terrorism in connection with the Crocus City Hall attack in Moscow, was found dead in his prison cell in what authorities described as an apparent suicide.

stories.title: DIU wants ‘moving map’ to help aircrews with situational awareness
stories.summary: The Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit is seeking a prototype "moving map" platform to improve situational awareness for mobility aircrews. The tool would address gaps in older aircraft that lack modern communications equipment.

stories.title: Kremlin says the whole Middle East is 'on fire'
stories.summary: The Kremlin declared on Monday that the entire Middle East is "on fire" due to the escalating US and Israeli attacks on Iran. Moscow said the Iran war was expanding in both geographic scope and economic impact.

stories.title: Hegseth says strikes on Iran increasing as Hormuz deadline looms
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced that Monday would see the largest volume of American strikes on Iran since the war began, as Trump's deadline over the Strait of Hormuz closure draws near.

stories.title: Russians strike Kramatorsk with 'Smerch' MLRS, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the courtyard of a multi-story building in central Kramatorsk, Donetsk region, using a Smerch multiple launch rocket system on April 6. One resident was injured, and surrounding buildings, vehicles, a school, and an administrative building sustained damage.

stories.title: Video: Iran’s top university hit in US-Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Footage emerged showing damaged research buildings at Sharif University of Technology in Tehran following a joint U.S.-Israeli strike on the prominent academic institution.

stories.title: Trump says Iranians 'animals' when asked why he would bomb power plants
stories.summary: President Trump referred to Iranians as "animals" when asked why bombing civilian infrastructure such as power plants would not constitute a war crime. He cited casualty figures from Iran's crackdown on domestic protests to justify the potential strikes.

stories.title: Israel's death penalty law draws inspiration from US policy, Ben-Gvir tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir told the Jerusalem Post that a proposed death penalty law draws on U.S. policy. Under the bill, terrorists in the West Bank would automatically face capital punishment unless specific appeals are made, while terrorists elsewhere could receive either the death penalty or life imprisonment.

stories.title: Reopening the Strait of Hormuz & Saving Downed Pilots
stories.summary: Two retired U.S. admirals, Admiral Jamie Foggo and Vice Admiral John "Fozzie" Miller, discussed the military challenges of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively blocked. The conversation covered Iran's use of mines, drones, and missiles, as well as potential U.S. strategies including air strikes and a possible Marine raid on Kharg Island.

stories.title: Trump threats cause dilemma for US officers: disobey orders or commit war crimes
stories.summary: Legal experts argue that U.S. President Donald Trump's threats to bomb Iranian civilian infrastructure, including power plants and bridges, would constitute war crimes. The situation raises a dilemma for U.S. military officers who could face orders to carry out such strikes by Trump's Tuesday deadline.

stories.title: Spanish PM's party gains on anti-war stance, support for far right stalls in polls
stories.summary: Spain's ruling Socialist Party has gained voter support following Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's opposition to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to two polls published on Monday. Meanwhile, the far-right Vox party, which supports the military offensive, has seen its poll numbers decline.

stories.title: Iran says electricity system can handle potential US bombing
stories.summary: Iranian officials stated that the national electricity system is prepared to remain operational even if the United States follows through on President Trump's threat to bomb the country's power plants.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz ‘deeply’ concerned after 3 Pakistani nationals injured in UAE amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Three Pakistani nationals were injured at Khor Fakkan port in the UAE after a missile was intercepted during Iran's retaliatory strikes against US and Israeli forces. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed concern and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured civilians.

stories.title: War update: 56 combat clashes since morning, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions remain most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 56 combat clashes with Russian troops since the start of the day, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Govt. denies report alleging more than 1,800 killed since junta took power
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's government denied a Human Rights Watch report alleging that more than 1,800 civilians have been killed since the military junta seized power three years ago, calling the findings false. The report was based on open-source information.

stories.title: Iran war continues to disrupt fuel supplies as US issues ultimatum [Africanews Today]
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has again postponed his ultimatum to Iran, threatening to destroy critical Iranian infrastructure if Tehran does not comply by a Tuesday deadline. The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict continues to disrupt fuel supplies across multiple regions.

stories.title: Israel launches fresh strikes in Beirut as Hezbollah faces homegrown anger over new war
stories.summary: Israel launched new airstrikes in Beirut targeting Hezbollah operatives accused of killing four Israeli soldiers. A Lebanese Forces party official was also reported killed in a strike intended for a Hezbollah operative, fueling domestic anger in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran rejects ceasefire proposal, wants definitive end to war
stories.summary: Iran formally rejected a proposed ceasefire truce in its war with the United States and Israel, calling instead for a definitive and permanent end to hostilities, despite Trump's threat to destroy Iranian power plants and bridges.

stories.title: Ex-captives slam choice of hostage point man Gal Hirsch to light Independence Day torch
stories.summary: Former Israeli hostages and their families criticized the selection of hostage envoy Gal Hirsch to light the Independence Day torch. They called the choice "a slap in the face," referencing their earlier demands for his resignation over comments about hostage protests benefiting Hamas.

stories.title: Hungary puts gas pipeline under military protection amid false-flag accusations
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán placed a gas pipeline near the Serbian border under military protection after Serbia reported finding explosives near the route carrying Russian gas to Hungary. Accusations of a false-flag operation have emerged ahead of a Hungarian election and a visit by U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

stories.title: Democrats blast Trump for Iran ‘war crimes’ threat; Republicans supportive
stories.summary: Democratic members of the U.S. Congress criticized President Trump's threats against Iranian infrastructure as potential war crimes, while Republican lawmakers voiced support. The backlash followed an expletive-laden Easter Sunday message from the president.

stories.title: Zelensky reviews reports from Syrskyi and Hnatov
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky reviewed battlefield reports from Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi and official Hnatov. Russian forces are concentrating their main efforts in the Oleksandrivka and Pokrovsk directions, where Ukrainian resistance is reportedly strongest.

stories.title: 10 killed in Israeli shelling, militia clashes at Gaza camp
stories.summary: At least 10 people were killed in the al-Maghazi camp in Gaza after Israeli shelling and a firefight broke out when gunmen believed to be affiliated with an anti-Hamas group attempted to detain people at the camp.

stories.title: How Asia became ground zero for the oil crisis
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war has disrupted oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, causing fuel shortages that have hit Asian markets first, raising concerns about a broader global energy crisis.

stories.title: Trump uses Neville Chamberlain jibe to mock Starmer over stance on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump appeared to compare UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to Neville Chamberlain over Starmer's refusal to back U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran. The remarks, made during an Easter Monday White House event, reflect Trump's frustration with Britain's skepticism about the conflict's aims and legality.

stories.title: Ongoing turbulence: How the Iran war is upending global aviation
stories.summary: The war involving Iran has caused major disruptions to global aviation, with grounded fleets, soaring fuel costs, and rising ticket prices threatening to reshape international air travel routes.

stories.title: House Democrats call for permanent solution to Cuban crises after witnessing energy blockade
stories.summary: U.S. House Democrats Pramila Jayapal and Jonathan Jackson visited Cuba and called for a permanent solution to crises on the island, including the effects of a U.S. energy blockade. They met with Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel and other officials during a five-day trip.

stories.title: Trump hails Iran rescue, warns of strikes as deadline looms
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that strikes on Iran's critical infrastructure could follow if negotiations fail by his Tuesday, April 7 deadline. The warning came after the White House described a rescue operation that recovered a wounded American pilot from Iran. Pakistan is involved in mediation efforts.

stories.title: Syria to issue law 'regulating' protests after anti-UAE demo
stories.summary: Syria's interior ministry announced it is drafting legislation to regulate public demonstrations after pro-Palestinian protesters stormed the UAE embassy in the country.

stories.title: Iran has formulated its response to ceasefire proposals, foreign ministry spokesperson says
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson announced that Tehran has formulated its response to ceasefire proposals. The spokesperson added that Iran's requirements have already been communicated through an intermediary channel.

stories.title: US Democratic lawmakers visit Cuba, call on Trump to ‘bring the rhetoric down’
stories.summary: US Democratic Representatives Pramila Jayapal and Jonathan Jackson visited Cuba, the first congressional delegation to the island in 2025. They called on President Trump to ease his de facto oil blockade, describing it as an illegal energy embargo causing widespread suffering on the ground.

stories.title: Trump warns deadline ‘final’ as Iran pushes proposal to end war
stories.summary: President Trump declared his deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is final, dismissing an Iranian peace proposal as insufficient to prevent strikes on the country's infrastructure.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks gas station in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a gas station with a drone in the village of Zolochiv, Bohodukhiv District, Kharkiv region, causing fuel tanks to catch fire.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Christian party official in Lebanon, widening divisions over Hezbollah
stories.summary: An Israeli strike in Lebanon killed an official from the Lebanese Forces, a Christian party opposed to Hezbollah, deepening existing divisions within Lebanon over the role of the Iran-backed group.

stories.title: PIA cuts operations, ends discounts amid rise in jet fuel prices due to war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines ended all passenger discounts except for children and infants and reduced flight operations due to soaring jet fuel prices driven by global supply chain disruptions linked to the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: 80% of Syrians still suffering food insecurity
stories.summary: The World Food Programme reports that 80% of Syrians continue to suffer from food insecurity amid widespread poverty in the war-ravaged country.

stories.title: IDF strikes three Tehran airports, targets dozens of Iranian fighter jets in attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force struck three airports in Tehran—Bahram, Mehrabad, and Azmayesh—targeting dozens of Iranian fighter jets in coordinated attacks involving IAF jets.

stories.title: The Moscow Zoo’s Manul Is a Social Media Star. He Still Can’t Find a Mate.
stories.summary: At least seven countries have reportedly declined to provide a mate for Timofei, a Pallas's cat (manul) at the Moscow Zoo who has become a social media celebrity in Russia.

stories.title: Intelligence officers discover body of Nepali mercenary who fought on Russia's side in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence officers discovered the body of a Nepali citizen among Russian forces killed in the Donetsk region. The individual had been fighting as a mercenary for Russia.

stories.title: 3 dead, 15 injured as Russia hits Ukraine’s port city Odesa in major drone strike
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes on the southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa on Monday killed at least three people, including a woman and her young daughter, and injured 15 others. A drone struck a multi-storey residential building, causing fires and significant destruction, according to military governor Oleh Kiper.

stories.title: Trump praised airman’s rescue in Iran during White House Easter event
stories.summary: During the White House Easter Egg Roll, President Trump praised the rescue of a downed American airman in Iran, highlighting the military operation in his public remarks.

stories.title: Iran hangs another young man as regime steps up executions of protesters under cover of war
stories.summary: Iran executed 23-year-old Ali Fahim for an alleged attack on a Basij base during January protests, marking the regime's 10th execution of political prisoners in eight days according to human rights groups.

stories.title: ICE agents reportedly detain wife of US soldier just days after their marriage
stories.summary: ICE agents detained Annie Ramos, 22, the wife of U.S. Army Staff Sergeant Matthew Blank, at his military base in Louisiana just days after their marriage. Blank, who has served over five years and previously deployed to the Middle East and Europe, was preparing for deployment at the time of his wife's detention.

stories.title: Greek PM vows to tackle ‘deep state’ in wake of farm fraud scandal
stories.summary: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis vowed to tackle what he called a "deep state" amid a political crisis over a farm fraud scandal involving the alleged scamming of EU agricultural funds. The scandal has already forced the resignation of multiple government ministers.

stories.title: Israeli officials do not expect a ceasefire in Iran any time soon, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli officials do not expect a near-term ceasefire in the five-week-old conflict with Iran. Although the US and Iran received a framework peace plan, Tehran rejected reopening the Strait of Hormuz as a condition.

stories.title: Iranian police fire at US helicopters on rescue mission for downed fighter jet in Iran
stories.summary: Iranian police released video footage showing heavy gunfire directed at U.S. helicopters conducting a rescue mission for a downed F-15E crew member near Isfahan, Iran.

stories.title: Iran accuses UN nuclear watchdog of inaction, warns of risk from attacks
stories.summary: Iran's atomic energy chief Mohammad Eslami accused the UN nuclear watchdog IAEA of inaction, saying its silence emboldens aggression against nuclear facilities such as the Bushehr power plant. The letter, addressed to the IAEA director, warned of escalating risks from military strikes near nuclear sites.

stories.title: Kharkiv under Russian drone attack, three more strikes recorded
stories.summary: Russian drones struck Kharkiv's Kyivskyi district in a series of attacks, with at least three additional strikes recorded. Authorities said the air threat remained ongoing.

stories.title: Libya’s oil disputes mirror Hormuz crisis, fuel European energy fears
stories.summary: Proxy conflicts over Libya's oil sector have intensified alongside the Strait of Hormuz crisis, compounding global supply vulnerabilities and heightening European energy security concerns.

stories.title: Intelligence head of Iran's Revolutionary Guards killed in strike, media say
stories.summary: The head of the intelligence organization of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was killed Monday in what Iranian media described as a strike by the "American-Zionist enemy." The IRGC confirmed the killing in an official statement carried by Iranian state media.

stories.title: Iranian state TV shows identity documents from the site of destroyed US planes
stories.summary: Iranian state television broadcast what appear to be identity documents recovered from a destroyed U.S. aircraft in Iran, attributed to an individual identified as Amanda M. Ryder. The documents included what appeared to be an Israeli border control permit.

stories.title: Myanmar’s new president Min Aung Hlaing faces genocide complaint in Indonesia
stories.summary: A group of civil society organizations filed a criminal complaint in Indonesia on Monday against Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing, accusing him of genocide against the Rohingya ethnic group. Indonesia hosts the ASEAN headquarters, and Myanmar's membership in the bloc has been strained since the 2021 military coup.

stories.title: Iran top university struck as war cripples healthcare system
stories.summary: The Sharif University of Technology in Tehran was struck in the latest high-profile attack on Iranian institutions, while healthcare services across Iran continue to be routinely targeted during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Russian troops attack Nikopol, leaving seven injured
stories.summary: On April 6, Russian forces attacked the city of Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, wounding seven people.

stories.title: US-Israel bet on minorities toppling Iran's regime is misguided
stories.summary: An opinion piece by analyst Ghazi Dahman argues that the U.S.-Israeli strategy of relying on ethnic minorities to topple Iran's regime is misguided, overestimating their role in regime change while ignoring Iran's complex social realities.

stories.title: Zhirinovsky’s ‘Spirit’ Warns of Nuclear Fire and American Collapse in Bizarre Interview
stories.summary: A pro-Kremlin Russian tabloid published an interview with a psychic who claimed to have summoned the spirit of the late ultranationalist politician Vladimir Zhirinovsky, who purportedly warned of nuclear fire and American collapse.

stories.title: IDF struck Iran's largest petrochemical plant, second facility hit in two days, Katz confirms
stories.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed Israeli strikes rendered Iran's largest petrochemical plant non-functional. He stated that strikes on two facilities responsible for 85 percent of Iran's petrochemical exports had taken them out of use.

stories.title: Lebanese Shi’a party Amal competing, coordinating with Hezbollah, experts tell ‘Post’
stories.summary: Experts told the Jerusalem Post that Lebanon's Shi'a party Amal is both competing and coordinating with Hezbollah. Unlike Hezbollah, Amal operates primarily as a political organization and has not been targeted by Israel.

stories.title: Georgia political candidate sorry for fluffy challah in a Passover ad
stories.summary: Georgia Democratic candidate Nathalie Kanani apologized after a Passover advertisement featured an image of fluffy challah bread, calling it "an oversight that should not have happened."

stories.title: Arizona hiker stung more than 100 times by bees left in critical condition
stories.summary: A hiker in north Phoenix, Arizona, was left in critical condition after being stung more than 100 times by bees on Lookout Mountain Preserve over the Easter weekend. Rescue teams airlifted the man by helicopter to a hospital after he was unable to descend on his own.

stories.title: Gaza: Israel shoots UN staff vehicle, kills 10 in strike on Maghazi refugee camp
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes and military vehicle fire killed at least 10 people near the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. A UN staff member was also killed and three others wounded when Israeli forces fired on a WHO vehicle in southern Gaza.

stories.title: Top Jerusalem Islamic official calls on West to tell Israel: Don’t mess with Al-Aqsa
stories.summary: Mustafa Abu Sway, deputy head of the Islamic Waqf in Jerusalem, urged Western nations to press Israel against altering the status quo at Al-Aqsa Mosque, warning that restrictions imposed by Israeli authorities risk destabilizing the region.

stories.title: What does 'Iran-linked' even mean?
stories.summary: An analysis piece examines how international media use the term "Iran-linked" when covering Western adversaries, arguing that outlets often follow narratives set by Israel and the United States regarding Middle Eastern conflicts.

stories.title: Rwanda: Why Rwanda's Fuel Demand Surged By Nearly 40 Percent in April
stories.summary: Rwanda's daily demand for petroleum products surged to 3.1 million litres in early April, up nearly 40 percent from the usual range of 2 to 2.5 million litres, according to Minister of Trade and Industry Prudence Sebahizi.

stories.title: Russian Crypto Payments Network Seeks Africa Expansion – FT
stories.summary: A Russian crypto payments network called A7 is seeking to expand into Africa, according to the Financial Times. The network offers Russia a way to circumvent Western financial sanctions imposed over the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine regains control of front-line areas in south-east and east, army chief says
stories.summary: Ukraine's army chief reported that Ukrainian forces have regained control of front-line areas in the country's south-east and east. However, Russian troops continue to press ahead with a spring offensive despite Ukraine's recent battlefield successes.

stories.title: Iran struck US forces relocated on Kuwait's Bubiyan island, military spokesperson says
stories.summary: Iran said it targeted US forces located on Kuwait's Bubiyan island, according to a spokesperson for Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters. The claim was made in a video statement shared by Iranian state media on Monday.

stories.title: Serbian intelligence denies involvement of Ukraine in explosives incident near TurkStream pipeline
stories.summary: The head of Serbian intelligence stated that Ukraine was not involved in the explosives incident near the TurkStream gas pipeline connecting Serbia and Hungary, directly contradicting claims by Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán implicating Kyiv.

stories.title: Iran Guards say preparing plan for new order in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced it is preparing a plan to establish a new order in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian lawmakers have also proposed imposing tolls and taxes on vessels transiting the strategic waterway.

stories.title: ‘Peace process ongoing’: FO neither confirms nor denies reports of Pakistan proposing framework to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office confirmed that a peace process regarding the US-Israel war on Iran is ongoing but declined to confirm or deny reports that Islamabad proposed a specific framework. Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi refused to comment on reported details of a 45-day ceasefire offer.

stories.title: North Korea: Kim's daughter now seen as likely heir — South
stories.summary: South Korea's intelligence service assessed that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's daughter is increasingly being positioned as his likely successor. Officials noted her growing appearances at military events are intended to normalize the idea of a female heir.

stories.title: Israel’s city of Eilat struck by Yemeni drones
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for a drone attack on the Israeli city of Eilat, which the Israeli military described as a coordinated assault from Iran, Lebanon, and Yemen. Explosions were also reported in Jerusalem and the greater Tel Aviv area.

stories.title: Gaza camp offers children a sense of safety
stories.summary: The Samir Project has established a camp in Gaza aimed at providing children with opportunities to learn, heal, and regain a sense of safety amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz will never return to previous status: Iran’s IRGC
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared that the Strait of Hormuz will never return to its previous status. The statement came after US President Donald Trump publicly demanded Iran reopen the critical waterway.

stories.title: Churches and politicians in South Sudan call for 'lasting peace' in Easter messages
stories.summary: Churches and political leaders in South Sudan issued Easter messages calling for lasting peace, amid growing fears the country could return to civil war less than a decade after its previous conflict ended.

stories.title: Senior Russian commander killed in March air crash, official says
stories.summary: Russian commander Alexander Otroshchenko, who led the 45th Army of the Northern Fleet's Air Force and Air Defence, was killed in an air crash in March, according to an official statement.

stories.title: Iran wartime executions mount as another protester hanged
stories.summary: Iran executed another man convicted in connection with nationwide January protests, as the number of wartime executions continues to mount amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Representatives from Pakistan’s fan industry seek policy interventions during meeting with finmin
stories.summary: Representatives from Pakistan's electric fan industry met virtually with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb to seek policy interventions. Led by FPCCI and PEFMA members, they requested measures to reduce raw material exports and promote energy-efficient fan manufacturing.

stories.title: How lessons from Iran war could shape mainland China’s calculus on Taiwan
stories.summary: Analysts are examining how the ongoing U.S.-Israeli war on Iran could influence mainland China's strategic calculations regarding a potential conflict over Taiwan. The analysis considers implications for asymmetric warfare, geopolitics, energy security, and Beijing's assessment of American military power.

stories.title: A bittersweet thrill: daytrippers watch US warplanes in action at RAF Fairford
stories.summary: Families and aviation enthusiasts gathered near the perimeter fence of RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England, to watch American warplanes take off and land as part of ongoing U.S. military operations related to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Liberia: Ministry of Health Tightens Access to Abortion Pills
stories.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Health announced stricter controls on the sale and use of misoprostol, a medication used in reproductive health. Critics warn the restrictions could push demand for abortion pills underground.

stories.title: Nigeria: What Cardoso's Legacy At CBN Would Look Like
stories.summary: The article examines the potential legacy of Olayemi Cardoso as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, focusing on his ongoing reform efforts and their long-term impact on the institution.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Called to Improve Business Climate to Fully Leverage China's Zero-Tariff Offer
stories.summary: Chinese Ambassador to Kenya Guo Haiyan urged Kenya to improve its business climate and support exporters to fully benefit from China's zero-tariff offer for African goods, warning that the advantages depend on domestic reforms and competitiveness.

stories.title: South Africa: Government to Engage Residents On Vaal Special Economic Zone
stories.summary: South Africa's Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, along with Gauteng provincial authorities and the Lesedi and Midvaal municipalities, will host public consultations on the planned designation of the Vaal Special Economic Zone.

stories.title: Israeli army fire on WHO vehicle in southern Gaza kills one, medics report
stories.summary: A WHO driver named Majdi Aslan was killed and a WHO doctor was wounded after Israeli army forces opened fire on a WHO vehicle in southern Gaza. Several other Palestinians were also injured in the incident.

stories.title: Associated Press pivots from newspaper journalism, offers buyouts to its US journalists
stories.summary: The Associated Press is shifting away from traditional newspaper journalism after 150 years, offering buyouts to U.S. journalists as it pivots toward visual journalism and AI-related ventures.

stories.title: Jerusalem man arrested, to be charged with spying for Iran
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man from Jerusalem was arrested and is expected to be charged with spying for Iran after reportedly being sent to film near a former prime minister's home. In a separate case, Israeli police suspect individuals manufactured and tested explosives on behalf of Iranian actors.

stories.title: Sweden to supply Ukraine with modern Tridon Mk2 air defense systems
stories.summary: Sweden announced plans to supply Ukraine's defense forces with Tridon Mk2 air defense systems. The advanced systems are intended to help counter Shahed-type drones and other aerial threats.

stories.title: IDF kills senior IRGC Quds Force officials in strikes against Iranian regime
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed it killed two senior IRGC Quds Force officials in separate strikes on Sunday: Imam Hussein Division artillery chief Kamil Melhem and Unit 840 chief Asghar Bagheri.

stories.title: Iran issues ceasefire demands, including protocol for Hormuz and lifting of sanctions
stories.summary: Iran delivered a 10-point list of demands in response to a Pakistan-mediated peace proposal, rejecting a temporary ceasefire and calling for a permanent end to the war. The demands include protocols for Strait of Hormuz transit, regional conflict resolution, reconstruction, and the lifting of sanctions.

stories.title: Iran’s internet blackout is longest national shutdown since Arab spring
stories.summary: Iran's internet shutdown, which began on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes started, has lasted more than 38 days, making it the longest national-scale blackout since the Arab spring. Iranian authorities cut all internet access, leaving citizens with limited information about the ongoing war.

stories.title: Indian envoy, Nepal's new Foreign Minister discuss bilateral ties
stories.summary: Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava met with Nepal's newly appointed Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal to discuss strengthening bilateral ties and cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Liberia: Two Nimba Natives Declare 2029 Presidential Bids, Eying Strong Local Support
stories.summary: Two prominent political figures from Nimba County, Liberia, have announced their candidacies for the 2029 presidential election, citing strong local support in the vote-rich county while also seeking backing from other regions.

stories.title: Gaza grandmother loses her family due to Israeli attacks
stories.summary: A grandmother in Gaza has lost members of her family as a result of ongoing Israeli military attacks on the territory.

stories.title: Border Police arrest Hamas-linked West Bank resident in terror plot
stories.summary: Israeli Border Police arrested a Hamas-affiliated suspect near al-Mughayir in the West Bank. The individual was found carrying a will and materials indicating terrorist links, and was allegedly planning to carry out an attack.

stories.title: Education minister says wartime school limitations will likely be extended
stories.summary: Israel's education minister indicated that wartime school restrictions will likely be extended. The prime minister and senior cabinet officials are set to meet on reopening plans, contingent on an IDF Home Front Command assessment of the Iranian missile threat.

stories.title: US Supreme Court paves way to drop Capitol riot charges against ex-Trump ally Steve Bannon
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday cleared the way for the Justice Department to drop criminal charges against Steve Bannon, a former chief ally of President Donald Trump. Bannon had been convicted of defying a congressional subpoena issued during the investigation into the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack.

stories.title: 'We're sinking deeper': Iranians brace for infrastructure strikes as Trump deadline nears
stories.summary: Iranians are bracing for potential U.S. strikes on power plants and bridges as President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches. Civilians have expressed growing anxiety over the threatened destruction of critical infrastructure.

stories.title: US and Iran receive peace proposal as Trump vows ‘hell’ if Strait of Hormuz stays shut
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have received a peace proposal featuring a two-tier approach that calls for an immediate ceasefire followed by a comprehensive agreement. The development comes as President Donald Trump vowed severe consequences if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

stories.title: Will the Iran war usher in a new regional diplomatic order?
stories.summary: Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt have taken lead roles in mediating an end to the Iran war, potentially reshaping the geopolitics of Middle East diplomacy and the regional diplomatic order.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes near public transport stop in Kharkiv, leaving people injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck near a public transport stop in Kharkiv, injuring people. It was the second Russian attack on the city in a single day.

stories.title: Russia’s Largest Business Lobby Says It’s Open to Windfall Tax to Plug Budget Gap
stories.summary: Russia's largest business lobby, the RSPP, indicated openness to a windfall tax to address the country's budget gap. However, RSPP President Alexander Shokhin noted that many companies are currently operating at a loss.

stories.title: US and Iran reviewing ceasefire deal, reports say
stories.summary: Pakistan delivered a ceasefire proposal, tentatively called the 'Islamabad Accords,' to US and Iranian officials. The two-tier plan calls for an immediate ceasefire followed by a comprehensive agreement within 15–20 days. Both sides are reportedly reviewing the proposal.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Fire Point company is working on revolutionary system which can also transform European air defense
stories.summary: Ukraine's Fire Point company is developing a new defense system that its creators say could significantly enhance ballistic missile defense capabilities and potentially transform European air defense.

stories.title: Are Perceptions the Reality?
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest, curates Ukrainian media commentary and analysis to provide perspectives beyond battlefield reporting. The series highlights how Ukrainians debate politics, daily life, and public issues during the ongoing war with Russia.

stories.title: US boots on the ground in Iran could lead to widespread regional conflict, experts say
stories.summary: Experts warn that deploying US ground forces in Iran could trigger a widespread regional conflict, potentially disrupting global shipping lanes, energy markets, and political stability across the Middle East.

stories.title: A 12-hour drive through Iran offers glimpses of destruction, defiance and daily life
stories.summary: Associated Press journalists drove 12 hours through Iran after crossing from Turkey, documenting normality in cities untouched by the war contrasted with significant destruction in and around Tehran.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes hit south Beirut, country's south
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit Beirut's southern suburbs and areas in southern Lebanon on Monday. Israel's military said it was targeting the Iran-backed militant group Hezbollah, while Lebanese authorities reported broad strikes across the country's south.

stories.title: Iran will allow ships from ‘friendly nations’ to pass through Hormuz, Al Jazeera reports
stories.summary: Iran announced it will allow ships from designated friendly nations to transit the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for security fees. An Iranian official said passage permits have been issued to Indian, Pakistani, Turkish, and French vessels.

stories.title: Russia says 'highly likely' that Ukraine planted explosives near gas pipeline
stories.summary: The Kremlin stated it was "highly likely" that evidence would emerge showing Ukraine planted explosives found near a gas pipeline in Serbia that carries Russian gas to Hungary. Russia said conclusive proof had not yet been established.

stories.title: Russia resumes oil loading at Ust-Luga after attacks – Bloomberg
stories.summary: Russia's key Baltic port of Ust-Luga resumed oil-loading operations after several days of disruptions caused by multiple drone strikes, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: IAEA says strikes near Iran nuclear power plant 'must stop'
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi warned that military strikes near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant pose a serious danger to nuclear safety and called for them to stop immediately.

stories.title: Israel hits three airports in Tehran in new wave of strikes, says military
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck three airports in Tehran—Bahram, Mehrabad, and Azmayesh—claiming to target dozens of aircraft, helicopters, and military infrastructure at the sites.

stories.title: 1,1000 Ukrainian officers complete “Captain’s Training” program—NATO-based 7-day-per-week curriculum to shape battlefield leaders
stories.summary: Approximately 1,100 Ukrainian officers have completed a NATO-based training program known as "Captain's Training," which operates seven days a week. The curriculum is continuously updated with lessons from active combat to prepare officers for evolving battlefield threats.

stories.title: Iran says it let a Malaysian ship pass through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Iranian embassy in Malaysia announced that the first Malaysian ship since the start of the war was permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, describing the move as a gesture toward friendly nations.

stories.title: US, Iran weigh peace plan as Trump vows ‘hell’ if Strait of Hormuz stays shut
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are weighing a peace plan known as the "Islamabad Accord," which calls for an immediate ceasefire followed by a comprehensive deal. President Trump has threatened severe repercussions if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.

stories.title: China’s yuan may be going global faster than Western data suggests, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts suggest China's yuan may play a larger role in global payments than Western tracking systems indicate. A growing share of transactions is routed through Beijing's own cross-border payment system, which may not be fully captured by conventional data sources such as SWIFT.

stories.title: Russia attacks Kherson with Molniya drone, four people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Korabelnyi district of Kherson using a Molniya drone, injuring four people.

stories.title: Horrors in Sudan Highlight Deterioration of Western Diplomatic Corps
stories.summary: Western diplomatic efforts in Sudan have been hampered by decades of neglect that hollowed out expertise and experience within diplomatic corps. The ongoing horrors of Sudan's conflict have highlighted these deficiencies in Western diplomatic capacity.

stories.title: UN nuclear watchdog: Strikes near Iran’s nuclear power plant ‘must stop’
stories.summary: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi warned that strikes near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant pose a serious radiological danger and must stop. The IAEA statement did not explicitly name the US or Israel as responsible for the attacks.

stories.title: Couple dies as car plunges into canal in East Godavari; four others, including two children, rescued
stories.summary: A couple died when their car plunged into an irrigation canal in East Godavari district, India. Four other occupants, including two children, were rescued from the vehicle.

stories.title: Where are Iran’s power plants that Trump has threatened to destroy?
stories.summary: President Trump has threatened to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges if Iran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by 8 p.m. Tuesday. The threat has drawn attention to the locations and vulnerability of Iran's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Dozens of people killed, injured in Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit Beirut and southern Lebanon, killing dozens of people. Hezbollah claimed retaliatory attacks on targets in northern Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkiye sign MoU in bid to enhance judicial cooperation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court and Türkiye's Constitutional Court signed a memorandum of understanding on judicial cooperation in Islamabad. Chief Justice Yahya Afridi and Turkish Constitutional Court President Kadir Özkaya signed the agreement during a visit by a high-level Turkish delegation.

stories.title: Drone strikes high-rise building in Kharkiv; casualties reported
stories.summary: A Russian drone hit a high-rise residential building in Kharkiv's Kyivskyi district. Preliminary reports indicate at least three people were injured in the strike.

stories.title: Russia rains “Krasnopol-M2” techno-lethal shells on Ukraine, as five Russian plants remain outside Western sanctions
stories.summary: Russia is deploying Krasnopol-M2 laser-guided artillery shells against Ukrainian positions, with the munition noted for its precision and operational flexibility. Five Russian production plants linked to the shells reportedly remain outside the scope of Western sanctions.

stories.title: UNDP invests over $550M in Ukraine's energy sector since 2022 – regional director
stories.summary: The UNDP's regional director reported that the agency has invested over $550 million in Ukraine's energy sector since 2022, improving access to reliable electricity for more than 6.6 million Ukrainians in 2025.

stories.title: Israel says struck Iran's largest petrochemical facility
stories.summary: Israel bombed Iran's largest petrochemical complex on Monday, followed shortly by an attack on a second petrochemical facility, according to Israeli military statements.

stories.title: Araghchi condemns US-Israeli strikes on ‘MIT of Iran’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi condemned US-Israeli strikes on Sharif University in Tehran, calling it the 'MIT of Iran.' He warned of Iranian retaliation, stating 'aggressors will see our might.'

stories.title: U.S.-Israeli strikes kill Iran Guards intelligence chief: Guards
stories.summary: US-Israeli air strikes killed Majid Khademi, the intelligence chief of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Khademi had assumed the position in 2025 after his predecessor was killed in earlier Israeli strikes.

stories.title: PMD predicts partly cloudy weather with chances of rainfall in Karachi today
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy weather for Karachi on Monday with chances of thunderstorms or light to moderate rain. A westerly wave was affecting southwestern parts of the country, with temperatures expected between 22 and 31 degrees Celsius.

stories.title: US oil prices flip-flop ahead of Trump's deadline to bomb Iranian power plants
stories.summary: US oil prices fluctuated ahead of President Trump's deadline threatening to bomb Iranian power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened. Markets showed volatility as diplomatic and military tensions between Washington and Tehran remained unresolved.

stories.title: Senior Russian commander Alexander Otroshchenko killed in March air crash, official says
stories.summary: Senior Russian military commander Alexander Otroshchenko was killed in an An-26 aircraft crash in March, attributed to a suspected technical malfunction. The incident raised concerns about the aging state of Russia's An-26 transport fleet.

stories.title: Middle East War: Iran and US receive temporary truce proposal
stories.summary: As the Middle East conflict enters its second month, both the United States and Iran have received a draft proposal calling for a 45-day ceasefire. The proposal also urges Iran to ease its control over the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane.

stories.title: Egypt: Wide-ranging energy effects of the war in the Gulf ‌region
stories.summary: Egypt raised electricity prices for higher-use residential and commercial consumers starting in April, citing a severe global energy crisis. The electricity ministry linked the increases to disruptions caused by the ongoing war in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Jamie Dimon says US should strengthen allies economically, in veiled criticism of Trump
stories.summary: JP Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon urged the US to strengthen allies economically in his annual shareholder letter, in what appeared to be a veiled criticism of President Trump's tariff and foreign policy approach. His comments came as the Middle East conflict entered its sixth week.

stories.title: US and Iran reviewing ceasefire deal, reports say
stories.summary: Reports indicate the United States and Iran are reviewing a ceasefire proposal that involves an immediate temporary ceasefire followed by a comprehensive agreement. Foreign ministers from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey have met in Islamabad to discuss regional de-escalation.

stories.title: Three dead, 16 injured: Emergency rescue operations completed in Odesa following Russian shelling
stories.summary: Emergency rescue operations concluded at a high-rise building in Odesa that was struck in a nighttime Russian attack. Three people were killed and 16 were injured.

stories.title: Serbia clears Ukraine—no link to pipeline sabotage amid Hungary elections
stories.summary: Serbia's military chief stated that explosives found near the TurkStream pipeline bore US markings but said this does not indicate who planted them. Serbia's findings cleared Ukraine of involvement amid discussions linked to Hungarian elections.

stories.title: US-Israeli forces attack another petrochemical complex in southern Iran, says Fars news agency
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported a US-Israeli strike on a petrochemical complex in Marvdasht, the second such attack in 24 hours. The previous strike targeted the South Pars complex at Asaluyeh, where Iranian officials said the resulting fire was quickly contained.

stories.title: Israeli restrictions causes formula shortage for Gaza's newborns
stories.summary: Israeli restrictions on goods entering Gaza have caused a severe shortage of infant formula. Tens of thousands of newborns depend on formula, and any disruption poses serious health risks.

stories.title: Proposals for immediate ceasefire to halt war circulated to US and Iran
stories.summary: Mediators from Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey circulated proposals for an immediate ceasefire to Washington and Tehran to halt the five-week-old war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran warned that peace talks are "incompatible with threats," as Trump's deadline to bomb Iranian power plants loomed.

stories.title: In Novorossiysk, Unmanned Systems Forces struck the Admiral Grigorovich frigate, carrying Kalibr missiles
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck the Russian frigate Admiral Grigorovich, a Kalibr cruise-missile carrier, in the port of Novorossiysk.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Black Sea energy hub Novorossiysk
stories.summary: Ukraine conducted strikes on Novorossiysk, a key energy hub on Russia's Black Sea coast, as part of an escalating campaign to disrupt Russian energy infrastructure and reduce war financing.

stories.title: Two mountain ranges, two deserts, two seas: Iran’s geography is its greatest weapon
stories.summary: Military and political analysts assess that Iran's geography—including two mountain ranges, two deserts, and two seas—would make a US ground invasion extremely costly and unpredictable. US troops are reportedly approaching the Gulf region.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill Iran Guards intel chief as Trump deadline looms
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed the intelligence chief of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached. Iran continued to defy US threats to devastate its civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: At least four killed in strike on Haifa
stories.summary: Iranian missiles struck the northern Israeli city of Haifa, hitting a residential building and killing at least four people. The victims were found in the rubble of the structure following the attack.

stories.title: ‘Deeply distressing for all of us’: families react to Girlguiding’s trans exclusion
stories.summary: Beginning in September, Girlguiding UK will exclude transgender girls and trans young women volunteers, requiring them to hand in their memberships. Families affected described the policy change as deeply distressing, with some parents facing the prospect of their children being forced to leave.

stories.title: In maps and photos: Five Iranian civilian bridges at risk of US strikes
stories.summary: An analysis identifies five major civilian bridges in Iran that could be targeted under a US ultimatum referred to as 'Bridge Day,' highlighting the multimillion-dollar mega structures potentially at risk.

stories.title: Public health takes center stage in US midterm campaigns: ‘It’s already been politicized’
stories.summary: Some US political candidates are making public health a central campaign issue for the midterm elections amid the Trump administration's contentious approach to science policy. The grassroots organization Defend Public Health launched guiding principles called the People's Health Platform on Monday.

stories.title: Republicans fooled by AI-generated image of US crew member rescued in Iran
stories.summary: An AI-generated image falsely depicting a rescued US warplane crew member in Iran was shared over 21,000 times on X, fooling Republican politicians including Texas Governor Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton. The hoax prompted calls for a national "crash course in media literacy."

stories.title: Israeli air strikes kill seven in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed seven people across southern Lebanon. Four died in a strike on a vehicle in Kfar Roummane, one in Siddiqune, and two in a drone strike in Haris, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: Iran says won’t open Hormuz for temporary truce after Pakistan proposes 45-day ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan proposed a 45-day ceasefire plan to the US and Iran that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and subsequent negotiations. Iran rejected the Hormuz condition, and a White House official said Trump has not signed off on the proposal.

stories.title: Two mountain ranges, two deserts, two seas: Iran’s geography is its greatest weapon
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Iran's geography—including two mountain ranges, two deserts, and coastlines on two seas—could impose significant costs on any potential U.S. ground invasion of the country.

stories.title: Dozens attend Passover prayers at Western Wall as Al-Aqsa remains closed
stories.summary: Dozens of worshippers attended Passover prayers at the Western Wall in occupied Jerusalem while Al-Aqsa Mosque remained closed to Muslim worshippers. National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir pushed to resume ultra-nationalist raids into the compound.

stories.title: Israel kills Islamic Guards intel chief, bombs largest Iranian petrochemical plant
stories.summary: Israel announced it killed the IRGC intelligence chief and the head of the Quds Force's clandestine Unit 840. Defence Minister Katz vowed to continue targeting Iranian leaders, while Israeli forces also bombed Iran's largest petrochemical plant.

stories.title: Ukraine missile maker targets ‘game changer’ air defense system by 2027
stories.summary: Ukrainian missile manufacturer Fire Point, maker of the Flamingo cruise missile, is in talks with European defense companies to develop a new air defense system by 2027. The company has described the planned system as a potential game changer for Ukraine's defense capabilities.

stories.title: UAE says the use of Hormuz must be guaranteed in any US-Iran deal
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates stated that any U.S.-Iran deal must guarantee free passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies normally transit the waterway each day.

stories.title: Two Palestinians hospitalized in settler attack on West Bank village
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked a West Bank Palestinian village, hospitalizing two people. Tents used for housing and vehicles were burned, and the phrases 'Zionists revenge' and 'price tag' were spray-painted on property.

stories.title: Will private capital and disruption reshape the defense industrial base?
stories.summary: Private capital investment is flowing into defense firms at an increasing rate, but industry observers warn that without alignment among key stakeholders, the surge may not produce adequate returns or meaningfully reshape the defense industrial base.

stories.title: Iran wartime killings increase as another protester hanged
stories.summary: Iran executed 23-year-old Ali Fahim on Monday in connection with January's nationwide protests, continuing a wave of politically charged hangings. Human rights groups say Fahim and other defendants faced torture, unfair trials, and denial of legal counsel amid the country's escalating conflict with Israel and the US.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief elected president — what comes next?
stories.summary: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing has been elected president, transitioning from military uniform to the top civilian office. Analysts say the move is unlikely to bring peace or meaningfully distance the government from the authoritarian system established by the 2021 coup.

stories.title: In pictures: Debris from US aircraft downed in Iran during rescue mission
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump confirmed the rescue of a second airman downed over Iran after an F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over southwestern Iran. An A-10 attack jet involved in the rescue effort was also lost over the Persian Gulf. Trump called it one of the most daring rescue operations in US history.

stories.title: Iran state media: Revolutionary Guards targeted US and Israeli ships
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have targeted the US amphibious assault ship LHA-7, reportedly forcing it to withdraw into the southern Indian Ocean. The IRGC also claimed a strike on an Israel-linked container ship at an unspecified location.

stories.title: Germany works to clarify new rules on fighting-age men leaving country
stories.summary: Germany is working to clarify new regulations restricting fighting-age men from leaving the country. The law took effect in January but drew little public attention until April 3.

stories.title: Russians attack car with drone in Zaporizhzhia region, two people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the village of Preobrazhenka in the Polohy district of Zaporizhzhia region with a drone, targeting a civilian car. Two people were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Gulf war batters India’s glass heartland, testing New Delhi’s manufacturing drive
stories.summary: The glass-making industry in Firozabad, India, known as the country's "Glass City," has been severely impacted by the Middle East war driving up energy costs. Gas-fired furnaces require constant temperatures above 1,000°C, and soaring gas prices have idled factories and displaced thousands of workers.

stories.title: Bombing of Iran's pharma producers threatens patients' lives
stories.summary: Ongoing US and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian pharmaceutical and medical facilities are disrupting access to essential medications. Doctors and activists warn that thousands of patients are being denied critical medical treatment as a result.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Ukraine's Odesa kills three, regional governor says
stories.summary: Russia launched a drone attack on the Ukrainian Black Sea port city of Odesa overnight on Monday, killing three people including a child. The regional governor reported damage to infrastructure, residential buildings, and administrative buildings.

stories.title: Polymarket criticized over ‘disgusting’ bets on fate of pilots on US jet shot by Iran
stories.summary: Polymarket, an online betting platform, stopped accepting wagers on when US warplane crew members shot down by Iranian forces would be rescued after criticism from Democratic Representative Seth Moulton. The Massachusetts congressman and Iraq war veteran condemned the bets as disgraceful.

stories.title: US Army wants new grenade launcher, ammunition to be able to destroy drones
stories.summary: The US Army is seeking prototype submissions for a new grenade launcher and specialized ammunition capable of destroying drones. The solicitation calls for 16 weapons, fire control systems, and approximately 25,000 rounds of ammunition.

stories.title: South Korea to send ships to Saudi Red Sea port to avoid Hormuz
stories.summary: South Korea announced plans to send five ships to the Saudi Arabian Red Sea port of Yanbu to establish alternative oil supply routes, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing tensions in the waterway.

stories.title: Israel says it killed leader of IRGC Quds Force undercover unit
stories.summary: Israel's military spokesperson announced the assassination of Asghar Barkeri, identified as the leader of an undercover unit within the IRGC Quds Force. Iran has not commented on the claim.

stories.title: UK police arrest protesters outside base linked to US jet downed in Iran
