stories.summary: US-Israeli air strikes on a residential area in Baharestan County, Tehran province, killed 13 people overnight, including six children under the age of 10, according to Iran's Fars news agency.

stories.title: Russians living in exile cope with grief far from home
stories.summary: Russians living in exile since the start of the war against Ukraine have been unable to return home for security reasons. Three exiles shared with DW how they cope with the loss of loved ones while separated from their families.

stories.title: Israel estimates 1,000 Iranian missiles still threaten it as war grinds into second month
stories.summary: Israel has assessed that Iran retains more than 1,000 ballistic missiles capable of reaching Israeli territory, while Hezbollah in Lebanon holds an estimated 10,000 shorter-range rockets. An Israeli air force officer disclosed the figures as the war enters its second month.

stories.title: A new regional order for the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council and Iran are exploring a new security framework for the Strait of Hormuz that could provide US President Trump with a diplomatic exit from the current crisis.

stories.title: Hungarian opposition leader outlines approach to Moscow
stories.summary: Péter Magyar, leader of Hungary's opposition party Tisza, stated that his future government would take a "pragmatic" approach toward Russia if elected.

stories.title: Nigeria: NAF Air Interdiction Eliminates Scores of Terrorist Fighters, Commanders in North-East
stories.summary: The Nigerian Air Force, operating under Joint Task Force North-East Operation Hadin Kai, conducted a precision air interdiction mission at Kangarwa in the Northern Tumbuns. The strike reportedly eliminated scores of terrorist fighters and commanders in the northeast.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Okays Payment of 10-Year-Old N3.3trn Debt to 15 Power Plants for Restoration of Constant Electricity Nationwide
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government approved payment of N3.3 trillion to 15 power plants to settle debts accumulated from 2015 to 2016. President Tinubu authorized the plan as part of efforts to address chronic electricity shortages nationwide.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Ramps Up Global Fight to Crush Insecurity - Information Minister
stories.summary: Nigeria's Information Minister Mohammed Idris stated that President Bola Tinubu is intensifying regional and international partnerships to combat insecurity. The effort aims to address ongoing security challenges across Nigeria.

stories.title: Japan’s Takaichi seeks urgent summit with Iran as Trump’s Hormuz deadline looms
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced that Tokyo is arranging summit-level talks with Iran as U.S. President Donald Trump's deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches. Takaichi said Japan would make every diplomatic effort amid rising Middle East tensions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Foil Kaduna Church Attack, Rescue 31 Abducted Worshippers
stories.summary: Nigerian Army troops rescued 31 worshippers who were abducted during an Easter service attack in Ariko Village, Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The military operation foiled the terrorist assault on the churches.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Kill Scores of Boko Haram Terrorists in Foiled Attack in Borno
stories.summary: Troops of the Joint Task Force North-East Operation Hadin Kai neutralized scores of Boko Haram and ISWAP terrorists in Borno State, Nigeria. The military foiled attacks on various communities in the state.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Approves N3.3trn Payment Plan to Restore Reliable Electricity
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu approved a N3.3 trillion payment plan to settle outstanding debts under the Presidential Power Sector Financial Reforms Programme. The plan aims to restore reliable electricity supply across Nigeria.

stories.title: Nigeria: Security Chiefs Condemn Ethnic Scapegoating, Demand Immediate Govt Action On Peace
stories.summary: Security experts from Beacon Security and Intelligence Limited and the Whiteink Institute for Strategy Education and Research held a two-day conference at Nigeria's National Counter Terrorism Centre in Abuja. Participants condemned ethnic scapegoating in security narratives and called for immediate government action on peace.

stories.title: Nigeria: Operation Safe Corridor Is Structured Response to Counterterrorism in Nigeria
stories.summary: The Nigerian military's high command described Operation Safe Corridor as a national security strategy forming part of a broader counterterrorism response. The program operates out of Abuja as a structured approach to addressing terrorism in Nigeria.

stories.title: Middle East war: ‘No indication that legitimate US-Iran talks taking place’
stories.summary: Reporting from Tehran, FRANCE 24's correspondent said there is no indication that legitimate negotiations are taking place between Iran and the United States. Iranians are aware of President Trump's deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but diplomatic channels appear inactive.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amnesty International Demands Probe of Military Over 14-Yr-Old Girl's Killing By Stray Bullet in Borno
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on Nigeria's federal government to investigate the alleged reckless use of firearms by military personnel in Maiduguri, Borno State. The incident reportedly resulted in the death of a 14-year-old girl struck by a stray bullet.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwandans Could Start Using Cooking Gas From Lake Kivu in 2028 - Minister
stories.summary: Rwanda's Minister of State for Infrastructure Jean de Dieu Uwihanganye announced that Rwandans may begin using methane gas extracted from Lake Kivu for cooking by early 2028. The initiative aims to provide an alternative energy source for households.

stories.title: Nigeria: Blessing CEO Goes Dark On Instagram Following Heated Medical Grill Over Cancer Claim
stories.summary: Nigerian social media influencer Blessing Okoro, known as Blessing CEO, deactivated her Instagram account after a televised encounter with a medical expert. The exchange reportedly exposed inconsistencies in her claims about having stage 4 breast cancer.

stories.title: Nigeria: Soldiers Rescue 31 Worshippers Abducted From Kaduna Church - Official
stories.summary: Nigerian troops rescued 31 worshippers who had been abducted from churches in Kaduna State during an Easter service. The attack had killed at least seven people and resulted in multiple kidnappings.

stories.title: North Korea appears to be distancing itself from Iran, South Korean lawmakers say
stories.summary: South Korean lawmakers, citing the National Intelligence Service, said North Korea appears to be distancing itself from Iran by not supplying weapons or sending public diplomatic messages since the Iran war began.

stories.title: 2 dead found in wreckage of Haifa building hit by missile; 2 more people still missing
stories.summary: Two bodies were recovered from a Haifa residential building struck by an Iranian missile, while rescue teams continued searching for two more missing people. Four people were lightly injured as the area was targeted again overnight.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bandits Kill Seven, Abduct Many in Attack On Kaduna Churches
stories.summary: Armed bandits attacked churches in Ariko Village, Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Nigeria, killing at least seven people and abducting numerous worshippers. Local councillor Mark Bawa confirmed the incident, noting that casualty figures were still being verified.

stories.title: Malawi: Bushiri Signals Possible Political Entry, Warns Critics and Dismisses Allegations
stories.summary: Prophet Shepherd Bushiri has signaled he may enter active politics in Malawi, including a possible presidential bid. He issued warnings to his critics and dismissed various allegations against him.

stories.title: World Cup 2026: Kinshasa celebrates the Leopards’ historic qualification
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's national football team, the Leopards, received a hero's welcome in Kinshasa after qualifying for the 2026 FIFA World Cup — their first World Cup appearance since 1974.

stories.title: Iranian missile attacks hit central Israel and Haifa, injuries reported
stories.summary: Iranian ballistic missiles struck central Israel and Haifa, with at least one carrying a cluster munition warhead. Four people were lightly injured in Haifa, where a car fire and an overturned vehicle were reported.

stories.title: Queues stretch past an hour as holiday traffic jams hit mega bridge
stories.summary: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge experienced peak traffic during the extended holiday period, with checkpoint queues exceeding one hour. Over 192,000 passengers and 30,000 vehicles crossed the bridge in the first two days, raising concerns about clearance capacity.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz to remain closed until Iran is compensated for war damages, Iranian official says
stories.summary: An Iranian official stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran receives compensation for war damages. The IRGC Navy said it was completing preparations for a "new order in the Persian Gulf."

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland President Names New Ministers, Reshuffles Deputies
stories.summary: Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi (Cirro) appointed new ministers and reassigned several deputy ministers in a cabinet reshuffle in Hargeisa. The presidential decree aims to strengthen government performance and coordination.

stories.title: Kenya: President Ruto Warns No Mercy for Oil Cartels As Fuel Scandal Investigation Deepens
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto vowed a crackdown on oil cartels amid deepening investigations into an alleged artificial fuel shortage. The scandal has led to arrests and resignations of top officials in Kenya's energy sector.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike on Tehran kills 4, local media reports
stories.summary: A US-Israeli strike on a residential area in eastern Tehran killed at least four people and wounded seven, according to Iran's Mehr news agency. Three residential units were destroyed and around 50 buildings were seriously damaged. A separate strike in Baharestan County killed at least 13.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s MPF set to report worst performance in 3 years in March
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Mandatory Provident Fund is expected to report a loss exceeding HK$100 billion (US$12.8 billion) for March, its worst monthly loss in 25 years. The decline was driven by falling global stock markets and uncertainty from the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Liberia: A Crisis On Liberia's Roads
stories.summary: Liberia is experiencing a growing road safety crisis, with the Liberia National Police recording 478 road traffic accidents between January and March 2026. The incidents resulted in 71 deaths and over 300 injuries nationwide.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amidst Supply Shortage, Tinubu Okays N3.3tn Electricity Debt Payment Plan
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved a payment plan to settle outstanding debts under the Presidential Power Sector Financial Reforms Programme. The plan covers approximately N3.3 trillion owed to power sector entities.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lassa Fever - Death Toll Hits 146 As Bauchi, Taraba Top Fatality Chart
stories.summary: Nigeria's Lassa fever outbreak has killed 146 people, with Bauchi and Taraba states recording the highest fatalities. Surveillance data indicates widening transmission and a deepening fatality burden across several states.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda's Food Security Rises As Hunger Declines
stories.summary: Rwanda reported improvements in food security as hunger rates declined. The country has set ambitious targets to increase agricultural productivity per hectare by 13 times by 2050.

stories.title: Rwanda: Key Things to Know About Rwanda's First Kinyarwanda ICT Dictionary
stories.summary: Rwanda has compiled over 1,700 technology-related terms into the first-ever Kinyarwanda ICT terminological dictionary. The milestone aims to strengthen use of the Kinyarwanda language in the digital era and standardize technical terminology.

stories.title: Sudan: 'Sudan War Has Pushed Women Hundreds of Years Back'
stories.summary: Hala Al-Karib, regional director of the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa, said the ongoing war in Sudan has driven women "hundreds of years backwards." She cited pervasive sexual violence and exploitation even in previously safer areas such as Khartoum and El Gezira.

stories.title: Africa: AI Is Fuelling the 'Digital Colonisation' of Africa, Warns UN Scientist
stories.summary: The United Nations launched its first global panel on artificial intelligence amid concerns that AI could deepen inequalities in Africa. A UN scientist warned that AI systems largely developed elsewhere risk fueling a form of "digital colonisation" on the continent.

stories.title: Chinese-made drone shot in Iran, Australia’s diplomacy pivot: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: A Chinese-made drone was shot down over Iran, with Tehran pointing blame at Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Separately, a Chinese lead scientist revealed the true purpose of China's ultra-large underwater drone.

stories.title: Trump appears to extend Iran deadline in cryptic post
stories.summary: President Trump appeared to extend his deadline for Iran in a cryptic social media post, with the Wall Street Journal reporting he confirmed new timing. Trump had not held public events since an April 1, 2026 address to the nation.

stories.title: Putin's trust rating drops 5% in Russia – ISW
stories.summary: According to the Institute for the Study of War, trust in Russian President Vladimir Putin has declined by five percentage points amid growing public dissatisfaction with censorship policies in Russia.

stories.title: Two Israelis dead in Haifa missile strike, two still feared trapped
stories.summary: Two bodies were recovered from the rubble of a residential building in Haifa struck by an Iranian missile. Rescue teams continued searching for two additional people believed trapped or unaccounted for.

stories.title: Beijing, Moscow push for ceasefire, Hormuz stability
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held a phone call discussing the war in Iran. Both urged a ceasefire and an objective approach, stating that ending hostilities is essential to restoring navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Axios: Iran rejects Gaza-style truce which exists on paper but US-Israel attack at will
stories.summary: Iran rejected a ceasefire arrangement modeled on those in Gaza or Lebanon, seeking stronger guarantees against resumed US-Israeli attacks, Axios reported. Negotiations are being conducted through Pakistani, Egyptian, and Turkish mediators.

stories.title: Sing, O Muse, of the Rage of Donald Trump!
stories.summary: The article draws parallels between the U.S.-Iran war and a Greek tragedy, framing the escalating conflict around President Donald Trump's actions in the Middle East.

stories.title: Warning issued after university student loses HK$190,000 in internship scam
stories.summary: Hong Kong police warned university students about internship scams after a 19-year-old first-year student lost nearly HK$190,000. English-speaking con artists used a fake 40-minute orientation session and detailed scripts to make fraudulent job offers appear legitimate.

stories.title: Orban on the brink: could Hungary’s election dent China’s influence in Europe?
stories.summary: Hungary's upcoming election is being closely watched by major powers, as polls show Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party trailing challenger Peter Magyar's Tisza Party by 19 to 23 points. An Orbán defeat could significantly affect Chinese and Russian interests in the European Union.

stories.title: US lawmakers condemn Trump's threats, warn of legal risks in Iran conflict
stories.summary: Several Democratic US senators criticized President Trump's threats against Iran, warning they could constitute war crimes. Senators Edward Markey, Chris Murphy, and Elissa Slotkin called for renewed negotiations and raised concerns about risks to US troops.

stories.title: Residential area hit in Tehran, rescue operations begin
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society deployed aid workers to a residential area in Tehran struck by a US-Israeli air attack. Rescue teams searched for survivors under rubble amid ongoing bombardment of the capital, including a reported strike near Sharif University of Technology.

stories.title: Russia’s key Baltic port resumes crude loading after attacks
stories.summary: Russia's key Baltic oil-export port at Ust-Luga resumed crude oil loadings after operations were disrupted for several days by multiple Ukrainian drone attacks in the region.

stories.title: Returned children take first steps toward reintegration in Ukraine
stories.summary: Seven Ukrainian children who were returned to Ukraine on April 3 visited the Child Rights Protection Center, where they began receiving legal assistance, material support, and psychological care as part of their reintegration process.

stories.title: South Korea’s Lee regrets drones sent to North: ‘irresponsible and reckless’
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret to Pyongyang over drones sent into North Korea in January, calling the actions "irresponsible and reckless." An investigation revealed government officials had been involved, despite initial denials of any official role.

stories.title: World Food Programme warns Iran war could trigger global food crisis
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that the war in the Middle East could trigger the worst global food crisis since the COVID-19 pandemic. Rising food and energy prices and supply chain disruptions could push an additional 45 million people into hunger.

stories.title: US-Israeli attack targets Sharif University as blasts rock Tehran
stories.summary: Iranian television reported a US-Israeli attack targeting Sharif University of Technology in western Tehran as explosions were heard across the capital. Air defenses were activated as warplanes flew overhead on the 38th day of the war.

stories.title: Nigerian army rescues 31 hostages after church attack
stories.summary: Nigeria's army rescued 31 civilians taken hostage during an attack on a church in Kaduna state in the northwest. Five people were found dead at the scene of the attack.

stories.title: Drone strikes hit Iraq’s Sulaimaniyah, explosions reported
stories.summary: Drone strikes hit Sulaimaniyah in Iraq's Kurdish region, with explosions, fire, and smoke reported across the city. Iraq is increasingly drawn into the US-Israeli war on Iran as Iraqi militia groups have launched attacks on American assets in the region.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones attacked cargo vessel that sank, killing one, Russia-installed official says
stories.summary: A cargo vessel carrying wheat sank in the Sea of Azov after a Ukrainian drone attack, killing one person and leaving two others missing, according to a Russia-installed official.

stories.title: Iran warns wider shipping lanes at risk beyond Hormuz
stories.summary: Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader, warned that shipping routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz, including the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, could be disrupted if US and Israeli attacks escalate.

stories.title: Middle East war live: More than 25 killed in new US-Israeli strikes on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli air strikes on Iran overnight into Monday killed more than 25 people, including at least six children, according to local and state media. Targets included a residential area in Tehran.

stories.title: Israel renews Lebanon strikes, forces Syria border crossing shut
stories.summary: Israel renewed strikes on Lebanon and forced the closure of the Masnaa border crossing between Lebanon and Syria, the main gateway between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel renews Lebanon strikes, forces Syria border crossing closed
stories.summary: Israel renewed air strikes in Lebanon and forced the closure of the Masnaa border crossing between Lebanon and Syria, the main gateway connecting the two countries.

stories.title: Iran hangs two convicted of links with Israel in pre-war protests: judiciary
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of having links with Israel during pre-war anti-government protests that peaked in January, according to the country's judiciary.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria agree to increase security ties as Zelensky tours Mideast
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Syrian leader Ahmad al-Sharaa in Damascus as part of a Middle East tour. Ukraine and Syria agreed to increase security ties as Kyiv seeks to share military experience amid the US-Israeli war with Iran.

stories.title: Crimean Tatar national movement veteran Asan Dzhemilev dies in Crimea
stories.summary: Asan Dzhemilev, an 88-year-old veteran of the Crimean Tatar national movement and brother of Crimean Tatar leader Mustafa Dzhemilev, died in the Russian-occupied city of Bakhchysarai in Crimea.

stories.title: Haaretz: Israel expects US-Iran talks to collapse
stories.summary: Israel believes US-Iran talks are likely to collapse without an agreement, according to Haaretz. Israeli officials reportedly have a target list including energy facilities ready if Washington expands its campaign. Prime Minister Netanyahu has signaled readiness to intensify strikes.

stories.title: Democrat calls Trump's Iran rhetoric ‘psychotic,’ warns of war crimes
stories.summary: US Representative Jim McGovern criticized President Trump's statements on Iran as "psychotic" and warned that US conduct in the war could violate international humanitarian law and the Geneva Conventions.

stories.title: Iran says 100,000 civilian sites including universities damaged in strikes
stories.summary: Iran's government spokesperson said more than 100,000 civilian sites, including dozens of universities, schools, and research facilities, have been damaged by US-Israeli air attacks since the war began on February 28.

stories.title: Trump, on Easter, threatens ‘hell’ on Iran’s infrastructure if Strait of Hormuz remains blocked
stories.summary: President Trump told Fox News on Easter that Iran is negotiating and a deal is possible, while threatening severe consequences if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked.

stories.title: Trump initially feared radio message from downed US airman was Iranian trap - Axios
stories.summary: Axios reported that President Trump initially suspected a radio message from a downed US airman over Iran was an Iranian trap. Trump said the pilot's phrase "Power be to God" "sounded like something a Muslim would say."

stories.title: Eight Israelis held after assault on Palestinian village
stories.summary: Eight Israelis were detained following an assault on a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank, where violence has escalated since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack triggered the Gaza war.

stories.title: US appeals court reinstates ruling allowing American terror victims to sue PA, PLO
stories.summary: A US appeals court reinstated a 2015 federal jury verdict awarding $656 million to American victims of terror attacks in Israel who sued the Palestinian Authority and the PLO under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

stories.title: Russian forces mine bridge over Kosheva River in Kherson
stories.summary: Russian occupation forces mined a road bridge over the Kosheva River in the Ukrainian city of Kherson, according to local reports.

stories.title: Flouting wartime restrictions, over 1,000 men gather for address by top Haredi rabbi
stories.summary: Over 1,000 men gathered in Bnei Brak for an address by a top Haredi rabbi, defying wartime restrictions. Police said they refused a permit for the event and requested its dispersal after learning it had taken place.

stories.title: A Pakistani strike killed her son in rehab. Now an Afghan mother demands answers
stories.summary: An Afghan mother, Samira Muhammadi, is demanding an international investigation after a Pakistani airstrike on March 16 struck a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, killing her son. Afghan officials said 411 people died, while a UN source verified at least 250 deaths.

stories.title: Hungary hints at Ukraine’s role in Serbia pipeline explosives find; Kyiv denies
stories.summary: Hungary suggested Ukraine may have been involved in the discovery of explosives near the TurkStream gas pipeline in Serbia. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry denied any involvement and called the incident a Russian false-flag operation aimed at interfering in Hungary's elections.

stories.title: Vietnam’s gig workers slammed by rising fuel costs amid fallout of Iran war
stories.summary: Vietnam's gig economy workers are facing sharply higher costs as diesel prices more than doubled following Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting livelihoods across the Southeast Asian nation.

stories.title: Nigeria troops rescue 31 Easter worshippers after deadly church attack
stories.summary: Nigerian troops rescued 31 worshippers abducted during Easter services at Catholic and evangelical churches in Kaduna state in northwestern Nigeria. At least five people were killed when gunmen attacked the churches, underscoring worsening insecurity in the region.

stories.title: South Korea eases Chinese travel visas but Southeast Asia rivals, Iran war cloud outlook
stories.summary: South Korea eased multiple-entry visa rules for Chinese nationals who have previously visited the country, now offering five-year visas. However, analysts say the impact on tourism may be limited due to competition from Southeast Asian destinations and higher airfares linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump draws criticism with fiery Easter message on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted an expletive-laden message on Truth Social demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to attack Iranian power plants and bridges. The post drew sharp criticism from politicians across party lines.

stories.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges over Hormuz Strait closure
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened on Sunday to bomb Iran's power plants and bridges if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping by Tuesday at 8:00 PM Eastern Time.

stories.title: Hamas armed wing says disarmament calls are unacceptable
stories.summary: Hamas's armed wing rejected calls for disarmament, characterizing such demands as an effort to continue what it described as genocide against Palestinians.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran until April 7 night to open Strait of Hormuz, report says
stories.summary: President Trump reportedly gave Iran until the night of April 7 to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, warning that Iranian power plants and bridges would be destroyed if the waterway remains closed.

stories.title: Appeals court reinstates $656M judgment against the PLO and Palestinian Authority
stories.summary: A US appeals court reinstated a $656 million judgment against the PLO and the Palestinian Authority, brought by victims who sued under the 1992 Anti-Terrorism Act, which opened US courts to victims of international terror attacks.

stories.title: Russia’s Lavrov says US should ‘abandon language of ultimatums’ on Iran
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov urged the United States to abandon ultimatums toward Iran and return to a negotiating track to help de-escalate tensions.

stories.title: A wheat cargo ship sank off the coast of Kherson, and Russian state media says a deadly drone attack is to blame
stories.summary: A cargo ship carrying wheat sank in the Sea of Azov off the coast of the Kherson region. Vladimir Saldo, the Russia-appointed head of occupied Kherson, attributed the sinking to a drone attack.

stories.title: Karachi board postpones matric exams to April 10
stories.summary: The Board of Secondary Education Karachi postponed Secondary School Certificate exams to April 10, originally scheduled to begin April 7. The delay was attributed to technical disruptions during the board's transition from a manual to a digital system.

stories.title: Belarus covers budget shortfalls with Russian funds – intelligence
stories.summary: Intelligence reports indicate that Belarus is covering budget shortfalls caused by declining tax revenues with non-tax income, primarily financial transfers from Russia.

stories.title: Putin orders transfer of 2 medieval icons from Tretyakov Gallery to Russian Orthodox Church, patriarch says
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the transfer of the Vladimir and Donskaya icons of the Mother of God from Moscow's Tretyakov Gallery to the Russian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Kirill announced at the Cathedral of Christ the Savior.

stories.title: Trump invokes religious rhetoric in praise of Iran rescue, drawing criticism
stories.summary: President Trump's use of religious rhetoric in praising the rescue of a downed US airman in the Iran conflict drew criticism, with some accusing him of betraying Christian values and escalating the war.

stories.title: Lebanon’s Christians mark Easter by praying for southern villages hit by war
stories.summary: Lebanese Christians marked Easter with prayers for southern villages affected by war. Worshipers in Beirut struggled to be heard over Israeli fighter jets flying low over the city during services.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran rejects Trump’s Hormuz deadline; 2 killed in Haifa
stories.summary: Iranian officials rejected President Trump's ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, condemning the latest US threats as incitement to war crimes. Meanwhile, two people were reported killed in Haifa.

stories.title: Petronas-chartered tanker loaded with Iraqi crude passes through Hormuz
stories.summary: A Petronas-chartered tanker loaded with Iraqi crude oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz. It was among seven Malaysia-linked vessels cleared by Iran to transit the waterway.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky meets Syria’s new leader in Damascus, pushes military deals
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Syria's new leader Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Sunday, accompanied by Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan. The visit aimed to deepen security cooperation and military deals as Kyiv seeks broader regional partnerships amid its war with Russia.

stories.title: At least 2 injured, including 1 seriously, in latest cluster missile attack on central Israel
stories.summary: At least two people were injured, including one seriously, in a cluster missile attack on central Israel launched by Iran. Mediated talks between Washington and Tehran on a potential 45-day truce were reportedly underway but chances for a deal remained slim.

stories.title: Ganga water sharing, visas, energy cooperation likely on agenda for Bangladesh FM visit
stories.summary: Bangladesh's foreign minister is expected to visit India on April 7–8, marking the first such visit since the fall of the Hasina government. Agenda items likely include Ganga water-sharing treaty renewal, visa issues, and energy cooperation, with the newly elected BNP signaling willingness to negotiate.

stories.title: General Staff reports 108 frontline clashes
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported 108 combat clashes along the frontline with Russian forces on April 5. The Pokrovsk sector saw the heaviest activity, with 24 Russian attacks recorded there.

stories.title: Israeli hit in Palestinian territory kills 4: Gaza civil defence agency
stories.summary: An Israeli military strike in Palestinian territory killed four people, according to Gaza's civil defence agency. Israel's military stated it had targeted a terrorist cell operating near its troops that posed an immediate threat.

stories.title: Trump hails victory after US mission to rescue pilot from Iran
stories.summary: U.S. commandos conducted a mission deep into Iranian territory to rescue a downed American pilot, according to U.S. news outlets. President Donald Trump announced the crew member had been recovered safely, hailing the operation as a success.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Israel says residential building hit by Iranian missile
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 reported on an Iranian missile strike that hit a residential building in Israel. Correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky described the situation of Israeli civilians in the north who are unable to evacuate from the conflict zone.

stories.title: 3-year-old girl raped, murdered in KP’s Lakki Marwat: FIR
stories.summary: Police in Lakki Marwat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, registered an FIR against unidentified suspects for the rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in the Langerkhel Hathi Khan area. The child went missing on April 3, and charges include intentional murder, kidnapping, and rape under the Pakistan Penal Code.

stories.title: Ukraine, Syria agree to reopen embassies in Kyiv and Damascus
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani agreed to reopen their respective embassies in Kyiv and Damascus following bilateral talks.

stories.title: At least 11 killed in Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon on Easter Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon on Easter Sunday killed at least 11 people. Lebanon's health ministry reported that 1,461 people had been killed in Israeli attacks in Lebanon as of April 5.

stories.title: DR Congo is latest African nation to receive third-country deportees from US under deal
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo became the latest African nation to agree to receive migrants deported from the United States under the Trump administration's third-country deportation programme. Arrivals are expected to begin this month.

stories.title: Against the odds, Tel Aviv Museum of Art makes world’s top 100 for visits
stories.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art ranked 77th globally for visitor numbers in 2025, despite frequent closures due to the ongoing security situation in Israel.

stories.title: Iran attacks energy infrastructure across UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait
stories.summary: Iranian drones struck oil, petrochemical, and power infrastructure across the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait. Two Kuwaiti power and water desalination plants sustained significant damage, and a fire broke out at a petrochemical plant in the UAE.

stories.title: Zelenskiy in Syria to discuss security cooperation with Sharaa
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Sunday to discuss security cooperation. Kyiv is seeking to promote its military expertise in the region following the outbreak of the Iran war.

stories.title: High Court issues conditional order in petition over Saturday night protests
stories.summary: Israel's High Court issued a conditional order in a petition concerning Saturday night anti-war protests, signaling it is now examining whether the state has a broader policy governing demonstrations under wartime conditions.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with total destruction
stories.summary: President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran, warning of total destruction if Tehran does not accept a deal, and declined to rule out targeting civilian infrastructure in an ABC interview.

stories.title: After Likud backlash, Netanyahu U-turns, says his embattled aide to be replaced
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reversed his initial decision to retain chief of staff Ziv Agmon after leaked racist comments by Agmon against Mizrahi Jews prompted backlash within the Likud party.

stories.title: Iran internet blackout is longest nationwide shutdown on record: NetBlocks
stories.summary: Internet monitoring group NetBlocks reported that Iran's nationwide internet blackout has entered its 37th consecutive day, making it the longest such shutdown on record.

stories.title: Zelensky holds trilateral talks in Damascus with Syria and Türkiye
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held trilateral talks in Damascus with representatives from Syria and Türkiye during his visit to the Syrian capital.

stories.title: Israel renews strikes on Lebanon, killing at least 11
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon on Easter Sunday killed at least 11 people. Seven died in a strike on the southern village of Kfarhata, and four were killed in Beirut's Jnah neighborhood. Hezbollah claimed it fired a cruise missile at an Israeli warship, though Israel said it was unaware of such an incident.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 11 in Lebanon on Easter Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least 11 people across Lebanon on Easter Sunday, including seven in the southern village of Kfarhata and four in Beirut's Jnah neighbourhood. Lebanon's health ministry reported a four-year-old child among the dead and 39 others injured.

stories.title: High Court raises wartime limit on Western Wall, Temple Mount access from 50 to 100
stories.summary: Israel's High Court increased the wartime visitor limit at the Western Wall and Temple Mount from 50 to 100 people, citing a balance between security concerns and the right to freedom of religion and worship.

stories.title: Nigeria's army rescues 31 hostages after church attack
stories.summary: Nigeria's army rescued 31 hostages following an attack on a church during Easter celebrations in Kaduna state in the country's northwest, a region that has experienced prolonged violence.

stories.title: Fuel tanker erupts in flames after toppling power lines in Texas
stories.summary: An 18-wheel fuel tanker carrying 9,000 gallons of gasoline crashed into another vehicle outside Fort Worth, Texas, toppling power lines and erupting in flames. The driver was treated for burns.

stories.title: Met Office forecasts widespread rain, thunderstorms in parts of Balochistan, KP, Punjab on Monday
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast widespread rain, thunderstorms, and possible hailstorms across northeast Balochistan, lower Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and south Punjab for Monday, April 6. Partly cloudy weather with isolated storms was also expected in Sindh, central Punjab, and other regions.

stories.title: Hamas armed wing says disarmament calls are unacceptable
stories.summary: Hamas's armed wing issued a statement rejecting calls to disarm, insisting that Israel must first fully implement the first phase of the ceasefire agreement and withdraw from Palestinian territory.

stories.title: Attack on Nigeria church leaves five dead, army rescues 31 civilians taken hostage
stories.summary: An attack on a church during an Easter service in Ariko village, Kachia local government area of Nigeria, killed at least five people. The Nigerian army rescued 31 civilians who had been taken hostage and said troops were pursuing the attackers.

stories.title: Plan in place to strike strategic Iran sites if deal not reached, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli officials have agreed on a target list of strategic sites in Iran to strike if diplomatic efforts fail, according to sources cited by the Jerusalem Post. The plan followed intensive high-level discussions to coordinate the two countries' responses.

stories.title: Israel says nearly 7,000 injured since war with Iran began
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported that 6,951 people have been wounded since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February. Of those, 123 patients remain hospitalized, with two in critical condition.

stories.title: German men must inform military of extended foreign trips
stories.summary: Germany's Defence Ministry announced that men aged 17 and older must obtain prior approval from the German armed forces before taking foreign trips lasting longer than three months.

stories.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran’s infrastructure on Tuesday if Strait of Hormuz remains blocked
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iran's infrastructure on Tuesday if the Strait of Hormuz remained blocked, stating he was considering "blowing everything up and taking over the oil."

stories.title: How China fell for a lobster: What an AI assistant tells us about Beijing's ambition
stories.summary: A Chinese AI assistant sparked a viral trend of virtual "lobster raising" in March, with millions of users training the tool to suit their preferences. The phenomenon illustrates Beijing's broader ambitions in consumer-facing artificial intelligence.

stories.title: ‘This is all embarrassing and juvenile’: Trump draws criticism for fiery, expletive-laden message on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden Easter Sunday message threatening Iran, warning of heavy bombing of power plants and bridges if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The post drew bipartisan criticism on Capitol Hill.

stories.title: Los Angeles arrest shines light on lavish life of slain IRGC general Soleimani’s niece
stories.summary: Hamideh Soleimani Afshar, a niece of slain IRGC General Qassem Soleimani, was arrested in Los Angeles. She had published pro-Tehran content while living a lavish Western lifestyle in the United States.

stories.title: You can hire house help in 15 minutes in India - is it fair?
stories.summary: Apps in India now allow users to hire domestic help within 15 minutes, bringing speed and structure to household services. However, workers using these platforms face tighter employer control and increasing job pressure.

stories.title: Andrew Tilton on China’s growth prospects, economic trajectory in wake of Iran war
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs chief Asia-Pacific economist Andrew Tilton discussed China's economic outlook and the impact of the oil crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran on Asian economies.

stories.title: Behind the US Air Force unit that spearheaded the mission to rescue downed airman
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force pararescue unit that led the mission to recover a downed American airman traces its origins to the end of World War II. The pararescueman qualification process is considered one of the most demanding in the U.S. military.

stories.title: ‘Choose peace’: Pope Leo XIV marks first Easter under cloud of war in West Asia
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV marked his first Easter, paying tribute to his predecessor Pope Francis, who made his last public appearance on Easter Sunday the previous year, hours before his death. The pontiff called for peace amid the ongoing war in West Asia.

stories.title: Appeal court reinstates US$656 million judgment against the PLO and Palestinian Authority
stories.summary: A U.S. appeals court reinstated a $656 million judgment against the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Palestinian Authority over attacks that killed or wounded Americans in Israel, following a U.S. Supreme Court ruling.

stories.title: US was arming Iranian dissidents through Kurds while negotiating with Tehran, Trump reveals
stories.summary: Donald Trump revealed on Easter Sunday that the United States had covertly supplied weapons to Iranian dissidents through Kurdish intermediaries, even while American negotiators were engaged in diplomatic talks with senior Iranian officials in Europe.

stories.title: Sources: IDF does not actually know how many ballistic missiles Iran has left
stories.summary: Israeli military intelligence reportedly does not have a confirmed count of how many ballistic missiles Iran retains. A key uncertainty is how many missiles buried under rubble from strikes can be salvaged and returned to operational status.

stories.title: Ukraine denies involvement in explosives incident near gas pipeline in Serbia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry denied any involvement in the discovery of explosives near the TurkStream gas pipeline in Serbia. Spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi stated that Kyiv has no connection to the incident.

stories.title: Explosives found near Serbian pipeline that carries Russian gas, say leaders
stories.summary: Explosives were discovered near a pipeline in Serbia that carries Russian gas. Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjártó did not directly accuse Ukraine of involvement but did not rule it out.

stories.title: Trump to Israeli TV: We were afraid downed US airman had been captured
stories.summary: President Trump told Israeli TV that U.S. officials feared a downed American airman had been captured in Iran after an unusual message raised concerns of an ambush. Israel assisted with the extraction, and the U.S. destroyed two C-130 aircraft stuck in sand.

stories.title: 'We are at the edge of a battlefield': BBC reports near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: BBC correspondent Orla Guerin reported from near the Strait of Hormuz, describing the area as being on the edge of a battlefield as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the critical waterway.

stories.title: Global South nations are insulating themselves from the heat of US actions
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Global South nations are increasingly insulating themselves from the consequences of U.S.-led actions, including the US-Israeli strikes on Iran, as developing countries seek to reduce their exposure to geopolitical and economic shocks.

stories.title: Iran says Trump threats amount to incitement for war crimes
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei condemned Donald Trump's threats against Iran, stating they reflect a criminal mindset and constitute incitement for war crimes and crimes against humanity, particularly regarding threats to attack critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Lebanon's Christians mark Easter in solidarity with war-hit south
stories.summary: Lebanese Christians marked Easter with prayers dedicated to southern Lebanon, where Israeli military operations have continued to displace residents and cause widespread destruction.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Kharkiv region leave three people injured
stories.summary: Three people were injured in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine as a result of Russian strikes throughout the day.

stories.title: How rescue of US airman in remote part of Iran unfolded
stories.summary: A complex, multi-agency U.S. operation successfully extracted a downed American airman from a remote area inside Iranian territory.

stories.title: IDF intelligence, strikes helped US rescue downed pilot, sources told the 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli military intelligence and strike operations assisted the U.S. in rescuing a downed American pilot, sources told the Jerusalem Post. IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and U.S. Central Command Commander Admiral Brad Cooper maintained direct contact throughout the 48-hour operation.

stories.title: Trump issues expletive-laden threat  to Iran over Hormuz Strait blockage
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iranian power plants and bridges if Iran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping waterway.

stories.title: Trump’s Hormuz ultimatum: the familiar dilemma between bluster or prelude to action - analysis
stories.summary: Analysts are debating whether President Trump's ultimatum regarding the Strait of Hormuz represents a genuine prelude to military action or familiar rhetorical bluster, as his latest deadline was set to expire Monday night.

stories.title: Zhytomyr RMA reports on condition of victims and restoration of housing after enemy strike on April 3
stories.summary: In Korosten, Zhytomyr region, eight people remain hospitalized in moderate condition following a Russian strike on April 3. Three additional victims are receiving outpatient treatment, and housing restoration efforts are underway.

stories.title: Western Wall priestly blessing limited to 50 as High Court permits larger anti-war protests
stories.summary: Israel's High Court permitted larger anti-war protests on Saturday nights while attendance at the Western Wall priestly blessing was restricted to 50 people, sparking controversy over the contrasting restrictions.

stories.title: Oxford University library marks bicentenary of sacred Hindu text Shikshapatri with U.K. tour
stories.summary: Oxford University's Bodleian Library is marking the bicentenary of the Shikshapatri, a sacred Hindu text composed in 1826 at Vadtal in Gujarat by Sahajananda Swami, with a tour across the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Balochistan, KP set closure timings for markets, eateries, wedding halls to conserve energy
stories.summary: The governments of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan announced energy conservation measures requiring markets and shopping centers to close by 8pm. Wedding halls, restaurants, and hotels must end operations by 10pm, with exemptions for pharmacies, tandoors, and bakeries.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria to cooperate on security, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited Damascus and announced that Ukraine and Syria have agreed to cooperate on security matters.

stories.title: Unifil warns Israel-Hezbollah attacks near positions risk escalation
stories.summary: The United Nations peacekeeping force in Lebanon, UNIFIL, warned that attacks by both Israel and Hezbollah near its positions risk triggering further escalation. UNIFIL urged all parties to de-escalate and pursue a ceasefire.

stories.title: Israeli rescuers search for the missing after Iran attack
stories.summary: Israeli rescue teams searched for people missing after an Iranian missile struck a seven-story residential building, injuring four, as the joint U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran continues.

stories.title: Border guards destroy three MLRS and rare 'Zoopark' radar in Zaporizhzhia sector
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported that its "Phoenix" drone unit destroyed three enemy multiple launch rocket systems and a rare Russian "Zoopark" counter-battery radar system in the Zaporizhzhia sector in a single night of operations.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Monday
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity supply restrictions were planned for Monday, April 6.

stories.title: Has the humanitarian crisis in Gaza been ignored?
stories.summary: Humanitarian conditions in Gaza continue to deteriorate as the conflict involving the United States and Israel against Iran intensifies, raising concerns about the crisis being overlooked.

stories.title: US media says commandos went deep into Iran to rescue downed airman
stories.summary: U.S. media reported that American special operations commandos conducted a deep penetration mission into Iran to rescue a downed airman. U.S. attack aircraft reportedly bombed and fired on Iranian convoys to keep them at a distance during the operation.

stories.title: Hamas armed wing says disarmament demands not acceptable
stories.summary: Abu Obeida, spokesperson for Hamas's armed wing, stated that demands for the group's disarmament are unacceptable, characterizing such calls as an attempt to perpetuate what he described as Israel's genocide.

stories.title: Israeli air strike hits crowd in Gaza City
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike struck a crowd in Gaza City, sending several Palestinians to hospital with severe injuries.

stories.title: US was arming Iranian dissidents through Kurds while negotiating with Tehran, Trump reveals
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump revealed that the United States had been arming Iranian dissident groups through Kurdish intermediaries while simultaneously negotiating with Tehran, weeks before the war began. Trump claimed the Kurds kept the weapons rather than distributing them.

stories.title: Hamas armed wing rejects disarmament while Israel continues attacks
stories.summary: Hamas's armed wing, the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, declared it will not discuss disarmament until Israel fully implements the first phase of the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Analysis: Trump declares victory in Iran war after rescue, but threats to US operation still loom
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that the successful rescue of a U.S. airman in Iran could influence President Trump's decision-making regarding potential ground operations targeting Kharg Island or Iranian uranium enrichment sites.

stories.title: Zelensky in Syria to discuss security cooperation with President Ahmed al-Sharaa
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus to discuss enhanced security cooperation and food security, as part of Zelensky's broader Middle East tour promoting Ukrainian military and agricultural expertise.

stories.title: Explosives discovered near pipeline in Serbia that carries Russian gas to Hungary
stories.summary: Powerful explosives were discovered near the Balkan Stream pipeline in Serbia, which transports Russian natural gas to Hungary. The discovery prompted political scrutiny in Hungary ahead of a national election.

stories.title: Russian troops shell Nikopol since morning, damaging homes and kindergarten
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the city of Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk Oblast starting in the morning, causing damage to residential buildings and a kindergarten. No casualty figures were immediately provided.

stories.title: Is war more profitable than peace? David Keen explains
stories.summary: Political economist David Keen discussed how armed conflict can generate financial profits and serve the political survival interests of those in power, questioning whether war can be more profitable than peace.

stories.title: Lost mosaic shows first visual depiction of women fighting beasts in Roman arenas - study
stories.summary: A study identified a Roman mosaic, recovered in 1860s Reims, France, and dated to the third century CE, as containing the first known visual depiction of women fighting beasts in Roman arenas. The mosaic features approximately 35 gladiatorial and hunting scenes.

stories.title: Jewish settlers burn farms, buildings in West Bank as retaliation for Palestinian stone attack
stories.summary: Jewish settlers set fire to farms and buildings in the occupied West Bank in retaliation after a settler was struck by stones. The settler had reportedly entered Palestinian private property while traveling between the outposts of Esh Kodesh and Ahiya.

stories.title: 4 injured, 4 feared trapped under rubble in Iranian missile strike on Haifa building
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck a seven-story residential building in Haifa, Israel, injuring four people, with four others feared trapped under the rubble. Separately, a Hezbollah rocket hit Deir al-Asad, lightly injuring six people.

stories.title: Iran allows Iraqi vessels to use Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian military officials announced that Iraqi vessels are exempt from navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. The decision allows Iraqi ships to transit the waterway freely.

stories.title: Dozens missing after boat carrying migrants capsizes near Libya
stories.summary: Dozens of migrants are missing and at least two have been confirmed dead after their boat capsized off the coast of Libya.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones attacked cargo ship that sank, killing 1, Russian official says
stories.summary: A cargo ship named Volgo-Balt carrying wheat sank in the Sea of Azov after a Ukrainian drone attack on Friday, killing one crew member and leaving two missing. Vladimir Saldo, Russia's installed leader of occupied parts of Kherson region, reported the crew was unable to communicate until Sunday.

stories.title: Operation Ghazab lil-Haq: Security forces foil attack on border post in KP, kill 37 militants
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 37 militants who attempted to attack a border post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Ghulam Khan Sector on the night of April 2-3 during Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the attackers included Afghan Taliban fighters, and more than 80 were injured.

stories.title: Hamas claims disarmament request a 'way for Israel to continue genocide against Palestinians'
stories.summary: Hamas rejected calls for disarmament, characterizing the demand as a means for Israel to continue what it described as genocide against the Palestinian people. Hamas accused Israel of seeking peace through force while spreading destruction across the region.

stories.title: El Al nixes regular flights through mid-April; United cancels Tel Aviv route until Sept 7
stories.summary: Israel's El Al airline canceled regular flights through mid-April, while United Airlines suspended its Tel Aviv route until September 7. A slight increase in the number of passengers allowed on departing flights was reported, now up to 100 per flight.

stories.title: Arab parties clash over delayed Joint List agreement, but deny breakdown in talks
stories.summary: Israeli Arab parties Hadash and Ra'am clashed over delays in reaching a Joint List agreement for a joint electoral run. Hadash officials accused Ra'am of stalling, though both sides said negotiations were continuing despite little visible progress over two months.

stories.title: Iran military says US airman rescue operation ‘completely foiled’
stories.summary: Iran's military claimed that a U.S. operation to rescue a downed American airman was "completely foiled." Iranian state media published images of charred wreckage scattered across a desert area as evidence.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria agree to share military experience as Zelenskyy makes first Damascus visit
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first visit to Damascus, where Ukraine and Syria signed agreements on sharing military and security experience and food supply. The deal marks a significant shift for Syria, which previously endorsed Russia's occupation of Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Former UK ambassador to Ukraine responds to Russia over damaged church in Tehran
stories.summary: Former UK Ambassador to Ukraine Melinda Simmons, now serving as Ambassador to Poland, accused Moscow of hypocrisy after Russia's Foreign Ministry expressed outrage over a church damaged during hostilities in Tehran.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran in expletive-filled social media post
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted a vulgar threat against Iran's leadership on social media as his deadline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz approached.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian strike of bus stop in Kherson rises to six
stories.summary: The number of people injured by a Russian strike on a public transport stop in Kherson's Korabelnyi district on April 4 rose to six. An additional local resident sought medical treatment for a concussion and blast injury.

stories.title: Starmer attacks Greens, saying vote for Labour rivals puts new workers’ rights at risk
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer attacked the Green Party, warning that voting for Labour's rivals could jeopardize new workers' rights on sick pay, parental leave, and zero-hours contracts taking effect on Monday. He described the measures as the biggest strengthening of workers' rights in a generation.

stories.title: UK police arrest protesters near base used by US
stories.summary: UK police arrested seven people near Royal Air Force Lakenheath, a base used by the U.S. military, on suspicion of supporting the banned group Palestine Action. The individuals had gathered to protest the base's use.

stories.title: Orban appears to blame Kyiv for Serbian gas pipeline explosives find
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán appeared to suggest Ukraine was involved in a sabotage plot after Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić reported that explosives were found on the Balkan Stream gas pipeline near the village of Velebit on the Hungarian border. The pipeline transports Russian natural gas from Turkey via Bulgaria to Serbia and Hungary.

stories.title: Several PTI supporters detained as police scuttle protest near Karachi Press Club
stories.summary: Police in Karachi detained between 15 and 20 PTI supporters near Karachi Press Club during a protest against rising fuel prices. South SSP Mahzor Ali said demonstrators pelted stones at officers, who responded with shelling and baton charges.

stories.title: TurkStream pipeline explosives in Serbia are “most probably” a Russian false-flag operation aimed at Hungary’s election, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Explosives were discovered near the TurkStream gas pipeline in Serbia one week before Hungary's April 12 elections. Ukraine's government suggested the incident was most likely a Russian false-flag operation targeting Hungary's vote, noting that Hungarian opposition leaders had publicly predicted such an operation.

stories.title: US rescues airman as Trump, Israel pressure Iran ahead of deadline
stories.summary: US forces rescued a downed American airman during the ongoing war in Iran. The rescue was described as a positive development amid a conflict that has killed thousands.

stories.title: Ukraine and Syria agree to cooperate for security and societal development – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa agreed to cooperate on security and societal development for both countries.

stories.title: Trump issues foul-mouthed threat to Iran after US airman rescued
stories.summary: President Trump issued new threats against Iran after a U.S. airman was rescued, setting a Tuesday 8:00 PM deadline for Iran to comply with his demands. The ultimatum drew international criticism.

stories.title: Israel continues deadly attacks on Gaza while striking Iran, Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel continued its military operations in Gaza on Sunday, killing at least four Palestinians, while also carrying out strikes against targets in Iran and Lebanon.

stories.title: ‘I will take up arms’: US-Israeli war in Iran prompts a surge of nationalism among Iranians
stories.summary: The US-Israeli military campaign in Iran has prompted a surge of nationalism among Iranian citizens. Iranians reportedly blame US and Israeli battlefield missteps for shifting public attitudes toward support of the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Frustration grows as Iran’s wartime internet shutdown breaks grim record
stories.summary: Iran has maintained a near-total internet shutdown since January, severely disrupting jobs and businesses across the country in what has become a record-breaking wartime blackout.

stories.title: Bangladesh says suspected measles outbreak kills about 100 children
stories.summary: Bangladesh reported that a suspected measles outbreak has killed at least 98 children over three weeks, with 6,476 children showing suspected symptoms. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman dispatched senior ministers to assess the crisis, and authorities have intensified vaccination campaigns in the worst-affected areas.

stories.title: Video captures Iranian missile striking residential building in Haifa
stories.summary: Video footage captured an Iranian ballistic missile directly striking a residential building in the city of Haifa, Israel.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz urges provinces to release funds for fuel subsidies
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif urged Pakistan's provinces to release funds for targeted fuel subsidies benefiting motorcyclists and public and goods transport operators. The federal government ended blanket fuel subsidies in favor of targeted relief. Provinces are collectively pooling approximately Rs200 billion over three months based on their NFC shares.

stories.title: Rodent infestations and attacks spread in Gaza tent camps
stories.summary: Rat infestations are spreading through displacement camps across Gaza, posing additional health risks to populations already affected by the ongoing conflict, according to Al Jazeera reporting from the ground.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran to reopen strait of Hormuz by Tuesday or face ‘hell’
stories.summary: President Trump set a Tuesday night deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to destroy Iranian power plants and bridges in an expletive-laden social media post. Iran's parliament speaker responded that the U.S. president's actions could engulf the entire region in conflict.

stories.title: On Easter, Pope Leo urges world leaders to end wars, renounce conquest
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV used his Easter message to urge world leaders to end wars and renounce conquest. The pontiff has become an outspoken critic of the ongoing war in Iran.

stories.title: Explosives found in Serbia near gas pipeline supplying Hungary, leaders say
stories.summary: Explosives described as having "devastating power" were discovered near the TurkStream natural gas pipeline in Serbia, which carries Russian gas to Hungary and other European countries. Serbian and Hungarian leaders announced the discovery on Sunday.

stories.title: War update: 41 combat clashes since morning, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors remain most active
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 41 attacks on Ukrainian defense positions since the start of the day. The most intense combat was recorded in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors of the front line.

stories.title: Lebanon: At least 11 killed in Israeli strikes on Easter Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Easter Sunday killed at least 11 people in southern Lebanon and Beirut, continuing Israel's military operations in the country.

stories.title: ‘Refuse to celebrate’: Christians in Gaza mark sombre Easter amid genocide
stories.summary: Christians in Gaza marked Easter with quiet prayer gatherings amid the ongoing military campaign, expressing hope for survival and peace rather than celebration.

stories.title: If peaceful Gaza protest is criminal, what’s left of UK freedom?
stories.summary: UK civil society leaders Ben Jamal and Chris Nineham were convicted over peaceful protests related to the Gaza conflict. The case has raised concerns about the state of protest rights and civil liberties in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Jet-powered Shahed drone strikes near apartment block in Kharkiv, injuries reported
stories.summary: A jet-powered Shahed drone struck the Shevchenkivskyi district of Kharkiv on April 5, landing near an apartment block. Injuries were reported in the attack.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes, shelling across Lebanon add to rising death toll
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes and shelling hit multiple locations across Lebanon on Sunday, targeting areas from Beirut to Tyre and contributing to a rising death toll.

stories.title: Iran’s internet blackout longest nationwide shutdown on record
stories.summary: Iran's nationwide internet blackout has entered its 37th day, making it the longest such shutdown on record. Residents have resorted to risky illegal workarounds to access connectivity amid ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Israel launches new strikes on Lebanon, forces closure of Syria border crossing
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes on Beirut and southern Lebanon on Sunday killed at least 11 people, including a family of six, and wounded dozens more. The strikes also forced the closure of Lebanon's main border crossing with Syria as Israel's conflict with Hezbollah intensifies.

stories.title: Serbia, Hungary say explosives found at Russian gas pipeline
stories.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić announced that detonators and explosives were found near the Balkan Stream pipeline, which carries Russian gas through Serbia to Hungary. Both Serbia and Hungary confirmed the discovery.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkiye to sign MoU on judicial cooperation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court is hosting a delegation from Turkiye's Constitutional Court from April 6 to 9, led by its president Kadir Özkaya. The two courts plan to sign a memorandum of understanding on judicial cooperation during the visit in Islamabad.

stories.title: Israel's 'war on children' continues in Gaza despite 'ceasefire'
stories.summary: The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics released data on Palestinian Child Day highlighting the impact of the conflict on children in Gaza, despite a ceasefire reportedly being in place.

stories.title: OPEC+ debates theoretical oil output hike amid Iran war paralysis, sources say
stories.summary: OPEC+ members are debating a theoretical increase in oil output amid disruptions caused by the war in Iran. Sources within the group indicated any agreed increase would have little immediate impact on supply.

stories.title: El Al cancels all scheduled flights till April 18 due to war in Middle East
stories.summary: El Al Airlines cancelled all scheduled flights through April 18 due to the ongoing Middle East war. The decision followed a government move to ease flight restrictions, with additional departures available under an emergency schedule.

stories.title: Trump draws criticism with fiery, expletive-laden Easter message attacking Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden Easter message threatening to bomb Iranian power plants and bridges if Tehran refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The post drew criticism from Capitol Hill and beyond.

stories.title: Ukrainian president arrives in Damascus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in the Syrian capital, Damascus, for a series of meetings with Syrian officials.

stories.title: Search for journalist Shelly Kittleson in Iraq enters sixth day
stories.summary: The search for journalist Shelly Kittleson, missing in Iraq, entered its sixth day. Iraqi authorities said the search continues but provided no official update on the circumstances of her kidnapping.

stories.title: Enemy leaflets spread fear in Nikopol as authorities warn of psychological operation
stories.summary: Russian leaflets containing threats of an offensive appeared in Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk region. Ukrainian authorities warned residents that the leaflets were part of a Russian psychological operation aimed at spreading fear.

stories.title: IDF strike kills Head of Commerce at Iranian regime's oil headquarters
stories.summary: An Israeli military strike killed the head of commerce at the Iranian regime's oil headquarters. The IRGC's Oil Headquarters reportedly generates billions of dollars annually for the Iranian regime through oil sales.

stories.title: Sources say Israel's defense establishment at odds, note force can't solve all war aims - analysis
stories.summary: Sources indicate growing disagreement within Israel's defense establishment over the Iran war. While government policy and most senior serving officials support the conflict, a rising number of current and former defense leaders strongly dissent.

stories.title: OPEC+ agrees to hike oil output, warns of slow recovery after attacks
stories.summary: OPEC+ agreed to increase oil output, though the move is largely symbolic as some key member states are unable to raise production due to the ongoing U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Syria's Sharaa in Damascus following Turkey visit
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Syrian leader Ahmad al-Sharaa in Damascus following a visit to Turkey. Zelensky said they discussed the circumstances of Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Chance of alien life ‘goes to heart’ of space missions, Nasa chief says
stories.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that investigating the possibility of alien life is central to the agency's mission planning. He made the remarks four days after the Artemis II rocket launched, saying the odds of finding evidence of extraterrestrial life are relatively high.

stories.title: Civilian car hits Russian mine in Kherson, one injured
stories.summary: A civilian car struck a Russian-laid mine in Kherson on the morning of April 5, injuring one man.

stories.title: Sindh CM secures fare freeze after talks with transporters amid fuel price hike
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah announced a province-wide transport fare freeze following negotiations with inter-city and intra-city transporters. The measure responds to rising petroleum prices linked to a global oil crisis. Sindh and Punjab have also introduced subsidies for motorcyclists, transporters, and small-scale farmers.

stories.title: Hungarian PM faces ‘false flag’ claims after Serbia says explosives found near pipeline
stories.summary: Serbia reported finding explosives near the TurkStream pipeline extension close to the Hungarian border, prompting Hungary's leading opposition candidate to allege a possible false flag operation ahead of elections. Prime Minister Viktor Orbán said he was informed of the discovery by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić.

stories.title: Easter in Jerusalem disrupted by war and restrictions at key Church of the Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Easter celebrations in Jerusalem were disrupted by the ongoing conflict, with police at checkpoints restricting access near the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. Only a small number of worshippers were allowed to approach the site.

stories.title: Israeli strikes rain down on Lebanon as country celebrates Easter
stories.summary: Lebanon experienced some of its heaviest Israeli strikes since March on Easter Sunday. Airstrikes hit multiple areas across the country, including Beirut, as Lebanese Maronite Christians held Easter services.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills four Palestinians in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed four Palestinians in the northern Gaza Strip on Sunday, according to local health authorities in Cairo. The violence came amid a fragile ceasefire and renewed mediation efforts to strengthen the agreement.

stories.title: Who is Viktor Orban, Hungarian PM fighting to stay in power after 16 years?
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is fighting to retain power after 16 years in office. Since 2010, he has reshaped Hungary's political system into what the European Parliament has described as a hybrid regime of electoral autocracy.

stories.title: ‘Unhinged madman’: US politicians react to Trump’s expletive-laden threat to Iran
stories.summary: U.S. politicians including Marjorie Taylor Greene and Bernie Sanders reacted with alarm to President Trump's expletive-laden social media threat to Iran demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump warned of attacks on Iranian power plants and infrastructure, prompting questions about his mental state.

stories.title: Iran strikes hit energy infrastructure across Gulf states
stories.summary: Iran launched strikes targeting energy infrastructure across Gulf states, accusing neighboring countries of permitting US military forces to operate from their territories.

stories.title: Trump threatens 'hell' for Iran over Strait Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iranian power plants and bridges if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened by Tuesday, promising "hell" for Iran.

stories.title: Iranian drone strikes hit Kuwait’s oil infrastructure before Opec+ supply talks
stories.summary: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's oil infrastructure on Sunday, causing severe material damage and threatening further disruption to global oil supplies. The attack came hours before an OPEC+ meeting where members reportedly agreed to increase output by 206,000 barrels per day in May, though the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed.

stories.title: Lviv officials deny claims of mass absenteeism among IDP children due to bullying
stories.summary: Lviv regional officials denied claims that internally displaced children in the area were missing school due to bullying or insufficient Ukrainian language skills.

stories.title: Levin says government should ignore High Court ruling allowing wartime protests
stories.summary: Israeli Justice Minister Yariv Levin urged the government to ignore a High Court ruling permitting wartime protests, calling the court's intervention illegal and claiming it could harm public discipline during the conflict.

stories.title: WATCH: Ten wounded in northern Israel after Iranian missiles damage car, hit building
stories.summary: Ten people were wounded in northern Israel after Iranian missiles struck the area, damaging a car and hitting a building. Medical responders said the injuries resulted from the shockwave rather than shrapnel or broken glass.

stories.title: How tech enabled the overnight rescue of a downed US airman in Iran- analysis
stories.summary: US forces rescued a downed American airman in Iran under the cover of substantial air support while facing fire from nearby Iranian troops. An analysis examined the technology that enabled the overnight operation.

stories.title: Iran internet blackout is longest nationwide shutdown on record: Global watchdog
stories.summary: Iran's nationwide internet blackout has entered its 37th consecutive day, making it the longest such shutdown on record according to a global monitoring organization.

stories.title: Hungary alleges plot to blow up gas pipeline ahead of election
stories.summary: Hungarian authorities reported an alleged plot to sabotage a gas pipeline ahead of national elections scheduled the following week. Officials warned the incident may be part of operations intended to influence voters.

stories.title: US commandos 'went deep' into Iran to rescue downed airman
stories.summary: The US military conducted a rescue operation deep inside Iranian territory to recover a downed American airman. Iran disputed US claims of success, stating the rescue attempt in the mountains was foiled.

stories.title: 3 killed including baby as high winds topple tree during Easter egg hunt in Germany
stories.summary: Three people, including a 10-month-old girl, were killed in Satrupholm in northern Germany on Sunday when high winds toppled a 30-meter tree onto a group of about 50 people attending an Easter egg hunt.

stories.title: OPEC+ raises oil production quotas by 206,000 barrels per day
stories.summary: The OPEC+ oil cartel, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, agreed on Sunday to increase production quotas by 206,000 barrels per day starting in May.

stories.title: ‘Open the F***in’ Strait’: Trump threatens to bomb Iran’s power plants, starting Tuesday
stories.summary: US President Trump demanded Iran immediately reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to bomb Iranian power plants starting Tuesday. He also confirmed the US had supplied weapons to anti-regime protesters inside Iran.

stories.title: Russia talks compromise, demands capitulation — and is lying to Trump while preparing more occupation, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of lying to U.S. President Donald Trump while preparing further occupation of Ukrainian territory. He characterized Moscow's demand for Ukrainian withdrawal as strategically unacceptable, arguing it would give Russia a foothold for additional territorial gains.

stories.title: At least 14 people killed in Israeli strikes across Lebanon
