stories.summary: Israeli military strikes across Lebanon killed at least 14 people, while Hezbollah launched projectiles at northern Israel. Israeli ground forces continued advancing deeper into southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Pope warns world is becoming ‘indifferent’ to violence
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered his first Easter mass at the Vatican, calling on world leaders to pursue peace and warning that the international community is growing indifferent to ongoing violence.

stories.title: Seven arrested over alleged support for Palestine Action at RAF Lakenheath protest
stories.summary: Seven people were arrested on suspicion of supporting the banned group Palestine Action during a protest outside RAF Lakenheath airbase in Suffolk on Sunday. The Lakenheath Alliance for Peace organized the encampment after reports that a U.S. fighter jet shot down in Iran had launched from the base.

stories.title: Intensified Israeli attacks across Lebanon
stories.summary: Heavy Israeli strikes hit locations across Lebanon on Sunday, particularly in Beirut and the south. Artillery shelling was also reported in southern areas, including Tebnine in the Tyre district. At least 11 people were killed since dawn.

stories.title: Iranian missile strikes industrial area in southern Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck the Ramat Hovav industrial area in southern Israel. Video footage captured the moment of impact at the industrial zone.

stories.title: Ex-hostages host radio shows on songs of strength in captivity
stories.summary: Former Israeli hostages Yarden Bibas, Guy Gilboa-Dalal, and Amit Soussana are set to host radio segments on Israel's Kan 88 during Passover, discussing songs that gave them strength during captivity.

stories.title: False flag operation: Expert tells how Orban could undermine Hungarian election with Russia, Vucic's help
stories.summary: Hungarian Russia expert András Rácz published a forecast warning that Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's government could attempt to disrupt a Hungarian election through a false flag operation. The scenario involves possible Russian and Serbian collaboration to blame Ukraine for pipeline sabotage.

stories.title: Army says it killed Hamas gunmen approaching troops in Gaza
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it killed Hamas gunmen who were approaching troops in Gaza, describing the cell as an immediate threat. Gaza officials reported four people died in a strike near the Darraj neighborhood in northern Gaza City.

stories.title: Mongols, Soviets, now Putin: every empire told Ukraine “you are one of us.” None were right.
stories.summary: A report from Lviv, Ukraine, examines the historical pattern of imperial powers claiming Ukraine as their own, from the Mongols to the Soviets to modern Russia. The piece follows a visit to Lviv's churches days after a Russian Shahed drone struck a 17th-century monastery.

stories.title: High Court hears petition on expanding Western Wall worship cap after protest ruling
stories.summary: Israel's High Court heard a petition on expanding worship access at the Western Wall. This followed the court's earlier intervention ordering the state to allow anti-war demonstrations, overruling the Home Front Command's restrictions.

stories.title: UAE is 'dealing with incident' at Khor Fakkan Port
stories.summary: The Sharjah media office said the UAE is responding to an incident at Khor Fakkan Port, with no injuries reported. The UK Maritime Trade Operations had received reports of multiple splashes from unknown projectiles near the port.

stories.title: 'Open the f***in' Strait': Trump says US will strike Iran's power plants if Hormuz stays closed
stories.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social reaffirming a 48-hour deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening strikes on Iranian power plants if the waterway remains closed.

stories.title: To secure a ceasefire with Iran, the US must abandon ideological war
stories.summary: Former Turkish Foreign Minister Ahmet Davutoglu argued that the US must distance itself from Israel's influence and abandon ideological motivations in its policy toward Iran in order to achieve a ceasefire.

stories.title: OPEC+ warns attacks on energy facilities will take 'long time' to repair
stories.summary: OPEC+ warned on Sunday that energy facilities damaged during the ongoing war will be costly and time-consuming to repair, potentially affecting global oil supplies long-term. The group emphasized the importance of safeguarding international maritime routes.

stories.title: Woman injured in Russian shelling of Kherson dies in hospital
stories.summary: A woman who was injured in a Russian shelling attack on the city of Kherson has died from her wounds in hospital.

stories.title: Lebanon's Aoun calls for Israel talks, warns of social division
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called for dialogue with Israel, stating that negotiations should not be viewed as a concession. He also warned against divisive rhetoric amid social pressures caused by the ongoing refugee crisis.

stories.title: Israel’s Ben-Gvir details plans for Palestinian ‘death row’
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir publicly outlined plans to establish a "death row" for Palestinian prisoners, detailing the proposed policy with enthusiasm.

stories.title: Eight Israelis held after assault on West Bank village of Qusra
stories.summary: Eight Israeli suspects aged 18 to 48 were arrested following an assault and arson attack on property in the West Bank village of Qusra.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Israeli strike on South Beirut kills at least 4 people
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on south Beirut killed at least four people. The strike is part of ongoing Israeli military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Roads near Karachi Press Club closed ahead of planned PTI protest against rising fuel prices
stories.summary: Authorities in Karachi closed Din Mohammad Wafai Road and Sarwar Shaheed Road near the Karachi Press Club on Sunday, citing security concerns ahead of a planned PTI protest against rising fuel prices.

stories.title: Netanyahu congratulates Trump for rescue of F-15 pilot who was shot down in Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu congratulated US President Trump on the rescue of an American F-15 pilot who had been shot down in Iran, praising the operation as incredible.

stories.title: Two dead, dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes in Mediterranean
stories.summary: A migrant boat that departed from the Libyan coast capsized in the Mediterranean Sea, killing at least two people and leaving around 70 others missing. An Italian NGO reported that 32 people were rescued from the vessel.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: the US rescues missing airman from Iran
stories.summary: Former US Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for European and NATO Policy Jim Townsend discussed the rescue of a missing American airman from Iran amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Despite propaganda coup of F-15 crew rescue, downing is reminder to US that Iran can fight back
stories.summary: The U.S. military completed the rescue of the second crew member from an F-15 fighter jet shot down by Iran, in an operation lasting roughly 48 hours. Analysts noted the incident demonstrates Iran's ability to impose costs on U.S. forces and should caution against plans for ground operations.

stories.title: Trump threatens ‘hell’ for Iran over Hormuz Strait as deadline approaches
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iranian power plants and bridges beginning Tuesday if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened, posting the threats in an expletive-laden social media message.

stories.title: Middle East war hits Britain’s fish and chip shops
stories.summary: Rising diesel costs linked to the Middle East war are affecting British fishing operations. Peter Bruce, a fisherman based in Peterhead, Scotland, reported his fuel expenses doubling from about £5,000 to £10,000 per trawling trip in the North Sea.

stories.title: Gaza civil defence, hospital say Israeli strike kills four
stories.summary: Gaza's civil defence and Al-Shifa hospital reported that an Israeli drone strike killed four people in Gaza. The hospital confirmed the casualty toll from the attack.

stories.title: Fuel reservoir hit at Russia’s Primorsk, NORSI refinery on fire after drone attacks
stories.summary: A drone attack struck a fuel reservoir at Russia's Baltic Sea port of Primorsk, causing a fuel leak, while the NORSI oil refinery caught fire following a separate drone strike, according to Russian authorities.

stories.title: Middle East war hits Britain’s fish and chip shops
stories.summary: Britain's fish and chip shops are facing economic pressure linked to the Middle East conflict. Operators report concerns about rising fuel and fertiliser prices as well as shortages of cooking oil affecting their supply chains.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts expected to reach far side of moon on Monday
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew is expected to reach the far side of the moon on Monday, venturing deeper into space than any humans in history. The mission, carrying three American and one Canadian astronaut, launched on Wednesday and is proceeding on schedule as a total solar eclipse approaches.

stories.title: Mearsheimer: No signs of quick end to US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: US political scientist John Mearsheimer stated there are no indications of a swift conclusion to the US-Israel war against Iran. He argued that Israel, rather than Iran, is the more aggressive actor in the Middle East.

stories.title: UKMTO reports unknown projectiles near UAE's Khor Fakkan port
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a container ship captain observed multiple splashes from unknown projectiles near the UAE's Khor Fakkan port on Sunday.

stories.title: DR Congo to receive ‘third-country’ deportees from the US under new deal
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo agreed to receive deportees from the United States under a new arrangement funded by Washington. The DRC government said arrivals would begin within the month under a temporary deal.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Naftogaz facilities in Poltava, Sumy regions overnight
stories.summary: Russian drones struck Naftogaz Group facilities in Ukraine's Poltava and Sumy regions in the early morning hours of April 5.

stories.title: Christian Lebanese families displaced as they celebrate Easter
stories.summary: Christian Lebanese families who had been displaced by ongoing conflict marked Easter Sunday away from their homes, amid continued instability in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran says it destroyed four US army aircraft
stories.summary: Iran's joint military command claimed it destroyed four U.S. Army aircraft during a complex rescue operation to recover an airman whose fighter jet was shot down on Friday.

stories.title: Iran’s first vice president slams Trump for lack of healthcare funding in US
stories.summary: Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref criticized US President Trump on social media after Trump cited the war on Iran as a reason for being unable to fund childcare and healthcare programs in the United States.

stories.title: Israel has killed 1,461 people in Lebanon since beginning of March
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israel has killed 1,461 people and wounded 4,430 others in Lebanon since operations began on 2 March.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 11 in Lebanon, Israel announces ‘security buffer’
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit two locations in Lebanon on Easter Sunday, killing at least 11 people. Seven died in Kfarhata in south Lebanon, including a 4-year-old child, while four were killed and 39 injured in Beirut's Jnah neighborhood. Israel announced a "security buffer" in the area.

stories.title: Strike kills 4 near Beirut hospital, as President Aoun pushes for talks with Israel
stories.summary: An Israeli strike killed four people near a hospital in Beirut as Lebanese President Joseph Aoun pushed for negotiations with Israel. Hezbollah increased rocket fire on northern Israel while the IDF struck Hezbollah targets in the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Iran strikes Gulf petrochemical and desalination facilities
stories.summary: Iran launched overnight strikes targeting petrochemical and desalination facilities in Kuwait, the UAE, and Bahrain. The attacks ignited fires and forced shutdowns at critical infrastructure across the Gulf states.

stories.title: Iran’s World Cup participation depends on relocation from US, minister says
stories.summary: Iran requested that FIFA relocate its 2026 World Cup matches from the United States to Mexico due to the ongoing US-Israeli war. Iran's sports minister said the country's participation depends on FIFA's response.

stories.title: US war on Iran: Trump pressures allies in war effort but offers 'no role in strategy'
stories.summary: Ian Lesser of the German Marshall Fund described the current Middle East crisis as a systemic shock to the global order. He highlighted the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz as a key development causing political, diplomatic, and economic challenges. The US is reportedly pressing allies to support its war effort while offering them no role in strategic planning.

stories.title: Why an attack on Bushehr nuclear plant would be catastrophic for the Gulf
stories.summary: Repeated US and Israeli strikes on Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant have raised concerns about potential radioactive contamination spreading across the Persian Gulf region and beyond Iran's borders.

stories.title: Trump says 'good chance' of deal with Iran, but he will 'blow up' everything if not
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told Fox News he believes there is a "good chance" of reaching a deal with Iran, stating negotiations are underway. He warned that if no deal is reached quickly, he would consider escalating military action and seizing Iran's oil.

stories.title: Trump's 'puppet regime': Home to world’s largest oil reserves, is Venezuela key to US economy?
stories.summary: Professor Amalendu Misra of Lancaster University characterized US policy toward Venezuela as a form of "regime change light," distinct from past interventions in Iraq or Libya. He argued that Washington is pursuing a subtler strategy aimed at reshaping Venezuela's political and economic structures while avoiding the destabilizing effects of total regime collapse.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on key Russian oil refinery and Baltic port
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its defense forces struck a major Russian oil refinery and a Baltic Sea port overnight on April 5, along with targets in temporarily occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Seeing ‘one big thing’: Is the Iran war at risk of turning nuclear? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis examined whether the ongoing war with Iran risks escalating to a nuclear conflict. The piece argued that a nuclear war in the Middle East could occur even while Iran remains a non-nuclear state.

stories.title: Israeli restrictions spoil Easter for Palestinian Christians
stories.summary: Palestinian Christians marked Easter Sunday under Israeli restrictions that included the closure of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. Shops in East Jerusalem were also shuttered.

stories.title: Inside the legal battle: High Court rules on wartime protests and freedom of speech - explainer
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ruled on the legality of wartime restrictions on anti-war protests held on Saturday, addressing tensions between security measures and freedom of speech. The ruling set a significant legal precedent.

stories.title: Nepal announces two-day weekends as fuel crisis caused by Iran war deepens
stories.summary: Nepal announced a shift to two-day weekends as a fuel crisis deepened due to the Iran war. The Himalayan nation, which relies almost entirely on India for fuel, had previously observed only Saturday as a day off.

stories.title: Oman, Iran hold talks on Strait of Hormuz: state media
stories.summary: Oman and Iran held diplomatic talks on ensuring smooth passage through the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. Officials said possible options were discussed between the Iranian and Omani foreign ministries.

stories.title: West Bank man indicted for extortion, impersonation of IAF pilot, Mossad agent, illegal entry
stories.summary: A 51-year-old West Bank resident was indicted in Israel on charges of extortion, impersonating an Israeli Air Force fighter pilot and Mossad agent, and illegally entering Israel.

stories.title: British military sees youth jobs crisis as an opportunity
stories.summary: The British military is leveraging a youth employment crisis to boost recruitment for its depleted armed forces. Military career opportunities are being actively promoted in job centres across the United Kingdom.

stories.title: King of Bahrain urges end to Iranian attacks across the region
stories.summary: Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa issued a statement condemning Iranian attacks on his kingdom and other regional countries, saying the strikes targeted civilians and infrastructure. He called for an immediate halt to the attacks.

stories.title: Egypt, US, and Iran discuss regional de-escalation as Mideast violence continues to flare up
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held phone calls with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, Iran's Abbas Araghchi, and other regional officials as part of fresh de-escalation efforts amid continuing violence across the Middle East.

stories.title: Of missiles and miracles: Residents of bombed cities count their blessings after weekend salvos
stories.summary: Residents across central Israeli cities described shock and diminishing feelings of safety after Iranian missile salvos struck over a dozen sites during the weekend. Some residents noted moments of fortune amid the widespread destruction.

stories.title: Iran says several ‘enemy flying objects’ destroyed during US pilot rescue mission
stories.summary: Iran's police command claimed an American C-130 aircraft was downed in southern Isfahan province during a US pilot rescue mission. Iranian authorities said several "enemy flying objects" were destroyed during the operation.

stories.title: 'They broke my leg for what happened in Sde Teiman': Bar Kupershtein recounts Hamas brutality
stories.summary: Released Israeli hostage Bar Kupershtein recounted brutality by Hamas captors, saying they broke his leg along with that of fellow captive Yosef Chaim Ohana. He said his captors cited Israeli actions at the Sde Teiman detention facility as justification.

stories.title: US-Israeli air strike hits airport in southwestern Iran
stories.summary: A joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike struck Shahid Qasem Soleimani International Airport in southwestern Iran's Khuzestan province on Sunday, according to Iran's official IRNA news agency, citing the province's deputy governor Valiollah Hayati.

stories.title: Israeli strike which killed four Gaza policemen tests ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel killed four Gaza policemen in a strike that tested the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025. The incident was described as Israel's latest violation of the truce.

stories.title: On Easter, President Zardari and PM Shehbaz hail Christian community’s ‘admirable services’
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif issued separate messages on Easter commending the Christian community's contributions to Pakistan's development. Christians across Pakistan celebrated the holiday marking the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

stories.title: Trump warns 'crazy bastards' in Iran to open the 'fuckin' strait' in Truth Social rant
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump posted an expletive-laden message on Truth Social threatening to destroy Iran's energy and transport infrastructure if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Deadly strike on Nikopol market: City declares day of mourning
stories.summary: The city of Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region declared a day of mourning after a Russian strike hit a local market, killing multiple people.

stories.title: Aid groups warn war in West Asia is hindering food, medicine from reaching millions
stories.summary: Aid organizations warn that the war in West Asia has disrupted critical supply routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and hubs in Dubai, Doha, and Abu Dhabi. Rising transport, fuel, and insurance costs are reducing the volume of food and medicine reaching millions of people.

stories.title: The week in pictures: Mideast war, a lunar mission and Holy Week processions
stories.summary: The week's major events included continued US-Iran tensions as President Trump exchanged threats with Tehran and oil prices surged on volatile markets. NASA launched its first crewed lunar mission in over fifty years, Italy failed to qualify for a third consecutive football World Cup, and Christians around the world observed Holy Week.

stories.title: Missile shrapnel hits southern Israel following latest barrage from Iran, no injuries reported
stories.summary: Missile shrapnel from Iran's latest barrage struck locations in southern Israel on Sunday afternoon, with no injuries reported. United Hatzalah and the IDF's Search and Rescue Brigade conducted searches at the impact sites.

stories.title: 'Choose peace': Pope Leo marks Easter under cloud of MidEast war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV used his first Easter blessing to call for peace in the Middle East, urging leaders to "choose peace" amid the ongoing regional war.

stories.title: UAE says air defences responding to Iran missiles, drones
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates activated its air defence systems in response to Iranian missiles and drones. Tehran stated it was targeting aluminium industries in the UAE as part of its broader strikes.

stories.title: Eighth Israeli attack reported in Beirut’s southern suburbs
stories.summary: Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported an eighth wave of Israeli airstrikes targeting Beirut's southern suburbs on Sunday. The agency noted heavy warplane activity in the skies over the capital.

stories.title: Armenia could quit Russia’s NATO-equivalent alliance and economic union if Moscow uses gas as leverage, parliament speaker says
stories.summary: Armenian Parliament Speaker Alen Simonyan stated on April 4 that Armenia could withdraw from both the Russian-led CSTO military alliance and the Eurasian Economic Union if Moscow raises gas prices as leverage against Yerevan.

stories.title: UK has detained 76 ‘age-disputed’ children under one in, one out scheme
stories.summary: Research shows that 76 children from conflict zones whose ages were disputed by the UK Home Office have been detained in adult detention centres since September. The detentions occurred under the government's "one in, one out" scheme, which allows forced removal of small boat arrivals to France.

stories.title: China reveals military capabilities in new space solar power plant design
stories.summary: Chinese scientist Duan Baoyan published a paper outlining a revamped design for the "Zhuri" space-based solar power initiative, revealing potential military applications. The technology could support surveillance and electronic warfare in addition to beaming energy from orbit to Earth.

stories.title: Iran fires missile salvos at Israel, strikes critical energy infrastructure across Gulf
stories.summary: Iran launched missile salvos at Israel, with one projectile striking the Neot Hovav industrial zone in southern Israel, causing damage but no injuries. The IDF is investigating the interception failure. Iran also targeted civilian energy facilities in the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait.

stories.title: Israeli assault near Lebanon's largest public hospital kills four
stories.summary: An Israeli strike near Rafik Hariri University Hospital in south Beirut killed at least four people and wounded 39 others, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The impact was approximately 100 metres from Lebanon's largest public hospital.

stories.title: Ukraine not asked to intervene in Strait of Hormuz, only to share expertise – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky clarified that Ukraine was not asked to intervene directly in the Strait of Hormuz situation. He said partners only requested Ukraine share expertise drawn from its experience unblocking the Black Sea grain corridor.

stories.title: Congo to take third-country deportees from the US under new deal
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo agreed to accept third-country deportees from the United States under a new deal. The Congolese Ministry of Communications said arrivals would begin in April but did not specify dates or numbers.

stories.title: As Iran war enters 6th week, escalation looks the most likely scenario
stories.summary: As the U.S.-Israel war against Iran entered its sixth week, analysts assessed that further escalation remained the most likely scenario. U.S. and Israeli forces were reportedly preparing to strike Iran's energy sites and considering actions regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's uranium stockpile.

stories.title: FIA to use AI-powered system to track down most wanted criminals
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency has developed an AI-powered system to track most-wanted criminals by generating updated visual projections of their appearance from old photographs. FIA Director General Dr. Usmar Anwar said the agency's red book of wanted criminals is being updated with the new tool.

stories.title: Trump vows 'hell' on Iran if Strait of Hormuz not opened
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened Iran with attacks on its power plants and bridges via a Truth Social post, warning of "hell" if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. He set a deadline and referred to a forthcoming "Power Plant Day" and "Bridge Day."

stories.title: US special forces rescue second F-15 airman from Iran
stories.summary: U.S. special forces rescued the weapons officer of an F-15 fighter jet that was shot down over Iran on Friday. President Trump announced the airman was wounded but expected to recover fully. The rescue marks the retrieval of the second crew member from the downed aircraft.

stories.title: Second US airman rescued from Iran, Trump issues ultimatum
stories.summary: A news roundup reported that the second U.S. airman was rescued from Iran and that President Trump issued an ultimatum, though specific details were not elaborated in the summary.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Defense Forces regain control of 12 settlements on Oleksandrivka axis – CinC Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces recaptured 12 settlements along the Oleksandrivka axis, Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi reported. Eight settlements were in the Dnipropetrovsk region and four in the Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Afghanistan wants US$10 billion in trade deals with Central Asia
stories.summary: Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi announced at a Kabul dialogue with Central Asian representatives that Afghanistan aims to increase trade with Central Asian nations to US$10 billion within three to four years. Trade with those countries reached approximately US$2.7 billion in 2025.

stories.title: Iran executes two men involved in January protests judiciary news outlet says
stories.summary: Iran executed two men connected to January protests. Iran's Supreme Court described the executed individuals as "rioters who sought to commit mass murder."

stories.title: Hezbollah rockets targeting Israel hit at least 165 UNIFIL positions in southern Lebanon, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it identified 165 Hezbollah rocket launches targeting Israel that struck near UNIFIL positions in southern Lebanon. The IDF said it continues operations against Hezbollah in the area.

stories.title: Trump offers no concrete plan as Strait of Hormuz closure shocks Europe
stories.summary: Economist James Meadway stated that U.S. President Donald Trump has issued threats but presented no concrete plan to resolve the crisis caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has shocked European markets.

stories.title: Inside the race to rescue a downed US airman in Iran
stories.summary: Conflicting accounts emerged over a reported U.S. special operations rescue of a downed American airman in central Iran. President Trump hailed the mission as successful, while Tehran insisted it was "foiled." The incident has generated viral images and competing narratives.

stories.title: Antisemitism in UK schools hit all-times high over last three years, investigation reveals
stories.summary: An investigation by The Telegraph found that antisemitic incidents in UK schools reached an all-time high over the past three years. A record 4,298 antisemitic incidents were recorded in Britain in 2023, following the Hamas October 7 attack.

stories.title: Russia shares satellite intelligence with Iran about Israel's energy system – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Russia shared satellite intelligence on 50 to 53 Israeli energy facilities with Iran, helping Tehran target civilian infrastructure in Israel.

stories.title: Ukrainian Strike Damages Central Russian Oil Refinery, Baltic Port Oil Facility
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry reported that 87 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight over Russian territory and annexed Crimea. Separately, strikes damaged an oil refinery in central Russia and an oil facility at a Baltic Sea port.

stories.title: IRGC claims hits on Gulf petrochemical plants
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for attacks on petrochemical plants in the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain. The IRGC warned it would intensify strikes against American economic interests if civilian targets continued to be hit.

stories.title: China’s push for hydrogen-powered planes takes step forward amid Iran energy crisis
stories.summary: A Chinese 7.5-tonne uncrewed cargo aircraft powered by the world's most powerful hydrogen turboprop engine of its kind completed a successful 16-minute maiden flight. The engine generates more than 1 megawatt. State news agency Xinhua reported the milestone as part of China's push for green aviation technology.

stories.title: Israel must annex the West Bank to prevent the next war - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion article argues that Israel should annex the West Bank to prevent future conflicts, citing polling from the Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research indicating 59% of West Bank Palestinians supported Hamas's October 7 attack.

stories.title: FIA arrests Nadra official ‘involved’ in issuing fake CNICs to Afghan nationals in Karachi
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency arrested a National Database and Registration Authority official in Karachi for allegedly issuing fake Pakistani identity cards to Afghan nationals. Two Afghan nationals were also detained during a raid in the Metroville SITE area after being found with illegal identity documents.

stories.title: Court orders Nazi-looted Modigliani painting be returned to Jewish art dealer’s estate
stories.summary: A New York judge ruled after an 11-year legal case that a Modigliani painting valued at approximately $25 million, held in storage in Switzerland, must be returned to the estate of Jewish art dealer Oscar Stettiner, from whom it was seized by Nazi forces in Paris during World War II.

stories.title: Pope urges peace in his first Easter mass: ‘Let those who have weapons lay them down’
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered his first Easter mass at St. Peter's Basilica, calling for peace and urging those with weapons to lay them down. He departed from the traditional practice of listing the world's conflicts by name in the Urbi et Orbi blessing, greeting the crowd in 10 languages.

stories.title: Satellite firm Planet Labs to indefinitely withhold Iran war images
stories.summary: California-based satellite imagery firm Planet Labs announced it would indefinitely withhold images of the Iran conflict region. The company said the US government had requested all satellite imagery providers to restrict access to photos of the area.

stories.title: Russia’s governor said a pipeline was hit in Primors. Two hours later he said it wasn’t. NASA showed a fire at the tank farm
stories.summary: Leningrad Oblast Governor Drozdenko revised his account of a April 5 drone strike on Primorsk, initially claiming pipeline damage before stating shrapnel hit a fuel tank. NASA satellite data showed a fire at the oil depot rather than the pipeline.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's threats, warns 'hell will open for you'
stories.summary: Iranian General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi rejected President Trump's latest threats against Iran, calling them "stupid" and warning Trump that "hell will be open for you."

stories.title: Prolonged war in Middle East could erode U.S. support for Ukraine – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that a prolonged U.S.-Israeli war against Iran could erode American support for Ukraine, diverting attention and resources from Kyiv's defense needs.

stories.title: Iran’s ex-FM Zarif proposes peace roadmap; Gulf points at erosion of trust
stories.summary: Former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif proposed a peace roadmap calling for limits on Iran's nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the lifting of sanctions. Gulf states responded by pointing to an erosion of trust.

stories.title: Russia says Ukraine attack damages oil pipeline
stories.summary: Russia reported that a Ukrainian attack damaged an oil pipeline on its territory. Ukraine has intensified strikes on Russian infrastructure targets in recent months as the war continues.

stories.title: Oman and Iran hold talks on reopening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Oman held discussions with Iran regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as Israel, the United States, and Iran continued to exchange fire across the Middle East.

stories.title: New footage shows moment US-Israeli double-tap strike in Iran
stories.summary: New footage emerged showing the moment a U.S.-Israeli double-tap airstrike hit Iran's tallest bridge. Local media reported at least 13 people were killed and dozens injured in the infrastructure attack.

stories.title: Indonesia lays to rest peacekeepers killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Three Indonesian peacekeepers killed the previous week in southern Lebanon were laid to rest in their respective hometowns in Indonesia on Sunday.

stories.title: Talk about death comes alive in ageing Hong Kong
stories.summary: A death education advocate in Hong Kong reports that residents have become more open to discussing death and funeral planning in recent years. Factors include the Covid pandemic, a wave of emigration, the deadly Tai Po fire, and the city's rapidly ageing population.

stories.title: On Easter, president and PM hail Christian community’s ‘admirable services’, contributions
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the Christian community's contributions to the country's development in separate Easter messages. Christians across Pakistan celebrated the holiday with religious observances.

stories.title: Airman whose F-15 was downed in Iran rescued, say US officials
stories.summary: A U.S. airman whose F-15 fighter jet was shot down over Iran has been rescued, according to U.S. officials. President Trump stated the crew member was injured but expected to fully recover.

stories.title: A long war in West Asia could take away support from Ukraine, says Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that a prolonged war in West Asia could divert US support away from Ukraine. Speaking in Istanbul, he stressed Ukraine's urgent need for more US-made Patriot air defence systems to counter daily Russian bombardments.

stories.title: Russian drones attack residential area in Velykyi Burluk, Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a morning drone strike on the settlement of Velykyi Burluk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, targeting a residential area.

stories.title: Oman, Iran discuss smooth transit in Strait of Hormuz, Muscat says
stories.summary: Oman and Iran held talks focused on ensuring smooth passage through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Muscat. The discussions took place as Tehran effectively continued to block the vital waterway.

stories.title: Iran executes two men who tried storming military facility during January protest crackdown
stories.summary: Iran executed two men convicted of attempting to storm a military facility during January's anti-government protests. The men were among four individuals facing execution as part of a broader crackdown on unrest.

stories.title: NGOs warn Iran war is hindering relief from reaching millions
stories.summary: Non-governmental organizations warned that the ongoing war involving Iran is blocking vital humanitarian aid from reaching millions of vulnerable people. The groups cited a global energy crisis and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz as compounding factors.

stories.title: China unveils handheld coil gun that works like a ‘less deadly’ pistol
stories.summary: China has developed a handheld electromagnetic coil gun designed for stealth and non-lethal operations, according to state broadcaster CCTV. The weapon can fire 1,000 to 2,000 projectiles per minute and penetrate wooden boards from dozens of metres. Its power levels can be adjusted for law enforcement use.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 4 Palestinians in Gaza ceasefire breach
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed at least four Palestinian civilians in Gaza City's Darraj neighbourhood and wounded others. The attack was described as a breach of the ceasefire.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF locates, kills two Hezbollah terror cells in southern Lebanon operations
stories.summary: The IDF reported locating and killing two Hezbollah cells during operations in southern Lebanon. IDF Arabic Spokesperson Col. Avichay Adraee issued an evacuation warning for residents of Ghobeiry in Beirut's southern suburbs.

stories.title: Rocket reportedly hits factory in southern Israel, Israeli reports say
stories.summary: A rocket struck a factory in the Ramat Hovav industrial zone near Beersheba in southern Israel, according to Israeli media. The Israeli Home Front Command had issued warnings after detecting missile launches from Iran toward Beersheba and Dimona. Sirens also sounded in Upper Galilee following rocket fire from Lebanon.

stories.title: Zelensky congratulates Western Christian faithful on Easter
stories.summary: President Zelensky extended Easter greetings to Western Christian faithful, wishing that prayers for protection from evil would be heard.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 5 – IDF soldiers absorb Hezbollah rockets in Lebanon push
stories.summary: IDF military correspondent Emanuel Fabian reported on Israeli soldiers encountering Hezbollah rocket fire during operations in Lebanon. The briefing also covered assessments of Iran's military capabilities and a significant shortage of IDF manpower.

stories.title: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation says Iranian hit causes 'severe' damage to units
stories.summary: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation reported severe material damage to operating units after an Iranian drone attack set facilities ablaze. No injuries were reported, and teams were working to contain the fires and prevent them from spreading.

stories.title: Uproar in Germany over law requiring men get military approval for long stays abroad
stories.summary: A clause in Germany's updated military service legislation, effective since January, requires men up to age 45 to obtain armed forces permission before extended stays abroad, even in peacetime. The broader law also mandates that all 18-year-old men complete a suitability questionnaire but stops short of conscription. The provision has sparked public uproar.

stories.title: Oman and Iran hold meeting on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Oman and Iran held deputy-minister-level talks focused on easing passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The Omani state news agency said specialists from both countries discussed possible options for ensuring smooth transit through the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Miracle in Sinaia: Israeli underdogs break Soviet chess dominance in 1965
stories.summary: The article recounts how a team of Israeli amateur chess players upset the dominant Soviet chess establishment at a 1965 tournament in Sinaia, Romania, in an event remembered as a symbol of Israeli resilience during the Cold War.

stories.title: Limited Passover and Easter ceremonies held at Jerusalem holy sites amid war restrictions
stories.summary: Limited Passover and Easter ceremonies took place at holy sites in Jerusalem's Old City amid wartime restrictions. Only a handful of clergy were permitted to conduct the Passover priestly blessing at the Western Wall and Easter Sunday services at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

stories.title: Pharmaceutical logistics in demand as war rattles supply chains
stories.summary: The pharmaceutical logistics sector is experiencing increased demand as the ongoing war disrupts global supply chains. Despite repeated crises, both the logistics and pharmaceutical industries continue to expand.

stories.title: Easter in Jerusalem overshadowed by war and restrictions at the Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Easter celebrations in Jerusalem's Old City were subdued, overshadowed by ongoing war and restrictions on access to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. The site, where Christians commemorate Christ's crucifixion and resurrection, saw limited attendance on Easter Sunday.

stories.title: Why Israeli goalkeeper Daniel Peretz is making headlines in Britain
stories.summary: Israeli goalkeeper Daniel Peretz drew widespread attention in British football media after helping Southampton defeat Arsenal in the British FA Cup.

stories.title: Israel army says it underestimated Hezbollah, Iran capabilities
stories.summary: An Israeli military commander acknowledged that the army underestimated the military capabilities of both Hezbollah and Iran. The commander stated that only a political settlement would bring an end to the war with Iran.

stories.title: Russian shelling of Kharkiv region leaves one killed and 11 injured over past day, including one child
stories.summary: Russian shelling in Ukraine's Kharkiv region killed one person and injured 11 others, including a child, over the previous day.

stories.title: French boats set sail from Marseille to join Gaza aid Flotilla
stories.summary: Approximately 20 French boats departed from Marseille on Saturday to join an international flotilla attempting to break the Israeli blockade of Gaza and deliver humanitarian aid to the territory.

stories.title: Pepsi drops Wireless sponsorship amid criticism of Kanye West booking
stories.summary: Pepsi withdrew its sponsorship of a UK music festival after Kanye West was announced as a headliner. British Prime Minister Keir Starmer called the booking "deeply concerning," referencing the rapper's controversial song titled "Heil Hitler." West has not yet applied for entry to the UK and could be blocked.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls for peace, dialogue amid Ukraine, Iran wars in Easter mass
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Easter Mass at St. Peter's Basilica, calling on warring parties worldwide to lay down arms and pursue dialogue. The first U.S.-born pope departed from tradition by not naming specific conflicts in his Urbi et Orbi blessing.

stories.title: Pope urges world to 'lay down arms" and names no wars in Easter blessing
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered his Easter Urbi et Orbi blessing from the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica, urging the world to lay down arms. He notably did not name specific wars or conflicts, departing from the tradition of previous popes.

stories.title: "We got him!": US rescues aviator whose fighter jet was shot down in Iran
stories.summary: The United States announced it rescued an American service member who had been missing behind enemy lines after Iran shot down a U.S. fighter jet. President Trump simultaneously escalated pressure on Tehran with a new deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: On Easter, Pope Leo urges world leaders to end wars, renounce conquest
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV used his first Easter message to urge world leaders to end wars and renounce territorial conquest. The address was delivered from Rome during Easter celebrations at the Vatican.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader to make ‘peace’ visit to China, first in 10 years
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairperson Cheng Li-wun is set to travel to China, becoming the first sitting KMT leader to visit in a decade. She stated her intention to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping to promote cross-strait peace. Taiwanese officials warn Beijing may use the visit to influence Taiwan's politics and hinder US arms sales.

stories.title: US forces rescue 2 airmen downed in Iran; Trump says crew member injured but ‘safe’
stories.summary: US forces recovered two airmen whose aircraft went down in Iran, with President Trump calling it one of the most daring rescue operations in US history. The rescue occurred as Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and Kuwait, and one day after Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Tehran.

stories.title: How US fooled Iran to rescue downed F-15 airman stranded in a mountain crevice
stories.summary: A CIA-led deception campaign enabled the rescue of a U.S. F-15 airman stranded for 36 hours in a mountain crevice in Iran. The operation thwarted Iranian search efforts and extracted the pilot successfully.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran Guards claim destroyed U.S. aircraft searching for missing pilot
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they destroyed a U.S. aircraft that had been searching for the missing pilot of a downed F-15 fighter jet near Isfahan. President Trump said two U.S. airmen were rescued from Iran after he issued a deadline for Tehran to agree to a deal.

stories.title: Ukraine struck a refinery 800 km inside Russia — then hit the power plant keeping it running
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Lukoil-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez refinery in Russia's Volga region, located roughly 800 km inside Russian territory, and subsequently hit the power plant supplying it. The facility processes up to 17 million tonnes of crude annually and is a key petrol supplier to Moscow Oblast.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Nikopol with FPV drone, leaving one killed and another injured
stories.summary: A Russian FPV drone strike on Nikopol in the Dnipropetrovsk region of Ukraine killed one person and severely injured another.

stories.title: US prepares to use close to entire stealth missile arsenal as Iran strikes intensify - report
stories.summary: The U.S. is preparing to deploy nearly its entire arsenal of stealth missiles as strikes on Iran intensify, according to Bloomberg. The missiles have been launched from B-52 and B-1B bombers as well as strike fighters.

stories.title: Indonesia lays to rest peacekeepers killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: Indonesia held funeral ceremonies for three of its UN peacekeepers killed by Israeli forces while deployed in southern Lebanon. Indonesian authorities called for an international investigation and demanded security guarantees for peacekeeping personnel.

stories.title: “We blame Trump”: Drivers line up for free gas as prices surge in the US
stories.summary: Drivers in Chicago lined up to receive free gasoline as fuel prices surged across the United States. The price spike has been driven by the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Afghan mother seeks justice after Pakistani bombing kills hundreds
stories.summary: An Afghan mother is seeking justice after Pakistani military strikes reportedly killed hundreds of people. Afghanistan and Pakistan remain locked in an escalating dispute, with Islamabad claiming Kabul harbors militants responsible for cross-border attacks, which the Taliban government denies.

stories.title: U.S. rescues airman whose F-15 was downed in Iran, say U.S. officials
stories.summary: U.S. officials confirmed the rescue of an airman whose F-15 fighter jet was shot down over Iran. President Trump described the operation as one of the most daring search and rescue missions in U.S. military history and said the crew member sustained injuries but would recover.

stories.title: Are China’s TV dramas obsessed with beauty? An industry regulator thinks so
stories.summary: China's National Radio and Television Administration has called on streaming platforms and production companies to move away from beauty-obsessed and traffic-driven programming in favor of higher-quality storytelling.

stories.title: Chinese firms trail US peers in AI adoption due to corporate culture: ex-OpenAI executive
stories.summary: Former OpenAI executive Zack Kass said traditional corporate culture and hierarchies are slowing AI adoption in Chinese enterprises compared to US counterparts. However, he noted that Chinese consumers are embracing AI agents at a rapid pace.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Chornobaivka in Kherson region with drones, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone attack on the village of Chornobaivka in Ukraine's Kherson region on the morning of April 5. A 40-year-old woman was wounded in the strike.

stories.title: Iran war driving up funeral costs in the UK
stories.summary: Funeral costs in the UK have risen to an average of £4,623, up 1.3% since January, partly due to higher gas prices linked to the war in Iran. Increased gas costs are affecting crematoria operations, according to a report by Pure Cremation.

stories.title: Israel’s Financial First Responders: Supporting Families and Business - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article highlights financial support programs for Israeli families, reservists, and small businesses affected by the ongoing military operation known as Operation Roaring Lion.

stories.title: Move over, Easter bunny: cats are the stars in Hong Kong this holiday
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Easter holiday featured large-scale cat-themed installations and murals across the city, including a giant ginger cat at Hong Kong International Airport and inflatable felines at the West Kowloon Cultural District, overshadowing the traditional Easter bunny.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks in Chernihiv region over past day leave one killed, damage  agricultural enterprise
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Snovsk area in Ukraine's Chernihiv region with Geran-type drones on the evening of April 4. A civilian man was killed, and an agricultural enterprise and a bread delivery vehicle were damaged.

stories.title: Australia receives fuel export guarantees from Singapore, Japan
stories.summary: Australia's Assistant Foreign Affairs and Trade Minister Matt Thistlethwaite announced that Japan, South Korea, and Singapore have pledged to maintain normal fuel shipments to Australia despite disruptions caused by the war in Iran.

stories.title: Terrorism case registered after Karachi judge gets threatening note with bullet
stories.summary: Police in Karachi registered a terrorism case after Judge Suhail Jabbar Malik, a civil judge and former Anti-Terrorism Court judge, received an envelope containing a bullet and a threatening note in his chamber. South DIG Syed Asad Raza confirmed the investigation is underway.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones damage oil pipeline near Russian port and spark fire at refinery
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck targets in Russia's Leningrad and Nizhny Novgorod regions overnight on April 5. In the Leningrad region, 19 drones were intercepted but debris damaged an oil pipeline near the port of Primorsk. A controlled burnoff was initiated with no injuries reported.

stories.title: ‘WE GOT HIM’: US commandos rescue downed F-15 airman in daring raid deep inside Iran
stories.summary: U.S. commandos rescued a downed F-15 airman from inside Iran after the aviator reportedly climbed to 7,000 feet to evade capture. Israeli intelligence contributed to the operation. Designated rescue aircraft became stuck and had to be destroyed.

stories.title: Package emitting smoke triggers hazardous materials operation at Ben Gurion Airport
stories.summary: A package emitting thick black smoke triggered a hazardous materials response at Ben Gurion Airport in Israel. Employees were evacuated from the affected area, and no injuries were reported. Firefighters identified the substance causing the smoke.

stories.title: Israeli strikes rain down on Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck Beirut's southern suburbs in the Ghobeiry neighbourhood after issuing an evacuation warning minutes earlier. Additional Israeli air strikes hit the towns of Beit Yahoun and Aaitit in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks leave 29 injured over past day in Sumy region
stories.summary: Russian drone attacks in Ukraine's Sumy region over the past day injured 29 people, including 19 children and 10 adults in an overnight strike, with two more people wounded during daytime attacks.

stories.title: Iran says Iraqi ships are allowed to use Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran declared that Iraqi ships are permitted to transit the Strait of Hormuz despite broader restrictions imposed by Tehran on the waterway. The exemption could release approximately three million barrels per day of Iraqi oil cargoes.

stories.title: US pilot from downed F-15E plane rescued in Iran: What we know
stories.summary: U.S. rescue forces retrieved the second pilot from an F-15E fighter jet that was shot down over Iran, ending a 48-hour ordeal. Details of the rescue operation have not been fully disclosed.

stories.title: Footage shows Israeli military dog attacking Palestinian man inside mosque
stories.summary: CCTV footage circulating online shows an Israeli military dog attacking a Palestinian worshipper as he exits a mosque. The location of the incident was not specified in initial reports.

stories.title: China’s luxury spending seen boosting global sales in 2026 despite headwinds
stories.summary: Analysts from HSBC, Deutsche Bank, and BNP Paribas forecast global luxury sales growth of 5.5 to 6 percent in 2026, with China's consumer recovery seen as a key driver despite uncertainty from the war in Iran.

stories.title: Pope Leo condemns ‘violence of war’ in first Easter Mass amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV used his first Easter Mass to condemn "the violence of war that kills and destroys," referencing the US-Israeli war on Iran and Russia's campaign in Ukraine. He singled out those who wage war, abuse the weak, and prioritize profits.

stories.title: Chinese man, 90, cycles across country after tragic losses of wife, son, daughter-in-law, grandson
stories.summary: A 90-year-old man named Zhang Zhongyi from Kaifeng, Henan province, China, has been cycling across the country for decades after the deaths of his wife, son, daughter-in-law, and grandson. His story gained nationwide attention after a woman in Putian, Fujian province, encountered him on the road.

stories.title: Ukraine hits port in Russia’s Primorsk, oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the port of Primorsk in Russia, causing fuel leaks, and targeted the NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, which caught fire. Russian authorities confirmed both incidents.

stories.title: Partisans disable key railway section in Sumy direction
stories.summary: Agents of the Ukrainian partisan movement ATESH disabled a relay cabinet on a railway line running from the Russian city of Bryansk toward Ukraine's Sumy region, disrupting a key logistics route.

stories.title: Iran war starts pinching U.S.; gas prices, transport costs surge
stories.summary: The average price of petrol in the United States rose to $4.09 per gallon by April 3, 2026, an increase of more than one dollar since before the Iran war began. This marked the highest fuel price level since August 2022, affecting transport costs nationwide.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes kill five IRGC fighters
stories.summary: U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran's Moghan Plain in northwestern Ardabil province killed five Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fighters, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA, citing an IRGC statement.

stories.title: Pera teams in Lahore accused of enforcing 10pm curbs on exempt sectors
stories.summary: Punjab Enforcement Regulatory Authority teams in Lahore are accused of forcing businesses and individuals exempt from 10pm closure restrictions to shut down, amid an ongoing fuel crisis lockdown. Reports include raids on sports activities and bakeries operating within legal hours.

stories.title: US rescues downed fighter pilot from Iran in 'daring' operation
stories.summary: U.S. forces rescued the second crew member of a downed F-15E fighter jet from inside Iran. Iranian media reported that five people were killed during the rescue mission.

stories.title: Israel says will strike Lebanon-Syria border crossing
stories.summary: Israel announced it would strike a border crossing between Lebanon and Syria, urging nearby residents to evacuate immediately. The threat came as Israeli forces continued strikes across multiple locations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Kuwait power, water desalination plants damaged by Iranian attack: government
stories.summary: Iranian military strikes damaged power and water desalination plants in Kuwait. Iran's army stated it was targeting aluminum industries in the UAE and U.S. military infrastructure in Kuwait, according to the official IRNA news agency.

stories.title: Africa faces growth slowdown due to war on Iran - Report
stories.summary: A joint report by the African Union and the African Development Bank warns that the war involving Iran threatens to raise living costs and slow economic growth across the African continent.

stories.title: Storm Dave: thousands of homes in Wales and Northern Ireland left without power
stories.summary: Storm Dave brought winds of up to 93mph to Capel Curig in north Wales and left thousands of homes in Wales and Northern Ireland without power. Road and rail travel across the UK was disrupted before weather warnings were lifted on Sunday.

stories.title: Fico joins Orbán in demanding the EU lift Russian energy sanctions — a week before Hungary’s election that could end Orbán’s 16-year rule
stories.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico joined Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán in demanding the EU lift sanctions on Russian energy. Fico called for restoring Druzhba pipeline flows, with critics noting the revenues fund Russia's war against Ukraine. Hungary faces elections that could end Orbán's 16-year rule.

stories.title: Drones attack Russia's Leningrad and Nizhny Novgorod regions: Oil refinery on fire, pipeline damaged
stories.summary: Drone strikes hit Russia's Leningrad and Nizhny Novgorod regions on April 5. An oil pipeline near the port of Primorsk in the Leningrad region was damaged, and a fire broke out at a facility in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

stories.title: US aviator missing after Iran shot down fighter jet has been rescued
stories.summary: A US military aviator who went missing after Iran shot down an American fighter jet has been rescued. The incident occurred during the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Iran FM Araghchi warns of contamination risk after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Bushehr nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that continued U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Bushehr nuclear power plant on Iran's southern coast could cause radioactive fallout reaching Gulf Cooperation Council capitals. He noted Bushehr is closer to Kuwait, Bahrain, and Qatar than to Tehran.

stories.title: Lebanon: In the city of Tyre, Christians mark Easter in a ghost town
stories.summary: In the southern Lebanese city of Tyre, Christians marked Easter amid near-deserted streets after Israel's military renewed strikes following evacuation warnings. Nearby attacks damaged a hospital.

stories.title: Khairpur sees mpox outbreak as seven babies test positive
stories.summary: An mpox outbreak in Khairpur, Sindh, Pakistan, has killed at least four newborns, with seven babies testing positive for the zoonotic viral infection. Health officials suspect contamination from unsterilized hospital equipment, and the Sukkur commissioner ordered comprehensive contact tracing.

stories.title: Ramstein: Controversy in Germany over military base's role in Middle East war
stories.summary: The US airbase at Ramstein, Germany, is playing a key role in coordinating American military operations in the Middle East war, sparking controversy despite Berlin's insistence that Germany is not a party to the conflict in Iran.

stories.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: PAKISTAN’S PRAGMATIC TURN
stories.summary: Pakistan is pursuing a foreign policy of principled multipolarity and strategic dynamism as the international order shifts from unipolarity to a more fragmented multipolar system. The country is positioning itself as a regional economic hub amid global instability.

stories.title: Sri Lanka struggles to avert economic collapse over Mideast war
stories.summary: Sri Lanka is working to prevent a repeat of its 2022 economic collapse as the prolonged Middle East war and the aftermath of a deadly November cyclone compound the country's financial pressures.

stories.title: Why crisis-hit Asia is unlikely to embrace Trump’s America 250 party
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump appointed Australian-American social media figure Nick Adams as special presidential envoy for American tourism, exceptionalism, and values ahead of major events including America's 250th anniversary, the FIFA World Cup, and the Olympics.

stories.title: Several people killed in Ukraine after a Russian drone strike on a market
stories.summary: Russia launched 286 long-range drones at Ukraine overnight from Friday to Saturday, with Ukrainian forces intercepting 260 of them. A Russian drone strike on a market in Ukraine killed several people.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran, gives deadline for Hormuz to be reopened
stories.summary: US President Trump issued a deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He also confirmed that a second US pilot had been rescued inside Iran, while Iranian media reported five people were killed during the operation.

stories.title: Trump confirms rescue of second US pilot as five Iranians killed
stories.summary: President Trump confirmed the rescue of the second U.S. pilot downed in Iran. Iranian media reported that five Iranians were killed during the rescue operation.

stories.title: Crowds march with giant phalluses at Japan’s fertility festival
stories.summary: Crowds gathered near Tokyo on Sunday for the annual Kanamara fertility festival, which featured giant phallus-shaped portable shrines and penis-themed confections parading through the streets. The event blends ancient Japanese tradition with modern efforts to break social taboos around sexuality.

stories.title: Russian drone damages enterprise in Poltava region
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck and damaged a company building in Ukraine's Poltava region. Further details on casualties or the specific enterprise were not immediately provided.

stories.title: War in Lebanon: Art to provide psychological support to children
stories.summary: As Israeli strikes continue in Lebanon, children are experiencing significant psychological trauma. Art therapy programs are being deployed to provide emotional support and a means of expression for affected children.

stories.title: US President Trump gives Iran 48 hours to open Strait of Hormuz, Iran rejects
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz or face severe consequences, which Tehran rejected. The ultimatum came as US and Iranian forces searched for a downed American airman.

stories.title: Countdown to Trump’s 48-hour Ultimatum - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article discusses the approaching deadline of President Trump's 48-hour ultimatum directed at Iran, examining whether it will lead to a decisive military strike or a last-minute diplomatic deal.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: US rescues pilot from downed fighter jet
stories.summary: US military forces rescued the pilot of an American fighter jet shot down over Iran during the ongoing Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Emerging dilemmas
stories.summary: Pakistan faces multiple simultaneous security challenges, including tensions with Afghanistan, pressures from the Iran-U.S. war, and renewed friction with India as the anniversary of a previous bilateral military standoff approaches.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A morning briefing summarized overnight escalations across the Middle East, including the rescue of the second downed F-15E crew member in Iran, strikes on infrastructure in multiple countries, and rising civilian casualties in the region.

stories.title: Iran command rejects Trump's ‘helpless, nervous’ ultimatum
stories.summary: General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters rejected President Trump's ultimatum, calling it a "helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action." The statement came in response to Trump's 48-hour deadline for Iran to reach a deal.

stories.title: A Hollywood Midrash- The Making of the Prince of Egypt - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article examines the production of the animated film "The Prince of Egypt" and its significance as a piece of Passover-related cultural work.

stories.title: Red-Green Alliance Explained, w/ Hussein Mansour & Izabella Tabarovsk - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article explores the concept of the "Red-Green Alliance," described as an ideological convergence between the radical left and political Islamists, featuring commentary from Hussein Aboubakr Mansour and Izabella Tabarovsky.

stories.title: Iranian drone attack sparks fire at Shuwaikh Oil Complex in Kuwait
stories.summary: An Iranian drone attack caused a fire at the Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex in Kuwait. No injuries were reported from the strike.

stories.title: War update: 149 clashes on front lines in past day
stories.summary: Ukrainian military officials recorded 149 combat engagements between Ukrainian and Russian forces along the front lines on Saturday, April 4.

stories.title: Flopped war could lead to chaos
stories.summary: The White House imposed a media blackout as President Trump met with his national security team after U.S. forces suffered significant aerial losses in the Persian Gulf, including an F-15 shot down over Iran and an A-10 downed over the Gulf. An F-16 was also hit but returned to base.

stories.title: Passover under the shadow of war: the challenge of hope - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The article discusses the challenge of observing Passover amid ongoing war, grief, and political division in Israel.

stories.title: UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait lose water, energy infrastructure to Iran strikes
stories.summary: Iranian drone and missile strikes damaged civilian energy and water infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Kuwait. Iran accused its Gulf neighbors of allowing US forces to launch attacks from their territories.

stories.title: Kuwait’s power, water plants damaged as Iran keeps attacking Gulf states
stories.summary: Iranian attacks damaged power and water plants in Kuwait. Bahrain and the UAE also reported Iranian strikes that caused fires, though authorities in both countries said the blazes were extinguished quickly.

stories.title: Is the Iran War bringing Israel and the UAE closer together? - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Emirati officials suggested that the confrontation with Iran could strengthen ties between the UAE and Israel. However, if the Iranian regime survives the war intact, the UAE may adopt a more cautious diplomatic stance.

stories.title: Ukraine air defenses down 76 of 93 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces shot down 76 of 93 Russian drones launched since the evening of April 4. Enemy strikes were recorded at ten locations across the country.

stories.title: Israel’s attack on UNRWA is central to its genocide of the Palestinians
stories.summary: The article discusses Israel's ongoing campaign against UNRWA, the UN agency mandated to provide services to Palestinian refugees. It frames the dismantling of UNRWA as integral to Israeli policy toward Palestinians.

stories.title: Satellite firm Planet Labs to indefinitely withhold Iran war images
stories.summary: Satellite imaging company Planet Labs announced it will indefinitely withhold imagery of Iran and the broader Middle East conflict zone. The decision was made to comply with a U.S. government request.

stories.title: Bannu bombing
stories.summary: A suicide bombing struck the Domel police station in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing at least five civilians from the same family. Separately, law enforcement in Lakki Marwat's Bittani area foiled a planned suicide attack on a police station and captured suspected terrorists.

stories.title: In Iran, social media posts noted explosions, aircraft in area US jet was downed
stories.summary: Social media posts from Iran reported explosions and aircraft activity near the city of Yasuj in central Iran, where a US F-15 jet was downed. About an hour later, President Trump confirmed that US forces had recovered a second missing airman.

stories.title: Gulf war erodes 90pc investment in T-bills
stories.summary: The ongoing Gulf war has led to the withdrawal of 90 percent of foreign investment in Pakistani treasury bills, according to State Bank of Pakistan data. Despite attractive returns of 11.5 percent, investor confidence has been undermined by more than 35 days of conflict in the region.

stories.title: Injury toll from Russian drone attack on Odesa rises to three
stories.summary: The injury toll from a Russian overnight drone attack on Odesa rose to three people. Residential buildings in the Khadzhybeyskyi district sustained damage.

stories.title: Iranian missile fragments damage MK Gafni's Bnei Brak house, none injured
stories.summary: Fragments from an Iranian missile struck the Bnei Brak home of Israeli lawmaker Moshe Gafni, causing damage but no injuries. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Gafni following the incident.

stories.title: ‘ME war compounds Asia humanitarian crises’
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that the Middle East escalation since February is generating spillover effects across Asia and the Pacific, raising fuel, power, and agricultural input costs in import-dependent countries including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh. UNOCHA also sought $151 million for Pakistan flood response targeting 1.9 million people.

stories.title: Thousands rally in Iraq against ‘senseless’ US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Thousands of protesters rallied in Iraq against the U.S.-Israeli military campaign targeting Iran. Demonstrators chanted against the U.S. and Israel and called on the international community to intervene in the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,180 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russia lost approximately 1,180 troops killed or wounded over the past 24 hours in its war against Ukraine, bringing estimated total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to roughly 1,303,550 personnel as of April 5, 2026.

stories.title: Former Co-op boss was paid almost £2m before leaving after group’s difficult year
stories.summary: Former Co-op Group CEO Shirine Khoury-Haq received a total pay package of £1.9 million in 2025 before her departure, including a £165,000 bonus, despite the retailer suffering a damaging cyber-attack and an underlying loss of £125 million.

stories.title: Growing Pains meets the ‘kill line’: a new Chinese hot take on the American dream
stories.summary: Chinese state media has revisited the 1990s American sitcom Growing Pains, which once served as many Chinese viewers' first glimpse of US middle-class life. The reappraisal reframes the show's depiction of suburban stability through a more critical lens of contemporary American society.

stories.title: How changes in home rental laws in England will impact Hong Kong, mainland investors
stories.summary: Proposed changes to home rental laws in England and Wales include a cap on ground rents for leasehold homeowners, which analysts say could benefit foreign investors, including those from Hong Kong and mainland China. However, tighter rent-setting rules are dampening demand ahead of implementation. An estimated 203,000 homes in the region are registered to overseas owners.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit hospital, homes in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes hit buildings and a major hospital in the southern Lebanese city of Tyre. Indonesia received the bodies of three of its UN peacekeepers killed in Lebanon, while Israeli forces destroyed 17 surveillance cameras linked to a UN agency office in Naqura.

stories.title: Trump seeks to end the war without it becoming ‘an abject failure’
stories.summary: Barbara Slavin of the Stimson Center said President Trump misread the situation in Iran and is now seeking a way to conclude the conflict without it being seen as a failure.

stories.title: Video: Israeli activist arrested as police disperse anti-war protest
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested activist Alon-Lee Green, a leader of the Jewish-Arab movement Standing Together, during an anti-war protest in Tel Aviv. Officers forcibly dispersed demonstrators who were opposing Israel's military operations in Gaza and across the region.

stories.title: Sisters of officer killed by Dezi Freeman plan to sue police for negligence, lawyer says
stories.summary: The sisters of Neal Thompson, a Victoria police officer fatally shot by Dezi Freeman in Porepunkah, Australia, last August, plan to sue Victoria police for negligence. Lawyer Jeremy King confirmed the claim would be brought after a coronial inquest into the officers' deaths.

stories.title: Israeli strike in south Lebanon kills displaced family including three children
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the town of Kfar Hatta in southern Lebanon killed a displaced family of five, including three children, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The family had fled from Kfar Tibnit in the Nabatieh district seeking safety.

stories.title: US president weighs broader cabinet shake-up
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is reportedly considering a broader cabinet reshuffle following Attorney General Pam Bondi's removal, driven by frustration over political fallout from the war with Iran. The conflict has caused rising gas prices and declining approval ratings ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Under Israeli restrictions, Palestinian Christians mark quiet Holy Week
stories.summary: Israeli authorities imposed restrictions in Jerusalem during Holy Week, leaving the Christian Quarter largely empty and forcing businesses to close. Palestinian Christians marked the occasion under constrained conditions.

stories.title: Fires reported at Abu Dhabi’s petrochemical plant, operations halted
stories.summary: Multiple fires broke out at the Borouge petrochemical plant in Abu Dhabi after debris from aerial interceptions fell on the facility. Operations were immediately suspended pending a damage assessment. No injuries were reported.

stories.title: Iran executes two men for breaking into a military base during January’s protests
stories.summary: Iran executed Mohammad-Amin Biglari and Shahin Vahedparast, who were convicted of breaking into a military base during January's anti-government protests. Authorities said the men attempted to steal weapons and military equipment.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 37 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the rescue of a US crew member who had been missing after Iran shot down an American fighter jet on day 37 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim cluster missile attack on Israel’s Ben Gurion airport
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces claimed responsibility for a cluster missile strike targeting Israel's Ben Gurion airport in Jaffa, according to the group's military spokesman.

stories.title: Over 100,000 sq km of Ukrainian land still potentially dangerous due to mines – Presidential Office
stories.summary: Ukraine's Presidential Office reported that over 100,000 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory remain potentially hazardous due to landmines and unexploded ordnance from the ongoing war.

stories.title: Tehran says Islamabad talks depend on terms
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied rejecting Islamabad as a venue for U.S.-Iran negotiations, stating that Tehran's participation depends on the terms and conditions offered. Pakistan has been facilitating diplomatic efforts between the two sides.

stories.title: CONFLICT: BOMBING TRUST
stories.summary: Ali Larijani, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, was killed in an Israeli airstrike on March 17, 2026. The latest round of US-Israeli military strikes on Iran began while Tehran was engaged in nuclear negotiations with Washington.

stories.title: Aid groups warn Iran war is hindering food and medicine from reaching millions
stories.summary: The United Nations described the Iran war's impact on supply chains as the most significant disruption since COVID-19, with shipment costs rising up to 20% and widespread delays as goods are rerouted away from conflict zones.

stories.title: Hong Kong rescuers search for man, 81, who went missing on hike in Tuen Mun
stories.summary: Hong Kong rescue teams are searching for an 81-year-old man surnamed He who went missing while hiking along Section 10 of the MacLehose Trail near Tai Lam Chung Reservoir in Tuen Mun. Authorities found one of his shoes roughly 20 hours into the operation after he became separated from his wife on Saturday.

stories.title: Fewer Russian drones last night. That’s when Ukraine starts watching the skies more carefully
stories.summary: After recent massive Russian drone attacks involving up to 542 drones, Russia launched 93 drones against Ukraine overnight on April 4–5. Analysts noted the dip may precede a surge attack or reflect a diversion of drone supplies to Iran.

stories.title: Crew member from downed US fighter jet rescued in 'miraculous' operation, says Trump
