stories.summary: Ukraine's 199th Air Assault Forces Training Center has adapted its program to focus on life-saving skills suited to modern warfare, according to its commander. The curriculum changes reflect evolving battlefield conditions in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Health ministry: 21 injured in Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: At least 21 people were wounded in Israeli air strikes on the town of Ma'raka and the Al-Housh area in southern Lebanon, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Health. Israel also struck the town of Qatrani in the Jezzine district. Hezbollah said it fired missiles at an Israeli position near Maroun al-Ras.

stories.title: Iran executes two members of banned opposition group
stories.summary: Iran executed two members of the banned opposition group People's Mujahedin of Iran (MEK). The two were convicted of actions aimed at overthrowing the Islamic Republic. The executions came as Tehran has stepped up the use of capital punishment amid its ongoing war with Israel and the United States.

stories.title: ‘The frontline is like Terminator’: fighting robots give Ukraine hope in war with Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine's use of unmanned ground vehicles on the front lines has grown exponentially since spring 2024, turning the conflict with Russia into an increasingly technological contest. The battery-powered land robots come in various configurations, including tracked and wheeled variants, some carrying anti-tank mines.

stories.title: China team releases world’s first bamboo drone flight control software – for free
stories.summary: Researchers at Northwestern Polytechnical University in China released what they describe as the world's first open-source flight control software designed for bamboo-frame drones. The system aims to address challenges of integrating non-traditional materials like bamboo into low-cost, eco-friendly unmanned aerial vehicles.

stories.title: Chinese woman whose pet dog was poisoned, killed by neighbour, sacrifices job for the cause
stories.summary: A Beijing woman named Li Yihan publicly revealed her identity after dedicating years to seeking justice for her pet dog Papi, a West Highland Terrier poisoned and killed by a neighbor in 2022. Police identified a 65-year-old man surnamed Zhang as the suspect.

stories.title: Karachi, other Sindh cities set new weather records for April
stories.summary: Karachi recorded 38.7 millimetres of rain in 24 hours, breaking a 41-year-old April rainfall record. Several cities across Pakistan's Sindh province also set new records for lowest nighttime and daytime temperatures. The Met Office warned of additional rain spells in the coming days.

stories.title: US intelligence warns Iran unlikely to ease Hormuz Strait chokehold soon, sources say
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence assessments indicate Iran is unlikely to relinquish control of the Strait of Hormuz soon, according to three sources familiar with the reports. Analysts believe Iran views its grip on the critical oil shipping route as its primary leverage against the United States.

stories.title: Video: US aircraft search for pilots after fighter jet shot down in Iran
stories.summary: Footage circulated online showing US planes and helicopters searching for crew members after a US F-15E fighter jet was shot down over Khuzestan province in central Iran. One crew member was reportedly recovered while the other remained missing.

stories.title: Divisions grow as US senator sets conditions on war funding
stories.summary: Republican Senator John Curtis of Utah said he cannot support funding for further US military operations against Iran without a formal congressional declaration of war. Curtis said he backs President Trump's campaign but insists on constitutional authorization.

stories.title: Debris fall in Dubai marina after aerial interception, one killed by shrapnel in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Debris from intercepted Iranian drones fell on buildings in Dubai Marina and damaged houses in Sitra, Bahrain, injuring four people. Separately, one person was killed and four wounded by shrapnel in an attack on Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Ukrainian Film Days will be held in Vilnius in April
stories.summary: The city of Vilnius, Lithuania, will host "Days of Ukrainian Cinema" from April 9 to 12, showcasing recent Ukrainian films to local audiences and the Ukrainian community in the Lithuanian capital.

stories.title: First Western vessel crosses Hormuz amid tight restrictions
stories.summary: A French ship became the first Western vessel to transit the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US-Iran war, passing through after weeks of Iranian restrictions. Iran has selectively allowed vessels from countries it considers friendly while blocking those linked to the US, Israel, and the UK.

stories.title: Health Ministry reveals wartime preparations in Eilat, Dead Sea amid tense security situation
stories.summary: Israel's Ministry of Health revealed wartime preparations in Eilat and the Dead Sea region, including increasing around-the-clock medical teams and intensive care unit capacity amid heightened security tensions.

stories.title: Dubai Media Office confirms debris strike on Internet City building
stories.summary: Dubai authorities confirmed that debris from an aerial interception struck the facade of the Oracle building in Dubai Internet City. Emergency services responded to the incident. Oracle had appeared on a list of US companies identified by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Could Paramount acquisition of CNN shift coverage of Israel?
stories.summary: Paramount's potential acquisition of CNN could place two major US news companies under the leadership of the Ellison-led firm. Analysts are examining whether the merger might affect editorial coverage of Israel and the broader Middle East, as the deal would expand an already growing media empire.

stories.title: Israel targets Iran-backed Hezbollah sites in Lebanon in fresh strikes
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck what it described as Hezbollah infrastructure in Beirut and destroyed a bridge in eastern Lebanon to block reinforcements. At least two explosions were heard in Beirut early Saturday, with smoke rising from the southern suburbs, an area repeatedly targeted in recent days.

stories.title: Iran's Ghalibaf raises questions over another global shipping route
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X highlighting the strategic importance of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, raising concerns about potential disruption to another key global shipping chokepoint amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Police investigate Lahav 433 officer accused of sexually harassing subordinate policewoman - report
stories.summary: Israeli police are investigating a Lahav 433 unit officer accused of making sexually explicit statements toward a subordinate policewoman, according to a report by Israeli broadcaster KAN.

stories.title: Live: Several blasts heard coming from northern Tehran
stories.summary: Several blasts were heard in northern Tehran on Saturday as the Middle East conflict neared its sixth week. Simultaneously, Iranian and American forces continued racing to recover a missing crew member from a U.S. warplane shot down by Iran.

stories.title: Damage reported as missiles hit residential areas in central Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile attack caused damage to residential areas in central Israel, injuring one person in Tel Aviv. Reports indicated cluster munitions were used during the strike, with a residential building in Rosh HaAyin among the sites hit.

stories.title: Rockets fired at Israeli position near Maroun al-Ras, Hezbollah says
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it fired rockets at an Israeli helicopter landing pad near the border town of Maroun al-Ras in southern Lebanon. The group described it as its fifth announced attack of the day. Israeli forces also carried out an air raid on al-Qatrani in the Jezzine district.

stories.title: ‘Over the top and fun:’ TGI Fridays boss insists time is right for a UK revival
stories.summary: Ray Blanchette, whose family firm Sugarloaf rescued TGI Fridays from administration in 2025, has outlined plans to revive the chain's UK business. The company retained 33 UK restaurants but closed 16 locations, resulting in 456 job losses, while pursuing a global expansion target of 1,000 outlets.

stories.title: Victoria police arrest two people as part of Dezi Freeman investigation
stories.summary: Victoria Police arrested a man and a woman at separate properties in the state's north-east as part of the investigation into fugitive Dezi Freeman. Freeman had survived on the run for seven months before being shot dead by police the previous week. The two suspects are being interviewed about how they may have aided his evasion.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: US and Iranian forces race to recover missing pilot from downed jet; Israel bombards Beirut
stories.summary: U.S. and Iranian forces are racing to recover a missing pilot from an F-15E jet confirmed shot down over southwestern Iran. Israel simultaneously carried out airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure in Beirut, Lebanon. Iran also fired missiles at central Israel, with Israeli forces working to intercept them.

stories.title: NASA unveils first images of Earth from Artemis II
stories.summary: NASA released the first photographs of Earth captured by the Artemis II crew as they travel toward the Moon.

stories.title: Iran, US race to recover missing crew member of crashed American fighter jet
stories.summary: Iranian and U.S. forces are racing to recover a missing crew member from an American F-15 warplane shot down by Iran on Friday. U.S. media reported that special forces rescued one of the two crew members.

stories.title: Iran downs US fighter jet, raising stakes in war
stories.summary: Iran shot down a U.S. fighter jet, escalating the ongoing conflict. One American crew member was rescued, while the other remains missing.

stories.title: Behind enemy lines: How US Air Force's well-oiled rescue machine operates
stories.summary: The US Air Force maintains a combat search-and-rescue capability developed since the Vietnam War, having successfully recovered thousands of downed aircrew in hostile territory including in Iraq and Bosnia using specialized helicopters and survival equipment.

stories.title: U.S.-Iran cease-fire talks have stalled, WSJ reports
stories.summary: Cease-fire negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled after Tehran officially informed mediators it is unwilling to meet US officials in Islamabad and considers American demands unacceptable, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

stories.title: Russian strike hits vet clinic near Kyiv, leaving dozens of animals dead
stories.summary: A Russian strike hit a veterinary clinic in Chabany, near Kyiv, killing dozens of animals during the massive attack on April 3. Ukraine's State Emergency Service conducted evacuation operations to rescue surviving animals from the damaged facility.

stories.title: 14 dead as Russia launches new daytime attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian forces killed at least 14 people in new daytime aerial attacks on Ukraine. Moscow has intensified daytime strikes in recent weeks, departing from its previous pattern of primarily nighttime bombardments during the four-year invasion.

stories.title: Safety fears bloom in Japan as ageing cherry trees collapse in Tokyo parks
stories.summary: In Tokyo, ageing Somei Yoshino cherry blossom trees, many planted during Japan's post-war growth in the 1960s, are increasingly collapsing. Two trees fell on Thursday at Kinuta Park and the Chidorigafuchi greenway, raising safety concerns during the popular cherry blossom season.

stories.title: Amber rainstorm warning in Hong Kong, with thunderstorms expected over weekend
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning on Saturday morning as thunderstorms were forecast for the weekend. Rain was particularly heavy in Tai Po district. The amber alert is the lowest tier in Hong Kong's three-level rainstorm warning system.

stories.title: Two U.S. aircraft shot down as war in Iran escalates; at least one crew member is missing
stories.summary: Two US aircraft have been shot down amid the escalating war in Iran, with at least one crew member reported missing. Iranian state media said a US A-10 attack aircraft crashed in the Persian Gulf after being struck by Iranian defense forces.

stories.title: Second Israeli air strike hits Beirut suburbs within an hour
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes carried out two airstrikes within an hour on the southern suburbs of Beirut, according to Al Jazeera. The Israeli military said it was targeting Hezbollah infrastructure in the Lebanese capital, though details on casualties were not immediately available.

stories.title: Iraqi group claims 19 attacks on 'enemy bases' in 24 hours
stories.summary: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed it carried out 19 operations using drones and missiles against "enemy bases" in Iraq and the wider region over 24 hours. Hezbollah separately said it targeted the Liman barracks north of Nahariya with attack drones.

stories.title: Iran’s military claims shooting down second US jet while hunt for crew of downed F-15 aircraft continues
stories.summary: Iran's military claimed it shot down a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle over southwestern Iran and a U.S. A-10 ground attack aircraft over the Gulf. American and Iranian forces raced to recover the F-15 crew, with U.S. media reporting one of two crew members was rescued by special forces. The pilot of the downed A-10 was also reportedly rescued.

stories.title: Second air strike hits PMF base in western Iraq
stories.summary: Air strikes targeted two headquarters of Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces, hitting a PMF base in al-Qaim in western Iraq and the PMF's 34th Brigade in Mosul. No immediate casualties were reported from either strike.

stories.title: Russian oil terminals under attack unable to accept shipments for second week, sources say
stories.summary: Russia's Baltic oil export terminals at Ust-Luga and Primorsk have been unable to handle shipments for a second consecutive week following Ukrainian drone attacks. Russian refineries are seeking alternative export routes due to the disruption.

stories.title: KMB told to probe machines that gave free bus rides as revised HK$2 scheme launched
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government ordered bus operator KMB to investigate a malfunction in its fare rebate machines that gave passengers free rides on the day a revised HK$2 transport subsidy scheme launched. KMB will be responsible for covering the cost of the accidental extra rebates provided to passengers.

stories.title: In a time of war, Chinese museums are a safe haven for ancient treasures of Iran
stories.summary: Iranian artifacts, including glassware and Persian carpets, are on display at the Inner Mongolia Museum in Hohhot, China, where they are safe from potential damage in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The exhibition, running since December, has drawn growing attention since the start of the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Pope Leo's Good Friday service offers prayer for deported children
stories.summary: Pope Leo led a Good Friday candlelit service at Rome's Colosseum attended by thousands of Catholics. The service included prayers for war orphans and deported immigrant children, along with a message to world leaders that their decisions will face divine judgment.

stories.title: Second US plane crashes in Gulf after F-15 downed, NYT says
stories.summary: A U.S. A-10 Warthog crashed near the Strait of Hormuz after being targeted, according to The New York Times. The incident occurred as American forces continued searching for the pilots of an F-15E previously downed over Iran.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 36 of US-Israeli attacks?
stories.summary: Iran claimed it shot down two US warplanes, and a search operation is under way for a missing crew member amid ongoing US-Israeli military operations against Iran on day 36 of the conflict.

stories.title: Connecticut school punishes students for antisemitic posts against hockey rivals
stories.summary: A Catholic school in Connecticut disciplined students who made antisemitic social media posts targeting a rival hockey team from New Canaan, including slurs referencing Jewish identity.

stories.title: Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashes in Crimea
stories.summary: A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in Russian-occupied Crimea. The aircraft's crew ejected and survived. No additional details about the cause of the crash were immediately provided.

stories.title: Electricity tariffs may rise by 20% this summer – expert
stories.summary: An expert warned that household electricity tariffs in Ukraine could rise by approximately 20% as early as summer 2026. The potential increase reflects ongoing pressures on Ukraine's energy infrastructure amid the war.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia alert lifted as sirens sound in Bahrain
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil defence briefly issued a warning to residents in the Eastern Province before lifting the alert without providing details. In neighboring Bahrain, sirens were activated and the interior ministry urged citizens to seek shelter.

stories.title: Pentagon: 13 US troops killed, 365 wounded in Iran war
stories.summary: The Pentagon reported that at least 13 US service members have been killed and 365 wounded in the war in Iran. Casualties span all military branches, with 247 Army soldiers, 63 Navy sailors, 19 Marines, and 36 Air Force airmen among the wounded.

stories.title: More than 200 strikes reported across Iran in 24 hours, rights group says
stories.summary: A US-based rights group reported more than 206 strikes across 13 Iranian provinces over 24 hours, killing at least one civilian. The group said US-Israeli attacks since the war began on February 28 have killed 1,607 civilians and 1,213 military personnel, though figures could not be independently verified.

stories.title: NASA Artemis II crew captures Earth’s brilliant blue beauty as they rocket to moon
stories.summary: The NASA Artemis II crew photographed Earth through their capsule window as they traveled toward the Moon. By Friday afternoon, they were more than 110,000 miles from Earth and are expected to pass the Moon by Monday.

stories.title: Debris from interception hits Dubai Marina building, no injuries reported
stories.summary: Debris from an aerial interception fell onto a building in Dubai Marina, with authorities reporting no fire or injuries. Separately, one person was killed and four wounded in an attack on Abu Dhabi's Habshan gas processing facility, the UAE's largest natural gas site.

stories.title: London mayor’s protection officers relieved of duties after bag of guns ‘misplaced’
stories.summary: Armed police officers guarding London Mayor Sadiq Khan were relieved of duty after a bag containing an MP5 carbine, a Glock pistol, a taser, and ammunition was left outside his home in south London. The bag was found by a member of the public on Tuesday evening.

stories.title: Trio facing arson charges over UK Jewish ambulance attack
stories.summary: Three men have been charged with arson in connection with an attack on ambulances operated by Hatzola, a Jewish emergency medical service, in north London.

stories.title: Iranian missile attack hits residential areas in central Israel
stories.summary: Iranian missiles struck residential areas in central Israel, causing damage, according to Israeli media reports.

stories.title: IDF extends time reservists must serve this year, amid Iran and Hezbollah wars
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces extended mandatory reserve duty from six weeks to nine weeks for 2026, citing mounting manpower shortages amid concurrent conflicts with Iran and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Iran’s military claims shooting down second US jet as hunt for crew of downed F-15 aircraft continues
stories.summary: Iranian forces shot down a U.S. F-15 fighter jet over Iranian territory, the first confirmed downing of a crewed American aircraft since the war began. American and Iranian forces raced to recover the crew, with one of two members reportedly rescued by U.S. special forces. Iran also claimed to have downed a U.S. A-10 Warthog near the Gulf.

stories.title: Second US fighter jet downed in Persian Gulf, pilot rescued after ejection
stories.summary: A second US fighter jet, an A-10, was downed in the Persian Gulf, with the sole pilot safely rescued after ejecting. Tehran claimed the shootdown as its second successful strike on a US aircraft within 24 hours.

stories.title: Explosion rocks Khartoum, police blame war-era landmine
stories.summary: A large explosion occurred in Khartoum, Sudan, which police attributed to a landmine left over from the country's war. Authorities reported no casualties from the blast.

stories.title: ‘Space plumber’ to the rescue as Artemis astronauts navigate life aboard Orion
stories.summary: The four-person crew of NASA's Artemis mission is traveling toward the Moon aboard the Orion spacecraft, managing both historic milestones and everyday challenges. Mission specialist Christina Koch became the first woman to venture into deep space. The crew has dealt with technical issues including a broken toilet and crashed email systems.

stories.title: Industrial zone damaged in Negev, falls in Sharon area after Iran fires missiles towards Israel
stories.summary: Missile shrapnel from an Iranian attack fell on an industrial site in Israel's Negev region, according to police. Additional missile debris landed in the Sharon area, with Israeli media reporting no hazardous material leaks.

stories.title: Guerrillas conducted reconnaissance of military airfield in Novofedorivka, Crimea
stories.summary: Agents of the ATESH partisan movement conducted detailed reconnaissance of a Russian military airfield near the town of Saky in the village of Novofedorivka in occupied Crimea. The facility is one of the key air bases used by Russia's Aerospace Forces on the peninsula.

stories.title: Cluster bomb attack collapses building in Israel, electricity line damaged
stories.summary: An Iranian cluster bomb attack caused a building to collapse in Ramat Gan, Israel, according to fire services. The strike also damaged a high-voltage electricity line in Rosh Ha'ayin, causing power outages. A fire from an earlier ballistic missile impact was reported at the Neot Hovav industrial zone in the Negev.

stories.title: ‘Silence’ stonewalls Pakistan-led US-Iran talks initiative
stories.summary: A Pakistan-led initiative to facilitate U.S.-Iran talks has stalled, with Tehran yet to formally respond to dialogue proposals despite back-channel exchanges. A senior Pakistani official told Dawn that while some ground had been covered relaying messages, Iran's silence has slowed momentum.

stories.title: Sydney councils fear new datacentres could cause blackouts, block housing and affect locals’ health
stories.summary: Several Sydney councils told a New South Wales inquiry that datacentre developments are competing with residential housing near public transport and contributing to local power blackouts. Councils raised concerns about health, environmental, and amenity impacts on surrounding communities.

stories.title: Iran reports mounting casualties as strikes intensify
stories.summary: The death toll from a US-Israeli strike on the B1 bridge between Tehran and Karaj rose to 13. Strikes also damaged Shahid Beheshti University and the Pasteur Institute in Tehran. Iran's health ministry reported at least 2,076 casualties as attacks hit cities including Isfahan, Qom, and Kermanshah.

stories.title: Here comes the ‘Mounjaro bride’: Indian women turn to weight-loss drug before wedding
stories.summary: Clinics in India are marketing weight-loss drug Mounjaro as part of pre-wedding transformation packages for brides and grooms. New Delhi's Klarity Skin Clinic offers a "Mounjaro bride" package combining the injectable medication with guided nutrition and workouts. The trend reflects growing demand for rapid weight-loss solutions before weddings.

stories.title: Air strike targets Iraqi paramilitary headquarters in Mosul
stories.summary: An air strike hit the headquarters of the 34th Brigade of Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces in Mosul, with no immediate casualties reported. The PMF is part of Iraq's state security apparatus and includes factions aligned with Iran.

stories.title: Voices Israel anthology 2025: Celebrating English poetry shaped by war, love, and memory
stories.summary: The Voices Israel 2025 anthology features English-language poetry from global contributors, with themes shaped by war, love, memory, and the aftermath of the October 7 attacks.

stories.title: Damage spreads across central Israel after missile interceptions
stories.summary: Fragments from intercepted Iranian missiles caused damage across 17 sites in central Israel, injuring one person in Bnei Brak. A building collapsed in Ramat Gan, significant damage and power outages were reported in Rosh HaAyin, and debris was found near a kindergarten.

stories.title: Pakistan to return $3.5bn UAE debt before month end: official
stories.summary: Pakistan decided to repay $3.5 billion in debt to the United Arab Emirates before the end of the month, after Abu Dhabi sought immediate return of the funds. A senior official said the repayment would significantly draw down foreign exchange reserves but was necessary to uphold national dignity.

stories.title: Evacuations ordered as two wildfires break out in southern California
stories.summary: Two wildfires erupted in southern California on Friday amid strong winds with gusts up to 50 mph. The Springs fire threatened Moreno Valley while the smaller Crown fire also burned nearby. The National Weather Service issued wind advisories as the fires marked the region's first significant blazes following a major spring heatwave.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut, US warns Iran may hit Lebanese universities
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out airstrikes on Beirut on Friday, targeting what the military described as militant infrastructure in Lebanon's capital. Separately, the United States issued a warning that Iran may strike Lebanese universities as the broader Middle East conflict continues to escalate.

stories.title: Trump wants out of NATO. Good. Let him go.
stories.summary: Debate has emerged over the future of NATO membership, with arguments framed around European strategic autonomy rather than opposition to the United States. The discussion centers on whether a U.S. withdrawal from the alliance could benefit Europe's own defense posture.

stories.title: UN to vote on Hormuz resolution as US-Iran tensions rise
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is expected to vote next week on a Bahraini resolution to secure transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The draft would authorize countries to use "all defensive means necessary" to protect passage through the waterway. The vote has been postponed from its original Friday date.

stories.title: Competition or ‘co-opetition’: how is convergence shaping AI race between China and US?
stories.summary: Moonshot AI founder Yang Zhilin, whose Beijing-based company develops the Kimi AI models, made a surprise appearance at Nvidia's GPU Technology Conference in San Jose, California. The event highlighted ongoing debate about whether the U.S.-China AI relationship is purely competitive or involves elements of cooperation.

stories.title: South Korea and Indonesia’s KF-21 fighter jet is ready. But will it sell?
stories.summary: South Korea unveiled the first mass-produced KF-21 Boramae fighter jet at Korea Aerospace Industries' facility in Sacheon on March 25. The aircraft was jointly developed with Indonesia beginning in 2015 after a decade-long, multi-billion-dollar program. Analysts say the jet could help South Korea expand its share of the global arms market.

stories.title: Pakistan offers 30 days of free public transport following 40% petrol hike
stories.summary: Pakistan announced 30 days of free state-run public transport in its capital and most populous province after a 42.7 percent petrol price hike triggered street protests and long fuel station queues. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif subsequently scaled back the increase. The price rises were driven by the impact of the Iran war on global oil markets.

stories.title: Senators urge Trump to bar Chinese automakers from building cars in US
stories.summary: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators urged President Trump to block Chinese automakers from building vehicles in the United States. Trump had said in January he was open to Chinese car manufacturers establishing factories on U.S. soil.

stories.title: Chinese overseas need not keep to ourselves. I certainly don’t
stories.summary: A Chinese-Australian comedian's joke about leaving democracy for "fascism" in the U.S. resonated with audiences in Adelaide, reflecting a broader shift in Australian public sentiment. Analysis suggests Australia's attitudes have shifted significantly over the past five years, with views toward China warming while skepticism toward the United States has grown.

stories.title: Satellite image confirms damage to oil refinery equipment in Russia's Bashkortostan
stories.summary: Satellite imagery confirmed damage to equipment at the Bashneft-Novoil oil refinery in Ufa, the capital of Russia's Bashkortostan region, following a strike on April 2. The images verified the impact on refinery infrastructure.

stories.title: U.S. experts say American strikes on Iran may amount to war crimes
stories.summary: More than 100 international law experts from U.S. institutions including Harvard, Yale, Stanford, and the University of California have raised concerns about U.S. military conduct in Iran. They stated that actions by U.S. forces and statements by senior officials may constitute violations of international humanitarian law, including potential war crimes.

stories.title: Hezbollah attacks damage homes in north; IDF said to destroy east Lebanon bridge
stories.summary: Hezbollah attacks damaged homes in northern Israel, while the IDF reportedly destroyed a bridge in eastern Lebanon to block Hezbollah reinforcements. The Israeli military also said it carried out airstrikes on Hezbollah sites in Beirut.

stories.title: US intelligence warns Iran unlikely to ease Hormuz Strait chokehold soon, sources say
stories.summary: US intelligence assessments indicate Iran is unlikely to ease its restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz in the near term. The strait, partly controlled by Iran, carries approximately one-fifth of global oil trade.

stories.title: Why South Korea, France prefer diplomacy over force in Hormuz
stories.summary: South Korea and France agreed to cooperate on ensuring safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, with both nations favoring a diplomatic approach over military force. President Lee Jae Myung and President Emmanuel Macron discussed plans for a potential post-war defensive armada. Analysts note both countries are wary of antagonizing Iran by joining the Middle East conflict directly.

stories.title: Chinese woman spits blood on train, receives US$58,000 in donations after viral video
stories.summary: A 23-year-old woman named Hu Xinyao, who has a rare vascular condition called ANCA-associated vasculitis, received 400,000 yuan (US$58,000) in donations after a video of her spitting blood on a Chongqing subway train went viral. The footage showed her wiping the bloodstain from the floor with her own coat as she traveled to a hospital.

stories.title: Japanese, French and Omani vessels cross the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Japanese, French, and Omani naval vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's current policy permits passage through the strait for vessels belonging to nations it considers friendly.

stories.title: Russia plans to keep wartime internet controls and restrictions after war – CCD
stories.summary: Russia plans to maintain wartime internet controls and expanded security-agency powers even after the conflict in Ukraine ends, according to a report by the Centre for Countering Digital Disinformation (CCD).

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russian army records almost no territorial gains for first time since 2023, analysis shows
stories.summary: Analysis of Institute for the Study of War data shows Russia's army seized only 23 square kilometers across the entire frontline in Ukraine in March 2025, the smallest gain since 2023. Russian advances have slowed due to Ukrainian localized breakthroughs in the south-east. Meanwhile, a massive Russian drone and missile salvo killed 14 people in Ukraine on day 1,501 of the war.

stories.title: Palestinian Christians in Gaza mark Good Friday
stories.summary: Palestinian Christians in Gaza observed Good Friday at the Holy Family Church while a fragile ceasefire held in the territory.

stories.title: 'We want a voice in our land' - the people evicted to build Nigeria's capital
stories.summary: Residents displaced during the construction of Abuja, Nigeria's capital, say the government failed to honor resettlement and compensation promises made to them. The affected communities continue to demand recognition and a voice in decisions about their land.

stories.title: Nine charged over alleged conspiracy to import tonnes of cocaine and meth via ‘mother ship’ in Australian waters
stories.summary: Nine men in Australia have been charged over an alleged conspiracy to import tonnes of cocaine and methamphetamine using a "mother ship" with a drop zone in Bass Strait. Police became suspicious after a commercial trawler sank off Victoria and four crew members needed rescuing. The drugs were allegedly to be distributed nationally using trucking connections.

stories.title: Syria says Israeli tank fire kills man in country's south
stories.summary: Syrian state media reported that Israeli tank fire killed a civilian in Quneitra province near the Golan Heights. The Syrian government in Damascus condemned the attack.

stories.title: How Bombay went from a fort city to a bustling metropolis
stories.summary: A new exhibition traces Bombay's transformation from a colonial fort city into the sprawling metropolis of Mumbai. The show features paintings, photographs, and prints spanning several centuries of the city's urban development.

stories.title: Southeast Asia seeks soft power to outlast US$300 billion buzz
stories.summary: Southeast Asian countries are investing in cultural soft power, with films like Indonesian director Joko Anwar's Ghost in the Cell premiering at the Berlin International Film Festival. The horror-comedy was praised by Variety for addressing societal anxieties about corruption and environmental destruction. The region is seeking cultural influence to outlast a US$300 billion economic buzz.

stories.title: Australia’s 180-degree shift from 5 years ago: China in favour; US out
stories.summary: Australian public sentiment has shifted markedly over the past five years, with growing warmth toward China and increasing skepticism toward the United States. Meetings with national-level officials and cultural events in Adelaide illustrated the changing dynamics in Australia's foreign policy orientation.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran downs 2 US warplanes; Israel bombs Lebanon bridges
stories.summary: Iran's military celebrated after claiming it downed two US warplanes, saying the strikes demonstrated its continued fighting capability. Separately, Israel bombed bridges in Lebanon.

stories.title: Regional effort to broker ceasefire between US and Iran reportedly hits dead end
stories.summary: Regional efforts to broker a ceasefire between the US and Iran have reportedly stalled, with Qatar resisting pressure to serve as mediator. Israel reportedly assesses the war will continue for at least two more weeks, and US intelligence believes Iran is unlikely to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Opinion: Iran war: Why US allies are suffering more than its enemies
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which began on 28 February, has inflicted more severe economic consequences on Washington's European allies than on Tehran itself, despite weakening Iran being a stated objective of the operation.

stories.title: The Jewish passion for freedom and human rights was hijacked by the West - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article argued that Western human rights institutions have strayed from their founding principles. The piece claimed these organizations now reinforce hostility toward Israel rather than championing freedom.

stories.title: Video shows the moment a Russian drone hit an apartment in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia carried out a large-scale wave of air strikes across Ukraine in what has been described as an "Easter escalation," with video showing a drone hitting an apartment building.

stories.title: Iran said restoring bombed missile bunkers within hours after being struck
stories.summary: US intelligence reportedly cannot determine how many Iranian missile launchers have been destroyed, as Iran deploys decoys and restores bombed missile bunkers within hours of being struck. One person was lightly injured by shattered glass in Bnei Brak during an Iranian missile attack on Israel.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kherson again, injuring two and causing water outages
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Korabelny district of Kherson at approximately 7:45 p.m., injuring two people. The attack also caused water outages in the city.

stories.title: US fighter jet shot down over Iran, search under way for crew member, US officials say
stories.summary: A U.S. fighter jet was shot down over Iran, marking the first such incident in the nearly five-week-old conflict. Search-and-rescue operations recovered one of the two crew members who ejected, while efforts continue to locate the second. The Pentagon and U.S. Central Command have not commented.

stories.title: Shrapnel from intercepted drone injures one in Bahrain
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry reported that four people sustained minor injuries and several homes in the Sitra area were damaged by shrapnel after Iranian drones were intercepted over the country. Civil defence and ambulance teams responded to the site.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni visits Saudi Arabia, Qatar and UAE amid Gulf tensions, energy worries
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni made an unannounced trip to Saudi Arabia on Friday, with planned stops in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The visits come amid regional Gulf tensions and European concerns over energy security.

stories.title: Faced with new energy shock, Europe asks if reviving nuclear is the answer
stories.summary: European countries are reconsidering nuclear energy as a path to energy independence, as the ongoing conflict drives up natural gas and fuel prices across the continent.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni on surprise ‘energy security’ visit to Saudi Arabia, source says
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited Saudi Arabia as part of a surprise trip focused on energy security. Italy, highly dependent on energy imports, has been increasingly concerned about rising energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: WHO warns about attacks on Iran health facilities, threats
stories.summary: The World Health Organization issued a warning about multiple attacks on healthcare facilities in Iran, following strikes that damaged medical infrastructure in Tehran. The WHO raised concerns about threats to health services amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Earthquake tremors felt in several parts of north India
stories.summary: An earthquake centered in Afghanistan at a depth of 150 kilometers sent tremors across several parts of northern India. The quake also shook areas of neighboring Pakistan.

stories.title: A ‘masculinity crisis’ is brewing in UK schools, union says
stories.summary: A UK teachers' union survey found that nearly a quarter of female teachers reported being targeted by misogynistic abuse from pupils in the past 12 months, the highest proportion in four years. Union leaders described a growing "masculinity crisis" in schools, with staff left feeling traumatised and humiliated.

stories.title: ‘India is going to face a food crisis’: Farmers panic over fertiliser shortages amid Iran war
stories.summary: Farmers in Punjab, India, and Sri Lanka are reporting anxiety over fertiliser shortages linked to the conflict in Iran and its impact on oil and fertiliser supply chains. Despite government assurances of adequate stock, agricultural workers fear the disruptions could threaten the upcoming rice season and broader food security.

stories.title: US removes Russian national Mikhail Zadornov from sanctions list
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department removed sanctions on Mikhail Zadornov, a prominent Russian banker and former Russian finance minister, according to its website updated on Friday.

stories.title: MP Hetmantsev: Tax change bills must be passed, no alternative
stories.summary: Ukrainian MP Hetmantsev stated that tax reform bills must be passed, saying there is no alternative. He noted that continued cooperation with the IMF and other international partners depends on the adoption of the government's fiscal initiatives.

stories.title: Syria says Israeli tank fire kills man in country's south
stories.summary: Syrian state media reported that Israeli tank fire killed a civilian in Quneitra province in southern Syria, near the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights. State news agency SANA said the man was killed when a civilian car was struck. Syria's foreign ministry condemned the attack.

stories.title: Hide, find water: Former pilots detail how to survive being shot down
stories.summary: As US and Iranian forces race to locate a downed US F-15E crew member in Iran, former military pilots described survival tactics for personnel shot down behind enemy lines. Key priorities include hiding, finding water, and awaiting extraction.

stories.title: US warplane downed over Iran, one crew member rescued: US media
stories.summary: A U.S. warplane was downed over Iran, with one crew member rescued, according to U.S. media reports. The incident marks the first known loss of an American jet inside Iran since President Trump ordered military operations in the country.

stories.title: Congo in talks with US over third-country deportations, sources say
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is in talks with the Trump administration about receiving deportees from third countries, according to government sources in Kinshasa. This would be the latest in a series of similar agreements reached with African nations.

stories.title: Navy shipbuilding request rises nearly 50% in 2027 proposal
stories.summary: The White House's fiscal year 2027 budget proposal requests funding for nearly 20 warships, representing a roughly 50 percent increase in Navy shipbuilding spending. The proposal also includes initial funding for a new battleship class.

stories.title: US military archbishop says Iran conflict does not meet ‘just war’ standard
stories.summary: Archbishop Timothy Broglio, head of the US Catholic Archdiocese for the Military Services, stated that the American military campaign in Iran does not meet the Catholic just war standard. He told CBS News that the conflict amounts to compensating for a threat before it is fully realized.

stories.title: US fighter jet shot down over Iran, search underway for crew, US officials say
stories.summary: A U.S. fighter jet was shot down over Iran and a search-and-rescue operation is underway for survivors, two U.S. officials told Reuters. The incident is the first confirmed downing of an American aircraft since the war began approximately five weeks ago.

stories.title: Trump says he cannot comment on what US will do if missing pilot in Iran is harmed: Report
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told The Independent he could not comment on potential U.S. actions if an American pilot missing over Iran is harmed by Iranian forces. Trump expressed hope that the situation would not escalate, without detailing any planned response.

stories.title: Russians bomb Kramatorsk again, killing four and wounding two
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk region, killing four people and wounding two others.

stories.title: Majority of commodities crossing Hormuz linked to Iran: AFP analysis
stories.summary: An AFP analysis found that the majority of commodities transiting the Strait of Hormuz are linked to Iran. Tehran has maintained a stranglehold on the key shipping lane since U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28.

stories.title: WHO warns about attacks on Iran health facilities, regional threat
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned of multiple attacks on health facilities in Tehran amid the escalating Middle East conflict. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus cited a strike on the Pasteur Institute, a public health and research center, and launched an urgent appeal to support health systems in the region.

stories.title: Ukraine’s top defense market segments doubled to $6.8 Billion in 2025
stories.summary: Ukraine's top defense market segments doubled in value to $6.8 billion in 2025. The country's defense-technology sector has been described as one of the most rapidly evolving and scalable parts of Ukraine's industrial economy.

stories.title: 6.1-magnitude earthquake jolts Islamabad, KP
stories.summary: A 6.1-magnitude earthquake originating in Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region at a depth of roughly 190 kilometers struck on Friday evening. Tremors were felt across Islamabad, Peshawar, Chitral, Swat, Shangla, and Rawalpindi, according to Pakistan's Meteorological Department.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts cross halfway point between Earth and Moon
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission passed the halfway point between Earth and the Moon on Saturday, with the Orion spacecraft carrying four astronauts toward a planned lunar flyby. NASA released initial images of Earth taken from inside the spacecraft. The crew could set a record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth by humans.

stories.title: National Assembly fails to take up agenda as opposition protests fuel price hike
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Assembly was unable to proceed with its 90-item agenda on Friday after opposition members protested fuel price increases of 43% for petrol and 55% for high-speed diesel. Officials attributed the hikes to a global fuel crunch linked to the Middle East war.

stories.title: ‘A game of whack-a-mole’: how could the scam industry bring China and the US together?
stories.summary: Cambodian authorities investigated a suspected telecoms scam compound in Kampot province near the Vietnamese border, finding it recently abandoned. The discovery highlights ongoing efforts by China and the US to combat the transnational scam industry operating across Southeast Asia.

stories.title: MoD preparing measures to strengthen infantry and overhaul contract system
stories.summary: Following a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky and Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's Ministry of Defense is preparing measures to strengthen infantry units, overhaul the military contract system, and improve oversight of Special Forces incidents.

stories.title: Golden Dome, out-years and lots of missiles: Details of Trump’s $1.5T defense budget request
stories.summary: The Trump administration submitted a record-setting $1.5 trillion fiscal year 2027 defense budget request, which includes funding for the Golden Dome missile defense system and significant missile procurement across future budget years.

stories.title: Budget seeks billions for Air Force's F-47 fighter jet, just millions for Navy’s F/A-XX
stories.summary: The fiscal year 2027 budget request allocates billions of dollars for the Air Force's F-47 fighter jet program but only millions for the Navy's F/A-XX next-generation fighter. The disparity in funding levels is expected to generate debate among the Pentagon, the White House, and Congress.

stories.title: One crew member rescued from downed U.S. fighter jet over Iran: U.S. media reports
stories.summary: U.S. media reported that one of two crew members aboard a U.S. fighter jet downed over Iran has been rescued by American special operations forces. A search operation continues for the second crew member.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire talks reach standstill, say mediators - report
stories.summary: Ceasefire talks between the US and Iran have reached a standstill after Iran told mediators it is unwilling to meet US officials in Islamabad. Regional intermediaries including Egypt and Turkey are seeking alternative diplomatic pathways.

stories.title: White House seeks $1.93 trillion defence budget as Iran war drives costs
stories.summary: The total year-on-year increase in Pentagon spending would be the largest since World War II.

stories.title: Watch: Artemis II crew make contact with Earth, describe breathtaking sights
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew made a video call to Earth on Thursday during their deep-space journey toward the Moon. The crew members described the views from their spacecraft as they continue the lunar flyby mission.

stories.title: Zelensky urges lawmakers to act as Ukraine funding hangs in balance
stories.summary: Lawmakers planned to meet on April 6 to discuss the legislation with the key ministers.

stories.title: Uganda in shock after 4 children killed in kindergarden
stories.summary: Four children were killed in an attack at a kindergarten in Kampala, Uganda, shocking the nation. Separately, Sudanese military leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan appointed Yasir al-Atta as the armed forces' new chief of staff. In Benin, opposition parties face internal crises one week before the country's general election.

stories.title: Israel destroys east Lebanon bridge
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike destroyed a bridge linking Sohmor and Mashghara in eastern Lebanon on Friday, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency. A second adjacent bridge over the Litani River was also reportedly hit. Israel had previously struck five other bridges over the Litani in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Ukraine says ten killed in ‘massive’ Russian missile and drone attacks
stories.summary: Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Ukraine, killing at least ten people, as Moscow intensifies daytime aerial strikes after more than four years of invasion. Kyiv has reported an escalation in attacks targeting civilian areas.

stories.title: Iran Shoots Down U.S. Fighter Jet, One Crew Member Still Missing
stories.summary: Iran shot down a US fighter jet, with one American crew member still reported missing. US intelligence assessments reportedly indicate that Iran's military remains operational despite White House claims that Tehran's forces have been largely defeated.

stories.title: Israel, US can’t bomb regime change, only defections and credible alternatives can - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that airstrikes by Israel and the U.S. cannot achieve regime change in Iran, and that only internal defections and credible opposition alternatives can. Groups such as the Iran Freedom Congress and figures like Reza Pahlavi are working toward a unifying framework that remains incomplete.

stories.title: Voices from the Arab press: US-Israel Iran war faces political limits
stories.summary: Arab press commentary noted that while the U.S. and Israel are exerting military pressure on Iran, domestic politics in both countries and broader regional dynamics may shape the conflict's trajectory and eventual resolution.

stories.title: Argentina offers reward for fugitive Chilean ex-guerrilla Apablaza ahead of Kast visit
stories.summary: Argentina's government offered a 20-million-peso reward (approximately $14,000) for information leading to the capture of Galvarino Apablaza, former leader of Chile's Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front. He is wanted by Chilean courts for the 1991 assassination of Senator Jaime Guzmán and the kidnapping of businessman Cristián Edwards.

stories.title: Trump says downing of US jet won't affect talks with Iran, NBC News reports
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said the downing of an American military jet would not affect ongoing negotiations over ending the month-old conflict with Iran, according to NBC News.

stories.title: Israeli PM says 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity destroyed
stories.summary: Steel is a strategically important material used in industrial and military production.

stories.title: 3 UNIFIL peacekeepers hurt in south Lebanon blast; IDF blames Hezbollah rocket
stories.summary: Three UNIFIL peacekeepers were injured in a blast in southern Lebanon, with two reported seriously hurt. The Israel Defense Forces said an examination of the rocket's trajectory indicated it was launched by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah.

stories.title: Ihnat: Russia constantly modernizing weapons and tactics
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesman Yuriy Ihnat stated that Russia is continuously modernizing its weapons systems and adapting its tactics, including varying the timing, number, and deployment methods of its UAVs.

stories.title: Report: Ukrainian military personnel stationed in Libya carried out attack on Russian tanker in Mediterranean
stories.summary: French broadcaster RFI reported that Ukrainian military personnel stationed in Libya carried out the attack on the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean in early March, citing sources.

stories.title: The twilight of US hegemony and Israeli expansionism
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that the U.S.-led war on Iran signals the decline of American hegemony, drawing parallels to the 1956 Suez crisis. The article contended that Israel's involvement exposes expansionist aims across the Palestinian territories, Iran, and Lebanon.

stories.title: China says peace talks between Afghanistan and Pakistan are advancing
stories.summary: China announced that peace talks between Afghanistan's Taliban government and Pakistan are making progress. The statement came two days after the two countries resumed negotiations following weeks of cross-border fighting that killed hundreds.

stories.title: Second US combat plane targeted by Iran crashes near Strait of Hormuz: Report
stories.summary: A U.S. A-10 Warthog crashed near the Strait of Hormuz after being targeted by Iranian air defenses, according to The New York Times. The lone pilot was rescued. Two U.S. helicopters involved in rescue operations were also reportedly hit by Iranian fire.

stories.title: IDF strikes Hamas terror cell operating near Israeli troops in northern Gaza
stories.summary: The IDF struck a Hamas terror cell operating near Israeli forces in northern Gaza. The military said the armed group posed an immediate threat to adjacent IDF troops before the strike was carried out.

stories.title: Iran downs two US warplanes; search continues for missing crew member
stories.summary: Iran shot down a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle over its territory, marking the first confirmed downing of a crewed American aircraft since the war began five weeks ago. A second U.S. plane, an A-10 Warthog, was also struck by Iranian fire and crashed after exiting Iranian airspace. A search continues for one missing crew member.

stories.title: White House seeks $1.5 trillion defence budget as Iran war drives costs
stories.summary: The White House requested a $1.5 trillion defense budget for fiscal year 2027, representing a more than 40 percent increase in Pentagon spending. The sharp rise, the largest since World War II, is driven by costs from the U.S. war with Iran and the need to rebuild depleted weapons stockpiles.

stories.title: Why Trump’s Speech Was So Worrying
stories.summary: Analysts assessed that certain outcomes of the U.S. conflict with Iran have become increasingly probable following a recent speech by President Trump, raising concerns about the trajectory of the war.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1500: Ukraine may be striking Russia’s shadow fleet from Libya — and Egypt just switched sides on stolen grain
stories.summary: An RFI investigation reported that more than 200 Ukrainian military specialists are stationed at three sites in Libya with Mediterranean access. Separately, Egypt pledged to stop purchasing Russian-supplied grain from occupied Ukrainian territory and to buy Ukrainian wheat instead.

stories.title: Second US combat plane targeted by Iran crashes near Strait of Hormuz: Report
stories.summary: A US A-10 Warthog combat aircraft crashed near the Strait of Hormuz after reportedly being targeted by Iranian forces. Two US helicopters also came under Iranian fire, according to media reports. Iran claimed responsibility for striking the aircraft.

stories.title: Christians in Lebanon observe Good Friday under Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Christians across Lebanon marked Good Friday amid continuing Israeli airstrikes and evacuation orders. Worshippers prayed for peace as military operations persisted in the country.

stories.title: Iran leaders join crowds on Tehran’s streets to project control in wartime
stories.summary: The appearances are part of a calculated effort by Iran’s leadership to project resilience and authority.

stories.title: Iran says it rejects Trump offer of 48-hour ceasefire: Report
stories.summary: Iran rejected a 48-hour ceasefire offer from U.S. President Donald Trump, according to reports. Tehran also indicated it was unwilling to meet with mediators for proposed talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Over 60 facilities damaged in Kyiv region due to Russian attack; one person killed, eight injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Ukraine's Kyiv region on April 3 damaged more than 60 facilities across the Bucha, Brovary, Fastiv, and Obukhiv districts. One man was killed and eight people were injured.

stories.title: Will force be used to reopen Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Several countries have discussed the possible use of force to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blockaded. The waterway is a critical global shipping route for oil exports.

stories.title: Emirates Global Aluminium says full production recovery from attack could take a year
stories.summary: Emirates Global Aluminium stated that a full production recovery at its Abu Dhabi facility could take up to a year after it was damaged by an Iranian missile strike.

stories.title: A-10 Warthog crashes near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A U.S. Air Force A-10 Thunderbolt II crashed near the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred around the same time a U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down in the area, though the cause of the A-10 crash was not immediately confirmed.

stories.title: Trump proposes 'historic' defense spending budget, eyes 10% cut to other federal programs
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump proposed a fiscal year 2027 budget that would increase defense spending from $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion. The plan includes roughly 10% cuts to other federal programs, including health and agriculture departments.

stories.title: Egypt was Russia’s biggest stolen-grain customer. Now it pledges to buy Ukrainian wheat instead.
stories.summary: Egypt, previously Russia's largest buyer of grain sourced from occupied Ukrainian territories, pledged to cease those purchases after a call with Ukrainian President Zelensky. The shift came as Russian President Putin was promoting Egypt as a hub for Russian commodities.

stories.title: Man arrested for setting off pyrotechnics on German train, injuring 12
stories.summary: Passengers locked the suspect in a bathroom after he set off the pyrotechnics.

stories.title: Russia chose 'Easter escalation' over ceasefire, says Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of choosing an "Easter escalation" instead of a ceasefire. Russian forces launched hundreds of drones and missiles, killing six civilians and injuring 40 others.

stories.title: Two US fighter jets downed in Mideast, one crew member rescued
stories.summary: Two U.S. fighter jets were lost over or near Iranian airspace on Friday. A search-and-rescue operation recovered one crew member from the first downed aircraft, but the status of any remaining crew from either jet remained unknown at the time of reporting.

stories.title: Survivors of Iran bridge attack recall terror of US-Israeli strike
stories.summary: Survivors of a joint U.S.-Israeli missile strike on Iran's largest road bridge described the attack. The strike hit the major infrastructure target, with witnesses recounting moments of terror as missiles struck.

stories.title: Iran targeted 'enemy' aircraft near Hormuz strait, state media says
stories.summary: Iran's state media reported that the country's air-defence system targeted a US A-10 aircraft over southern waters near the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, the New York Times reported a second US Air Force combat plane crashed in the Gulf region on Friday, with the pilot subsequently rescued.

stories.title: French, Japanese ships cross Strait of Hormuz in first since war
stories.summary: A small number of vessels, including French and Japanese-linked ships, have crossed the Strait of Hormuz despite Iran's near-blockade, according to maritime tracking data. The transits mark the first such crossings since the war began.

stories.title: Israel's Netanyahu vows  to continue attacks on Tehran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared on Friday that Israel will continue its military campaign against Iran. Netanyahu vowed to "crush Iran" as attacks on Tehran persist.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Defense Forces hit over 151,200 enemy targets in March
stories.summary: In March 2026, Ukraine's Armed Forces struck over 151,200 enemy targets and neutralized 35,351 Russian personnel, according to Ukrainian defense data.

stories.title: The reality of 'neurodiversity': Autism awareness under Iranian missile attacks
stories.summary: A health affairs report highlighted challenges facing neurodivergent individuals, particularly those with autism, during Iranian missile attacks. The piece illustrated the gap between neurodiversity awareness ideals and wartime realities.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills two, 15 wounded in Lebanon’s Bekaa Valley
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the town of Sahmar in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley killed at least two people and wounded 15, according to Lebanon's health ministry as cited by Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Senator decries new shoes-on security policy at US airports as ‘reckless’
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth, an Illinois Democrat, criticized the TSA's nine-month-old policy allowing passengers to keep shoes on during airport security screenings. In a letter to the agency, Duckworth called the change a potentially catastrophic security deficiency and urged reinstatement of the shoes-off requirement.

stories.title: Iraqi PMF presence in Iran raises alarm over crackdown, potential US ground war
stories.summary: Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces units reportedly entered Iran in January and have been assisting the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Reports allege PMF involvement in a massacre of civilians, raising concerns about a potential escalation to a US ground war.

stories.title: Pope Leo speaks to Israeli, Ukrainian presidents: Vatican
stories.summary: The Vatican said Pope Leo wished for peace amid ongoing wars.

stories.title: French-owned CMA CGM container ship passes Strait of Hormuz, data shows
stories.summary: PARIS, April 3 - A container ship belonging to French shipping group CMA CGM has passed through the Strait of Hormuz, MarineTraffic vessel tracking data shows, in a sign that Iran may not consider Fra

stories.title: US embassy in Beirut warns that Iran, terror groups may target Lebanese universities
stories.summary: The U.S. embassy in Beirut warned that Iran and allied groups may target Lebanese universities in retaliation for U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian universities. Several schools in the region moved classes online, and the U.S. reiterated its call for American citizens to leave Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut, US warns Iran hit Lebanese universities
stories.summary: Three large blasts struck Beirut following Israeli air strikes on the city. Separately, the US warned that Iran could target university campuses in Lebanon as the regional conflict escalates.

stories.title: US warns its citizens to leave Lebanon citing escalating security risks
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department urged American citizens to leave Lebanon, citing escalating security risks. The warning followed reports of a U.S. jet being shot down and ongoing Israeli strikes on areas of Beirut.

stories.title: As Israel’s PTSD crisis deepens, new treatment offers hope for scarred IDF veterans
stories.summary: Israel is facing a growing PTSD crisis among combat veterans, with many struggling for recognition and adequate care. A new drug treatment has emerged as a potential option for veterans suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder.

stories.title: Over 40 strikes hit Dnipropetrovsk region: one civilian killed, child among injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched more than 40 strikes on four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region using missiles, drones, and artillery. One civilian was killed and 12 others were injured, including a child.

stories.title: Magyar’s Birds took out a Buk-M1, wiped fuel stocks, and hit logistics in Luhansk – all in one night
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone units known as Magyar's Birds conducted coordinated strikes destroying a Russian Buk-M1 air defense system, fuel stockpiles, and logistics targets in Luhansk. Additional strikes over three days also hit Orion drones in Crimea and a Buk-M3 system in Luhansk Oblast.

stories.title: Second US Air Force plane crashed in Persian Gulf region, report says
stories.summary: A second US Air Force combat plane crashed in the Persian Gulf region on Friday, according to the New York Times, citing two US officials. The aircraft's sole pilot was rescued afterward.

stories.title: Drone hits aid warehouse in Iran, Red Cross says
stories.summary: GENEVA, April 3 - A drone strike in southern Iran hit a warehouse holding aid containers and emergency vehicles, a spokesperson for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies

stories.title: IDF destroys Hezbollah rocket launcher as Multidimensional Unit carries out southern Lebanon ops.
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announced that its Multidimensional Unit destroyed a Hezbollah rocket launcher during ground operations in southern Lebanon. The IDF said the unit has killed over 40 Hezbollah fighters since operations began.

stories.title: Italian PM begins visit to Saudi Arabia on Gulf tour
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia as part of a Gulf tour aimed at strengthening Italy's energy security. The trip comes amid escalating Middle East tensions.

stories.title: Ukraine says six killed in ‘massive’ Russian daytime attacks
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russia launched nearly 500 drones and missiles in what Kyiv described as massive daytime attacks, killing at least six people.

stories.title: Mediazona reports Russia adds Meduza correspondent to federal wanted list on criminal charge
stories.summary: Russia's Interior Ministry has placed Andrei Pertsev, a correspondent for the independent outlet Meduza, on its federal wanted list on criminal charges, according to a report by Mediazona.

stories.title: Ukraine strengthening control on border with Transnistria due to risk of Russian actions – Podolyak
stories.summary: Ukrainian presidential adviser Mykhailo Podolyak stated that Ukraine is reinforcing control along its border with Moldova's Transnistria region. Kyiv does not rule out that Russia may use Transnistrian territory to pressure Ukrainian forces or conduct sabotage operations.

stories.title: Moscow court dismisses case against Russian soccer player over cafe brawl after settlement
stories.summary: A Moscow magistrate dismissed a criminal case against former Russian national soccer player Fyodor Smolov over a brawl at a Moscow café after the parties reached a settlement, according to RIA Novosti.

stories.title: Tehran rejected 48-hour ceasefire proposal from US, Iranian media, citing source, says
stories.summary: Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported that Tehran rejected a US proposal for a 48-hour ceasefire. An unnamed source said the proposal was conveyed on Wednesday through an unidentified intermediary country. The US has not confirmed or commented on the report.

stories.title: Trump seeks massive $1.5 trillion defence budget amid Iran war
stories.summary: The White House released its proposed fiscal year 2027 budget, requesting Congress approve a more than 40 percent increase in U.S. defense spending amid the ongoing war with Iran. If approved as submitted, the approximately $1.5 trillion defense budget would set a record in recent U.S. history.

stories.title: Russia’s Investigative Committee orders review of journalist Yury Dud’s interview with Russian Volunteer Corps commander
stories.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee ordered a legal review of journalist Yury Dud's interview with Denis Kapustin, commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps, an armed group fighting against Russian forces.

stories.title: Italian prime minister begins visit to Saudi Arabia during Gulf tour
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni began a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia as part of a Gulf tour focused on national energy security. She arrived in the Red Sea port city of Jeddah, becoming the first EU or NATO leader to visit the region since the war began on February 28.

stories.title: White House seeks $1.5tr defence budget as war on Iran drives costs
stories.summary: United States President Donald Trump asked lawmakers on Friday to approve a massive $1.5 trillion defence budget for 2027, as the country faces rising costs from its war on Iran and mounting global se

stories.title: White House requests giant $1.5 trillion defence budget amid Iran war
stories.summary: Trump requests a ‌10% cut in ‌non-defence and discretionary ‌spending ⁠for the ⁠2027 fiscal year and an ​increase to ‌defence spending by $500 billion, according to ‌a White ​House budget document

stories.title: FSB says it foiled plot to kill senior law enforcement official using bomb hidden in electric scooter
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service announced it foiled an assassination plot against a senior law enforcement official involving a bomb concealed inside an electric scooter.

stories.title: Iran shoots down US jet; 1 crew member rescued, search for 2nd ongoing, officials say
stories.summary: Iran claimed to have shot down a US jet, with one crew member rescued by US forces and a search ongoing for a second. In a separate incident, a US A-10 Warthog crashed near the Strait of Hormuz, and that pilot was also rescued. Israel's IAF reportedly postponed strikes in the area to facilitate the search.

stories.title: Seven more Ukrainian teenagers returned from temporarily occupied territories
stories.summary: Seven Ukrainian teenagers aged 13–17 have been returned from Russian-occupied territories under President Zelensky's Bring Kids Back UA initiative, with assistance from the Office of the Ombudsman.

stories.title: Sanaullah says petrol prices increased as a consequence of Middle East war, govt has ‘nothing to do with it’
stories.summary: Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday said that the prices of petroleum products had increased due to the ongoing war in the Middle East, adding that the government “h

stories.title: Unanswered questions remain after Australia's most wanted fugitive killed in standoff
stories.summary: Australian fugitive Dezi Freeman, wanted for a double murder, was killed in a police standoff after evading capture for seven months in bushland. Authorities believe he received outside assistance during his time on the run.

stories.title: Moscow court partially grants Rosnano’s lawsuit against former CEO over flexible tablet project losses
stories.summary: A Moscow arbitration court partially granted a lawsuit by Russian state nanotechnology company Rosnano seeking damages from former CEO Anatoly Chubais and several other ex-managers over losses from a flexible tablet project.

stories.title: More than 20 attacks on Iranian healthcare facilities since March 1: WHO
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reported that more than 20 attacks on healthcare facilities in Iran have been documented since March 1, describing them as 'multiple attacks.'

stories.title: WHO warns about ‘multiple attacks on health’ in Iran
stories.summary: The World Health Organization raised concerns about multiple attacks on health infrastructure in Iran. The WHO paid tribute to Tehran's Pasteur Institute, which was destroyed in an air strike.

stories.title: In Defense of the Hive Mind
stories.summary: Vince Gilligan's new project "Pluribus" explores the concept of a society governed by artificial intelligence. The work examines whether AI-led collective decision-making could offer benefits over traditional governance structures.

stories.title: Quadruple amputee cornhole pro says he fatally shot person in self-defense
stories.summary: Dayton Webber, a 27-year-old quadruple amputee professional cornhole player, is accused of fatally shooting 27-year-old Bradrick Michael Wells twice in the head during an argument inside a Tesla in Charles County, Maryland, on March 22. Webber's attorney claims he acted in self-defense. A judge noted Webber left Maryland after the shooting.

stories.title: Moscow shoppers and travellers hit by payment system problem
stories.summary: A payment system malfunction disrupted commerce across Moscow on Friday, forcing the metro system to open turnstiles without payment. A regional zoo asked visitors to pay in cash as electronic transactions failed.

stories.title: Christians mark subdued Good Friday in Jerusalem, wider region amid Iran war
stories.summary: Christians observed a subdued Good Friday across the region, from Jerusalem to Dubai, as the ongoing Iran war disrupted pilgrimages and forced churches to cancel in-person services or switch to livestreaming.

stories.title: Sberbank says services have been restored after outages hit major Russian bank apps
stories.summary: Major Russian banking apps including Sberbank, VTB, and T-Bank experienced significant service outages. Sberbank later announced that its services had been restored.

stories.title: Bahrain cracks down on dissent as Iran war reignites Sunni-Shiite unrest in kingdom
stories.summary: Bahrain is intensifying its crackdown on dissent as the Iran war reignites sectarian tensions between the Sunni-led government and the Shiite-majority population. Relatives of a man who died in detention allege his body showed signs of torture.

stories.title: Israel planning to allow up to 90 passengers on departing flights starting Sunday
stories.summary: Israel is planning to allow up to 90 passengers on departing flights starting Sunday, modestly expanding outbound travel. The country's airspace remains largely closed under wartime restrictions, and the plan depends on ongoing security assessments.

stories.title: At least one killed at UAE’s Habshan gas facility after intercepted attack
stories.summary: The UAE's Habshan gas facility, the country's largest, sustained significant damage after an air-defence interception triggered fires. At least one person was killed in the incident.

stories.title: Iran’s Zarif Wants a Bilateral Reset With U.S. That the Gulf Can’t Accept
stories.summary: Former Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif has proposed terms for a bilateral reset with the United States to end the ongoing war. However, his framework reportedly excludes Gulf states that absorbed significant damage during the conflict, raising objections from those nations.

stories.title: Egypt no longer to accept grain exported by Russia from occupied territories – Zelensky
stories.summary: Following a conversation between Presidents Zelensky and Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Egypt agreed to stop accepting grain exported by Russia from occupied Ukrainian territories, according to Zelensky.

stories.title: Stoltenberg Proposed Discussing NATO Troop Limits with Russia — Without Baltic Backing
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg's memoir reveals he proposed discussing NATO troop withdrawal limits with Russia without the knowledge or consent of the alliance's Baltic member states.

stories.title: Russia’s River of Consciousness
stories.summary: An undercover journalist traveled along Russia's Volga River to document everyday life under President Vladimir Putin's rule. The report offers a ground-level perspective on Russian society amid ongoing political and social pressures.

stories.title: Rwanda’s Kagame blasts US sanctions, cites bias toward DR Congo
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame condemned new US sanctions imposed on Rwanda's military, calling them insults and accusing Washington of bias toward the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: IDF strikes over 70 IRGC targets, including missile launch sites, in western, central Iran
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces struck over 70 IRGC targets in western and central Iran, including missile launch sites, drone storage units, and air defense system positions.

stories.title: US fighter jet downed. Spencer Boyer speaks to France 24
stories.summary: France 24 interviewed Spencer Boyer, former U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense, regarding Iran's claim that it shot down a U.S. fighter jet. The segment discussed the implications of the incident in the context of the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: One dead after debris from intercepted attack hits Abu Dhabi gas site
stories.summary: One Egyptian worker was killed and four others injured after debris from an intercepted attack struck Abu Dhabi's Habshan gas facilities. Abu Dhabi's media office reported significant damage to the site, with an assessment ongoing.

stories.title: Another Russian national off the US sanctions list — this time a former finance minister who ran Russia’s third-largest bank
stories.summary: Mikhail Zadornov, a former Russian finance minister who headed Otkritie Bank, was removed from the US sanctions list after petitioning OFAC. He had been sanctioned in 2022, and the US Treasury stated the delisting does not reflect a broader policy change.

stories.title: Sindh announces Rs2,000 for bikers as part of fuel subsidy; Punjab, Islamabad make public transportation free
