stories.summary: The Sindh and Punjab governments announced a host of relief measures on Friday, a day after the Centre announced an unprecedented increase of 43 per cent and 55pc in the prices of petrol and high-spee

stories.title: President Zelensky awards representatives of Crimean Tatar people
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded state honors to representatives of the Crimean Tatar people and recalled a decree granting additional powers to the Mejlis, the Crimean Tatar representative body.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A weekly news quiz covers events from the week of March 28, including the impact of the Iran war on global energy markets, Russia's expulsion of a diplomat, and the intensifying conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

stories.title: US embassy says Iran, aligned groups may 'target' universities in Lebanon
stories.summary: The US embassy in Lebanon warned that Iran and allied groups may seek to target universities in the country. Lebanon hosts several prominent institutions, including the American University of Beirut in the capital.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. can take Strait of Hormuz with more time
stories.summary: Nearly five weeks after it started with a ​joint U.S.-Israeli aerial assault, ‌the war in Iran continues to spread chaos across the region and roil financial markets, raising ‌the pressure on Mr. Trum

stories.title: Drone strike on Sudan hospital kills 10, medical charity MSF says
stories.summary: Two drone strikes hit Al Jabalain Hospital in White Nile State, Sudan, striking an operating theatre and a maternity ward. Médecins Sans Frontières reported that 10 people were killed in the attack.

stories.title: Iran still maintains half its missile launchers and drones, US assessment finds: Report
stories.summary: A US intelligence assessment found that Iran retains roughly half of its missile launchers and half of its suicide drones more than a month into the US–Israeli war. The finding contradicts rhetoric from US and Israeli officials suggesting Iran's military capabilities have been destroyed.

stories.title: Trump seeks US$1.5 trillion for defence in new budget request amid Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump submitted a budget proposal to Congress requesting approximately $1.5 trillion in defense spending for fiscal year 2027. The proposal represents a 44 percent increase over the current U.S. defense budget, driven in part by ongoing military operations in the Middle East conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Rooted in resistance: Mattar and Kennard's olive trees exhibit
stories.summary: Gazan artist Malak Mattar and British artist Peter Kennard are presenting a joint exhibition in London centered on olive trees. The show uses art to address themes of occupation, memory, and Palestinian resilience.

stories.title: Iran: US fighter jet downed, War “It’s not a show”, The Space Race, Will Syrians leave Germany?
stories.summary: President Trump delivered his first national address since the Iran war began five weeks ago, offering no clear signal of ending the conflict or launching a ground offensive. He reiterated rhetoric about being close to finishing operations while threatening to strike Iranian power plants if no deal is reached, and told allies to forcibly take the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukraine may be using Libya as launchpad for Mediterranean strikes on Russian shadow fleet – RFI
stories.summary: An RFI investigation found that more than 200 Ukrainian military officers and technical specialists are stationed across three sites in Libya with Tripoli's approval. The presence may be linked to operations targeting Russia's shadow fleet in the Mediterranean.

stories.title: US upends global supply programme for malaria and HIV amid warnings of gaps
stories.summary: The United States has disrupted a global supply programme for malaria and HIV treatments, with warnings that the move could cause shortages or gaps in the provision of life-saving medical products in some countries.

stories.title: Israeli attack injures six people in northern Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike injured six civilians in the Abu Sharkh area north of Jabalia in the northern Gaza Strip, according to the Wafa news agency. The wounded were transported to Al-Shifa Medical Complex for treatment.

stories.title: Chinese national arrested in multi-million rupees crypto currency scam in Nepal
stories.summary: During preliminary investigation, it was found that Zhu Yi-eng was involved in cheating local Nepalese by contacting them through social media platforms and winning their confidence by showing various

stories.title: EXCLUSIVE: SDA’s Sandhoo likely to lead Space Force Missile Warning & Tracking portfolio
stories.summary: Gurpartap "GP" Sandhoo, currently acting director of the Space Development Agency, is expected to take on leadership of the U.S. Space Force's Missile Warning and Tracking portfolio. It remains unclear whether Sandhoo will retain his SDA role in a dual-hat arrangement, though industry sources consider that the most likely near-term solution.

stories.title: Govt withdraws increase in toll taxes on highways; Pakistan Railways to keep fares unchanged
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: The government on Thursday withdrew the increase in toll taxes, freezing all adjustments for the current fiscal year, while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the Pakistan Railways not

stories.title: Your Taxes: You can't have your matzah and eat it, too
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court ruled that employees who benefit from tax breaks on share or share-option plans cannot also claim additional tax benefits, requiring taxpayers to choose one avenue of relief.

stories.title: FSB Says It Defused ‘Scooter Bomb’ Parked Near Moscow Business Center
stories.summary: Russia's FSB said it defused a bomb hidden in an electric scooter parked near a Moscow business center, alleging Ukraine planned to use the device in an assassination plot targeting a high-ranking Russian security official.

stories.title: Trump wants $18B for Golden Dome. It would require reconciliation funds, again
stories.summary: The Trump administration is seeking $18 billion in funding for the Golden Dome missile defense program. Defense experts have raised concerns that the program rests on unstable footing because it would depend on mandatory reconciliation funds rather than standard appropriations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zhytomyr region reels after missile and drone strike
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone strikes hit Ukraine's Zhytomyr region, killing one person and injuring 10. Dozens of homes and public buildings were destroyed in the attack.

stories.title: Russia offers to increase supply of crude oil, LNG to India amid war in West Asia
stories.summary: The energy cooperation figured prominently in meetings Russia’s First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov held with National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar

stories.title: World food prices set to continue soaring if Iran war persists, says UN report
stories.summary: A UN report warns that global food prices will continue rising if the Iran war persists, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts a key Middle Eastern shipping route for oil and commodities.

stories.title: Palestine 36: A film about a revolt that nearly changed history
stories.summary: Director Annemarie Jacir's film Palestine 36 examines how the roots of the current Palestinian crisis trace back to the period of British colonial rule. The film centers on a revolt that Jacir argues nearly altered the course of history.

stories.title: Presidential Office responds to Poroshenko: More emotion than facts
stories.summary: Iryna Mudra, Deputy Head of Ukraine's Presidential Office, responded to former President Petro Poroshenko's allegations of court pressure in a sanctions case, characterizing his statements as an emotional reaction ahead of a court hearing rather than a fact-based position.

stories.title: World food price rise set to continue if Iran war lasts, FAO says
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reported that global food prices continued to rise, driven partly by the Iran war. Meat prices increased by 1 per cent, with higher pig meat prices in the EU and bovine meat prices in Brazil.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia suffers over 35,000 losses in March – highest since start of war
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Russia suffered its highest monthly losses since the start of the full-scale war in March 2026, with more than 35,000 Russian personnel killed or severely wounded.

stories.title: Global anger over Israel's 'racist' death penalty law continues
stories.summary: Scores of Syrians gathered at the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus after Friday prayers to protest Israel's new death penalty law. The legislation has been widely condemned internationally as racist.

stories.title: One US pilot rescued, another missing after Iran says it downed fighter jet
stories.summary: One crew member of a U.S. F-15E fighter jet shot down over Iran was rescued by American forces, while a second remains missing. Iran claimed responsibility, releasing photos of apparent wreckage, as the U.S. launched a search-and-rescue operation.

stories.title: French-owned ship passes through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A French-owned vessel transited the Strait of Hormuz, marking what appears to be the first passage by a ship from a major European firm since the current conflict began.

stories.title: Iran still maintains half its missile launchers and drones, US assessment finds: Report
stories.summary: A US intelligence assessment found that Iran still retains approximately half of its missile launchers and drone capabilities despite ongoing conflict. The report also noted that Iran's targeting accuracy has improved, contributing to the downing of a US jet on Friday.

stories.title: Iran war: Why US allies are suffering more than its enemies
stories.summary: An analysis argues that US allies in Europe and Asia are bearing disproportionate economic costs from the Iran war, as the conflict disrupts global oil and gas supply chains passing through the Middle East.

stories.title: White House seeks $1.5tn defense budget as Iran war drives costs
stories.summary: The White House is seeking a $1.5 trillion defense budget, driven in part by the costs of the Iran war. US media reports estimate the conflict may be costing approximately $2 billion per day.

stories.title: Three killed in strike on residential area in Tehran
stories.summary: At least three people were killed in a strike on a residential area in north Tehran, according to Iran's Mehr news agency.

stories.title: Cambodia parliament approves law to combat cybercrime scam rings
stories.summary: Cambodia's parliament approved a new law aimed at combating cybercrime scam rings operating in the country. Justice Minister Keut Rith said the legislation is intended to enhance a nationwide "cleaning operation" against such networks.

stories.title: Russian strike on Zhytomyr region leaves one killed, injury toll rises to 10
stories.summary: A Russian missile and drone strike on Ukraine's Zhytomyr region killed one person and injured at least ten others.

stories.title: US unemployment rate drops despite economic uncertainty and Iran war
stories.summary: The US unemployment rate fell in March despite ongoing economic uncertainty and the Iran war. The White House highlighted stronger-than-expected job gains, particularly in the healthcare and construction sectors.

stories.title: Israeli soldier uses blindfolded Palestinian to promote brand
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier shared images online appearing to use a blindfolded Palestinian detainee to promote a commercial brand. Activists and social media users condemned the act as emblematic of the mistreatment of Palestinians.

stories.title: Iran leaders join crowds on Tehran’s streets in show of defiance
stories.summary: Senior Iranian officials joined crowds on Tehran's streets in a public show of defiance amid the ongoing war. Families gathered in parks for music and barbecues, using public spaces as both refuge and a demonstration of loyalty.

stories.title: Russian strike on Kharkiv: 29-year-old woman dies in hospital from injuries
stories.summary: A 29-year-old woman injured during the April 3 Russian attack on Kharkiv has died in a hospital in the city.

stories.title: Nigeria worshippers mark Easter with Lagos street procession
stories.summary: Hundreds of Catholic faithful in Lagos, Nigeria, marked Good Friday with a public street procession reenacting the Stations of the Cross, linking Christ's suffering to the country's economic hardships.

stories.title: Rwanda: UN Envoy Warns Rwanda Under FDLR Genocidal Threat
stories.summary: A United Nations envoy warned that armed groups such as the FDLR, backed by the Democratic Republic of Congo, continue to pose a genocidal threat to Rwanda despite the country's significant post-genocide recovery.

stories.title: Turkey continuing talks to stop Iran war spiralling, Erdogan tells Putin
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told Russian President Vladimir Putin that Ankara is maintaining contact with all parties to prevent the Iran war from spiraling further. Erdogan stated Turkey opposes both the attacks on Iran and Iran's retaliatory strikes on neighboring countries.

stories.title: China urges respect for Palestinian rights after Israel passes death penalty law
stories.summary:
China called on Friday for Palestinians’ rights to be protected after Israel approved a bill to allow the execution of Palestinians convicted on terror charges for deadly attacks.
Under the new law, p

stories.title: China Reports Outbreak of Livestock Disease Near Russian Regions Hit by Mass Cattle Culling
stories.summary: The outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in China comes amid growing concern about possible cross-border spread following months of mass cattle culls in Russia.

stories.title: Yale report links Russian oil sector to child deportation from Ukraine
stories.summary: A Yale University report alleges that Russian state energy companies Rosneft and Gazprom supported wartime camps where more than 2,000 Ukrainian children were taken, providing transportation and funding. The findings prompted some US lawmakers to call for reinstating sanctions against both firms.

stories.title: Trump: ‘With a little more time’ the US ‘can easily’ reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social that the US could "take the oil and make a fortune" in Iran, listing bridges and power plants as future targets. Separately, reports emerged that the US quietly expelled Iran's deputy UN envoy in December.

stories.title: Crew member rescued after US fighter jet downed over Iran, US media report
stories.summary: A US crew member was rescued after a fighter jet was shot down over Iran. Iranian media report that a reward is being offered for the capture of a second crew member believed to still be missing.

stories.title: Wadephul: NATO’s shared interest is Ukraine’s victory over Russia
stories.summary: German politician Johann Wadephul stated that NATO countries share a common interest in Ukraine's victory over Russia. He described the Alliance as the strongest military bloc in the world, emphasizing collective support for Ukraine's defensive war.

stories.title: Iran reeling after B1 bridge strike as Trump threatens further attacks
stories.summary: A U.S. airstrike destroyed the B1 bridge near Karaj, Iran, leaving collapsed roadway sections and extensive damage to the surrounding residential area. President Trump has threatened further attacks against Iran.

stories.title: UNIFIL says 3 peacekeepers wounded in Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon reported that three of its peacekeepers were wounded in southern Lebanon. UNIFIL is deployed near the border where Israel and Hezbollah have been engaged in fighting for a month.

stories.title: What we know about the US fighter jet shot down in Iran
stories.summary: The White House confirmed that President Donald Trump was briefed after a US fighter jet was shot down over Iran. Details about the incident and the fate of the crew are still emerging.

stories.title: Relationship with Trump may be beyond repair, Keir Starmer told
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer was warned that his relationship with President Trump may be irreparably damaged after Trump mocked Starmer during a White House Easter speech, imitating his voice and saying the UK was "not our best" ally.

stories.title: One of the American crew members shot down in Iran has been rescued, report says
stories.summary: One American crew member from a fighter jet shot down over Iran was rescued alive, according to Israel's Channel 12 citing an Israeli official. A search continues for a second crew member still missing.

stories.title: As Kremlin Cuts Off the Internet, VPNs Become a Way of Life
stories.summary: The Kremlin has intensified efforts to block VPN services in Russia, but the number of Russian VPN users continues to grow as citizens increasingly rely on the technology to circumvent internet restrictions.

stories.title: For Millions of Russians, the Kremlin's Internet Curbs Make VPNs a Necessity
stories.summary: Moscow has ramped up efforts to block VPNs as they have become more popular — but the number of users continues to grow.

stories.title: Zelensky says frontline situation best for Ukraine in the last 10 months
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the frontline situation was the best it had been for Ukraine in ten months. He said Ukrainian forces had successfully foiled a Russian offensive during March.

stories.title: Trump seeks to double number of ship requests with 2027 defense budget
stories.summary: President Trump's proposed fiscal year 2027 defense budget of $1.5 trillion would allocate $65.8 billion for shipbuilding, seeking to roughly double the number of ship procurement requests compared to current levels.

stories.title: Can the Christian Palestinian population survive Israel’s occupation?
stories.summary: Ahead of Easter, Palestinian Christians face heightened Israeli restrictions on access to holy sites in Jerusalem, Gaza, and the occupied West Bank. Site closures and ceremony cancellations have been imposed amid the broader regional war with Iran.

stories.title: The petrol crisis that could electrify Pakistan
stories.summary: The impact of the ongoing US-Iran war on ordinary Pakistani households and business is already being felt. With petrol at Rs458 per litre and diesel at over Rs520, citizens are going to be facing real

stories.title: Qatar says multiple Iranian drone attacks ‘intercepted’
stories.summary: Qatar's defense ministry announced that multiple drones launched from Iran targeted the country on Friday. Qatari armed forces said all incoming drones were successfully intercepted and neutralized.

stories.title: Iran’s former top diplomat urges deal with US to end war
stories.summary: Iran's former top diplomat publicly urged Tehran to pursue a deal with the United States to end the ongoing war. He emphasized the need to stop the conflict to prevent further civilian casualties.

stories.title: AeroSentinel production facility severely damaged after Iranian ballistic missile strike
stories.summary: AeroSentinel's production facility sustained severe damage after an Iranian ballistic missile struck just meters from the site late Thursday night. The 400-kilogram warhead caused heavy structural damage to the facility.

stories.title: Paramilitary forces in Sudan kill at least 10 people in hospital drone attack, says medical group
stories.summary: Paramilitary forces in Sudan killed at least 10 people in a drone attack on a hospital, according to a medical group.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kramatorsk with glide bombs: two civilians killed, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped glide bombs on the city of Kramatorsk in the Donetsk region, killing two civilians and wounding three others.

stories.title: Forget democracy, Burkina Faso military leader Traore says
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military leader Ibrahim Traoré, who seized power in a September 2022 coup, told journalists that people should forget about democracy, calling it harmful. The remarks signal his intention to maintain long-term rule in the West African nation.

stories.title: Why Jet Fuel Is the Real Harbinger of the Energy Crisis
stories.summary: An analysis examines how jet fuel shortages have become a critical indicator of the broader energy crisis triggered by the Iran war, disrupting global supply chains for essential petroleum products.

stories.title: Cyberattack targeted Italy's Uffizi but nothing stolen, museum says
stories.summary: Florence's Uffizi Galleries confirmed they were targeted by a cyberattack earlier this year but denied reports of a major security breach or data theft. The museum stated that nothing was stolen in the incident.

stories.title: Three tankers, including one Japanese-owned, cross Strait of Hormuz near Oman
stories.summary: Three tankers, including one co-owned by a Japanese company, crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday by navigating close to Oman's coast. The route is unusual and reflects Iran's ongoing disruption of shipping through the strategic waterway since the war began on February 28.

stories.title: Sindh announces Rs2,000 for bikers as part of fuel subsidy; Punjab makes public transportation free
stories.summary: Pakistan's Sindh province announced a Rs2,000 fuel subsidy for motorcyclists and Punjab made public transportation free after the federal government raised petrol and diesel prices by 43% and 55% respectively, linked to global oil price shocks from the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: China affirms Palestinian rights after death penalty law passes
stories.summary: China reaffirmed its support for Palestinian rights following the passage of Israel's new death penalty legislation. Multiple countries, including Saudi Arabia and several EU member states, have criticized the law.

stories.title: US defense spending would rise $445bn under Trump budget plan, with steep cuts elsewhere
stories.summary: President Trump's proposed budget would increase U.S. defense spending by $445 billion, bringing it to its highest level in decades. Other government programs would face 10% cuts, drawing sharp criticism from Democrats over the administration's priorities.

stories.title: Ukraine’s forces thwart Russian breakthrough attempt in Udachne, Donetsk region
stories.summary: Assault units of Ukraine's Skelia regiment repelled an attempted Russian breakthrough near the settlement of Udachne in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: US fighter jet shot down over Iran, source confirms to 'Post'
stories.summary: A US fighter jet was shot down over Iran, and a source confirmed to The Jerusalem Post that search and rescue operations are underway to locate the two US pilots who were aboard the aircraft.

stories.title: Seven rockets fired from southern Lebanon towards northern Israel, report says
stories.summary: Seven rockets were fired from southern Lebanon toward northern Israel, prompting air-raid sirens in Nahariya and parts of western Galilee, according to the Israeli Home Front Command.

stories.title: Iran war: French and Japanese-owned ships make first Strait of Hormuz crossings
stories.summary: A French-owned CMA CGM container ship and a Japanese-owned Mitsui OSK Lines tanker crossed the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first known Western-linked transits since the Iran war effectively closed the critical waterway over a month ago.

stories.title: French far-left MEP Rima Hassan to be tried in July over post on X
stories.summary: French far-left European Parliament member Rima Hassan will face trial in Paris in July over a post on X referencing a 1970s attack on an Israeli airport. The Paris prosecutor's office confirmed the charges.

stories.title: French-owned container ship exits Hormuz in first since Iran war
stories.summary: A French-owned container ship transited the Strait of Hormuz, the first such passage since the outbreak of the Iran war. Tehran has permitted some vessels from friendly nations to pass through a pre-approved route.

stories.title: US F-15E jet confirmed shot down over Iran as Tehran releases wreckage images
stories.summary: A U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle was confirmed shot down over Iran, the first American manned aircraft lost since the start of the five-week-old war. Iran released images of wreckage while U.S. forces launched a rescue operation for the two crew members.

stories.title: Russians shell church in central Kherson, one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled a church in central Kherson, injuring one woman.

stories.title: Drones caused 96% of Russia’s losses in March – 34,000 troops killed or wounded
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that drones accounted for 96% of Russian losses in March 2026, with approximately 34,000 Russian troops killed or wounded. Unmanned systems far surpassed all other weapons combined in inflicting casualties.

stories.title: RBC reports Russia seeks to lift moratorium on telecom inspections to verify wiretapping systems
stories.summary: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry is considering lifting the moratorium on scheduled inspections of telecommunications operators, the Russian business outlet RBC reported, citing two sources.

stories.title: Domestic helper arrested after 6-month-old girl dies in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested a domestic helper on suspicion of child neglect after a six-month-old girl was found unconscious at a home in Yuen Long's Fairview Park. The infant was taken to Pok Oi Hospital and later transferred to Tuen Mun Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

stories.title: Villagers in South Lebanon hang on to hope and their homes as war continues
stories.summary: Villagers in southern Lebanon are refusing to leave their homes despite ongoing conflict in the region. Residents describe their houses as their only shelter as military operations continue in the area.

stories.title: French-owned container ship transits Hormuz Strait in first since Iran war
stories.summary: A CMA CGM container ship became the first French-owned vessel to transit the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US–Israeli war on Iran, marking a notable resumption of commercial shipping through the contested waterway.

stories.title: Netanyahu vows to continue crushing Iranian regime during security assessment
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue military operations against Iran during a security assessment, stating that Israel and the US are eliminating commanders, bombing bridges, and striking infrastructure in Iran.

stories.title: 7 cars of passenger train derail in Russia, injuring more than 20
stories.summary: Seven cars of passenger train No. 302, traveling from Chelyabinsk to Moscow, derailed near the Bryandino station in Russia’s Ulyanovsk region, Russian Railways said.

stories.title: Iran says two US jets shot down, crews rescued
stories.summary: Iran claimed it shot down a second US aircraft, an A-10, which state media said crashed into the Persian Gulf after being hit by Iranian air defenses. This followed Iran's earlier claim of downing a US F-15E over Khuzestan province.

stories.title: One US crew member rescued after Iran downs jet, reports say
stories.summary: US special operations forces reportedly rescued one crew member after Iran claimed to have shot down an American military aircraft. Details about additional crew members remained unclear.

stories.title: Iranian media says US jet shot down, bounty offered for pilot
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that a US fighter jet was shot down over Iran, and a bounty has been offered for the pilot's capture. US officials confirmed that search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew.

stories.title: Palisa discusses battlefield situation, successful technological solutions in Ukraine’s military with former CIA Director
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Pavlo Palisa met with former CIA Director and US Central Command chief David Petraeus to discuss battlefield conditions and successful technological solutions being used by Ukraine's military.

stories.title: Blindfolded Palestinian used to advertise Israeli business in photo
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier posted a photo online showing a blindfolded Palestinian detainee holding a sign promoting a private jewelry business. The man was reportedly detained during an Israeli raid on his home in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Medvedev says Russia should drop its 'tolerant attitude' towards Ukraine's EU drive
stories.summary: Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, stated that Moscow should abandon its tolerant stance toward Ukraine's pursuit of European Union membership. The remarks signal a hardening of Russia's position on Ukraine's Western integration efforts.

stories.title: US confirms downed aircraft is F-15E
stories.summary: US authorities confirmed that the fighter jet shot down over Iran on Friday was an F-15E, correcting earlier reports that suggested it was an F-35. The F-15E is a strike aircraft built by McDonnell Douglas, designed for fast strike-and-withdrawal missions.

stories.title: Baltic Sea strikes: How Ukraine aims to undermine Russia's oil profits from Iran war
stories.summary: Ukraine intensified drone strikes on Russian ports and oil refineries in the Leningrad region along the Baltic Sea. Kyiv's strategy aims to prevent Moscow from profiting off energy market disruptions caused by the Iran war, though the approach carries significant risks.

stories.title: World anxious to open Hormuz Strait while Trump and Iran trade threats
stories.summary: Dozens of countries sought ways to resume energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. President Donald Trump escalated threats against Iran, driving oil prices higher. Trump urged Iran to make a deal, while the crisis deepened strain on global consumers.

stories.title: Yair Lapid’s divisive rhetoric threatens israel’s unity, national security - opinion
stories.summary: Opposition leader Yair Lapid faced criticism for inflammatory statements that some argue risk weakening Israeli social cohesion and undermining national unity during wartime.

stories.title: Trump’s budget proposes massive defense spending with 10% cut to other programs
stories.summary: The Trump administration's proposed budget includes a massive surge in defense spending along with a 5–7% pay raise for military personnel. Other federal programs would face cuts of approximately 10%.

stories.title: In call, Pope urges Herzog to pursue ‘all paths of dialogue’ to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pope Francis urged Israeli President Isaac Herzog to pursue "all paths of dialogue" to end the Iran war during a phone call marking Passover and Easter. The pontiff stressed the protection of civilians and respect for international law.

stories.title: Don Cheadle and Ayo Edebiri bring “Proof” back to broadway
stories.summary: Don Cheadle and Ayo Edebiri are making their Broadway debuts in a new revival of David Auburn's Pulitzer Prize– and Tony Award–winning play "Proof." Edebiri, known for her Emmy-winning role in "The Bear," said the experience has not yet fully sunk in.

stories.title: Zelensky: Strait of Hormuz can be reopened only through joint international action
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the blockade in the Strait of Hormuz can only be resolved through joint international action, emphasizing the need for coordinated multilateral efforts.

stories.title: 8 die in Ukraine in Russian strikes as Kyiv holds door open for Easter truce
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed at least eight people across Ukraine on Friday, including casualties from a large-scale missile and drone attack near Kyiv. President Zelensky signaled openness to a potential Easter truce, with the holiday falling on April 12 in both countries.

stories.title: Over 100 legal experts declare strikes on Iran possible war crimes
stories.summary: Over 100 US-based legal experts signed a letter declaring the US–Israeli war on Iran, launched on February 28, a violation of international law. The letter states that US strikes may constitute war crimes under the UN Charter.

stories.title: Pakistan raises petrol prices amid U.S.-Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan's government imposed a 55% increase in diesel prices and significant petrol price hikes amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran war, aiming to control fuel consumption as global energy costs surge.

stories.title: Drone footage shows a factory in Israel damaged by Iranian missile debris
stories.summary: Drone footage from Petah Tikva, Israel, shows damage to a factory caused by debris from an Iranian missile that was intercepted. The images reveal the extent of structural damage at the site.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Air Assault Forces commander names most successful operations of his units
stories.summary: Major General Oleh Apostol, commander of Ukraine's Air Assault Forces and a Hero of Ukraine, outlined the most successful operations carried out by his units during the war.

stories.title: Trump seeks historic $1.5 trillion for military in Congress budget request
stories.summary: President Donald Trump submitted a budget request to Congress seeking approximately $1.5 trillion in military spending, the largest defense budget request in decades. The proposal includes significant cuts to domestic programs.

stories.title: US aircraft seen over Iran in rescue mission, says Iranian media
stories.summary: Iranian media reported US aircraft, including helicopters and a C-130 Hercules, conducting a search and rescue mission over central Iran for the crew of a downed fighter jet. Iranian outlets affiliated with the IRGC said one US aircraft retreated after receiving heavy fire.

stories.title: By claiming total failure, Israel's opposition hurts itself - and helps Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israel's opposition has been criticized for claiming total government failure, with analysts suggesting the rhetoric may undermine the opposition's own credibility while inadvertently strengthening Prime Minister Netanyahu's position.

stories.title: Ukraine slows enemy advances, liberates land, drains Russia’s war chest
stories.summary: Ukraine has slowed Russian advances and recaptured territory, aided by a growing domestic drone production capability. The battlefield gains are reportedly helping to drain Russia's war resources.

stories.title: Iranian forces launch search for crew of downed US fighter jet
stories.summary: Iranian forces launched a search operation for the crew of a downed US fighter jet. Iranian news outlets shared photos of wreckage and what appeared to be an ejection seat with an attached parachute found at the crash site.

stories.title: India to acquire more air defense systems and drones for modern warfare
stories.summary: India announced plans to acquire additional Russian S-400 air defense systems and drones to modernize its military capabilities. The S-400 systems were assessed as effective during India's brief war with Pakistan last year.

stories.title: Commendation for capture or killing of F-35 crew, says province governor
stories.summary: The governor of a southwestern Iranian province offered a commendation for anyone who captures or kills the crew of the downed US fighter jet. Iranian authorities are racing to locate the pilot before US search and rescue teams reach them.

stories.title: US F-15E fighter jet downed by Iran, rescue operations underway
stories.summary: A U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet was downed over Iran during Operation Epic Fury, with rescue operations underway for the crew. The incident is reported as the first loss of a manned American aircraft over Iran during the current military campaign.

stories.title: Ukraine downs 541 air targets in massive Russian strike
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 541 air targets during a massive Russian strike, including 26 missiles and 515 drones of various types.

stories.title: Turkey establishes Istanbul maritime command for Ukraine security mission
stories.summary: Turkey established a maritime command in Istanbul to oversee the Black Sea component of a post-war security mission in Ukraine. Romania and Bulgaria are expected to support the operation as littoral Black Sea states.

stories.title: Ship passes through Strait of Hormuz after signaling French ownership, data shows
stories.summary: A vessel passed through the Strait of Hormuz after signaling French ownership, one day after French President Emmanuel Macron said a military operation to reopen the waterway would be unrealistic. Tracking data confirmed the ship's transit.

stories.title: French-owned CMA CGM container ship passes Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A French-owned CMA CGM container ship passed through the Strait of Hormuz, the first French-linked vessel to transit the waterway since U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began in late February. The passage suggests Iran may not consider France a hostile nation.

stories.title: Russia conducting rolling aerial attack on Ukraine, Kyiv says
stories.summary: Ukraine's air force reported that Russia launched a sustained rolling aerial attack beginning Thursday evening, with a large number of enemy drones entering Ukrainian airspace. Kyiv described the assault as ongoing into Friday.

stories.title: FAO: World food price rise set to continue if Iran war lasts
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reported that global food prices rose 2.4 percent from February levels and warned that prices could continue climbing if the Iran war persists.

stories.title: Over 100 US-based legal experts declare Trump's strikes on Iran as possible war crimes
stories.summary: More than 100 US-based legal experts, including prominent scholars and former government legal advisors, signed a letter declaring that US strikes on Iran may constitute war crimes. The letter denounces the illegality of the US military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Massive Russian attack: Five killed across four regions of Ukraine
stories.summary: At least five civilians were killed across four regions of Ukraine as a result of Russian attacks on Friday.

stories.title: On the ground: 'Massive explosion' rocks northern Tehran
stories.summary: A large explosion struck northern Tehran on Friday, with smoke visible rising from the blast site. The Israeli military announced it had launched a "wide-scale wave" of strikes on Iran, alongside parallel attacks in Beirut, Lebanon.

stories.title: National Forensic Agency ‘now fully functional’, says interior ministry
stories.summary: Pakistan's first National Forensic Agency has officially begun operations in Islamabad, established under legislation passed in 2024. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the agency will assist law enforcement in national security matters and crime reduction.

stories.title: Ukraine’s anti-corruption court upholds 6-year term for ex-tax chief in gas scheme
stories.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court upheld a six-year prison sentence for a former tax chief convicted in a gas-related corruption scheme. The appeals chamber confirmed the sentence roughly nine years after the case began.

stories.title: ‘War crime’: Amnesty slams Iran’s recruitment of children as young as 12 to Basij militia
stories.summary: Amnesty International accused Iran's IRGC of recruiting children as young as 12 into the Basij militia, citing eyewitness accounts and video evidence. The rights group said deploying child soldiers at checkpoints violates a UN convention to which Iran is a signatory.

stories.title: Sri Lanka arrests 152 in alleged Chinese-run cyberscam
stories.summary: Sri Lankan police arrested 152 foreign nationals, mostly Chinese, in the coastal town of Chilaw for allegedly operating a cyberscam from a hotel. Authorities said those involved in scamming would face criminal charges while others could be deported.

stories.title: Three peacekeepers wounded in blast in Lebanon, says UN
stories.summary: Three UN peacekeepers were wounded, two of them seriously, by an explosion inside a UN position in southern Lebanon on Friday. The UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNFIL) said the origin of the blast is not yet known. It was the third such incident in the past week.

stories.title: In Lebanon, displaced Shiites feared over potential Hezbollah ties amid IDF strikes
stories.summary: Approximately one million displaced Shiites in Lebanon face housing discrimination as landlords elsewhere in the country refuse to rent to them. Locals fear that undisclosed ties to Hezbollah could make their buildings targets for Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Trump says with more time, US can ‘take the oil’ in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on social media that with more time the US could "take the oil" in Iran. He asserted Washington could easily reopen the Strait of Hormuz despite Iran's weeks-long blockade of the waterway.

stories.title: Russian military training at low level, says Ukraine’s Air Assault Forces commander
stories.summary: Major General Oleh Apostol, commander of Ukraine's Air Assault Forces, assessed that Russian military personnel currently receive low-level training for combat operations in Ukraine.

stories.title: Red Crescent supply warehouse attacked in southwest Iran
stories.summary: A video released by the Iranian Red Crescent shows the aftermath of a strike on a supply warehouse in Bushehr, southwestern Iran. The attack targeted a storage site used for humanitarian supplies.

stories.title: Iran release videos of US aircraft searching for pilots shot down in Iran
stories.summary: Iranian media broadcast videos purportedly showing US aircraft, including helicopters, conducting search operations over central Iran for the pilots of a fighter jet downed by Iranian defenses on Friday.

stories.title: Mozambique: Road Rehabilitation Launched in Nampula
stories.summary: Nampula Mayor Luís Giquira launched a project to rehabilitate approximately 2.6 kilometers of roads in the northern Mozambican city.

stories.title: Mozambique: U.S. Donates Protective Equipment Against Nuclear Threats
stories.summary: The United States government donated chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear protective equipment to Mozambique in a ceremony in Maputo.

stories.title: Italy's famed Uffizi admits cyber-attack but denies security breach
stories.summary: Italy's Uffizi Gallery in Florence acknowledged that hackers infiltrated its IT systems in a cyber-attack. However, the gallery denied any security breach affecting its art collection, stating that its works remain safe.

stories.title: Kremlin’s drive for a state-backed messaging app touches a nerve for some
stories.summary: Russian officials are promoting a state-backed messaging application, arguing that foreign messaging platforms have been compromised by hostile intelligence services. The initiative has provoked unease among some Russian users concerned about government surveillance.

stories.title: Nigeria: FCT Residents Demand Take-Off of Kugbo, Mabushi Bus Terminals
stories.summary: Residents of Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory called on Minister Nyesom Wike to expedite the opening of bus and taxi terminals built in Kugbo and Mabushi to ease transportation challenges in Abuja.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lenacapavir - a Welcome Development
stories.summary: Nigeria began rolling out Lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable HIV prevention drug, in eight states including Anambra, Ebonyi, Gombe, Kwara, Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Benue, and the Federal Capital Territory.

stories.title: Israel's campaign against Unrwa could set precedent to dismantle other UN agencies, chief warns
stories.summary: UNRWA Commissioner-General Philippe Lazzarini warned that Israel's campaign against the agency could set a precedent for dismantling other UN bodies. He said failure to protect UNRWA, the main provider of education and health services to Palestinians, may have far-reaching consequences.

stories.title: Nigeria: Bandits Strike Again in Kaduna, Abduct 7 Family Members
stories.summary: Bandits abducted seven family members and three other residents in Unguwar Sabon-Titi along the Katari-Hayin Dam road in Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Nigeria.

stories.title: Nigeria: Why Tinubu Didn't Leave Airport During Jos Visit - Presidency
stories.summary: Nigeria's presidency explained that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu did not leave the airport during his visit to Jos, Plateau State, due to scheduling constraints and logistical challenges.

stories.title: Africa: Mólly Ephraim Academy - 10years of Empowering Africa's Next Generation of Entrepreneurs
stories.summary: Mólly Ephraim Academy, founded by Nigerian entrepreneur Mólly Ephraim, has spent a decade providing affordable entrepreneurship education across Africa. Since launching its first program, PROJECT 1000, in March 2016, the academy has aligned its initiatives with UN Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 1 on poverty reduction.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone units destroy Russian Buk-M1, fuel tanks, depots in Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian unmanned systems units destroyed a Russian Buk-M1 surface-to-air missile system, fuel tanks, and supply depots overnight in the temporarily occupied part of the Luhansk region on April 3.

stories.title: Nigeria: NHRC Demands End to Killings, Urges FG to Prosecute Perpetrators
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission called on the Federal Government to take urgent action to halt killings across the country, particularly recent attacks in Jos, Plateau State, and to prosecute those responsible.

stories.title: Russians launch airstrikes on Kherson: One woman killed, one man wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out airstrikes on the Dniprovskyi district of Kherson, killing a 60-year-old woman and injuring a man.

stories.title: White House requests $1.5tn in defence funding
stories.summary: The Trump White House requested $1.5 trillion in defense funding for fiscal year 2027, roughly a 40 percent increase over the most recent fiscal year. The budget, the highest in modern US history, would entail up to $73 billion in cuts to housing, climate, and education agencies amid the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: Yilwatda - Shedding of Innocent Blood in Plateau Must No Longer Be Treated With Routine Outrage
stories.summary: APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda called for an end to routine outrage over violence in Plateau State, Nigeria, urging more substantive and lasting responses to the continued killings of civilians.

stories.title: Nigeria: 10 Years On - How Panama Papers Rewrote Nigeria's Transparency Law, Sparked Regulatory Policies
stories.summary: Ten years after the Panama Papers leak, Nigeria's only media organization with direct access to the files—Premium Times—published over 30 stories that contributed to changes in the country's transparency laws and regulatory policies.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Kagame - Habyarimana's Son Is Part of Kinshasa-FDLR Network
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame stated that the Democratic Republic of Congo's links with the son of former Rwandan leader Juvénal Habyarimana pose a security threat to Rwanda, alleging connections to a Kinshasa-FDLR network.

stories.title: Liberia: FIFA Threatens LFA With Global Ban Over 'Third-Party Interference' in Elections
stories.summary: FIFA warned the Liberia Football Association that the country faces a potential suspension from all global football activities after a court order halted the LFA's elective congress, citing third-party interference.

stories.title: Russian Su-30 fighter crashes in occupied Crimea — fourth Russian military aircraft loss in four days
stories.summary: A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in occupied Crimea on April 3 during a scheduled training flight, marking the fourth Russian military aircraft loss in four days. Russia's Ministry of Defense said both crew members ejected safely and the jet was unarmed.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Reaffirms Commitment to Tackle Insecurity, Boost Economy in Easter Message
stories.summary: In an Easter message, Nigerian President Bola Tinubu reaffirmed his administration's commitment to addressing insecurity and stabilizing the economy.

stories.title: Nigeria: Don't Deport Our Fleeing Members, Massob Begs Int'l Communities
stories.summary: The Movement for Actualization of the Sovereign State of Biafra (MASSOB) in Nigeria has appealed to the international community not to deport its members who are seeking asylum abroad.

stories.title: Nigeria: Police Rescue Abducted Three-Day-Old Baby in Nasarawa, Detain Suspects
stories.summary: Police in Nigeria's Nasarawa State rescued a three-day-old baby who had been abducted and arrested two suspects in connection with the crime. The operation was carried out by the Nasarawa State Police Command.

stories.title: Nigeria: Why Tinubu Only Addressed Victims of Plateau Violence At Airport - Presidency
stories.summary: Nigeria's presidency responded to criticism that President Tinubu only addressed victims of Plateau State violence at the airport during his visit, with spokesman Onanuga defending the arrangement.

stories.title: Africa: Ethiopia Assumes Chairship of AU Peace and Security Council
stories.summary: Ethiopia assumed the chairship of the African Union Peace and Security Council for April 2026, marking its first time leading the body since rejoining the council in April 2025.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Justice Reforms Revise Various Laws, Strengthen Institutional Independence - Ministry of Justice
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Ministry of Justice announced that various laws and regulations have been amended under a national reform initiative aimed at strengthening the justice system and empowering democratic institutions. The reforms were detailed in a statement from Addis Ababa.

stories.title: Russian Fighter Jet Crashes in Annexed Crimea
stories.summary: A Russian fighter jet crashed in Russian-annexed Crimea on the Black Sea peninsula, marking the second military aircraft crash there in the same week.

stories.title: The Lost Children of Minab
stories.summary: One month after missiles struck a school in the Iranian port town of Minab, a report examines the impact on children and the local community affected by the attack.

stories.title: Israel threatens to destroy more Lebanon bridges as crisis mounts
stories.summary: Israel has threatened to destroy additional bridges in Lebanon as its military invasion of the country's south expands. The escalation has driven further displacement and deadly attacks on Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Russian troops keep crawling through the pipelines. Ukraine’s drone units have every exit covered.
stories.summary: Ukraine's "Eyes" battalion has integrated pipeline networks into its real-time surveillance systems to monitor Russian troops attempting to infiltrate through the infrastructure. The unit watches for engineering modifications and infiltration preparations at pipeline exits.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Peacemaking Is a Setback for India
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a mediator in the Iran war, a diplomatic move that an analysis says sidelines India's regional influence. Islamabad's peacemaking role represents a setback for New Delhi's strategic standing.

stories.title: Hamas presses for full Israeli withdrawal in Cairo visit
stories.summary: A Hamas delegation visited Cairo and insisted that Israel must fully withdraw and comply with the terms of the existing truce before any disarmament discussions. The delegation highlighted the dire humanitarian conditions in the territories.

stories.title: Ukraine confirms strike on Bashneft-Novoil refinery in Ufa
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on the Bashneft-Novoil oil refinery in Ufa, Bashkortostan, Russia. Ukrainian forces also struck the Kulikovsky training ground and an ammunition depot in the Russian-occupied part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Iranian army begins search for pilot of downed US jet: Reports
stories.summary: Iran's army began searching for the pilot of a US F-35 jet shot down over Iranian territory on Friday, according to Fars news agency. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the jet was launched from a British base in Suffolk, England. It is the second F-35 downed by Iran since the war began.

stories.title: Filmmaker Ilker Catak’s ‘Yellow Letters’ pits artists against the powerful
stories.summary: Filmmaker Ilker Catak discussed his political thriller "Yellow Letters," which won the top prize at the Berlin Film Festival. The film explores authoritarianism and censorship, drawing from a Turkish setting but offering a broader warning about threats to artistic and fundamental freedoms.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kharkiv: One dead, seven wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Shevchenkivskyi district of Kharkiv with a drone, killing one person and wounding seven others.

stories.title: Iran Is the Dumb, Disastrous Remake of Desert Storm
stories.summary: An analysis characterizes the U.S. military campaign in Iran as a poorly executed attempt to replicate the 1991 Gulf War, arguing that the current international environment does not support such an approach.

stories.title: How a Russian influence network is spreading anti-Ukrainian propaganda in Ivory Coast
stories.summary: An investigation by FRANCE 24 and an international journalist consortium revealed that a Russian influence network called "The Company" has been running a propaganda campaign against the Ukrainian embassy in Ivory Coast, using disinformation operations documented in leaked files.

stories.title: US fighter jet shot down over Iran
stories.summary: A U.S. fighter jet was shot down over Iran, and a search and rescue operation has been launched to locate survivors. No further details on the aircraft type or crew status were immediately provided.

stories.title: From 250 to 700 dollars per article: How Russia influenced West African media content
stories.summary: Leaked documents reveal that a Russian agent network paid between $250 and $700 per article to place hundreds of propaganda pieces in 35 West African French-language media outlets. The FRANCE 24 Observers team and the Forbidden Stories consortium analyzed the documents.

stories.title: 'They're sending us to die:' Hezbollah operatives express fear, exasperation with war effort
stories.summary: Hezbollah operatives have reportedly expressed fear and frustration with the group's war effort. Members of the Radwan unit said fighters are being sent on missions against their will, with one stating that leaving home is involuntary.

stories.title: US mercenary 'paid millions to carry out killings for UAE'
stories.summary: Court documents cited by the New York Post reveal that former US special forces commando Abraham Golan allegedly made millions of dollars carrying out assassinations for the United Arab Emirates in Yemen. Yemeni lawmaker Anssaf Ali Mayo, who survived an alleged assassination attempt, named Golan as a defendant.

stories.title: Ukrainian factories join France’s Alstom in building 55 locomotives for Ukraine
stories.summary: Manufacturers from seven Ukrainian oblasts have been selected by France's Alstom to produce components for 55 UA8AC freight locomotives destined for Ukraine's rail network, in a joint industrial collaboration.

stories.title: One killed, one injured as Russian attack damages apartment blocks, vet clinic in Kyiv region
stories.summary: Russia's large-scale attack on April 3 damaged apartment blocks and a veterinary clinic in the Kyiv region, killing one person and injuring another. Damage was recorded in the Bucha, Fastiv, and Obukhiv districts.

stories.title: Reward promised for capture of F-35 pilot, says Turkish outlet
stories.summary: A Turkish social media outlet, Clash Report, reported that Iranian state TV announced a reward for anyone who captures alive the US pilot of an F-35 jet shot down over Iran on Friday. Middle East Eye said it was unable to immediately verify the report.

stories.title: For acquisition reform to succeed, the Pentagon needs civilian agency budget flexibilities
stories.summary: Defense policy analyst Bill Greenwalt argues that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth's efforts to accelerate and commercialize Pentagon acquisition processes require Congress to grant the Department of Defense the same flexible budget authorities currently available to civilian agencies.

stories.title: Northern Ireland leads surge in fuel prices since start of Iran war
stories.summary: Petrol has risen 19% and diesel 35%, while in England the north has had the sharpest increasesFuel prices have risen faster in Northern Ireland than in any other UK region since the beginning of the I

stories.title: China’s gravity-detecting SQUID gets closer to spotting US nuclear submarines
stories.summary:
Chinese researchers unveiled a gravity detector with world-leading precision last month, potentially expanding the military applications of the technology.
It uses a superconducting quantum interferen

stories.title: US mercenary 'was paid millions to carry out killings for UAE in Yemen'
stories.summary: Court documents reportedly show that former US special forces commando Abraham Golan admitted to carrying out assassinations sanctioned by the UAE in Yemen. The revelations emerged from legal filings related to the attempted killing of a Yemeni lawmaker.

stories.title: EPA moves to designate microplastics and pharmaceuticals as contaminants in drinking water
stories.summary: Proposal, a win for RFK Jr’s Maha movement, is a ‘first step’ toward tackling plastic pollution, advocates sayThe Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposed on Thursday to include microplastics an

stories.title: In Sumy region, enemy attacks car and motor cultivator, killing two men
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Sumy region, Russian troops attacked a civilian car and a motor cultivator, killing two men. The strikes targeted civilians in the frontline border region.

stories.title: Border town of Tiné caught in the crossfire as Sudan war spills into Chad
stories.summary: A drone strike in mid-March killed 20 people in the Chadian border town of Tiné, marking the fourth and deadliest cross-border attack from Sudan. Neither the Sudanese army nor the Rapid Support Forces have claimed responsibility. Chad's military has been placed on maximum alert as civilians flee the area.

stories.title: Iran fires multiple cluster munitions at Israel, wounding 1; Tehran claims to down US jet
stories.summary: Iran fired multiple cluster munitions at central Israel and the Haifa area, wounding at least one person and causing damage. Tehran also claimed to have downed a US jet, with two American air crew members reported missing. The UN is set to debate a plan regarding the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: MI6 assesses current frontline situation as Ukraine's best in past ten months – Zelensky
stories.summary: British intelligence agency MI6 has assessed the current frontline situation as the most favorable for Ukraine in the past ten months, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, though conditions on the front remain difficult overall.

stories.title: Israel plans 'Yellow Line' in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military proposed establishing a "Yellow Line" in southern Lebanon modeled on its approach in Gaza, involving the seizure of territory and demolition of villages to create a deep defensive buffer zone. Officials said disarming Hezbollah was not a realistic objective.

stories.title: A lost 1943 novel envisioned the still-unfolding Holocaust. Now, it has been recovered
stories.summary: Friedrich Torberg's 1943 novel "Vengeance is Mine," written by the Austrian refugee, depicted Nazi concentration camps with striking accuracy despite the author never having been imprisoned in one. The lost work has been recovered and is being translated into English for the first time.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts rocket toward the moon after spending a day around Earth
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew, comprising three American astronauts and one Canadian, fired their engines for translunar injection approximately 25 hours after liftoff. The maneuver set the spacecraft on course for a lunar flyby early next week, marking the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since the Apollo era.

stories.title: In Pokrovsk sector, paratroopers kill Russians on motorcycles with assault rifles, says commander of Air Assault Forces
stories.summary: In the Pokrovsk sector of eastern Ukraine, soldiers from Ukraine's Air Assault Forces have been engaging Russian troops advancing on motorcycles, using automatic rifles to neutralize them.

stories.title: Israel plans 'Yellow Line' model in Lebanon by razing southern villages
stories.summary: The Israeli army proposed creating a buffer zone inside Lebanese territory by razing southern villages, replicating its Gaza "Yellow Line" model. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich stated that the Litani River should become Israel's new border as the war with Hezbollah escalates.

stories.title: Asian nations ramp up coal power amid Middle East energy crunch
stories.summary: Asian nations are accelerating coal-fired power generation in response to energy supply disruptions linked to restricted access through the Strait of Hormuz amid the Middle East conflict. The shift to coal risks undermining international climate commitments.

stories.title: French, South Korean leaders say they'll work together on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: French and South Korean leaders met at a summit in Seoul and agreed to cooperate on issues related to the Strait of Hormuz. The meeting took place as U.S. President Donald Trump criticized allied nations for insufficient support in the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: UK deploys Rapid Sentry anti-drone air defence system to Kuwait
stories.summary: The United Kingdom deployed its Rapid Sentry anti-drone air defense system to Kuwait following drone strikes on a power and desalination plant and the Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery. Kuwait is located approximately 80 kilometers from Iran.

stories.title: Congo declares end of two-year mpox outbreak that killed over 2,000
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the end of a two-year mpox outbreak that infected thousands and claimed more than 2,200 lives, according to health officials.

stories.title: Russia launched nearly 500 drones, cruise missiles at Ukraine on Friday – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reported that Russia launched nearly 500 drones and cruise missiles against Ukraine on a single Friday, coinciding with Ukraine's proposal for an Easter ceasefire that Moscow rejected.

stories.title: First French ship passes through Hormuz since start of war
stories.summary: A French-owned container ship became the first French vessel to pass through the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, after signaling its French ownership. A Japanese LNG tanker was also granted safe passage earlier on Friday. French President Macron had previously advocated diplomacy to end the blockage.

stories.title: Mass Outage Hits Sberbank and Other Major Russian Lenders
stories.summary: Sberbank and other major Russian financial institutions experienced a mass service outage, with customers reporting problems making payments and transferring money beginning around 10 a.m. Moscow time.

stories.title: Ukraine to finalize security guarantees document in coming days, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukraine will finalize its security guarantees document in the coming days after resolving remaining questions. A U.S. delegation may travel to Kyiv once the documents are agreed upon.

stories.title: Three teenagers arrested after 14-year-old boy shot dead in south-east London
stories.summary: Boys aged 14 and 16 and 18-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder after shooting in WoolwichPolice have launched a murder investigation after a 14-year-old boy was fatally shot in Woolwich, sout

stories.title: US can take Strait of Hormuz ‘with more time’, says Trump
stories.summary:
President Donald ⁠Trump on Friday said the ⁠US can open the Strait of Hormuz with a little more time, as pressure mounts for his administration to find a ‌quick resolution to a war against Iran.
“With

stories.title: Ukraine says six killed in 'massive' Russian daytime attacks
stories.summary: Russian forces launched massive daytime attacks across Ukraine, killing at least six people. In the Kyiv region, one person was killed and eight were wounded, according to regional governor Mykola Kalashnyk.

stories.title: Experts dispute US account of deadly Iran sports hall strike in Lamerd
stories.summary: Six weapons experts have disputed the US military's claim that video evidence indicates an Iranian missile struck a sports hall in Lamerd, Iran, challenging the official American account of the deadly strike.

stories.title: ‘Detect, deploy, reassure’: NYC Jewish security group launches patrols as threats abound
stories.summary: The Community Security Service, a Jewish security organization in New York City, launched street patrols aimed at detecting threats and reassuring Jewish communities. The initiative provides what organizers describe as a subtle additional layer of security amid rising threats.

stories.title: Drone strike hits aid warehouse, says Red Cross
stories.summary: A drone strike in Iran's southern Bushehr province destroyed two containers, two buses, and emergency vehicles at an aid warehouse, according to the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. The IFRC did not assign blame and noted it has lost three responders during the conflict.

stories.title: Islamist rebels kill at least 43 in overnight raid in DR Congo
stories.summary: At least 43 people have been killed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo after militants linked to the Islamic State launched a deadly overnight raid, local officials said on Thursday.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts approach 100,000 miles from Earth on voyage to the moon
stories.summary: Capsule’s engine fires up for six minutes, putting crew on track to reach  farthest distance travelled by humans in spaceThe four astronauts on the Artemis II mission are approaching 100,000 miles fro

stories.title: In Oleksandrivka sector, paratroopers liberate 11 settlements
stories.summary: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces units operating in the Oleksandrivka sector have liberated 11 settlements. All civilians had previously been evacuated from the areas.

stories.title: F-35 jet shot down by Iran came from British base in Suffolk, says IRGC
stories.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that a US F-35 jet shot down over Iran was launched from RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, eastern England. The incident drew attention to the British base, which the US is believed to be using to conduct strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine's Easter ceasefire proposal still on the table
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukraine's proposal for an Easter ceasefire remains on the table and that the request has been communicated to the United States for relay to Russia.

stories.title: Trump’s anger over Iran thrusts NATO into fresh crisis
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has declared he is considering withdrawing the United States from NATO amid escalating tensions over Iran, thrusting the alliance into a fresh crisis.

stories.title: Glide bomb kills one in Shostka apartment block as Russia batters Ukrainian cities—newborn among five wounded in Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian glide bomb struck an apartment block in Shostka, killing one person, while five people including a newborn were wounded in Kharkiv. Russia targeted at least five Ukrainian oblasts overnight using ballistic missiles, guided aerial bombs, and strike drones.

stories.title: Inside India's courts, AI's growing role sparks concern
stories.summary: The increasing use of artificial intelligence in courtrooms raises worries that the technology may aggravate bias and structural distortions in the legal system.

stories.title: Is the US committing war crimes by targeting Iran’s civilian infrastructure?
stories.summary: International law experts ‘seriously concerned’ about ‘strikes on schools, health centres and homes’ in contravention of Geneva conventionsDonald Trump, other senior US officials and their cheerleader

stories.title: Burkina Faso’s Traoré rejects democracy, extends military rule
stories.summary: Nearly four years after seizing power, Burkina Faso’s military leader Ibrahim Traoré is calling on citizens to abandon democratic ideals.

stories.title: Limited Good Friday ceremony held at Holy Sepulchre as Israel bans worshippers
stories.summary: The Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem led a scaled-down Good Friday ceremony at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre with only about 15 clergy members. Israeli authorities barred the public from attending, imposing sweeping restrictions across occupied East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Limited Good Friday ceremony held at Holy Sepulchre as Israel bans worshippers
stories.summary: Israel has barred Christian and Muslim worshippers from accessing Jerusalem's holy sites for over a month. A limited Good Friday ceremony was held at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre on April 3, 2026, with pilgrims praying outside its closed doors.

stories.title: Global food prices climb again in March, the second straight monthly rise
stories.summary: Global food prices rose for a second straight month in March, driven mainly by higher energy costs linked to the conflict in the Near East. That’s according to the latest Food Price Index from the UN’

stories.title: Japanese LNG tanker crosses Hormuz
stories.summary: The Panama-flagged LNG tanker Sohar LNG, co-owned by Japan's Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, transited the Strait of Hormuz with all crew safe. Japanese media reported it was the first Japanese vessel to exit the strait since the war began.

stories.title: How the US and Israel are waging war on Iran’s medicines, vaccines
stories.summary: The Pasteur Institute of Iran has been targeted as part of US and Israeli actions affecting healthcare facilities in Iran, raising concerns about the impact on the country's access to medicines and vaccines.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian EW system worth $20M on Zaporizhzhia front
stories.summary: National Guard of Ukraine special drone unit Lasar's Group destroyed a Russian Palantin electronic warfare system valued at approximately $20 million on the Zaporizhzhia front, operating in coordination with adjacent units.

stories.title: Sweden finds a 12 km oil slick east of Gotland — boards sanctioned “shadow fleet” tanker
stories.summary: Swedish authorities discovered a 12-kilometer oil slick east of Gotland and boarded the Flora 1, a sanctioned tanker linked to Russia's so-called shadow fleet. The vessel, with unclear flag status, is now anchored near Ystad as prosecutors investigate potential environmental crimes.

stories.title: Iran warns UN Security Council against ‘provocative action’ on Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged the UN Security Council to avoid what he called provocative action regarding the Strait of Hormuz. His remarks came ahead of a scheduled Security Council vote on a draft resolution to mandate a force to protect shipping through the strait.

stories.title: Russians storming Pokrovsk agglomeration in small groups and on ATVs, says Shapoval
stories.summary: Russian forces have intensified assault operations in the Pokrovsk-Myrnohrad agglomeration in eastern Ukraine, deploying small groups using light vehicles including ATVs and attempting flanking advances toward Hryshyne and Rodynske, according to Ukrainian commander Shapoval.

stories.title: UN lauds efforts by Indian peacekeepers in opening key corridor in South Sudan
stories.summary: The United Nations praised Indian peacekeepers for opening a key corridor in South Sudan. As of January 2026, India was the largest troop-contributing country to the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS), with 1,779 personnel deployed.

stories.title: Strikes hit Lebanon as Israel vows to occupy swathe of south after war
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit near Beirut's main airport road in Lebanon, prompting an urgent UN Security Council session after three peacekeepers were killed in southern Lebanon. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz declared that Israeli forces would maintain an occupation of a swathe of southern Lebanon even after the war against Hezbollah concludes.

stories.title: At least 12 injured by missile debris after interception in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: At least 12 people were injured in Abu Dhabi's Ajban area after debris from a successfully intercepted missile fell to the ground. The Abu Dhabi Media Office confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Real Madrid coach insists Spain ‘not racist’ despite Islamophobic chant
stories.summary: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal spoke out against Islamophobic chants directed at him during Spain's match against Egypt. Real Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti responded by insisting that Spain is not a racist country.

stories.title: US jobs market surpassed expectations in March but February losses were worse than first reported
stories.summary: U.S. employers added 178,000 jobs in March, surpassing economists' expectations of roughly 70,000, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.3%. February's job losses were revised downward, showing a sharper contraction than initially reported.

stories.title: 8 killed, 95 wounded in US-Israeli attacks on Iran bridge
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli missile strikes targeted the B1 bridge in Karaj, the capital of Iran's Alborz province, killing at least eight civilians and wounding 95 others. Iran's official IRNA news agency reported the bridge, one of the tallest in the Middle East, was struck twice on Thursday.

stories.title: Iran`s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it struck US F-35 jet
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it struck a U.S. F-35 stealth fighter jet over central Iran on Thursday. The claim was reported from Tehran, though independent verification was not immediately available.

stories.title: East Asia’s crisis of confidence in the US is militarising China’s backyard
stories.summary: The dust and debris of the US-Israeli war on Iran have yet to settle, but its strategic shock waves have reached East Asia. From Tokyo to Taipei, a reassessment is under way. The conflict, intended to

stories.title: US vows to target more Iranian infrastructure as nations seek to open Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States has pledged to target additional Iranian infrastructure as international efforts continue to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Negotiations conducted through intermediaries with new Iranian leaders have shown limited progress.

stories.title: Sahel sees drop in terror attacks, but remains global epicenter of extremism
stories.summary: The 2026 Global Terrorism Index is showing a mixed picture in the Sahel, offering a glimpse of progress, but also a stark reminder of ongoing risks.

stories.title: Gaza health minister warns of disease risk as Israeli siege continues
stories.summary: Gaza Health Minister Majid Abu Ramadan warned of mounting disease risks across the Strip as Israel's siege continues. He said widespread destruction, untreated waste, and rubble have fueled a surge in rodents, raising the threat of illnesses including hantavirus, plague, and leptospirosis.

stories.title: Seven injured after train derails in Russia: local media
stories.summary: A train derailed in Russia's Ulyanovsk region, approximately 900 kilometers east of Moscow, injuring seven people. Local media reported the incident, though further details on the cause were not immediately available.

stories.title: Zelensky: Intelligence warns Russia may target railways and water supply systems
stories.summary: President Zelensky disclosed that Ukrainian intelligence has warned Russia may target the country's railway network and water supply infrastructure, including bridges, dams, hydroelectric power plants, and pumping stations. Ukraine is working to strengthen protection of these systems.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published Shabbat candle lighting times for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: In Sumy, injury toll after Russian strikes climbs to four
stories.summary: The number of people wounded in Russian strikes on the city of Sumy in northeastern Ukraine rose to four following attacks earlier in the day.

stories.title: Overcrowded, understaffed, overpriced: Kyiv’s wartime kiosk wave collapses
stories.summary: Kyiv's wartime boom in commercial kiosks has collapsed due to market oversaturation, declining consumer purchasing power, labor shortages, and rising electricity costs.

stories.title: War crimes are no longer shameful. That should terrify you
stories.summary: Warring parties in the latest Middle East escalation have shown disregard for civilian life, with observers noting that violations of international humanitarian law are increasingly met without accountability or public condemnation.

stories.title: These are Iran’s key islands in the Gulf
stories.summary: Several of Iran's roughly 400 islands hold strategic importance, particularly those located in the Persian Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz. The strait is a vital global chokepoint through which approximately a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passes.

stories.title: MSF condemns 'appalling' attack on Sudan hospital
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières condemned an attack on a hospital in Sudan as "appalling." The organization expressed outrage over repeated and escalating attacks on healthcare facilities in recent weeks.

stories.title: Cuba to pardon more than 2,000 prisoners as US eases fuel blockade
stories.summary: Havana calls releases a Holy Week humanitarian gesture as Russian tanker is allowed to reach oil-starved islandCuba has announced plans to pardon 2,010 prisoners as a “humanitarian” gesture during Hol

stories.title: Suicide car bomb blast kills five in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: A suicide car bomb attack targeted a police station in northwest Pakistan, killing five people. Preliminary information indicates the police station was the primary target of the bombing.

stories.title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing elected President by pro-military parliament
stories.summary: Myanmar's pro-military parliament elected junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as president. The 69-year-old general led the 2021 coup that ousted Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, triggering mass protests and armed resistance across the country.
