stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Urged to Lift Constraints On Aviation Revenues As Khartoum Airport Reopens
stories.summary: Khartoum airport has reopened for air traffic after years of disruption caused by Sudan's civil war. Advocates are urging the Sudanese government to ease restrictions on aviation revenues to support the sector's recovery.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Displacement Surges As Blue Nile Clashes Compounds Suffering
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported a surge in displacement in Sudan's Blue Nile region due to intensifying clashes between the Sudan Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces, and the SPLM-N faction led by Abdelaziz El Hilu.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: The article references the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping lane. No further details were available from the source material.

stories.title: France bans planned gathering of Muslims in Paris area, citing security risk
stories.summary: French authorities banned a planned Muslim gathering in the Paris area, citing security concerns. The decision came after France heightened security at sensitive sites across Paris following a foiled bomb attack targeting Bank of America offices.

stories.title: Cubans take to bikes and electric tricycles to protest US sanctions
stories.summary: Cuban activists, accompanied by President Miguel Díaz-Canel, paraded on bicycles and electric tricycles along Havana's Malecón boulevard on Thursday. The demonstration was a protest against US sanctions that activists say are designed to deprive Cuba of fuel supplies.

stories.title: How China Reinvented the BRI
stories.summary: Western tariffs have accelerated the transformation of China's Belt and Road Initiative into a more sophisticated extension of Beijing's industrial policy, according to an analysis of BRI's evolution.

stories.title: A day in the life of Asia’s fuel crisis
stories.summary: An oil crisis triggered by the war in Iran is causing widespread fuel disruptions across Asia. Effects are being felt from farms in New Zealand to factories in Delhi, impacting daily life and industry across the region.

stories.title: Hong Kong police on the hunt for 2 men who attacked taxi driver after quarrel
stories.summary: Hong Kong police are searching for two non-ethnic Chinese men who allegedly attacked a 57-year-old taxi driver in Yuen Long after a quarrel over a blocked road. The suspects fled the scene following the early-morning incident.

stories.title: Canadian woman held with daughter by ICE is released after nearly three weeks of detention
stories.summary: Canadian citizen Tania Warner and her seven-year-old daughter Ayla Luca were released from U.S. ICE detention after nearly three weeks, upon posting a $9,500 bond. Warner, originally from British Columbia, was fitted with an ankle monitor and deemed not a flight risk.

stories.title: Golden Dome, ships and missiles top Trump’s $1.9 trillion fiscal 2027 defence wish list
stories.summary: President Trump's fiscal 2027 defense budget request totals $1.9 trillion, representing the largest year-over-year increase in defense spending since World War II. Key priorities include the Golden Dome missile defense system, naval ships, and missiles.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts leave Earth's orbit, rocket towards moon
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II crew has left Earth's orbit and begun their trajectory toward the Moon after a successful thruster firing. The mission marks the first time humans have traveled to the Moon in over 50 years.

stories.title: Russians intensify forced draft in Luhansk
stories.summary: Russian occupation forces have intensified forced conscription in the temporarily occupied city of Luhansk in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: ICE arrests West Bank-born Wisconsin mosque president over terror funding suspicions
stories.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested Salah Sarsour, president of a Wisconsin mosque and a West Bank native, on suspicions of terror funding. Sarsour, who was convicted of rock-throwing as a teenager in Israel, moved to the U.S. in 1993. His lawyers say the arrest targets pro-Palestinian advocacy.

stories.title: US strikes on Iran may constitute war crimes, international law experts announce
stories.summary: International law experts stated that U.S. strikes on Iran may constitute war crimes. President Trump had previously offered shifting timelines and objectives for the conflict and warned of further escalation if Tehran did not accept Washington's terms.

stories.title: UN set to vote on a watered-down proposal to open Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to vote on a diluted resolution aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. China and Russia have opposed stronger versions of the proposal.

stories.title: Lebanese artist files war crimes complaint against Israel over death of parents in Beirut - report
stories.summary: Lebanese contemporary artist Cherri, whose work has appeared in galleries including the Guggenheim, filed a war crimes complaint against Israel over the killing of his parents in a strike on Beirut.

stories.title: Hongkongers opt for mainland Chinese tours during Easter amid Middle East war
stories.summary: More Hong Kong residents are choosing mainland China tours during Easter, with outbound tour groups to the mainland rising 30 percent year on year. The shift is partly driven by disrupted air traffic due to the ongoing Middle East conflict.

stories.title: UN to vote on using 'all defensive means' to secure navigation in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Nations is preparing to vote on a resolution authorizing the use of "all defensive means" to secure navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier drafts had included language permitting "all necessary means," which in UN terminology can encompass military action to deter interference with international shipping.

stories.title: In Sumy and Chernihiv regions, Russians drop counterfeit money with QR codes from drones
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped counterfeit banknotes embedded with QR codes from drones over Ukraine's Sumy and Chernihiv regions, likely as a psychological or intelligence-gathering operation.

stories.title: Paris police ban French Muslim gathering, citing security risk
stories.summary: Paris police banned the annual gathering of French Muslims scheduled north of the capital on Thursday, citing a "major terrorist risk" that the event could be targeted.

stories.title: Iran vows retaliation after deadly US strike on bridge in Karaj
stories.summary: Iranian officials vowed retaliation after a U.S. strike destroyed a major bridge in Karaj, described as the country's largest. Tehran pledged to rebuild the bridge while condemning Washington's military actions.

stories.title: Middle East live: UN Security Council to vote on force to protect Hormuz access
stories.summary: The UN Security Council is set to vote on a U.S.-backed draft resolution authorizing a defensive force to protect shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The measure responds to Iranian disruptions of the vital global trade route amid rising tensions over energy supplies.

stories.title: Iran vows 'crushing' attacks as strikes hit regional infrastructure
stories.summary: Iran and its regional allies exchanged fire with Israel and the United States, with strikes hitting energy facilities and civilian infrastructure. American-linked assets across the Middle East were also targeted.

stories.title: Will Philippines’ anti-disinformation bills empower state to ‘decide the truth’?
stories.summary: The Philippines is considering anti-disinformation legislation, but digital rights advocates warn the proposals could grant the government sweeping powers to determine what constitutes truth while failing to address actual influence campaign networks.

stories.title: Leapmotor targets global growth with Europe R&D hub, eyes Canada assembly
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Leapmotor, backed by Stellantis, is establishing a research and development hub in Europe and exploring assembly operations in Canada. The company raised its overseas sales target by 50 percent amid growing global demand.

stories.title: Could China’s metal-like composite make drones, planes and rockets 26% stronger?
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have proposed a new composite material manufacturing method that could increase the strength of structures used in drones, aircraft, and spacecraft by up to 26 percent. The technique improves the balanced lay-up approach for stacking fibre layers.

stories.title: Trump hails destruction of Iran’s tallest bridge, warns of ‘much more to follow’
stories.summary: President Trump announced the destruction of Iran's tallest bridge, the B1 in Alborz province near Karaj. Iranian officials reported eight people killed and 95 wounded in the strike. Trump had earlier threatened to bomb Iran back to the Stone Ages.

stories.title: Germany bans planned rally against Israel’s ‘genocide’ at Buchenwald former Nazi camp
stories.summary: German authorities banned a planned protest rally at the former Buchenwald Nazi concentration camp that was to denounce Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide. Organizers appealed the ban in court. Jewish leaders condemned the event as an attempt to relativize the Holocaust.

stories.title: Russian court sentences former lawmaker to 19 years in prison over antisemitic pogrom at airport
stories.summary: Dagestan's Supreme Court sentenced former Russian State Duma deputy Ilya Ponomarev in absentia to 19 years in prison for his role in the antisemitic pogrom at Makhachkala airport in October 2023.

stories.title: The long and lingering shadow of war
stories.summary: The article examines the long-term consequences of violent conflict, noting that the effects of war persist for years even after a ceasefire is declared. Communities face prolonged challenges in recovery and healing well beyond the cessation of active hostilities.

stories.title: Education Minister slams 'extremist, deranged criminals' for trying to enter his home during siren
stories.summary: Israeli Education Minister Yoav Kisch was confronted by individuals attempting to enter his home during an air raid siren. One person, identifying as a teacher, blamed Kisch for the Iranian missile attack and demanded protection.

stories.title: Hegseth fires US Army chief of staff, sources say, shaking up Pentagon amid Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed General Randy George as U.S. Army chief of staff amid an ongoing American military buildup in the Middle East related to the Iran conflict. No official reason was given for the dismissal. Reports suggest the FBI director may also face removal.

stories.title: Pakistan says onus on Afghanistan to end hostilities
stories.summary: Pakistan stated that the responsibility for ending cross-border hostilities lies with Afghanistan. The two countries held preliminary talks aimed at de-escalating their border conflict.

stories.title: Don’t let geopolitical rivalry skew debate over Jimmy Lai’s sentencing
stories.summary: The article discusses the sentencing of Hong Kong media figure Jimmy Lai to 20 years' imprisonment on charges including conspiracy to collude with foreign forces. Western officials have cited the case as evidence of decline in Hong Kong's legal system.

stories.title: 50 minutes, 50,000 calls, US$1.2 million lost: Singapore’s high-speed scam
stories.summary: Singapore police uncovered a scam operation in which a Malaysian electrician set up devices in a rented house that blasted over 50,000 automated scam calls in 50 minutes, targeting approximately 18,000 phone numbers. The scheme resulted in losses of around US$1.2 million.

stories.title: Two NSW teenagers charged over violent extremist material allegedly linked to terror
stories.summary: Two teenagers aged 15 and 16 from Moree in northern New South Wales, Australia, were charged by Australian federal police and NSW police with possessing violent extremist material. Officers reportedly found a ballistic-style vest, notebooks, and literature containing alleged extremist references during a home search.

stories.title: Ukraine's defense tech market reaches $6.8B in 2025
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense technology market reached approximately $6.8 billion in 2025, with unmanned aerial vehicles accounting for the largest share of the sector.

stories.title: Hegseth asked US Army chief of staff to step down
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked General Randy George to step down from his position as chief of staff of the U.S. Army. An official confirmed the request on Thursday but no public reason was provided.

stories.title: Britain says 40 countries discuss reopening Strait of Hormuz after Iran blockade
stories.summary: Representatives from approximately 40 countries convened discussions, facilitated by Britain, on reopening the Strait of Hormuz following Iran's blockade. The United States, whose February 28 strikes on Iran triggered the war that closed the strait, was not involved in the talks.

stories.title: France bans annual gathering of Muslims in Paris amid terrorism fears, security risks
stories.summary: France banned an annual Muslim gathering in Paris, citing terrorism fears and security risks. The decision followed increased security at sensitive sites across Paris after a foiled bomb attack on Bank of America's offices, linked to tensions surrounding the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: More Hongkongers to travel over long Easter break despite higher costs
stories.summary: More Hong Kong residents are expected to travel during the five-day Easter break despite rising fuel surcharges. Tour groups to the Middle East have been cancelled until October due to the ongoing conflict, redirecting travel demand to other destinations.

stories.title: Chinese man uses septic tank trucks on wedding day; bride happily embraces unique choice
stories.summary: In Suixi county, Anhui province, China, groom Pan Haonan used nine septic tank trucks as his wedding convoy on March 28, drawing on his family's sewage removal business. Video of the event went viral on Chinese social media, garnering 5 million views.

stories.title: French police ban Muslim gathering near Paris over fears far-right groups could target it
stories.summary: French police banned an annual Muslim gathering planned near Paris, citing a "major terrorist risk" in the context of heightened international and domestic tensions. Authorities expressed concern that far-right groups could target the event.

stories.title: Firm backed by Trump sons tries to sell drone interceptors to Gulf states being attacked by Iran
stories.summary: Florida-based drone manufacturer Powerus, which announced a partnership with Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr., is seeking to sell drone interceptors to Gulf states under Iranian attack. Critics note the company could profit from a war initiated by their father, President Trump.

stories.title: Govt hikes petrol price to Rs458 per litre, HSD price to Rs520 per litre
stories.summary: Pakistan's Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced sharp fuel price increases, raising petrol to Rs458.4 per litre and high-speed diesel to Rs520.35 per litre. The hikes of Rs137.24 and Rs184.49 per litre respectively took effect on Friday. Kerosene prices also rose by Rs34.08 to Rs457.80 per litre.

stories.title: Democrats pay visit to ICE detention facility where abuse claims rife
stories.summary: Two California Democratic House members, including Representative Mike Levin, conducted an oversight visit at ICE's Otay Mesa detention center, which faces allegations of overcrowding, poor conditions, and sexual assaults. Levin indicated he plans additional unannounced visits following a court ruling on congressional access.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth allows troops to carry personal firearms on military bases
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a memo allowing military service members to request permission to carry personal firearms on military installations, including bases, naval yards, and recruitment centers. The policy is framed as enabling personnel to defend themselves in case of an attack.

stories.title: Hamas wants guarantees of Israeli troop withdrawal before disarmament talks, sources say
stories.summary: Hamas told mediators it will not discuss disarmament without guarantees that Israel will fully withdraw from Gaza, as outlined in a plan from US President Trump's "Board of Peace." The group's position was conveyed through three sources to Reuters in Cairo.

stories.title: War Diary Day 34: Trump’s speech deepens escalation, pushing war into prolonged phase
stories.summary: On the 34th day of the US-Israel military campaign against Iran, President Trump's speech hardened positions rather than opening paths to de-escalation. Trump declared objectives were nearing completion while committing to two to three more weeks of intensified strikes. Iran responded with swift retaliatory action.

stories.title: Hamas wants Israeli troop withdrawal before disarmament talks
stories.summary: Hamas informed mediators that it will not enter discussions about disarmament unless Israel provides guarantees of a full military withdrawal from Gaza, as outlined in a proposed disarmament plan.

stories.title: Ukrainian rail worker jailed for 8 years for spying on Ukrainian forces in Sumy region for Russia's FSB
stories.summary: A Ukrainian court sentenced a railway worker to eight years in prison for spying for Russia's FSB. The worker tracked deployment sites and flight schedules of Ukrainian military aviation units in the Sumy region.

stories.title: Uruguayan national admits to scheme to circumvent US sanctions linked to Venezuela
stories.summary: A 60-year-old Uruguayan citizen pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court on March 25 to conspiring to run an unlicensed money transmitting business to circumvent American sanctions linked to Venezuelan government officials.

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian flotilla's new Gaza mission to start on April 12
stories.summary: A pro-Palestinian flotilla announced it will launch a new mission to reach Gaza on April 12. The group previously attempted to sail to the enclave last year.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy offers expertise on keeping waterways open amid Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered Ukraine's expertise in maritime security and reopening sea lanes to countries working to keep the Strait of Hormuz open. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha participated in a virtual meeting on the issue attended by approximately 40 countries.

stories.title: US Army Chief of Staff asked to step down by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked the Army Chief of Staff to step down. Hegseth, a former Fox News host, has been moving to reshape the Defense Department by firing top generals and admirals as part of President Trump's national security agenda.

stories.title: 'Alarming' risk of long-term mass displacement in Lebanon: IOM
stories.summary: The head of the International Organization for Migration warned of an "alarming" risk of long-term mass displacement in Lebanon resulting from the ongoing conflict between Hezbollah and Israel.

stories.title: Watch: Who is the coup leader who will be Myanmar's next president?
stories.summary: Myanmar's military leader Min Aung Hlaing presided over his final military parade before transitioning to the role of president, consolidating his authority after seizing power in a coup.

stories.title: Legal experts warn US role in war raises risk of international law violations
stories.summary: More than 100 US-based international law experts issued a letter through the Just Security Forum warning that the US-Israeli war on Iran raises "profound concern" over potential violations of the UN Charter, human rights law, and humanitarian law, including possible war crimes. They cited growing civilian harm and environmental damage.

stories.title: ‘It’s drones fighting drones’: Ukrainian officer offers inside look at roboticized war
stories.summary: A Ukrainian counter-drone officer described front-line combat increasingly dominated by unmanned systems, where drones fight drones and human soldiers remain in hiding. Survival depends on real-time adaptation to rapidly evolving robotic warfare tactics.

stories.title: Solomon Islands residents live in fear of WWII bomb explosions
stories.summary: Residents of Yandina village in the Russell Islands, Solomon Islands, continue to face health risks from unexploded World War II ordnance and chemical contamination. Families, including that of 50-year-old farmer Billy, report rashes, boils, and poisoning symptoms linked to contaminated local food sources and forested areas.

stories.title: Kharkiv hit by renewed shelling: Fire breaks out in residential area, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled Kharkiv, causing a fire in a four-story building in the Osnovianskyi district. Casualties were reported in the residential area.

stories.title: Medical needs surging in Iran and supplies under threat, Red Cross warns
stories.summary: The International Red Cross warned that medical needs are surging in Iran as US and Israeli strikes continue. More than 1,900 people have been killed and 21,000 injured since the military campaign began. Medical supplies are under increasing threat.

stories.title: Russian court convicts German sculptor in absentia for depicting Putin and patriarch in sex act
stories.summary: A Russian court convicted German sculptor Jacques Tilly in absentia for creating artwork depicting President Vladimir Putin and the Russian Orthodox patriarch in a sexual act. Tilly is known for his provocative carnival float creations.

stories.title: Six Ukrainian children to be returned from Russia and reunited with families, US says
stories.summary: The United States announced that six Ukrainian children will be returned from Russia and reunited with their families. Ukraine says close to 20,000 children have been illegally transferred to Russia and Belarus since the conflict began.

stories.title: War update: 213 clashes on frontline, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 213 combat engagements along the frontline, with the fiercest fighting in the Pokrovsk sector. Russian forces launched nearly 50 attacks on Ukrainian positions there and lost more than 130 troops.

stories.title: Kremlin aide says Strait of Hormuz remains open to Russia
stories.summary: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to Russian shipping, according to the state-run TASS news agency.

stories.title: US intelligence said to assess around half of Iran’s missile launchers are still intact
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies assessed that approximately half of Iran's missile launchers remain operational despite ongoing strikes. President Trump stated that Israel would follow his directives on attacking Iran. An Iranian cluster warhead struck central Israel, causing damage but no injuries.

stories.title: Iran war could make beer and bottled water pricier for Indians
stories.summary: The ongoing war involving Iran is disrupting raw material supply chains, affecting Indian manufacturers of plastic and glass bottles. This could raise prices for beer and bottled water in India.

stories.title: Trump to propose $1.5 trillion defense budget, banking on $350 billion from reconciliation
stories.summary: President Trump is set to propose a $1.5 trillion defense budget for fiscal year 2027, with base defense spending exceeding $1 trillion for the first time. The proposal relies on an additional $350 billion from the congressional reconciliation process.

stories.title: Pakistan says onus on Afghanistan to end hostilities
stories.summary: Pakistan has placed the onus on Afghanistan to end hostilities between the two nations. Islamabad claims Afghanistan is harboring militants responsible for cross-border attacks, an allegation the Taliban government denies. The escalating conflict has strained relations between the neighboring countries.

stories.title: Polish prosecutors to investigate attack on Polish UN soldiers in Lebanon
stories.summary: Polish prosecutors in Warsaw opened an investigation into a bomb attack that wounded a Polish soldier serving with a UN peacekeeping patrol in Lebanon. The investigation was announced by the District Prosecutor's Office on Thursday.

stories.title: Syrskyi: Fixing communication was critical to holding Kyiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that fixing communication between different military units operating on different radio frequencies was a critical challenge during the early defense of the Kyiv region.

stories.title: Palestinian dies after being shot by Israeli forces near Khan Younis
stories.summary: A Palestinian man died after being shot by Israeli forces on the outskirts of Khan Younis in Gaza, according to the Wafa news agency.

stories.title: Between war and wins: Maccabi Tel Aviv’s Euroleague playoff push fueled by resilience - interview
stories.summary: Maccabi Tel Aviv's general manager Claudio Coldebella discussed the basketball club's Euroleague playoff campaign and the resilience the team has shown during wartime conditions in an interview with Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport.

stories.title: Argentina expels Iran’s charge d’affaires
stories.summary: Argentina expelled Iran's chargé d'affaires amid escalating diplomatic tensions. Iran accused Argentine President Javier Milei of being complicit in military attacks on Iranian territory.

stories.title: AJK High Court bars detention, deportation of Afghans without due process
stories.summary: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir High Court ruled that Afghan nationals in the region cannot be detained or deported without due process of law. Justice Syed Shahid Bahar directed the government to establish a legal mechanism to regulate repatriation cases. The ruling addressed constitutional petitions challenging police detention of Afghans.

stories.title: Israel says Hezbollah chief to pay ‘heavy price’ for Jewish holiday attacks
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz warned that Hezbollah's chief would pay a "heavy price" following rocket attacks on northern Israel. Hezbollah claimed responsibility for a series of strikes timed to coincide with the start of the Jewish Passover holidays.

stories.title: Star-Spangled exodus: How MLS became a Mecca for Israeli soccer stars
stories.summary: A growing number of Israeli soccer players are moving to Major League Soccer in the United States. The trend marks a shift in how Israeli athletes view overseas careers, with MLS becoming a prominent destination.

stories.title: Kellogg calls for new defense alliance which may include Ukraine
stories.summary: Retired Lieutenant General Keith Kellogg called for the United States to create a new defense alliance that could include Ukraine, citing NATO's perceived ineffectiveness in the context of the Iran war.

stories.title: Which countries’ ships are hit by Hormuz crisis?
stories.summary: An analysis examined which countries' shipping vessels have been most affected by the crisis at the Strait of Hormuz. The reported figures may understate actual totals, as some vessels may have turned off their transponders to avoid detection.

stories.title: Houthis claim missile attack on Israel, vow further escalation
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group claimed it launched a barrage of ballistic missiles targeting what it described as vital Israeli sites. The group said the operation was coordinated with Iran and Hezbollah and vowed gradual escalation depending on developments in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Top US army officer steps down after Hegseth reportedly demanded removal
stories.summary: General Randy George, the US Army's 41st Chief of Staff, is stepping down after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reportedly demanded his immediate retirement. The Pentagon confirmed the departure, which takes effect immediately. No official reason was provided for the removal.

stories.title: Trump signs order threatening up to 100% tariffs on pharmaceuticals
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order imposing pharmaceutical tariffs that could reach 100% unless drugmakers agree to pricing deals with his administration. The move is framed around national security concerns and could significantly affect global pharmaceutical supply chains and consumer costs.

stories.title: Russia fired record number of drones in March: Ukraine air force data
stories.summary: Ukraine's air force data showed Russia launched at least 6,462 long-range drones into Ukraine in March, a record number. This represented a nearly 28 percent increase over February and marked the second consecutive monthly rise in drone attacks.

stories.title: Israeli lyricist Tzruya Lahav dies at 74 after cancer battle
stories.summary: Israeli lyricist Tzruya Lahav died at 74 after a battle with cancer. She was widely recognized for shaping popular Israeli music and writing lyrics to many songs considered part of the national canon.

stories.title: Russia will send second ship with oil to Cuba: minister
stories.summary: Russia announced it will send a second oil shipment by ship to Cuba. Cuba has been experiencing an energy crisis since January.

stories.title: Hegseth asks Army’s top general to retire immediately as Iran war rages
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked Army Chief of Staff General Randy George to retire immediately amid the ongoing US war with Iran. A Pentagon official said the Army's next leader would be aligned with Hegseth and President Trump's vision for the service.

stories.title: UN Secretary-General warns world on edge of wider war
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged all parties in the Middle East conflict to immediately cease hostilities, warning the war risks expanding across the entire region with serious global consequences.

stories.title: Report: Apple lets Russian users keep iCloud+ data after subscriptions lapse
stories.summary: Apple announced that as of April 1, payment processing for App Store and other Apple service purchases in Russia is no longer available. Russian users can reportedly retain iCloud+ data after their subscriptions lapse.

stories.title: Trump family-linked firm seeking to sell drone interceptors to Gulf states amid war
stories.summary: A drone company called Powerus, backed by Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr., is seeking to sell drone interceptors to Gulf states during the US-Israeli war on Iran. The firm is holding demonstrations across the region, showcasing equipment designed to counter Iranian attacks.

stories.title: Myanmar's coup leader who set off a brutal civil war is set to become president
stories.summary: Myanmar's military coup leader, General Min Aung Hlaing, is set to be selected as the country's next president by the newly elected parliament. Min Aung Hlaing seized power in a 2021 coup that triggered a prolonged and brutal civil war across Myanmar.

stories.title: President of Wisconsin’s largest mosque detained by US immigration agents
stories.summary: Salah Sarsour, president of Wisconsin's largest mosque and a Palestinian-born US green card holder, was detained by nearly a dozen ICE agents in Milwaukee on Monday. His attorneys allege he was targeted for his public criticism of Israel. Local officials and religious leaders have accused authorities of politically motivated enforcement.

stories.title: Three men face trial in Poland over alleged Russia‑linked arson attacks
stories.summary: Three men will stand trial in Poland over a series of arson attacks in Warsaw and the Baltic States. Polish prosecutors said the attacks were part of a Russian-orchestrated sabotage campaign targeting multiple countries.

stories.title: The US-China trade war 1 year on: who really holds the upper hand?
stories.summary: One year into the renewed US-China trade war, the two sides completed their sixth round of trade talks in Paris in March. Despite an existing truce, the broader trade dispute remains unresolved, with both Washington and Beijing continuing to navigate tensions over tariffs and economic policy.

stories.title: Work underway at 245 energy facilities nationwide as Ukraine preparing for winter – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky reported that restoration work and installation of alternative power generation are underway at 245 energy facilities across Ukraine in preparation for winter.

stories.title: Chinese drone downed in Iran, sparking questions about UAE or Saudi Arabian role
stories.summary: A Chinese-made Wing Loong II drone was shot down over Shiraz, Iran, raising questions about whether the UAE or Saudi Arabia—both known operators of the platform—played a role in offensive operations against Iran.

stories.title: Attacking through Russia’s best drones, a Ukrainian column lost a precious M-1 tank—and potentially a lot of troops
stories.summary: A Ukrainian armored column led by an M-1 Abrams tank attempted to reinforce positions northwest of Pokrovsk but lost the tank and potentially sustained significant troop casualties while navigating through Russian drone attacks.

stories.title: Rights group head warns of ‘alarming’ risk of long-term mass displacement in Lebanon
stories.summary: The head of the International Organization for Migration, Amy Pope, warned of an alarming risk of long-term mass displacement in Lebanon. She described the crisis as far more severe than in previous Israel-Hezbollah conflicts.

stories.title: Nasa’s Artemis crew gets green light to make big push to the moon
stories.summary: NASA authorized the four-member Artemis crew, currently orbiting Earth, to proceed toward the moon on Thursday. Flight Director Jeff Radigan approved a nearly six-minute engine burn of the Orion capsule to set a lunar trajectory. The mission marks the first crewed lunar fly-by in more than 50 years.

stories.title: Sudan appoints Yassir al-Atta armed forces Chief of Staff
stories.summary: Sudan appointed General Yassir al-Atta as chief of staff of the country's armed forces. Al-Atta is a member of Sudan's Sovereign Council and serves as assistant to commander-in-chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. The appointment was confirmed by a military spokesman.

stories.title: Iran digital repression surged amid war and protests: Rights group
stories.summary: A rights group reported that Iran's digital repression surged amid the ongoing war and domestic protests. Some of the documented activities bore clear signs of involvement by the Tehran government.

stories.title: At least 5 killed as heavy rain lashes Karachi; city administration declares emergency
stories.summary: At least five people were killed in Karachi, Pakistan, as heavy rain struck the city, prompting the administration to declare an emergency. Four deaths resulted from electrocution and one from a building collapse.

stories.title: Could Israel and the US achieve victory over Iran? An expert weighs in
stories.summary: Shmuel Rosner, a senior fellow at the Jewish People Policy Institute, discussed the prospects of an Israeli-US victory over Iran in an interview for the Deep Dive podcast.

stories.title: Putin floats idea of 'grain and energy hub' in Egypt
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin proposed that Russia and Egypt discuss creating a joint "grain and energy hub" in Egypt.

stories.title: What’s Next for the Iran War?
stories.summary: Following a prime-time address by President Trump on the US military campaign in Iran, analysts noted the speech offered few concrete details about the conflict's next steps. The war continues with uncertainty about its duration and strategic objectives.

stories.title: Epstein accusations and pressure from the boss: Bondi’s time as Trump’s chief enforcer
stories.summary: President Donald Trump fired US Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday after months of tension over her handling of the Epstein files and efforts to prosecute the president's political adversaries. Trump named his former personal lawyer as acting head of the Justice Department.

stories.title: New agreements reached: Zelensky on cooperation with countries targeted by Iran
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine has reached new agreements with countries targeted by Iran, under which Ukraine will have a greater presence in emerging security formats.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1499: Ukraine struck ten Russian oil refineries, twelve air defense systems in March
stories.summary: Ukraine struck ten Russian oil refineries and twelve air defense systems during March. Separately, Hungary's continued block on €90 billion in EU funds for Ukraine is deepening a rift within the bloc, with 26 member states increasingly bypassing Budapest.

stories.title: Red Cross warns medical supplies in Iran under strain as casualties mount
stories.summary: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies warned that medical supplies in Iran are under strain as casualties mount from the US-Israeli air campaign. More than 2,000 people have been killed and over 26,500 wounded since strikes began on February 28. Three aid workers have been killed, including one in a strike on a clinic in Zanjan.

stories.title: Trump threatens 100% tariff on US drug makers that don’t strike deals to lower prices
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced 100% tariffs on pharmaceutical companies that fail to negotiate lower US drug prices. The tariffs target branded drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients but exempt generic medications, which account for over 90% of US drug sales, for at least one year.

stories.title: West has luxury of studying how modern warfare works. No American drone manufacturer can match what Kyiv built under fire
stories.summary: A Pentagon assessment concluded that no American drone manufacturer can match the capabilities Ukraine developed under combat conditions. Western nations have the opportunity to study the modern warfare innovations emerging from the conflict.

stories.title: Russian tanker 'out of control' after failed towing: Libya authorities
stories.summary: Libyan authorities reported that efforts to tow a Russian gas tanker failed due to bad weather, leaving the vessel adrift in the Mediterranean Sea.

stories.title: Bahrain takes aim at Iran at UN, warns Hormuz threat endangers global economy
stories.summary: Bahrain's representative Al Zayani addressed the UN Security Council, warning that Iranian threats to the Strait of Hormuz endanger the global economy. He praised international stabilization efforts while pointing to escalating Iranian aggression.

stories.title: Gulf states seek UN mandate for force to protect Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council's secretary general called on the UN Security Council to authorize the use of force to protect the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian attacks. Iran has restricted commercial shipping through the vital waterway in retaliation for U.S.-Israeli strikes during the ongoing Middle East war.

stories.title: Ukrainian army draft officer fatally stabbed on duty
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military draft officer was fatally stabbed in the neck while on duty in the western city of Lviv on Thursday. The killing occurred amid ongoing tensions over mobilization efforts in Ukraine's war against Russia.

stories.title: Hegseth ousts army’s top uniformed officer, even as US wages war on Iran
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked General Randy George, the Army's 41st Chief of Staff, to retire immediately. The Pentagon confirmed the departure without providing a reason. George had held the position since August 2023, during a period when the United States is engaged in military operations against Iran.

stories.title: 9-year-old boy recounts airstrike in Lebanon that killed whole family
stories.summary: A nine-year-old boy, Karim Al-Haj Hussein, survived an Israeli airstrike on his home in Baalbek, Lebanon. The strike killed members of his family.

stories.title: Melania Trump brokers return of abducted Ukrainian children in fourth mediation effort
stories.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump mediated an agreement between Russia and Ukraine to return six abducted Ukrainian children to their families. This marked her fourth mediation effort on the issue.

stories.title: Civilians killed as Sudan's civil war spills into Chad: MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières reported that drone strikes by parties to Sudan's civil war are killing and wounding civilians in the border region with neighboring Chad.

stories.title: Serbian president invites parties for talks as anti-government protests continue
stories.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić invited political parties to begin talks on Friday to address the country's political crisis as anti-government protests continue. Opposition critics dismissed the negotiations as pointless ahead of any potential early election.

stories.title: 'Any weapon Europe buys from the US is a liability', rearmament expert says
stories.summary: European NATO members have reduced their dependence on US weapons imports while increasing defense spending over the past year. Guntram Wolff of the Bruegel think tank argued that European purchases of American weapons create technology dependence and undermine the development of domestic defense industries.

stories.title: A month into war, Lebanon’s prime minister says no end in sight
stories.summary: Lebanon's prime minister said there is no end in sight to the conflict a month into the war. Families fleeing Israeli strikes in Lebanon reported exhaustion from repeated rounds of conflict and displacement.

stories.title: Russia’s deputy digital development minister volunteers to fight in Ukraine, Kommersant reports
stories.summary: Andrei Zarenin, Russia's deputy digital development minister, volunteered to fight in Ukraine, according to Russian business daily Kommersant on April 2.

stories.title: Oil shock triggers global price spikes as Iran war drags on
stories.summary: Disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran are causing global fuel price spikes. The oil shock is rippling across international markets.

stories.title: Milei reaffirms Falklands sovereignty, warns oil firms and vows to rebuild the armed forces
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei reaffirmed Argentina's sovereignty claim over the Falkland Islands and warned of a diplomatic response to British oil exploration in the area. He also announced that 10% of fiscal revenue from privatizations would be allocated to purchasing weapons and equipment for the armed forces.

stories.title: Russian forces drop four bombs on Druzhkivka, wounding nine
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Druzhkivka in Ukraine's Donetsk region with four FAB-250 guided aerial bombs on April 2, injuring nine civilians.

stories.title: Bipartisan group of senators vow to keep US in NATO despite Trump threats
stories.summary: A bipartisan group of US senators publicly reaffirmed America's commitment to NATO, one day after President Trump threatened to withdraw from the transatlantic alliance. The senators vowed to maintain US membership in the military bloc.

stories.title: Iran says army forces are ready to repel US-Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Iran's military declared its forces are prepared to repel any US-Israeli attacks. Officials insisted the country's military capabilities remain intact despite the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: UN calls for probe into killing of journalists in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on 28 March in southern Lebanon killed Al-Manar correspondent Ali Shoeib, Al-Mayadeen reporter Fatima Ftouni, and her cameraman brother Mohammed. The UN human rights office called for an independent international investigation, while Israel claimed Shoeib was a Hezbollah intelligence operative.

stories.title: Man files war crimes complaint in France over deadly 2024 IDF strike in Beirut
stories.summary: French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri filed a war crimes complaint in France over a 2024 Israeli Defense Forces airstrike in Beirut that killed his parents. He is seeking an investigation into why civilians were targeted. The IDF has not commented but has previously said it follows international law.

stories.title: Meetings with Imran continue to remain suspended as authorities stop PTI leaders outside Adiala jail
stories.summary: Authorities at Adiala jail in Islamabad again prevented PTI leaders from meeting incarcerated party founder Imran Khan on Thursday. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja had submitted a list of six party members for the visit. The meeting suspension has continued despite repeated attempts by the party to gain access.

stories.title: Russia says will send second ship with oil to Cuba
stories.summary: Russia announced it will send a second ship carrying oil to Cuba. The island nation has been suffering from a severe energy crisis since January.

stories.title: Russia sending second ship with oil to Cuba amid US blockade
stories.summary: Russia is sending a second oil shipment to Cuba amid the island's energy crisis and a US blockade. A Russian tanker recently delivered approximately 700,000 barrels of crude oil to Cuba.

stories.title: America’s War Machine Runs on Tungsten—and It Could Run Out
stories.summary: US military operations in Iran are raising concerns about the depletion of America's limited tungsten stockpiles. Tungsten is a critical material used extensively in weapons manufacturing and defense systems.

stories.title: Sudan army names new chief of staff in biggest wartime shakeup
stories.summary: Sudan's military named General Yasser al-Atta as its new chief of staff in its largest command shakeup since the war with the Rapid Support Forces began in 2023.

stories.title: Dubai’s luxury stores take hit as Middle East war drags on
stories.summary: Luxury retail stores in Dubai are experiencing declining business as the Middle East war continues. Mall developers have cautioned against closing or shortening operating hours to avoid causing unnecessary alarm among consumers.

stories.title: Hegseth fires Army’s top officer, Gen. Randy George
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth directed the removal of General Randy George as the Army's top uniformed officer. A Defense Department official confirmed that George was asked to step down from his role as Army Chief of Staff.

stories.title: Drone maker backed by Trump’s sons looks to sell to Gulf states attacked by Iran
stories.summary: Powerus, a drone company with Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. as stakeholders, is seeking to sell defensive drone interceptors to Gulf states targeted by Iranian attacks. A former White House ethics chief said the countries face enormous pressure to buy from the firm.

stories.title: UN experts call for investigation into killing of 3 Lebanese journalists in Israeli strike
stories.summary: UN experts called for an international investigation into the killing of three Lebanese journalists, including Al Manar correspondent Ali Shoeib, in an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon on March 28. The experts said Israel had not provided credible evidence supporting its claims that the journalists were linked to armed groups.

stories.title: At least 43 people killed in ADF attack in northeast DR Congo, army says
stories.summary: At least 43 people were killed in an attack by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the Congolese army. ADF attacks in the region have intensified in recent months.

stories.title: Russia's military campaign in Ukraine stalls for first time in more than two years
stories.summary: Russia's military advance in Ukraine stalled in March, with no territorial gains recorded for the first time in over two years, according to the Institute for the Study of War. Ukrainian forces recaptured small areas, signaling a slowdown in Moscow's momentum after months of incremental progress.

stories.title: Wall Street falls, oil surges after Trump threatens more attacks on Iran
stories.summary: US stock markets fell and oil prices surged after President Trump vowed to continue attacks on Iran without offering a clear timetable for ending the conflict. The remarks heightened uncertainty in global financial markets.

stories.title: Trump sacks attorney general Bondi, Hegseth asks US Army Chief of Staff to step down
stories.summary: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday and named his former personal lawyer as acting head of the Justice Department. Separately, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked Army Chief of Staff General Randy George to step down and take immediate retirement.

stories.title: As war drags on, US reiterates Trump open to diplomacy with Iran
stories.summary: The US State Department reiterated that President Trump remains open to diplomacy with Iran as the war continues. Simultaneously, the department accused Iran of striking civilian sites, while Trump shared footage of the destruction of an Iranian bridge.

stories.title: Iran arrests prize-winning rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh: daughter
stories.summary: Iranian authorities arrested prize-winning human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh, according to her daughter. The arrest occurred amid an ongoing crackdown on civil society in Iran.

stories.title: Burkina army, jihadists killed more than 1,800 civilians since 2023
stories.summary: A Human Rights Watch report found that Burkina Faso's government forces and jihadist groups together killed more than 1,800 civilians between 2023 and 2025. The findings highlight the severe toll of the ongoing conflict on the civilian population in the West African nation.

stories.title: Hamas wants guarantees of Israeli troop withdrawal before disarmament talks, sources say
stories.summary: Hamas conveyed demands and amendments to a proposed plan, including an end to what it calls Israeli violations, full implementation of all provisions, and the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza before entering disarmament talks.

stories.title: U.K. Hosts Coalition Talks to Reopen Hormuz—Without the U.S.
stories.summary: The United Kingdom hosted coalition talks with other nations aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz without direct US participation. President Trump has insisted that other countries should bear the responsibility of securing the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Will the Iran War Evaporate the Gulf’s AI Oasis?
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Iran war is disrupting the Gulf region's technology and artificial intelligence ambitions. While the conflict has not completely ended the region's tech investments, it has significantly undermined confidence in the Gulf as an emerging AI hub.

stories.title: State Department claims Iran ‘continually’ pursuing nuclear weapon
stories.summary: A US State Department spokesman claimed Iran was "continually" pursuing a nuclear weapon, citing it as justification for launching the war against Tehran.

stories.title: Iran war: music and barbecues in Tehran despite Trump’s ‘Stone Age’ threats
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran gathered in parks for picnics on the final day of Persian new year holidays despite ongoing US military strikes and President Trump's threats to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Age." The US and Israel launched the conflict on February 28, and powerful blasts shook the Iranian capital on Thursday.

stories.title: Russian forces struck Kharkiv with “Shahed” drones for first time - Terekhov
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv using Shahed drones for the first time, according to Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov. The attacks began overnight.

stories.title: Red Cross warns medical supplies in Iran under strain as casualties mount
stories.summary: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies warned that emergency medical supplies in Iran are under severe strain. Over 2,000 people have been killed and more than 26,500 wounded since US-Israeli air strikes began on 28 February. Three aid workers have died, including one in a strike on a clinic in Zanjan.

stories.title: 'They call me king': Highlights from Trump's unusual Easter lunch speech
stories.summary: During an Easter lunch at the White House, President Trump delivered unusually candid remarks, including referencing being called "king." The White House later deleted the video of the speech, which was held without reporters present.

stories.title: CPS considering 13 suspected cases of assisted dying in England and Wales
stories.summary: The Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales is currently considering 13 suspected cases of assisted dying. Between April 2009 and March of this year, police referred 209 cases recorded as assisted dying to the CPS. Encouraging or assisting suicide remains illegal under the Suicide Act 1961.

stories.title: Argentina declares Iranian envoy persona non grata, gives him 48 hours to leave
stories.summary: Argentina declared Iranian envoy Mohsen Tehrani persona non grata and gave him 48 hours to leave the country. Argentina cited Iran's response to the IRGC terrorist designation and Tehran's failure to cooperate with the investigation into the 1994 bombing of a Jewish community center in Buenos Aires.

stories.title: Pakistan approves host of transshipment measures to stregthen maritime sector
stories.summary: Pakistan's federal government approved a series of transshipment initiatives to strengthen its maritime sector amid regional security shifts following the US-Israeli attack on Iran. The measures were recommended by a high-level committee headed by Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, constituted by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

stories.title: Pakistan to seek flexibility in IMF programme for evolving contingencies amid war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan announced it would seek flexibility in its International Monetary Fund programme to manage contingencies arising from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and surging global petroleum prices. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb discussed the matter with the U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ahead of IMF spring meetings.

stories.title: What might end Israel’s war on Iran?
stories.summary: Israel and the United States continue sustained attacks on Iran, while Iranian forces strike back. The ongoing conflict has raised questions about what conditions might bring hostilities to an end.

stories.title: Iran digital repression surged amid war and protests: rights group
stories.summary: A rights group reported that cyber threats and digital repression targeting Iranians inside the country and abroad have surged over the past nine months during wars and protests.

stories.title: Hospital evacuated in Lebanon's Bint Jbeil as Israeli forces advance
stories.summary: Medical staff were evacuated from Salah Ghandour Hospital in Lebanon's Bint Jbeil province as Israeli forces advanced deeper into southern Lebanon. The Lebanese health ministry reported that five hospitals are now closed and nine facilities have been targeted by Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Fact-checking Trump's address on the war in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump delivered a 19-minute address from the White House defending the US military campaign in Iran, now in its second month, calling it a success nearing completion. Fact-checkers noted he overstated certain battlefield victories and misrepresented the state of the US economy.

stories.title: Macron says Trump marriage jibe does not 'merit response'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron dismissed President Trump's public remarks mocking his marriage, calling them "neither elegant nor appropriate." Amid broader US-French tensions over strikes on Iran and NATO disputes, Macron criticized the tone of discourse, saying "there is too much talk" and "this is not a show."

stories.title: Europe, NATO under pressure over Iran war: 'Trump strong with the weak and weak with the strong'
stories.summary: French Senator Hélène Conway-Mouret argued that President Trump's Iran war strategy is creating significant volatility for European security and transatlantic relations. She noted that NATO withdrawal threats are being used to pressure European compliance with US demands.

stories.title: 'He wasn't convincing to the world and to the American people', former US ambassador to NATO says
stories.summary: Former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder said President Trump's national address on the Iran war failed to convince the American public or the world. Daalder compared the administration's communication strategy to Vietnam-era messaging, noting an emphasis on targets hit rather than strategic objectives.

stories.title: French far-left MEP Rima Hassan arrested over X post justifying attack on Israeli airport
stories.summary: French authorities arrested far-left MEP Rima Hassan over a post on X made on March 26 that was suspected of justifying an attack on an Israeli airport. She was detained on suspicion of showing support for terrorism.

stories.title: Rubio raises concerns over China’s detention of Panama-flagged ships
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed serious concerns over China's intensified inspections and detentions of Panama-flagged vessels. Rubio accused Beijing of using economic tools to undermine Panama's sovereignty and pledged US support for the Latin American nation.

stories.title: Iranians celebrate New Year in parks despite ongoing attacks
stories.summary: Iranians gathered in parks across Tehran to celebrate the end of the Persian New Year holiday, despite ongoing military attacks affecting the country.

stories.title: One killed and 16 wounded in Kherson region during day amid Russian attacks
stories.summary: One person was killed and 16 others were wounded in the Kherson region of Ukraine on the afternoon of April 2 as a result of Russian attacks.

stories.title: Democrats cheer Trump’s firing of Pam Bondi and attack Epstein files ‘cover-up’
stories.summary: Democrats celebrated President Trump's firing of Attorney General Pam Bondi, with House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries predicting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth could be next. Trump announced Bondi's departure on Truth Social, saying she would transition to a private sector role.

stories.title: European nations say Israel, Hezbollah fighting 'must cease'
stories.summary: Several European nations called on Israel and Hezbollah to cease fighting, expressing concern over Israeli plans to maintain control of parts of southern Lebanon after the war.

stories.title: RBC: Russia asks major online platforms to block users with active VPNs by April 15
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry has requested that the country's largest online platforms block access for users with active VPNs by April 15, according to the Russian business outlet RBC.

stories.title: Leo, the first US pope, emerges as pointed Trump critic
stories.summary: Pope Leo, the first American pope, has emerged as a pointed critic of the U.S.-led war on Iran in recent weeks.

stories.title: Unrealistic to open Strait of Hormuz by force: Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron stated it is unrealistic to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force. He has been working with allies to build a coalition to guarantee free passage through the strategic waterway.

stories.title: IDF kills Iranian Oil Headquarters commander, destroys IRGC finance facility
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it killed a commander of Iran's Oil Headquarters and destroyed an IRGC finance facility. The IDF stated the Oil Headquarters enables Iranian military buildup through oil sale profits.

stories.title: Trump warns Tehran ‘more to follow’ after strike destroys Iran’s largest bridge
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed responsibility for destroying Iran's largest bridge, the newly built $400 million B1 suspension bridge between Tehran and Karaj. The strike killed two people and split the 136-meter-high structure in half. Trump had previously threatened to bomb Iran "back to the stone ages" if no deal was reached.

stories.title: The Next Global Food Crisis Has Already Begun
stories.summary: Blocked fertilizer shipments combined with La Niña weather patterns are creating conditions for a new global food crisis. Farmers worldwide face disrupted supply chains and adverse growing conditions that threaten harvests.

stories.title: A lost novel from 1943 that predicted the Holocaust has been recovered
stories.summary: A lost 1943 novel by Friedrich Torberg titled "Mein ist die Rache" has been recovered. The book depicted a German concentration camp decades before the term "Holocaust" entered common usage.

stories.title: Videos show explosions in central Iran as conflict with Israel intensifies
stories.summary: Massive explosions and thick plumes of smoke were reported over Baharestan in the Esfahan region of central Iran on Wednesday, as the conflict between Iran and Israel intensified. Videos circulating online captured the strikes hitting the area.

stories.title: Israel's Lebanon endgame: 'Dismantle Hezbollah entirely as a political and social movement'
stories.summary: Analyst Yezid Sayigh of the Carnegie Middle East Center argued that Israel's military operations in southern Lebanon aim to dismantle Hezbollah entirely as a political and social movement. He said the actions are driven by domestic political imperatives, regional power calculations, and Lebanon's structural fragility.

stories.title: Trump raises Nato exit again, faces resistance in Congress
stories.summary: President Trump again raised the possibility of the United States leaving NATO during a private lunch. Senate Majority Leader John Thune said congressional approval for a withdrawal would be difficult, emphasizing that many lawmakers view NATO as a critical alliance.

stories.title: Golden Dome, ships and missiles top Trump’s $1.5 trillion defense wish list
stories.summary: President Trump is set to unveil a fiscal 2027 defense budget request of $1.5 trillion, with priorities including the Golden Dome missile defense system, naval vessels, and missile programs.

stories.title: How international media covered President Trump’s first address to the nation on Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump delivered a 19-minute address from the White House on the war against Iran, claiming to have severely degraded Iran's military capabilities. He vowed to continue bombing for two to three weeks but did not outline a clear strategy. International media, including CNN, noted the lack of a defined endgame.

stories.title: From the Chrism Mass to the washing of the feet: Pope Leo’s first Easter season begins
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Easter season as pontiff by washing the feet of priests during Holy Thursday services, continuing a tradition practiced by his predecessor Pope Francis. He also issued a warning against domination in a troubled world.

stories.title: Space for war between two nuclear states inconceivable, Asif reminds Indian counterpart
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned his Indian counterpart Rajnath Singh that the prospect of war between two nuclear-armed states is "inconceivable and has drastic consequences." The statement responded to Singh's warning against Pakistani "misadventure" during the ongoing Middle East war.

stories.title: Alleged maple syrup scam in Quebec uncovered by Canadian broadcaster
stories.summary: A Radio-Canada investigation revealed that a major Quebec maple syrup producer had been adulterating its product with cane sugar and selling it to grocery chains. The discovery began when a reporter noticed an unusual taste, and subsequent testing confirmed the fraud.

stories.title: USS George H.W. Bush deploys to Middle East, third US aircraft carrier to join war
stories.summary: The USS George H.W. Bush aircraft carrier has been deployed to the Middle East, becoming the third US carrier to join the conflict. The Wall Street Journal had earlier reported the vessel was under consideration for deployment.

stories.title: Iran not looking to ‘restart’ uranium enrichment, atomic envoy tells AFP
stories.summary: Iran's atomic envoy told AFP that Tehran is not seeking to restart uranium enrichment. The ambassador also stressed that targeting Iran's nuclear plants constitutes a war crime.

stories.title: The role of Britain's Cyprus bases in a Middle East at war
stories.summary: Britain's military bases in Cyprus, which have long operated with limited public scrutiny, have drawn increased attention due to their role in operations related to the ongoing Iran war.

stories.title: Russian Tanker 'Out of Control' After Failed Towing, Libyan Authorities Say
stories.summary: Libyan authorities said the Russian LNG tanker Arctic Metagaz is out of control in the Mediterranean after a failed towing attempt. The vessel had been abandoned after a series of explosions while transporting LNG from Russia to Egypt.

stories.title: US defense stocks see no Iran war lift after early surge
stories.summary: US defense stocks have declined despite the ongoing Iran war, following an initial surge at the conflict's outset. The sector has not sustained the early gains investors anticipated from wartime spending.

stories.title: Children as young as 12 buying and selling knives and weapons via the internet
stories.summary: UK policing and crime minister Sarah Jones revealed that children as young as 12 are buying and selling knives online. She made the remarks at the opening of the new National Knife Crime Centre in Bloomsbury, central London, and called for the government to crack down on the online weapons trade.

stories.title: US and Israel 'again bombing what were clearly non-military sites' in Iran
stories.summary: FRANCE 24 correspondent Reza Sayah reported from Tehran that US and Israeli forces again bombed what appeared to be non-military sites in Iran in broad daylight. President Trump subsequently appeared to boast about the strikes publicly.

stories.title: UK convenes 40 countries to discuss reopening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Kingdom convened foreign ministers from approximately 40 countries in a virtual summit to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, blocked by Iran during the US-Israeli war. The US did not participate. The summit was chaired by Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper.

stories.title: Goldman, Citi staff to work remotely after foiled bomb attack on another bank in Paris
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs and Citigroup instructed staff in Paris and Frankfurt to work remotely following a foiled bomb attack on Bank of America's Paris offices the previous Saturday.

stories.title: Four suspects in foiled Bank of America Paris bombing put in pretrial detention
stories.summary: French authorities placed four suspects — one adult and three underage teenagers — in pretrial detention in connection with the foiled bombing of the Bank of America offices in Paris.

stories.title: Goldman Paris is warned of Iran group bomb threat: Parisien
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs's Paris office received a bomb threat from a group linked to Iran, according to Le Parisien. The incident follows a recently foiled bombing attempt near the Bank of America office in Paris.

stories.title: Trump fires Pam Bondi, appoints own ex-lawyer to temporarily head justice department
stories.summary: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi amid criticism over her handling of the Epstein files and appointed his own former lawyer to temporarily lead the Justice Department.

stories.title: GCC chief urges UN to halt Iranian attacks, protect Gulf waterways
stories.summary: GCC Secretary General Jassim al-Budaiwi called on the UN Security Council to ensure uninterrupted navigation through strategic waterways, including the Strait of Hormuz, amid regional hostilities.

stories.title: Can Russia help fill the global energy gap?
stories.summary: Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have driven up global crude oil prices, enabling Russia to increase its revenue from energy exports.

stories.title: A Russian private military company founder faces charges over an alleged scam targeting recruits. Journalists list him among officers accused of executing their own men.
stories.summary: Alexey Marushchenko, founder of the Russian private military company "Yastreb," and several associates are in pre-trial detention on charges of defrauding nearly 100 contract soldiers. Journalists have also listed Marushchenko among officers accused of executing their own personnel.

stories.title: Children’s hospital in Tehran keeps hopes and smiles alive during war
stories.summary: Staff at Tehran's Children's Medical Center organized activities to provide a joyful experience for hospitalized children amid the ongoing conflict in Iran.

stories.title: U.S.-South Korea Relations Are at Breaking Point
stories.summary: The Iran war has severely strained US-South Korea relations, with analysis suggesting the conflict has demonstrated Washington's limited regard for its ally's welfare. The bilateral relationship is described as reaching a breaking point.

stories.title: Sixteen Kenyans missing in Russia after army recruitment
stories.summary: Kenya's foreign minister said more than 250 Kenyans have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine, mostly willingly. Sixteen Kenyans recruited into the Russian army are currently missing.

stories.title: Videos capture projectile falling in central Israel after Iran strike
stories.summary: Videos circulating online captured the moment a projectile struck central Israel following an Iranian attack, with a loud explosion heard on impact.

stories.title: How Hezbollah Stands to Benefit From an Israeli Invasion
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that an Israeli ground invasion of Lebanon could benefit Hezbollah by playing to the group's guerrilla warfare strengths. A renewed occupation would shift the conflict to terrain where Hezbollah has historically operated effectively.

stories.title: The US has declared ‘space superiority’ over Iran. What does that mean?
stories.summary: The United States declared "space superiority" over Iran, having destroyed Iran's nascent space program during the ongoing conflict. Iran reportedly continues to rely on other nations' satellite intelligence capabilities despite the loss of its own space assets.

stories.title: IRGC attacking Amazon cloud computing center in Bahrain, Iran's ISNA reports
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reportedly attacked an Amazon Web Services cloud computing center in Bahrain. The Financial Times reported the facility had already been damaged in an earlier Iranian strike on Wednesday.

stories.title: Israel says missiles launched from Iran, alerts issued for central areas
stories.summary: The Israeli military detected missiles launched from Iran and issued early warning alerts for Jerusalem and the greater Tel Aviv area.

stories.title: Deputy PM Kachka identifies promising sectors for expanding Ukraine–Netherlands economic cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Taras Kachka identified several promising sectors for expanding economic cooperation between Ukraine and the Netherlands, describing the potential partnerships as mutually beneficial.

stories.title: Russia Bans Producers From Exporting Gasoline Until July 31
stories.summary: The Russian government banned producers from exporting gasoline until July 31, citing the need to stabilize domestic fuel supplies amid rising global oil prices linked to the Middle East war and ahead of the spring planting season.

stories.title: India slams attacks on UNIFIL soldiers, does not name Israel
stories.summary: India condemned attacks on UNIFIL peacekeeping soldiers in Lebanon without explicitly naming Israel as the responsible party. The Ministry of External Affairs cited UN Security Council resolution 2589, calling for accountability for crimes against peacekeepers. India is one of the largest and longest-serving contributors to UN peacekeeping operations.

stories.title: Hegseth forces out Army’s top general in ‘widely anticipated’ move
stories.summary: The removal of General Randy George as Army Chief of Staff by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was described as "widely anticipated." Signs of the move emerged late last year when George's deputy was replaced by Hegseth's senior military aide.

stories.title: Ros Atkins on…the cost of the Iran war
stories.summary: BBC Analysis Editor Ros Atkins examined the financial costs the United States is bearing as it continues its military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Iran hangs 18-year-old over protests in latest wartime execution
stories.summary: Iran executed 18-year-old protester Amir Hossein Hatami following a fast-track trial. Amnesty International condemned the proceedings as grossly unfair. The execution is the latest in a series of wartime executions in Iran.

stories.title: UK-led talks on stopping Iran holding world ‘hostage’ in Hormuz draw some 40 nations
stories.summary: The UK hosted talks with nearly 40 nations, including France, Germany, and the UAE, on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The US did not participate. French President Macron described a military operation to open the strait as unrealistic, while Gulf nations pushed for such action.

stories.title: Iran conflict could open door for new players in Gulf defense market
stories.summary: Analysis from CSIS suggests the Iran conflict could open opportunities for new entrants in the Gulf defense market. Gulf states are reassessing their defense needs in light of the conflict, potentially creating openings for non-traditional suppliers.

stories.title: Eight Muslim-majority countries condemn Israel’s new death penalty law
stories.summary: Eight Muslim-majority countries issued a joint condemnation of Israel's newly passed death penalty law. The countries described the legislation as a "dangerous escalation."

stories.title: Iran claims drone attack on US jets in Jordan as Kuwait intercepts missiles
stories.summary: Iran claimed it carried out a drone attack targeting US fighter jets at the al-Azraq base in Jordan. Separately, Kuwait's military said it intercepted two Iranian cruise missiles and 13 drones over 24 hours, reporting no damage or injuries.

stories.title: No longer so mighty? Iran war tests US strength and resolve
stories.summary: Analysis suggests the Iran war is testing US military strength and global credibility. While 2026 began with a successful US commando operation to seize Venezuela's president, Trump's first prime-time war address unsettled markets rather than reassuring them, and his responses to energy security concerns drew criticism.

stories.title: Russia’s 14th general killed since war began. His An-26 may have been shot down by Russia’s own air defense
stories.summary: Russia's 14th general killed since the start of the war, the commander of the Northern Fleet's mixed aviation corps, died when his An-26 aircraft may have been shot down by Russia's own air defense systems.

stories.title: President Putin holds talks with Egyptian Foreign Minister Abdelatty in Moscow
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty in Moscow. Their discussions focused on the ongoing war in the Middle East and bilateral economic cooperation between Russia and Egypt.

stories.title: Gulf states seek UN mandate for force to protect Hormuz
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council has called on the UN Security Council to authorize the use of force to protect the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian disruption to maritime traffic.

stories.title: On birthright citizenship, Trump’s restrictive immigration agenda hits a rare roadblock
stories.summary: A U.S. court dealt a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict birthright citizenship. The court indicated that the legal arguments supporting Trump's executive action are invalid, marking a rare obstacle to his immigration agenda.

stories.title: Sadiq Khan warns of ‘zero-tolerance approach’ to any repeat of Clapham disorder
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan warned of a zero-tolerance approach following disorder in Clapham, where young people stormed shops as part of a social media trend. Khan said more arrests would follow and urged against any repeat of the violence over the Easter weekend.

stories.title: Invaders attack Solonytsivka community in Kharkiv region, killing one and wounding others
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Solonytsivka community in the Kharkiv district, killing one man and injuring a woman and a child.

stories.title: Putin calls for end to war in talks with Saudi crown prince
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed the war on Iran by phone, with both sides calling for intensified diplomatic efforts to halt hostilities and pursue a long-term settlement.

stories.title: War update: 127 clashes on front, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 127 Russian attacks along the front line since the start of the day. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: On the Radar: Brazil’s ‘Escobar,’ Haiti’s Latest Massacre, and Venezuela’s Former First Lady Under Scrutiny
stories.summary: This week's security roundup covers a major drug trafficking figure in Brazil dubbed the country's "Escobar," a recent massacre in Haiti, and legal scrutiny facing Venezuela's former first lady.

stories.title: Azerbaijan upholds conviction of opposition politician, lawyer says
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's Supreme Court in Baku rejected an appeal by a prominent opposition politician serving a nine-year prison sentence. The ruling, issued on Thursday, upholds the politician's original conviction, according to his lawyer.

stories.title: Iran executes man arrested over January protests
stories.summary: Iran executed a man who had been arrested in connection with protests that took place in January. In March, Iran had already executed three men convicted of killing two police officers during the same wave of demonstrations.

stories.title: 'An eye for an eye': Israel’s death penalty law is retaliatory and electorally motivated
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a law establishing the death penalty for terrorists, which in practice would apply only to Palestinians. The legislation has drawn international condemnation, with critics arguing it is both retaliatory and politically motivated ahead of elections.

stories.title: UN experts urge investigation into Israel’s killing of Lebanese journalists
stories.summary: UN experts called for an investigation into Israel's killing of journalists in Lebanon, Gaza, and the West Bank, saying Israel has been emboldened by impunity for previous attacks on media workers.

stories.title: Lebanese artist files complaint in France against Israeli strike
