stories.title: Trump’s fragile ex-China mineral-alliance plan faces cost surge amid Iran war oil shock
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran is causing oil-supply disruptions that complicate President Trump's strategy to build mineral alliances outside China. Energy-intensive rare earth refining and critical metal supply chains are particularly vulnerable to the oil shock.

stories.title: Army’s enterprise contracting vehicles likely to speed procurement but not without risk
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is pursuing enterprise contracting vehicles featuring high-ceiling, long-duration contracts to accelerate procurement. Experts and former defense officials noted that while this approach could speed acquisition, its long-term effectiveness remains uncertain.

stories.title: ‘Back to Stone Age’: Trump says conflict nearing end, threatens wider attacks on Iran
stories.summary: In a 19-minute White House address, US President Donald Trump said the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran could conclude within weeks but threatened to intensify strikes, warning he would bomb Iran "back to the Stone Age."

stories.title: Security forces kill 8 terrorists along Pak-Afghan border in North Waziristan: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's military reported that security forces killed eight militants along the Pak-Afghan border in North Waziristan district. The ISPR said the engagement targeted members of Fitna al-Khwarij, and weapons and ammunition were recovered.

stories.title: Trump primetime Iran address raises more questions than answers
stories.summary: President Trump's primetime address on Iran was described as delivering contradictory messages that raised more questions than it answered about US strategy in the conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan-bound ships pass through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Two ships successfully passed through the Strait of Hormuz and arrived at Pakistan's Karachi Port, amid ongoing disruptions to maritime traffic in the waterway.

stories.title: DRC launches first census in 40 years with $30M UNFPA backing - Interview
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has launched its first national census in over 40 years, backed by $30 million in funding from the UN Population Fund. UN officials say the census could reshape development planning across the country.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuelan interim leader Delcy Rodríguez
stories.summary: The United States lifted sanctions on Venezuelan acting president Delcy Rodríguez. The move signals warming U.S.-Venezuela relations following the commando raid in which former President Nicolás Maduro was seized and taken to New York to face drug trafficking charges.

stories.title: ‘Vile, horrifying, evil’: Democrats demand ceasefire as Trump defends costly war on Iran
stories.summary: US Democratic lawmakers demanded a ceasefire following President Trump's national address on the Iran war, criticizing the conflict as costly and lacking clear objectives. Trump had described the campaign as a "decisive, overwhelming victory."

stories.title: NATO chief to visit Washington next week as Trump threatens exit
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte plans to visit Washington next week amid rising tensions after President Trump criticized European allies over the Iran war and the Hormuz crisis. Trump has also renewed threats about a possible US exit from NATO.

stories.title: Macron says Hormuz military option ‘unrealistic’
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron rejected the use of military force to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, calling such an option unrealistic and dangerous. Speaking during a visit to South Korea, Macron pushed back against proposals sometimes voiced by the United States.

stories.title: NABU foils scheme to embezzle ₴776 million in grain from state corporation
stories.summary: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau has uncovered a large-scale corruption scheme involving the embezzlement of ₴776 million worth of grain from the State Food and Grain Corporation of Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran’s chief foreign affairs strategist ‘gravely wounded’ in US-Israeli attack
stories.summary: Former Iranian foreign minister Kamal Kharazi, described as Iran's chief foreign affairs strategist, was reportedly gravely wounded in a US-Israeli attack. The strike has been characterized as an assassination attempt targeting a high-profile Iranian official.

stories.title: Eight Muslim countries slam Israel’s new death penalty law as risk to regional stability
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from eight Muslim-majority countries — Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE — condemned Israel's new death penalty law. They called the legislation discriminatory toward Palestinians and warned it risks exacerbating regional tensions.

stories.title: What’s real anymore? AI warps truth of Middle East war
stories.summary: The volume of AI-generated fake content related to the Middle East conflict has reportedly outpaced the verification capacity of professional fact-checkers, raising concerns about the distortion of information during wartime.

stories.title: Four children killed in nursery school stabbing attack in Uganda
stories.summary: Four children were killed in a stabbing attack at a nursery school in Kampala, Uganda. Police said a suspect has been taken into custody, but the motive remains unknown.

stories.title: Iraq revives Syria land route to export oil to Europe
stories.summary: Iraq resumed overland oil exports through Syria to the Mediterranean, shipping 50,000 barrels per day of Basra medium crude with plans to increase volumes. The shift in energy logistics comes as the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupts traditional shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UK firms expect to raise prices more quickly as Iran war pushes up costs
stories.summary: A Bank of England survey of over 2,000 chief financial officers conducted in March found that UK firms expect to raise prices by 3.7% over the coming year. The anticipated increases are driven by rising costs linked to the war in the Middle East involving Iran.

stories.title: Swedish arms maker to set up major ammunition plant in Estonia
stories.summary: A Swedish arms manufacturer plans to establish a major ammunition production facility in Estonia. Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur noted the company had been promised confidentiality until contracts are finalized, according to local broadcaster ERR.

stories.title: Drivers told to hunt for cheapest fuel as Easter set to be busiest on UK roads since 2022
stories.summary: UK petrol prices surged by 20p per litre during March, rising from 132.83p to 152.83p for unleaded, driven by oil price increases linked to the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Easter weekend is expected to be the busiest on UK roads since 2022, with an estimated 21.7 million journeys planned. Drivers are being urged to seek the cheapest fuel available.

stories.title: IDF destroys IRGC Ground Forces base in Tehran, begins striking mobile command centers
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it destroyed an IRGC Ground Forces base in Tehran and began targeting mobile command centers. According to IDF intelligence, Iran's military has shifted to using mobile units to evade US and Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Armenia’s unique salt mine asthma clinic faces closure as funds dry up
stories.summary: A rare underground asthma clinic located 235 metres below Yerevan in Armenia's Avan salt mine is facing closure due to a lack of funding. The facility treats asthma and allergy patients using mineral-rich air in the subterranean setting.

stories.title: ‘From high flyer to dead parrot’: former billion-dollar eco-shoe brand Allbirds sold for $39m
stories.summary: Allbirds, the San Francisco-based sustainable shoe brand once valued at over $4 billion, is being sold to American Exchange Group for $39 million. The wool-based footwear company failed to sustain global demand despite earlier celebrity backing and significant market hype.

stories.title: UN appoints former Haiti PM Conille to Kenya role
stories.summary: The United Nations appointed former Haitian Prime Minister Garry Conille as its resident coordinator in Kenya. The announcement was made on Wednesday, with Conille taking up the post the same day in the new role based in Nairobi.

stories.title: Trump’s White House ballroom project faces panel vote after judge ordered halt – US politics live
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron accused U.S. President Donald Trump of undermining NATO by creating "daily doubt about his commitment" to the alliance, speaking during a state visit to Seoul. Separately, the National Capital Planning Commission faces a vote on Trump's White House ballroom project after a judge ordered a halt and thousands of negative public comments were received.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau: Civil society activist Vigário Luís Balanta found dead
stories.summary: Vigário Luís Balanta, a 35-year-old civil society activist and vocal critic of Guinea-Bissau's military junta, was found dead in the Ndam area approximately 30 kilometres from the capital Bissau.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages implemented in seven regions due to massive Russian attack
stories.summary: As of the morning of April 2, users in seven regions are without power due to a massive drone attack on energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Military Holds Workshop On Civilian Protection During Anti-Shabaab Operations
stories.summary: Somalia's Joint Operations Coordination Center commander Mohamed Ali Bariise opened a workshop in Mogadishu for Somali National Army officers focused on civilian protection during anti-Al-Shabaab operations.

stories.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel face stark shelter shortages, legal group warns
stories.summary: Israeli legal advocacy group Adalah warned of severe shelter shortages for Palestinian citizens of Israel. The group called on the Israeli government to close life-threatening gaps in shelter provision, citing damage from projectile strikes in Palestinian-populated cities like Kfar Qassem.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 7 in southern Lebanon, Hezbollah targets ground troops
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed seven people in southern Lebanon as Israel continues efforts to establish a security zone. Hezbollah fighters targeted Israeli ground troops operating in the area.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Eliminated Over 280 Terrorists During Ramadan, Theatre Commander Saystroopstroops Eliminated Over 280 Terrorists During Ramadan, Theatre Commander Says
stories.summary: Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar, Theatre Commander of Nigeria's Joint Task Force North-East Operation Hadin Kai, reported that troops eliminated over 280 terrorists during the Ramadan period. Forces also disrupted logistics networks and rescued abducted civilians.

stories.title: The war on the womb: Gaza’s reproductive genocide
stories.summary: A report examines how the war in Gaza has systematically targeted Palestinian maternal health infrastructure, including destruction of neonatal facilities and cryopreserved embryos, framing it as an assault on reproductive capacity.

stories.title: WhatsApp says Italian surveillance company tricked around 200 users into downloading spyware
stories.summary: WhatsApp disclosed that ASIGINT, a subsidiary of Italy-based SIO, carried out a campaign that tricked approximately 200 users into downloading spyware on the Meta-owned messaging platform.

stories.title: 40,000 taxi drivers sign up for e-payment systems as new rules come into force
stories.summary: Over 40,000 Hong Kong taxi drivers have adopted AlipayHK and WeChat Pay HK electronic payment systems as new e-payment regulations take effect. The move addresses a longstanding issue for mainland Chinese visitors ahead of the Ching Ming Festival holiday.

stories.title: Man admits preventing lawful burial in relation to 30 bodies found at Hull funeral home
stories.summary: Funeral director Robert Bush, 48, admitted to preventing a lawful burial after 30 bodies and a quantity of ashes were found at Legacy funeral home on Hessle Road in Hull in 2024. Bush had previously pleaded guilty to dozens of counts of fraud at a hearing in October following a police raid on the premises.

stories.title: Over 1,800 killed since junta seized power in Burkina Faso, rights group says
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reports that over 1,800 people have been killed since Captain Ibrahim Traoré's military junta seized power in Burkina Faso. The rights group says Traoré, other military leaders, and jihadist groups may bear liability for the killings.

stories.title: Gaza death toll rises to 72,289 as victims remain under rubble
stories.summary: The death toll in Gaza has risen to 72,289 Palestinians killed and 172,043 wounded since October 7, 2023, according to the Wafa news agency. Since a ceasefire on October 11, an additional 713 people have been killed, while rescue teams remain unable to reach many areas.

stories.title: How Israel’s record budget will finance expanding illegal settlements
stories.summary: Israel approved a record $271 billion budget that includes expanded funding for settlements in the occupied West Bank. The budget comes amid reports of increasing settler violence against Palestinians.

stories.title: Russian Shahed drones attack Kharkiv
stories.summary: Kharkiv is under attack by Russian UAVs.

stories.title: Death of Rohingya refugee in New York ruled homicide
stories.summary: The death of Rohingya refugee Nurul Amin Shah Alam in New York has been ruled a homicide. Details of his health and final days remain undisclosed, as his autopsy report is confidential under New York law.

stories.title: Australia PM says Iran war objectives met, 'not clear' what more to achieve
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister stated that objectives in the Iran war have been met and questioned what more could be achieved. Defence Minister Richard Marles emphasized Australia's interest in reopening the Strait of Hormuz but noted conditions do not yet allow it.

stories.title: Netanyahu rejects the gospel of Christ for the doctrine of Genghis Khan
stories.summary: Israeli authorities blocked the Catholic Patriarch of Jerusalem from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre during Palm Sunday. The incident involved barriers, delays, and restrictions at one of Christianity's holiest sites during the most sacred days of the Christian calendar.

stories.title: ICC moves forward with case against chief prosecutor Khan
stories.summary: Member states at the International Criminal Court voted to advance disciplinary proceedings against chief prosecutor Karim Khan following allegations of sexual assault. In the vote, 15 member states voted in favor, two abstained, and four voted against the measure.

stories.title: Libyan military leader may have combat drones despite UN embargo
stories.summary: Satellite images obtained by Reuters show at least three combat drones stationed at Al Khadim airbase in Libya between April and December. The presence of the drones at the base controlled by Libyan military leader Khalifa Haftar may violate the UN arms embargo on Libya.

stories.title: PLA upgrades ageing tanks with protection system for potential Taiwan operation
stories.summary: China's People's Liberation Army has upgraded Type 96A main battle tanks with GL-6 active protection systems to counter drones and anti-tank missiles, according to state media. The tanks belong to the 71st Group Army under the Eastern Theatre Command, responsible for potential Taiwan operations.

stories.title: UK to gather more than 30 countries to discuss methods of reopening Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The UK is convening more than 30 countries to discuss diplomatic and political measures to restore navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. The meeting, led by UK Home Secretary Yvette Cooper, will not include US participation, while Bahrain's UN resolution on Hormuz faces fresh obstacles.

stories.title: Trump laid out 5 goals for the Iran war on Feb 28. Here’s where they stand
stories.summary: An assessment of U.S. President Donald Trump's five stated goals for the Iran war, outlined on February 28, indicates that U.S. and Israeli militaries have destroyed many of Iran's ballistic missiles and launchers through airstrikes. Progress on the remaining objectives was evaluated.

stories.title: Takeaways from Trump’s speech on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump delivered his first prime-time address since the war on Iran began, defending his handling of the month-old conflict. The speech covered the administration's stated rationale and progress in the military campaign.

stories.title: Armenia Cannot Be in Both EU and Russian-Led Customs Bloc, Putin says
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Armenia cannot simultaneously belong to the EU and the Russian-led customs bloc. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan acknowledged the incompatibility but said pursuing both paths remained possible for the time being.

stories.title: Armenia Cannot Be in Both EU and Moscow-Led Customs Bloc, Putin says
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Armenia cannot simultaneously be a member of the EU and the Moscow-led Eurasian Customs Union. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan acknowledged the incompatibility but said pursuing both paths was possible "for now."

stories.title: Liberia: Rodney Sieh Urges National Apology Over Murder of Former Leaders, Warns Liberia Is Repeating the Errors That Fueled Conflict
stories.summary: FrontPageAfrica Managing Editor Rodney Sieh has called for a national apology over the murder of former Liberian leaders. He warned that Liberia continues to repeat the governance failures that previously fueled civil conflict.

stories.title: The hottest point on 1,200 km of front — and Ukraine just held it for another week, top commander says
stories.summary: Four Ukrainian brigades repelled 291 Russian attacks across multiple sub-sectors of the Pokrovsk-Myrnohrad area along a 1,200-kilometer front line. The successful defense prompted a personal visit from Ukraine's commander-in-chief to the hotly contested area.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuela’s acting president Delcy Rodríguez
stories.summary: The United States lifted sanctions on Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez as part of efforts to normalize relations between the two countries. The move follows the U.S. abduction of former President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, who were taken to New York to face drug trafficking charges. Both have pleaded not guilty.

stories.title: Milei presides over Falklands fallen tribute amid thaw in relations with London
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei led a Veterans Day and Falklands War commemoration ceremony at Plaza San Martín in Buenos Aires's Retiro neighborhood. The event honored soldiers killed in the 1982 conflict and included a presidential address, wreath-laying, and a minute of silence. The tribute comes amid improving relations between Argentina and the United Kingdom.

stories.title: ‘Back to the Stone Ages’:  #Trump says #Iran war nearly over in national #address
stories.summary: President Donald Trump delivered his first nationwide address since the start of the U.S.-led war in the Middle East, claiming the U.S. was "very close" to achieving its objectives in Iran. He vowed to strike the country "extremely hard" in the coming days.

stories.title: Archaeologists discover wreck of Danish warship sunk by Nelson 225 years ago
stories.summary: Marine archaeologists discovered the wreck of the Danish warship Dannebroge on the seabed of Copenhagen harbour, more than 200 years after it was sunk by Admiral Horatio Nelson's British fleet. Divers are racing to excavate the 19th-century vessel before the site is developed into a new housing district.

stories.title: Iran pledges safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz for Philippine oil shipments
stories.summary: Iran pledged to ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz for Philippine-flagged vessels, energy shipments, and Filipino seafarers. The assurance was conveyed by Iran's foreign minister to the Philippines as Manila works to secure energy supplies.

stories.title: Low government approval deepens internal tensions within Uruguay's Frente Amplio
stories.summary: Polls from major Uruguayan survey firms show unusual discontent among Frente Amplio voters roughly one year into the left-wing coalition's fourth administration. The low government approval ratings are intensifying factional disputes within the party ahead of internal elections expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

stories.title: Eight countries condemn Israel’s one-sided death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: Eight Muslim-majority countries issued a joint condemnation of Israel's new death penalty legislation applicable to Palestinians. The nations described the law as discriminatory and said it entrenches what they called a system of apartheid.

stories.title: Rain begins in Karachi, surrounding areas as local authorities declare emergency
stories.summary: Heavy rain from a westerly weather system reached Karachi and surrounding areas, prompting local authorities to declare an emergency. Rainfall was recorded across multiple neighborhoods including Gulistan-i-Jauhar, Saddar, Clifton, and Keamari.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis coordinate with Iran, but retain independence, despite war
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement coordinates its military and political activities with Iran but retains operational independence, according to analysts. The Houthis pursue their own domestic objectives while aligning broadly with Iran's regional strategy.

stories.title: Wild neighbours: Why animals are moving into our cities?
stories.summary: Wild animals are increasingly appearing in urban areas worldwide, including leopards in Indian cities, bears roaming streets in Japan, and foxes in central London. The phenomenon is driven by animals entering cities in search of food, generating widespread attention on social media.

stories.title: Liberia: Barbu Urges World Body to Boost Support for Liberia's War Crimes Court
stories.summary: Dr. Jallah A. Barbu, Executive Director of the Office for the Establishment of Liberia's War and Economic Crimes Court, has renewed calls for robust international support to establish the court.

stories.title: First Thing: Trump claims Iran war is ‘nearing completion’ in address to nation
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared in a prime-time national address that the month-long U.S.-Israeli war against Iran was "nearing completion." Democrats criticized the speech for failing to answer fundamental questions about the conflict, which has caused global economic disruption and strained transatlantic alliances.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks and its impact on Iran’s economy
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is affecting the Iranian economy. The strikes have disrupted economic activity, though specific details on the scale of the impact remain unclear.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 2: Picassos and other veiled masterpieces in Iran
stories.summary: A report highlighted art collections amassed by former Iranian Queen Farah Pahlavi, including works by Picasso, currently held in Iran. The briefing also covered a Passover Haggadah examining the influence of Egyptian culture on Jewish traditions.

stories.title: Nigeria: 30 Students, 1 Teacher Hospitalised Over Suspected Chemical Leak in Ogun
stories.summary: Approximately 30 students and one teacher at Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School in Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, Nigeria, were hospitalized after a suspected chemical or gas leak at the school premises.

stories.title: Civilian infrastructure and high-rise buildings damaged in Chornomorsk due to Russian attack
stories.summary: In Chornomorsk, Odesa region, civilian infrastructure and high-rise buildings were damaged as a result of a Russian attack on the night of April 2.

stories.title: Israelis spend Passover under shadow of Iran war, as businesses cling to survival
stories.summary: Israeli businesses are struggling economically during Passover amid the ongoing war with Iran. Israel's Finance Ministry estimates the economy is losing at least 4.3 billion shekels per week, with business owners like a Tel Aviv florist struggling during what is normally a peak sales period.

stories.title: Democrats demand ceasefire as Trump defends costly war on Iran
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers criticized President Trump's national address on the U.S.-led war in Iran, calling the conflict deadly and lacking clear objectives. Trump described it as a decisive victory and threatened further escalation over the coming weeks.

stories.summary: NASA launched four astronauts aboard the Artemis II mission from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, marking the first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years. The crew of three Americans and one Canadian launched atop NASA's Space Launch System rocket.

stories.title: Iran's cluster warheads expose gaps in Israel's defences
stories.summary: About half of all Iran's ballistic missiles launched at Israel in this conflict have carried cluster warheads, turning one missile into dozens.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israel says intercepting Iran missile attack, after Trump speech
stories.summary: Israel reported intercepting an Iranian missile attack following President Trump's address claiming U.S. forces would soon finish operations in Iran. Iran's President responded by accusing the U.S. of war crimes and acting under Israeli influence.

stories.title: UN appoints former Haiti PM Garry Conille as Resident Coordinator in Kenya
stories.summary: The United Nations has appointed Garry Conille, a former two-time prime minister of Haiti, as UN Resident Coordinator in Kenya. His second term as Haiti's prime minister in 2024 overlapped with the deployment of Kenyan troops to a UN-backed security force in Haiti.

stories.summary: Source: Hezbollah using homes as hiding spots for reconnaissance, launchpads for anti-tank fire • More fighters detained after surrendering to Israeli soldiers

stories.title: Russians injure three residents of Donetsk region
stories.summary: Over the past 24 hours, on April 1, Russian invaders wounded three residents of the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Two Israeli infants among wounded by shrapnel in overnight Iranian missile barrage
stories.summary: In northern Israel, two men aged 85 and 34 were moderately injured on Thursday morning by shrapnel after a Hezbollah attack, MDA reported.

stories.title: Trump polled advisers about replacing Tulsi Gabbard as intelligence chief
stories.summary: President Donald Trump privately asked cabinet officials in recent weeks whether he should replace Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. Trump's frustration reportedly stemmed from Gabbard shielding a former deputy who undermined his rationale for the war with Iran. No replacement candidate has been identified.

stories.title: China EV makers surge back in March as subsidies and financing spur demand
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle makers reported a strong sales rebound in March, driven by local government subsidies and aggressive financing incentives. Further momentum is expected as dozens of new models prepare to debut at the Auto China show in Beijing.

stories.title: China youth flock to TCM bars for ‘prescription cocktails’ amid rise of ‘punk wellness’ lifestyle
stories.summary: Young Chinese consumers are frequenting traditional Chinese medicine-themed bars where certified TCM practitioners take pulses and craft herbal-infused cocktails. The trend reflects a growing "punk wellness" lifestyle blending nightlife with health culture.

stories.title: Whispers in Supreme Court as Trump takes front-row seat for oral arguments
stories.summary: President Trump attended oral arguments at the U.S. Supreme Court, accompanied by Attorney General Pam Bondi and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, as the administration defended its executive order challenging birthright citizenship protections.

stories.title: US op to seize Iran’s uranium would take weeks, require building a runway — report
stories.summary: Reports indicate the US has briefed President Trump on a plan to seize Iran's enriched uranium, which would require weeks and the construction of a runway. The operation could involve airlifting thousands of troops and heavy equipment while forces remain exposed to hostile fire.

stories.title: Occupied Donetsk’s drinking water crisis is so bad that Russia is now proposing heavy-metal-laced mine drainage as a substitute
stories.summary: Russian-occupied Donetsk faces a severe drinking water crisis, with authorities proposing heavy-metal-laced mine drainage as a substitute source. Ukraine linked the inadequate response to local officials' interest in maintaining access to financial flows from Moscow rather than solving the problem.

stories.title: Artemis II astronauts bound for moon after rocketing away on NASA's first lunar voyage in decades
stories.summary: Four astronauts launched aboard NASA's Artemis II mission on Wednesday, marking humanity's first crewed lunar voyage in over 50 years. The flight around the moon is a precursor to a planned lunar landing in approximately two years. The launch took place from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

stories.title: Takeaways from Trump's address: No end date for Iran war and few details on strategy ahead
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's prime-time address on the war against Iran offered few new strategic details and no definitive end date for the conflict. Notably absent was any mention of negotiations with Iran or plans to deploy ground troops, despite Trump having previously claimed talks were underway.

stories.title: Lebanon hit by fresh Israeli raid and Hezbollah response
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck a building in Zebdine, near Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, causing casualties. Hezbollah responded by launching rockets and drones across the border into Israel, further escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Protests erupt in West Bank as Israel approves death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters demonstrated across the West Bank on Tuesday following the Israeli parliament's passage of a law establishing the death penalty by hanging for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis.

stories.title: Critical aid supplies to Sudan disrupted by 'ripple effect' from Middle East war
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that the Iran war's "ripple effect" is disrupting critical aid supplies to Sudan. Gas, oil, fertilizers, and food aid are facing severe delays as shipments remain stuck in the Persian Gulf due to the conflict.

stories.title: Trump’s address to the nation: We are on the cusp of ending Iran’s sinister threat to America, the world
stories.summary: President Trump delivered a national address stating that core strategic objectives of the war against Iran are nearing completion within two to three weeks. He warned that if Iran attempts to retrieve its enriched uranium, the US would launch further strikes.

stories.title: War update: 146 clashes on front lines, fiercest battles are in Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk, and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Over the past 24 hours, on April 1, there were 146 combat engagements between the Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian troops on the front lines. The enemy attacked most intensely in the Kostiantynivk

stories.title: Crises and institutions
stories.summary: The article examines how modern states use specialized institutions such as disaster management authorities and apex committees to manage crises, with specific reference to Pakistan's federal and provincial structures.

stories.title: Mozambique clears IMF debt early
stories.summary: Mozambique has fully repaid its debt to the International Monetary Fund ahead of schedule, clearing more than $630 million in obligations.

stories.title: Iran vows 'more destructive' attacks after Trump threats
stories.summary: Iran threatened "crushing" attacks against the United States and Israel on Thursday, firing missiles at Tel Aviv after President Trump vowed to bomb Iran "back to the Stone Ages." The U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, which began over a month ago, has spread across the Middle East and disrupted the global economy.

stories.title: Iranian President says in letter that Iran harbors no enmity towards ordinary Americans
stories.summary: Iranian President addressed a letter to the American public stating that Iran harbors no enmity toward ordinary Americans. He argued that portraying Iran as a threat was inconsistent with historical reality and present-day facts.

stories.title: Macron arrives in South Korea after Japan visit, touts Europe’s ‘predictability’

stories.title: Bondi terrorist loses bid to prevent media from reporting on his family
stories.summary: Naveed Akram, convicted of a terrorist attack in Bondi, lost a court bid to prevent media from reporting on his family. The judge ruled that any suppression order would be ineffective since it could not cover social media platforms.

stories.title: Farage and Jenrick to speak on pensions triple lock as calls grow to sack Reform’s housing spokesperson – UK politics live
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and Conservative figure Robert Jenrick are set to speak on the pensions triple lock amid growing calls to dismiss Reform's housing spokesperson Simon Dudley. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer urged Farage to act over Dudley's comments about Grenfell Tower, which Starmer called shameful.

stories.title: Oil price jumps and markets slide after Trump warning to Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged more than 7%, surpassing $108.50 per barrel, after U.S. President Donald Trump vowed in a televised speech to strike Iran "extremely hard" in the coming weeks. Global stock markets fell as investor hopes for a near-term de-escalation in the Middle East conflict faded.

stories.title: Oil price shock incoming
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the ongoing war is beginning to cause physical fuel shortages across Asia, which depends heavily on Persian Gulf energy supplies. Rising freight and insurance costs have already driven oil price volatility.

stories.title: Trump’s threats to withdraw US from Nato ‘look like Putin’s dream plan’, says Tusk – Europe live
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said U.S. President Trump's threats to withdraw from NATO resemble what he called Putin's dream plan. Tusk also cited the prospect of a European energy crisis and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's moves to block support for Ukraine as benefiting Russia.

stories.title: Nearly 1,200 children killed or injured in Yemen despite truce: NGO
stories.summary: Save the Children reported that nearly 1,200 children have been killed or injured in Yemen despite a truce being in place. The NGO said nearly half of child casualties were caused by landmines and explosive remnants of war.

stories.title: Iran sets up 'tollbooth' in Strait of Hormuz for ships seeking safe passage
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly begun collecting tolls from ships seeking safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices rose and stocks fell following President Trump's speech warning of strikes against Iran over the next two to three weeks. Questions remain about whether Iran's toll collection could become a formalized system.

stories.title: Russian drones attack port infrastructure in Odesa region overnight, causing damage
stories.summary: On the night of April 2, Russian drones attacked port infrastructure in the Odesa region.

stories.title: U.S. lifts sanctions on Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez
stories.summary: The United States lifted sanctions on Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez, further recognizing her authority following the U.S. military capture of former President Nicolás Maduro.

stories.title: Trump takes a dig at Macron, saying France President’s wife treats him ‘badly’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized NATO allies for not joining the military campaign against Iran and directed a personal remark at French President Emmanuel Macron, claiming Macron's wife treats him "badly."

stories.title: Sindh CM Murad orders demolition of fire-hit Gul Plaza structure
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah ordered the demolition of the fire-damaged Gul Plaza structure in Karachi to facilitate reconstruction. A devastating fire at the building killed dozens on January 17.

stories.title: Israeli settlers are using 'fencing' to seize land in West Bank
stories.summary: 'Fencing' has become common among Israeli settlers in the West Bank to arbitrarily extend control over Palestinian land at minimal cost.

stories.title: ‘Dumbest alliance break-up in history’: Trump threatens to leave NATO
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to withdraw the United States from NATO, a move the Wall Street Journal called the "dumbest" alliance break-up in history. Separately, NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched from Cape Canaveral, marking a crewed return toward the Moon.

stories.title: Chakwera warns: Fighting corruption comes at a cost - Interview
stories.summary: Malawi's former president Lazarus Chakwera discussed the personal and political costs of fighting corruption, describing the challenges and pushback leaders face when confronting entrenched interests.

stories.title: First Chadian police arrive in Haiti to join UN-backed Gang Suppression Force
stories.summary: An advance contingent of Chadian police arrived in Haiti on Wednesday to join the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force helping Haitian security forces combat gangs controlling much of Port-au-Prince. Chad has pledged 800 officers, though it remains unclear which other countries will contribute personnel.

stories.title: Babies evacuated from Gaza two years ago returned to their overjoyed parents
stories.summary: Eleven toddlers born prematurely in Gaza and evacuated to Egypt in November 2023 were reunited with their families in Gaza City through a UN-organized mission. The children had been among 29 preterm babies evacuated from Al Shifa hospital.

stories.title: Reactions as Artemis II astronauts lift off on historic lunar mission
stories.summary: Four astronauts launched from Florida on NASA's Artemis II mission, a 10-day trip around the moon representing the farthest distance humans have ever traveled. The mission is a major step toward returning people to the lunar surface this decade.

stories.title: South Africa: Good Friday in a Time of War
stories.summary: A reflection published from Cape Town, South Africa, examined the significance of Good Friday and Holy Week in the context of ongoing global conflicts and human suffering.

stories.title: US, Israel bomb Iran civilian sites after Trump Stone Age threat
stories.summary: US and Israeli forces struck civilian sites in Iran after US President Trump threatened widespread destruction. Tehran vowed a crushing response to the attacks and demands.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with 'Stone Age' as Tehran vows response
stories.summary: Following Trump’s threat to bomb Iran into the “Stone Ages”, Tehran warns of broader and more destructive strikes on the US and Israel.

stories.title: Why China and Vietnam are shifting from confrontation to calm in South China Sea claims
stories.summary: China and Vietnam have shifted toward pragmatic restraint over their competing South China Sea claims, despite continued Chinese dredging at Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands. Vietnam lodged a formal protest in March calling the activities illegal.

stories.title: Trump says US close to completing Iran mission, vows intensified strikes
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the military campaign against Iran was nearing completion but vowed to intensify strikes over the coming weeks, signaling both a possible endgame and further escalation.

stories.title: Trump sends crude surging as Iran speech fails to allay war concerns
stories.summary: US President Trump's televised address on the Iran war failed to ease market concerns, sending crude oil prices surging. Trump said the conflict was nearing completion but threatened to strike Iran intensely for two to three more weeks.

stories.title: Today marks fourth anniversary of liberation of Kyiv region from Russian invaders
stories.summary: Four years ago, on April 2, 2022, the Ukrainian Defense Forces completely drove Russian troops out of the Kyiv region.

stories.title: Five-point plan
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar visited Beijing, where China endorsed a five-point plan to end the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The plan calls for an immediate ceasefire, U.S.-Iran talks, and security for the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Surging ‘Jewish terrorism’ in West Bank condemned but goes unpunished
stories.summary: Violence by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has escalated to unprecedented levels since the start of the Iran war, with NGOs and opposition figures condemning widespread impunity.

stories.title: Egypt races to rescue Gaza ceasefire as Iran war pushes it aside
stories.summary: Progress in implementing the Gaza ceasefire deal is also largely contingent on de-escalation with Iran and renewed high-level diplomacy, analysts said.

stories.title: Russian attacks hit three districts of Dnipropetrovsk region, one killed, several injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked three districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than ten times with drones and artillery as of the morning of April 2, killing one person and injuring two others.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. objectives in Iran ‘nearing completion’
stories.summary: President Trump stated in a national address that U.S. objectives in the military campaign against Iran are nearing completion, threatening to strike extremely hard over the next two to three weeks.

stories.title: Malaysian minister offers personal aid to family of man killed in drink-driving crash
stories.summary: Malaysian Transport Minister Anthony Loke personally visited and provided financial aid to the widow of motorcyclist Amirul Hafiz Omar, who was killed in a drink-driving accident that threatened to inflame racial tensions.

stories.title: From Iran to Israel: An Iranian volunteer’s unlikely stand in wartime
stories.summary: Mehran Rezvani, an Iranian who grew up during the Islamic Revolution, has become a volunteer and supporter of Israel during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Burkina Faso army, jihadists have killed more than 1,800 civilians since 2023, HRW says
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that more than 1,800 civilians have been killed in Burkina Faso since 2023 by both the national army and jihadist groups. The report accused the military and allied civilian militias of killing more civilians than jihadists and called on the International Criminal Court to investigate war crimes by all parties.

stories.title: Why is a French sugar giant—with a former president on payroll—still supplying Russian military?
stories.summary: Its Russian subsidiaries made camouflage nets and anti-drone equipment—while a former French president is on the payroll.

stories.title: Trump says conflict nearing end, threatens wider attacks on Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared in a White House address that the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran could conclude within weeks, while threatening intensified strikes. He described the conflict as a decisive victory.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,300 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia's cumulative combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,300,030 personnel as of April 2, 2026. An estimated 1,300 Russian soldiers were killed or wounded in the past 24 hours alone.

stories.title: Iran’s ex-foreign minister Kharazi ‘gravely wounded’ in attack on his home
stories.summary: Apparent assassination attempt comes as Iran's army pledges to fight until the US, Israel face 'permanent surrender'.

stories.title: Oil price surges, Asian stocks fall as Trump vows to continue Iran attacks
stories.summary: Asian stocks also took a hit after Trump’s speech as most Southeast Asian countries rely heavily on oil imports.

stories.title: Fact check: Donald Trump speaks on Iran, oil and economy
stories.summary: In a nationally televised address, US President Donald Trump made claims about the war in Iran, asserting that all of Iran's original leaders had been killed and that the US was fully independent of Middle Eastern oil. Fact-checkers scrutinized the accuracy of these statements.

stories.title: Indonesia calls for probe into  UN peacekeepers’ killing
stories.summary: Indonesia called on the United Nations to investigate the deaths of three Indonesian peacekeepers killed by Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon. Indonesia's UN representative demanded a direct UN inquiry during an emergency Security Council meeting.

stories.title: A 250-Year Arsenal of Innovation: A Call for Articles on American Defense Technologies
stories.summary: The publication Cogs of War issued a call for articles examining American defense technologies ahead of the United States' 250th anniversary on July 4, 2026. The project aims to chronicle innovations from early submarine designs through nuclear weapons, GPS, and artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Coordinated conflict: how the Ukraine and Iran wars are starting to overlap
stories.summary: Analysts say the wars in Ukraine and Iran are becoming increasingly intertwined through shared weapons, intelligence exchanges, and their combined impact on the global economy. The interconnection is drawing more countries into both conflicts, extending instability across Europe and the Middle East.

stories.title: Thames Water ‘close to deal that would spare it new Ofwat fines until 2030’
stories.summary: Thames Water is reportedly close to an agreement with regulator Ofwat that would spare the company from new fines until 2030 in exchange for investment commitments. The deal was proposed by creditors seeking to prevent the struggling English water utility from being temporarily renationalised.

stories.title: Trump signs executive order for crackdown on mail-in voting ahead of mid-term election
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order seeking to restrict mail-in voting ahead of U.S. midterm elections. Democrats and legal experts anticipated court challenges, with questions about the president's authority to impose such measures.

stories.title: ‘China shock 2.0’ is a false narrative born of Western anxiety: Chinese media
stories.summary: China's state-run Economic Daily published editorials pushing back against claims of a "China shock 2.0," asserting that China's 2026 growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent far exceeds the projected 2.6 percent global growth rate.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drones return to Bashneft-Novoil refinery in Ufa 1,300+ km from the front — the primary distillation unit is burning again

stories.summary: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the Molucca Sea off Ternate in North Maluku, Indonesia, on April 2, killing at least one person. A tsunami warning was briefly issued and subsequently lifted.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Kharkiv, cars catch fire
stories.summary: Russian drones struck Kharkiv's Kyivskyi district overnight, setting several cars on fire in the Ukrainian city.

stories.title: In historic first, woman among four set for Moon voyage
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission includes astronaut Christina Koch, who will become the first woman on a lunar mission. The four-member crew represents the first crewed journey to the Moon in over 50 years.

stories.title: Bahamas heads for early election on May 12
stories.summary: The Bahamas will hold an early general election on May 12, as announced by the prime minister on Wednesday. The Caribbean nation is contending with affordability issues that prompted the decision to go to the polls ahead of schedule.

stories.title: ‘Unintended target’: Seven-month-old girl in stroller fatally shot in Brooklyn
stories.summary: A seven-month-old girl in a stroller was fatally shot in Brooklyn by stray gunfire in what authorities described as a suspected gang-related shooting. Officials said the infant was an unintended target.

stories.title: Russia is luring students with large financial packages to join drone units
stories.summary: Russia is offering large financial incentives to university students to join drone units fighting in Ukraine as operators and engineers. Companies in Russia's Ryazan region have also been given quotas to recruit workers for the military.

stories.title: Mourners vow resistance as Iran marks Islamic Republic’s 47th anniversary
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in Tehran to honour a commander, vowing resistance amid heightened tension with US and Israel.

stories.title: UK to host 35-state  moot on reopening of Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced it will host a meeting of approximately 35 countries to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Middle East war. British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper will lead the discussions.

stories.title: From Filament to Firepower: 3D Printing’s Impact on Warfare
stories.summary: A report highlights how 3D printing and additive manufacturing are transforming weapons production in armed conflicts, particularly among non-state actors. Beyond enabling drone warfare in Ukraine, the technology now allows firearms and even ammunition to be produced using digital files and commercially available parts.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs economist sees Iran war testing China’s self-reliance
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs chief Asia-Pacific economist Andrew Tilton discussed how the oil crisis triggered by the US-Israel war against Iran is testing China's economic self-reliance and affecting growth prospects across Asian economies.

stories.title: Trump says war with Iran 'nearing completion,' could conclude within weeks
stories.summary: President Trump stated in his address that the war with Iran is "nearing completion" and estimated it could conclude within two to three weeks.

stories.title: Alleged Bondi terrorist Naveed Akram denied suppression order over identities of family members
stories.summary: A judge at Sydney's Downing Centre Local Court denied accused Bondi attacker Naveed Akram's request for a 40-year suppression order over the identities and addresses of his family members. The ruling followed a challenge by a collective of media organisations against the interim suppression order.

stories.title: Iranians vow to ‘resist until the end’ at Guards naval chief’s funeral
stories.summary: Large crowds gathered at Enghelab Square in Tehran for the funeral of a senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps naval commander, with attendees unfurling massive Iranian flags. Government supporters vowed to "resist until the end" amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Mohmand’s unregulated marble industry raises environmental, safety concerns
stories.summary: Unregulated marble factories in Mohmand district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, are discharging untreated waste into waterways, blocking streams and silting dams. Experts warn the environmental damage increases flood risks and undermines irrigation and water storage.

stories.title: Pakistan may become ‘fourth most populated nation’ in five years
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal warned that Pakistan, currently the world's fifth most populous country, is projected to surpass Indonesia in population within five years, creating major challenges for healthcare, education, and infrastructure.

stories.title: Heavy rains, flash floods wreak havoc across Balochistan
stories.summary: Heavy rains and flash floods struck more than 30 districts across Balochistan, Pakistan, causing widespread infrastructure damage and communication disruptions. A 12-year-old girl was killed by lightning, and authorities banned travel as severe flooding warnings continued.

stories.title: UK looks to relax planning rules for factory farms after industry lobbying
stories.summary: UK ministers are revising national planning rules to make it easier to build intensive livestock farms following lobbying by leading chicken producers. Documents obtained under Freedom of Information laws show the industry campaign has lasted at least two years, despite concerns over water pollution and air quality.

stories.title: Argentina names IRGC as terrorist group, triggering financial sanctions
stories.summary: Argentina officially designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, citing the 1992 and 1994 attacks on Israeli and Jewish targets in Buenos Aires. The designation triggers financial sanctions and restrictions.

stories.title: How China’s ‘pig semen eyedrop’ could help deliver Alzheimer’s treatment
stories.summary: Researchers at China's Shenyang Pharmaceutical University developed eye drops using pig semen-derived exosomes that can penetrate retinal tissue, potentially offering a new delivery method for treating Alzheimer's disease. The research was published in Science Advances.

stories.title: Southern Africa: Undiagnosed TB Pose Challenge for South Africa, Mozambique
stories.summary: Experts report that while Africa is making progress in reducing tuberculosis, undiagnosed TB cases and drug-resistant infections continue to pose significant challenges in South Africa and Mozambique.

stories.title: Nigeria: Atiku Criticises National Assembly for Hurried Approval of Tinubu's $6bn Loan Requests
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Vice President Atiku Abubakar criticized Nigeria's National Assembly for what he called a rushed approval of President Tinubu's $6 billion loan requests, questioning the lack of debate and oversight.

stories.title: FBI arrives in Cuba to investigate deadly speedboat shoot-out
stories.summary: FBI agents arrived in Cuba to investigate a deadly speedboat shoot-out. Cuban authorities said the assailants were Cuban exiles who traveled from the United States.

stories.title: Russian drone hits apartment building in Chuhuiv, fire breaks out, three women injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential apartment building in Chuhuiv, Kharkiv region, igniting a fire across two floors and injuring three women.

stories.title: Wreck of Danish flagship sunk by famed British admiral discovered after 225 years
stories.summary: Marine archaeologists discovered the wreck of the Danish flagship Dannebroge on the seabed of Copenhagen Harbour, more than 225 years after it was sunk by British Admiral Horatio Nelson. Divers worked in near-zero visibility to excavate the site.

stories.title: Trump to address nation as Iran war batters approval
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was expected to deliver a televised address to reassure the American public that he has a plan for completing the war against Iran, amid falling approval ratings linked to the conflict.

stories.title: Explosions at Burundi ammunition depot kill 13 civilians - army
stories.summary: Explosions at an ammunition depot in Bujumbura, Burundi, killed at least 13 civilians on Tuesday night. The blasts destroyed homes and caused widespread panic in the city.

stories.title: Influencer Myron Gaines performs Nazi salute at Ohio University, mocks Holocaust death toll
stories.summary: Influencer Myron Gaines performed a Nazi salute and mocked the Holocaust death toll during an appearance at Ohio University, sparking widespread outrage. He also reportedly spread antisemitic conspiracy theories on campus.

stories.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges citizens to flee, warns of imminent attacks
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Baghdad raised Iraq to its highest advisory level (level four), urging American citizens to leave the country immediately. The embassy warned that Iran-aligned fighters could carry out attacks in central Baghdad within 24 to 48 hours.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty law is not about executing Palestinians
stories.summary: It is about eliminating Palestinian existence in Palestine.

stories.title: Trump says war almost over, warns of weeks of heavy strikes, Iran calls US demands ‘irrational’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned of weeks of heavy strikes against Iran and insisted Tehran must reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's government dismissed U.S. demands as "irrational" amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Bondi Beach terrorist Naveed Akram loses bid to give family anonymity
stories.summary: Naveed Akram, accused of carrying out a terrorist attack at Bondi Beach during a Hanukkah celebration, lost his legal bid to grant his family anonymity. He faces 59 charges, including 15 counts of murder and 40 counts of wounding with intent to murder.

stories.title: NATO chief to visit Washington next week as Trump threatens exit from alliance
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General is scheduled to visit Washington next week as U.S. President Donald Trump threatens to exit the alliance. Trump criticized European NATO members for refusing to send ships to help unblock the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Three minors among four charged over foiled attack at Bank of America Paris branch
stories.summary: French anti-terror prosecutors charged four people, including three minors, over an alleged attempt to detonate a homemade explosive device outside the Bank of America headquarters in Paris. Authorities said the plot may be linked to a little-known Islamist group with possible but unconfirmed ties to Iran.

stories.title: From Wagyu to joss paper: rise of pet spirit money, luxury farewell ceremonies take China by storm
stories.summary: A growing trend in China involves elaborate pet funerals featuring spirit money in various currencies and luxury paper offerings such as Wagyu beef and salmon, extending traditional joss paper mourning customs to deceased pets.

stories.title: Full text of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s letter to Americans
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's open letter to Americans questioned whether the U.S. government's current policies truly align with the "America First" agenda promoted by the administration.

stories.title: Thursday briefing: ​Why does Donald Trump have it in for the UK?
stories.summary: Britain's refusal to join the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran has triggered a backlash from the White House, straining the transatlantic relationship. President Trump has mocked the UK's navy and suggested allies concerned about jet fuel supplies should take resources from the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran president asks US people if Mid-East war puts ‘America First’
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed an open letter to the American public, questioning whether the Middle East conflict serves the "America First" agenda and stating that ordinary Americans are not Iran's enemy.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s CLP Power to give out HK$100 shopping coupons to 600,000 customers
stories.summary: Hong Kong's CLP Power announced it will distribute HK$100 shopping coupons to approximately 600,000 eligible customers using HK$60 million from its Community Energy Saving Fund. The move follows a fuel cost adjustment increase linked to energy disruptions from the U.S.-Israel war against Iran.

stories.title: Why Asean neutrality in Iran war is key to unlocking Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: ASEAN's neutrality in the Iran conflict is being viewed as strategically important for securing access through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has leveraged control of the waterway to restrict oil supplies to the U.S. and its allies amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: Stubb discusses NATO, Ukraine, and Iran with Trump
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb spoke by phone with U.S. President Donald Trump, discussing NATO, Ukraine, and Iran.

stories.title: Fresh fire from Iran towards Israel
stories.summary: Israel's military reported that its air defenses were responding to a fourth wave of Iranian strikes within six hours, marking continued Iranian fire directed at Israeli territory.

stories.title: Trump: US 'on the cusp' of ending Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump says his core "objectives are nearing completion" in Iran, during a primetime televised speech from the White House.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: markets and oil prices suffer after Trump defends Iran war in prime-time address
stories.summary: Global markets and oil prices fell further after U.S. President Donald Trump defended the Iran war in a prime-time address but offered limited detail on how the conflict would conclude. Trump claimed Iran was near obtaining a nuclear weapon, while Israel continued strikes on Iranian targets.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran war ‘nearing completion’ and seeks to justify conflict in prime-time address
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared the month-long war in Iran a success "nearing completion" in a prime-time address, but offered no clear exit plan or timeline. The conflict has caused global economic turmoil, fractured transatlantic alliances, and eroded the president's approval ratings.

stories.title: New leader of UN-backed force arrives in Haiti with Chadian advance team
stories.summary: A new commander of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force arrived in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on Wednesday accompanied by an advance deployment of Chadian troops to bolster security operations against armed gangs.

stories.title: One killed and buildings damaged as magnitude 7.4 earthquake strikes Indonesia
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck near Indonesia's Ternate island in North Maluku province, killing one person and damaging buildings. The quake, at a depth of 35 kilometers, triggered small tsunami waves and prompted regional tsunami warnings.

stories.title: Donald Trump vows to hit Iran 'extremely hard' in the coming weeks
stories.summary: During a televised national address, President Donald Trump vowed to hit Iran "extremely hard" in the coming weeks. The speech rattled global markets, with oil prices rising amid fears of a widening conflict and disruption to key supply routes.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia's New Northeastern State Detains Journalist for Criticizing President
stories.summary: Authorities in Somalia's newly formed Northeastern State detained journalist Abdiqani Abdirahman Mohamed without charge on March 26 over a video criticizing state President Abdiqadir Ahmed Aw-Ali. The Committee to Protect Journalists has called for his release.

stories.title: Sirens blare across Israel, as Hezbollah claims more attacks
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it launched drones and rockets at northern Israel on Thursday. Israel's Home Front Command activated air raid sirens across the area in response to the attacks.

stories.title: Trump’s primetime speech on Iran war: Key takeaways
stories.summary: In a primetime televised address, US President Donald Trump stated that Washington is close to achieving its goals in Iran and threatened to bomb the country into the "Stone Ages."

stories.title: South Africa: Soldiers Hit the Streets of Mitchells Plain a Day After a Shooting
stories.summary: South African soldiers conducted operations in Mitchells Plain, Cape Town, searching homes in Beacon Valley for firearms one day after a shooting incident in the area.

stories.title: Gulf states considering new pipeline amid Iran curb on Hormuz Strait: Report
stories.summary: Gulf states are reconsidering plans for new oil pipelines that would bypass Iranian restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Financial Times. The projects would be expensive, politically complex, and take years to complete.

stories.title: Missile interception in Abu Dhabi causes minor damage, authorities say
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi authorities reported a successful missile interception by air defense systems near Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi (KEZAD). Minor damage was reported, but no injuries were sustained.

stories.title: Hong Kong man, 89, rescued after being found clinging to care home exterior wall
stories.summary: An 89-year-old man in Hong Kong's To Kwa Wan district was rescued after being found clinging to the exterior wall of a care home. He had fallen from a second-floor window while attempting to retrieve an object.

stories.title: Mozambique: Mozambique Pays Debt to IMF in Full
stories.summary: The Mozambican government fully repaid its outstanding debt of approximately 630.1 million U.S. dollars to the International Monetary Fund in March.

stories.title: Trump’s national address on Iran ’embarrassing, incoherent’
stories.summary: Harlan Ullman, a former senior US naval officer, criticized President Trump's national address on the Iran war, calling it "embarrassing" and "incoherent."

stories.title: ‘People need hope’: Greens court voters in battle for north-east council seats
stories.summary: Former Labour North of Tyne mayor Jamie Driscoll is standing as a Green Party candidate for Newcastle city council's central Monument ward. The Greens are courting voters in north-east England local elections, with Driscoll among the party's highest-profile recruits.

stories.title: Your Party to focus local election efforts on backing independent candidates
stories.summary: Your Party, whose parliamentary leader is Jeremy Corbyn, plans to back around 250 candidates in UK local elections, focusing on urban areas with large Muslim populations. The party will support independent candidates in London boroughs including Tower Hamlets, Newham, and Redbridge.

stories.title: Teachers made ill by rats and hit by toaster receive share of £15m payout
stories.summary: The UK teaching union NASUWT revealed that school staff received a share of £15 million in compensation for workplace injuries and other claims. Cases included a teacher made ill by a rat infestation and another injured when a pupil threw a toaster and chair.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘success’ in Iran in just 32 days compared to lengthy US wars
stories.summary: During his national address, US President Donald Trump claimed success in Iran after 32 days of conflict, calling Iran the "bully of the Middle East" and declaring it "no longer a threat," contrasting the timeline with longer US wars.

stories.title: Trump threatens to bring Iran ‘back to the Stone Ages’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to bring Iran "back to the Stone Ages" by intensifying US military strikes against the country.

stories.title: Fuel prices to fall another 5.7 cents a litre after states and Canberra strike GST deal
stories.summary: The Australian government struck a deal with states to redirect GST revenue on fuel sales, reducing petrol prices by an additional 5.7 cents per litre for three months. Combined with this week's halving of fuel excise, the total reduction reaches 32 cents per litre.

stories.title: Trump urges countries ‘get involved’ in war on Iran if they can’t get fuel
stories.summary: In his televised address, President Trump urged oil-dependent nations that rely on shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to "get involved" in the war on Iran, calling on them to show courage.

stories.title: Australia’s Albanese says Iran war goals met, asks what more is left to achieve
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran appears to have met its core objectives of curbing Tehran's nuclear and missile capabilities. Speaking at the National Press Club in Canberra, he questioned what further goals remain after expressing support for the original aims.

stories.title: Trump admits Iran war was only at behest of 'allies', gives no withdrawal timeline
stories.summary: President Trump acknowledged in a scripted evening address that the US launched its war on Iran to assist regional allies. He emphasized US energy independence, stating Washington does not need Middle Eastern oil, and offered no timeline for withdrawal.

stories.title: Warhead from Russian Kinzhal missile discovered in field in Kyiv region
stories.summary: Explosive ordnance disposal teams from Ukraine's State Emergency Service defused the warhead of a Russian Kh-47 Kinzhal hypersonic missile discovered in a field in the Kyiv region.

stories.title: France charges man over failed attack on US bank
stories.summary: French authorities charged a man in connection with a failed attack on a U.S. bank in France. Investigators explored suspicions that a pro-Iran group may have been involved in the plot.

stories.title: Malaysian woman’s apology for damaging double-parked car triggers outcry
stories.summary: A parking dispute in the Wangsa Maju suburb of Kuala Lumpur sparked a national debate in Malaysia over public shaming and online bullying. A woman who damaged a double-parked Perodua Ativa blocking her vehicle issued a public apology that many Malaysians said appeared coerced.

stories.title: Death of near-blind Myanmar refugee in freezing cold New York ruled a homicide
stories.summary: A near-blind Myanmar refugee died in freezing conditions in New York, and the death has been ruled a homicide. At least 14 people have died in U.S. immigration custody in 2026.

stories.title: Trump says US 'on the cusp' of ending war, threatens to hit Iranian electric plants 'very hard'
stories.summary: President Trump stated that the US is "on the cusp" of ending the Iran war and threatened to strike all of Iran's electric generating plants "very hard and probably simultaneously" if no deal is reached.

stories.title: Penny Wong to join talks with 35 countries, excluding US, to explore ways to reopen strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong will join UK-convened talks with 35 countries, excluding the United States, to explore diplomatic measures to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is hosting the summit to address the blockade of oil shipments.

stories.title: Is Germany’s Postwar Consensus on Israel in Peril?
stories.summary: Germany's postwar consensus on support for Israel is facing challenges as the political left becomes simultaneously more mainstream and more radical in its positions on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

stories.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake hits off Indonesia, killing one
stories.summary: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck between the Indonesian islands of Manado and Ternate, killing one person. Tsunami warnings were issued but have since been lifted.

stories.title: ‘Weak and pathetic’: why is the EU not using its leverage to stop Israel?
stories.summary: The European Union faces criticism for failing to use its leverage against Israel over military operations in Lebanon and Gaza, as well as settler violence in the West Bank. Deep divisions among EU member states on the Israel issue have hindered collective action.

stories.title: ‘Impossible for Chinese’: Yale scientist Zhang Kai leaves US to break racial ceiling
stories.summary: Chinese scientist Zhang Kai left his position at Yale University to return to China, where he is building an ultra-large-scale cellular structure data bank. Zhang told China Science Daily that it would be nearly impossible for a Chinese scholar to lead such a project in the United States.

stories.title: After Trump claims war left Iran 'decimated', Tehran targets Israel's Haifa port
stories.summary: Shortly after President Trump declared Iran "decimated" in his address, Iranian television reported that missiles struck the port of Haifa in Israel.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuela acting president, opening door for assets control
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department removed sanctions on Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez on Wednesday, less than three months after American forces seized former President Nicolas Maduro in a raid on the capital Caracas.

stories.title: Australian Prime Minister 'not clear' what more to achieve in war on Iran
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in Canberra that the original objectives of the war on Iran had been met and questioned what more needs to be achieved. He warned that prolonging the conflict would significantly impact the global economy.

stories.title: Democrats to weigh resolution against AIPAC, fueling concerns about ‘undercurrent of antisemitism’
stories.summary: The Democratic National Committee is set to consider an amendment condemning the influence of AIPAC, the pro-Israel lobby, and the role of "dark money" in US elections. The resolution has raised concerns about antisemitism within the party.

stories.summary:

stories.title: Trump leaves key questions unanswered as he seeks to calm nerves over Iran war
stories.summary: There were some glaring omissions in the president's primetime address, writes the BBC's Gary O'Donoghue.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war to continue, rehashes recent statements
stories.summary: President Trump stated in his address that the war on Iran will continue, giving a timeline of two to three weeks for the US to complete its military objectives. He largely reiterated points from recent statements.

stories.title: US intelligence assessments indicate Iran currently unwilling to negotiate end to war - report
stories.summary: Multiple US intelligence agencies assessed that Iran's regime currently believes it is in a strong enough position to continue the war and is unwilling to negotiate an end to the conflict on US terms.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearing: management company may have breached duty to ensure safety
stories.summary: An independent committee in Hong Kong is examining whether property management firm ISS EastPoint may have breached its duty to ensure safety at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, the site of the city's deadliest fire in decades. The first round of evidential hearings was expected to conclude on Thursday.

stories.title: Estonian start-ups eye Singapore as ‘natural gateway’ to build digital trust in Asean
stories.summary: Estonian start-ups, including identity-verification unicorn Veriff, are looking to Singapore as a gateway to expand digital trust services across Southeast Asia. Veriff, founded in Tallinn in 2015 by Kaarel Kotkas, has reached a valuation of US$1.5 billion and counts PayPal, Bumble, and Visa among its clients.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez
stories.summary: The United States lifted sanctions on Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez as part of a broader easing of measures following the removal of former President Nicolás Maduro.

stories.title: Iran launches attacks on Israel after Trump address ends
stories.summary: The Israeli military said its air defenses responded to a third wave of Iranian missile salvos within three hours, launched shortly after President Trump's national address. Air raid sirens sounded across northern Israel.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Delcy Rodríguez, clearing the way for her visit to Washington
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department removed Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez from its Specially Designated Nationals list, lifting financial sanctions and allowing her to conduct transactions with U.S. entities and travel to American territory.

stories.title: Trump vows to send Iran "back to the Stone Age" as oil surges back above $100
stories.summary: Oil prices surged after U.S. President Donald Trump vowed in a televised address to hit Iran "extremely hard" over the next two to three weeks. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 4.1% to $104.21 per barrel, while Brent gained 5% to $106.42.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war objectives 'nearing completion' in address to nation
stories.summary: The US president's first televised address of the conflict with Iran did little to quell uneasy markets.

stories.title: Explainer-Can Trump pull the US out of NATO?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened on Wednesday to withdraw the United States from NATO, citing European members' refusal to send ships to help unblock the Strait of Hormuz near Iran. However, U.S. law requires an act of Congress or a Senate resolution to formally leave the alliance.

stories.title: Countries should show 'courage' and seize Hormuz Strait, Trump urges
stories.summary: In his national address, President Trump urged countries that receive oil through the Strait of Hormuz to show "courage" and seize the key waterway. He declared Iran "no longer a threat" and said the war is nearly won.

stories.title: In March, nearly thousand individuals attempting to illegally cross Ukraine’s border detained
stories.summary: Ukrainian border guards detained nearly one thousand individuals attempting to illegally cross the country's state border during March.

stories.title: Middle East live: Israeli air defences intercept multiple Iranian missile waves
stories.summary: Israeli air defences intercepted three waves of Iranian missile fire early Thursday, with several people lightly wounded in the Tel Aviv area. The attacks triggered widespread sirens across Israel and raised fears of further escalation in the regional conflict.

stories.title: Malaysia’s Anwar warns against ‘sabotage, hatred’ over fuel prices
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim urged enforcement agencies to act against what the government considers false claims about fuel and electricity prices. The communications regulator identified 96 misleading social media posts, and Anwar called on police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to respond.

stories.title: Trump vows to bring Iran back to 'Stone Ages'
stories.summary: In a televised address, President Trump said the war on Iran has left the country "decimated," claiming Iran's navy, air force, and most of its leadership have been destroyed. He vowed to strike Iran "extremely hard" over the next two to three weeks.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuela’s acting President Rodriguez, who praises Trump
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department lifted sanctions on Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez, removing her from the Specially Designated Nationals list. The move follows the U.S. military's capture of former president Nicolás Maduro and his wife in Caracas on January 3; the pair were taken to New York to face drug charges.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia responds to Zelenskyy’s Easter truce offer with drone attack
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized Russia for responding to his Easter ceasefire proposal with drone attacks, including more than 700 drones targeting western and central Ukraine. Russia dismissed the truce offer as a "PR stunt" on day 1,499 of the war.

stories.title: Indonesia: Strong earthquake strikes Molucca ⁠Sea, killing 1
