stories.summary: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the Molucca Sea in northern Indonesia, killing at least one person. An initial tsunami warning was issued but has since been lifted.

stories.title: Powerful earthquake strikes Molucca ⁠Sea near Indonesia
stories.summary: A major 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the Molucca Sea near eastern Indonesia, prompting a tsunami warning that was subsequently lifted.

stories.title: New Zealand signs defence pact with Cook Islands after quarrel over China deal
stories.summary: New Zealand and the Cook Islands signed a defence and security declaration, resolving a year-long diplomatic dispute that began after the Cook Islands entered strategic agreements with China. Wellington had previously halted millions in aid to its former colony over the Chinese partnership.

stories.title: IEA, IMF and World Bank to coordinate response to Middle East war's impact
stories.summary: The heads of the International Energy Agency, International Monetary Fund, and World Bank announced on April 1 that they would form a coordination group. The group aims to maximize their collective response to the significant economic and energy impacts of the war in the Middle East.

stories.title: UK to host multi-nation meeting on Strait of Hormuz shipping on April 2
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced it would host a multi-nation meeting on April 2 to address shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has virtually closed the vital waterway since U.S.-Israeli strikes triggered a broader Middle East war on February 28.

stories.title: Read the full text of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s letter to the American public
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian published an open letter addressed to the American public, urging them to question the motives behind the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran and highlighting Iran's ancient civilization and history.

stories.title: UAE, Saudi Arabia intercepting attacks
stories.summary: The UAE defense ministry reported its air defenses were intercepting missile and drone attacks from Iran. Saudi Arabia announced it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile headed toward its Eastern Province.

stories.title: Centcom says it struck 12,300 targets in Iran since February
stories.summary: US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced it had struck over 12,300 targets in Iran since the war began in late February. More than 155 Iranian vessels were reported damaged or destroyed.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s next 5 years must take city from alignment to action
stories.summary: Hong Kong is preparing a medium-term development blueprint to align with China's forthcoming 15th five-year plan, which officials have called a "golden strategic period." The effort marks the city's first attempt to synchronize its policy cycle with national planning priorities in advance.

stories.title: Unmanned Systems Battalion commander: Drones eliminate 80% of occupiers
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Battalion commander stated that drones account for 80 percent of cases involving the detection and destruction of Russian forces on the battlefield.

stories.title: Controlled escalation? Trump hails ‘victories’ in Iran but vows more strikes in next few weeks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump declared the U.S.-Israel war on Iran had delivered "decisive, overwhelming victories" but signaled that further strikes could continue over the next two to three weeks. He warned of heavy damage to remaining targets while noting that discussions with Iran were ongoing.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims several attacks on Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it launched missiles targeting Israeli army infrastructure in Kiryat Ata, east of Haifa, and attacked Israeli troops near the settlements of Malkia and Metula in northern Israel. The group also said it struck forces attempting to enter southern Lebanon.

stories.title: A war meant to break Iran could leave Tehran stronger, and Gulf exposed
stories.summary: Analysts warn that if President Trump ends the war with Iran without securing a deal, Tehran could retain a stranglehold over Middle East energy supplies. Gulf Arab oil and gas producers face significant fallout from a conflict they did not initiate or shape.

stories.title: China woman clings to truck to follow husband; man threatens divorce after male doctor examines wife
stories.summary: A woman in Bachu county, Xinjiang, China, was found clinging to the outside of her husband's truck after suspecting him of infidelity. Traffic police stopped the vehicle after spotting her hanging from the trailer without protective equipment. The driver was unaware his wife was attached to the truck.

stories.title: Trump pledges to 'finish the job' in Iran in national address but offers no exit plan
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said in a televised address that U.S. forces would continue striking Iran "very hard" for two to three more weeks, threatening to bring the country "back to the Stone Ages." He argued Washington had accomplished its goals but offered no clear timeline for ending the war.

stories.title: Indonesia earthquake kills 1, triggers tsunami waves
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck Indonesia's Northern Maluku Sea on Thursday, killing one person and damaging buildings. Tsunami waves were reported in five locations, with the highest reaching 0.75 metres in North Minahasa, North Sulawesi. About 50 aftershocks were recorded.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky, NATO’s Rutte hold talks with US negotiators, source says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte held talks with U.S. negotiators. Kyiv reportedly plans to raise the possibility of an Easter ceasefire during the discussions.

stories.title: Intel identifies Russian archaeologists behind illegal excavations in TOT
stories.summary: Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate identified seven individuals involved in illegal archaeological excavations in temporarily occupied territories and documented 20 looted Ukrainian cultural artifacts.

stories.title: NASA Artemis II astronauts blast off to moon, the first crewed lunar mission in decades
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission launched with astronauts aboard, marking the first crewed lunar mission in decades. The crew is set to travel approximately 4,000 miles past the Moon before returning to Earth.

stories.title: Is it time to call an end to Hong Kong’s boar war?
stories.summary: A wild boar roughly 1.2 metres long stormed through Hong Kong's Wu Kai Sha MTR station before rush hour, knocking down an elderly man and injuring three other people. The incident left a trail of blood across the concourse and reignited debate over the city's approach to managing its wild boar population.

stories.title: US Supreme Court justices skeptical of Trump’s order to restrict birthright citizenship
stories.summary: U.S. Supreme Court justices signaled skepticism toward President Donald Trump's executive order to restrict birthright citizenship during oral arguments on Wednesday. Trump attended the hearing in person, marking the first time a sitting president has been present for Supreme Court oral arguments.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump claims goals nearing completion, vows to ‘finish job’
stories.summary: Iran denied seeking a truce and continued counterattacks as US and Israeli air raids caused deaths and damage across the country. Trump claimed US goals were nearing completion and vowed to finish the campaign.

stories.title: Why Japan’s advanced fighter project may get Canadian tailwinds
stories.summary: Canada has signaled its intention to join the Global Combat Air Programme, a multinational sixth-generation fighter jet consortium involving Japan, the United Kingdom, and Italy. Japan aims to replace its ageing F-2 fleet and narrow the gap with China's rapidly modernizing air force.

stories.title: How to take down a US F-35 over Iran? Chinese engineer’s prophetic tutorial goes viral
stories.summary: A detailed tutorial on countering the U.S. F-35 fighter jet appeared on Chinese social media and went viral, subtitled in Persian by the account "Laohu Talks World." The video reflects a trend of technically skilled Chinese civilians volunteering expertise online to help Iran counter U.S. military operations.

stories.title: Trump says Iran president requests ceasfire, Tehran says 'false'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had requested a ceasefire, but Tehran denied the assertion, calling it false. Pezeshkian had earlier stated Iran possessed the necessary will for a ceasefire only if guarantees against renewed hostilities were provided.

stories.title: Death of Rohingya refugee left in parking lot by US border agents ruled a homicide
stories.summary: Authorities ruled the death of Nurul Amin Shah, a 56-year-old visually impaired Rohingya refugee, a homicide after U.S. Border Patrol agents left him in a Tim Hortons parking lot in Buffalo, New York, on a cold winter night. Shah died on February 24, five days after being dropped off without notification to his family or attorney.

stories.title: Magnitude 7.4 quake hits off Indonesia’s Ternate, tsunami warning lifted
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck approximately 120 kilometers from Ternate in Indonesia's North Maluku province. A tsunami warning was issued but later lifted.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis threaten potential closure of key Red Sea strait if Gulf states join war
stories.summary: A senior Houthi official in Yemen threatened to close the Bab el-Mandeb strait in the Red Sea if Gulf states join the war against Iran and Lebanon. The warning came as Iranian-aligned proxy groups continued attacks in the region.

stories.title: Christians in Lebanon's south fear expanding war will reach their towns
stories.summary: Thousands of Christians in towns along Lebanon's southern border report feeling trapped and fearful after a nearby Israeli military advance prompted Lebanese troops to withdraw from the area.

stories.title: Bilawal calls on Fazl at his residence, two leaders discuss political matters
stories.summary: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari met JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman at his Islamabad residence on Wednesday to discuss political matters, including elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. Senior leaders from both parties were present.

stories.title: Ecuador says homicides fell 28% in March amid localized curfew
stories.summary: Ecuador's government reported that intentional homicides fell 28% nationwide in March 2025, attributing the decline to military operations conducted during a two-week nightly curfew imposed in four provinces.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Beirut kills senior Hezbollah commander
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the Jnah neighborhood of Beirut on April 1, 2026, killed a senior Hezbollah commander. Several large explosions were heard across the city, and smoke was seen rising from the residential and commercial area.

stories.title: Bahrain's Strait of Hormuz resolution runs into fresh obstacles at UN
stories.summary: Bahrain's draft UN resolution on the Strait of Hormuz, which initially invoked Chapter VII of the UN Charter authorizing measures including sanctions and military force, has encountered new obstacles at the Security Council.

stories.title: Kharkiv hit by another enemy attack, casualties reported after apartment building strike
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the Shevchenkivskyi district of Kharkiv, striking an apartment building and injuring two people.

stories.title: Russia warns citizens not to travel to states that have extradition treaties with US
stories.summary: Russia's government warned its citizens on April 1 not to travel to countries that have extradition treaties with the United States. No specific reason for the advisory was detailed in the announcement.

stories.title: Fuel prices surge in Somalia and Tanzania amid supply disruption
stories.summary: Somalia and Tanzania reported sharp fuel price increases linked to regional tensions disrupting global supply routes. In Somalia, fuel prices surged 150 percent, from $0.70 to $1.75 per liter, while Tanzania's energy ministry announced a 33 percent rise.

stories.title: US Vice-President Vance spoke to intermediaries about Iran conflict as recently as March 31, source says
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance spoke with intermediaries about the Iran conflict as recently as March 31. A source indicated that Vance privately signaled President Trump's openness to a ceasefire.

stories.title: Switzerland says cancelling US Patriot missile system order an option
stories.summary: The Swiss government said it will continue withholding payments to the United States for a Patriot missile system order until Washington provides binding delivery dates, adding that cancelling the purchase remains an option.

stories.title: First troops from UN-backed Gang Suppression Force arrive in Haiti
stories.summary: The first troops from a UN-backed Gang Suppression Force arrived in Haiti with an initial 12-month mandate to combat widespread gang violence ahead of the country's planned elections.

stories.title: As American bombs fall on Iran, South American countries brace for impact
stories.summary: South American countries are bracing for the economic and geopolitical fallout of U.S. bombing operations in Iran. The situation is compounded by the unresolved kidnapping of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro amid what has been termed Trump's war on narco-terrorism.

stories.title: West Bank Palestinians protest, go on strike against new death penalty law
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank went on strike and protested against a new Palestinian Authority law mandating the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of deadly acts of terrorism. Shops closed and universities shut down across the territory.

stories.title: PMF says strike on Tal Afar brigade killed commander, wounded four
stories.summary: Iraq's Iran-aligned Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) said a US-Israeli air strike hit one of its units in Tal Afar, northern Iraq, killing a commando battalion commander and one soldier and wounding four. Similar strikes have reportedly targeted PMF positions in Nineveh province.

stories.title: Fire at critical infrastructure facility in Bukovyna extinguished after Russian attack
stories.summary: Rescuers from Ukraine's State Emergency Service extinguished a 100-square-meter fire at a critical infrastructure facility in the Chernivtsi region of Bukovyna, caused by a Russian attack.

stories.title: Fire at critical infrastructure facility in Bukovyna extinguished after Russian attack
stories.summary: Rescuers in Ukraine's Chernivtsi region extinguished a 100-square-meter fire at a critical infrastructure facility caused by a Russian attack in the Bukovyna area.

stories.title: Trump says Iran has asked for a ceasefire, US wants to see Hormuz open first
stories.summary: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran had asked the United States for a ceasefire. He said Washington would consider the request only after the Strait of Hormuz was reopened.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan officials hold meeting in China’s Urumqi under trilateral mechanism
stories.summary: Officials from Pakistan, Afghanistan, and China met in the Chinese city of Urumqi under their trilateral diplomatic mechanism. The meeting was the first significant contact between Pakistan and Afghanistan since Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan on February 26. A Pakistani official said no major outcomes were expected.

stories.title: How Algeria Is Navigating the War in Iran
stories.summary: Algeria is navigating the ongoing war in Iran while maintaining its historically close ties with Tehran. Analysts suggest Algiers may benefit from the conflict's impact on regional dynamics and energy markets.

stories.title: France court blocks extradition of ex-Tunisian president’s daughter
stories.summary: A French court blocked the extradition of the daughter of a former Tunisian president. Her lawyer argued that returning her to Tunisia would be tantamount to a death sentence.

stories.title: Beirut strike killed top Hezbollah commander, group says
stories.summary: Hezbollah confirmed that a strike on Beirut killed Haj Youssef Ismail Hashem, whom Israel identified as the commander of Hezbollah's southern front.

stories.title: Russia’s 2026 goals are slipping away as Ukraine fights back
stories.summary: With nine months remaining in 2026, Russia's military objectives in eastern and southern Ukraine are reportedly slipping behind schedule as Ukrainian forces continue to resist Kremlin advances.

stories.title: Could NATO be collateral damage from Trump’s Iran war?
stories.summary: Analysts are questioning whether NATO could become collateral damage from President Trump's war in Iran, the latest in a series of existential crises facing the 77-year-old alliance since Trump returned to power.

stories.title: US assures UN of support but stresses reform needed to 'exceed' potential
stories.summary: The Trump administration's UN reform envoy affirmed continued U.S. support for the United Nations but emphasized that reforms are needed for the organization to reach its full potential. The envoy specifically said peacekeeping missions must be scaled back.

stories.title: Once again, Trump declines to describe desired end-state to his Iran war
stories.summary: In a primetime address, President Trump spoke about the conflict with Iran but did not outline specific military objectives or articulate what concessions or outcomes the United States is seeking from Tehran. The speech left the desired end-state of the U.S. campaign against Iran undefined.

stories.title: US embarks on world’s first crewed moon mission in decades amid race with China
stories.summary: Four astronauts launched from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, on NASA's Artemis II mission, the first crewed lunar voyage in decades. The crew includes three American astronauts and one Canadian astronaut aboard the Space Launch System rocket and Orion capsule.

stories.title: Iraq begins oil exports via Syria amid disruptions
stories.summary: Iraq's oil ministry announced it has begun exporting crude oil via tankers through Syria to support the national economy. Officials said they are coordinating with the Syrian government to ensure safe passage, with plans to gradually increase shipment volumes.

stories.title: Watch: Trump says Iranian leader has ‘asked for ceasefire’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that Iran's new leader had requested a ceasefire. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson denied the claim, calling Trump's statement false and baseless.

stories.title: War Diary Day 33: Trump keeps everyone guessing ahead of address to nation
stories.summary: On the 33rd day of the U.S.-Israel war against Iran, attention focused on an upcoming address by President Trump, which analysts viewed as potentially pivotal for the conflict's trajectory. Developments on the ground pointed toward possible escalation over control of critical maritime routes rather than de-escalation.

stories.title: A Lego on the seder plate: Temple Israel calls for new ritual object after attack
stories.summary: Temple Israel in the United States called on congregants to add a Lego block to their Passover Seder plates as a new ritual object. The gesture was introduced in response to a recent attack on the community.

stories.title: Iran’s president urges Americans to reject ‘propaganda’ on Iran, calls US Israel's proxy
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian urged Americans to reject what he called propaganda, describing the United States as acting as Israel's proxy. He stated that Iran has never initiated a war in modern history and questioned whether the conflict serves American interests.

stories.title: In Senate panel meeting, banks and telcos trade blame for overcharging for messaging services
stories.summary: In Islamabad, telecom companies and banks traded blame before a Pakistani Senate Standing Committee on Finance over an estimated 26 billion rupees in extra charges to bank customers for messaging services. Committee chair Senator Saleem Mandviwalla directed both sides and the State Bank of Pakistan to provide transaction records.

stories.title: France tells US NATO serves Euro-Atlantic security, not Hormuz offensive missions
stories.summary: France responded to President Trump's threats to leave NATO by stating the alliance was designed to ensure Euro-Atlantic security, not to conduct offensive operations in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: DNA links serial killer Ted Bundy to unsolved murder of teen girl
stories.summary: Utah officials announced they had closed a five-decade-old case after DNA evidence provided definitive proof that serial killer Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Laura Ann Aime. Aime disappeared on October 31, 1974, after leaving a party, and her body was found on Thanksgiving Day that year.

stories.title: Enemy drone strikes residential building in Chuhuiv, causing fire
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential building in Chuhuiv, Ukraine, causing a fire that spread across two floors of the structure.

stories.title: Trump declares US ‘nearing completion’ of ‘core strategic objectives’ in the Iran war
stories.summary: In a national address, President Trump said US forces are "nearing completion" of core strategic objectives in Iran and will strike "extremely hard" over the next two to three weeks. Separately, an Iranian ballistic missile attack wounded four people, including two babies, in Bnei Brak, Israel.

stories.title: Iraqi group says it carried out 41 attacks on US bases
stories.summary: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed it carried out 41 operations targeting U.S. military bases in Iraq and across the region. The group said it used dozens of drones in the attacks, announcing the operations via Telegram.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s Tretyakov Gallery to transfer 2 medieval icons to Orthodox Church
stories.summary: Russia's Tretyakov Gallery is set to transfer the Vladimir and Donskaya icons of the Mother of God to the Russian Orthodox Church, according to a report by the Russian business daily Kommersant citing a source close to the gallery.

stories.title: US removes sanctions on Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez
stories.summary: The United States removed sanctions on Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez. The move follows Washington's growing influence over the Venezuelan government after the abduction of former President Nicolás Maduro.

stories.title: Iranian leader says Israel will fight 'to last US tax dollar' as US weighs invasion
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian wrote a letter to the American public stating that Israel will fight using U.S. resources. The letter was released as the Trump administration was expected to make an announcement regarding the war on Iran, with strikes continuing in Tehran.

stories.title: Trump to deliver 'important update' on Iran war in televised speech
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump planned to deliver a prime-time televised address on Wednesday providing an update on the Iran war. The speech was expected to reiterate his timeline for rolling back U.S. military operations in the region.

stories.title: In historic first, Trump attends Supreme Court arguments on limiting birthright citizenship
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump made a historic visit to the Supreme Court to attend oral arguments on his executive order limiting birthright citizenship, signed on his first day back in office. Trump sat in the public seating section before departing while the challengers' attorney was presenting.

stories.title: Suspect in foiled Paris bank attack hit with ‘terrorist criminal conspiracy’ charges
stories.summary: A man in his early twenties was charged with "terrorist criminal conspiracy" in connection with a foiled attack on a Bank of America branch in Paris. French prosecutors indicated possible links to an Islamist group with ties to Iran.

stories.title: Zelensky: Turkey shows interest in Ukraine’s defense expertise
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky said Turkey has shown interest in Ukraine's defense expertise. National Security and Defense Council head Rustem Umerov is continuing discussions with interested countries on defense cooperation.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims rocket and drone attacks on Israeli positions
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched rocket barrages targeting the Nahariyya settlement in northern Israel and fired artillery at Israeli soldiers and vehicles near Shomera. The group also said it struck Israeli troops in al-Bayyadah in southern Lebanon using rockets and a drone.

stories.title: Russia pulls 30% of library books in Ural city over Soros Foundation funding
stories.summary: Approximately 30 percent of books in Yekaterinburg's public libraries will be removed from circulation because they were purchased with funding from George Soros's foundation, according to the director of the city's municipal library network.

stories.title: Australia news live: Angus Taylor urges clarity on fuel crisis and says PM’s national address ‘could have been a social media post’
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor criticized Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's national address on the fuel crisis, calling for more specific details and commitments. Shadow energy minister Dan Tehan also dismissed the address as lacking substance.

stories.title: Trump threatened to halt Ukraine aid unless Europe joined Hormuz coalition - report
stories.summary: President Trump reportedly threatened to halt military equipment supplies to NATO's Ukraine procurement initiative unless European allies joined a coalition to address the Strait of Hormuz situation. The threat targeted the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List, which is funded by European nations.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi: Defense forces repel Russian offensive on multiple settlements in Pokrovsk direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi reported that defense forces repelled a Russian offensive targeting multiple settlements in the Pokrovsk-Myrnohrad urban area along the Pokrovsk direction.

stories.title: Top Senate Democrat says ‘House Republicans caved’ as deal to fund DHS moves forward – live
stories.summary: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer declared that House Republicans had capitulated as a bipartisan deal to fund the Department of Homeland Security moved forward on Wednesday. Separately, President Trump made a historic visit to the Supreme Court for oral arguments on birthright citizenship.

stories.title: Reinflate the property sector? No, China wants an ambitious redesign
stories.summary: China's government is deliberately choosing not to bail out its embattled real estate sector, instead pursuing a systemic redesign of the property industry's role in the broader macroeconomy rather than short-term market stabilization.

stories.title: Israel says over 400 strikes carried out in Tehran in two days
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it conducted over 400 air strikes on Tehran over two days, using approximately 650 munitions. Targets included government-linked infrastructure, about 15 weapons production facilities, and a complex affiliated with Iran's defense ministry.

stories.title: West Bank on strike against Israeli death penalty law
stories.summary: Residents across the West Bank went on strike to protest an Israeli law authorizing the death penalty. Approximately 150 people gathered to march against the legislation.

stories.title: China targeted in US birthright citizenship debate, but Supreme Court justices sceptical
stories.summary: China emerged as a focal point during U.S. Supreme Court oral arguments on birthright citizenship on Wednesday, with Solicitor General D. John Sauer citing birth tourism concerns. Justices appeared skeptical of the Trump administration's arguments to restrict the constitutional provision.

stories.title: NASA moon mission a ‘contrast’ to US war on Iran, says US senator
stories.summary: NASA astronauts have boarded the Orion capsule ahead of the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years. A U.S. senator described the mission as a contrast to the ongoing U.S. military engagement with Iran.

stories.title: US to leave Iran ‘pretty quickly’ and return if needed, says Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said US forces would leave Iran "pretty quickly" and could return if needed. He claimed American military action had ensured Iran would not acquire a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: UN warns of rights clampdown in Iran, across Mid-East amid war
stories.summary: The United Nations warned of a human rights clampdown in Iran and across the Middle East amid the ongoing war. The UN also denounced attempts to restrict press freedom in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Swiss government eyes dropping purchase of US Patriot air defence system
stories.summary: Swiss Defence Minister Martin Pfister said Switzerland is considering cancelling its agreed purchase of U.S. Patriot air-defence systems due to severe delivery delays. The defence ministry announced it would continue suspending payments until the United States provides firm new delivery dates. Switzerland ordered five Patriot systems in 2022.

stories.title: 'There's a certain romanticism to sending humans into space'
stories.summary: Dr. David Brown of Warwick University expressed enthusiasm about the Artemis II mission, calling it potentially the start of a new era of human spaceflight and noting the enduring public inspiration of crewed space exploration.

stories.title: Trump says US may exit Iran war soon and threatens to quit NATO as oil crisis escalates
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran had requested a ceasefire but that Washington would not consider it until Tehran stopped blocking the Strait of Hormuz. He also threatened to withdraw the US from NATO as the global oil crisis escalated.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia rerouted nearly 1 million barrels a day of crude away from Hormuz strait
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia rerouted nearly one million barrels per day of crude oil away from the disrupted Strait of Hormuz, using its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Flows through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait rose to nearly four million barrels per day in March, the highest since October 2023, according to Kpler.

stories.title: “トランプ大統領 NATO離脱を真剣に検討” 英テレグラフ報道
stories.summary: British newspaper The Telegraph reported that US President Donald Trump is seriously considering withdrawing the United States from NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

stories.title: Smoke and embers seen over Iran’s Isfahan after strike
stories.summary: Video footage showed a large column of smoke and burning embers rising over Isfahan, Iran, following a joint U.S.-Israeli military strike on the city.

stories.title: Special Operations Center 'Alpha' preemptively eliminate Russian drone operators
stories.summary: Fighters from Ukraine's Special Operations Center "Alpha" carried out a preemptive operation to eliminate Russian drone operators. The unit described the mission as a unique tactical strike.

stories.title: Celebrations erupt as DR Congo ends over 50-year World Cup wait
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo defeated Jamaica in extra time to qualify for the FIFA World Cup, ending a drought of more than 50 years. Fans celebrated in heavy rain after the victory.

stories.title: Russia launches rare daytime drone attack on Ukraine, killing four, Ukrainian officials say
stories.summary: Russia launched a rare daytime drone attack on Ukraine on Wednesday, killing four people in the central Cherkasy region. The strikes also damaged energy infrastructure and industrial facilities in western Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump Mulls Pulling U.S. Out of NATO
stories.summary: President Trump is considering withdrawing the United States from NATO, but U.S. law requires an act of Congress or a Senate resolution to formally exit the alliance.

stories.title: ‘Devoid of facts’: Info ministry rubbishes claims of barbed wire being removed along Pak-Afghan border
stories.summary: Pakistan's information ministry dismissed claims that barbed wire was being removed along the 2,640-kilometre Pak-Afghan border as fabricated. The ministry attributed the claims to the Afghan Taliban regime and Indian intelligence-linked outlets.

stories.title: Trump administration lifts sanctions on Venezuela’s interim leader
stories.summary: The U.S. lifted sanctions on Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez following the ouster of Nicolas Maduro. Rodriguez has begun opening Venezuela's energy sector to American companies as relations between Washington and Caracas improve.

stories.title: The Seder’s message: Why we diminish our joy for others’ pain on Passover
stories.summary: The Passover Seder tradition of spilling drops of wine serves as a reminder that liberation came at the cost of others' suffering. The ritual calls on participants to temper their joy with empathy for all who have experienced pain.

stories.title: What are the consequences of Israel’s death penalty law for Palestinians?
stories.summary: Israel's parliament voted to approve capital punishment for certain offenses, becoming the first country to enact such legislation in the 21st century. The law applies to Palestinians and has drawn significant attention regarding its legal and humanitarian consequences.

stories.title: ‘Which interests being served by war?’ Iran’s Pezeshkian asks US public
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian published an open letter addressed to the American public, questioning whose interests are served by the ongoing war and urging Americans to look past what he called distorted narratives.

stories.title: Iranian president says it does not view American people as enemies
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in a letter that Iran does not consider ordinary Americans to be enemies. He stated that Iran distinguishes between foreign governments and their people, describing this as a deeply rooted principle rather than a temporary political stance.

stories.title: Nepal’s New Leaders Go on the Offensive
stories.summary: Nepal's new leadership arrested former officials over the weekend in connection with a crackdown on protesters that took place the previous year, signaling an aggressive stance against the prior administration.

stories.title: Iran’s president sends message to Americans in unusual open letter
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed an open letter to the American people criticizing the U.S. war against Iran, calling the path of confrontation costly and futile. He urged dialogue, noting that historical aggressors against Iran are remembered only by their tarnished legacies.

stories.title: Russian drones attack civilian vehicles in Kherson, leaving one dead, five injured
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped explosives from a drone onto a civilian vehicle in Kherson, killing one person and injuring five others, including the driver and passengers. The attack targeted civilian cars in the city.

stories.title: Afghans Fear for Safety as War Returns
stories.summary: Afghans express growing fears for their safety as military conflict involving Iran, Pakistan, and Afghanistan intensifies, drawing less international attention amid the broader focus on the Iran war.

stories.title: 4 cops among 9 injured in IED blast in KP’s Lakki Marwat
stories.summary: An improvised explosive device exploded on Bannu-DI Khan Road in Serai Naurang, Lakki Marwat district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, injuring nine people including four police officers. Police said the attackers targeted a patrol party from the Shaheed Asmatullah Khan Khattak police station.

stories.title: 19 migrants found dead by Italian coastguard
stories.summary: The Italian coastguard recovered the bodies of 19 migrants from an inflatable boat south of the island of Lampedusa on Wednesday.

stories.title: Jewish former NBA star Amar’e Stoudemire reportedly heading to Hall of Fame
stories.summary: Former NBA All-Star Amar'e Stoudemire, a six-time All-Star who became an Israeli citizen and converted to Judaism, is reportedly set to be inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame. Stoudemire also played in the Israeli basketball league after his NBA career.

stories.title: South Africa deploys military to Cape Town townships hit by crime
stories.summary: South Africa deployed soldiers to crime-affected townships in Cape Town as part of a government crackdown on gang violence. Separately, DR Congo qualified for a World Cup opportunity for the first time in over 50 years.

stories.title: Ecuador claims 28% drop in homicides amid concerns over anti-crime campaign
stories.summary: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa has overseen a hardline anti-crime campaign, including joint military operations with the United States targeting local criminal networks. The government claims homicides have dropped by 28 percent, though the approach has raised concerns.

stories.title: ‘I always knew they were a paper tiger’: Could war on Iran create unbridgeable rift between US and Nato?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has intensified criticism of NATO allies, calling the alliance a "paper tiger" after European partners, including the U.K., France, and Spain, refused to support the U.S. war on Iran. Trump told The Telegraph he is strongly considering pulling the U.S. out of NATO.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1498: Ukraine crushes Russia’s biggest assault on Sloviansk front of 2026
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces repelled what is described as Russia's largest assault on the Sloviansk front in 2026, on day 1,498 of the war. Separately, leaked transcripts revealed Hungary's foreign minister removed 72 Russian entities from EU sanctions and asked Moscow to draft arguments for further delistings.

stories.title: IEA, IMF and World Bank form group to address war’s economic impact
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency, International Monetary Fund, and World Bank announced the formation of a coordination group to address the economic and energy fallout from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The group will assess impacts across countries and mobilize support for those most affected.

stories.title: Trump mulls Nato withdrawal, stopping weapons to Ukraine over Europe's response to Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump is reportedly considering withdrawing the United States from NATO and halting weapons supplies to Ukraine over European allies' response to the Iran conflict. The threat came as the administration has failed to address Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Coordination with partners to end war: Zelensky holds conversation with UK Prime Minister Starmer
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer about coordinating efforts with international partners, including the United States, to bring the war to an end.

stories.title: Republican leaders agree to advance funding deal to end DHS shutdown
stories.summary: Congressional Republican leaders agreed on Wednesday to advance legislation funding most Department of Homeland Security operations while excluding money for ICE immigration enforcement. The deal could end the longest partial government shutdown in U.S. history, which had caused extended security lines at airports.

stories.title: Burundi says at least 13 killed, dozens injured in military base blast
stories.summary: An explosion at an ammunition depot on a military base in Burundi killed at least 13 people and injured dozens more. The blast destroyed nearby houses, buildings, vehicles, and military equipment, according to an army spokesperson.

stories.title: Iranian authorities warned Bulgaria not to let US use airports
stories.summary: Iran warned NATO member Bulgaria last month not to allow the United States to use Bulgarian airports for aircraft involved in military operations against Iran, according to Bulgaria's foreign ministry.

stories.title: Russia says it will expel Dutch journalist in tit-for-tat move
stories.summary: Russia announced it would expel a Dutch journalist in retaliation for what it described as the expulsion of a correspondent from Russian state news agency RIA from the Netherlands.

stories.title: India begins counting its population in historic census
stories.summary: India has launched its first national census since 2011, undertaking the task of counting approximately 1.4 billion people. It is the largest census exercise in the world.

stories.title: US is tripling Patriot heads production under Boeing deal. Ukraine needs missiles to stop Russian ballistics
stories.summary: The United States is tripling production of Patriot missile interceptor heads under a deal with Boeing. Reports indicate Washington told allies that PAC-3 missiles may be diverted from Ukraine to support operations against Iran.

stories.title: IDF chief warns of manpower crisis in pre-Passover letter to lawmakers
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir sent a letter to Israeli lawmakers ahead of Passover warning of a looming manpower crisis. He cautioned that shortening mandatory military service to 30 months would cause serious harm to the IDF's operational readiness.

stories.title: Fourth soldier killed in southern Lebanon clash on Monday laid to rest in Modiin
stories.summary: Staff Sgt. Gilad Harel, the fourth Israeli soldier killed in a clash in southern Lebanon on Monday, was laid to rest in Modiin. His family described him as a driven and sensitive young man.

stories.title: Syrskyi discusses frontline situation, air defense needs with Inspector General of Bundeswehr Breuer
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi met with Inspector General of the German Bundeswehr Carsten Breuer. They discussed the current frontline situation and Ukraine's air defense requirements.

stories.title: Trump attends birthright citizenship hearing at Supreme Court in historic first
stories.summary: President Donald Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend oral arguments at the Supreme Court on Wednesday, observing the case challenging his executive order to restrict birthright citizenship. Justices across the ideological spectrum appeared skeptical of the policy's legality.

stories.title: Russia says it has taken full control of Ukraine’s Luhansk region
stories.summary: Russia's defense ministry claimed on Wednesday that its forces had taken full control of Ukraine's Luhansk region in the east. A Ukrainian military spokesman disputed the claim, saying there had been no battlefield changes in the area over the past six months.

stories.title: Debunking claims Israeli Jews are 'stealing land' in Morocco
stories.summary: FRANCE 24's fact-checking unit investigated viral claims that Israeli Jews were stealing land in Morocco, finding that the video being shared online was taken out of context and did not support the allegations being made.

stories.title: Drone crash in Poltava region: Injury toll rises to six, including three children
stories.summary: A drone attack in Ukraine's Poltava region injured six people, including three children. The casualty toll from the strike on the Poltava community rose as more victims were identified.

stories.title: This is Moscow’s parallel war: Russian intelligence orders spying on German drone supplier for Ukraine — Spiegel
stories.summary: German outlet Spiegel reported that Russia's GRU military intelligence recruited a Ukrainian refugee in Germany via Telegram to spy on a Bavarian businessman who supplies drones to Ukraine.

stories.title: Is the US running out of Tomahawk missiles? Here’s what the experts say
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly fired at least 850 Tomahawk cruise missiles within roughly one month of Operation Epic Fury, prompting expert debate over whether U.S. stockpiles of the long-range weapon could face depletion.

stories.title: Artemis II ready for launch as NASA set to make 1st trip around moon in over 50 years
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission is prepared for launch, aiming to send three American astronauts and one Canadian astronaut on a trip around the Moon. It will mark the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years and take the crew farther from Earth than any humans before.

stories.title: South Africa deploys 2,200 soldiers as gang violence plagues Cape flats
stories.summary: South Africa deployed 2,200 soldiers into gang-affected townships on the Cape Flats in Cape Town on Wednesday, nearly 50 days after the president ordered the deployment. Two people were killed in fresh violence on the same day.

stories.title: 'It's a nightmare for Keir Starmer' as UK PM sees 'special relationship' with US unravel
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the global instability from the Iran war requires Britain to strengthen economic and defense ties with Europe. Analysts note the conflict is damaging the UK economy and weakening Starmer's political position amid repeated criticism from President Trump.

stories.title: Ukraine's EU accession: Zelensky discusses unblocking negotiation process with Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee
stories.summary: President Zelensky met with Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee to discuss unblocking Ukraine's EU accession negotiations. The talks focused on Ireland's priorities during its presidency of the European Union in the second half of 2026.

stories.title: Trump is at a strategic dead end on Iran; the war will reshape Gulf’s security architecture: Vali Nasr
stories.summary: In an interview with The Hindu, analyst Vali Nasr said the U.S. has reached a strategic dead end on Iran, arguing the war will reshape the Gulf's security architecture. He suggested Iran might accept a deal on its nuclear program but not on its missiles or control of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: British police arrest three more men over arson attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: British police arrested three more men in connection with an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances that were set on fire on March 23 in north London.

stories.title: SpaceX files for IPO, offering investors stake in Musk’s moon, Mars ambitions
stories.summary: SpaceX has filed for an initial public offering that could value the company above $1.7 trillion. The filing follows SpaceX's merger with Elon Musk's xAI and could reinvigorate the sluggish IPO market.

stories.title: Central Israel hit by one of Iran’s largest missile barrages in weeks
stories.summary: One of Iran's largest missile barrages in weeks struck central Israel, injuring at least 14 people and causing damage across multiple areas.

stories.title: Israel's perpetual war with Iran may be hard to win with military might alone
stories.summary: The war with Iran has not yet resolved any of Israel's regional conflicts in the way its prime minister suggested it would.

stories.title: Knesset goes on recess after approving key war laws, death penalty
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset approved several key wartime laws, including a death penalty measure, before going on recess. The summer session beginning May 10 will be the government's last opportunity to pass legislation before elections scheduled no later than October.

stories.title: How China’s state insurer is turning Brazil’s credit crisis into an export advantage
stories.summary: China's state-owned credit insurer, Sinosure, is helping Brazilian importers manage high borrowing costs by backing deferred payment terms from Chinese suppliers. The arrangement sustains bilateral trade flows that reached $158 billion in 2024 amid Brazil's elevated interest rates.

stories.title: Air Force neutralizes 345 out of more than 360 Russian drones since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 345 out of more than 360 Russian drones launched starting from the morning of April 1. Fourteen drone strikes were recorded hitting their targets.

stories.title: Resident doctors accuse Keir Starmer of sabotaging talks to end pay and jobs dispute
stories.summary: British resident doctors accused Prime Minister Keir Starmer of undermining negotiations to resolve their pay and jobs dispute by threatening to cut 1,000 new NHS medical positions. The British Medical Association said the move made upcoming strike action more likely ahead of a Thursday deadline.

stories.title: Israel bombardment pushes Syrians from Lebanon to ruined Syria
stories.summary: As Israeli strikes on Lebanon intensify, thousands of Syrian refugees are fleeing Lebanon and returning to Syria. They face ruined homes and severe humanitarian conditions after years of displacement.

stories.title: Sirens during Seder?: Rabbis advise on how to observe Passover under fire
stories.summary: Israeli rabbis issued guidance on observing Passover amid ongoing missile threats, addressing the possibility of sirens sounding during the Seder. Rabbi Yitzhak Yaakov Fuchs emphasized that safety precautions must be taken despite the holiday's traditional association with divine protection.

stories.title: KamAZ may cut its workweek to 4 days again as Russian truck sales fall and Chinese surplus weighs on market
stories.summary: Russian truck manufacturer KamAZ is considering reducing its workweek to four days starting June 1 due to declining heavy truck sales in Russia. The company's press service confirmed the plan to the outlet RBC, citing market pressures including a surplus of Chinese trucks.

stories.title: NY suspect indicted for ‘brutally assaulting’ Jewish man on subway
stories.summary: A New York grand jury indicted Neil Hurlock for allegedly assaulting a Jewish man on a Brooklyn subway train. Hurlock reportedly shouted an antisemitic slur while punching and manhandling the victim.

stories.title: NATO 'doesn't really exist anymore other than on paper', experts say
stories.summary: Experts say NATO has been effectively hollowed out, with President Trump calling the alliance a "paper tiger" and stating he has moved "beyond reconsideration" of U.S. membership. Analysts note Trump has no intention of defending Europe against a potential Russian invasion.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran wants truce, but set to say war will last 2-3 more weeks
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran wants a truce but said he expects the war to last two to three more weeks, stating he would consider a ceasefire when the Strait of Hormuz is reopened. Iran denied the truce claim as baseless, and aides said Trump was improvising.

stories.title: Palestinians in West Bank protest, strike against Israeli death penalty law
stories.summary: Palestinians across the West Bank held protests and a general strike against Israel's newly passed death penalty law. The strike was called by Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah party.

stories.title: Israel strikes force Syrians to flee Lebanon for shattered Syria
stories.summary: Thousands of Syrian refugees in Lebanon are fleeing back to Syria as Israeli strikes on Lebanon intensify. Many are returning to destroyed homes and facing severe humanitarian conditions after years of displacement.

stories.title: French peacekeeping troops in Lebanon subject to 'unacceptable intimidation' -junior minister
stories.summary: France's junior army minister said French peacekeeping troops serving in Lebanon had been subjected to "absolutely unacceptable intimidation," without specifying the source.

stories.title: From plastic jars to transport, Iran war drives up beauty industry costs
stories.summary: The war in Iran is driving up costs across the global beauty industry, from plastic jar materials to transportation logistics. One industry group estimates additional logistics costs of approximately €1.5 million in 2026.

stories.title: Israel hits Iran with waves of attacks and says it killed top Hezbollah commander
stories.summary: Israel launched two waves of attacks on Tehran on Wednesday and said it killed a senior Hezbollah commander. The strikes continued despite President Trump's claim that Iran's leadership had requested a ceasefire, which Tehran denied.

stories.title: US offers $3m reward for information on Iraq attacks
stories.summary: The US State Department's Rewards for Justice programme is offering $3 million for information on recent attacks on US diplomatic sites in Iraq. The targeted sites include the US Embassy in Baghdad, the Baghdad Diplomatic Support Center, and the US Consulate General in Erbil. Iran-aligned armed groups are suspected.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike missile components facility in Bryansk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a facility in Russia's Bryansk region that manufactured components for Strela cruise missiles. Additional strikes targeted enemy positions in territories temporarily occupied by Russian forces.

stories.title: SBP says teenagers can now independently own, operate bank accounts
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan launched a new framework allowing teenagers to independently own and operate bank accounts and digital wallets. The initiative aims to foster early financial inclusion and participation of young people in the formal economy.

stories.title: U.K. can lead Strait’s opening, Starmer says, as transatlantic ties fray
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Britain could lead efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz but reiterated the U.K. would not be drawn into the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. He stated the conflict was not in Britain's national interest, as transatlantic tensions continued to grow.

stories.title: France suspects pro-Iran group was behind foiled attack on bank
stories.summary: French authorities are investigating a foiled attack on a Bank of America branch in Paris. Investigators suspect the pro-Iran group HAYI was behind the plot, in which teenagers were allegedly paid to plant an explosive device.

stories.title: Iranian strikes target the infrastructure behind US airpower
stories.summary: Iran conducted strikes against U.S. military infrastructure, hitting radar systems, satellite communications, and mission-critical aircraft at bases in Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran wants a ceasefire, Iran says remarks are ‘false and baseless’
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran asked the U.S. for a ceasefire, conditioned on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran's Foreign Ministry called the remarks "false and baseless." The exchange came hours before Trump's scheduled primetime address to the nation.

stories.title: Memorial honours Indonesian UN peacekeeper killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: A memorial was held in Indonesia for UN peacekeeper Farizal Rhomadhon, who was killed while serving in Lebanon. Families and colleagues attended the ceremony to honor his service.

stories.title: Israeli military says 10 soldiers killed, over 300 wounded in war
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that 10 soldiers have been killed and 309 wounded since fighting began with Lebanon and Iran. In the past 24 hours alone, 48 Israeli officers and soldiers were injured in combat in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: ‘Historic milestone’: Pakistan, Norway sign carbon market deal under Paris Agreement
stories.summary: Pakistan and Norway signed the first bilateral carbon market agreement under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. The deal opens the door to international carbon trading, climate finance, and investment in clean energy and climate-smart agriculture.

stories.title: Estonia says stray Ukrainian drones targeting Russia entered its territory this week
stories.summary: Estonia's armed forces said drones detected entering Estonian territory this week appeared to have originated from Ukraine and were likely intended to strike targets in Russia.

stories.title: US believes in possibility of negotiations between Ukraine and Russia despite war in Iran — Bloomberg
stories.summary: Despite the ongoing escalation involving Iran, the United States remains optimistic about the prospects for negotiations between Ukraine and Russia, according to Bloomberg. Washington believes meaningful talks are still possible.

stories.title: Why Iran says its universities are being targeted
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly carried out retaliatory actions against American universities, following attacks that struck two Iranian research universities. Iranian officials say their academic institutions have been deliberately targeted.

stories.title: Kremlin, asked about its Donbas demands, says Ukraine should have pulled out 'yesterday'
stories.summary: The Kremlin stated on Wednesday that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy should have withdrawn forces from the Donbas region "yesterday" to end what Moscow called the "hot phase" of the war. The remarks came in response to questions about Russia's demands regarding the disputed eastern Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Russia says its troops have taken full control of Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed its forces had taken full control of the Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine, capturing a small remaining sliver of territory that had eluded them since 2022.

stories.title: Burundi ammunition store blasts kill four, residents say
stories.summary: Explosions at a military ammunition store in Bujumbura, Burundi's commercial capital, killed four people on Tuesday night. Residents reported the blasts lasted several hours before subsiding.

stories.title: When the oil runs dry: What next for globalization as Asia bears brunt of Iran war?
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the U.S.-led war against Iran is disrupting global energy supplies and disproportionately affecting Asian nations, including the Philippines, which declared an energy emergency. The conflict raises questions about a major turning point for globalization.

stories.title: Swedish PM offers deal that could see far-right allowed into government
stories.summary: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson has offered to bring the far-right Sweden Democrats into government for the first time, promising key ministerial posts in immigration policy if his four-party coalition wins the next general election in September. The party has neo-Nazi roots.

stories.title: Trump to address nation at 9pm EST, outline Iran war endgame as Washington debates next phase
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the nation at 9pm EST on Wednesday to provide an update on the Iran conflict. The White House fueled speculation that Trump may declare an end to the five-week war, with or without a negotiated settlement.

stories.title: Ukraine halts Russian advances across key sectors as Moscow prepares a new offensive. Meduza analyzes the latest battlefield developments.
stories.summary: Meduza published an analysis of recent battlefield developments in Ukraine, reporting that Ukrainian forces have halted Russian advances across key sectors while Moscow prepares a new offensive. The analysis draws on open-source information.

stories.title: Pakistan says holding talks with Afghan government in China
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan have begun a new round of talks hosted in China aimed at ending the deadliest fighting between the two nations. The negotiations seek to de-escalate the conflict between the two Muslim-majority countries.

stories.title: Putin likely to participate in September BRICS summit in Delhi: Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister
stories.summary: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister indicated that President Vladimir Putin is likely to attend the September BRICS summit in Delhi. He added that Russia would honor past oil export contracts despite Moscow's ban on gasoline exports.

stories.title: Hormuz disruption will change trade — and defense — at other chokepoints
stories.summary: US Navy Supply Corps Capt. Michael Kidd warns that disruption at the Strait of Hormuz will trigger cascading pressure across the global shipping network, affecting other maritime chokepoints and requiring coordinated international defense responses.

stories.title: Russian drone injures bus passengers in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack in the Cherkasy district injured four people, including bus passengers hit by falling debris. Critical infrastructure in the area was also damaged in the strike.

stories.title: Heavy fighting and strikes intensify along Lebanon’s southwest coast
stories.summary: Intense fighting and air strikes have escalated along Lebanon's southwestern coast over the past 48 hours. An Israeli air strike killed two people on a motorcycle in the coastal town of al-Mansouri. Clashes between Hezbollah and Israeli forces continued in nearby Biyyada.

stories.title: U.S. is considering exiting ‘paper tiger NATO’, says Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said the U.S. is considering exiting NATO, which he called a "paper tiger," after alliance partners including the U.K., France, and Spain refused to join the war on Iran. Trump expressed disbelief that NATO did not respond to his call for support.

stories.title: What a U.S. Operation to Get Iran’s Uranium Would Look Like
stories.summary: An analysis explores the logistical and military complexities of a potential U.S. operation to secure Iran's uranium stockpiles, describing the challenge as even more difficult than the capture of Venezuelan President Maduro.

stories.title: Africa: Mozambique Becomes Africa's Most Distressed Sovereign As Spreads Surge
stories.summary: Mozambique has overtaken Senegal as Africa's most distressed sovereign borrower, according to Daba Finance, as rising global energy costs add pressure to the country's finances and bond spreads surge.

stories.title: Israel underground hospitals 'at risk of disease outbreak'
stories.summary: Israeli underground hospitals are facing increased risk of disease outbreaks due to overcrowding and inadequate hygiene conditions. Health officials have raised concerns about the potential spread of infections in these wartime facilities.

stories.title: First Russian Translation of Khamenei Memoir to Hit Bookstores in April
stories.summary: The first Russian-language translation of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei's memoir is scheduled to appear in bookstores in April. The book was translated from Persian by writer and critic Alexander Andryushkin, who specializes in Iranian literature.

stories.title: Iraq coach says World Cup can help ‘change perception’ of country
stories.summary: Iraq's national football team coach said the country's World Cup participation can help shift international perceptions of Iraq. The nation has endured decades of wars, crises, and separatist movements.

stories.title: Stronger polls buy Flavio Bolsonaro time on economic team as Brazil race heats up
stories.summary: Rising poll numbers for Brazilian opposition Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign have allowed him to delay naming key economic advisers. The delay comes as right-wing rivals enter the field ahead of Brazil's October election.

stories.title: Three teens facing terrorism charges over foiled Bank of America bombing
stories.summary: Three teenagers and one adult face terrorism charges in connection with a foiled bomb plot targeting a Bank of America location. The four suspects are accused of forming a criminal terrorist conspiracy.

stories.title: Waiting for the War to End in Tehran
stories.summary: Iranians living under bombardment in Tehran are experiencing surges of patriotism alongside growing criticism of their own government as they wait for the war to end.

stories.title: Occupied West Bank on strike against Israeli death penalty law
stories.summary: A general strike shut down shops and public institutions across the occupied West Bank, including Hebron, Ramallah, and Nablus. The strike, called by Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah party, protested an Israeli law permitting the execution of Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks.

stories.title: Iran fires major missile salvo ahead of Passover holiday
stories.summary: Iran launched approximately ten ballistic missiles in a significant salvo timed ahead of the Passover holiday. The barrage was described as one of the most substantial Iranian missile attacks in recent weeks.

stories.title: War update: 64 clashes on front lines, most clashes reported in Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 64 combat clashes with Russian troops along the front lines in a single day. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: Trump says ceasefire tied to Hormuz reopening, vows continued strikes
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he would consider a ceasefire with Iran only if the Strait of Hormuz is fully reopened. In a social media post, Trump vowed to continue strikes on Iran until that condition is met.

stories.title: Starlink a 'legitimate' target for Iran, state media says
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Tehran may begin targeting Elon Musk's Starlink satellite systems in the region. The warning followed Iran's announcement that it would expand strikes against American commercial interests.

stories.title: British PM Starmer pledges push to reopen Strait of Hormuz as Trump aims more barbs
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged to push for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz while reaffirming that Britain did not wish to be drawn into the US-led military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Russia claims troops have taken full control of Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine: reports
stories.summary: Russia claimed its troops have taken full control of Ukraine's Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine. Luhansk and neighboring Donetsk make up the industrialized Donbas area, and this is the third time Russia has made such a claim since its February 2022 invasion.

stories.title: France suspects pro-Iranian group HAYI was behind foiled attack on Bank of America Paris
stories.summary: French authorities suspect the pro-Iranian group HAYI of planning a foiled attack on the Bank of America office in Paris. The group had previously posted a video threatening Jewish communities in France and across Europe.

stories.title: Babies evacuated from Gaza two years ago returned to their overjoyed parents
stories.summary: Twenty-nine preterm babies evacuated from a hospital in Gaza in 2023 have been reunited with their parents after spending roughly two years separated due to the conflict.

stories.title: France suspects link to pro-Iranian group in foiled BofA Paris plot
stories.summary: French authorities suspect a link to a pro-Iranian group called HAYI in a foiled plot targeting a Bank of America location in Paris. The group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiyya, had posted a social media video threatening European Jewish communities.

stories.title: SpaceX confidentially files to go public on stock market, reports say
stories.summary: SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket and satellite communications company, has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the U.S. stock market, according to Bloomberg and the Wall Street Journal. The company could go public as early as June and may seek a valuation upward of $1.75 trillion.

stories.title: Trump says he is ‘absolutely’ considering withdrawing US from Nato
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he is "absolutely" considering withdrawing the United States from NATO, escalating his criticism after allied nations refused to join the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. A former U.S. ambassador described the threats as the worst crisis the 77-year-old alliance has faced.

stories.title: After attack, Michigan synagogue calls to add Lego to Seder plate
stories.summary: Temple Israel in Detroit, Michigan, which was the site of a vehicle-ramming attack last month, has proposed adding a Lego brick to the Passover Seder plate. The synagogue said the object symbolizes both vulnerability and rebuilding.

stories.title: 3 more men arrested in suspected antisemitic torching in London
stories.summary: Three additional men were arrested in London in connection with an arson attack that destroyed four volunteer ambulances operated by a Jewish organization. The incident is being investigated as a suspected antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: A new Israeli wall could sever the West Bank's Jordan Valley
stories.summary: Israel is constructing a new military barrier in the West Bank that could sever the Jordan Valley from the rest of Palestinian territory. Palestinian farmers caught between the wall and expanding Israeli settlements are reportedly being forced from their homes.

stories.title: AOC reportedly signals opposition to all Israel aid, including defensive spending
stories.summary: US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has reportedly signaled opposition to all US aid to Israel, including defensive spending such as Iron Dome funding. She also reportedly opposes adoption of the IHRA definition of antisemitism.

stories.title: Kuwait says airport fuel tank fire extinguished after drone attack
stories.summary: Kuwaiti authorities reported that firefighters extinguished a blaze at Kuwait airport fuel tanks caused by an Iranian drone strike. No casualties were reported, and damage was limited to property.

stories.title: Switzerland considers ‘complete termination’ of US Patriot order, vows to extend payment freeze
stories.summary: Switzerland warned that the Patriot air-defense system delivery delays could affect the broader F-35 fighter jet sale and its entire foreign military sales portfolio with the United States. Bern said it is considering complete termination of the Patriot order and will extend its payment freeze.

stories.title: UK will not be drawn into war, will free energy bills from Russian, Iranian control, PM says
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Britain would not be drawn into the wider war and pledged to pursue diplomatic avenues for de-escalation. He also vowed to free UK energy bills from dependence on Russian and Iranian supplies and push for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russia’s Rubicon center claims it ramped up kill rate of Ukrainian forces in March
stories.summary: Russia's Center for Advanced Unmanned Technologies, known as Rubicon, claimed it significantly increased its destruction of Ukrainian military targets in March. The center specializes in drone warfare operations.

stories.title: From Theory to Reality: Evaluating the U.S.-Ukrainian Minerals Deal
stories.summary: A reassessment of the U.S.-Ukraine critical minerals deal examines how the investment plan established in 2026 compares to recommendations made in a 2025 analysis. The original argument called for a Washington strategy ensuring Ukrainian control and allied access to Ukraine's significant mineral reserves.

stories.title: Iran authorities await war ‘victory’ as supporters mark 1979 anniversary
stories.summary: Iranian officials and government supporters rallied in cities across Iran to mark Islamic Republic Day, commemorating the 1979 revolution. The demonstrations took place as US and Israeli military operations against Iran continued.

stories.title: Russians attack Nikopol with drones; ten people wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the city of Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region using drones and artillery. Ten people were wounded in the assault.

stories.title: Trump to address nation as Iran war batters approval
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is scheduled to deliver a national address on the war with Iran as his approval ratings decline. The speech comes amid growing economic concerns and uncertainty over ceasefire prospects.

stories.title: IDF warns of coordinated Iran, Hezbollah fire during Passover eve
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces warned of a possible coordinated attack by Iran and Hezbollah timed to coincide with Passover eve. Security officials cautioned that an escalation during the holiday period remained a significant risk.

stories.title: PSX gains over 6,700 points on hopes of Middle East de-escalation
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index surged 6,768 points, or 4.55 percent, to close at 155,511.56 on Wednesday amid investor optimism over potential Middle East de-escalation. The rally followed signals that the Iran conflict might be nearing an end.

stories.title: Iraqi armed factions launch recruitment drive amid Iran war
stories.summary: Several Iraqi Shiite armed factions have launched recruitment drives to assemble volunteer battalions to fight alongside Iranian forces. The mobilization comes as the United States is massing ground troops in the region.

stories.title: Brilliant ambush plan: Ukrainian troops impress experienced NATO instructors with superior “tactical imagination”
stories.summary: Ukrainian troops impressed experienced NATO instructors by devising an exceptionally sophisticated ambush plan within a six-hour timeframe. The instructors praised the Ukrainians' superior tactical imagination during the training exercise.

stories.title: ‘System malfunction’ causes robotaxis to stall in the middle of the road in China
stories.summary: A system malfunction caused multiple Baidu-operated Apollo Go robotaxis to stall in the middle of roads in Wuhan, China. Riders were stranded for hours, and police confirmed receiving numerous calls about the incidents on Tuesday night.

stories.title: UK is most vulnerable European country to jet fuel shortages, Ryanair boss says
stories.summary: Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary warned that the UK is the most vulnerable European country to jet fuel shortages caused by the Iran war disrupting Gulf supplies. He noted that Britain relies on Kuwait for approximately 25% of its jet fuel supply.

stories.title: ‘This is an apartheid regime’: Critics decry Israel’s new death penalty law
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a new death penalty law designed to apply exclusively to Palestinians. Critics condemned the legislation as discriminatory, while supporters in parliament celebrated its passage.

stories.title: Uganda, Egypt discuss Iran war impact on Africa's energy and food prices
stories.summary: Uganda's state minister for foreign affairs met with Egypt's foreign minister in Cairo to discuss the impact of the ongoing war involving Iran on Africa. Talks focused on rising energy costs, inflation, and food price pressures across the continent.

stories.title: Zelensky on cooperation with Middle East: Our interceptors already show results
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is expanding military and security cooperation with Middle Eastern and Gulf nations. He noted that Ukrainian-made interceptors deployed in the region are already showing results.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan officials hold talks in China’s Urumqi under trilateral mechanism
stories.summary: Officials from Pakistan, Afghanistan, and China met in the Chinese city of Urumqi under the trilateral mechanism, marking a resumption of diplomatic contact since Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq on February 26. A Pakistani official said there was no breakthrough, though China committed to continued engagement.

stories.title: IRGC says Hormuz under its control amid Trump ceasefire remarks
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared the Strait of Hormuz is firmly under its control and will not be opened under US pressure. The statement came shortly after President Trump conditioned any ceasefire on the strait being reopened.

stories.title: Search for abducted US journalist underway south of Baghdad
stories.summary: Iraqi security officials have blamed the pro-Iran group Kataib Hezbollah for the kidnapping of US journalist Shelly Kittleson south of Baghdad. A search operation is underway, but Kittleson has not yet been located.

stories.title: Greenpeace accuses oil companies of reaping Mid-East ‘war profits’
stories.summary: Greenpeace has accused major oil companies of profiting from the Middle East conflict, claiming they have earned more than €80 million per day in what the organization describes as war-related profits.

stories.title: Ukraine crushes Moscow’s largest assault of 2026 on Donetsk fortress belt that held back Russians since 2014
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces repelled what was described as Moscow's largest motorcycle assault of 2026 on the Sloviansk direction in the Donetsk region. The defensive fortification belt in the area has held against Russian advances since 2014.

stories.title: FY27 budget ‘to reflect’ Space Force need for rapid capabilities growth: Saltzman
stories.summary: U.S. Space Force Chief of Space Operations Gen. Chance Saltzman stated that the fiscal year 2027 budget will reflect the service's need for rapid capabilities growth. He said the White House, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Department of Defense all agree the Space Force needs to expand.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz says Pakistan successfully addressed demand, supply of essential goods amid regional conflict
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan was successfully managing the demand and supply of essential commodities despite global disruptions from regional conflict. He made the remarks during a review meeting on strategies to mitigate financial and economic impacts.

stories.title: Israeli wounded after rocket strikes Kiryat Shmona
stories.summary: One person was wounded after a rocket struck the northern Israeli city of Kiryat Shmona, according to Israeli medics. Israeli media reported extensive damage from Hezbollah shelling in the area.

stories.title: You don’t have to be Moses: This generation must rise to lead in a time of war - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion column urges ordinary Israelis to take on leadership roles during wartime rather than waiting for a singular figure. The piece calls on citizens to pursue justice and victory for the country.

stories.title: High times or low blows? Experts fail to clear air over German drug legalisation
stories.summary: Two years after Germany legalized personal recreational cannabis use for adults, the policy remains divisive. The SPD has praised the legislation, while a CDU minister warns it poses risks to young people's health, and experts disagree over its impact on consumption and organized crime.

stories.title: Robotaxi outage in China’s Wuhan leaves passengers stranded in moving traffic
stories.summary: More than 100 Baidu-operated robotaxis stopped running in Wuhan, China, due to a system malfunction, leaving some passengers stranded in moving traffic. Police confirmed the incident in a statement, and no injuries were reported.

stories.title: Russian drones attack infrastructure facilities in two districts of Zakarpattia region
