stories.summary: Russian drones struck critical infrastructure facilities in two districts of Ukraine's Zakarpattia region, near the borders with EU and NATO countries. One person was injured in the attacks.

stories.title: Israeli lab decodes the building talents of a tropical ant
stories.summary: Researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel used time-lapse technology and geometric analysis to study the collective building behavior of tropical weaver ants. The study examined how the ants coordinate construction as a cognitive unit.

stories.title: We need to stop using the word 'resilience' to describe Israel, here's why
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the word "resilience" is inadequate to describe Israelis' experience after years of physical and emotional hardship. The author contends the term minimizes what the nation has endured.

stories.title: 'Death to Jews, Vucic' call during Belgrade protest sparks criticism from Serbians, Israelis
stories.summary: Chants of "Death to Jews" and "Death to Vučić" during a protest in Belgrade drew condemnation from Serbian and Israeli figures. MK Boaz Toporovsky, Dr. Efraim Zuroff, and Aleksandar Nikolić issued a joint statement rejecting such calls regardless of political motivation.

stories.title: In latest warning, Zamir says IDF faces ‘severe harm’ if manpower crunch isn’t solved
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir warned that the Israeli military faces severe harm if its manpower shortage is not addressed. He called for extending mandatory service, reforming the reserves, and passing a conscription law, noting the army could lose thousands of troops by January.

stories.title: Rheinmetall’s contract for Ukraine stalls — FV-014 Raider loitering munition’s price has been revealed
stories.summary: German defense company Rheinmetall's contract to deliver FV-014 Raider loitering munitions to Ukraine has stalled despite the weapon being combat-tested. Two hundred units are reportedly ready for delivery, and the unit price has been disclosed.

stories.title: Parents told to ‘take responsibility’ after two days of TikTok-led London disorder
stories.summary: Six teenage girls were arrested after hundreds of young people gathered in Clapham, south-west London, over two days of disorder linked to a TikTok trend called "swarming the streets." The Metropolitan Police urged parents to take responsibility and said more arrests would follow based on CCTV and body camera footage.

stories.title: Two dead and one missing after trying to cross Channel to UK
stories.summary: Two people died and one person went missing while attempting to cross the English Channel from France to the UK on Wednesday, marking the first fatal Channel crossing incident of the year. The deaths occurred hours after the UK and France agreed on an interim £16.2 million deal to curb Channel crossings.

stories.title: Ukraine names seven archaeologists Russia sent to steal treasures from occupied Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine identified seven Russian archaeologists who were sent with Kremlin-issued permits to occupied territories in Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea. The individuals are accused of participating in the looting of Ukrainian cultural heritage.

stories.title: Families cram into Greek court for trial into deadliest train crash
stories.summary: A trial has begun in Greece for 36 defendants accused in connection with the country's worst rail disaster. Fifty-seven people were killed when two trains collided in 2023, and the trial is expected to last several years.

stories.title: March sees 35pc decline in terrorism fatalities, coinciding with Operation Ghazab lil-Haq: PICSS
stories.summary: Pakistan recorded a 35 percent decline in combat-related fatalities in March, with 331 deaths compared to 506 in February, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies. The decline coincided with the ongoing Operation Ghazab lil-Haq.

stories.title: Iranian officials ‘laugh’ at Trump’s claim Iran wants a ceasefire
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official publicly laughed at US President Donald Trump's assertion that Iran had requested a ceasefire. The response underscored Tehran's rejection of Washington's characterization of diplomatic dynamics between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel says strikes targeting Iranian government infrastructure
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it is conducting strikes targeting dozens of Iranian government infrastructure sites. The air force said it is simultaneously intercepting threats across multiple regions.

stories.title: VkusVill Closed Hundreds of Stores in 2025
stories.summary: Russian grocery chain VkusVill closed hundreds of stores in 2025 as part of an optimization strategy. A company spokesperson said the retailer is shifting its focus toward online delivery services.

stories.title: Kenya’s tea industry suffers crisis caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: Kenyan tea farmers are experiencing a crisis as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran has disrupted key export routes through the Middle East. Kenya's tea industry relies heavily on those shipping lanes to reach major markets in the region.

stories.title: Damascus alcohol crackdown fuels debate over Syria's future
stories.summary: Authorities in Damascus have intensified a crackdown on alcohol sales, sparking public debate about regulation, social norms, and the limits of state power in post-conflict Syria.

stories.title: Security forces kill 13 terrorists in 2 separate intelligence-based operations in KP: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 13 terrorists in two intelligence-based operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on March 30, according to ISPR. Ten were killed in Bara, Khyber district, and three in a separate engagement. The militants belonged to Fitna al Khawarij, the state's term for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

stories.title: British PM Keir Starmer touts cost of living help to ease Iran war pressure
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is facing mounting domestic pressure to announce additional cost-of-living support as the economic fallout from the Iran crisis affects UK households. He has sought to respond with measures aimed at easing financial strain on citizens.

stories.title: Gale-force winds forecast across northern UK over Easter weekend
stories.summary: The UK Met Office issued a yellow weather warning for gale-force winds across Scotland, Northern Ireland, and parts of north Wales and northern England over the Easter weekend. Gusts of up to 90 mph are expected in some areas, with possible travel disruption and power outages from Saturday evening through Sunday midday.

stories.title: Enterprise damaged, and fire breaks out in Ternopil region following drone attack
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack struck an enterprise in Ukraine's Ternopil region on April 1, sparking a fire. Authorities reported damage to the facility but did not immediately detail casualties.

stories.title: History’s biggest census: Why India’s new population count is controversial
stories.summary: India is preparing to conduct its first population census in over a decade after a five-year delay. The count will include caste enumeration for the first time in roughly a century, making it a politically sensitive exercise.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll rises
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that at least 1,318 people have been killed and 3,935 wounded in Israeli attacks on the country since March 2, 2026.

stories.title: Russia is ordering companies to nominate employees for military service — 2 to 5 names depending on size
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly ordering companies to nominate employees for military service, requiring two to five names depending on company size. The measure comes as voluntary enlistment rates have been declining in major Russian cities despite financial incentives.

stories.title: Iranian missile hit oil tanker in Qatari waters, says Qatar
stories.summary: Qatar reported that an Iranian missile struck an oil tanker in Qatari waters, approximately 17 nautical miles north of the Ras Laffan industrial hub. The incident highlights the growing threat to maritime traffic in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Israeli army detects another Iran missile attack
stories.summary: Israel's military detected another ballistic missile attack launched from Iran toward central Israel. The detection came shortly after approximately 10 missiles were fired at the same area, with most intercepted by air defenses.

stories.title: Air Force strategy to protect aircraft was designed for China. Will it work for Iran?
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth acknowledged that Iran managed to strike American aircraft in Saudi Arabia despite the U.S. having maximized its defensive posture. The Air Force's aircraft protection strategy, originally designed for a potential conflict with China, is being tested against Iranian capabilities.

stories.title: International Finance Corporation briefs Aurangzeb on ‘growing portfolio’ in Pakistan
stories.summary: A delegation from the International Finance Corporation briefed Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on IFC's growing portfolio in the country, which now exceeds $2 billion annually. Discussions covered financial sector support, risk-sharing mechanisms, and broader investment engagement.

stories.title: Largest Iranian missile salvo since beginning of war fired at central Israel
stories.summary: Iran launched approximately 10 ballistic missiles at central Israel in the largest single salvo since the war began, according to the Israeli military. Most missiles were intercepted by air defenses, though some hit open areas per protocol. Emergency teams responded but reported no immediate injuries.

stories.title: Iran denies Trump claim that Iran's new leader has asked for a ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran's leadership denied President Trump's claim, posted on Truth Social, that Iran's new leader had requested a ceasefire with the United States. The conflicting statements highlight ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Families condemn UK ‘impotence’ over UAE ‘social media misuse’ detentions
stories.summary: Families of UK citizens detained in the United Arab Emirates for allegedly sharing images related to the Iran conflict have criticized the British government's response. More than 100 foreign nationals have been detained under UAE laws prohibiting the sharing of material deemed to disturb public security.

stories.title: Sharaa spells his vision for Syria during landmark UK visit
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa made a landmark visit to Germany and the United Kingdom. Speaking in London, Al-Sharaa outlined his vision for Syria's future amid the ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Four people killed in Russian drone attack in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: A Russian unmanned aerial vehicle killed four people in the Zolotonosha district of Ukraine's Cherkasy region. The attack is part of an intensified pattern of Russian drone strikes on Ukrainian civilian areas.

stories.title: Northern Fleet personnel among 29 killed in Russian military transport crash in Crimea
stories.summary: A Russian military transport aircraft crashed in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board, including seven crew members and 22 passengers. Murmansk Governor Andrei Chibis confirmed that personnel from Russia's Northern Fleet were among the dead, though the exact number was not specified.

stories.title: FCC seeks response from KP CM Afridi over plans to form ‘Imran Khan release force’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court directed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to respond within 10 days to a petition seeking to block mobilization of a "release force" for jailed PTI founder Imran Khan. The three-judge bench also issued notices to the KP government, PTI, the federal government, and the Election Commission.

stories.title: ISIS: The March to Dystopia: Azmi Bishara on war & power vacuums
stories.summary: A discussion of Azmi Bishara's book examines how prolonged conflict, sectarian divisions, and political chaos in the Middle East created conditions for the rise of the Islamic State group. The work analyzes the relationship between war and power vacuums.

stories.title: Netanyahu to fast-track law giving Haredi men draft exemption
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu moved to fast-track legislation granting ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) men exemptions from mandatory military service. The controversial bill would provide sweeping draft exemptions amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: Pope Leo celebrates first Easter amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Easter as pontiff during the ongoing Middle East conflict. He expressed hope that the U.S.-Israel war on Iran could conclude soon in remarks to reporters.

stories.title: Trump attends supreme court hearing on birthright citizenship case that could upend rights for millions
stories.summary: President Donald Trump attended US Supreme Court oral arguments on a case challenging birthright citizenship. Trump issued an executive order in 2025 seeking to end the constitutional guarantee; overturning it could affect hundreds of thousands of children born annually in the US.

stories.title: Iran, Hezbollah launch attacks as Israelis host Passover Seders, sending millions to shelters
stories.summary: Iran and Hezbollah launched missile and rocket attacks on Israel during Passover Seder celebrations, sending millions of Israelis to shelters. The IDF reported at least 10 missiles in the Iranian salvo. No injuries were reported, though homes, cars, and a playground sustained damage.

stories.title: Two teenagers say Russian police detained and beat them on the day of a planned protest against internet blocking
stories.summary: In Yekaterinburg, Russian police detained a 17-year-old and an 18-year-old on the day of a planned protest against internet blocking. Both told the outlet Mediazona that officers physically beat them, one during the detention and the other at the police station.

stories.title: UAV crashes in Poltava community, three adults and child injured
stories.summary: An enemy drone crashed in the Poltava community, injuring four people including a child. The strike is part of a broader wave of Russian UAV attacks across central Ukraine.

stories.title: What can nations do to make up for the ongoing energy shortfall?
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has disrupted approximately 20 percent of the global fuel supply. Nations worldwide are seeking alternative energy sources to compensate for the shortfall.

stories.title: China’s FM Wang Yi appreciates Pakistan’s active diplomatic efforts in promoting Middle East peace: FO
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi expressed appreciation for Pakistan's diplomatic efforts toward Middle East peace during a meeting with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar in Beijing. The two sides issued a five-point initiative aimed at restoring peace in the region.

stories.title: On Passover, former Gaza hostages say freedom 'takes on a different meaning' - interview
stories.summary: Former Gaza hostages David Cunio and Keith Siegel spoke about their experience of freedom after returning home. In interviews ahead of Passover, both said the holiday's theme of liberation now carries a deeply personal meaning for them.

stories.title: Russia says will continue helping Cuba after first oil shipment arrives
stories.summary: Russia's first oil shipment to Cuba has arrived, and Moscow pledged to continue assisting the island nation. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called on the United States to lift its energy blockade on Cuba.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei’s rumoured injury or death won’t change Iran’s trajectory
stories.summary: Rumors have circulated about the injury or death of Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Analysts note that Ali Khamenei built the supreme leader's office into an institutional structure not dependent on any single individual.

stories.title: Indonesia urges UN probe into killing of peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: Indonesia called for a United Nations investigation into the killing of three Indonesian soldiers serving with UNIFIL in Lebanon. The deaths marked the first UNIFIL fatalities since hostilities between Hezbollah and Israel began in 2023.

stories.title: U.S. Lifts Sanctions on 3 Russian Cargo Vessels Linked to Exports From Occupied Ukraine
stories.summary: The United States lifted sanctions on three Russian cargo vessels reportedly linked to the export of resources extracted from occupied Ukrainian territory. The vessels were also tied to Russian war finance and government insiders.

stories.title: French Film Show: ‘Mrs’ lays bare bourgeois family tensions
stories.summary: The French film "Mrs," directed by David Roux and starring Mélanie Thierry, explores bourgeois family tensions through the story of a seemingly perfect wife and mother. Critics note the film's minimalist approach draws on the legacy of French director Claude Chabrol.

stories.title: Romania, Ukraine advance talks on EU-funded joint drone production
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone manufacturers met with Romanian defence ministry and army officials in Bucharest to discuss joint drone production. The talks focus on leveraging a new European Union rearmament funding mechanism to support collaborative defence manufacturing.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghan Taliban resume talks in China as Beijing seeks ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistani and Afghan Taliban representatives resumed talks in Urumqi, China, under a trilateral mechanism involving Beijing. The meeting follows a breakdown in diplomatic contact after Pakistan's military operations against militant targets in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Russia adds 22 glucose-monitoring apps to list of services exempt from internet restrictions
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry added 22 glucose-monitoring apps to a list of services exempt from mobile internet restrictions. The decision was reported by the Russian news agency Interfax.

stories.title: Russians try to intensify offensive operations on front lines, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russia is attempting to intensify its offensive operations along the front lines. The statement reflects ongoing pressure on Ukrainian positions across multiple sectors.

stories.title: Pentagon, Boeing agree to triple PAC-3 seeker production
stories.summary: The Pentagon and Boeing agreed on a contract framework to triple production of PAC-3 missile seekers over seven years. The arrangement parallels Lockheed Martin's ongoing effort to surge production of the PAC-3 MSE all-up interceptor round.

stories.title: Eurovision Song Contest expanding with Asian edition
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest is expanding with its first Asian edition, set to take place in Bangkok, Thailand, later in 2026. At least 10 countries including South Korea, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Malaysia have confirmed participation, with more expected before the November finale.

stories.title: The Many Lives of ‘Iván Mordisco,’ Colombia’s Most Wanted
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro has intensified military operations against Iván Mordisco, the country's most wanted guerrilla leader who commands a dissident FARC faction of over 4,000 members across 10 departments. Despite years of offensives and false reports of his death, Mordisco remains at large.

stories.title: Deadly arsenal explosions rock Bujumbura
stories.summary: Dozens of people were killed in Bujumbura, Burundi, after a fire at a military ammunition depot in the Musaga neighborhood triggered powerful explosions late Tuesday night. The blasts sent shockwaves across the city and caused widespread panic among residents.

stories.title: Transatlantic rift widens as Trump lashes out at NATO
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he is strongly considering pulling the US out of NATO, intensifying criticism of European allies over disagreements related to America's war alongside Israel against Iran. The remarks have widened the transatlantic rift.

stories.title: 24 Iranian health workers killed in US-Israeli attacks: Emergency medical organisation
stories.summary: Iran's Emergency Medical Services Organisation reported that at least 24 health workers have been killed and 114 wounded in U.S.-Israeli attacks on the country. The organisation said over 330 healthcare facilities have been damaged, with one rescue helicopter destroyed.

stories.title: Israel says will reduce French defence imports 'to zero'
stories.summary: Israel announced it will reduce its military imports from France "to zero" in retaliation for French policies it considers hostile. According to the French parliament, France does not export weapons directly to Israel but supplies components for defense systems.

stories.title: Britain to host 35 countries for strait of Hormuz talks, says Starmer
stories.summary: The United Kingdom will convene 35 countries, excluding the United States, to explore ways to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blocked. Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the talks are part of joint British-French diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Russia lost two military aircraft in one day — an An-26 military transport killing all 29 aboard and an unconfirmed Su-34 fighter-bomber
stories.summary: Russia lost two military aircraft in a single day. An An-26 transport plane crashed into a cliff in occupied Bakhchisarai's mountains in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board, while Russian bloggers reported the loss of an Su-34 fighter-bomber.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan officials meet in China’s Urumqi under trilateral mechanism
stories.summary: Officials from Pakistan, Afghanistan, and China met in Urumqi under a trilateral mechanism to discuss the latest escalation in tensions. Diplomatic contact between Islamabad and Kabul had largely ceased since Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq against militant hideouts in Afghanistan on February 26.

stories.title: Bedouins in Israel’s Negev desert face bomb shelter shortage
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Bedouins in Israel's southern Negev desert lack access to bomb shelters amid continuing Iranian and Hezbollah air strikes. NGOs are installing mobile shelters while calling on the Israeli government to address what they describe as discriminatory planning policies.

stories.title: Mamdani says Iran war 'should be opposed' on all grounds
stories.summary: New York politician Zohran Mamdani called for opposition to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran "on every single ground." He linked opposition to the war with concerns over a historic affordability crisis affecting Americans.

stories.title: Palestinians in West Bank strike after Israel passes death penalty law
stories.summary: Palestinians in the occupied West Bank held a general strike on April 1, 2026, after Israel passed legislation allowing the execution of Palestinian prisoners. Families of detainees vowed resistance, while human rights organizations and multiple countries condemned the law.

stories.title: Tehran Is Setting a Trap for Trump
stories.summary: Iran's current leadership is characterized as more radical and less risk-averse than previous administrations, raising concerns about Tehran's strategic posture toward the United States under President Trump.

stories.title: Tehran Is Setting a Trap for Trump
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that Iran's current leadership is more radical and less risk-averse than previous administrations, potentially setting strategic conditions to draw the United States into unfavorable positions amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Australia’s Albanese says war's economic shock will be felt for months; urges using public transport
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned that economic shocks from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran would be felt for months and urged citizens to use public transport. Australia imports about 90 percent of its fuel and has experienced petrol price surges and localized shortages due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: Iran War: What a Marine Expeditionary Unit is – and other US military terms
stories.summary: The United States has deployed thousands of additional Marines and airborne troops to the Middle East since the outbreak of war with Iran. The article explains key military terms, including what a Marine Expeditionary Unit is.

stories.title: Iran denies Trump’s claim Iranian president requested ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran denied U.S. President Donald Trump's claim that Iran's president requested a ceasefire. Trump stated the U.S. would continue strikes on Iran until the Strait of Hormuz is reopened.

stories.title: 700,000 barrels of Russian oil arrived in Cuba: Kremlin keeps island’s lights, as its mercenaries bolster war ranks
stories.summary: A Russian tanker on a U.S. sanctions list delivered 700,000 barrels of oil to Cuba's largest fuel terminal on March 31. It was the first major Russian oil delivery to the island since Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in early 2026.

stories.title: Israel to occupy parts of Lebanon and keep out 600,000 residents
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced plans to occupy parts of southern Lebanon and prevent the return of approximately 600,000 residents. He stated that all homes in villages along the border would be destroyed.

stories.title: Building collapses in Tel Aviv, Houthis join the fight
stories.summary: Reports emerged of a building collapse in Tel Aviv and Houthi forces joining the broader regional conflict. The developments were highlighted in a Jerusalem Post news roundup.

stories.title: Why Israel's death penalty law is a massive setback for human rights
stories.summary: Israel passed a death penalty law applicable to Palestinians under occupation, which critics say undermines rights to life, dignity, due process, and equality. The legislation has drawn widespread condemnation from human rights advocates.

stories.title: Spanish police open probe into anti-Muslim chants at friendly match with Egypt
stories.summary: Spanish police opened an investigation into Islamophobic and xenophobic chants directed at Egypt's team during a 0-0 friendly match at Barcelona's RCDE Stadium. Stadium authorities had to appeal to fans multiple times to stop offensive remarks during the pre-World Cup fixture.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz discusses investment opportunities, digital economy with VEON group chief
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with VEON Group CEO Kaan Terzioglu to discuss investment opportunities and digital economy promotion in Pakistan. Sharif highlighted the recent 5G spectrum auction, in which 480 MHz was sold for $507 million.

stories.title: Iran targets Qatar tanker and Kuwait airport in Iran escalation
stories.summary: Iran struck an oil tanker off the coast of Qatar and targeted Kuwait's airport on Wednesday amid ongoing U.S.-Israeli airstrikes on Tehran. The attacks represent a significant escalation of Iran's regional military operations.

stories.title: 4 Hong Kong schools to close as 9 seek mergers over insufficient enrolment
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Education Bureau announced that four public primary schools facing insufficient enrolment will close by the 2029-30 academic year at the latest, while nine others have applied to merge with other institutions.

stories.title: How Donald Trump could reframe US goals in Iran war to justify finishing it
stories.summary: Chinese analysts suggest that shifting US objectives in the war against Iran could allow President Donald Trump to declare success and end the conflict earlier than expected. However, divergent endgame visions between Washington and Israel may complicate a swift conclusion.

stories.title: US threats for new Chile leader, China tariff on Mexico: 7 Latin America relations reads
stories.summary: A roundup of Latin American relations developments highlights US pressure on Cuba amid its Iran campaign, new threats directed at Chile's incoming leader, and China's tariff actions affecting Mexico.

stories.title: Top Hezbollah commander killed in Beirut as IDF presses deeper into Lebanon
stories.summary: A senior Hezbollah commander was killed in an Israeli strike on Beirut as the IDF advanced deeper into Lebanon. Lebanese officials reported seven dead in overnight strikes, while Hezbollah rocket fire continued hitting northern Israel and the Lebanese army withdrew from some border towns.

stories.title: As Russia breaks air attack record, Ukraine’s interception rate climbs to 90%
stories.summary: Russia set a new record for air attacks against Ukraine, but Ukraine's interception rate has climbed to 90%. Ukraine's Defense Ministry credited newly deployed air defense systems and upgrades to existing ones for the improved performance.

stories.title: Russia’s Supreme Court upholds 16-year sentence against dissident
stories.summary: Russia's Supreme Court upheld a 16-year prison sentence against 68-year-old dissident Alexander Skobow, rejecting his cassation appeal. Skobow was convicted of justifying terrorism and participating in an organization designated as terrorist by Russian authorities.

stories.title: UK police arrest three more suspects in arson attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police arrested three men, aged 17, 19, and 20, in east London in connection with an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances. The counter-terrorism chief said the arrests demonstrate police commitment to protecting the Jewish community.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike on Iran's Mianeh killed five
stories.summary: A U.S.-Israeli airstrike on a residential area in the northwestern Iranian city of Mianeh killed at least five people, according to Iranian media reports.

stories.title: Pentagon awards Pratt & Whitney $6.6 billion for F-35 engines
stories.summary: The Pentagon awarded Pratt & Whitney a $6.6 billion contract to produce engines for two upcoming production batches of F-35 Joint Strike Fighter aircraft.

stories.title: The Folly of Seizing Kharg Island
stories.summary: Five weeks into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, Tehran has not capitulated despite significant destruction of its military assets. Iran's strategic confidence reportedly stems from its control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy chokepoint, where the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has strengthened its position.

stories.title: Ukraine receives nearly $1.3 billion grant from Japan for social spending
stories.summary: Japan provided Ukraine with a grant of nearly $1.3 billion earmarked for social spending. The funding was allocated under the G7's Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) mechanism.

stories.title: Russia Says It Took Full Control of Ukraine’s Luhansk (Again)
stories.summary: Russia claimed it has taken full control of Ukraine's Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine. This marks the third time Moscow has made such a claim since launching its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

stories.title: Joy and heartbreak as World Cup qualifying marathon ends
stories.summary: Iraq defeated Bolivia 2-1 in an intercontinental playoff held in Monterrey, Mexico, to claim the 48th and final spot in FIFA's expanded World Cup. Earlier, Bosnia and Herzegovina eliminated four-time champion Italy on penalties in the European playoffs, marking Italy's third consecutive failure to qualify for the tournament.

stories.title: French truck drivers protest over rising fuel prices
stories.summary: French truck and coach drivers staged a nationwide go-slow protest, traveling at speeds below 30 kilometers per hour, to demand greater government support amid soaring fuel prices. The drivers attribute the price surge to the ongoing war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Ali Zafar wins defamation case against Meesha Shafi: Why it matters
stories.summary: A Pakistani court ruled in favor of singer Ali Zafar in a defamation case against fellow artist Meesha Shafi. Shafi had made sexual harassment allegations against Zafar in 2018 in what became Pakistan's most prominent #MeToo case.

stories.title: Nigeria: Mob violence reported in Jos days after deadly gunman attack
stories.summary: Mob violence erupted across the Nigerian city of Jos on Wednesday, days after a deadly gunman attack. An AFP reporter on the scene observed the mobs, which appeared to result in at least two deaths.

stories.title: Royal Navy captain steps back from duties over link to MP whose husband faces China spy claims
stories.summary: A Royal Navy captain commanding a British nuclear-armed submarine stepped back from his duties over his relationship with MP Joani Reid, whose husband faces allegations of spying for China. The navy investigated the contact over potential blackmail risks.

stories.title: UK PM calls NATO world's 'most effective military alliance' after Trump criticism
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer publicly defended NATO as the most effective military alliance in history after U.S. President Donald Trump called the organization a "paper tiger" in an interview with the UK's Telegraph newspaper. Starmer reaffirmed the UK's full commitment to the alliance.

stories.title: Iran stands firm as diplomatic efforts remain indirect
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official reiterated that Tehran will not accept any agreement unless its core conditions are fully met. The statement came as indirect diplomatic efforts continue amid mounting pressure for a resolution to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: France's Macron and Japan's Takaichi give nod to 'Dragon Ball' franchise
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron, on a state visit to Tokyo, shared a playful "kamehameha" pose with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi referencing the Dragon Ball franchise. The visit focused on discussions about security ties and industrial cooperation between France and Japan.

stories.title: Trump threatens NATO exit, scaling up tensions with allies
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to withdraw the United States from NATO, citing allies' refusal to help secure the Strait of Hormuz. The threat has intensified transatlantic tensions over burden-sharing and Middle East security responsibilities.

stories.title: Jailed Palestinians fear death by hanging without due process under new Israeli law
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law making the death penalty the default sentence for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks deemed to negate Israel's existence. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank expressed fears that jailed relatives could face execution without due process. Rights groups are expected to challenge the law before Israel's Supreme Court.

stories.title: Jubilation as Iraq, Turkey, and Bosnia qualify for World Cup
stories.summary: Iraq, Turkey, and Bosnia and Herzegovina each qualified for the FIFA World Cup on Tuesday. For all three nations, the achievement marks their first World Cup appearance in decades.

stories.title: South African army arrive in crime hotspots to help tackle gangs
stories.summary: The South African military has been deployed to crime hotspots across five of the country's nine provinces. The deployment is part of a year-long operation aimed at tackling gang-related violence.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: World more concerned by politics than the humanitarian fallout
stories.summary: UNICEF MENA Communication Officer Salim Oweis highlighted the deteriorating humanitarian situation in the Middle East, particularly for children. He said displacement, trauma, and loss of basic services are becoming normalized, and urged the international community to understand the crisis through its cumulative human impact rather than statistics alone.

stories.title: In Europe, lobbyists are using soaring fuel prices to make the case for more dirty energy
stories.summary: Lobbyists in Europe are using soaring fuel prices caused by the Iran war's disruption of oil and LNG shipments through the Gulf to argue against the EU's carbon pricing scheme and in favor of expanded fossil fuel use, despite experts saying renewables offer the clearest path forward.

stories.title: France suspects link to pro-Iranian group HAYI in foiled Paris bomb plot
stories.summary: France's anti-terrorism prosecutor said authorities suspect the pro-Iranian group HAYI (Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiyya) was behind a foiled bomb plot targeting Bank of America's offices in Paris, though the link has not been formally confirmed. HAYI had posted a video in March targeting Jewish interests in France and Europe.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit hopes, UN ‘manipulation’, stand-up comedy: 7 US-China relations reads
stories.summary: A US-China relations roundup covers expectations for an amicable Trump-Xi summit, allegations of UN manipulation, and other bilateral developments from recent weeks.

stories.title: Large-scale fires caused by Russian strikes extinguished in Lutsk
stories.summary: Rescue workers in Lutsk extinguished large-scale fires at civilian facilities caused by Russian strikes. The attacks targeted the western Ukrainian city, causing significant damage to civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Most Israelis back death penalty law, call for it to be expanded
stories.summary: A majority of Israeli respondents expressed support for a recently passed death penalty law. On social media, critics called it a political stunt, while many users demanded even harsher measures targeting Palestinians.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran's 'new regime president' asked for a ceasefire
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on social media that Iran's president requested a ceasefire. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded that the Strait of Hormuz remains under its control and will not be opened. Trump said the U.S. would continue strikes until the strait is cleared.

stories.title: Death penalty bill an 'extension of the genocidal measures of the State of Israel': Palestinian FM
stories.summary: Palestinian Foreign Minister Varsen Aghabekian condemned Israel's new death penalty legislation as an extension of what she called genocidal measures by the Israeli state. She accused Israeli settlers and the army of operating as a unified force and reaffirmed that the two-state solution remains the only viable path forward.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. considers withdrawing from NATO
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated he is seriously considering withdrawing the United States from NATO, citing allies' refusal to support U.S. military action against Iran.

stories.title: Gaza's families, former employees doubt UNRWA will get justice
stories.summary: Families of deceased individuals and former employees of UNRWA have expressed doubt that the agency will receive accountability or justice. Some staff members were dismissed or suspended during the war in Gaza, leaving them feeling abandoned by the organization.

stories.title: South Africans load up on fuel as Iran war leads to major price hike
stories.summary: South African motorists rushed to fuel stations ahead of record price hikes taking effect at midnight, driven by the Iran war's disruption of global oil markets. Diesel and petrol prices surged significantly due to the conflict's impact on fuel supply chains.

stories.title: Ramallah shut down in strike against Israel's death penalty law
stories.summary: A near-total general strike shut down Ramallah and much of the West Bank on Wednesday. The action was organized to protest Israel's death penalty law, which Palestinians say specifically targets them.

stories.title: PSX gains over 7,400 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index surged over 7,400 points, or about 5 percent, during intraday trading on Wednesday, reaching 156,204.89. Analysts attributed the continued rally to signs of de-escalation in regional tensions and intensifying diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: UK will seek closer ties with EU in light of Iran war, Starmer says
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced that Britain would seek closer ties with the European Union in response to the Iran war. The move comes as UK-US relations have been strained by Starmer's refusal to deepen British involvement in the conflict.

stories.title: Is China’s commercial rocket now cheaper than Elon Musk’s SpaceX Falcon 9?
stories.summary: Chinese commercial space firm CAS Space launched the Kinetica-2 Y1 (Lijian-2 Y1) rocket on its maiden flight, delivering three satellites into orbit. Reports suggest its launch cost undercuts the per-mission price of SpaceX's reusable Falcon 9.

stories.title: Federal government claims some states standing in the way of ‘getting those guns off our streets’
stories.summary: Australia's federal government accused several state and territory leaders of obstructing a proposed national gun buyback scheme. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's end-of-March deadline passed with half the nation's governments refusing to participate.

stories.title: ‘Fossil-fuel imperialism’: Trump’s hankering for Iranian oil runs deep
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated he wants to "take the oil in Iran" by seizing a key export hub, echoing rhetoric he has used for over a decade. Experts characterize this as disregard for international law and a form of "fossil-fuel imperialism."

stories.title: ‘Human tragedy’: Leqaa Kordia on how ICE jail echoes life in occupied Palestine
stories.summary: Palestinian immigrant Leqaa Kordia, released after a year in a Texas ICE detention center, told the Guardian she sees similarities between conditions in ICE custody and life under Israeli occupation. She was detained following her arrest at a protest against Israel's war in Gaza.

stories.title: Pope Leo celebrates first Easter amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Easter as pontiff amid the ongoing Middle East war. His "Urbi et Orbi" blessing was anticipated to address both spiritual and political themes related to the conflict.

stories.title: Iraq seal FIFA World Cup return after 40 years; Turkiye end 24-year drought
stories.summary: Iraq qualified for the FIFA World Cup for the first time in 40 years by defeating Bolivia 2-1 in an intercontinental playoff in Mexico. Iraq will play in Group I alongside France, Senegal, and Norway. Turkey also ended a 24-year World Cup absence.

stories.title: Pentagon, Boeing announce plan to triple Patriot PAC-3 seeker production
stories.summary: The Pentagon and Boeing announced a seven-year framework agreement to triple production of Patriot PAC-3 missile seekers. The deal follows a similar January agreement with PAC-3 prime contractor Lockheed Martin to expand overall interceptor production capacity.

stories.title: Can Russia help fill the global energy gap?
stories.summary: Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz linked to the Iran conflict have driven up global crude oil prices. The higher prices have boosted Russia's energy export revenues, raising questions about its role in filling the global energy gap.

stories.title: Israel and Egypt: Frosty neighbors' ties tested by Iran war, but remain stable
stories.summary: Israel and Egypt find themselves aligned during Israel's Operation Roaring Lion against Iran. Analysts note that while bilateral ties remain stable, the post-war period could test the relationship between the two neighbors.

stories.title: Israel strikes drug factory in Iran, says it made fentanyl for chemical weapons R&D
stories.summary: Israel struck a pharmaceutical factory in Iran, claiming it produced fentanyl for chemical weapons research and development. Iran said the facility manufactured cancer medications. The IDF also announced it killed a senior Quds Force engineer and would target all critical Iranian arms industry assets.

stories.title: Russian women decry plans to therapise them into having children
stories.summary: Russia faces a demographic crisis with fertility rates at 1.4 children per woman. Russian women are pushing back against government plans to use therapy as a means of encouraging them to have more children.

stories.title: Reverse exodus: How the Iran war turned Egypt's Taba into Israelis’ escape route
stories.summary: Thousands of Israelis and tourists have been leaving Israel through the Taba border crossing into Egypt amid the war with Iran. The mass departure has been described as a modern-day reverse Exodus.

stories.title: ‘Infrastructure is the weapon’: Inside the race to build portable interceptor factories
stories.summary: Defense startups are developing portable, shipping-container-sized production lines for interceptor drones amid surging global demand driven by the Iran conflict. The effort reflects a growing emphasis on decentralized, rapidly deployable manufacturing infrastructure for air-defense systems.

stories.title: Ireland allocates additional €40.3 million in humanitarian aid to Ukraine
stories.summary: Ireland announced an additional €40.3 million in humanitarian and stabilization aid to Ukraine. The allocation brings Ireland's total assistance for the year to its highest level since Russia's full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: Starmer insists 'this is not our war' as Iran weighs up attacking UK bases
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer declared that the Iran war is "not our war" as Iran reportedly considered attacking British military bases. Starmer outlined a plan for Britain to emerge from the crisis stronger but provided no specific details.

stories.title: Slain soldier considered missing since 1948 found in mass grave in north — IDF
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it identified the remains of Pvt. Dov Parmet, a soldier missing since 1948, in a mass grave near Maoz Haim. Parmet was killed in fighting with Syrian-Lebanese forces near Kibbutz Malkia and was buried alongside 16 others.

stories.title: The Passover playbook: Jerusalem activities the whole family can rally around during war
stories.summary: Jerusalem announced Passover holiday activities for families, subject to Home Front Command instructions due to the ongoing war. Organizers warned that events could face last-minute changes depending on the security situation.

stories.title: Russia claims to take full control of Ukraine’s Luhansk region
stories.summary: Russia claimed it has taken full control of Ukraine's Luhansk region, part of the broader industrial Donbas area. Ukraine did not immediately comment on the Kremlin's assertion of the territorial advance.

stories.title: Russia demands France release woman arrested for suspected espionage
stories.summary: Moscow demanded the release of Anna Novikova, a Russian-French dual national detained in France on suspicion of espionage. Novikova is accused of attempting to obtain information related to French economic interests.

stories.title: French President Macron visits Japan to discuss the energy crisis
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron traveled to Tokyo to meet Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The leaders discussed the economic fallout from the war on Iran, including the energy crisis affecting both nations.

stories.title: Iranian Red Crescent: Over 115,000 civilian units damaged in attacks
stories.summary: Iran's Red Crescent reported that over 115,000 civilian structures—including residential, medical, and relief centers—have been damaged in U.S.-Israeli attacks. A significant share of damage was in Tehran province, and some 1,526 people have been pulled from rubble.

stories.title: For Passover, an interactive map brings the haggadah down to earth
stories.summary: Product management expert Alon Gildoni and Weizmann Institute professor Ron Milo created an interactive map tracing the Exodus story across real-world locations. The tool was developed as a resource for the Passover seder.

stories.title: Trump war: Could end in two, three weeks, Israel strikes Tehran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated the ongoing Middle East war could conclude within two to three weeks. The White House also announced that Trump would deliver a national address, as Israeli forces carried out strikes on Tehran.

stories.title: How the Exodus story subverts pharaonic texts to mock ancient Egypt
stories.summary: Bar-Ilan University scholar Joshua Berman curated a new haggadah titled "Echoes of Egypt" exploring how the biblical Exodus narrative reinterprets and subverts ancient Egyptian texts. Berman argues the biblical account deliberately appropriates elements of pharaonic culture.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran president wants ceasefire, no response from Tehran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed on social media that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire, stipulating the Strait of Hormuz must first be reopened. Iran struck an oil tanker near Qatar and hit Kuwait's airport on Wednesday while US air strikes continued to target Tehran. Iran did not immediately respond to Trump's claim.

stories.title: Blasts reported in Damascus
stories.summary: Syrian state television reported blasts in the capital Damascus and surrounding areas. No further details on the source or targets of the explosions were immediately available.

stories.title: Nighttime attack is Russia’s response to peaceful diplomatic efforts, says Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky characterized a massive Russian drone attack on the night of April 1 as Moscow's response to peaceful diplomatic efforts. Those efforts had included proposals for an energy truce and an Easter ceasefire.

stories.title: Russia’s Defense Ministry says it has completed capture of Luhansk region, but Ukrainian forces hold a small stretch of territory
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry claimed its forces have taken full control of the territory corresponding to the self-proclaimed Luhansk People's Republic, according to the Interfax news agency. However, Ukrainian forces still hold a small stretch of territory in the area.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia executes prominent businessman over participation in 2011 Qatif protests
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia executed businessman Saud al-Faraj, 42, over his participation in the 2011 anti-government protests in Qatif. A rights group said he was allegedly tortured into confessing and had been motivated to protest against injustices.

stories.title: Honeywell, Odys Aviation team up on airborne C-UAS program
stories.summary: Honeywell and Odys Aviation announced a partnership to develop an airborne counter-unmanned aircraft system. The program will integrate Honeywell's SAMURAI detection and intercept system with Odys Aviation's Laila aircraft to defend against drone threats.

stories.title: Russia imposing ban on all gasoline exports due to Iran war
stories.summary: Russia announced a ban on all gasoline exports in response to the ongoing Iran war. The move reflects the conflict's widening impact on global energy markets.

stories.title: The war against Iran is anything but over, and Passover can be no complacent celebration of freedom
stories.summary: The article argues the war against Iran remains far from concluded, citing ongoing nuclear dangers, missile threats, and proxy forces. It frames the Passover holiday as a moment for vigilance rather than complacent celebration of freedom for Israel and the Jewish people.

stories.title: Russians Lose Access to Apple ID Mobile Payments
stories.summary: Russian users lost access to Apple ID mobile payments, and Russian state media reported the government is pressuring Apple to restore Russian apps to its App Store after their removal due to Western sanctions.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills four family members in southern Lebanon: reports
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a home in Houmine El Tahta in southern Lebanon killed four members of the same family, including a husband, wife, and their two daughters. Israel has launched a ground invasion into parts of southern Lebanon while conducting overnight strikes on southern Beirut that killed at least seven people.

stories.title: Doctor’s son says father confessed he ‘tried to kill’ wife after cheating claim
stories.summary: In a Hawaii murder trial, 19-year-old Emile Konig testified that his father, doctor Gerhardt Konig, confessed via FaceTime that he had "tried to kill" his wife Arielle during a cliffside attack on Oahu on March 24, 2025.

stories.title: Is Israel a regional power or is its military prowess overhyped?
stories.summary: Analyst Rami Nasrallah argues that Israel's claim to regional power status is undermined by its heavy dependence on the United States and the continued occupation of Palestinian territories. The piece questions whether Israel's military campaigns truly demonstrate strength.

stories.title: US church launches search for new HKIS school head amid legal row with operator
stories.summary: The Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod, co-founder of Hong Kong International School, announced it would lead the search for a new school head, accusing the school's operator of failing to nominate candidates since 2022 and creating a risk of leadership disruption.

stories.title: Brussels urges EU states to 'coordinate' in face of oil price hike
stories.summary: The European Commission urged EU member states to make coordinated preparations to secure oil supplies amid surging energy prices driven by the Middle East conflict. U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory actions have disrupted global markets and pushed energy costs sharply higher.

stories.title: ‘Feels like a dream’: GB’s blossom season brings calm in a troubled world
stories.summary: Visitors to Gilgit-Baltistan's spring cherry and apricot blossom season are finding respite from global tensions, including the Middle East conflict and rising costs. The region's scenic foothills offer a contrast to the stress of ongoing wars and economic pressures.

stories.title: Russian forces strike car in Kherson with drone: Two dead, one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped an explosive device from a drone onto a car in Kherson, killing two female passengers and injuring the driver.

stories.title: US Trump says will be leaving Iran 'very soon'
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated the military could conclude its Iran offensive within two to three weeks and plans to transfer responsibility for securing the Strait of Hormuz to countries that depend on it for oil and shipping. The White House announced a prime-time presidential address on the war.

stories.title: Anti-government protesters boost rallies against war as support for fighting slips
stories.summary: Anti-government protests in Israel have grown as public support for the war on Iran shows signs of slipping. Antiwar groups are seeking to attract anti-Netanyahu moderates, though ongoing missile threats have kept some potential demonstrators at home.

stories.title: NASA set for first crewed moon return in over half a century
stories.summary: NASA is preparing to launch its Artemis II mission, which will send astronauts toward the Moon for the first time in over 53 years. The mission serves as a key test flight supporting broader lunar exploration goals as the U.S. seeks to maintain its lead in space amid growing competition from China.

stories.title: Kremlin says Zelensky should immediately order Ukrainian forces to withdraw from Donbas
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated at a briefing that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky should have ordered Ukrainian forces to withdraw from the Donbas region immediately, saying the decision should have been made "yesterday."

stories.title: Lebanon faces growing displacement crisis
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that Lebanon is experiencing a cycle of coercive displacement as more than one million people have fled Israeli attacks. The growing displacement crisis is straining the country's resources.

stories.title: What does the China-Pakistan plan for the Iran crisis mean for a post-war order?
stories.summary: China and Pakistan issued a joint five-point plan on the Iran crisis calling for a ceasefire and renewed diplomacy. Chinese analysts described the initiative as an early effort to shape the post-war Middle East order amid growing strain on the US-dominated regional security framework.

stories.title: Gulf allies privately make the case to Trump to keep fighting Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are privately urging President Donald Trump to continue military operations against Iran, arguing that Tehran has not been sufficiently weakened by the monthlong U.S.-led bombing campaign. The lobbying effort was described by U.S., Gulf, and Israeli officials.

stories.title: Philippines seeks Iran talks for safe passage of vessels through Hormuz amid energy crisis
stories.summary: The Philippines is seeking talks with Iran to secure safe passage for Philippine-bound tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro and Energy Secretary Sharon Garin met Iranian Ambassador Yousef Esmaeilzadeh to discuss energy cooperation amid an ongoing energy crisis.

stories.title: US public media under pressure from White House
stories.summary: U.S. public media outlets face increasing pressure under President Donald Trump's second term, including verbal attacks, restrictions on press credentials, and financial threats. Outlets reliant on federal funding are particularly vulnerable as the White House seeks to influence reporting and label critical journalists as adversaries.

stories.title: Is Pakistan setting up a buffer zone in Afghanistan?
stories.summary: Tensions along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border are escalating amid reports that the Pakistani government is attempting to establish control over parts of Afghan territory. The developments have raised questions about whether Pakistan is creating a buffer zone inside Afghanistan.

stories.title: U.S. report flags high import duties, non-tariff barriers in India
stories.summary: A U.S. government report flagged India's high import duties and non-tariff barriers as trade concerns. The report also alleged that India modifies tariff rates on an ad hoc basis through gazette notifications without providing opportunity for public comment.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Govt Repatriates 1,230 Citizens From Niger
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government repatriated 1,230 stranded Nigerian citizens from the Republic of Niger. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed the operation.

stories.title: West Africa: CDD Unveils 5-Year Plan to Tackle Democratic Decline, Insecurity in West Africa
stories.summary: The Centre for Democracy and Development unveiled a five-year plan to address democratic decline and insecurity in West Africa. The initiative cites the resurgence of military coups and constitutional manipulations by civilian leaders in countries including Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea, and Togo.

stories.title: How Canada's double standards on Iran put the world at risk
stories.summary: The article examines what it characterizes as Canada's contradictory positions regarding the Iran conflict in the context of Prime Minister Mark Carney's January Davos speech calling for a rules-based international order. It argues Canada's stance on the war undermines the values Carney espoused.

stories.title: BREAKING: Russia attacks Ukrainian regions bordering Poland and Hungary with nearly 650 drones
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 650 drones targeting Ukrainian regions bordering NATO members Poland and Hungary. The strikes on western Ukraine came one week after a Russian attack killed a father and daughter outside a maternity hospital.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Tigray Agenda Gathering Forum Opens in Addis Ababa
stories.summary: The Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission launched its first agenda-gathering consultation forum for stakeholders from the Tigray region in Addis Ababa. The forum is part of a broader national dialogue process.

stories.title: Ukraine claims near-90% air-defense success in March as attacks increase
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense reported a nearly 90% success rate for its air-defense systems in March, even as the frequency of incoming attacks increased. Officials said defensive performance has improved despite the escalating pace of strikes.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia, Russia Cement Nuclear Energy Cooperation With New Strategic Roadmap
stories.summary: Ethiopia's Foreign Affairs Minister Gedion Timothewos held talks in Addis Ababa with Nikolay Spassky, Deputy Director General of Russia's Rosatom State Corporation. The two sides agreed on a new strategic roadmap to deepen cooperation in nuclear energy development.

stories.title: DR Congo qualify for World Cup: 'Amidst pain and war, this victory makes us proud’
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo qualified for the FIFA World Cup for the first time since 1974 after a 1-0 play-off victory over Jamaica. Fans in Kinshasa celebrated the milestone achievement.

stories.title: ‘Permanent scar’: Iran minister on US-Israeli attacks on monuments
stories.summary: Iran's cultural heritage minister told Al Jazeera that U.S.-Israeli attacks have damaged 56 cultural and heritage sites across the country. The minister described the destruction as a deliberate assault on Iran's national identity.

stories.title: Uganda: Museveni, World Bank Delegation Discuss Strategic Development Priorities
stories.summary: Ugandan President Museveni met with a World Bank delegation led by Qimiao Fan, Division Director for Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, and Uganda. The discussions focused on strategic development priorities for the country.

stories.title: Support for Ukraine is ‘turning critical, badly’—the warning comes from its most committed corner
stories.summary: Support for Ukraine is reportedly weakening even among its most committed backers. Estonian members of the European Parliament have voiced warnings that backing for Kyiv is turning critical, signaling a potential shift in allied resolve.

stories.title: US to send dozens of farm companies to the Philippines in April trade mission
stories.summary: The United States plans to send dozens of farm companies to the Philippines in an April trade mission. The Philippines ranks as the tenth-largest market for U.S. agricultural and food products.

stories.title: 9 people missing after explosion and fire at Russian chemical plant, Sibur says
stories.summary: An explosion and fire struck the Nizhnekamskneftekhim chemical plant in Russia, leaving nine people missing. Plant owner Sibur said the missing include employees of contractor organizations, and rescuers are conducting a search.

stories.title: Russian forces attack two villages in Chernihiv region with drones; damage reported
stories.summary: Russian strike drones hit two villages in the Novhorod-Siverskyi community of Ukraine's Chernihiv region overnight, destroying a house and an administrative building.

stories.title: Trump says US strongly considering NATO exit, Telegraph newspaper says
stories.summary: President Trump told the Telegraph newspaper that the U.S. is strongly considering exiting NATO, describing the alliance as a "paper tiger." He said withdrawal was "beyond reconsideration" after allies failed to support U.S. military action against Iran.

stories.title: Strikes on Iranian steel mills deal painful blow to economy
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli strikes hit Iran's two largest steel plants, likely impairing Tehran's war-making capacity. Analysts warn the damage could also inflict lasting harm on Iran's broader economy.

stories.title: Iran war: Strikes on steel deal painful blow to economy
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli forces struck Iran's two largest steel mills, dealing a significant blow to Tehran's war-making capacity. Analysts warn the strikes could also cause irreversible damage to Iran's broader economy.

stories.title: South Africa: South Africans Pay More for Water and Security After Fuel Increase
stories.summary: South Africa experienced sharp fuel price increases, with diesel rising by R7.51 and petrol by R3.06, after oil flows from the Middle East were disrupted. Security companies and water suppliers have begun charging extra fees, while taxi associations warned of potential fare increases.

stories.title: Third drone in a week comes down in Finland, authorities reportedly believe it flew in from Ukrainian territory
stories.summary: Finland's Border Guard recovered a crashed drone on the ice of Lake Pyhäjärvi in the municipality of Parikkala, near the Russian border — the third such incident in a week. Finnish authorities believe the drone flew from Ukrainian territory and was carrying a warhead. The National Bureau of Investigation has opened a criminal inquiry.

stories.title: What the Iran war reveals about Nato’s appetite for conflict over Taiwan
stories.summary: The US-led attack on Iran without consulting European NATO allies has exposed doubts about the alliance's willingness to support conflicts it did not collectively choose. Analysts say the episode raises questions about NATO's appetite for potential confrontation over Taiwan.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces repel largest Russian motorized assault on Sloviansk sector this year
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces repelled the largest Russian motorized assault on the Sloviansk sector recorded since the beginning of the year.

stories.title: No promises this will be Israel’s ‘last war’, says Israeli foreign minister
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar stated that while Israel's adversaries can still launch attacks, they do not pose an existential threat. He said Israel must remain vigilant and declined to promise the current conflict would be the country's last war.

stories.title: Trump to outline endgame as Washington debates Iran war’s next phase
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was scheduled to address the nation on Wednesday to provide an update on the Iran conflict, fueling speculation he may declare an end to the five-week war. Trump previously told reporters that U.S. forces would likely leave Iran within two to three weeks, even without a formal agreement.

stories.title: After the Iran war: A turning point for Iraq's political order?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that the war involving Iran and the United States could fundamentally reshape Iraq's political landscape. Iraq faces altered relationships with both Tehran and Washington, alongside internal power struggles among domestic factions.

stories.title: Israel says air defences responding to missile from Yemen
stories.summary: Israel's air defense systems intercepted a missile fired from Yemen. Israeli media reported no casualties or damage from the incident.

stories.title: Africa: World Bank, Partners Unveil Private Sector Council to Boost Electricity, Jobs in Africa
stories.summary: The World Bank Group, the African Development Bank, and The Rockefeller Foundation launched the Mission 300 Private Sector Council. The initiative aims to mobilize billions in private investment to connect 300 million people across Africa to electricity by 2030 while creating jobs.

stories.title: Australia’s Albanese urges public transport amid war shock
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned that war-driven fuel supply disruptions could cause elevated petrol prices for months. He urged Australians to use public transport to cope with the surge in fuel costs.

stories.title: Taiwan’s KMT chair Cheng Li-wun to honour Sun Yat-sen on landmark mainland China trip
stories.summary: Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun will visit mainland China next week, traveling to Shanghai and then Nanjing to pay tribute at the mausoleum of Sun Yat-sen, founder of the Republic of China and a symbol of shared history between Taiwan and the mainland.

stories.title: British gunners are first to get ‘ace’ title for downing UAVs
stories.summary: Four British servicemen became the first to earn the "ace" designation for downing unmanned aerial vehicles, each having destroyed at least five Iranian drones during Middle East operations. The honor dates back to a World War II tradition for aerial combat achievements.

stories.title: Former Russian Finance Ministry official jailed on charges of sexual violence against child
stories.summary: A Moscow court ordered the pretrial detention of a former Russian Finance Ministry official on charges of violent sexual acts against a child under the age of 14, according to the Russian outlet RBC.

stories.title: French peacekeeping troops in Lebanon subject to 'unacceptable intimidation' -junior minister
stories.summary: France's junior army minister condemned what he called "absolutely unacceptable intimidation" against French peacekeeping troops serving with UNIFIL in Lebanon. Indonesia separately called for a UN investigation into the deaths of three of its UNIFIL peacekeepers following Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan - Rebels Using Sexual Violence in Darfur As 'War Weapon', Says MSF
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) released a major report accusing Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and allied militias of using sexual violence as a weapon of war in Darfur. The report states the violence is being used systematically to control civilian populations.

stories.title: Syrian President Sharaa says no involvement in Iran war unless 'targeted'
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa stated during a visit to London that Damascus would remain uninvolved in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran unless Syria itself is attacked. He stressed Syria's desire to avoid new conflict after 14 years of civil war.

stories.title: Ghana: Supreme Court to Hear Arguments in Wesley Girls Religious Rights Case April 21
stories.summary: Ghana's Supreme Court is scheduled to hear arguments on April 21 in a case challenging alleged discriminatory religious practices against Muslim students at Wesley Girls' Senior High School. The suit concerns religious rights at the institution.

stories.title: Lebanon: At least nine killed in Israeli strikes on south Beirut
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on south Beirut killed at least nine people, with an early morning attack in Jnah destroying several vehicles and sparking a large fire. A separate strike targeted a vehicle in the nearby town of Khaldeh.

stories.title: Trump says seriously weighing bolting NATO over allies’ failure to join Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump said he is seriously considering leaving NATO, calling the alliance a "paper tiger" after European allies refused to join the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. UK Prime Minister Starmer defended NATO as the greatest alliance the world has ever seen.

stories.title: UN peacekeepers in Lebanon were killed by roadside bomb
stories.summary: Three Indonesian peacekeepers serving with the United Nations mission in Lebanon were killed by a roadside bomb. Five other UN personnel were wounded in the attack.

stories.title: Sudan: There is No Safe Place for Women in Darfur - MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières released a report documenting the increasing use of sexual violence as a weapon of war in Sudan's Darfur region. MSF's emergency coordinator described deteriorating humanitarian conditions affecting women both in active conflict zones and beyond the frontlines.

stories.title: How are NATO allies pushing back against Trump’s Iran war demands?
stories.summary: President Trump said he is considering withdrawing the United States from NATO after allied nations resisted joining the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. NATO allies have pushed back against Trump's demands for cooperation in the conflict.

stories.title: Starmer says UK to host multi-nation meeting on Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced that Britain will host a meeting of 35 nations to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the ongoing war, halting vital global oil and gas shipments.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Beirut kill Hezbollah commander for Iraq
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in the Jnah area of Beirut killed Hezbollah's top commander for Iraq military affairs, Yousef Hashem, according to Lebanese security and Hezbollah sources. He was reportedly in a meeting inside a tent near several vehicles at the time of the strike.

stories.title: Huge fire after drone attack hits engine oil warehouse in Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a massive fire at an engine oil storage facility in Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan region. The regional capital Erbil hosts a major U.S. consulate and an airport with military advisors, both of which have been regularly targeted since the war began.

stories.title: Qiushi reaffirms China’s trade-rebalance push, calls old export-led growth ‘unsustainable’
stories.summary: China's top Communist Party journal Qiushi reaffirmed Beijing's push to rebalance trade away from export-driven growth, calling the old model unsustainable. The article cited rising global protectionism and geopolitical tensions as adding urgency to the economic shift.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: The Navy’s MUSV pivot; NGA taps Vantor for $2.3M spy satellite contract; and a bit more
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy is pivoting its approach to medium unmanned surface vessels (MUSVs), while the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency awarded Vantor a $2.3 million spy satellite contract. Additional defense business developments were also noted.

stories.title: Drone attack targets Kuwait airport, fuel tanks on fire
stories.summary: An Iranian drone attack targeted Kuwait's airport, setting fuel tanks on fire. Iran has launched missiles and drones at Israel and U.S. allies in the Gulf since the beginning of the conflict.

stories.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Crimea, killing 29, defence ministry says
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed into a cliff in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board, including six crew members and 23 passengers. Russia's defence ministry said the crash may have been caused by a technical malfunction after communication was lost during a planned flight.

stories.title: Japan, France to draw road map for supply of critical minerals
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to develop a road map for critical minerals supply cooperation amid China's dominance of global rare earths. They also committed to close communication on Middle East de-escalation and launched a high-level AI dialogue.

stories.title: Drone attack leaves large part of Sumy region without power, outages hit three other regions
stories.summary: A massive Russian drone attack caused widespread power outages across Ukraine's Sumy region as of the morning of April 1. Consumers in three additional regions also lost electricity as a result of the strikes.

stories.title: UK PM says war on Iran will impact Britain’s future
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated that the war on Iran will have significant implications for Britain's future. Starmer addressed the nation but offered few specific policy details on how the government would respond.

stories.title: Passover under fire: Israelis balance fatigue with cautious hope after month of war
stories.summary: Israelis marked Passover amid ongoing conflict with Iran, balancing war fatigue with cautious hope after a month of fighting. Public support for the military operation, dubbed Operation Roaring Lion, reportedly remains high despite the toll on daily life.

stories.title: Liberia: Nimbaians Panic As Guinean Army Chief Enters Ganta
stories.summary: Residents of Ganta in Nimba County, Liberia, grew uneasy after a Guinean army chief entered the town. Authorities described the visit as a routine military engagement, but locals linked it to ongoing Liberia-Guinea border tensions in Lofa County.

stories.title: Passover candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: Passover candle lighting times were published for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Iran recruiting teenagers for Tehran checkpoints
stories.summary: Iran's security forces are recruiting teenagers as young as 12 to operate checkpoints in Tehran. The measure comes amid the ongoing conflict and heightened domestic security operations.

stories.title: West Bank strikes over Palestinian-only death penalty
stories.summary: Palestinians across the occupied West Bank launched a general strike after Israel passed a law allowing the death penalty for Palestinian prisoners. The strike, observed in cities including Hebron, drew condemnation from human rights groups and multiple countries.

stories.title: US Supreme Court to hear constitutional test of birthright citizenship
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear a constitutional challenge to President Trump's executive order seeking to end birthright citizenship. Advocates warned the case could have far-reaching consequences for immigrants in the United States.

stories.title: Israel pushing Trump to expand attacks on Iran's infrastructure
stories.summary: Reports indicate Israeli officials are urging President Trump to expand military strikes against Iranian infrastructure, arguing it would be the quickest path to ending the war.

stories.title: Ukraine files extradition request with Israel for Midas suspects—outcome far from certain
stories.summary: Ukraine filed an extradition request with Israel for suspects in the Midas case, but the outcome remains uncertain. Both suspects hold Israeli citizenship, and Israel has a longstanding policy of rarely extraditing its own nationals.

stories.title: Umerov meets Turkish officials on talks with Russia and Ukrainian POWs
stories.summary: Ukraine's Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council Rustem Umerov met with Turkish ministers and an advisor to President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Turkey. Discussions focused on the negotiation process with Russia and the return of Ukrainian prisoners of war.

stories.title: At Least 30 Dead After Russian Military Transport Plane Crashes in Annexed Crimea
stories.summary: A Russian military transport plane crashed in a mountainous forest area near Simferopol in annexed Crimea, killing at least 30 people. Russia's Defense Ministry attributed the crash to a likely technical malfunction.

stories.title: Australian PM Albanese: War's economic shock will be felt for months, urges using public transport
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned that the economic shock from the war would be felt for months and urged citizens to use public transport. Australia imports about 90% of its fuel and has experienced price surges and localized shortages due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: Iraq celebrates qualification for FIFA World Cup 2026
