stories.summary: Pope Leo issued a direct appeal to President Donald Trump from Castel Gandolfo, Italy, urging him to seek an "off-ramp" to end the war in Iran as the regional conflict expands.

stories.title: US lawmaker says American families 'paying the price' for 'war of choice'
stories.summary: US Democratic Senator Chris Coons criticized the war with Iran as a "war of choice," saying American families are bearing rising costs in fuel, groceries, and utilities. He called on the Trump administration to clarify the conflict's rationale and timeline.

stories.title: Iraqi armed group warns US against using Kuwait for Iran attack
stories.summary: Iraqi armed group Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada warned the US against using Kuwait as a staging ground for a ground invasion of Iran, saying such action would escalate the conflict into an all-out regional war.

stories.title: China-Pakistan five-point plan to end Iran war
stories.summary: China and Pakistan jointly unveiled a five-point peace plan on Tuesday aimed at restoring stability in the Persian Gulf. The initiative comes after five weeks of US-Israeli military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Hezbollah says 'fierce clashes' ongoing in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah reported fierce clashes with Israeli troops near the town of Chama in southern Lebanon. The group also claimed rocket attacks on Israeli soldiers near El Qantara and strikes on targets in northern Israel, including near Haifa and Safed.

stories.title: Hegseth says ‘no punishment’  for Army pilots who flew near Kid Rock’s house
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said there would be no punishment for Army pilots who flew near musician Kid Rock's residence. The pilots had previously been reported as suspended over the incident.

stories.title: Army suspends helicopter aircrew that flew near Kid Rock's house, official says
stories.summary: March 31 - The U.S. Army has suspended the aircrew of two Apache attack helicopters that flew near the house of singer Kid Rock, seemingly in support of the vocal backer of U.S. President Donald Trump

stories.title: Global protests condemning Israel’s new death penalty law for Palestinians
stories.summary: Protests took place globally against an Israeli bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for certain Palestinian detainees.

stories.title: Iran says Elon Musk’s Starlink now 'legitimate target', state media reports
stories.summary: Iran declared Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet system a legitimate military target, with state media mapping its infrastructure across Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE. Use of Starlink is restricted in Iran and carries prison sentences.

stories.title: US warns Americans in Saudi Arabia to shelter in place after threats
stories.summary: The U.S. government warned American citizens in Saudi Arabia to shelter in place, citing potential threats against hotels, U.S. businesses, and U.S. educational institutions.

stories.title: Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone
stories.summary: Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone after reports emerged that he had briefed Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on efforts to lift EU sanctions on Gulbahor Ismailova, the sister of sanctioned Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov.

stories.title: Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone
stories.summary: Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó accused foreign intelligence services of tapping his phone after reports emerged that he had briefed Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov on efforts to lift EU sanctions against Gulbahor Ismailova, sister of sanctioned Russian oligarch Alisher Usmanov.

stories.title: US judge says Trump administration can demand list of Jews at Penn for antisemitism probe
stories.summary: A US federal judge ruled that the Trump administration can request a list of Jewish students at the University of Pennsylvania as part of an antisemitism investigation, finding the request consistent with standard discrimination probes.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearing: estate management staff tearfully reject failure to help claims
stories.summary: An independent inquiry in Hong Kong is examining the November 26 fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, which killed 168 people and displaced nearly 5,000 residents. Staff from property management firm ISS EastPoint testified, rejecting claims they failed to assist during the blaze that burned through seven of eight towers over 43 hours.

stories.title: U.S. journalist kidnapped in Baghdad, security forces hunt captors, says Iraqi officials
stories.summary: Iraqi officials report that an American female journalist has been kidnapped in Baghdad. Iraqi security forces are actively pursuing the group responsible for the abduction.

stories.title: Al-Sharaa says Syria to stay out of war on Iran unless attacked
stories.summary: Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa stated that Syria will not enter the US-Israeli war on Iran unless Syria itself is attacked, citing 14 years of prior conflict as sufficient.

stories.title: Machado meets Rubio in Washington, says her return to Venezuela is near
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department on Tuesday, saying her return to Venezuela is near. It was their second meeting since the U.S. military operation that captured Nicolás Maduro in Caracas on January 3.

stories.title: Japan races to limit fallout from Chinese embassy break-in
stories.summary: Japan is working to contain diplomatic fallout after a member of its Self-Defence Forces broke into the Chinese embassy in Tokyo on March 24. National Police Agency Commissioner Yoshinobu Kusunoki called the incident "extremely unusual and serious." Observers note Beijing may use the event to reinforce claims of rising Japanese militarism and anti-China sentiment.

stories.title: How China is building faster high-speed railways using vast underwater tunnels
stories.summary: China completed the underwater excavation of a high-speed rail tunnel stretching over 14 kilometers beneath the Yangtze River. The tunnel will connect Shanghai's Chongming Island with Taicang city in Jiangsu province and is expected to be finished by the end of the year.

stories.title: Trump’s order to limit mail-in voting: does he have the authority?
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order seeking to restrict mail-in voting and create a national list of confirmed eligible voters. The order directs the US Postal Service to send mail-in ballots only to those on the list. Critics describe the move as unconstitutional and expect legal challenges.

stories.title: Top Chinese developers’ losses mount as debt overhaul props up operations
stories.summary: Major Chinese property developers including China Vanke reported mounting operating losses in 2025, with Vanke posting a record 88.56 billion yuan loss. Some headline profits were driven mainly by non-cash gains from debt restructuring rather than operational recovery.

stories.title: Jailed Palestinians fear death by hanging without due process under new Israeli law
stories.summary: RAMALLAH/JERUSALEM, March 31 - Palestinians in the occupied West Bank voiced fears on Tuesday that their jailed relatives could be hanged without due process after Israel adopted a new law making the

stories.title: Burundi says explosions in Bujumbura caused by short-circuit at ammunition store
stories.summary: NAIROBI, March 31 - Explosions heard on Tuesday in Bujumbura, Burundi's commercial capital, were caused by an electrical short-circuit at an ammunition store in a military camp, an army spokesperson s

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran war could end in 'two weeks, maybe three'
stories.summary: President Trump stated Tuesday that the war with Iran could end within two to three weeks. He also said that responsibility for securing the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil shipping channel, should fall to the countries that depend on it rather than the United States.

stories.title: US war on Iran 'last best chance' to avoid a nuclear Islamic regime, Rubio says
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the war on Iran as the "last best chance" to prevent a nuclear-armed Islamic regime. He said a country run by what he called radical Shia clerics must never possess nuclear weapons.

stories.title: US FDA warns of liver injury cases tied to Amgen’s rare disease drug
stories.summary: The agency has identified 76 cases of drug-induced liver injury with evidence suggesting a causal link to Amgen's Tavneos.

stories.title: Argentina: court demands university salary restoration amid faculty strikes
stories.summary: Argentina's Federal Administrative Litigation Chamber upheld an injunction ordering President Javier Milei's government to enforce Law 27,795 on University Funding. The law mandates salary adjustments for public university staff and restoration of student scholarship programs, amid ongoing faculty strikes.

stories.title: Israel refused normalization with Syria last minute, says Al-Sharaa
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Israel backed away from normalization with Syria at the last minute. He stated that although negotiations had reached promising points, Israel ultimately changed its position.

stories.title: Applying Israel’s death penalty law would be a ‘war crime’: UN
stories.summary: The UN rights chief said that the death penalty is profoundly difficult to reconcile with human dignity.

stories.title: Man wounded during Odesa shelling on March 28 dies in hospital
stories.summary: A 76-year-old man who was severely injured during a Russian attack on Odesa on March 28 has died in hospital.

stories.title: Iran Guards say will target U.S. tech firms if more leaders killed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target U.S. technology companies, warning employees at those institutions to leave their workplaces immediately to preserve their lives.

stories.title: Why China is always misunderstood and misrepresented
stories.summary: The article examines longstanding questions about China's historical development, including "Needham's question" about why China did not develop its own scientific and industrial revolutions despite its many early discoveries. It also explores why capitalism did not emerge during the Song dynasty despite favorable economic conditions.

stories.title: Trade war meets tradition: Canadian Jews confront a Manischewitz-free Passover
stories.summary: Canadian Jews faced a Passover without Manischewitz wine due to Canada's ban on American alcohol imposed in response to US tariffs. The ban reportedly created new market opportunities for Israeli wineries in Canada.

stories.title: American journalist kidnapped in Baghdad, police officials say
stories.summary: An American journalist was kidnapped in Baghdad, according to Iraqi police officials. The U.S. State Department confirmed it was aware of the reported abduction.

stories.title: Trump says US could end Iran war in two to three weeks
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters the US could end the war with Iran in two to three weeks. He stated that without a deal, the US could put Iran "into the stone ages" and prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: US Forest Service to move headquarters from Washington DC to Salt Lake City
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will relocate the US Forest Service headquarters from Washington, DC, to Salt Lake City and close its regional offices. The USDA described the reorganisation as a commonsense approach, while critics called it an attack on science and scientists within the federal land management agency.

stories.title: Scottish man linked to gang arrested in Indonesia’s Bali after Interpol issues red alert
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities arrested Steven Lyons, a 45-year-old Scottish man described as a senior figure in an international crime syndicate, at Ngurah Rai International Airport in Bali. He was detained by immigration officers upon arrival from Singapore after being flagged by an Interpol red notice.

stories.title: Tuanzebe sends DR Congo back to World Cup after 52 years
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo qualified for its first FIFA World Cup since 1974 after Axel Tuanzebe scored the winning goal in a 1-0 play-off victory over Jamaica.

stories.title: Japan’s Shibuya to fine litterbugs on the spot from June as visitor numbers surge
stories.summary: Tokyo's Shibuya ward will begin imposing on-the-spot fines of 2,000 yen (US$12.50) for littering starting June 1, abandoning its previous policy of asking visitors to take rubbish home. The change comes as rising visitor numbers have led to increasing litter problems in the district known for its famous scramble crossing.

stories.title: Why Empress Dowager Cixi and people in ancient China used animal faeces in beauty routines
stories.summary: The article discusses historical beauty practices in ancient China, including the use of animal excrement in skincare routines. Empress Dowager Cixi, who effectively ruled the Qing dynasty for nearly 50 years from 1861 to 1908, reportedly incorporated bird droppings into her lifelong skincare regimen.

stories.title: Emergency workers search for victims of Israeli airstrikes on Beirut
stories.summary: Emergency workers in Beirut searched through rubble in the Jnah neighbourhood after Israeli airstrikes struck the area.

stories.title: ‘A law of death that only applies to Palestinians’
stories.summary: Protesters in the United Kingdom called on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to take concrete action against Israel's death penalty legislation targeting Palestinian detainees, rather than merely condemning it.

stories.title: Trump says US will leave Iran in "two or three weeks," claims regime change achieved
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said from the Oval Office that U.S. forces will withdraw from Iran within two to three weeks, claiming the military campaign has achieved its core objectives including regime change.

stories.title: Israel says will reduce French defence imports 'to zero'
stories.summary: Israel announced it will reduce French defence imports to zero, citing disagreements with Paris over policies related to Palestine, airspace restrictions, and defence cooperation.

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten to target US tech firms if more leaders killed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target US technology companies including Apple, Google, and Meta if more Iranian leaders are killed. Iran alleged these companies were involved in tracking individuals targeted for assassination during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Russian military plane crashes into Crimea cliff, killing 29 people
stories.summary: A Russian An-26 military transport plane crashed into a cliff in Crimea, killing all 29 people on board. Russia's defense ministry said contact with the aircraft was lost around 6 p.m. local time Tuesday during a planned flight. A possible technical malfunction is suspected as the cause.

stories.title: ‘I’m not dumb’: Hong Kong’s London trade office manager denies running spy network
stories.summary: Bill Yuen Chung-biu, a manager at Hong Kong's trade office in London, denied in a British national security trial that he ran a spy network targeting Hong Kong activists and UK politicians on behalf of China. He challenged prosecution claims that he operated a "shadow" policing operation two years after his arrest.

stories.title: Trump tells allies ‘get your own oil’, says Iran war could end in 2-3 weeks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told allied nations to source their own oil and claimed the war on Iran could conclude within two to three weeks, amid rising domestic petrol prices.

stories.title: Billion-plus people, three million officials, 33 questions - India begins huge census
stories.summary: India launched its massive census exercise, deploying three million officials across the country to count over a billion people using a 33-question survey conducted in two phases.

stories.title: Angela Buchdahl: This Passover, have faith in the story of the Exodus
stories.summary: Rabbi Angela Buchdahl of New York City's Central Synagogue discussed the challenges facing Zionist rabbinic leaders in North America and finding meaning in Passover amid current events.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF strikes, dismantles missile launchers in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military released footage showing strikes on missile launchers in southern Lebanon. The IDF said the launchers were used in a recent barrage against Israel that injured three people, including a six-year-old child.

stories.title: Iran says no decision taken on US talks despite message exchanges
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran has not made any decision on negotiations with the United States and has not responded to any US proposals. He confirmed that messages have been exchanged with Washington but said all communications are handled through official channels.

stories.title: Will surging fuel prices push Filipinos deeper into credit card debt?
stories.summary: Rising fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict could push more Filipinos deeper into credit card debt, analysts warn. Although credit card ownership in the Philippines remains relatively low, cardholders are using them more intensively as living costs outpace income growth, with receivables growing consistently.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says conflict to end in 2-3 weeks; Kuwait airport hit
stories.summary: US-Israeli strikes continued across Iran, hitting pharmaceutical companies and steel plants in Isfahan and Farokhshar. Separately, Kuwait's international airport was struck during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: War update: 151 clashes on front line, Pokrovsk sector remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 151 combat engagements along the front line, with the Pokrovsk sector seeing the most activity at 51 Russian attacks. Russian forces lost more than 120 troops in the fighting.

stories.title: In Lebanon, UN peacekeepers are caught in the firing line
stories.summary: Three UN peacekeepers were killed in southern Lebanon this week amid the ongoing war between Israel and Hezbollah. The deaths make this conflict one of the deadliest chapters for the UN peacekeeping mission in Lebanon, whose decades-long mandate expires this year.

stories.title: DR Congo beat Jamaica to reach World Cup via intercontinental finals
stories.summary: DR Congo defeated Jamaica 1-0 in an intercontinental World Cup qualifying playoff, with former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe scoring the winning goal in extra time.

stories.title: Syria will stay out of Iran conflict unless it faces aggression
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria will remain out of the Iran-Israel conflict unless directly attacked. He stressed that Damascus seeks to avoid involvement in any new war.

stories.title: Trump says US will be leaving Iran in two to three weeks
stories.summary: Speaking from the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump told reporters that US forces could leave Iran within two to three weeks.

stories.title: Warren Buffett will not commit to more donations to Gates Foundation
stories.summary: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett indicated he would not commit to further donations to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. Buffett said he did not regret past donations but expressed reservations about certain developments at the foundation.

stories.title: Power outage schedules for industrial consumers to be in effect on Wednesday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that power limitation schedules for industrial consumers would be in effect across all regions on Wednesday, April 1, from 12:00 to 17:00.

stories.title: Power outage schedules for industrial consumers to be in effect on Wednesday – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced power outage schedules for industrial consumers on Wednesday, April 1, from 12:00 to 17:00 across all regions of the country.

stories.title: 11-year-old girl seriously wounded in Iranian cluster bomb impact in Bnei Brak
stories.summary: An 11-year-old girl was seriously wounded by an Iranian cluster munition strike in Bnei Brak, central Israel, with at least 13 others injured. Separately, the IDF intercepted a Houthi projectile targeting southern Israel.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in southern Lebanon within an hour
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon killed at least eight people within one hour. A strike on Jebchit in the Nabatieh district killed a pregnant woman and her husband, while a separate raid in Kafra killed two more people.

stories.title: Hegseth says suspensions lifted for helicopter crews who hovered over Kid Rock home
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth lifted suspensions for the crews of two US Army AH-64 Apache helicopters that hovered near singer Kid Rock's home and swimming pool in Tennessee on Saturday. Hegseth declared there would be no punishment or investigation into the incident.

stories.title: UN says initial findings show roadside blast killed Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations said initial findings indicate a roadside blast killed Indonesian peacekeepers serving in Lebanon. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned the attack on the peacekeeping force.

stories.title: 'You're no longer my sister' - rows erupt as war divides Iranian families
stories.summary: Families across Iran are experiencing internal divisions and strained relationships over differing views on the ongoing war, with relatives reportedly cutting ties over political disagreements.

stories.title: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief, elected as Vice-Presidentscvnks
stories.summary: The upper house elected Nan Ni Ni Aye, a regional MP from Karen State with the military-aligned Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP), as another V-P, local media reported

stories.title: Zelensky discusses peace talks and security cooperation with Merz
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz about the peace negotiation process and security cooperation with partners to end the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: 'A million things could go wrong' - why seizing Iran's uranium would be so risky for the US
stories.summary: A former US defence official told the BBC that seizing Iran's uranium stockpile would be one of the most complicated special operations in history, citing enormous logistical and security risks.

stories.title: Israel says it struck rocket launch sites in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military spokesperson Avichay Adraee said the army struck rocket launch sites in southern Lebanon that were used in recent barrages toward Israel. Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,268 people, including over 100 children, since March 2.

stories.title: Pope Leo urges Trump to end war on Iran
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV publicly urged US President Donald Trump to find an off-ramp from the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: More than 200,000 fled Lebanon for Syria in March: UNHCR
stories.summary: Lebanon was pulled into the West Asia conflict in early March when Israeli-U.S. strikes killed Iran's supreme leader and Tehran-backed Hezbollah responded by firing rockets at Israel.

stories.title: Lapid: Netanyahu incapable of reaching victory, is dismantling Israel from within
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu, arguing he is incapable of achieving victory, noting Hamas still controls Gaza, Hezbollah continues firing rockets, and Khamenei remains in power in Iran.

stories.title: German chancellor clarifies Syrian refugee comments after backlash
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz walked back comments about the return of Syrian refugees to their homeland after facing backlash. Economists and politicians had warned that a mass departure of Syrian refugees could have a significant negative economic impact on Germany.

stories.title: US exempts Gulf of Mexico oil drillers from endangered species protections
stories.summary: The Trump administration exempted Gulf of Mexico oil drillers from endangered species protections, citing the need to maintain US energy competitiveness during the ongoing war on Iran.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes Nikopol, leaving 11 injured, including one child
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on Nikopol in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region injured 11 people, including one child.

stories.title: On global tensions and India’s economy
stories.summary: In an economy that imports more than four-fifths of its crude oil, external shocks transmitted through energy prices, shipping route, and volatile commodity markets can significantly reshape fiscal ar

stories.title: EU warns oil and gas prices won’t quickly return to normal after Iran war
stories.summary: The EU's energy commissioner warned that oil and gas prices will not return to normal soon, as the war on Iran continues to disrupt global energy markets.

stories.title: Trump says US-Israeli war on Iran ‘coming to an end’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump told NBC that the US-Israeli war on Iran is "coming to an end." He suggested the fighting would soon be wrapped up but did not provide a specific timeline.

stories.title: Israeli chess player expected a forfeit, her Iranian opponent showed up
stories.summary: Israeli chess player Yarden Bloch expected her Iranian opponent to forfeit their match, as Iranian athletes have often been prevented from competing against Israelis. Instead, the Iranian player showed up to compete.

stories.title: Funerals held for 3 of the soldiers killed fighting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Funerals were held in Israel for three soldiers killed fighting Hezbollah in southern Lebanon: Staff Sgt. Maxsim Entis, 21; Cpt. Noam Madmoni, 22; and Staff Sgt. Ben Cohen, 21.

stories.title: Asia's migrant workers debate if Gulf jobs are worth deadly risk of Iran war
stories.summary: Migrant workers from across Asia are reconsidering employment in Gulf states as Iranian strikes on the region raise safety concerns, threatening livelihoods that support families back home.

stories.title: Tunisian journalist sentenced to two years, union denounces systemic attack on media
stories.summary: A Tunisian court sentenced news website editor Ghassen Ben Khelifa to two years in prison. Tunisia's journalists' union denounced the prosecution as part of a systemic attack on press freedom and free speech in the country.

stories.title: Australia politics live: Chalmers announces support package for businesses hit by fuel crisis including tax relief
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced a support package including tax relief for businesses affected by a fuel crisis. Separately, AI company Anthropic signed a memorandum of understanding with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to support Australia's national AI plan.

stories.title: EU says 'necessary' to reduce fuel demand to cope with crisis
stories.summary: The EU urged member states to reduce fuel demand amid a crisis caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran. The conflict has practically halted maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries a fifth of global crude supplies.

stories.title: Pentagon declines to reaffirm NATO’s collective defence, says up to Trump
stories.summary: The Pentagon declined to reaffirm NATO's Article 5 collective defense commitment, stating the matter was up to President Trump. The move came as Trump criticized NATO member states for not supporting the US during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses consequences of blockade of Strait of Hormuz and countering Russian propaganda with Tajani
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky, during a meeting with Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Antonio Tajani, discussed the consequences of a potential blockade of the Strait of Ho

stories.title: U.S.-Israel targeted major pharmaceutical company: Iran govt
stories.summary: Iran's government stated that US and Israeli strikes damaged one of the country's largest pharmaceutical companies producing anti-cancer, anesthetic, and specialized medicines. The government said the attack on the civilian facility disrupted drug production lines.

stories.title: Lebanon bracing for long-term displacement crisis amid funding crunch, minister says
stories.summary: Lebanese Social Affairs Minister Haneen Sayed said Lebanon is preparing for the possibility that hundreds of thousands of people displaced by Israeli strikes and evacuation orders may not return home in the long term. The country faces a funding shortfall as it confronts a prolonged displacement crisis.

stories.title: Trump says US could end war in Iran in 2 to 3 weeks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated from the White House that the U.S. military campaign against Iran could conclude within two to three weeks. The month-long war has disrupted global energy markets and reshaped Middle Eastern geopolitics.

stories.title: Watch: UNRWA and EU condemn Israel death penalty law
stories.summary: UNRWA and the European Union condemned the Israeli parliament's approval of a death penalty law targeting Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. The law has drawn widespread international criticism.

stories.title: Pope urges Trump to seek ‘off-ramp’ from war on Iran
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV called on US President Donald Trump to find an "off-ramp" to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Speaking near Rome at Castel Gandolfo, the US-born pontiff expressed hope that Trump was seeking ways to reduce the violence.

stories.title: U.S. strikes Isfahan as Iran targets fully loaded oil tanker off Dubai
stories.summary: An Iranian drone struck a Kuwaiti oil tanker in waters off Dubai, sparking a fire that was later extinguished, according to the Dubai Media Office. Separately, US forces struck the Iranian city of Isfahan as hostilities continued in the broader conflict.

stories.title: Europe pushes back on US military operations as concerns over Iran war mount
stories.summary: European nations pushed back against US military operations as concerns over the Iran war mounted. President Trump singled out NATO allies in Europe as unhelpful during the month-long conflict.

stories.title: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear criticizes Gaza ‘genocide’ discourse ‘litmus test’ for Democrats
stories.summary: Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear criticized what he called a "litmus test" around Gaza genocide discourse within the Democratic Party. His remarks reflect growing tension among Democrats over their stances on Israel amid declining support for the country among their base.

stories.title: Explainer-When do attacks on civilian installations amount to war crimes?
stories.summary: Legal experts noted that widening airstrikes on civilian infrastructure in the Iran conflict, including attacks on oil facilities, electricity production sites, and desalination plants, could constitute war crimes. The strikes and threats to target such installations raise questions under international humanitarian law about proportionality and the protection of civilian objects.

stories.title: American journalist kidnapped in Baghdad, suspect detained, US says
stories.summary: The US State Department confirmed that American journalist Shelly Kittleson was kidnapped in Baghdad. Iraqi authorities detained a suspect believed to have links to the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, and the FBI is working to secure her release.

stories.title: Imprisoned Nobel laureate Mohammadi may have had a heart attack
stories.summary: One of Narges Mohammadi's lawyers said the imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate may have suffered a heart attack while held at Zanjan Prison in Iran.

stories.title: Iran Flexes Its Cyber Chops
stories.summary: Hackers linked to the Iranian government are escalating cyberattacks against the United States and Israel as the ongoing military conflict intensifies.

stories.title: Peacekeepers killed by roadside explosion in Lebanon, initial report finds
stories.summary: Two Indonesian UN peacekeepers were killed by a roadside explosion in Lebanon. Their deaths occurred less than a day after another Indonesian peacekeeper was also killed in the country.

stories.title: China’s science awards system is plagued by shadowy practices. Can reforms fix it?
stories.summary: China's science and technology awards system faces accusations of widespread misconduct, including exaggerated achievements, cronyism, and bribery. Critics within academia say these problems remain deeply entrenched despite repeated reform efforts by authorities.

stories.title: Australia’s superb fairywren could be extinct within decades due to climate crisis, researchers say
stories.summary: Researchers tracking superb fairywren populations over nearly 30 years in Canberra's Australian National Botanic Gardens warn the species could go extinct within 30 to 40 years due to climate change impacts on weather patterns.

stories.title: Couple convicted of stealing trade secrets for China loses US citizenship
stories.summary: A federal judge in California's Southern District revoked the U.S. citizenship of Li Chen and Yu Zhou, a naturalized couple from China convicted in 2021 of stealing medical trade secrets and sharing them with China.

stories.title: Kallas on peace talks: Even if US and Russia agree on something, they can not implement it without Europe
stories.summary: EU High Representative Kaja Kallas emphasized the importance of Europe’s role in the peace process regarding Ukraine.

stories.title: Lebanon condemns Israel’s 'clear intention' to impose new occupation of its territory
stories.summary: Lebanon condemned Israeli strikes near Beirut's airport road and warned of Israel's "clear intention" to impose a new occupation. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said troops would occupy parts of southern Lebanon post-war, as the UN Security Council met after three peacekeepers were killed.

stories.title: 'Go take your oil:' Nato fissure erupts over Iran as allies brush off US
stories.summary: Several NATO allies, including Spain, Italy, and Poland, have expressed reluctance to support US attacks on Iran, fearing exposure to broader risks. The disagreement has opened a fissure within the alliance over the conflict.

stories.title: ‘What can you expect from a govt with people like Netanyahu?’: Palestinians horrified by Israel’s new death penalty law
stories.summary: The Israeli parliament approved a law permitting the execution of Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank expressed fear and outrage, with families of detained prisoners joining protests in Ramallah against the legislation.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon killed at least eight people. A strike on al-Najjariya killed at least five, while a separate attack on Srifa in the Tyre district killed three and wounded 19 others.

stories.title: Bennett pledges to restore Israel’s standing, form gov’t with only those who serve - interview
stories.summary: “The next government will be based on a ‘covenant of those who serve,’" said Bennett. "Anyone who can be with me in a tank in Gaza can be with me in the government.”

stories.title: Iran ambassador refuses to leave Lebanon despite expulsion order
stories.summary: Lebanon ordered Iran's ambassador to leave the country, but the Iranian envoy has refused to comply with the expulsion order.

stories.title: Spain's PM labels Israel's death penalty law 'step towards apartheid'
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez condemned the Israeli parliament's approval of a death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks, calling it a "step towards apartheid." The law allows military courts to impose death sentences on Palestinian defendants.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses Ukraine's EU path and European integration coordination with Wadephul
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky and Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul discussed in detail Ukraine's progress toward European Union membership during a meeting.

stories.title: Hamas urges Hezbollah to kidnap Israeli soldiers in wake of Knesset passing death penalty bill
stories.summary: Hamas spokesperson Abu Ubaida of the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades called on Hezbollah to kidnap Israeli soldiers in response to the Israeli Knesset's passage of a death penalty bill.

stories.title: Passover and peoplehood: The ongoing struggle with empire - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between the current US-Israeli conflict with Iran and the ancient Passover narrative of resisting imperial power.

stories.title: Israel to destroy 'all houses' near Lebanon border, defence minister says
stories.summary: Israel's defense minister announced plans to destroy all homes in Lebanese villages near the border and said 600,000 displaced residents of southern Lebanon would not be allowed to return until northern Israel is secure. The minister vowed to inflict destruction comparable to that seen in Gaza.

stories.title: American journalist kidnapped in Baghdad; Iraq says manhunt underway, one detained
stories.summary: Freelance American journalist Shelly Kittleson was abducted in Baghdad after being shoved into a car by unknown assailants. A man claiming to be her contact said an Iran-backed militia was behind the kidnapping, and Iraqi authorities launched a manhunt.

stories.title: Romanian state institutions face 10,000 cyberattacks daily, defence minister says
stories.summary: Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruta disclosed that Romanian state institutions face more than 10,000 cyberattacks daily. The statement highlighted the scale of digital threats targeting the country's government infrastructure.

stories.title: How selective outrage over Iran war exposes the limits of realpolitik
stories.summary: An analysis examines how partisan reactions to the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran reflect selective outrage, noting that some justify the attacks by citing Tehran's destabilizing regional activities through the IRGC's Quds Force.

stories.title: Iran Says It Will Target U.S. Tech Companies in the Middle East
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target U.S. technology companies operating in the Middle East. The warning came as U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signaled a decisive phase ahead in the war.

stories.title: Russian tanker reaches Cuba amid critical energy shortage
stories.summary: A Russian tanker arrived in Cuba carrying enough fuel to cover the island's energy needs for up to ten days. The delivery followed a three-month blockade that had caused a critical energy shortage.

stories.title: UK and France extend talks over new small boats deal
stories.summary: The United Kingdom and France extended negotiations over a deal to combat small-boat migrant crossings in the English Channel. The existing three-year agreement, which funded additional French patrols to intercept smuggling gangs, was set to expire at midnight.

stories.title: ‘I need to leave’: Cuba’s tourism workers reel from US oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's tourism industry has collapsed under the impact of a US oil blockade. Workers including taxi drivers and tour guides are struggling to survive as thousands face economic hardship.

stories.title: International Baccalaureate exams scrapped in UAE amid Iran war
stories.summary: International Baccalaureate exams have been canceled in the United Arab Emirates due to the ongoing Iran war. The UAE also extended distance learning for students until April 17 as the conflict continues to disrupt normal operations in the region.

stories.title: Six-year-old girl dies in hospital in Sumy region after Russian attack on March 28
stories.summary: A six-year-old girl who was injured during a Russian attack on March 28 has died in a hospital in the Sumy region.

stories.title: Next days in Iran war will be ‘decisive’, claims Pentagon chief Hegseth
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed the coming days in the Iran war would be "decisive." Hegseth said he visited US troops in West Asia on March 28 to observe military operations against Iran firsthand.

stories.title: UN aid chief warns of new Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher warned of a potential new Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon, raising concerns about the humanitarian impact in the region.

stories.title: Hijacked car driven to Northern Irish police station contained improvised bomb, police say
stories.summary: Police in Northern Ireland said a hijacked car driven to a police station contained an improvised explosive device. A fast-food delivery driver was forced to stop by two masked men who directed him to drive the vehicle to the station.

stories.title: ‘Of course’ Navy leader ‘concerned’ that Iran conflict diminishes US ability to deter China
stories.summary: Admiral Daryl Caudle, a senior U.S. Navy leader, expressed concern that the Iran conflict is diminishing America's ability to deter China, noting that committing finite military resources to one theater necessarily reduces capacity elsewhere.

stories.title: Pakistan, China issue 5-point initiative for restoring peace in Middle East
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar visited Beijing and met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to discuss regional developments. The two countries issued a five-point initiative calling for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the launch of peace talks to restore stability in the Gulf and Middle East.

stories.title: EU faces 'largest oil supply disruption in history', energy expert says
stories.summary: Energy geopolitics expert Francesco Sassi of the University of Oslo warned that the Iran war has caused the largest oil supply disruption in history. He cautioned that unilateral government actions to secure energy supplies could further increase oil and natural gas costs across Europe.

stories.title: US journalist Shelly Kittleson kidnapped in Baghdad

stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed doubt that Russia plans a general mobilization in the near future, while noting he lacks complete information on the matter. He also suggested that if Russia halts its energy strikes, Ukraine could mirror such a ceasefire.

stories.title: Israeli strike in southern Gaza kills 5-year-old
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike in southern Gaza killed a father and his five-year-old son, according to health officials at Nasser hospital. Nearly 709 Palestinians have been killed since a ceasefire was reached in October, as Israeli strikes have continued almost daily.

stories.title: Iran’s regime remains defiant despite absorbing massive blows from Israel and the US
stories.summary:
While the US insists Tehran is 'effectively neutralized,' experts say the regime is entrenched, looks to 'cause sustained pain and to drive up the costs of the war' for Trump
The post Iran’s reg

stories.title: Italy refuses US aircraft use of Sicily base for Middle East operations, source says
stories.summary: Italy has refused to allow the United States to use the Sigonella air base in Sicily for military operations in the Middle East, according to a source. Local media reported that the US had not sought Italy's authorization beforehand.

stories.title: One month of war on Iran cost Arab countries up to $194bn: UNDP
stories.summary: Even if conflict is 'short but intense', countries like Sudan, Yemen, Lebanon will see major increases in poverty rates.

stories.title: Carol Fesler appeal puts sentence in Rafael Edna hit-and-run case back before court
stories.summary: A French court is reviewing the appeal filed by Carol Fesler in the hit-and-run case involving the death of Rafael Edna in May 2023. The case became a rallying point for concerns about road violence accountability, particularly within Israel's Ethiopian community.

stories.title: Zelensky on Bucha and other war crimes: Path to justice is long, but we push through
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky affirmed that Ukraine is working to ensure accountability for all perpetrators of war crimes, including those committed in Bucha, acknowledging that the path to justice is long.

stories.title: Trump says other countries should 'just take' Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump criticized countries that declined to join the U.S. and Israel's military campaign against Iran, urging other nations to "just take" control of the Strait of Hormuz and seize oil from the strategically vital waterway.

stories.title: Pussy Riot co-founder Nadya Tolokonnikova on her support for Ukraine, her OnlyFans work, and the Council of Europe’s Russia platform
stories.summary: Pussy Riot co-founder Nadezhda Tolokonnikova has been an active participant in the Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly platform for Russian democratic forces in exile. She initiated the platform's first public statement on Russia's responsibility for its aggression in Ukraine and opposed Russia's return to the Venice Biennale.

stories.title: On last day in office, UNRWA head urges probe into alleged IDF killing of nearly 400 workers
stories.summary:
Lazzarini blasts what he calls 'extraordinary level of impunity' for Israeli actions in Gaza; he leaves behind an agency facing 'collapse' amid accusations it has extensive terror ties
The post On las

stories.title: Drone attacks on Ust-Luga port damage oil loading terminal – Reuters
stories.summary: A drone attack on the Russian port of Ust-Luga on the Baltic Sea damaged an oil loading terminal, according to Reuters. The strike is expected to further complicate Russia's oil export operations.

stories.title: Ethiopia rations fuel as shortages hit supplies
stories.summary: Ethiopia began rationing fuel as the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted global energy supplies. Daily diesel supply dropped from 9.2 million litres to 4.5 million litres, and authorities prioritized public transport and essential goods vehicles. Ethiopia imports all its fuel, mainly from the Gulf.

stories.title: Washington questions NATO alliance, as Spain fences off airspace
stories.summary: “When we ask for additional assistance or simple access… we get questions or roadblocks or hesitation,” US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said today when asked about US support to NATO&#82

stories.title: Trump tells affected nations to go to Hormuz and ‘get your oil’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump urged countries affected by the Strait of Hormuz crisis to secure their own oil supplies, stating the U.S. would no longer assist them. He declared Iran had been "essentially decimated" and told nations to go to the strait and take the oil themselves.

stories.title: China and Pakistan issue five-point plan for 'immediate ceasefire' in war on Iran
stories.summary: China and Pakistan issued a joint five-point plan calling for an immediate ceasefire in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar presented the proposal after talks in Beijing. The plan also calls for normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Major explosion at Russian petrochemical plant
stories.summary: A massive explosion occurred at a major petrochemical plant in Russia, killing at least two people and injuring dozens.

stories.title: Holding Water Hostage
stories.summary: Parts of the Middle East — especially around the Persian Gulf — rely on desalinated water. Worst-case scenarios for war in the region have often included attacks on desalination facilities

stories.title: Zelensky deepens defense ties in Middle East as Arab states seek Ukraine’s drone expertise but look to preserve ties with Russia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky toured several Middle Eastern countries from March 26 to 29, signing military cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Plans for similar agreements with the UAE and Jordan were also announced, as Arab states seek Ukraine's drone expertise.

stories.title: Foreign journalist kidnapped in Iraq: Interior Ministry
stories.summary: Iraq's Ministry of Interior says one suspect arrested after 'unknown individuals' kidnap journalist.

stories.title: Nigel Farage’s biggest problem? Donald Trump
stories.summary: Nearly a quarter of voters cite Reform leader’s support for US president as main reason against voting for his partyBy day 31 of the war in the Middle East, Nigel Farage had become somewhat less vocal

stories.title: Merz criticised after calling for Syrians in Germany to ‘go back’ home
stories.summary: The German chancellor has drawn condemnation from NGOs and members of his own governmentFriedrich Merz has drawn condemnation from NGOs and members of his own government after he called for the vast m

stories.title: Iran says will target Apple, Google and Meta if more of its leaders are killed
stories.summary:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday that they would target leading US technology firms like Apple, Google and Meta if more Iranian leaders were killed in “targeted assassinations”.
“These comp

stories.title: Trump says France blocked US military flights bound for Israel
stories.summary:
Trump says France blocked US military flights bound for Israel

    
    

        
    
                US President Donald Trump said France refused to allow US military supply flights heading to Is

stories.title: How Hezbollah is slowing Israel's invasion of south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's ground invasion of southern Lebanon is reportedly being slowed by Hezbollah fighters employing an attrition-based strategy. Despite Israel's superior firepower and sustained aerial bombardment, the advance has faced resistance from Hezbollah forces in the region.

stories.title: UNRWA head seeks investigation into killing of staff in Gaza war
stories.summary: UNRWA Commissioner-General has called for an investigation into the killing of agency staff during the two-year Gaza war. More than 390 UNRWA employees have been killed in the conflict.

stories.title: War update: 88 clashes on front line since morning, Pokrovsk sector remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 88 combat engagements with Russian troops since the start of the day. The Pokrovsk sector in eastern Ukraine remained the most active area along the front line.

stories.title: Iran steps up executions as experts warn state killing being used to suppress political dissent
stories.summary: Iran has escalated executions, with Amnesty International reporting that two people were executed on Monday without advance notice, denying them access to lawyers or family. Experts warn the state is using capital punishment to suppress political dissent.

stories.title: Israel says it will keep control over part of southern Lebanon after war with Hezbollah ends
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Israel intends to maintain control over parts of southern Lebanon after its war with Hezbollah concludes. He also stated that houses in Lebanese villages near the Israeli border would be demolished.

stories.title: Iran media says strikes put desalination plant on Gulf island out of service
stories.summary: Iranian state news agency ISNA reported that Israeli strikes knocked a desalination plant on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf completely out of service. A Health Ministry official said the facility cannot be repaired in the short term.

stories.title: China and Pakistan outline five-point plan to end MidEast war
stories.summary: China and Pakistan jointly proposed a five-point plan to end the ongoing war involving Iran. The plan calls for an immediate cessation of attacks and the initiation of dialogue between the parties involved in the conflict.

stories.title: Exposing the hidden forces in the Iranian war
stories.summary: Journalist Shir Perets examined viral claims and competing narratives surrounding Israel and the war with Iran, seeking to debunk misinformation driving public discourse about the conflict.

stories.title: Leaked UN report reveals Haftar family is smuggling oil and arms in Libya
stories.summary: A leaked UN panel of experts report found that the Haftar family in Libya is smuggling oil and arms. The report identified Arkenu, Libya's first privately owned oil company, as being indirectly controlled by Saddam Haftar, son of Libyan commander Khalifa Haftar.

stories.title: Gazans hold vigil as Israel set to execute Palestinian prisoners
stories.summary: Relatives of Palestinian prisoners held a vigil in Gaza City after the Israeli Knesset passed a law authorizing capital punishment exclusively for Palestinians. The legislation has drawn accusations of discrimination.

stories.title: ‘Get your own oil’: Trump launches tirade against Europe for not joining Iran war
stories.summary: Many countries in Europe have called the conflict illegal, with some blocking Israeli and US planes from moving weapons through their airspaceDonald Trump has launched a tirade against European countr

stories.title: Why Iran believes it can outlast the US
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly preparing for deeper escalation by the United States while maintaining that it is prevailing in the conflict. Analysts are questioning whether the war can be resolved before it expands further across the region.

stories.title: Army aiming for ITEP to reach full qualification by 2028, senior leaders say
stories.summary: U.S. Army leaders said the Improved Turbine Engine Program (ITEP) is now targeting full qualification by 2028. The engine, originally scheduled for delivery in 2022, has faced years of delays due to pandemic-related supply chain disruptions and manufacturing challenges.

stories.title: Kuwait says missiles and drones intercepted over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Kuwait's defence ministry announced it intercepted and destroyed five ballistic missiles and seven drones that entered its airspace over a 24-hour period. The intercepts occurred amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Qatar says ‘ready to help’ with US-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari announced that Qatar is prepared to assist with negotiations between the United States and Iran amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: 8th Corps pioneers “Uber” for strikes — Russians once had three days to flee, now they have “minutes to pray”
stories.summary: Ukraine's 8th Corps developed a rapid strike coordination system likened to a ride-hailing app. The system assigns the nearest available unit to engage detected Russian targets, drastically reducing enemy response time from days to minutes.

stories.title: Powerful explosion occurs at petrochemical plant in Tatarstan, leaving over 50 injured, one dead
stories.summary: A major explosion occurred at the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical facility in Tatarstan, Russia, on March 31. The blast left more than 50 people injured and at least one person dead.

stories.title: UNRWA chief seeks probe into killing of hundreds of staff in Gaza
stories.summary: Outgoing UNRWA Commissioner-General Philippe Lazzarini called for a high-level panel of experts to investigate the killing of more than 390 UNRWA staff during the conflict in Gaza. He made the appeal at a press conference in Geneva on his final day in the role.

stories.title: 'Iran will be at World Cup' and play in US: FIFA's Infantino
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the World Cup as scheduled and will play its matches in the United States. Infantino stated that all aspects of Iran's participation remain on track.

stories.title: Who are the two Arab MKs who voted for Israel death penalty law?
stories.summary: Two Druze Arab members of the Israeli Knesset voted in favor of a death penalty law targeting Palestinians. Their support for the legislation drew widespread international condemnation.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox IDF reserve battalion was not suspended after CNN incident, CEO says
stories.summary: The CEO of the Netzah Yehuda ultra-Orthodox IDF reserve battalion denied reports that the unit had been suspended by IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir following an altercation between reservist soldiers and CNN reporters.

stories.title: Fifa confirms Iran will play at World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup despite the ongoing war and US objections. Iran has sought to relocate its matches to Mexico, and its sports ministry barred teams from traveling to countries deemed hostile. Trump had previously said Iran's participation would not be "appropriate."

stories.title: IRGC 'recruiting child soldiers' in US-Israel war on Iran: HRW
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has been recruiting child soldiers amid the U.S.-Israeli war on the country. The organization cited personnel shortages as a factor driving the IRGC to place children in key security roles.

stories.title: Umerov in Gulf region holds further talks with partners
stories.summary: A delegation from Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council, led by Secretary Umerov, is conducting negotiations with partners in the Gulf region. The talks aim to deepen cooperation and develop long-term strategic agreements.

stories.title: UN diplomat resigns over claims of planned nuclear strike on Iran
stories.summary: Mohamad Safa, a UN representative for the Patriotic Vision Association NGO, resigned from his position after making claims about a planned nuclear strike on Iran. He also alleged that senior UN figures were serving a powerful lobby.

stories.title: Russia gives Ukraine two months to leave Donbas, Zelenskyy says. It has been trying to take the region by force since 2022.
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said Russia issued a two-month ultimatum for Ukraine to leave the Donbas region. Zelenskyy expressed surprise that anyone believes ceding eastern Ukraine would end the war Russia has been waging since 2022.

stories.title: EU tells members to prepare for ‘prolonged disruption’ to energy markets from Iran war
stories.summary: The European Union has instructed member states to prepare for prolonged disruption to energy markets stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran. European gas prices have risen more than 70 percent since the conflict began.

stories.title: EU tells members to prepare for 'prolonged disruption' to energy markets from Iran war
stories.summary: The EU's energy commissioner warned member states to prepare for prolonged disruption to energy markets resulting from the Iran war, ahead of an emergency ministerial meeting in Brussels on Tuesday.

stories.title: Eight children evacuated during Israeli siege on al-Shifa return to Gaza
stories.summary: Eight children who were evacuated during an Israeli siege on al-Shifa hospital in Gaza City have returned to the territory. The toddlers were reunited with family members, some of whom had not seen them since their birth more than two years earlier.

stories.title: US says respects Israel ‘right’ to legislate as death penalty bill for Palestinians widely condemned
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department said it respects Israel's sovereign right to set its own laws after the Israeli parliament introduced the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of killings. The legislation was sharply criticized by European nations and rights groups.

stories.title: ‘Hunuz Dilli Dur Ast’: Climate crisis in the age of war
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws on historical South Asian references to discuss the climate crisis in the context of ongoing wars. It uses the phrase 'Hunuz Dilli Dur Ast' to reflect on human complacency toward distant threats.

stories.title: South Africa launches major security operation to tackle crime and gang violence
stories.summary: South Africa deployed approximately 500 military and police personnel in Cape Town as part of a year-long security operation. The deployment targets gang violence, illegal mining, and organized crime across the Western Cape province.

stories.title: Russia goes after VPNs as ‘great crackdown’ gathers pace
stories.summary: Russia has intensified its crackdown on VPN services as part of broader internet restrictions. The measures are part of the most repressive laws imposed since Soviet times, enacted after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran warns of death penalty, asset seizures for spying, aiding enemies
stories.summary: Iranian media reported more than 1,000 arrests since the start of the war, as Iran warned of the death penalty and asset seizures for those found guilty of spying or aiding enemies.

stories.title: UK sends more troops to Gulf amid Trump jibes over British military role
stories.summary: The UK is increasing its military deployment in the Gulf to 1,000 troops. Defence Secretary John Healey, speaking from Qatar, described the move as a defensive response to an "expanding threat" from Iran, amid criticism from President Trump over Britain's refusal to join offensive operations.

stories.title: UN aid chief warns of new Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher warned that Israel's expanding military operations in southern Lebanon could result in a new occupied territory. He questioned how the international community would respond to such a development.

stories.title: IRGC threatens to target US tech firms in region
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to target more than 15 US technology companies operating in the region, warning staff and nearby residents to evacuate. The IRGC said firms involved in designing and tracking targets using ICT and AI would be considered legitimate targets if more Iranian leaders are killed.

stories.title: KSE-100 gains 1,900 points day after war-driven meltdown
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index rebounded by 1,900.34 points, or 1.29 percent, closing at 148,743.31 on Tuesday. The recovery followed a sharp sell-off the previous day driven by war-related market fears.

stories.title: Israel's new death penalty law marks moral break, sparks discrimination fears, expert says
stories.summary: Israeli criminal and constitutional law scholar Prof. Yoram Rabin described Israel's new death penalty law as a moral rupture and a legally vulnerable measure. Experts have raised concerns that the law creates a discriminatory legal framework.

stories.title: Debris from Iranian missile fell 30 meters from Ukrainian embassy in Israel – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reported that fragments of an Iranian cluster missile landed approximately 30 meters from Ukraine's embassy in Israel on March 31.

stories.title: Fakhar Zaman suspended for two PSL matches for ball-tampering
stories.summary: Pakistan Cricket Board suspended Lahore Qalandars batter Fakhar Zaman for two PSL matches after a ball-tampering incident. The breach occurred during the final over of a match against Karachi Kings, involving Fakhar, captain Shaheen Afridi, and bowler Haris Rauf.

stories.title: Lib Dem mayor forced to resign for sharing Israeli 'false flag' ambulance attack posts
stories.summary: Bharat Pankhania, the mayor of Bath in the United Kingdom, was forced to resign as mayor and as a Liberal Democrat councillor after sharing social media posts alleging an Israeli false flag ambulance attack.

stories.title: Israel vows to occupy large parts of southern Lebanon to expand buffer zone
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to occupy territory south of the Litani River in Lebanon—roughly 19 miles from the border—and destroy homes along the frontier. Defence Minister Israel Katz said some 600,000 displaced residents would be prevented from returning, raising concerns of long-term forced displacement.

stories.title: Estonia detects air threat overnight, defence forces say
stories.summary: Estonia and Latvia detected foreign drone activity near their borders with Russia overnight, their defense forces reported. The incidents represent the latest airspace intrusions unsettling NATO's eastern flank.

stories.title: Three hospital doctors’ groups threaten to coordinate strike action in England
stories.summary: The British Medical Association announced plans to ballot consultants and specialist doctors in England about coordinated strike action alongside resident doctors. The potential industrial action concerns pay and working conditions across the NHS's three main hospital doctor groups.

stories.title: As Trump signals retreat from war, Israel may have to keep fighting Iranian threat
stories.summary: Reports suggest President Trump is signalling a potential withdrawal from the war on Iran, even if Iran's government remains standing and retains its ability to threaten neighbors. For Israel and Gulf states, this could mean continuing military operations independently.

stories.title: Nearly half of tech firms struggling with worker shortages due to Iran war – survey
stories.summary: A survey found that nearly half of Israeli tech companies are struggling with worker shortages due to the Iran war. Companies reported that over a quarter of their workforce is absent because of reserve duty, school closures, and security restrictions.

stories.title: Arab nations may lose $260 billion from Iran war, UN study finds
stories.summary: A United Nations study found that Arab nations could lose up to $260 billion as a result of the Iran war. Some regions may see GDP losses exceeding 5.2 percent.

stories.title: Trump attacks NATO allies as pressure mounts over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly criticized NATO allies as tensions mount over control of the Strait of Hormuz. The remarks come amid broader disputes with allied nations over the US role in the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: What NATO wants most, and how Breaking Defense is expanding in Europe
stories.summary: Breaking Defense announced plans to expand its coverage in Europe as NATO allies focus on defense priorities across the continent.

stories.title: ‘Discriminatory’ Israeli death penalty law sparks international criticism
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a bill authorizing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of deadly terror attacks in military courts, while not applying the same measure to Jewish extremists. The EU, Spain, Germany, and human rights groups condemned the legislation as discriminatory.

stories.title: Centuries-old pottery firm Denby set to call in administrators
stories.summary: Denby, a 217-year-old pottery firm based in Derbyshire, England, has called in administrators, putting nearly 600 jobs at risk. The company, which also owns the Burleigh brand, has been struggling with rising gas and labor costs alongside weakening consumer demand.

stories.title: From Airstrikes to Cooperation: Will the ‘New Phase’ of Ecuador’s Drug War Deliver?
stories.summary: Ecuador is escalating its drug war by combining traditional security measures such as curfews and mass arrests with U.S.-backed airstrikes and joint operations with European agencies targeting transatlantic drug trafficking organizations.

stories.title: Kremlin Rebuffs Zelensky’s Easter Ceasefire Proposal
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected President Zelensky's proposal for an Easter ceasefire, calling it vague and insufficient for achieving a lasting peace.

stories.title: EU Ministers in Bucha: Evidence of Russia's war crimes demands full accountability
stories.summary: EU ministers visited Bucha in the Kyiv region, where evidence collected after the withdrawal of Russian troops underscores the need for full accountability for war crimes committed by Russia in Ukraine.

stories.title: ‘Risk children’s lives for some extra manpower’: IRGC recruits 12 year olds to fill personnel gaps
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC launched a program called "For Iran" to recruit homeland defense fighters as young as 12 years old. IRGC official Nadali confirmed the registration program to state media, citing personnel gaps during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Jerusalem's Christians urge church leaders to challenge harsh Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: Palestinian Christians in Jerusalem urged church leaders to challenge Israeli restrictions on access to holy sites in the Old City. The call came after Catholic Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa was denied entry to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, with Palestinians saying Israel is using the war as a pretext.

stories.title: Qatar says Iran’s attacks on neighbours crossed ‘many red lines’
stories.summary: Qatar accused Iran of crossing "many red lines" by attacking its neighbors. Doha said the Iranian strikes are having a catastrophic effect on relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Cuba crisis explained: Who holds power, and could Diaz-Canel be replaced?
stories.summary: Cuba is experiencing one of its worst humanitarian crises in history, raising questions about the future of President Miguel Díaz-Canel's leadership. Observers are examining who holds power on the island and whether a leadership change is possible.

stories.title: #Iran: Massive explosion in Isfahan
stories.summary: A massive explosion was reported in the Iranian city of Isfahan on March 31. A local security official confirmed that strikes targeted military locations in the city, which is home to a nuclear enrichment facility.

stories.title: EU shows support to Ukraine at Bucha commemoration
stories.summary: A delegation of EU foreign ministers traveled to Kyiv on March 31 to commemorate the fourth anniversary of the Bucha massacre. Russian forces withdrew from Bucha in 2022, leaving behind hundreds of civilian bodies in what became a symbol of wartime atrocities in Ukraine.

stories.title: Does Iran’s Future Look Like Cuba, Syria, or North Korea?
stories.summary: Analysts assess competing strategies toward Iran from Gulf states and Israel, suggesting neither approach is likely to achieve its desired outcome. Comparisons are drawn to the trajectories of Cuba, Syria, and North Korea.

stories.title: Israeli military says it conducted over 230 strikes on Iran in last 24 hours
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported conducting over 230 strikes across Iran in 24 hours, saying the attacks aimed to degrade Iranian military capacity. Iran has reported that multiple strikes hit civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: High Court begins reviewing death penalty law as Adalah files petition after ACRI challenge
stories.summary: Israel's High Court began reviewing the newly passed death penalty law after legal organizations Adalah and ACRI filed petitions challenging it. The petitions argue the law is discriminatory because West Bank amendments apply exclusively to Palestinians.

stories.title: Nigeria: ICPC Takes El-Rufai Back Into Custody As Court Postpones Bail Hearing
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent Corrupt Practices Commission took former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai back into custody after temporarily releasing him to attend his mother's funeral. A court postponed his bail hearing.

stories.title: Qatar: Gulf states 'unified' in calling for war de-escalation
stories.summary: Gulf states announced a unified position calling for de-escalation in the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, according to Qatar. The conflict has reportedly spilled over into the Arabian Peninsula.

stories.title: Ukraine’s goal: produce every air defense component domestically – including anti-ballistic interceptors
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy outlined plans for Ukraine to domestically produce all air defense components, including anti-ballistic interceptors. The initiative aims to reduce Ukraine's dependence on Washington for its most advanced defensive layer.

stories.title: Turkey captures spy who kidnapped Syrian Assad army defectors
stories.summary: Turkish and Syrian intelligence services jointly captured Onder Sigircikoglu, who had escaped from a Turkish prison in 2014 while serving a 20-year sentence. He was accused of kidnapping defectors from the Syrian Assad-era army.

stories.title: UN says initial probe findings show Lebanon peacekeepers killed by blast
stories.summary: A UN investigation found that initial evidence indicates two Indonesian peacekeepers in southern Lebanon were killed by a roadside explosion on 30 March. A third Indonesian soldier died in a separate incident on Sunday. UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council the probe is ongoing.

stories.title: The Islamic State Sahel Threat Is Transnational
stories.summary: The Islamic State's operational hub is increasingly shifting to the Sahel region of Africa. Analysts warn that the jihadist threat has become transnational, with the group's reach expanding beyond traditional conflict zones.

stories.title: Plans for gaudy Trump presidential library in Miami spark ridicule
stories.summary: Plans for a proposed 50-storey Donald J. Trump presidential library in Miami were posted on social media, depicting a gold-clad structure featuring Air Force One and a giant statue of Trump. The design has drawn widespread ridicule in the city known for its art deco architecture.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Ust-Luga port again, sources say oil terminal hit
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga for the fifth time in ten days on Tuesday. Industry sources told Reuters that an oil loading terminal was hit, likely compounding Russia's difficulties in exporting crude oil.

stories.title: Vasiukivka in Donetsk region under control of Armed Forces of Ukraine – military
stories.summary: Ukraine's military confirmed that the settlement of Vasiukivka in Donetsk region remains under the control of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, denying reports that Russian forces had captured it.

stories.title: NY candidate joins anti-Israel streamer’s show, sparking ire from Jewish-heavy district
stories.summary: Democratic congressional candidate Effie Phillips-Staley appeared on streamer Hasan Piker's show and accused Israel of genocide and apartheid, drawing criticism from officials in her Jewish-heavy New York district. Democratic party officials expressed "deep disappointment" over her remarks.

stories.title: Frustrated with allies, Trump tells countries needing fuel to go to Hormuz and ‘just take it’
stories.summary: President Trump urged countries facing fuel shortages to go to the Strait of Hormuz and "just take it," expressing frustration with allies. He also accused France of blocking US military flights carrying arms to Israel, while Israeli PM Netanyahu reportedly said some Arab countries are considering fighting alongside Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan and China propose five-part peace plan for Middle East
stories.summary: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in Beijing and released a joint five-part peace proposal for the Middle East. Pakistan is seeking to position itself as a mediator between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: The Navy’s ‘Fighting Instructions’ fails its own test
stories.summary: A critique by defense analyst Bruce Stubbs argues that Admiral Daryl Caudle's "Fighting Instructions" for the U.S. Navy fails to make the necessary tradeoffs and force-design decisions required of a true strategy document.

stories.title: Those Who Cannot Remember the Past Condemn Others to Repeat It
stories.summary: Critics argue that the U.S. administration's rhetoric on Iran misuses historical analogies to justify its policies. Analysts describe Washington's framing of the conflict as particularly egregious in its distortion of historical precedent.

stories.title: Homicides in Sweden hit lowest level in over a decade in 2025
stories.summary: Homicides in Sweden fell to their lowest level in over a decade in 2025. Authorities credited new tools and methods that helped police drive down gang violence.

stories.title: Haiti: At least 30 people dead after gang attacks town
stories.summary: The Gran Grif gang attacked the town of Petite-Rivière de l'Artibonite in Haiti early Sunday, burning homes and killing at least 30 people. The gang launched a second attack on Monday, according to a local activist group spokesperson.

stories.title: ‘God squad’ waives endangered species law to allow US drilling in Gulf of Mexico
stories.summary: The U.S. Endangered Species Committee, convened for the first time in over three decades at Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's request, voted to exempt oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico from the Endangered Species Act. Critics warn the decision could endanger the rare Rice's whale.

stories.title: China and Pakistan call for 'immediate cessation of hostilities'
stories.summary: China and Pakistan's foreign ministers issued a joint five-point plan calling for an immediate ceasefire in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Pakistani Deputy PM Ishaq Dar presented the proposal following talks in Beijing, urging an end to attacks on civilians and the start of peace negotiations.

stories.title: As Ukraine commemorates the Bucha massacre, Russia rejects idea of Easter truce
stories.summary: Ukraine marked the fourth anniversary of the Bucha massacre, in which residents were killed by Russian forces during the early weeks of the invasion. Russia rejected a proposed Easter truce as fighting continues across Ukraine.

stories.title: Schools across Balochistan to re-open from April 1, have classes 5 days a week
stories.summary: The Balochistan provincial government announced that all public and private schools will reopen from April 1 with a five-day working week. Schools had been closed since March 10 due to a global fuel crisis linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Mozambique: Government Launches Free Birth Registration
stories.summary: Mozambique's Justice Ministry launched a free birth registration campaign in Maputo aimed at promoting citizens' access to civil identification documents.

stories.title: Israel to halt security procurement from 'hostile' France
stories.summary: Israel announced it would halt security procurement from France, labeling it "hostile." Tensions between the two countries have escalated since Paris became critical of Israel's military conduct in Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel to occupy swaths of south Lebanon and destroy houses near border
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Israel's military will destroy all homes in Lebanese border villages and block roughly 600,000 displaced residents from returning to southern Lebanon.
