A search warrant dated 19 March was obtained by the Associated Press.

stories.title: Russia overhauls vaccine production after cattle disease triggers mass culling
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on March 30 overhauling animal vaccine production following a cattle disease outbreak in a Siberian region. The outbreak led to mass culling of livestock, a measure that proved deeply unpopular among local populations.

stories.title: Michigan synagogue attack was Hezbollah-inspired terrorism, FBI confirms
stories.summary: The FBI confirmed that the March 12 attack on a synagogue in the Detroit, Michigan, area was Hezbollah-inspired terrorism. Ayman Ghalazi, 41, loaded his truck with fireworks and rammed it into the region's largest synagogue around midday.

stories.title: Huge fires at Russian oil facilities following Ukraine strikes, satellite images show
stories.summary: Satellite imagery analyzed by BBC Verify shows large fires at three Russian oil export facilities near the Baltic Sea following Ukrainian strikes. The damage targeted key infrastructure involved in Russia's oil exports.

stories.title: Chinese coffee brands need more than low prices to compete with global players: analysts
stories.summary: Analysts say Chinese coffee brands seeking overseas expansion must move beyond low-price strategies and develop stronger global brand identities. Experts noted that overseas consumers primarily associate Chinese brands with cost performance rather than quality or innovation.

stories.title: US raises concern over Israel’s closure of Jerusalem holy sites
stories.summary: The White House said the United States raised concerns with Israel over the closure of holy sites in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces to focus on strategic defense and counteroffensives on 'weak' fronts –Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced that Ukraine will focus on strategic defense operations to contain Russian advances in 2026 while pursuing counteroffensives on weaker sections of the front line.

stories.title: Iran war is dimming outlook for many economies, IMF says
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund has warned that the war involving Iran is dimming economic outlooks globally, causing an asymmetric shock across economies and leading to tighter financial conditions worldwide.

stories.title: Iranian Parliament mulls possible exit from nuclear treaty
stories.summary: Iran's parliament is considering a possible withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty amid the ongoing conflict. Iran maintains its nuclear program is peaceful and asserts its right to nuclear enrichment under the NPT.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign ministry rejects US ceasefire demands
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman rejected US ceasefire conditions, describing them as excessive, unrealistic, and unreasonable.

stories.title: White House ballroom project to include 'massive' military complex
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump revealed plans for a large military complex beneath a new White House ballroom that will replace the East Wing. Trump displayed a rendering of the project to reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday.

stories.title: Sybiha: Ukraine receives requests from partners on maritime security and strait unblocking
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said international partners have approached Ukraine for cooperation on maritime security, including potential efforts to unblock the Strait of Hormuz, drawing on Ukraine's experience with the Black Sea grain corridor.

stories.title: Taylor Swift sued for trademark infringement over Life of a Showgirl album title
stories.summary: Las Vegas performer Maren Wade sued Taylor Swift for trademark infringement, alleging that Swift's album "The Life of a Showgirl" creates confusion with Wade's long-running "Confessions of a Showgirl" stage show. Universal Music Group was also named as a defendant.

stories.title: NASA starts countdown for first crewed Moon mission in over 50 years
stories.summary: NASA began a two-day countdown Monday for the Artemis 2 mission, its first crewed lunar flight in over 50 years, targeting a Wednesday launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The four-astronaut crew includes the first woman, person of colour, and non-American assigned to a Moon mission. The flight will orbit the Moon and test the Space Launch System rocket.

stories.title: Rain, storms kill 45 people in Afghanistan and Pakistan
stories.summary: Severe rain and storms across Afghanistan and Pakistan have killed at least 45 people. Officials in central and eastern Afghanistan reported the closure of several highways, with additional rainfall and storms forecast for March 31.

stories.title: Somali national army takes control of part of biggest city in South West state
stories.summary: Somalia's national army has taken control of part of the largest city in South West state, according to local residents on March 30. The move comes two weeks after South West state officials announced they were severing ties with the federal government in Mogadishu.

stories.title: Why most Jewish Israelis back the death penalty for terrorists - analysis
stories.summary: A majority of Jewish Israelis support the death penalty for those convicted of terrorism, according to polling analysis. However, many simultaneously doubt that capital punishment would serve as an effective deterrent against future attacks.

stories.title: Ukraine tests next-generation bomber drones with longer range, secure communication
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry tested a new generation of bomber drones at the Brave1 training ground, featuring extended range and improved secure communications capabilities.

stories.title: Turkey says NATO defences downed fourth inbound Iranian missile
stories.summary: Turkey's defence ministry reported on March 30 that a ballistic missile launched from Iran entered Turkish airspace before being intercepted by NATO air and missile defence systems deployed in the eastern Mediterranean. It was the fourth inbound Iranian missile shot down by NATO defences.

stories.title: Russia ‘glad’ oil cargo reached its ally Cuba amid U.S. blockade
stories.summary: Russia expressed satisfaction that an oil shipment successfully reached its ally Cuba despite the U.S. blockade. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Moscow and Washington had been in communication regarding the delivery.

stories.title: Iran’s Islamic republic will ‘collapse internally’, says Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated his belief that Iran's Islamic republic will eventually "collapse internally" but said regime change is not the stated objective of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign. He said current operations focus on degrading Iran's military, missile, and nuclear capabilities.

stories.title: Facing a resurgent Hezbollah, Israel slouches back to a security zone in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces have established an extended presence in southern Lebanon amid renewed clashes with Hezbollah, drawing comparisons to Israel's previous 18-year security zone in the country. Israeli leaders have spoken of an indefinite stay in a new buffer zone.

stories.title: Key moments from Marco Rubio’s interview with Al Jazeera
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio gave an exclusive interview to Al Jazeera's Hashem Ahelbarra discussing the ongoing war on Iran.

stories.title: Petition targets newly passed death penalty law, calling it discriminatory, unconstitutional
stories.summary: A rights group petitioned Israel's High Court to immediately freeze the newly passed death penalty law, arguing it is discriminatory and unconstitutional. Additional legal challenges are expected.

stories.title: War Diary Day 31: Economic shockwaves deepen in absence of diplomatic off-ramps to Iran war
stories.summary: On day 31 of the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes continued targeting Iranian military, energy, and civilian infrastructure. The conflict's economic shockwaves deepened amid a high-intensity, multi-domain phase with no diplomatic off-ramps in sight.

stories.title: France holding five in custody after foiled Bank of America bombing
stories.summary: French authorities are holding five suspects in custody following a foiled bombing plot targeting Bank of America's offices in Paris. Officials have linked the planned attack to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: France arrests two more suspects on Bank of America's foiled attack
stories.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutors announced on March 30 that two additional suspects were arrested in connection with a foiled attack on Bank of America's Paris offices. The arrests bring the total number of people detained over the plot to five.

stories.title: Zelensky on security cooperation with Gulf countries: New requests from Bahrain, Oman
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced historic security agreements with Gulf states, including Bahrain and Oman, covering areas such as air defense strengthening and defense industry development.

stories.title: The architect of Iran’s military survival remains defiant
stories.summary: Ahmad Vahidi, a senior Iranian military figure well known to Israel and Western governments, has emerged as a prominent face of Iran's defiant military posture amid ongoing conflict, favoring confrontation over pragmatic diplomacy.

stories.title: Is a peaceful settlement possible in Iran?
stories.summary: Pakistan announced its readiness to host negotiations aimed at ending the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: US says Trump ‘interested’ in asking Arab countries to pay for war on Iran
stories.summary: White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt said President Donald Trump is interested in asking Arab countries to help cover the costs of the war on Iran.

stories.title: US used new ballistic missile in strike that killed teens in Iran sports hall: Report
stories.summary: A report indicates the US military used a new Precision Strike Missile in a strike that hit a sports hall in Lamerd, Iran, killing teenagers. Damage at the site was found to be consistent with the weapon type.

stories.title: Mexican immigrant died in US immigration custody, ICE says, marking 14 deaths in 2026
stories.summary: A Mexican immigrant died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody, marking the 14th such death in 2026. ICE detention numbers have reached record levels, with approximately 68,000 people held as of early February.

stories.title: FBI: Armed man who rammed pickup into Michigan synagogue was inspired by Hezbollah
stories.summary: The FBI said Ayman Ghazali, who rammed a pickup truck into Temple Israel synagogue in Michigan while a preschool was in session, was inspired by Hezbollah. He reportedly declared in a video his intent to kill as many people as possible.

stories.title: Watch: ‘Mr. President, please help us stop the war’: Egyptian President’s plea to Donald Trump
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi publicly appealed to U.S. President Donald Trump to help end the ongoing war in the Middle East during a recorded address.

stories.title: Islamabad businessman succumbs to injuries after being shot during dacoity at farmhouse
stories.summary: Prominent Islamabad businessman Amir Awan was fatally shot during an armed robbery at his farmhouse in the Orchard Scheme area. CCTV footage showed five gunmen armed with submachine guns and wearing bulletproof vests.

stories.title: Long queues in Myanmar as Iran war fuel crisis deepens
stories.summary: Myanmar is experiencing a fuel crisis linked to the ongoing Iran war, with drivers queuing for hours at petrol stations. The conflict's disruption of global energy supplies has sent shockwaves across fuel-importing nations.

stories.title: Defense sources: Trump Hormuz, nuke decisions determine war's end, Israel giving US intel on Strait
stories.summary: Israeli defense sources indicated that decisions by President Trump regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program will determine when the war ends. Sources expressed skepticism that Iran would accept a deal in the coming week, with Israel providing the US intelligence on the Strait situation.

stories.title: Europe’s crisis tourism: how the Iran war swallowed the EU’s geopolitical agenda
stories.summary: In the wake of US and Israeli strikes on Iran, European leaders responded with divergent positions. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz both voiced support for regime change, while questioning the international rules-based order.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces liberate 480 sq km on Oleksandrivka axis – CinC Syrskyi
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Ukrainian forces have liberated 480 square kilometers of territory along the Oleksandrivka axis.

stories.title: Gas pipeline blown up in southern Pakistan by unknown assailants, says official
stories.summary: Unknown assailants blew up a gas pipeline in southern Pakistan, according to officials. The attack disrupted gas supply to several parts of the city and at least five additional districts in the region.

stories.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran’s Kharg Island oil hub if no deal reached
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub and other critical infrastructure unless Tehran agrees to a deal to end the U.S.-Israeli war. The threat rattled global energy markets and raised fears of broader conflict, with Iran signaling potential retaliation near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Born in the USA? China targeted in America’s birthright citizenship fight
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court is set to hear arguments on birthright citizenship, with Chinese nationals at the center of disputed claims. President Trump has framed the issue around alleged abuse of the policy by foreign nationals.

stories.title: Spain denies U.S. permission to use its airspace for ‘illegal’ war on Iran
stories.summary: Spain denied the United States permission to use its airspace for military operations against Iran. Madrid also barred U.S. forces from using jointly operated military bases on Spanish territory, with Defence Minister calling the war 'profoundly illegal and unjust.'

stories.title: Australia politics live: Wong rules out lifting sanctions on Russian oil; Hastie downplays tensions with Taylor
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong ruled out lifting sanctions on Russian oil amid global energy disruptions. Energy Minister Chris Bowen said Australia remains on stage two of its national fuel plan, noting that cancelled fuel shipments have so far been replaced.

stories.title: Fire at superstore located in Karachi’s Zamzama area brought under control
stories.summary: A large fire at Imtiaz Superstore in Karachi's Zamzama shopping district was brought under control after hours of firefighting. CCTV footage indicated the blaze originated at an ATM inside the store.

stories.title: Limited missions, big risks: What a US ground fight in Iran could become
stories.summary: Military analysts outlined potential U.S. ground operations in Iran, including coastal assaults and raids on nuclear sites. Experts warned that even limited missions carry significant risks of escalation in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: 'The hypocrisy was so stark' expert says, as US reverses course on Cuba oil blockade
stories.summary: The White House allowed a sanctioned Russian tanker to deliver fuel to Cuba for humanitarian reasons on a case-by-case basis. Experts highlighted the contradiction between Washington's criticism of Iran restricting maritime movement and its own oil blockade against Cuba.

stories.title: Zelensky holds Staff meeting on air defense issues
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky convened a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief's Staff focused on air defense issues facing Ukraine.

stories.title: Knesset passes death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly acts of terror
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a death penalty law mandating hanging for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks, with no right to appeal. Security and legal officials opposed the measure, and rights groups plan to petition the High Court to overturn it.

stories.title: Trump administration sues Minnesota for allowing trans athletes in girls’ sports
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice sued Minnesota's education department and the state's high school athletics body for allowing transgender athletes to compete in girls' sports. The lawsuit alleges Minnesota is violating Title IX, the federal law prohibiting sex-based discrimination in federally funded programs.

stories.title: Trump Claims ‘Great Progress’ in Iran Peace Talks
stories.summary: President Trump claimed "great progress" in peace talks with Iran. Simultaneously, the White House threatened to destroy Tehran's energy sector if a deal is not reached soon, sending mixed signals about the status of negotiations.

stories.title: Congo army launches disarmament push against Rwanda genocide-linked militia
stories.summary: Congo's army announced the launch of a disarmament campaign against a militia linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The operation represents a key step toward implementing a U.S.-brokered peace deal between the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighbouring Rwanda.

stories.title: What could Trump achieve by threatening Iran’s Kharg Island?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to obliterate Iran's Kharg Island, the nerve center of Iranian oil exports handling the vast majority of the country's crude shipments. The Pentagon has reportedly eyed the island for potential ground operations.

stories.title: Why India is quietly deepening its engagement with the Taliban
stories.summary: India is quietly expanding its diplomatic engagement with the Taliban government in Afghanistan amid rising Pakistan-Afghanistan border tensions, cross-border strikes, and the persistent threat posed by TTP fighters operating from Afghan territory.

stories.title: How Yemen’s Houthis could worsen the oil crunch
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces have restricted shipping traffic through a key waterway for approximately two years, raising concerns about worsening the global oil supply crunch amid the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Army investigates after two helicopters hovered by Kid Rock’s pool as he saluted
stories.summary: The U.S. Army launched an administrative review after two AH-64 Apache helicopters on a training run hovered near Kid Rock's hillside home in Nashville. The Trump-supporting musician posted videos showing himself saluting and clapping as the helicopters flew alongside his pool.

stories.title: ‘Dangerous escalation’: World reacts to Israel passing death penalty law
stories.summary: International rights groups condemned Israel's newly passed death penalty law as a violation of international law, warning it places Palestinian prisoners at heightened risk.

stories.title: 'It's a prison': Afghans stranded in US camp in Qatar exposed to Iranian strikes
stories.summary: Afghan asylum seekers stranded at Camp As Sayliyah, a US transit facility in Qatar, have been exposed to Iranian strikes. The camp is set to close as a transit hub for vetted Afghans, but residents have not been told where they will be relocated.

stories.title: Israel Knesset set to vote on death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset was set to vote on March 30 on legislation making the death penalty a default sentence for Palestinians convicted in military courts of deadly attacks. The bill fulfils a key pledge made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition allies.

stories.title: ‘We miss the simplest things’: Tehran residents on edge after month of war
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran are living under fear and uncertainty after a month of war, clinging to daily routines amid ongoing strikes on Iran's capital.

stories.title: Ukraine, Bulgaria sign security cooperation agreement
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Bulgaria's Acting Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov signed a bilateral security cooperation agreement in a meeting between the two countries' leaders.

stories.title: UN condemns killing of Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon
stories.summary: The United Nations condemned the killing of three Indonesian peacekeepers in Lebanon, who died in two separate incidents. No further details on the perpetrators were immediately provided.

stories.title: Germany's Merz says Berlin will work with Syria to return refugees
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced on March 30 that Germany and Syria would cooperate to facilitate the return of hundreds of thousands of Syrian refugees. Merz said the refugees had an important role to play in rebuilding their country.

stories.title: Opposition mistakenly approves millions to haredi institutions, A-G halts transfer
stories.summary: Israeli opposition lawmakers mistakenly voted to approve hundreds of millions of shekels in allocations to ultra-Orthodox institutions during a budget maneuver. The Attorney General subsequently halted the fund transfers, as the allocations had previously been blocked by legal advisors. Some opposition members issued public apologies.

stories.title: Trump interested in calling on Arab states to help pay for Iran war, White House says
stories.summary: The White House said President Trump is interested in calling on Arab states to help finance the war against Iran. Press Secretary Leavitt warned that any private commitments made by Iran to Washington would be tested and that Tehran would be held accountable.

stories.title: 'Like a dream': Gaza mother reunited with evacuated baby daughter
stories.summary: Sundus al-Kurd, a Gazan mother, was reunited with her baby daughter after being separated when Shifa Hospital in Gaza was evacuated more than two years ago during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks face death penalty under new Israeli law
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law allowing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks against Israelis. The legislation was championed by far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and approved on Monday.

stories.title: Israeli Knesset approves death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset approved legislation permitting the death penalty for Palestinians found guilty of killing Israelis. The measure has drawn widespread controversy domestically and internationally.

stories.title: ‘All roads lead to higher prices and slower growth’: IMF says Iran war is dimming outlook for many economies
stories.summary: The IMF warned that the US-Israeli war on Iran is causing significant global economic disruption, including tighter financial conditions. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and damage to regional infrastructure have caused major energy supply disruptions.

stories.title: Air Canada CEO to quit after furore about crash condolence video
stories.summary: Air Canada's CEO announced his resignation following public backlash over a condolence video he released about a deadly crash. The video, issued only in English, created a significant public relations controversy in Canada.

stories.title: Houthi attacks stoke fears of more shipping disruption
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched attacks on Israeli targets after entering the broader conflict, driving a surge in global oil prices. The Iran-allied group had previously targeted commercial ships near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, raising fears of wider disruption to energy and goods trade between Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal.

stories.title: The war in Iran: Key takeaways from Al Jazeera’s interview with Marco Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed the objectives of the US military campaign against Iran in an interview with Al Jazeera's Hashem Ahelbarra.

stories.title: FBI says man who crashed his truck into Michigan synagogue was inspired by Hezbollah
stories.summary: The FBI announced that Ayman Ghazali, who crashed his pickup truck into Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield Township, Michigan, was inspired by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah and had recorded a video expressing intent to kill.

stories.title: Trump gives Iran one‑week deadline on deal, says US response to Haifa strike coming soon
stories.summary: President Trump gave Iran a one-week deadline to reach a deal and said a US response to the missile strike on Haifa is forthcoming. Trump also stated that Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not been heard from and is believed to be 'very seriously injured.'

stories.title: Syrian army says drone attacks targeted its bases near Iraq
stories.summary: The Syrian army reported on March 30 that drone attacks struck several of its military bases near the Iraqi border. The strikes represent a rare targeting of Syrian positions since U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran a month ago triggered a wider Middle East war.

stories.title: ‘We have to destroy Iran’s ability to launch missiles’, Rubio says
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that eliminating Iran's missile-launch capability is essential for achieving regional stability.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 70 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one and wounding 12
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 70 drone and artillery attacks on the Nikopol and Kryvyi Rih districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, killing one person and wounding 12 others.

stories.title: Missile hits fuel tanker at Israel's Oil Refineries
stories.summary: Debris from an intercepted missile struck an industrial building and a fuel tanker at Oil Refineries Ltd in Haifa, northern Israel, on March 30. Israel's Fire and Rescue Service confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Israel’s parliament passes death penalty bill targeting Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a death penalty bill targeting Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks. The Palestinian Authority condemned the legislation as a war crime and a breach of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

stories.title: At least 70 people killed and 30 injured in Haiti gang attack
stories.summary: A gang attack in Haiti's Artibonite region killed at least 70 people and injured 30, according to a human rights group, far exceeding initial official estimates of 16–17 dead. Nearly 6,000 people were forced to flee the area, and the group criticized authorities for abandoning affected communities.

stories.title: War boosts counter-drone sales, joint ventures
stories.summary: The ongoing conflicts have driven a surge in counter-drone technology sales and joint ventures, with defense-technology companies forming new partnerships and nations under threat placing orders in recent weeks.

stories.title: Islamabad businessman succumbs to injures after being shot during dacoity at farmhouse
stories.summary: Islamabad businessman Amir Awan was fatally shot by armed robbers during a dacoity at his farmhouse in Orchard Scheme. Police said CCTV footage showed five gunmen armed with submachine guns and wearing bulletproof jackets.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1496: Kyiv secures 10-year defense treaty with Bulgaria and new agreements with Gulf states
stories.summary: On day 1,496 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine signed a 10-year defense treaty with Bulgaria and reached new agreements with Gulf states. However, Kyiv faces a looming domestic budget crisis that threatens to reduce war funding.

stories.title: Iranian spy network operating in London under cover of Press TV, source tells ‘Post’
stories.summary: A source told the Jerusalem Post that an Iranian spy network has been operating in London under the cover of Press TV, Iran's state-funded English-language broadcaster. Despite losing its UK broadcast license and being banned from YouTube, Press TV journalists allegedly used their credentials to identify recruitment targets.

stories.title: Rubio says NATO must be re-examined after Spain blocks US operation on Iran
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized NATO allies, particularly Spain, for blocking the use of their bases for US military operations against Iran, calling the refusal "very disappointing" and suggesting the alliance needs re-examination.

stories.title: Ukraine and Bulgaria to establish energy corridor by year’s end - Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukraine and Bulgaria will establish an energy corridor by year's end capable of delivering approximately 10 billion cubic meters of gas, providing an alternative if certain European countries block energy imports.

stories.title: In defence of Benjamin Netanyahu
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that singling out Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as uniquely responsible for state policy obscures a broader historical record of Israeli territorial expansion and repression that predates his leadership.

stories.title: Nigeria's gasoline pump ⁠prices rise by 65%, ​highest in Africa
stories.summary: Nigeria's gasoline pump prices rose by 65 percent, the highest in Africa, as consequences of the Middle East war affected fuel costs. Separately, the Democratic Republic of Congo's armed forces launched a disarmament campaign against the FDLR militia linked to the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

stories.title: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz review regional situation, implications for Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met to review the regional security situation, a day after a quadrilateral ministerial meeting in Islamabad involving Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt focused on ending the regional conflict.

stories.title: Czechs detain fifth suspect over arson attack on drone factory
stories.summary: Czech authorities detained a fifth suspect on March 30 in connection with an arson attack on an optics and drone factory in the Czech Republic, according to a public prosecutor.

stories.title: White House ballroom project to include ‘massive’ military complex
stories.summary: The Trump administration confirmed the US military is upgrading White House facilities as part of a project to build a new ballroom atop a fortified military complex, replacing the East Wing at an estimated cost of $400 million.

stories.title: Germany's Merz says 80 percent of Syrian immigrants should return home
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa agreed that roughly 80 percent of Syrian immigrants in Germany should return to Syria within three years. Al-Sharaa visited Berlin in his first presidential trip to Germany, which hosts Europe's largest Syrian diaspora.

stories.title: Bennett vows to investigate ‘sabotage of Haredi enlistment’ if elected PM
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett pledged to investigate what he called the sabotage of ultra-Orthodox military enlistment if elected. He criticized the current coalition for increasing funding to Haredi institutions while the IDF faces manpower shortages.

stories.title: Unknown gunmen kill more than 70 in South Sudan after dispute at gold mine
stories.summary: Unknown gunmen killed more than 70 people at the Jebel Iraq gold mining site in South Sudan following a dispute. The area has seen violent clashes between illegal miners and mining companies.

stories.title: Both Hezbollah and Iran weighed preemptive strikes on Israel, defense sources say
stories.summary: Israeli defense sources revealed that both Hezbollah and Iran had considered launching preemptive strikes against Israel before the current conflict. However, joint IDF and American attacks on Iran disrupted Hezbollah's calculations and derailed its plans for a preemptive operation.

stories.title: Israel to keep effective control of southern Lebanon, attacks on Hezbollah to continue post-war
stories.summary: Israeli defense sources said the IDF plans to maintain effective control of southern Lebanon after the war, using sensors, surveillance, aerial power, artillery, tanks, and ground troops. Military operations against Hezbollah in the area are expected to continue even in a post-war scenario.

stories.title: Israeli Knesset passes law to execute Palestinians for 'acts of terrorism'
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed legislation making the death penalty the default sentence for Palestinians convicted of killings classified as 'acts of terrorism.' The law applies specifically to Palestinians and was approved during Monday evening's final readings.

stories.title: Iran’s Houthi gamble at Bab al-Mandab might strengthen Washington - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Iran's use of Houthi forces as a pressure lever at the Bab al-Mandab strait opens a sensitive new front that could ultimately strengthen Washington's strategic position.

stories.title: Fact check: Iranian hackers did not leak a video of FBI chief Kash Patel dancing; it is unrelated
stories.summary: A video shared on social media falsely claimed to show leaked footage of FBI Director Kash Patel dancing, allegedly from an Iranian hacker breach. The video is old and shows an unidentified man, though Patel's email was confirmed to have been breached by Iran-linked hackers.

stories.title: Trump interested in calling on Arab states to help pay for Iran war, White House says
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said President Trump is interested in asking Arab states to help finance the war with Iran. She made the statement on Monday without specifying which countries would be approached.

stories.title: Zelensky: Blocked EU loan could leave Ukraine short on time to prepare for winter
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that a blocked €90 billion EU loan—€45 billion of which was due this year—could leave Ukraine without enough time to prepare critical infrastructure for the coming winter.

stories.title: IDF investigating after UN says two peacekeepers killed in explosion in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF is investigating after the United Nations reported two peacekeepers were killed in an explosion in southern Lebanon. The incident followed a separate blast that killed another UNIFIL peacekeeper at a position in a southern Lebanese village within the previous 24 hours.

stories.title: Trump again warns Iran to open Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump again warned Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on March 30. He also stated that the U.S. was engaged in talks with what he described as a "more reasonable regime" to end the war.

stories.title: Fast bowler Naseem Shah slapped with Rs20m fine for contract breach
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board fined fast bowler Naseem Shah 20 million rupees for breaching his central contract, reportedly linked to a social media post criticizing Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz during a Pakistan Super League event.

stories.title: Israel approves $45B defense budget as Iran war rages
stories.summary: Israel approved a $45 billion defense budget as the war with Iran continues. The country's defense spending has increased sharply since the multi-front conflict that began with the October 7, 2023, attack.

stories.title: Ukraine hits back against Rheinmetall CEO's housewives' drones comments
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials criticised Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger after he dismissed Ukraine's drone-based defence innovations as basic technology assembled by housewives in kitchens. The comments drew widespread backlash in Kyiv on March 30.

stories.title: Fake images falsely claim Iran captured US marines on Kharg Island
stories.summary: Fabricated images circulated online falsely claiming that Iran had captured U.S. Marines on Kharg Island. The claims were debunked as misinformation.

stories.title: Rubio denies US actions punitive, blames Cuba for economic failures
stories.summary: In an interview with Al Jazeera, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that American actions toward Cuba are punitive and attributed the island's economic and fuel crises to the Cuban government's own failures.

stories.title: Stray Ukrainian drone that fell in Finland had a warhead, police say
stories.summary: Finnish police confirmed that a stray Ukrainian drone that landed in Finland was carrying a warhead. The incident marks the first time the Russia-Ukraine war has physically spilled onto Finnish territory.

stories.title: Lawmaker: Ukraine’s EU integration should not be held back by other candidates or Hungary
stories.summary: A Ukrainian lawmaker argued that Ukraine's EU accession negotiations should not be delayed by other candidate countries' progress or by individual member states such as Hungary blocking advancement.

stories.title: US reopens embassy in Venezuela months after military operation to remove Maduro
stories.summary: The United States formally reopened its embassy in Caracas, Venezuela, resuming normal diplomatic operations after a seven-year closure. The restoration followed the Trump administration's military removal of President Nicolas Maduro in January.

stories.title: Settler violence spikes amid Iran war, Herzog responds to Diaspora Jews' call for action
stories.summary: Diaspora Jewish leaders urged Israeli President Isaac Herzog to press Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right coalition ministers to act against a spike in settler violence occurring amid the Iran war.

stories.title: Air defence units of Ukrainian companies start intercepting drones, minister says
stories.summary: Ukraine's defence minister announced on March 30 that the first air defence unit formed by Ukrainian industrial enterprises has begun combat duties. New units are being established at 13 additional enterprises across the country.

stories.title: Navy unveils final RFP for new trainer aircraft to replace T-45 Goshawk
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy released the final request for proposals for the Undergraduate Jet Training System, which will replace the T-45 Goshawk trainer aircraft. The T-45 fleet has been in service since the early 1990s.

stories.title: Egypt's Sisi says only Trump can stop war, warns oil could top $200
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi urged U.S. President Donald Trump on March 30 to halt the Iran war, stating only Trump could end the conflict. Sisi warned that fears of oil prices exceeding $200 per barrel were not exaggerated.

stories.title: Iran long-range strikes expose gaps in Europe’s air defense, expert tells 'Post' - interview
stories.summary: Iran fired two long-range ballistic missiles at the Diego Garcia joint UK-US military base, located approximately 4,000 kilometers away. A defense expert told the Jerusalem Post that the strikes demonstrate Iran's capability to potentially reach most European countries, exposing gaps in Europe's air defense systems.

stories.title: Bulgaria’s acting PM just outran the pro-Russian president — 10-year treaty signed with Ukraine, SAFE-funded joint weapons production agreed, PURL commitment made
stories.summary: Bulgaria's acting Prime Minister signed a 10-year security treaty with Ukraine, including jointly funded weapons production. President Zelensky said Bulgaria's PURL accession would bolster Ukrainian air defense ahead of the next heating season.

stories.title: Brazil's Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro seen tied in presidential run-off, poll shows
stories.summary: A BTG Pactual/Nexus poll released Monday showed Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro tied in a simulated presidential run-off for this year's election.

stories.title: Israel passes law to give death penalty to Palestinians convicted of lethal attacks
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed legislation making the death penalty the default punishment for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank convicted of carrying out fatal attacks classified as terrorism. European nations and rights groups have sharply criticized the measure as discriminatory.

stories.title: US reopens embassy in Venezuela after seizing Nicolas Maduro
stories.summary: The US State Department formally reopened its embassy in Caracas, Venezuela, after a seven-year closure. The reopening followed a US military operation in January that seized President Nicolas Maduro and led to restored diplomatic ties.

stories.title: Chinese container ships pass through Strait of Hormuz at second attempt, data shows
stories.summary: Two Chinese container ships successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday on their second attempt, becoming the first container vessels to pass through the critical waterway since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28. Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic showed the vessels sailed in close formation into open waters.

stories.title: 'The Houthis hold serious cards' expert says, amid threats to choke off Red Sea passage
stories.summary: Dr. Elisabeth Kendall of Cambridge University warned that if Houthi forces block the Bab el-Mandeb strait, it would dramatically impact global oil supply. She noted that with the Strait of Hormuz under threat, the Red Sea has become a vital alternative export route.

stories.title: Russian oil tanker arrives in Cuba as Moscow vows to stand by Havana
stories.summary: A Russian oil tanker carrying 100,000 metric tons of crude oil has arrived in Cuba as Moscow pledged to continue supporting Havana with further supplies despite a US blockade that had cut off Venezuelan oil exports to the island.

stories.title: What we know about attack on key Israeli oil refinery
stories.summary: A large fire broke out at an oil refinery in Haifa, Israel, after the facility was struck by debris. Israeli authorities said they were working to contain the blaze. The refinery is a key energy infrastructure site in northern Israel.

stories.title: First set of defensive cyber kits to be delivered to CYBERCOM units
stories.summary: The first standardized defensive cyber kits, called Joint Cyber Hunt Kits, are being delivered to U.S. Cyber Command units. The kits will provide CYBERCOM's defensive cyber warriors with standardized tools to conduct hunt missions for the first time.

stories.title: French police make two more arrests over foiled attack on Bank of America
stories.summary: French police arrested two more suspects in connection with a foiled attack on a Bank of America location in France. Prosecutors are investigating a suspected link to the Iran conflict, citing similarities with other recent attempted attacks across Europe.

stories.title: Trump's options in Iran range from bad to worse
stories.summary: Amid reports that President Trump is frustrated with the prolonged war in Iran, analysts note that Washington's options are increasingly limited. A U.S. ceasefire proposal has gained no traction, leaving the administration facing difficult choices as the conflict continues.

stories.title: Two Indonesian UN peacekeepers killed in explosion in Lebanon
stories.summary: Two Indonesian United Nations peacekeepers serving with UNIFIL were killed in an explosion in southern Lebanon. The incident occurred within 24 hours of another fatal attack, as Israel expanded its military operation against Hezbollah in the region.

stories.title: Fire at super store in Karachi’s Zamzama brought 70pc under control: Rescue 1122
stories.summary: A fire broke out in the basement of Imtiaz Superstore's Zamzama branch in Karachi during early Monday hours. Rescue 1122 officials reported the blaze had been brought 70 percent under control.

stories.title: Iran blows hole in US aluminum supply chain with strikes on Gulf smelters
stories.summary: Iranian strikes on aluminum smelting facilities in the UAE and Bahrain have disrupted a critical segment of the US supply chain. The United States imports approximately 60 percent of its aluminum annually, raising concerns about significant shortages and economic consequences.

stories.title: African countries feel impact of war on Iran [Africanews Today]
stories.summary: One month into the Iran war, African countries are facing severe economic consequences, particularly in fuel supply. Nigeria saw record-high fuel prices despite output from the Dangote refinery.

stories.title: Russian forces strike energy facility near Kharkiv region border
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an energy facility in the Derhachi border community in Kharkiv district, leaving more than 800 customers without electricity.

stories.title: Moshe Yitzchak Katz, Israeli-US soldier killed in Lebanon, laid to rest in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Moshe Yitzchak Katz, a dual Israeli-US citizen who moved from Connecticut to Israel to serve in the military, was killed in Lebanon. He was laid to rest in Jerusalem and remembered by loved ones as a loyal friend and proud soldier.

stories.title: European Commission adopts $1.7B work program to ramp up weapons production
stories.summary: The European Commission adopted a €1.7 billion work program under the European Defence Industry Programme to boost weapons production across the EU from 2026 through 2027. The first round of calls for proposals will open on the EU's tender portal starting Tuesday.

stories.title: Cuba waits for Russian oil tanker to arrive amid US blockade
stories.summary: Cuba is awaiting the arrival of a sanctioned Russian oil tanker carrying thousands of barrels of oil amid a US blockade. The shipment is expected to alleviate energy shortages on the island caused by restricted access to fuel imports.

stories.title: Leaders killed, U.S. strikes and Iranian response: a month of Iran-U.S. war
stories.summary: One month into US-Israeli military strikes on Iranian targets, the conflict has seen key Iranian leaders killed, continued US strikes, and Iranian retaliatory actions in an ongoing escalation.

stories.title: Massive flooding in Russia’s North Caucasus destroys bridges, swamps homes, and leaves tens of thousands without power
stories.summary: Heavy rains triggered massive flooding across Russia's North Caucasus. Dagestan lost power to tens of thousands of residents, Chechnya declared a state of emergency after 17 bridges were damaged, and disruptions were reported in Ingushetia and Kabardino-Balkaria.

stories.title: Trump threatens to strike Iran’s civilian infrastructure if no deal is reached
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iran's civilian infrastructure if a nuclear deal is not reached, while stating that discussions were underway with what he described as a "more reasonable regime."

stories.title: ‘Get them out of casinos’: Bannon wants Netanyahu’s son and Gulf royals on Iran front lines
stories.summary: Former White House chief strategist Steve Bannon called for Netanyahu's son and Gulf royal family members to serve on the front lines of the Iran conflict. Bannon also suggested that the UAE should seize Iran's Kharg Island, a key oil export terminal.

stories.title: Israeli parliament approves death penalty for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law making the death penalty by hanging the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of nationalistic killings of Israelis. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu voted in person. The measure was a major victory for Israel's far-right coalition partners.

stories.title: French Court Sentences Russia-Linked Tanker Captain to 1 Year in Jail
stories.summary: A French court sentenced the captain of a tanker suspected of transporting Russian oil in violation of Western sanctions to one year in prison. The vessel had falsely claimed to be flagged in Benin.

stories.title: Iran says envoy will remain in Beirut, defying order to leave
stories.summary: Iran announced its ambassador would remain in Beirut despite an order to leave. Lebanon stated the Iranian envoy had violated diplomatic convention by refusing to depart.

stories.title: When individual acts become a national indictment - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines how individual acts of violence in Israel are frequently used to indict the broader society, arguing that the distinction between isolated perpetrators and the general population often collapses in public discourse.

stories.title: Russians drop two guided bombs on dormitory in Hlukhiv, injuring 11 including child
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped two guided aerial bombs on a dormitory at an educational institution in Hlukhiv, Sumy region. Eleven people were injured, including a child.

stories.title: Small boats deal between France and UK is on verge of collapse
stories.summary: The UK's agreement with France to fund beach patrols aimed at curbing small boat Channel crossings is on the verge of collapse. The three-year, £480 million deal expires at midnight on Tuesday, with negotiations deadlocked over interception targets and asylum seeker safety concerns.

stories.title: Police arrest two more over attempted attack on US bank HQ in Paris
stories.summary: French police arrested two additional suspects on Monday in connection with an attempted bombing outside a Bank of America branch near the Champs-Élysées in Paris, bringing total arrests to five. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez suggested the ongoing Middle East war may have motivated the attack.

stories.title: Trump threatens to ‘obliterate’ Iran’s energy grid if ceasefire not reached ‘shortly’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to 'obliterate' Iran's power stations and fresh water plants if Tehran does not agree to peace terms soon. Oil prices are on course for a record monthly rise amid the ongoing U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran has described U.S. peace proposals as unrealistic.

stories.title: Sir Westmacott challenges Trump rationale as war on Iran sparks 'serious' economic fallout worldwide
stories.summary: Former British Ambassador Sir Peter Westmacott discussed the economic fallout from the U.S.-led war on Iran, challenging the Trump administration's rationale for the conflict. Westmacott, now with the Atlantic Council's Europe Center, spoke on France 24's Spotlight program about the crisis's global impact.

stories.title: Iran’s grip on Hormuz is tighter than ever after a month of war
stories.summary: After a month of war, Iran is tightening its control over the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran is preparing legislation that would require ships transiting the strait to share detailed information and pay fees.

stories.title: Georgia’s Only Refinery to Replace Russian Crude With Turkmen, Kazakh Oil
stories.summary: Georgia's only refinery plans to replace Russian crude oil with supplies from Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan. The shift comes after the Kulevi oil terminal on the Black Sea coast narrowly avoided inclusion on an EU sanctions list targeting Russia.

stories.title: Israel legalises death penalty for Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed a law on Monday approving the death penalty for Palestinians convicted on terror charges of carrying out deadly attacks on Israelis. The legislation also allows courts to impose the death penalty on Israeli citizens. Israeli and Palestinian rights groups have harshly criticized the measure.

stories.title: Norway cuts petrol, diesel taxes over Mid-East war
stories.summary: Norway's government announced cuts to taxes on petrol and diesel in response to the economic impact of the Middle East war. The tax reductions also apply to mineral oils used in the fishing and hunting industries.

stories.title: Boots on the ground? Trump eyes Iran oil hub Kharg Island
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is reportedly considering seizing Iran's Kharg Island, the hub for nearly 90 percent of Iranian crude exports, as oil prices surpass $110 per barrel. U.S. assault troops are being positioned in the region amid repeated threats of a Venezuela-style seizure of Tehran's oil infrastructure.

stories.title: Two more UN peacekeepers killed in southern Lebanon: UNIFIL
stories.summary: UNIFIL reported that two more UN peacekeepers were killed in southern Lebanon, bringing the week's total to at least three. The deaths occurred amid escalating violence as Israel expanded its ground invasion of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: AG halts transfer of budget funds for Haredi institutions after contentious vote
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara halted the transfer of budget funds allocated to ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) institutions. She ruled that a parliamentary maneuver used to approve the funds was designed to circumvent a High Court ruling barring financial benefits for Haredi men who avoid military conscription.

stories.title: Kuwait assures full facilitation of diesel, jet fuel supplies to Pakistan
stories.summary: Kuwait has assured Pakistan of full facilitation in diesel and jet fuel supplies, which were disrupted by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Tehran has allowed 20 Pakistani-flagged cargo ships to pass through the strait.

stories.title: Most Syrian refugees in Germany expected to return home in three years, Merz says
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that most Syrian refugees in Germany are expected to return to Syria within three years. The announcement reflects his government's stricter stance on refugees and migrants, amid growing support for the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

stories.title: In Canada's far north, some fret Carney's military plan overlooks everyday needs
stories.summary: In Cambridge Bay, Nunavut, residents expressed concern that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's military spending plan overlooks everyday needs. The remote Arctic hamlet of 2,000 people lacks resident doctors, has limited dental visits, and requires trucked-in water.

stories.title: Israel ramps up arms production amid Iran war, Lebanon assault
stories.summary: Israel is significantly ramping up arms production amid the ongoing war with Iran and its military campaign in Lebanon. Tel Aviv is tripling its output of air defense munitions as the conflict shows no immediate signs of ending.

stories.title: Iran confirms killing by Israel of Guards navy commander
stories.summary: Iran confirmed that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy commander Alireza Tangsiri was killed by Israel. Tangsiri was described as one of the longest-serving senior figures in the force.

stories.title: Three UN peacekeepers killed in south Lebanon in 24 hours amid Israel-Hezbollah conflict
stories.summary: Two UN peacekeepers were killed in an explosion in southern Lebanon on Monday, and a third was killed in a separate blast the previous day, bringing deaths to three within 24 hours. The UNIFIL peacekeeping force operates in the area amid the ongoing Israel-Hezbollah conflict.

stories.title: How economic attrition is central to Iran's war strategy
stories.summary: Iran is employing an economic attrition strategy in its war effort, leveraging low-cost drones, energy chokepoints such as the Strait of Hormuz, and broader market disruption. The approach aims to impose disproportionate economic costs on adversaries through asymmetric warfare tactics.

stories.title: Shock, sadness and relief in town at centre of Australia's seven-month police manhunt
stories.summary: A seven-month police manhunt in an Australian town ended, prompting mixed reactions of shock, sadness, and relief. The search began after Dezi Freeman fatally shot two police officers.

stories.title: Knesset approves death penalty for terrorists bill, Netanyahu in favor
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a bill legislating the death penalty for individuals convicted of terrorism in Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu voted in favor of the measure, which was approved in final readings on Monday evening.

stories.title: New rehabilitation center for soldiers opens in Kyiv
stories.summary: A new rehabilitation center for military personnel opened in Kyiv as part of the national RECOVERY rehabilitation network program, aimed at supporting injured soldiers.

stories.title: Bank of Israel slashes growth prospects as Iran war takes toll on economy
stories.summary: The Bank of Israel reduced its economic growth forecasts as the ongoing war with Iran weighs on the economy. The central bank kept borrowing costs elevated and raised concerns about the campaign's intensity and duration. Governor Yaron criticized the government for approving coalition spending during wartime.

stories.title: New York Times accuses Pentagon of flouting judge’s order blocking its press access policy
stories.summary: The New York Times accused the Pentagon of defying a federal court order that blocked a policy restricting reporters' access to the Defense Department's headquarters. A Times lawyer urged U.S. District Judge Paul Friedman to compel government compliance with the 10-day-old order. The judge did not immediately rule.

stories.title: Exiled Intelligence Expert Andrei Soldatov Jailed 4 Years in Absentia for Breaking ‘Foreign Agent’ Law
stories.summary: Russian-born intelligence expert Andrei Soldatov, who lives in London, was sentenced in absentia to four years in prison for violating Russia's "foreign agent" law. Soldatov is known for co-authoring books on Russia's security services with Irina Borogan.

stories.title: German Ambassador honors victims of Russian occupation in Yahidne
stories.summary: German Ambassador Heiko Thoms visited Yahidne in the Chernihiv region to honor victims of Russian occupation ahead of the fourth anniversary of the village's liberation.

stories.title: What is the ‘Greater Israel’ project?
stories.summary: The concept of a 'Greater Israel,' once considered a fringe political idea, is being voiced more openly by Israeli political figures. The project envisions expanded Israeli territorial control and is increasingly visible in policy discussions and actions on the ground.

stories.title: Zelensky says allies asked him to scale back attacks on Russian energy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that allied partners asked him to scale back Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure as global energy prices surge due to the Iran war.

stories.title: American University in Armenia halts in-person teaching over Iran threat
stories.summary: The American University of Armenia halted in-person teaching due to threats related to the Iran war. American universities in Lebanon and Jordan have similarly moved classes online.

stories.title: Iran believes Ukraine is involved in US and Israeli aggression against Tehran after sending thousands of civilian terror drones to Moscow
stories.summary: Iran accuses Ukraine of involvement in US and Israeli aggression against Tehran, citing Ukraine's drone transfers to Moscow. Iran has deployed thousands of Shahed UAVs against Ukrainian civilian targets since 2022.

stories.title: Trump says he expects deal ‘shortly’ with Iran, threatens to ‘blow up’ power plants if not
stories.summary: President Trump said he expects a deal with Iran 'shortly' but threatened to destroy power plants if negotiations fail. Trump confirmed the US is negotiating with Iranian hardliner Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, while Secretary of State Rubio cautioned that Washington must prepare for the possibility of talks collapsing.

stories.title: Most American Jews disapprove of US military action against Iran, new poll shows
stories.summary: A new poll found that 55% of American Jews oppose US military action against Iran, while 32% support it and roughly a quarter of respondents described themselves as torn on the issue.

stories.title: Zack Polanski meets unions in attempt to get them to switch party funding to Greens
stories.summary: UK Green Party leader Zack Polanski has begun engaging with trade unions to convince them to redirect funding away from Labour to the Greens. He has held discussions with 10 unions, including some affiliated with Labour, and is scheduled to address the University and College Union and the Bakers' union.

stories.title: Iran says $700m US surveillance plane destroyed at Saudi base
stories.summary: Iran claimed it destroyed a US AWACS surveillance aircraft valued at approximately $700 million at a Saudi Arabian military base. Tehran said the strike on the Gulf base exposed vulnerabilities in American air defense systems in the region.

stories.title: The Houthis Are Now in the War—But How Deep?
stories.summary: Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen have entered the broader Middle East conflict, raising concerns they could target Red Sea shipping routes. Analysts warn that Houthi involvement could worsen an already strained energy market if the group disrupts traffic through the critical waterway.

stories.title: Gold mine attack in South Sudan kills at least 73 people
stories.summary: An attack on a gold mine in South Sudan killed at least 73 people. Authorities are investigating the identity of the assailants amid rising tensions between rival armed forces in the country.

stories.title: Avi Lewis, elected to lead Canada’s New Democratic party, promises ‘NDP comeback’
stories.summary: Former broadcaster Avi Lewis was elected leader of Canada's New Democratic Party on a first ballot at the party's leadership convention. Lewis, a self-proclaimed socialist, pledged to rebuild the NDP around equity, higher wealth taxes, green energy, and tuition-free education after the party lost official status in the last federal election.

stories.title: Iran executes two men linked to opposition group, judiciary outlet reports
stories.summary: Iran executed two men linked to an opposition group, according to a judiciary outlet. Both had been arrested in early 2024 and held at Evin prison in Tehran.

stories.title: Kosovo approves troops to Gaza under US-backed scheme
stories.summary: Kosovo's government approved the deployment of troops to Gaza under a U.S.-backed scheme. Officials did not disclose the number of personnel being sent.

stories.title: War update: 46 clashes on front line since morning, two sectors remain most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 46 Russian attacks on their positions since the morning, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector of the front line.

stories.title: Nigeria: Curfew in Jos area after attack near university
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a bar near a university in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, reportedly killing dozens. Authorities imposed a 48-hour curfew and said the perpetrators had not yet been identified.

stories.title: Saudi oil pricing in disarray as buyers seek alternatives
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's oil pricing system is in disarray amid the Iran conflict, as buyers seek alternative supply mechanisms. Soaring prices have prompted customers to push the kingdom toward new pricing arrangements.

stories.title: Israeli forces shoot dead two Palestinians in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot dead two Palestinians in separate incidents in the occupied West Bank. Violence in the territory has intensified since the Gaza war began, with a rising toll on both sides of the conflict.

stories.title: Israel Police arrest twenty-one as anti-war protests grow despite broad support for Iran war
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested 21 people during anti-war protests in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, and Beersheba. A survey found broad but uneven support among Jewish Israelis for the military operation against Iran, dubbed Operation Roaring Lion.

stories.title: IMF warns Middle East conflict will lead to higher prices and slower global growth
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that continued conflict in the Middle East will lead to higher prices and slower economic growth worldwide. The IMF said disruptions to oil, gas, and fertiliser exports from the Gulf are driving up energy and food costs, with potentially lasting economic damage globally.

stories.title: US reopens embassy in Venezuela in significant thawing of relations
stories.summary: The United States reopened its embassy in Venezuela, resuming diplomatic operations nearly three months after former President Nicolás Maduro was abducted and detained in the U.S. The move signals a significant shift in U.S.-Venezuela relations as Washington engages with the government of Delcy Rodríguez.

stories.title: Ukraine inks defense agreements with Qatar and Saudi Arabia, with UAE to follow
stories.summary: Ukraine signed defense cooperation agreements with Qatar and Saudi Arabia, with a similar deal with the UAE expected to follow. Analysts note that Ukraine's years of experience countering Iranian drones make its defense capabilities particularly attractive to Gulf states.

stories.title: PMD predicts fresh showers across country from April 1
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department has forecast widespread rain, thunderstorms, and possible hailstorms across the country from April 1 through April 4, driven by a westerly wave approaching southwestern Balochistan.

stories.title: French court convicts Chinese captain of oil tanker linked to Russian shadow fleet
stories.summary: A French court in Brest convicted Chinese captain Chen Zhangjie in absentia and sentenced him to one year in prison for failing to comply with orders to stop his vessel. The Boracay tanker, linked to Russia's shadow fleet, was boarded by the French navy in September before being released.

stories.title: PMDC takes notice of filming of video during medical procedure at Lahore’s Lady Willingdon Hospital
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council took notice of a video filmed during surgeries at Lahore's Lady Willingdon Hospital showing two C-sections performed simultaneously. Punjab authorities had already suspended several hospital staff members.

stories.title: Latvia sent €6.8 million to Ukraine’s Chernihiv and Sumy oblasts, bordering Russia
stories.summary: Latvia provided €6.8 million in aid to Ukraine's Chernihiv and Sumy oblasts, both bordering Russia. Chernihiv Oblast is the only Ukrainian region that borders both Russia and Belarus.

stories.title: Damage reported in three districts: Odesa shows cleanup after Russian attack
stories.summary: Residential buildings in three districts of Odesa were damaged following a Russian attack on March 28. Cleanup operations are underway across the affected areas.

stories.title: Last week, Ukrainian drones reportedly landed in Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania. Russian propaganda was quick to react.
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly landed in Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, and Finland after veering off course. Baltic and Finnish authorities attributed the incursions to Russia's full-scale war, while Russian propaganda falsely claimed the countries had opened their airspace to Ukrainian strikes.

stories.title: Egypt's Sisi asks Trump to 'help us stop the war'
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi urged US President Trump to help end the war on Iran, warning that oil prices could reach $200 per barrel. Sisi cited supply shocks, food security risks, and tensions over the Strait of Hormuz as threats to the global economy.

stories.title: Israel army withdraws West Bank battalion after CNN journalist assault
stories.summary: The Israeli military withdrew a battalion from the West Bank after a soldier assaulted a CNN photojournalist, placing him in a chokehold and slamming him to the ground.

stories.title: South Korea Revives Naphtha Imports From Russia Amid Looming Shortage
stories.summary: South Korea's LG Chem purchased 27,000 metric tons of naphtha from Russia amid a looming domestic shortage. The shipments were expected to arrive on Monday, marking a revival of South Korean naphtha imports from Russia.

stories.title: 'Death was not our fate': Syrian father crosses seas to save his ailing son
stories.summary: Abdulaziz Aldarwish, a Syrian father, undertook a dangerous sea crossing to Athens seeking medical treatment after his son Yahia suffered kidney failure.

stories.title: Scott Mills sacked by BBC after allegations about his personal conduct
stories.summary: The BBC fired Radio 2 breakfast show presenter Scott Mills over allegations about his personal conduct related to a reported 'historic relationship.' Mills, who hosted Britain's most popular radio breakfast show, was taken off air and had his contract terminated.

stories.title: Palestine Action hunger striker arrested in dawn raid by masked police
stories.summary: British police arrested 21-year-old Palestine Action activist Qesser Zuhrah in a dawn raid by masked officers. Zuhrah had previously conducted a 46-day hunger strike to protest her detention conditions during 15 months of remand. Her arrest reportedly followed an Instagram post calling for 'direct action.'

stories.title: UK comedian Russell Brand trial on rape, sex assault charges delayed
stories.summary: A London judge ruled Monday that British comedian and actor Russell Brand's trial on seven charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women will take place in October.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone masters eye Iran war to kick-start export ambitions
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone manufacturers are looking at the Iran war as an opportunity to expand their military drone technology into global export markets. The Middle East conflict could serve as a proving ground for Ukrainian-made systems.

stories.title: Iranian livelihoods are being blown apart by US and Israeli bombs
stories.summary: US and Israeli air strikes are devastating small businesses in Tehran, leaving Iranian civilians jobless and indebted. A café in the Iranian capital was among the premises destroyed in a strike on March 29, 2026.

stories.title: Gulf states harden positions against Iran as economic toll of war mounts
stories.summary: Gulf Arab states are hardening their positions against Iran as the economic toll of the ongoing conflict mounts. Closure of the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on energy infrastructure are driving Arab states to push for the war to continue until specific demands are met.

stories.title: Israel shifts to hitting Iran’s economy, as it enters ‘completion phase’ of war
stories.summary: Israel has shifted its military strategy to targeting Iran's economic infrastructure as it enters what officials describe as the 'completion phase' of the war. The IDF has nearly finished striking all military targets outlined at the campaign's outset and is now focused on causing economic damage to the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Four in Gaza and West Bank killed by Israeli fire, health officials say
stories.summary: Israeli fire killed four people in Gaza and the West Bank, Palestinian health officials reported. The violence persisted despite the Gaza ceasefire and amid the broader U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

stories.title: Russia expels British diplomat on spying allegations
stories.summary: Russia expelled a British diplomat on allegations of espionage. The diplomat was ordered to leave the country within two weeks.

stories.title: New US missile hit Iranian sports hall and school, analysis shows
stories.summary: Analysis revealed that a new U.S. missile struck an Iranian sports hall and school. Children at volleyball practice in the sports hall were among the 21 casualties of the strike.

stories.title: US copies Ukraine: Washington launches Amazon-backed UAVs marketplace, inspired by Kyiv’s Brave1 Market and DOT-Chain Defense
stories.summary: Washington launched an Amazon-backed UAV marketplace inspired by Ukraine's Brave1 Market and DOT-Chain Defense platforms. The system compares specifications, analyzes user feedback, and simplifies procurement for defense customers.

stories.title: Drone purchases in Russia and Iran surge using crypto, report says
stories.summary: A new report reveals that pro-Russia groups have raised more than $8.3 million in cryptocurrency donations since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to purchase drones. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has also been linked to a crypto wallet used to buy drone components abroad.

stories.title: Serbia extends its gas import agreement with Russia for another three months
stories.summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić extended his country's gas import agreement with Russia for an additional three months following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Bab al-Mandab strait: Iran’s Houthi allies enter the conflict, raising fears over key trade route
stories.summary: Iran has threatened to disrupt shipping in the Bab al-Mandab Strait with the help of its Houthi allies in Yemen, who have entered the broader Middle East conflict. Blocking this strategic waterway linking the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea and Suez Canal could disrupt European energy supplies and Asian imports.

stories.title: How Spain's memory of Iraq shaped Sanchez's response to war on Iran
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has opposed the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran since its outset, drawing on Spain's experience with the Iraq War. His anti-war stance is reportedly gaining broader traction among European leaders.

stories.title: ‘Strait of Hormuz will reopen one way or another’, Rubio tells Al Jazeera
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Al Jazeera that the United States will not accept Iran's claim over the Strait of Hormuz. Rubio stated that the strategically vital waterway will be reopened 'one way or another.'

stories.title: UK must have independent nuclear deterrent, says major parliamentary report
stories.summary: A major UK parliamentary report from the Joint Committee on the National Security Strategy argues Britain must maintain an independent nuclear deterrent. The report recommends reducing dependence on the United States for nuclear and intelligence capabilities.

stories.title: Naftogaz, Greek delegation discuss expanding LNG supplies via Vertical Gas Corridor
stories.summary: Executives of Ukraine's Naftogaz met with a Greek delegation to discuss expanding liquefied natural gas supplies via the Vertical Gas Corridor, aimed at broadening energy cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Many Jewish Americans have holiday plans canceled as others seek path home from Israel
stories.summary: Disruptions caused by war have left many Jewish Americans stranded or forced to reroute through Egypt and Jordan when traveling from Israel. Some families with ties to Israel have had holiday plans canceled, leaving relatives separated.

stories.title: Spain summons Israeli envoy over Latin Patriarch’s church access
stories.summary: Spain summoned Israel's envoy over the blocking of the Latin Patriarch's access to a church. Spanish officials denounced the action as an "attack on religious freedom."

stories.title: Iran War Shatters South Asians’ Gulf Dreams
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is severely disrupting South Asian migrant workers' prospects in the Gulf region. Flights and job opportunities are vanishing as the conflict continues to destabilize the area's economy.

stories.title: Iran says expelled ambassador won't leave Lebanon
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador to Lebanon has refused to leave Beirut despite a Lebanese government expulsion order. The defiance has heightened diplomatic tensions amid the ongoing conflict in Lebanon.

stories.title: First study of Ukraine’s 160,000 mothers of disabled children finds 15% contemplated self-harm. 70% get zero hours of respite.
stories.summary: A first-of-its-kind study of Ukraine's approximately 160,000 mothers of disabled children found that 15% had contemplated self-harm and 70% receive no respite care whatsoever.

stories.title: News outlets falsely report Somaliland called for extradition of Ilhan Omar
stories.summary: Multiple news outlets, including Fox News and the New York Post, falsely reported that Somaliland's government called for the extradition of U.S. Representative Ilhan Omar. The reports were based on a post from an unofficial X account that does not represent the Somaliland government.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 30 in attack on university community in Nigeria's Plateau state
stories.summary: Gunmen killed at least 30 people in an attack on a university community in Nigeria's Plateau state. The state government said the attackers were unidentified and imposed a 48-hour curfew in the affected district. The University of Jos suspended examinations that were scheduled to begin on Monday.

stories.title: USF destroys satellite antenna used by Russians as alternative to Starlink
stories.summary: Fighters of the "Raid" regiment of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces detected and destroyed a Russian communication antenna configured to the Yamal-601 satellite, which served as an alternative to Starlink on one section of the front.

stories.title: The Corruption Engine Behind Sebastián Marset’s Empire
stories.summary: An investigation reveals the corruption network behind Uruguayan drug trafficker Sebastián Marset's criminal empire. In October 2020, Paraguayan congressman Erico Galeano Segovia and businessman Hugo Manuel González Ramos signed a property deal linked to Marset's operations near Asunción, Paraguay.

stories.title: Punjab schools to open on April 1 with classes five-days a week, minister says
stories.summary: Punjab province in Pakistan announced that schools will reopen on April 1 with five-day weekly schedules. Educational institutions had been closed since March 10 due to the global fuel crisis triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Missile-wielding Airbus interceptor engages one-way attack drone in test
stories.summary: Airbus has tested a missile-armed drone interceptor against a one-way attack drone. The manufacturers claim the drone-missile combination makes large-scale aerial interception economically viable compared to traditional defense systems.

stories.title: Kyiv useful to US, Gulf at critical time: Drone interceptors 'more effective than Patriot missiles'
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskiy's outreach to Gulf states reflects efforts to reposition Ukraine within shifting global alliances, according to Dr. Samuel Ramani of the Royal United Services Institute. The strategy aims to strengthen ties with Gulf nations, reinforce Ukraine's value to the U.S., and attract defense investment.

stories.title: France investigates possible Iran link after bomb attack foiled outside Bank of America
stories.summary: French authorities are investigating a possible Iranian link to a foiled bomb attack outside a Bank of America building in Paris. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the suspected connection stems from similarities to other recent attempted attacks in Europe claimed by a pro-Iran group.

stories.title: Moscow Patriarchate monk in Ukraine lured underage girls with sweets, gave them alcohol so they couldn’t resist
stories.summary: A Moscow Patriarchate monk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region has been charged with sexual crimes against underage girls, allegedly luring them with sweets and giving them alcohol to prevent resistance.
