stories.summary: Large-scale "No Kings" protests took place across the United States and in parts of Europe on Saturday, opposing President Trump's policies and the war in Iran. Minnesota drew particularly large crowds rallying against aggressive immigration enforcement.

stories.title: Israeli police bar top Catholic figure in Jerusalem from holding Palm Sunday mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli police barred the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday mass. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the incident, though it remains unclear whether the blockade was intentional.

stories.title: Lebanon mourns three journalists killed in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners gathered south of Beirut to attend funerals for journalists Ali Shoeib, Fatima Ftouni, and Mohammed Ftouni, killed in an Israeli airstrike. Israel acknowledged the attack, claiming Shoeib had militant affiliations, while Lebanese officials condemned it as a violation of international law.

stories.title: Iranian missile hit on Ne'ot Hovav factory leads to fear of chemical leakage
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck a factory in the Ne'ot Hovav industrial zone in southern Israel, raising fears of chemical leakage. Israel's Environmental Protection Ministry said it was investigating but found no immediate risk to nearby communities.

stories.title: Funeral held for Lebanese journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Lebanon held funerals for three journalists killed in an Israeli strike on Saturday. The journalists were targeted while reporting in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Drone attacks hit Iraqi Kurdistan amid Iran war
stories.summary: Drone strikes hit multiple targets in Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region, including the residence of the Barzani family and a US-linked military base. The attacks occurred amid escalating violence connected to the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Russia put a hula hoop on its attack drone. Now it flies 50 km into Ukraine’s rear.
stories.summary: Russian forces have added a plastic hula-hoop-shaped ring to attack drones, reportedly enabling them to fly up to 50 kilometers deeper into Ukrainian-held territory to target logistics and supply lines.

stories.title: Iran hits industrial zone in southern Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile barrage struck a chemical plant near Beersheba in southern Israel, causing a fire at the facility.

stories.title: The war with Iran may be ushering in a new nuclear age
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is accelerating nuclear proliferation concerns, as nations increasingly believe that forgoing nuclear weapons leaves them vulnerable. Analysts warn the conflict may be ushering in a new nuclear age driven by a global scramble for atomic deterrence.

stories.title: FM Sybiha: Giving platform to war criminals has nothing to do with free speech
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's appearance on a major French television channel, saying giving a platform to those he characterized as war criminals is not a matter of free speech. The remarks coincided with the G7 summit in France.

stories.title: Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem prevented from entering Church of Holy Sepulchre by Israel Police
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa and Father Francesco Ielpo, Guardian of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, from entering the church to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Elite sports training opens new doors for Hong Kong youth
stories.summary: A youth fencing event was held at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong, featuring national silver medallist Ho Sze-long and junior medallist Chan Lok-hei. Nearly 170 young fencers competed in the Champions Cup for spots in an elite training program.

stories.title: Islamabad to ramp up cooperation with Ankara, Cairo in areas of mutual interest
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Türkiye and Egypt met with Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad to strengthen bilateral cooperation. The meetings took place ahead of a quadrilateral gathering involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt, which is seen as a diplomatic effort linked to ending regional conflict.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts regional powers for Iran talks, focus on Hormuz
stories.summary: Turkish, Egyptian, and Saudi officials arrived in Islamabad on Sunday for multilateral talks focused on de-escalating Middle East tensions, with a particular emphasis on security around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Jurgen Habermas' death ends the illusion of a universal European philosophy
stories.summary: German philosopher Jürgen Habermas died on 14 March 2026. His legacy is being reassessed in light of his stance on Gaza, which critics say exposed limitations in European philosophical traditions long considered universal.

stories.title: Russia's Ust-Luga port damaged by Ukrainian drones, fire breaks out
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a drone attack on Russia's Ust-Luga port in the Leningrad region, one of the country's largest petroleum export facilities. Governor Alexander Drozdenko confirmed the port sustained damage and a fire broke out.

stories.title: Israelis told to stay indoors after strike on chemical site
stories.summary: Authorities in southern Israel urged residents to stay indoors after an Iranian missile strike damaged a chemical storage facility in the Neot Hovav industrial zone near Beersheba. No injuries were reported, but fears of a hazardous materials leak prompted shelter-in-place orders.

stories.title: Philippine oil refiner Petron buys Russian crude, eyes alternatives
stories.summary: Petron Corp., the Philippines' sole oil refiner, purchased 2.48 million barrels of Russian crude oil as the country seeks alternative energy suppliers amid disruptions caused by the war in Iran. Parent company San Miguel Corp. said Petron may continue sourcing Russian crude if the crisis persists.

stories.title: How many missiles have fallen on the Pope’s children? - comment
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses the tension between Pope Leo's calls for restraint and condemnation of war and the perspective of Israelis who face daily missile threats from Iran.

stories.title: Iran Parliament Speaker says U.S. plots ground attack despite diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged national unity, claiming the United States is plotting a ground attack on Iran despite ongoing diplomatic efforts. He characterized the current situation as a critical stage of what he called a major global war.

stories.title: Russian forces drop aerial bomb on Kramatorsk, killing three and wounding seven
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped an aerial bomb on the city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine, killing three people including a teenager and wounding seven others.

stories.title: Three arrested in Paris after attempted bomb attack outside Bank of America
stories.summary: Three people were arrested in Paris after an attempted bomb attack outside a Bank of America branch. France's anti-terrorism prosecutor's office immediately assumed control of the investigation.

stories.title: Venezuela’s ousted leader Maduro thanks supporters in first online post from US prison
stories.summary: Venezuela's ousted leader Nicolás Maduro posted his first online message from a US prison, thanking supporters. Maduro and his wife were captured by US forces in January.

stories.title: Renewed air strike targets university in Isfahan
stories.summary: An air strike hit the Isfahan University of Technology in Iran on Sunday, the second attack on the institution in one week. Provincial official Akbar Salehi said the strike damaged several buildings and wounded four staff members. Iran's IRGC warned of possible retaliation.

stories.title: Israeli police block Catholic cardinal from Holy Sepulchre on Palm Sunday
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented a Catholic cardinal from accessing the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, with authorities citing safety concerns related to the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Funeral held for Lebanese journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Hundreds attended a funeral in Beirut's southern suburbs for three Lebanese journalists killed in an Israeli strike.

stories.title: UK’s Green Party fails to pass ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion after infighting, tech issues
stories.summary: The UK Green Party failed to pass a motion at its conference that would have declared "Zionism is Racism" and called for Israel's replacement with a single Palestinian state. The vote was postponed due to internal disagreements and technical problems.

stories.title: Hundreds in Beirut mourn journalists killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners gathered in Beirut for the funerals of three journalists killed by an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon, as reported by the BBC.

stories.title: Israel, US cannot miss the chance to disarm Hezbollah - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel and the United States should seize the opportunity presented by Hezbollah's weakened state to push for its disarmament, urging that the Lebanese state enforce this before 2026.

stories.title: Houthis open new front in Iran war: Will Yemeni group block Bab al-Mandeb?
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement is reportedly considering a blockade of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, one of the world's busiest maritime chokepoints, which could severely disrupt global trade amid the broader Iran conflict.

stories.title: Africa: CAF's Senegal Decision Exposes a Deeper Crisis in African Football
stories.summary: The Confederation of African Football penalized Senegal for walking out of a match, a decision that has drawn criticism as emblematic of deeper institutional governance problems within African football.

stories.title: No tuition, no grades, no power grid: why are people flocking to a ‘college’ in the middle of the desert?
stories.summary: Mars College, an off-grid community located roughly 200 miles from Los Angeles with roots in Burning Man, offers a tuition-free, ungraded educational experience in the desert. The experimental program has been attracting growing interest.

stories.title: Government allocates ₴22.35 billion to protect critical infrastructure, says Kuleba
stories.summary: The Ukrainian government allocated 22.35 billion hryvnias for the construction of protective structures for critical water, heating, electricity, and railway infrastructure, according to official Kuleba.

stories.title: Over 5,000 still in need of food for Pesach - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A charitable appeal highlighted that over 5,000 families in Israel still need food assistance for Passover, with some requesting help for the first time due to school closures preventing parents from working.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl injured in shelling of Mykolaiv region dies in hospital
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl who was wounded during Russian shelling of the Voskresenske community in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region has died in hospital from her injuries.

stories.title: France's Macron condemns Israeli police blocking Jerusalem's Latin Patriarch
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned Israeli police for blocking Latin Patriarch Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa from celebrating Palm Sunday Mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. Macron called it part of a troubling pattern of violations of the status of holy places in the city.

stories.title: 30 Days of War - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish People Policy Institute announced a public webinar assessing whether objectives of the current war have been met after 30 days and examining challenges and opportunities ahead.

stories.title: Day of zero waste: International Chef Massimo Bottura speaks to France 24
stories.summary: The UN's International Day of Zero Waste highlighted the issue of food sustainability, noting that roughly one billion tonnes of edible food is discarded annually worldwide. Chef Massimo Bottura, a UN Environment Programme Goodwill Ambassador based in Modena, Italy, discussed efforts to combat food waste.

stories.title: Qatari news channel AI Araby condemns attack on its office
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary speaker warned the United States against a ground invasion, threatening intensified attacks on U.S. allies. Meanwhile, diplomats from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt gathered in Pakistan to push for an end to the Iran conflict as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a 15-point peace proposal. An American-born Israeli soldier was killed in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: How the US memeifies its war on Iran
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Linh Nguyen examined how the United States has employed meme-based propaganda techniques in its military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan maintains ‘delicate balancing act’ as it hosts Iran talks
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from multiple countries met in Islamabad, Pakistan, for diplomatic talks aimed at de-escalating the US-Israel war on Iran, as Pakistan navigates a careful balancing act among regional powers.

stories.title: Pentagon reportedly preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran. U.S. military assets, including the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit, continue to deploy to the region.

stories.title: How safe are Israel’s safe rooms? - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines the effectiveness of Israel's residential safe rooms after incidents in Petah Tikva. The Home Front Command acknowledged that safe rooms are not designed to withstand direct missile hits.

stories.title: Iran: 3.500 US troops arrive in the region
stories.summary: Iran's navy chief warned that the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier would be targeted as soon as it enters range. Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Washington of planning a ground attack on Iran while claiming to pursue diplomacy, as approximately 3,500 additional U.S. troops arrived in the region.

stories.title: Pope seems to rebuke Trump in remarks about leaders with ‘hands full of blood’
stories.summary: Pope Leo stated that God ignores the prayers of leaders who wage war and have "hands full of blood," in remarks widely interpreted as directed at the Trump administration. The comments followed U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's public prayer calling for violence against enemies deserving "no mercy."

stories.title: Woman killed and two people wounded in Zaporizhzhia region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: A woman was killed and two men were wounded by Russian shelling in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: Pope Leo condemns using God to justify war in Palm Sunday mass
stories.summary: Pope Leo condemned the use of God to justify warfare during his Palm Sunday Mass, saying God rejects the prayers of those who wage war with "hands full of blood." He also prayed specifically for Christians in the Middle East.

stories.title: ‘Nowhere is really safe’: Iranian dissidents grapple with US war in Iran
stories.summary: Iranian dissidents living in exile say they face dual fears amid the US war on Iran: potential retribution from Iran's government and rising anti-immigrant sentiment in their host countries.

stories.title: Israel army says impact on industrial complex could be from missile shrapnel
stories.summary: The Israeli military said an impact at the Ramat Hovav industrial zone in the Negev desert may have been caused by missile shrapnel following a new barrage fired from Iran. Israeli television showed thick black smoke rising from the site.

stories.title: Pentagon preparing for US ground assault in Iran, says report
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that the Pentagon is preparing options for a ground assault in Iran as thousands of U.S. troops and marines arrive in the Middle East. Officials said any such operation would involve raids rather than a full-scale invasion.

stories.title: First PIA direct flight to London in 6 years takes to the skies
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines resumed direct flights from Islamabad to London's Heathrow Airport for the first time in six years. The inaugural flight, PK-785, was launched at a ceremony attended by Pakistan's Defence Secretary, the British High Commissioner, and PIA Consortium Chairman Arif Habib. Four weekly flights are planned.

stories.title: Knesset set to hold final 2 votes on passing 2026 state budget
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset was set to hold its final two votes on the 2026 state budget ahead of a March 31 deadline. The spending plan increases defense funding amid the war with Iran and includes allocations for ultra-Orthodox constituencies. Failure to pass would trigger early elections.

stories.title: Ukrainian FM: Another country to join agreement on Special Tribunal for Russia’s aggression
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced at the G7 summit in France that another country has indicated readiness to join the agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Arkia cancels Jordan flights after authorities block approvals, limiting alternatives from Israel
stories.summary: Israeli airline Arkia canceled flights to Jordan after Jordanian authorities blocked flight approvals. Some flights were rerouted to Taba, Egypt, where crossing fees have been doubled.

stories.title: Police stop top Catholic figures from reaching Holy Sepulchre for Palm Sunday Mass
stories.summary: Israeli police blocked the Latin Patriarch from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre for Palm Sunday Mass in Jerusalem, citing wartime security. The Prime Minister's office said there was no malicious intent and promised a resolution amid international criticism.

stories.title: A toothless Iran? Missile and drone strikes show it can still inflict pain
stories.summary: Despite sustained US-Israeli strikes, Iran demonstrated a continued capacity to retaliate through a wave of recent missile and drone attacks targeting adversaries in the region.

stories.title: Al Araby TV condemns Israeli attack on Tehran office
stories.summary: Al Araby TV condemned an Israeli strike on the building housing its Tehran office, calling the attack on a civilian commercial building a violation of international law. The Iranian Red Crescent Society said at least 10 people were wounded in the strike.

stories.title: ‘Doctrine of the Mean’: how the US lost a 2-decade race to China in brain implants
stories.summary: A Chinese research team has developed a commercially approved semi-invasive brain-computer interface using a middle-path approach, overtaking the United States in a technology race that Washington had led for two decades.

stories.title: Farmers plead for tax breaks, diesel guarantees and help buying fertiliser as national cabinet meets on fuel crisis
stories.summary: Australian farmers are urging the federal government for tax breaks, diesel supply guarantees, and fertiliser purchasing assistance amid a fuel crisis driven by rising petrol prices. National cabinet was set to meet Monday to discuss broader assistance for affected business sectors.

stories.title: Helplines buzz with alerts from seafarers trapped in war
stories.summary: Over 1,000 emails and messages have been received from seafarers stranded near the Strait of Hormuz as the Middle East conflict disrupts maritime traffic and traps crews aboard their vessels.

stories.title: From appeasement to escalation: Europe's dangerous Iran blind spot - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between Europe's appeasement of hostile ideologies in the 1930s and what it describes as Europe's current failure to confront Iran's stated ambitions.

stories.title: Israel blocks top Catholic leaders from Palm Sunday Mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli forces blocked Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, and Father Francesco Ielpo, custos of the Holy Land, from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in occupied East Jerusalem to celebrate Palm Sunday Mass.

stories.title: Finland reports drone crashes, alleges territorial violation
stories.summary: Two unidentified drones crashed in southern Finland. Finnish Prime Minister stated the drones may have been Ukrainian drones that strayed into Finnish airspace, and authorities are investigating a possible territorial violation.

stories.title: Enemy attacks Naftogaz facilities for fourth day; damage reported
stories.summary: Russian troops attacked Naftogaz Group production facilities in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones, marking the fourth consecutive day of strikes. Damage to the energy infrastructure was reported.

stories.title: Palestinian economy recedes by 20% over two years amid Gaza War
stories.summary: The Palestinian economy has contracted by approximately 20 percent over two years due to Israel's military operations in Gaza and intensified restrictions in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli footballer’s role in assault on southern Lebanon sparks outrage
stories.summary: Israeli Premier League player Menashe Zalka was filmed firing alongside Israeli army soldiers during an assault in southern Lebanon, generating widespread public backlash.

stories.title: Indonesia cuts free meals to save US$2.3 billion as fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Indonesia announced it will reduce its free school meal program from six to five days per week, aiming to save approximately 40 trillion rupiah (US$2.3 billion). The austerity measure responds to price pressures stemming from the Middle East war.

stories.title: Iran ‘hits’ US AWACS, air tankers: What else has it targeted in past month?
stories.summary: Iran reportedly struck U.S. E-3 Sentry airborne early-warning aircraft, which are used to track drones, missiles, and aircraft from hundreds of kilometers away, as part of a series of Iranian attacks over the past month.

stories.title: Bahrain announces curfew for maritime traffic
stories.summary: Bahrain announced a nighttime maritime curfew from 6:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time to protect seafarers and enhance coastal security amid Iranian attacks on the region.

stories.title: Fire Reported After Ukrainian Strike on Ust-Luga Port
stories.summary: A fire was reported at Russia's Ust-Luga port in the northwest after it was targeted by drones in an attack claimed by Ukraine's military.

stories.title: The week in pictures: Massive daytime attack on Ukraine, 'No Kings' and France's adieu to Jospin
stories.summary: France held a national tribute to former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, Russia launched one of its largest daytime attacks on Ukraine, and a third round of "No Kings" protests against President Trump took place across the US and other capitals.

stories.title: Sybiha: Weapons from PURL not to be redirected; another country to join program
stories.summary: At the G7 summit in France, US partners assured Ukraine that weapons allocated under the PURL program would not be redirected. An additional country expressed interest in joining the program to procure weapons for Ukraine, according to Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha.

stories.title: Israeli army kills 6 Palestinians in attack on Gaza police
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least six Palestinians in strikes targeting police checkpoints in the al-Mawasi area near Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Pope Leo says God rejects prayers of leaders who wage wars
stories.summary: Pope Leo used his Palm Sunday address at St. Peter's Square to criticize wars and express concern for Christians in the Middle East, saying God rejects the prayers of leaders who wage wars.

stories.title: Lebanese family launches mobile aid initiative for displaced
stories.summary: A Lebanese family in Beirut launched a mobile aid initiative to provide support to people displaced by the ongoing conflict in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russia wants to legalize cars stolen in EU
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly considering legislation that would allow the legal registration of vehicles stolen from European Union countries, raising concerns among German police that it could incentivize increased car thefts across Europe.

stories.title: DR Congo conflict: M23’s alleged withdrawal shrouded in confusion
stories.summary: Conflicting reports from local sources, rebel leaders, and the Kinshasa government have left it unclear whether M23 fighters in the Democratic Republic of Congo are genuinely withdrawing or simply rotating troops along front lines.

stories.title: One in five UK hospitality businesses fear collapse as costs surge
stories.summary: A UK industry survey found that one in five hospitality businesses fear collapse within the next 12 months. Pubs, restaurants, and hotels face mounting pressure from upcoming increases in business rates and minimum wage thresholds taking effect.

stories.title: ‘No Kings’ flagship protest brings spotlight back to Minneapolis
stories.summary: Bruce Springsteen headlined a "No Kings" rally in St. Paul, Minnesota, declaring that "invasions will not stand." The event was part of a broader series of protests drawing public attention back to Minneapolis and the Twin Cities area.

stories.title: Nepal's former Energy Minister arrested in money laundering probe
stories.summary: Nepal's former Energy Minister was arrested in a money laundering investigation, one day after ex-Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak were detained over a deadly crackdown on anti-corruption protesters in September.

stories.title: JD Vance’s Jewish chief of staff seems unfazed by GOP antisemitism – though he’s a target
stories.summary: A New York Magazine profile reveals that Jacob Reses, the Jewish chief of staff to U.S. Vice President JD Vance, shares Vance's reluctance to confront antisemitic figures on the political right.

stories.title: Unmanned Systems Forces destroy three Russian Smerch multiple rocket launchers overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces destroyed three Russian BM-30 Smerch/Tornado-S multiple rocket launchers overnight on March 29. The strikes targeted occupied Crimea and fuel tanks in the occupied portion of the Luhansk region.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Baltic port, hundreds of drones shot down
stories.summary: Ukraine claimed a drone strike that ignited a fire at Russia's Baltic port of Ust-Luga, marking the second hit on the major export hub in days. Ukraine has intensified strikes on Russian infrastructure including refineries, oil depots, and ports to disrupt war funding.

stories.title: Drap dismisses reports of essential medicine price hikes amid global supply chain uncertainty
stories.summary: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority dismissed reports of essential medicine price hikes, stating prices had not been officially revised upward. However, stakeholders alleged significant increases since February 2024, including a reported 114% rise in the price of the insulin device HumaPen Ergo II.

stories.title: Quieter, stealthier, further: new hybrid unit to power China’s small battle drones
stories.summary: China has completed flight tests of a hybrid propulsion system for small battlefield drones, combining fuel-powered electricity generation with electric motors. The system is designed to increase stealth and extend the operational range of small military drones.

stories.title: A costly plan will keep a steel plant in JD Vance’s hometown running. Locals are aghast: ‘It’s horrible’
stories.summary: A plan to extend fossil-fuel burning at a steel plant in Middletown, Ohio — Vice President JD Vance's hometown — is drawing concern from residents over environmental and health risks, including worsened asthma conditions among children.

stories.title: Americans struggle as Iran war puts strain on everyday costs: ‘I’m worried we won’t make it through’
stories.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran has driven sharp increases in everyday costs for Americans, with gas prices rising roughly 30 percent over the past month. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and retaliatory strikes have disrupted global markets, pushing up grocery bills and mortgage rates.

stories.title: Collection of 7,000-year-old ostrich eggs discovered under sand dunes in southern Israel
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered a collection of ostrich eggs estimated to be 7,000 years old beneath sand dunes in southern Israel, near the remains of a campfire linked to prehistoric desert nomads.

stories.title: Unidentified drones crash in Finland
stories.summary: Two unidentified drones crashed in southern Finland on Sunday, prompting the defence ministry to describe it as a suspected territorial violation. Estonia, Lithuania, and Latvia experienced similar drone incidents on their territory earlier in the week.

stories.title: Iran vows to target USS Abraham Lincoln carrier if it moves within range
stories.summary: Iran's navy chief Shahram Irani stated that the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier would be targeted with sea-to-sea missiles if it enters firing range. He said the strike would avenge the Iranian frigate Dena, which was sunk by the U.S. on March 4.

stories.title: Israel blocks top Catholic leaders from Palm Sunday Mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Israeli police barred the Latin Patriarch and other senior Catholic leaders from reaching the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem for Palm Sunday Mass, citing wartime safety concerns. Church bodies condemned the move as setting a grave precedent. Prime Minister Netanyahu's office promised a resolution.

stories.title: Israel prevents Jerusalem Latin Patriarch from celebrating mass
stories.summary: Israeli police prevented Jerusalem's Latin Patriarch, Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, from celebrating Palm Sunday Mass at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

stories.title: ‘It’s biblical’: Maga anxiety over Iran war on display at CPAC as Trump skips event
stories.summary: At the annual CPAC gathering near Dallas, supporters of President Trump expressed a mix of support and anxiety over the Iran war. Trump did not attend the event, and attendees voiced concerns about the conflict's direction and consequences.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Lebanon ambulance kills paramedic and patient
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on an ambulance in southern Lebanon killed a paramedic and a patient as Israel continued its military operations in the area.

stories.title: Sybiha: Ukrainian drones and anti-drone systems are our “oil”
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha described Ukrainian drones and anti-drone systems as a strategic resource comparable to oil. He emphasized Ukraine's importance for European security and broader regional processes, including in the Middle East.

stories.title: Russian students duped into signing contracts with military
stories.summary: Reports indicate that Russian university students are being recruited into military drone units fighting in Ukraine with promises of lucrative pay and assurances they will not be sent to the front lines. Those promises are reportedly not always honored.

stories.title: Mediation talks in Islamabad: Middle East powers meet to discuss how to end the fighting
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused the US of planning a ground attack on Iran while claiming to pursue diplomacy, as more American Marines arrived in the region. Meanwhile, regional powers convened mediation talks in Islamabad to discuss ending the conflict.

stories.title: Europe’s response to Iran war risks becoming its ‘darkest hour’
stories.summary: The European Union faces a difficult position regarding the Iran war, with public opinion opposing the conflict while the continent remains dependent on the United States for energy and security. Taking a definitive anti-war stance risks alienating President Trump.

stories.title: Russia Reports Fire in Strike on Major Baltic Port
stories.summary: A major port in Russia's Baltic region suffered damage and fire after being targeted by drones in an attack claimed by Ukraine's military.

stories.title: Iran strike on Saudi Arabia’s Sultan Airbase destroys key US Air Force platforms
stories.summary: An Iranian strike on Saudi Arabia's Sultan Airbase on Friday destroyed U.S. Air Force refueling aircraft and an E-3 Sentry early-warning plane, in addition to injuring troops stationed at the base.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russians launch over 3,000 drones, more than 1,450 guided aerial bombs, and 40 missiles at Ukraine this week
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported that Russian forces launched over 3,000 drones, more than 1,450 guided aerial bombs, and 40 missiles of various types at Ukraine over the past week.

stories.title: U.S., Israeli strikes hit Iran port city near Strait of Hormuz: state media
stories.summary: Loud explosions were heard across Tehran as US and Israeli forces struck a port city near the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media.

stories.title: Iran targets Bahrain aluminium, 2 injured amid Hormuz closure
stories.summary: Iranian strikes hit Aluminium Bahrain, one of the world's largest smelters, injuring two employees. Emirates Global Aluminium in the UAE also sustained significant damage from missile and drone strikes the same day, amid the broader Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure.

stories.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: GHOSTS ON THE SCREEN
stories.summary: A column discusses the pattern of Western media scheduling Holocaust-related content in response to international criticism of Israeli military actions in the Middle East.

stories.title: UAE adviser calls for guarantees and compensation in any deal with Iran
stories.summary: UAE diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash said any political resolution to the conflict with Iran must include guarantees against future attacks and compensation for Iranian strikes on civilian infrastructure across Gulf states.

stories.title: Brace yourself for conditions at fire-hit Wang Fuk Court, returning residents told
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities warned former residents of fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court to prepare for poor conditions when they return in April to collect belongings. Officials distributed psychological assessment questionnaires and advised those with health issues not to enter the buildings.

stories.title: Israel kills Palestinian girl and police officers in Gaza bombing
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit two police checkpoints in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip, killing a Palestinian girl and police officers amid continuing ceasefire violations.

stories.title: The US-Israeli war on humanity
stories.summary: An article alleges that U.S.-Israeli military operations in Gaza have expanded in scope, affecting other parts of the world amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un oversees test of high-thrust engine: state media
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw a ground test of an upgraded high-thrust rocket engine, state media KCNA reported. Defense experts assess that North Korea intends to use solid-fuel engines for intercontinental ballistic missiles, which enable faster launches with minimal preparation.

stories.title: Danish Eurovision contestant addresses pro-Israel Instagram story backlash
stories.summary: Danish Eurovision contestant faced backlash over a pro-Israel Instagram story. Several participating countries have called for Israel's exclusion from Eurovision due to the war in Gaza, but the European Broadcasting Union declined to hold a vote on the matter.

stories.title: Man arrested for attempted murder after car hits pedestrians in UK, wounding 7
stories.summary: A man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a car struck pedestrians in Derbyshire, United Kingdom, injuring seven people. Police said the suspect was originally from India, and a government minister said there was no wider public threat.

stories.title: Under shadow of war with Iran, Jerusalem heads into subdued Passover and Easter
stories.summary: Jerusalem's Passover and Easter celebrations were subdued after Iranian missile fragments fell in the Old City. Israel's Home Front Command limited religious gatherings to 50 people amid the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: US-Israeli plan for Kurdish invasion of Iran reportedly collapsed amid leaks, distrust
stories.summary: A reported U.S.-Israeli plan for a Kurdish ground incursion into Iran, intended to spark a wider rebellion, collapsed after the plan was leaked. Iran subsequently bolstered its defenses and regional U.S. allies lobbied President Trump to abandon the operation.

stories.title: Japan upgrades destroyer with Tomahawk missiles. Why it might pose a threat to China
stories.summary: Japan's Aegis destroyer Chokai has been upgraded with Tomahawk long-range missile launch capabilities following modifications and crew training in the United States. Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi confirmed the upgrade, with a first firing test expected this summer.

stories.title: Toxic Pfas residue identified on 37% of California produce, new analysis finds
stories.summary: A new analysis found PFAS pesticide residues on 37 percent of conventional California produce, with peaches, strawberries, and grapes nearly always contaminated. California legislators have introduced a bill to fully ban PFAS as active pesticide ingredients by 2035.

stories.title: Ten wounded in Mykolaiv region in past 24 hours, nine of them children
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the Voskresenka community in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region injured ten people, including nine children. Three of the wounded are in critical condition.

stories.title: Israeli police bar top Catholic figure in Jerusalem from holding Palm Sunday mass at Holy Sepulchre
stories.summary: Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, was prevented by Israeli police from entering the Church of the Holy Sepulchre to celebrate Palm Sunday mass. His office confirmed the incident, which drew condemnation from Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who called it an "offence to the faithful," and prompted a response from French President Emmanuel Macron.

stories.title: Bets that anticipated Trump's policy surprises warrant scrutiny
stories.summary: Experts are urging authorities to investigate possible insider trading linked to a series of well-timed trades that preceded policy announcements by President Trump.

stories.title: French prosecutors open terror probe after Bank of America attack attempt
stories.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutors opened an investigation into a suspected attack on Bank of America's Paris headquarters. A suspect was arrested overnight after allegedly attempting to ignite an improvised explosive device outside the building.

stories.title: France: Two new arrests over foiled Bank of America attack
stories.summary: French police arrested two additional suspects in connection with a foiled attack on Bank of America's Paris offices. The custody of the first suspect, who was arrested earlier, has been extended.

stories.title: Al Araby TV office in Tehran hit by missile strike
stories.summary: A missile strike damaged Al Araby TV's office in Tehran, injuring 10 people and cutting the channel's live broadcast. The attack occurred amid the continuing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Protests erupt in Syrian Christian city Al-Suqaylabiyah, demand security accountability
stories.summary: Protests erupted in the Syrian Christian city of Al-Suqaylabiyah amid heightened security tensions. The unrest followed an altercation that escalated into a broader mobilization, with demonstrators demanding security accountability.

stories.title: Milei's Cabinet Chief formally charged with alleged illicit enrichment
stories.summary: Argentine Cabinet Chief Manuel Adorni has been formally charged with alleged illicit enrichment. Federal prosecutor Gerardo Pollicita requested twelve evidentiary measures from Judge Ariel Lijo to reconstruct Adorni's asset history since 2022.

stories.title: France foils bomb attack outside Bank of America in Paris
stories.summary: French police thwarted an apparent bomb attack outside a Bank of America branch in Paris on Saturday. The French counter-terrorism prosecutor's office opened an investigation into what it described as a "terrorist criminal conspiracy." Details of the plot and any suspects involved were reported by FRANCE 2.

stories.title: Israeli strike on ambulance kills paramedic in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on an ambulance in southern Lebanon killed a paramedic and a patient, according to the Islamic Health Committee. The attack followed the killing of nine first responders the previous day. Approximately 47 paramedics have been killed in Lebanon since the conflict began.

stories.title: A week to forget for Milei: Adorni scandal, skeptical markets, cultural battle collapse
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei's administration faced one of its worst weeks, beset by an expanding judicial investigation into Cabinet Chief Manuel Adorni, negative market signals, and the failure of its narrative campaign on historical memory.

stories.title: Russian troops strike energy facility in Odesa region overnight, causing power outages
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an energy facility and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, causing power outages across the area.

stories.title: China biotech deals hit record as innovative drugs draw interest of multinationals
stories.summary: Chinese biotech firms achieved a record US$60 billion in cross-border outlicensing deals in the first quarter of 2026, a 73 percent increase from the same period a year earlier. Multinational pharmaceutical companies are driving demand for China's drug candidates.

stories.title: Argentine lawyer held in Brazil on racial slur charges faces new uncertainty after court reversal
stories.summary: Agostina Páez, a 29-year-old Argentine lawyer, has been detained in Rio de Janeiro since January 14 after being filmed making racist gestures toward bar employees in Ipanema. She faces three criminal complaints for racial slurs, each carrying two to five years in prison under Brazilian law.

stories.title: Helplines buzz with alerts from seafarers trapped in Middle East war
stories.summary: Seafarer helplines, including the International Transport Workers' Federation's support team, report being overwhelmed with messages from crews stranded in the Gulf amid the Middle East conflict, seeking repatriation, compensation, and emergency provisions.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 29 – Northerners feel grim amid war but firm on need to defeat Hezbollah
stories.summary: Reporters in northern Israel described a sense of isolation and grimness among residents of Kiryat Shmona and Haifa amid the ongoing war, while also covering trauma assistance for Arab Israelis and hospitals treating patients in underground facilities.

stories.title: Oil on track for record monthly surge as Iran war disrupts markets
stories.summary: Brent crude oil has surged 51 percent since the start of March due to the Iran war, putting it on track for its largest monthly gain on record. The previous record was a 46 percent rise in September 1990 following Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts four-nation bid to encourage US, Iran towards diplomacy
stories.summary: Top diplomats from Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye met in Pakistan to lay the groundwork for diplomatic de-escalation between the United States and Iran amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: ‘We will see a new government in Venezuela, in Cuba and in Iran’
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Ted Cruz stated that President Donald Trump's foreign policy approach could lead to government changes in Venezuela, Cuba, and Iran.

stories.title: Iran issues directive to counter potential US ground operation
stories.summary: Iran's state-affiliated Tehran Times reported that Iranian authorities have issued a directive to counter a potential US ground operation. An Iranian security analyst indicated that Iran would seize coastlines in the UAE and Bahrain in response to any US land attack.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran attacks aluminium plant in Bahrain; 2 wounded
stories.summary: The Pentagon is preparing plans for weeks of ground operations in Iran, though President Donald Trump has not yet approved any deployment, the Washington Post reported

stories.title: UK police question suspect after Derby car incident
stories.summary: Seven people were seriously injured when a car struck pedestrians in Derby, central England. A man originally from India was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, and police are questioning the suspect.

stories.title: Iran Guards say struck Bahrain, UAE aluminium plants
stories.summary: Aluminium Bahrain, one of the world’s largest aluminium producers, said two employees were wounded in an Iranian strike targeting its facility on Saturday (March 28, 2026)

stories.title: US mulling 'weeks-long ground operations' in Iran: report
stories.summary: Reports indicate the United States is considering weeks-long ground raids inside Iran, a move that would expose US troops to drone and missile threats. The Trump administration is weighing the escalation as the conflict continues.

stories.title: Pentagon preparing for US ground assault in Iran, says report
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly preparing a potential ground assault in Iran that could last weeks or months. Proposed operations may include seizing Kharg Island or conducting raids along coastal areas near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Two Arab men killed in separate incidents as police fail to rein in soaring crime
stories.summary: Ibrahim Abu Zayid was killed in Rahat and Taj Nofi was killed in Yafia in separate incidents, bringing the homicide toll among Arab citizens of Israel to 77 so far this year amid a continuing wave of violent crime.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran war: could Republican rift and Maga discontent doom midterms?
stories.summary: Observers in China say the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its fifth week, has exposed divisions within the Republican Party and President Trump's political base. Mixed signals from the Trump administration regarding Operation Epic Fury and its exit strategy are raising questions about the conflict's trajectory and potential midterm election consequences.

stories.title: Air defenses down 380 of 442 Russian drones used in attacks since evening
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 380 of 442 Russian drones launched since the previous evening. Enemy strikes were recorded at seven locations across Ukraine.

stories.title: Fact check: Fake satellite images distort Middle East conflict from above
stories.summary: Amid the intensifying Iran war, manipulated and AI-generated satellite images are increasingly circulating online, blurring the line between verified facts and fabricated visuals in the information battle over the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Syria says repelled drone attack from Iraq on US base
stories.summary: Syria's government said it repelled a drone attack targeting one of the remaining US military bases in the country. Damascus blamed Iraq for launching the drones.

stories.title: North Korea conducts engine test for missile capable of targeting U.S. mainland
stories.summary: The test likely indicates Mr. Kim is intent on enlarging and modernising an arsenal of missiles capable of reaching the United States mainland.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kharkiv region with airstrikes and drones over 24 hours, injuring six
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked nine settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region with airstrikes and drones over 24 hours, wounding six people.

stories.title: Islamabad set to host meeting for Middle East de-escalation
stories.summary: • Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Egypt foreign ministers arrive for quadrilateral huddle• PM speaks to Pezeshkian for over an hour to push for peace, condemns strikes on Iran• Iranian president underscores ‘d

stories.title: Iran Guards say struck Bahrain, UAE aluminium plants
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it struck aluminium production facilities in the UAE and Bahrain, alleging the plants had ties to US military sectors.

stories.title: 'Helplessness, uncontrollable fear': Romi Gonen shares how Iran war brings back Gaza trauma
stories.summary: Former Hamas hostage Romi Gonen described how the Iran war triggered trauma from her captivity in Gaza. She recounted experiencing helplessness and uncontrollable fear when caught in sirens during Iranian missile attacks on Israel.

stories.title: IDF documents first-ever Alpinist Unit cross-border mountain operation
stories.summary: The IDF documented its first cross-border mountain operation conducted by the Alpinist Unit. Troops operated in complex mountainous terrain using specialized capabilities to gather intelligence and locate militant infrastructure.

stories.title: Iranian attack on Saudi air base heavily damages key US surveillance aircraft
stories.summary: An Iranian attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia heavily damaged key US surveillance aircraft and wounded 12 American soldiers. Ukrainian President Zelensky said Russian satellite imagery of the base had been shared with Iran days before the strike.

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten to hit U.S. universities in West Asia
stories.summary: Iran Guards said, "We advise all employees, professors, and students of American universities in the region and residents of their surrounding areas" stay a kilometre away from campuses.”

stories.title: Hong Kong’s MPF authority to propose 2-tier surcharges for late employer contributions
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority plans to propose a two-tier surcharge mechanism targeting employers who fail to make timely pension contributions. Data shows only one in six employers settle arrears within the required two-week deadline. The proposal is expected to be presented to the government by mid-year.

stories.title: Wild ultimatums and ‘bombing our little hearts out’: A portrait of Trump at war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly shifted his stated goals during the ongoing conflict, reflecting what observers describe as an inconsistency of purpose. The changing objectives have characterized the administration's wartime decision-making.

stories.title: Chinese analogue chipmakers join wave of global price rises as mature-node firms eye gains
stories.summary: Several Chinese analogue chipmakers, including Novosense Microelectronics, SG Micro, and Silan Micro, have announced price increases alongside global peers such as Texas Instruments. Analysts say the broader semiconductor pricing wave could give China's mature-node producers an opportunity to gain market share.

stories.title: China mum, inspired by son’s heroic death, has handcrafted shoe pads for soldiers for 20 years
stories.summary: Zhang Xinghui, a mother from Chongqing, China, has handcrafted over 1,000 pairs of shoe pads for army recruits over 20 years in memory of her son, Gu Nu. The 19-year-old soldier died in 2005 while rescuing a comrade during a landslide while patrolling a mountain in Tibet.

stories.title: Regional diplomats gather in Pakistan for talks to end Iran war
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Egypt gathered in Islamabad for talks aimed at ending the war in the Middle East involving the U.S., Israel, and Iran. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reported holding extensive discussions with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, though little progress was evident as strikes continued.

stories.title: Five wounded in Donetsk region over past 24 hours in Russian shelling
stories.summary: Five people were wounded in the Donetsk region of Ukraine on March 28 as a result of Russian shelling over the preceding 24-hour period.

stories.title: Pak-Afghan peace jirga to meet in Peshawar on Tuesday
stories.summary: PESHAWAR: A Pak-Afghan peace jirga will be held in Peshawar on March 31 to urge the leadership of both countries to immediately de-escalate tensions and work towards peace, former chief secretary Arba

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Al Araby TV office in Tehran
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit a building housing Al Araby TV's Tehran office, wounding at least 10 people according to the Iranian Red Crescent Society. The Qatari news channel said the attack caused extensive damage and forced a halt to live broadcasting.

stories.title: Anti-war protests in Israel: Hundreds gather in Tel-Aviv
stories.summary: Hundreds of protesters gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday to oppose the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, continuing a series of weekly demonstrations since the conflict began a month ago. Participation appears to be growing, prompting Israeli authorities to move to disperse the crowds.

stories.title: Two new suspects arrested over foiled Bank of America bomb plot in Paris
stories.summary: French prosecutors announced the arrest of two additional suspects connected to an apparent bomb plot targeting the Bank of America headquarters in Paris. The arrests came a day after police detained a man who was about to detonate a homemade explosive device outside the U.S. bank's offices.

stories.title: US troops arrive in Middle East, Houthis launch second operation
stories.summary: The United States is reinforcing its military presence in the Middle East with additional troop deployments. Meanwhile, regional powers are meeting in Islamabad to seek de-escalation of the widening conflict. Yemen's Houthis launched a second military operation.

stories.title: Tehran threatens to target US universities in the region
stories.summary: Powerful explosions were reported in eastern and western Tehran overnight as U.S.-Israeli strikes continued. In southern Iran, strikes killed five people in Bandar Khamir near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards threatened to target U.S. university campuses in the Middle East, and Iranian officials report nearly 2,000 people killed since the war began.

stories.title: Congo-Brazzaville court confirms Sassou Nguesso re‑election with 95%
stories.summary: A court in Congo-Brazzaville confirmed President Denis Sassou Nguesso's re-election with approximately 95% of the vote. The result extends his rule of over four decades amid controversy over the margin of victory.

stories.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf accuses US of ‘secret ground war plans’
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Washington of publicly calling for negotiations while secretly preparing a ground offensive. He warned that Iranian armed forces are ready to confront any US land incursion and would retaliate against American troops and regional allies.

stories.title: Dozens detained in Tel Aviv as anti-war protest turns violent
stories.summary: Police in Tel Aviv dispersed an anti-war protest on Saturday, arresting up to 18 people. The demonstrators were opposing the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Russia’s Ust-Luga port after overnight drone attack
stories.summary: A fire broke out at Russia's Ust-Luga port, a major petroleum export terminal in the Leningrad region, following a nighttime drone attack attributed to Ukraine.

stories.summary: • 42-year-old rickshaw driver was sole breadwinner and father of three• Experts urge govt to relocate all dogs from streets to shelters with animal rights activists’ support• Absence of life-saving RI

stories.summary:

stories.title: Hundreds of kilos of protected plant siezed by Israel Nature and Parks Authority in Golan
stories.summary: Israel's Nature and Parks Authority seized hundreds of kilograms of protected plant species in the Golan Heights. In a separate operation in the Menashe region, inspectors confiscated approximately 6 kilograms of akoub and 25 kilograms of hyssop.

stories.title: Pentagon readies for weeks of US ground operations in Iran: Report
stories.summary: Reports indicate the Pentagon is preparing plans for limited ground operations in strategic regions of Iran. Uncertainty remains over whether President Trump will approve the proposed missions.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1494: Ukraine hits Russia’s export ports for third time in five days
stories.summary: Ukraine struck Russian export ports for the third time in five days on day 1,494 of the Russo-Ukrainian war. The drone and missile campaign has targeted facilities from Baltic ports to fuel hubs in Yaroslavl as part of an economic warfare strategy.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Explosions were reported in Tehran on Sunday with air defenses activated. A strike on a port in Hormozgan province killed five people, while Iran launched missiles toward southern Israel, claiming hits on Israeli radar and airport facilities.

stories.title: Exhausted Palestinians struggle to put lives back together as world’s gaze fixes on Iran
stories.summary: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, Palestinians continue to face airstrikes, shelling, and dire humanitarian conditions. Displaced residents in Deir al-Balah report constant drone surveillance and gunfire, while the international community's attention has largely shifted to the war in Iran.

stories.title: Kenya faces deadly flooding with at least 108 people killed
stories.summary: Kenya reported at least 108 deaths from several weeks of torrential rains and severe flooding. The updated death toll was released by the country's National Police Service on Saturday.

stories.title: Umrah visa being used for travel to Europe, says FIA
stories.summary:

stories.title: 'Targeted assassination': Araghchi condemns killing of journalists in Lebanon
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi condemned the killing of three journalists in Lebanon, calling it a "targeted assassination" by Israel. He accused Israel of attempting to silence media reporting on the conflict.

stories.title: Petroleum cargo handling rises at Karachi’s Port Qasim Authority
stories.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Port activities in Pakistan have increased following Iran’s retaliatory closure of the Strait of Hormuz in response to illegal US-Israel attacks.

stories.title: A crisis of faith: The Christian debate over Jews, covenant, and Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines a theological debate among Christians over Jewish covenant claims and the State of Israel, arguing that some Christian thinkers are reshaping doctrine to deny the significance of Jewish return to the land.

stories.title: Jiang Xueqin, the viral ‘prophet’ predicting the world’s fate from a Beijing classroom
stories.summary: Beijing-based Chinese-Canadian high school teacher Jiang Xueqin has gained a large online following through his Predictive History YouTube channel, earning him the nickname "China's Nostradamus." His geopolitical commentary and lectures have been widely shared on both international and Chinese social media platforms.

stories.summary:

stories.title: War update: 236 clashes on front lines, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 236 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines over 24 hours. The heaviest fighting occurred in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: 'No Kings' rallies draw crowds across US
stories.summary: Large crowds across the United States and Europe participated in "No Kings" rallies on Saturday, protesting President Trump's policies and the war in Iran. Minnesota drew particularly large turnout, with thousands demonstrating against Trump's immigration enforcement actions.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran: What’s happening on day 30 of attacks?
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia convened in Islamabad on day 30 of the US-Israeli war on Iran. The talks aimed at finding a path to end the ongoing military conflict.

stories.title: Will defiant Iran win peace?
stories.summary: AS missiles, drones and bombs were hitting targets on all sides of the Persian Gulf, news broke of a mediation effort led by Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt that generated a faint hope that at some stage

stories.title: Three Lebanese journalists killed in strikes
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon on Saturday killed three journalists, including a veteran Hezbollah television correspondent. A subsequent strike killed rescuers at the scene, and separate Israeli raids reportedly killed nine paramedics. Israel also announced one of its soldiers was killed in clashes with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Shadow of crisis
stories.summary:
THE latest staff-level agreement between the IMF and Pakistan could not have come at a more volatile moment.
What might otherwise have been read as a routine milestone under the IMF’s balance-of-payme

stories.title: Yemen's rebels could further threaten global shipping
stories.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen carried out a second missile strike against Israel and pledged to continue attacks. The escalation has raised fears of the conflict spreading into the Red Sea region, where Saudi Arabia has already begun redirecting significant oil exports away from normal shipping routes.

stories.title: Iran: 3,500 US marines arrive in Middle East
stories.summary: The amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli arrived in the Middle East carrying approximately 3,500 U.S. Marines as American military reinforcements continue building up in the region. Uncertainty remains over whether U.S. ground forces will be formally deployed in the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Analyst says that Iran’s interest is in an extended war
stories.summary: Analyst Rob Geist-Pinfold assessed that Iran's strategic interest lies in prolonging the current war, while the United States seeks a quicker resolution to the conflict.

stories.title: Australia’s Karratha LNG plant closed after cyclone amid fuel shortages
stories.summary: Woodside Energy's Karratha LNG plant in Western Australia remained offline on Sunday after a cyclone knocked out power to thousands of residents. The closure of one of the world's largest LNG facilities is compounding fuel supply shortages already worsened by the ongoing war in the Middle East.

stories.title: World Bank to provide $250m for KP resilience, disaster readiness
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank is expected to approve a loan of $250 million to Pakistan for resilience, early action, and disaster preparedness in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one of the country’s most flood-prone

stories.title: One killed, two injured as Russian attacks hit 42 settlements in Kherson region
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked 42 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region over the past 24 hours, killing one person and injuring two others.

stories.title: Syrian forces repel drones targeting US base, official says
stories.summary: Syria's Deputy Defence Minister Sipan Hemo said Syrian forces intercepted a drone attack launched from Iraqi territory targeting a US military base at Qasrak. Four drones were involved, and Hemo called on Iraq to prevent future cross-border attacks.

stories.title: IDF strikes Tehran command centers, weapon production sites
stories.summary: The Israeli military struck command centers in Tehran that had been relocated to mobile units, along with weapons production sites. The strikes followed weekend attacks on Iranian nuclear development facilities.

stories.title: How to assess China’s real chance of winning AI race against US
stories.summary: A senior Chinese AI researcher, Lin Junyang, told an industry summit in Beijing that Chinese companies have less than a 20 percent chance of surpassing leading U.S. AI firms within three to five years. Lin previously worked on Alibaba's Qwen, one of China's most capable open-source AI models.

stories.title: Gilgit-Baltistan tourism bounces back despite Middle East war
stories.summary: GILGIT: While concerns had been raised about the potential adverse impact of the escalating war in the Middle East and the resulting rise in fuel prices on Gilgit-Baltistan’s tourism and hospitality i

stories.title: Living in the dark: Gaza’s struggle for electricity
stories.summary: The ongoing war has destroyed Gaza's electrical power grid. Families across the territory are now dependent on generators and private charging points for electricity.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 780 strikes on Zaporizhzhia region over past day, three women injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 780 strikes on 41 settlements across Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region in a single day, using missiles, guided aerial bombs, drones, airstrikes, and artillery. Three women were injured in the attacks.

stories.title: Bilateral relations between China and Seychelles enter a new phase
stories.summary: China and Seychelles are deepening bilateral relations, with increasing trade and growing private-sector collaboration. New areas of cooperation include the blue economy and digital innovation.

stories.title: Pakistan hosts top Saudi, Turkish, Egyptian diplomats over war in Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan is hosting diplomatic talks in Islamabad with senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt. The Pakistani government is acting as a mediator between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Pentagon preparing for ground operations in Iran, reports U.S. media
stories.summary: Any ground operation would stop short of a full-scale invasion, instead involving raids by special operations forces and conventional infantry troops, the Washington Post said, citing unnamed official

stories.title: Oman says no group claimed responsibility for recent attacks
stories.summary: Oman's Foreign Ministry said no group has claimed responsibility for recent attacks on its territory, including two drone strikes on the port of Salalah on Saturday that injured a worker and damaged a crane. Authorities said an investigation into the source and motives is ongoing.

stories.title: IDF soldier Moshe Yitzchak Katz, 22, from Connecticut, killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: IDF soldier Moshe Yitzchak Katz, a 22-year-old lone soldier from Connecticut, was killed in a Hezbollah rocket attack in southern Lebanon. Three other soldiers were wounded in the same incident, according to the IDF.

stories.title: China’s high-end yacht owners say industry growth stifled by structural gaps
stories.summary: Despite China having the world's largest number of billionaires, the yacht industry there faces regulatory hurdles and infrastructure gaps. E-commerce billionaire Richard Liu recently announced a multibillion-dollar investment in a new yacht company.

stories.title: Some 100 shelters to be placed in Bedouin communities after doctor, infant son wounded
stories.summary: The IDF Home Front Command is placing approximately 100 shelters in Bedouin communities following an incident in which a doctor and his infant son were wounded. The move responds to appeals from local council heads about the lack of protection in the area.

stories.title: Missing sailboats carrying aid arrive in Cuba after being located by Mexican Navy
stories.summary: Upon arriving to the island, Adnaan Stumo, the coordinator of the sailing convoy, said bad weather was responsible for the delay because the boats had to take a longer route and the sailors were “neve

stories.title: Iran Guards threaten to hit US universities in the Middle East
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened to strike U.S.-affiliated universities in the Middle East. The threat was issued in retaliation for joint U.S.-Israeli strikes that destroyed two Iranian universities.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,360 troops in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russia's total estimated combat losses in its war against Ukraine have reached approximately 1,295,830 personnel from February 2022 to March 29, 2026, including 1,360 soldiers killed or wounded in the past 24 hours.

stories.title: Russia says 'situation deteriorating' after strikes near Bushehr nuclear plant in Iran
stories.summary: Rosatom, Russia's state nuclear corporation, warned that the situation at Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant was deteriorating after a US-Israeli strike near the facility. The IAEA confirmed Iran reported a third strike in the vicinity of Bushehr within ten days.

stories.title: Israeli strikes hit two Gaza police checkpoints, killing six, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit two Hamas-run police checkpoints in Gaza, killing at least six Palestinians including a child, according to local health officials in Cairo. The strikes occurred despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that has been in place for over five months.

stories.title: Air strikes target Popular Mobilisation Forces sites in Iraq's Mosul
stories.summary: Air strikes hit Popular Mobilisation Forces sites in the Rashidiya area of Mosul and at a headquarters in Tuz Khurmatu in Salah al-Din province. A drone also reportedly crashed on the outskirts of the Dujail district south of the province.

stories.title: Houthis join fray by firing ballistic missiles at Israel
stories.summary: • Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain hit by Iranian missiles, drones; strike wounds US troops at Saudi airbase• Drone strike disrupts shipping hub in Salalah• Explosions rock Tehran as Israeli attacks intensi

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis join Mid-East war – what comes next?
stories.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched their first missile at Israel in months on March 28, marking their entry into the broader Middle East conflict. The attack raised concerns about further regional escalation.

stories.title: Report: Strike on Iran port kills five, damages vessels
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that five people were killed and four wounded in a US-Israeli strike on a pier in Bandar Khamir in Hormozgan province. Two vessels and a vehicle were damaged. Israel's military said it had completed another wave of strikes across Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine's SBU Alpha unit neutralizes over 2,100 Russian troops in one week
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU Alpha Special Operations Center reported killing or wounding 2,158 Russian troops over the past week during operations against invading forces.

stories.title: Hundreds of Israelis protest against war, clash with police
stories.summary: Weekly protests against the war launched by Israel and the United States against Iran on February 28 have been taking place in Tel Aviv and elsewhere, initially drawing only a few dozen participants

stories.title: Punish Russia for Helping Iran Target the U.S. Military
stories.summary: The article discusses Russia's role in supporting Iran amid tensions with the U.S. military in the Middle East. It references President Trump's claim that Vladimir Putin wants to be helpful in the region and a reported exchange between Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the EU foreign policy chief over U.S. diplomatic approaches to Russia and Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran’s IRGC claims attacks on UAE, Bahrain aluminium facilities
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for strikes on Aluminium Bahrain and Emirates Global Aluminium facilities in the UAE and Bahrain, describing the attacks as retaliation for US-Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s ageing challenge: is Singapore’s Kampung Admiralty model the answer?
stories.summary: Singapore's Kampung Admiralty integrated housing model is being examined as a potential solution for Hong Kong's ageing population, as elderly residents express reluctance to enter traditional care homes, preferring less restrictive living arrangements.

stories.title: Finance chief says Hong Kong remains stable as oil prices surge amid Mideast turmoil
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said authorities are monitoring the impact of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran and resulting global oil price volatility. He noted that while international investor sentiment has been shaken, the city's financial markets continue to operate smoothly with limited immediate economic impact.

stories.title: Hundreds of Israelis protest against war, clash with police
stories.summary: Hundreds of Israelis protested against the war with Iran and clashed with police. Despite the demonstrations, public opinion surveys indicate that broad support for the military campaign against Iran remains high in Israel.

stories.title: ‘Trump has to open the Strait of Hormuz’ with ground forces
stories.summary: Analyst Kenneth Katzman argued that US military objectives in Iran that cannot be achieved through air power alone would require a ground invasion, including the use of ground forces to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Thick plumes of smoke rise over Iraq’s Mosul after strikes
stories.summary: Air strikes targeting sites belonging to Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces in Mosul produced thick plumes of smoke visible over the city.

stories.title: Toddler rescued after US-Israeli strike on Iran
stories.summary: Iranian Red Crescent rescue teams pulled a toddler alive from a building destroyed by a US-Israeli strike on Iran. No further details on the location or broader casualties were provided.

stories.title: Houthi attacks on Israel open new front in Mideast war, threaten Red Sea shipping
stories.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have claimed two missile launches targeting Israel, opening a new front in the broader Middle East conflict. Analysts warn that renewed Houthi attacks could disrupt global shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait off the Red Sea, a route that has grown more critical since Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Ukraine's military intelligence releases documentary on agent operating behind enemy lines
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence agency, HUR, has released a documentary film about the activities of a Ukrainian agent operating behind enemy lines.

stories.title: Anger over Iran war adds fuel to anti-Trump rallies in US
stories.summary: WASHINGTON: Demonstrators decrying President Donald Trump’s policies took to city streets across the United States on Saturday in the third edition of the “No Kings” rallies that organisers hoped will

stories.title: 22 migrants die off Greece after six days at sea
stories.summary:
ATHENS: Twenty-two migrants hoping to reach Europe from North Africa have died off the coast of Greece after six days at sea in a rubber boat, survivors told the Greek coastguard on Saturday.

The coa

stories.title: Action plan unveiled to combat drought
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has developed a national drought action plan in an attempt to transition from a reactive to a proactive risk-based approach for drought management, as climate change is making drou

stories.title: Undercover police officer was sacked for assaulting partner, spycops inquiry hears
stories.summary: The UK public inquiry into undercover policing heard that officer Rob Hastings, who infiltrated pro-Palestinian and left-wing protest groups during a three-year covert deployment, deceived a woman into an intimate relationship. He was later convicted of assaulting his long-term partner and dismissed from the Metropolitan Police for gross misconduct in 2014.

stories.title: Iran warns of blasts as army clears munitions from 'American-Zionist attacks'
stories.summary: Iranian authorities warned residents of Isfahan province to expect explosions as military teams conduct controlled detonations to clear unexploded ordnance from recent US-Israeli strikes in areas south and west of the city.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in battle while fighting in Lebanon, military announces
stories.summary: IDF Sergeant Moshe Yitzhak HaCohen Katz, 22, born in New Haven, Connecticut, was killed during fighting in Lebanon. Three other soldiers were moderately wounded in the same attack.

stories.title: Israel says Iran moving military command centres to mobile structures
stories.summary: The Israeli military stated that Iran has begun relocating its command centres to mobile structures after fixed headquarters were struck during the conflict. The Israeli Air Force reportedly bombed several temporary headquarters in Tehran while Iranian commanders were present.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers open low-cost digital front as US-Israeli attacks mount
stories.summary: Iran-linked hackers sent Israeli Android users texts during missile strikes offering a fake bomb-shelter app that instead installed spyware providing access to cameras, locations, and personal data. The operation reflects a broader low-cost cyber campaign by Iran and its proxies against the US and Israel.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it bombed Israeli base near Safed
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it launched missiles at the Israeli military base of Mahfa Alon southwest of Safed. The group also said it attacked an Israeli armoured unit in Deir Siryan in southern Lebanon and fired an air-defence missile at an Israeli helicopter near Adaisseh.

stories.title: Kremlin plans to shift Russians' pension savings into state program – intelligence
stories.summary: The Kremlin is planning to forcibly transfer Russians' pension savings into a new state scheme – the long-term savings program.

stories.title: U.S. amphibious assault ship arrives in West Asia
stories.summary: The ship, which is usually based in Japan, arrived in the region on March 27, Centcom said in a post on X, noting that the vessel is the flagship for a contingent of "about 3,500" Marines and sailors.

stories.title: Pentagon said prepping weeks-long ground operation in Iran, short of full invasion
stories.summary: The Pentagon is reportedly preparing a weeks-long ground operation in Iran short of a full invasion. Separately, the IRGC struck aluminium plants in the UAE and Bahrain, and Iran launched overnight missile attacks targeting southern Israel.

stories.title: Russian forces strike civilian infrastructure in Konotop – mayor
stories.summary: Russian forces have attacked civilian infrastructure and residential areas in the city of Konotop, Sumy region.

stories.title: Israeli military says fifth soldier killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced the death of a fifth soldier in combat in southern Lebanon since the start of the latest war. The announcement underscores the continuing ground clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah fighters in the border region.

stories.title: Smoke rises over Tehran after explosions, targets remain unclear
