stories.summary: Multiple large explosions were heard in northern Tehran and the nearby city of Karaj, with smoke rising over the capital. Iran's Fars news agency confirmed the blasts, while the targets remained unclear.

stories.title: Israeli embassy refuses statement from Nagasaki atomic bomb survivors
stories.summary: The Israeli Embassy in Tokyo refused to accept a statement from Nagasaki atomic bomb survivor groups criticising the US-Israeli war on Iran. The document was returned unread, according to Japan's Kyodo news agency.

stories.title: Israeli strikes and US troop buildup put Pakistan’s peacemaker role under pressure
stories.summary: Pakistan is seeking to leverage its neutral standing and good relations with both Iran and the United States to host peace talks between the two countries. However, intensifying Israeli airstrikes on Iranian targets and a growing U.S. military presence in the Gulf are undermining Islamabad's diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Israel’s manpower crisis: IDF Chief’s warning, a wake-up call for Israeli leaders - editoral
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff warned Israel's political leadership about a growing military manpower crisis. He stressed the urgent need for a conscription bill to sustain the armed forces amid escalating tensions with Iran.

stories.title: New China school system rewards diligent pupils with ‘digital pets’ to motivate them
stories.summary: Schools across China have introduced a digital pet-raising program in which students earn points for good behavior to nurture virtual pets. The initiative, gaining widespread attention, was highlighted at Hangzhou Shenglan Middle School.

stories.title: Israel Adesanya knocked out by Joe Pyfer at UFC Fight Night in Seattle
stories.summary: Former two-time UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya was knocked out by Joe Pyfer in the second round at UFC Fight Night in Seattle, marking Adesanya's fourth consecutive loss.

stories.title: North Korea tests powerful missile engine. Will an ICBM launch follow?
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un oversaw a test of a high-thrust solid-fuel engine for intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) capable of reaching targets around the globe, touting the development

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Explosions in Tehran as Yemen’s Houthis heighten risks of Iran war
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces conducted fresh strikes on Tehran, targeting what it described as temporary Iranian command centres, ballistic missile production and storage facilities, and aerial defense systems. Yemen's Houthi rebels confirmed a second wave of attacks on Israel after joining the war on Saturday, further escalating the conflict.

stories.title: 4 injured in multi-vehicle collision on busy Hong Kong road
stories.summary:
Four people have been injured in a multi-vehicle collision in Hong Kong’s Kowloon City after a van mounted a pavement and crashed into a wall.
Police received a report at 8.34am on Sunday that a drive

stories.title: As Iran war grinds on, rising toll on global economy has many worried about recovery
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict with Iran has been described as causing the largest supply disruption in global oil market history. Countries have imposed energy restrictions, and food prices are expected to rise in poorer regions as the economic toll mounts.

stories.title: Two powerful explosion shake Tehran as air defenses respond, AFP reports
stories.summary: Two powerful explosions shook northern Tehran early Sunday as air defences were activated, AFP reported. The targets were not immediately clear, and Iranian authorities had not issued an official confirmation.

stories.title: Bahrain confirms Iranian attack on aluminum facility as UAE, Kuwait air defenses intercept missiles
stories.summary: Bahrain confirmed that Iran attacked the Alba aluminium facility, while the UAE and Kuwait reported intercepting missiles with air defences. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the strikes were in retaliation for attacks on two Iranian steel plants.

stories.title: North Korea tests high-thrust engine for missile capable of striking US mainland
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un oversaw a test of a high-thrust, solid-fuel engine intended for strategic weapons, according to state media. Analysts assessed that the test reflects Pyongyang's efforts to develop a missile capable of carrying multiple warheads and reaching the United States mainland.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Loud blasts rock Tehran as Yemen's Houthis widen conflict
stories.summary: Two powerful explosions struck northern Tehran early Sunday as Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a second missile attack on Israel, widening the monthlong Middle East conflict. The Israeli military also announced the combat death of a fifth soldier in south Lebanon.

stories.title: US says 1,000 'rioters' surrounded federal building, attacked officers
stories.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security said approximately 1,000 people surrounded the Royal Federal Building in Los Angeles. Two individuals were arrested for assaulting federal officers, and two officers were struck with cement blocks and required medical care.

stories.title: The Philippines loves Jollibee. Overseas Filipinos love it even more
stories.summary:
No fast-food chain has ever meant quite what Jollibee means to Filipinos.
Forget McDonald’s and KFC, Jollibee – with its sweet spaghetti and crispy Chickenjoy – is something else entirely: a cultural

stories.title: Report: Britain plans mine-hunting ship for Hormuz deployment
stories.summary: Britain is considering deploying the Royal Navy vessel Lyme Bay to the Strait of Hormuz, equipped with mine-detection drones, according to The Times. Defence Secretary John Healey approved planning, but a final decision has not yet been made.

stories.title: North Korea's Kim inspects solid-fuel engine, new tank as Pyongyang steps up military development
stories.summary: KCNA said the new high-thrust solid-fuel engine had a maximum thrust of 2,500 ‌kilonewtons and that the ground test formed part of a new five-year defence development plan ‌aimed at upgrading the coun

stories.title: South Korea defence stocks surge after Iran war
stories.summary: South Korean defence stocks surged following the outbreak of the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. Hanwha Aerospace's market capitalisation rose 11.7 percent, LIG Nex1 jumped 44.4 percent, and Hanwha Systems gained 9.2 percent, while other sectors declined.

stories.title: Iran says Israeli radar centre, airport targeted in strikes
stories.summary: Iran's state media reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted Israeli military and infrastructure sites, including a radar centre and an airport facility. Iran also claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 drone and struck an F-16 fighter jet.

stories.title: What happens in the occupied West Bank under the shadow of the Iran war
stories.summary: Since the outbreak of the Israel-Iran war, settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has reportedly surged, with the conflict providing cover for increased aggression.

stories.title: In 2011, Hong Kong film actor Alan Tang dies at 62 – SCMP archive
stories.summary:
This article was first published on March 30, 2011
by Danny Mok
‘Student Prince’ dies after heart problem
Former actor Alan Tang Kwong-wing, known as the “Student Prince”, has died at home. He was 62.

stories.title: Hong Kong passengers caught off guard by new airport limit of 2 power banks
stories.summary: Air passengers departing from Hong Kong have said they were unaware of a new rule limiting the number of power banks they could carry to two, with few reminder signs visible at the airport on the firs

stories.title: Israel hits Iran naval research site, fresh blasts rattle Tehran
stories.summary: Israel carried out strikes on a naval research site in Iran while additional explosions were reported in Tehran. Separately, Yemen's Houthi rebels announced their entry into the broader Middle East conflict by launching a missile toward Israel.

stories.title: Moira Deeming loses spot on Victorian Liberal election ballot after preselection standoff against moderate candidate
stories.summary: Moira Deeming lost her place on the Victorian Liberal Party's ballot for the November state election after a preselection challenge in Melbourne. Moderate-backed candidate Dinesh Gourisetty, a prominent figure in Melbourne's Indian community, defeated her at the western metropolitan region convention.

stories.title: Why are smugglers swarming East Africa for ants to send to China and Europe?
stories.summary: For most people, ants are unwelcome guests at a picnic, but international demand for the insects is driving a new black market in East Africa, where it could threaten ant populations and the broader e

stories.title: Pentagon preparing for week-long ground operation in Iran, according to officials - Washington Post
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported the Pentagon is preparing for a possible week-long ground operation in Iran, though not a full-scale invasion. President Trump had not yet approved the plans due to the high risks posed to American soldiers.

stories.title: As Iran’s drones swarm Gulf, Ukraine’s wartime tech lands billion-dollar deals
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that his country had “undoubtedly changed the geopolitical situation” in the Middle East with a series of decade-long defence agreements with Gu

stories.title: Son of Iran’s ousted shah wins ovation from US conservatives
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's ousted shah, received a standing ovation at a US conservative gathering. He framed the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran as a historic opportunity to overthrow the country's clerical leadership.

stories.title: IRGC threatens universities across Middle East after alleged strike against Iran University
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC issued threats against universities across the Middle East following alleged strikes on an Iranian university. The IRGC warned staff, students, and nearby civilians to maintain a one-kilometre distance from university sites to preserve their safety.

stories.title: Don't strike a deal with Iran's current leaders, opposition figure Pahlavi warns
stories.summary: Iranian opposition figure Reza Pahlavi warned at a gathering in Grapevine, Texas, that negotiating peace with Iran's current leaders would only delay threats to Americans. He said he would again call on Iranians to take to the streets in protest.

stories.title: Iran launches missiles toward southern Israel, sirens sounded
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported a new salvo of missiles launched toward southern Israel, with sirens sounding in locations including Dimona. Sirens also activated in Metula after rockets were fired from Lebanon, and Hezbollah claimed strikes on Israeli forces in the Malkiya area.

stories.title: One rule for Israel and another for Iran risks nuclear disaster
stories.summary:
Israel’s avowed goal in the Middle East war is to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Yet the double standard associated with this is hardly sustainable in the long run.
The worst-kept secret

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli forces, helicopter in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it carried out multiple attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, including shelling an armoured unit in Deir Siryan and firing an air-defence missile at an Israeli helicopter over Adaisseh. The group also targeted Israeli soldiers at the al-Malikiyah site.

stories.title: Iran shuts down Tehran cafe chain over ‘suspicious’ cup designs
stories.summary: Iranian authorities shut down the Lamiz cafe chain in Tehran over cup designs featuring an empty chair, which officials deemed suspicious. No further details on the specific concerns were provided.

stories.title: Gulf strikes threaten fuel, fertiliser and medical supplies globally
stories.summary: Strikes across Gulf countries have raised concerns about global supplies of fuel, fertiliser, and medical resources. Aluminium Bahrain reported its facility was targeted, injuring two people, and incidents were also reported in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: IRGC condemns attack on Iraqi Kurdish leader’s residence
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps condemned a drone attack on the residence of Iraqi Kurdistan President Nechirvan Barzani, blaming the United States and Israel. Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani spoke with Barzani following the incident.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis strike at Israel in their first such attack since Iran war began
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces fired missiles at Israel on Saturday, marking their first such strike since the Iran war began. The attack, launched from Yemen, raises concerns about the five-week-old conflict spreading further across the Middle East.

stories.title: Iran's Pezeshkian clashes with IRGC's chief over control of Iran, marking rifts in regime - report
stories.summary: Iran International reported a clash between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and the IRGC chief over control of Iran's direction. Pezeshkian reportedly criticized the IRGC's approach of escalating regional tensions and attacking neighbouring countries.

stories.title: In Israel’s shelters, an ‘underground’ entertainment scene is born under missile fire
stories.summary: Amid ongoing Iranian missile bombardment of Israel, entertainers, DJs, and musicians have begun performing in bomb shelters, creating an impromptu underground entertainment scene that has gained popularity on social media.

stories.title: Yelabuga authorities jam communications and block Telegram at drone production site
stories.summary: Kremlin authorities are jamming cellular communications and blocking Telegram in Yelabuga (Tatarstan), where a factory producing Shahed-type combat drones is located.

stories.title: Tens of thousands turn out for central London rally against the far-right
stories.summary: Tens of thousands gathered in central London for a rally against the far-right. Leading Jewish groups said they were excluded from participating, while a separate pro-Palestinian protest joined the route, with many participants waving Iranian flags.

stories.title: Drone strike targets Kurdish party headquarters near Erbil, local media says
stories.summary: Iraqi media reported a drone attack on the Kurdistan Democratic Party headquarters east of Erbil. Separately, the residence of Iraqi Kurdistan President Nechirvan Barzani was also targeted in an attack, according to the Iraqi Prime Minister's media office.

stories.title: Iranian-backed militias escalate in Iraq, targeting Kurdistan Region president Nechirvan Barzani
stories.summary: A drone attack targeted the residence of Iraqi Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani. France and Iraq condemned the attack, while Iran distanced itself from the incident. Iranian-backed militias are suspected of escalating operations in Iraq.

stories.title: ‘Violent assault’: Israeli forces slammed after CNN crew detained in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces detained a CNN crew in the occupied West Bank while the team was reporting near the Palestinian village of Tayasir on the aftermath of an assault by Israeli settlers. The Foreign Press Association condemned the incident.

stories.title: Thousands of US Marines arrive in Middle East, Centcom says
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that approximately 3,500 additional troops, including Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit, arrived in the Middle East aboard the USS Tripoli. The deployment includes transport and strike aircraft and amphibious assault assets.

stories.title: Zelensky claims Russia surveilling US military bases for Iran
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence shows Russia has conducted surveillance of US and allied military bases in the Middle East and Gulf regions. He cited seven locations monitored in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Qatar, and the US-British base on Diego Garcia.

stories.title: China proposes a new way to measure academic influence in a departure from impact factor
stories.summary: Chinese researchers unveiled the Dongbi Index in Shanghai on March 21, proposing a new methodology for ranking medical and life-science journals that bypasses the traditional impact factor. The index covers over 7,000 journals selected from more than 40,000 worldwide. Experts say the initiative reflects China's effort to expand its academic discourse power.

stories.title: As Cambodia’s scam crackdown deadline looms, criminal gangs flee
stories.summary: As Cambodia approaches a deadline for its crackdown on scam operations, criminal gangs are fleeing the country. Indonesian victims, including young men trafficked into the scam trade, have been left stranded and penniless outside their embassy in Phnom Penh after Chinese-run operations confiscated their passports.

stories.title: Marines repel massive enemy assault in Oleksandrivka sector
stories.summary: Soldiers of the 37th Separate Marine Brigade of the Naval Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine repelled a massive assault by Russian invaders in the Oleksandrivka sector.

stories.title: South African Jew killed after being kidnapped, police confirm, no proof of antisemitic intent
stories.summary: A South African Jewish man was found dead after being kidnapped, according to the Jewish Community Security Organization. The victim disappeared on the evening of March 27 and was found by police two days later. Authorities said there was no evidence of antisemitic motivation.

stories.title: Errors in Hong Kong Tai Po blaze hearing transcript raise transparency concerns
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post found errors in the official transcript of a public hearing into a deadly fire in Hong Kong's Tai Po district. Incorrect figures were recorded for residents who escaped by lift and the percentage of severely damaged flats. An academic called for future proceedings to be live-streamed to improve transparency.

stories.title: China woman uses an old photo to find brother who was lured away with bread 33 years ago
stories.summary: A 44-year-old woman named Li Lin from Xiantao, Hubei province, located her younger brother Li Xin using a childhood photograph after a 33-year separation. The siblings were orphaned as children after their mother died of cancer and their father left home following a mental collapse. Li Xin had been lured away with a piece of bread.

stories.title: As war on Iran enters second month, Yemen’s Houthis open new front
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement has opened a new front in the expanding Israel-Iran conflict, now in its second month, pledging additional attacks on Israel and raising fears of further regional escalation.

stories.title: Air raid sirens sound across Kuwait, Bahrain and Israel
stories.summary: Air raid sirens sounded across Kuwait, Bahrain, and Israel amid missile and drone threats. Bahrain's Interior Ministry urged residents to shelter, Kuwait's defence ministry reported hostile attacks, and Israel's military worked to intercept missiles launched from Iran.

stories.title: Video: US lawmaker Bernie Sanders calls Iran war unconstitutional and illegal
stories.summary: At a "No Kings" protest rally in St. Paul, Minnesota, US Senator Bernie Sanders condemned the ongoing US and Israeli military campaign against Iran, arguing it lacked constitutional authority and violated international law.

stories.title: Pentagon prepares for weeks of ground operations in Iran, report says
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported that the Pentagon is preparing for possible weeks of ground operations in Iran, though limited in scope. Discussions include joint special operations raids in coastal areas near the Strait of Hormuz and potential strikes on strategic sites like Kharg Island.

stories.title: Kuwait airport hit by drones, radar system damaged, no casualties reported
stories.summary: Drones struck Kuwait's airport, damaging its radar system, though no casualties were reported. A spokesman said the attacks were carried out by Iran and its proxies.

stories.title: MFA announces Ukrainian-Polish historians’ conference
stories.summary: Ukraine and Poland will host a conference of historians on May 6–8, which will serve as a professional forum for discussing complex chapters of their shared history, fostering constructive dialogue, a

stories.title: DPM Dar says Iran has allowed ‘20 more ships’ under Pakistan flag to cross Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced that Iran agreed to allow 20 additional Pakistani-flagged ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, with two vessels crossing daily. Dar described the move as a constructive gesture and a harbinger of regional peace.

stories.title: Iran shuts down Tehran coffee shop chain over ‘suspicious’ cup designs
stories.summary: Iranian authorities shut down a Tehran coffee shop chain over cup designs featuring a painting of an empty chair deemed "suspicious." The café said the designs were created months earlier for the Nowruz holiday and were unconnected to current events.

stories.title: Death toll from Kenyan floods rises to 108, police say
stories.summary: Weeks of heavy rains and flooding in Kenya have killed at least 108 people, according to an updated death toll from the National Police Service.

stories.title: Saudi pipeline that bypasses Strait of Hormuz hits 7 million barrel capacity
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, has reached a capacity of 7 million barrels. Tanker flotillas have redirected to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to collect oil amid disruptions in the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Israeli military kills 15-year-old Palestinian in West Bank, health ministry says
stories.summary: The Israeli military killed a 15-year-old Palestinian boy near Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank on Friday, the Palestinian health ministry reported, amid a surge of violence in the territory.

stories.title: “Shahed” attack in Mykolaiv region injures seven children and one adult
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed drone attack in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region hospitalized eight people, seven of whom were children. The strike caused injuries requiring immediate medical treatment.

stories.title: Kyoto is eyeing taller buildings. Critics warn it will look like ‘every other city in Japan’
stories.summary: An advisory panel recommended that Kyoto revise its building height restrictions near Kyoto Station, raising the limit from 31 metres to 60 metres to accommodate towers and tourism infrastructure. Critics argue the change would damage the historic skyline of Japan's former imperial capital and make it resemble other Japanese cities.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran warns US, Israeli universities; Houthis fire missiles
stories.summary: Antiwar protests took place in Tel Aviv and multiple US cities as strikes killed a family of four in Iran's Bushehr province. Tehran also issued warnings directed at US and Israeli universities, while Houthi forces fired missiles.

stories.title: Israel ranks eighth globally in 2026 World Happiness Index despite war
stories.summary: Israel ranked eighth globally in the 2026 World Happiness Index despite the ongoing war. The ranking reflects the country's resilience amid the emotional and social challenges of the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine says it struck Russia’s Yaroslavl oil refinery
stories.summary: Ukraine said it struck Russia's Yaroslavl oil refinery and also targeted an explosives and ammunition production facility in Russia's Samara Region.

stories.title: IDF says almost done targeting ‘critical’ Iranian military sites as waves of strikes hit Tehran
stories.summary: The IDF said it is nearly finished targeting critical Iranian military sites as waves of strikes continued to hit Tehran. US Vice President stated Washington would continue the war to ensure Iran is "neutered," while Israel struck an Iranian naval weapons production headquarters.

stories.title: IDF soldier Sgt. Moshe Yitzhak HaCohen Katz, from Connecticut, killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: IDF Sergeant Moshe Yitzhak HaCohen Katz, originally from Connecticut, was killed in a Hezbollah rocket attack in southern Lebanon. Three other soldiers were moderately wounded in the same incident. Iran separately fired two missile salvos at southern Israel.

stories.title: Police arrest 18 as anti-war protests spread across Tel Aviv, Haifa, Jerusalem
stories.summary: Police arrested 18 people as anti-war protests spread across Israel, with thousands demonstrating at rallies in Tel Aviv's Habima Square, near Haifa's Horev Center, and at Paris Square in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Defense forces repel massive assault in Zaporizhzhia sector, destroy armored vehicle column
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 65th Separate Mechanized Brigade and supporting units repelled a large-scale Russian assault in the Zaporizhzhia sector. The defenders destroyed a column of armored vehicles during the engagement.

stories.title: Ukraine isn’t just burning Russia’s oil — it’s going after two refineries that keep Russian tanks moving and bombers flying
stories.summary: Ukrainian energy analyst Mykhailo Honchar identified Russia's KINEF and YANOS refineries as leading producers of specialized military oils and greases essential for armoured vehicles, helicopters, and missile systems. Ukraine has been targeting these facilities to degrade Russia's military capabilities.

stories.title: Foreign media association slams Israeli forces’ assault on CNN crew in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: The Foreign Press Association condemned what it called a violent assault by Israeli soldiers on a CNN crew in the occupied West Bank. The journalists were detained near the Palestinian village of Tayasir while reporting on Israeli settler activity and the establishment of an illegal outpost.

stories.title: India restoring a centuries-old royal kitchen that never stopped serving food
stories.summary: A centuries-old royal kitchen in India, which has continuously served food over the years, is undergoing restoration as the historic complex has deteriorated with age.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three journalists in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on a car in southern Lebanon killed three journalists. Israel claimed one of the victims was a Hezbollah member.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three Lebanese journalists, Al Manar TV says
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a vehicle in southern Lebanon killed three Lebanese journalists, according to Al Manar TV. The victims included reporters from Al Manar and the pro-Hezbollah outlet Al Mayadeen.

stories.title: Man injured and house damaged in drone attack in Kyiv region
stories.summary: A drone attack in the Brovary district of Ukraine's Kyiv region on the evening of March 28 damaged a house and injured one man. The strike targeted a residential area.

stories.title: Pedro Sanchez | Europe’s only anti-war Prime Minister
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez described Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide and characterized the US-Israel war on Iran as a violation of international law. He is the only European head of government to publicly reject the conflict on principle.

stories.title: France foils bomb attack outside US bank in Paris
stories.summary: French police arrested a man attempting to set off a homemade explosive device outside a US bank in Paris, foiling the attack.

stories.title: Shops and restaurants in Egypt told to close early as energy crisis deepens
stories.summary: Egypt's government ordered shops and restaurants to close by 21:00 nightly for the next month to conserve electricity amid a deepening energy crisis. The measure affects retail and dining establishments nationwide.

stories.title: Mohammad Bagher Zolqadr | Ascent of the Guardsman
stories.summary: Mohammad Bagher Zolqadr, a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander, has risen to become Secretary of Iran's National Security Council. His appointment signals a tightening of IRGC influence over Iran's state decision-making apparatus.

stories.title: Russian drones kill four in Ukraine, damage key infrastructure and maternity hospital
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 273 drones targeting Ukrainian positions, with the southern Odesa region being the primary focus. The attacks killed four people, damaged key infrastructure, and struck a maternity hospital.

stories.title: Joe Kent | The rebel within
stories.summary: Joe Kent, who resigned as US National Counterterrorism chief, said Israel and its lobby drew the United States into the war on Iran. The former soldier publicly broke with the administration over the conflict.

stories.title: Key moments in first month of US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: One month after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, the conflict has escalated across the Middle East, with multiple fronts and actors drawn into the fighting.

stories.title: Air defences down drone near residence of senior Iraqi politician
stories.summary: Air defense systems intercepted a drone near the residence of Masoud Barzani, the leader of Iraq's Kurdistan Region, in Erbil. Security sources confirmed the incident to Reuters early Sunday. No casualties or significant damage were reported.

stories.title: Baghdad orders probe after drone targets Kurdistan president’s home
stories.summary: A drone attack targeted the home of the president of Iraq's Kurdistan Region early Saturday, according to security sources in Baghdad. Iraqi authorities ordered a probe into the incident amid rising tensions across northern Iraq.

stories.title: Air strikes in Iraq kill three PMF fighters, two police
stories.summary: Air strikes in Iraq killed three fighters from the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) and two police officers. The strikes are part of a widening conflict in Iraq that began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Saudi pipeline circumventing the Strait of Hormuz running at full capacity
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, is now operating at its full capacity of 7 million barrels per day. Exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu have reached approximately 5 million barrels per day, with additional refined product shipments of 700,000 to 900,000 barrels daily.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon kills 3 journalists covering the war
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon killed three journalists. The Israeli military claimed one of the targets, Al Manar TV journalist Ali Shoeib, was a Hezbollah intelligence operative, without providing evidence.

stories.title: Israel claims 142 injured in 24 hours, total war casualties reach 5,689
stories.summary: Israel's Health Ministry reported 142 people were hospitalized in the past 24 hours, bringing total war-related injuries to 5,689. Of 132 patients still hospitalized, 15 are in serious condition and one is critical.

stories.title: ‘Blatant crime’: Israeli strike kills 3 journalists in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon killed three journalists, including Al Manar reporter Ali Shoaib and Al Mayadeen reporter Fatima Ftouni, along with her brother Mohammed, a cameraman. Lebanese authorities condemned the attack as a war crime, noting the vehicle was clearly marked as a press car.

stories.title: Reza Pahlavi pledges to ‘make Iran great again’ at 2026 CPAC conference
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's exiled shah, spoke at the 2026 CPAC conference and called on the Trump administration to continue its military campaign against Iran. The Iranian opposition figure pledged to restore Iran's greatness.

stories.title: Israel strikes towns, villages across southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on towns and villages across southern Lebanon as part of its ongoing military operations in the region.

stories.title: How China is stepping into the cultural repatriation void left by a retreating US
stories.summary: China is positioning itself as a leader in the repatriation of looted cultural artefacts, using legal frameworks, diplomacy, and a Global South coalition to reshape international restitution norms. This effort, examined by journalist Xinlu Liang, comes as the United States withdraws from heritage and science organizations worldwide, leaving a gap Beijing aims to fill.

stories.title: IDF says up to 90% of Iran’s weapons industry could be hit within days
stories.summary: Israeli defense officials stated that most of Iran's military-industrial infrastructure has already sustained damage from strikes. They indicated that continued operations could disable up to 90 percent of Iran's weapons industry within days.

stories.title: ‘Exercise in deflection masquerading as concern’: FO rejects India’s comments on Pakistan’s Shia community
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office rejected India's comments regarding the treatment of Pakistan's Shia community, calling them "cynical and diversionary." The statement followed Indian remarks about comments attributed to Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir during a meeting with Shia clerics.

stories.title: Pakistan secures Iran deal to send 20 ships through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Pakistan secured a diplomatic agreement with Iran allowing 20 Pakistani ships to transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The deal comes as international observers watch for signs of broader diplomatic progress amid the ongoing regional conflict.

stories.title: Journalism body condemns Israeli assault on CNN crew in West Bank
stories.summary: The Foreign Press Association condemned what it called a violent assault by Israeli soldiers on a CNN crew near the Palestinian village of Tayasir in the occupied West Bank. Soldiers reportedly pointed rifles at journalists, physically assaulted a cameraman, and detained the crew.

stories.title: Double fears over Red Sea, Hormuz
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels escalated their involvement in the Middle East conflict by firing two missiles toward Israel. The development has heightened concerns that the group could again disrupt Red Sea shipping routes, a critical corridor for global trade, adding further instability to an already volatile regional situation.

stories.title: Watch: Iran war: Iran just needs to play the longer game, says Trita Parsi
stories.summary: Analyst Trita Parsi argued that Iran's strategy in the current war relies on patience and long-term resilience rather than seeking a quick military victory, suggesting Tehran aims to outlast its adversaries through sustained pressure.

stories.title: Israeli military kills three Palestinian men in Gaza, health officials say
stories.summary: The Israeli military killed three Palestinian men in two separate airstrikes in Gaza on Saturday, according to local health officials. The killings occurred more than five months after a US-brokered ceasefire was established.

stories.title: Three Lebanese journalists killed in Israeli strike, say broadcasters
stories.summary: Three Lebanese journalists were killed in an Israeli military strike. The Israeli military confirmed it killed Ali Shoeib, a correspondent for Hezbollah-affiliated Al Manar TV. The broadcasters of the other two journalists also confirmed their deaths.

stories.title: Another two India-bound LPG tankers exit Gulf through Hormuz
stories.summary: Two India-bound LPG tankers transited the Strait of Hormuz, following two other India-bound tankers that were granted safe passage earlier in March. The transits occur amid ongoing tensions affecting shipping in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis launch ballistic missile at Israel as Middle East conflict escalates
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels fired a ballistic missile toward Israel on Saturday, marking their formal entry into the widening Middle East war. The launch occurred amid ongoing U.S.-Israeli airstrikes on Iran and growing disruptions to Red Sea shipping lanes that threaten global trade and energy markets.

stories.title: Iran accuses US-Israel of targeting universities in ongoing war
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused the United States and Israel of deliberately targeting universities and research centers in Iran, including facilities in Isfahan and Tehran. He said the strikes aimed to undermine Iran's scientific and cultural institutions.

stories.title: Iran President lauds Pakistan for mediation to stop U.S., Israel ‘aggression’
stories.summary: Iran's president praised Pakistan for its mediation efforts aimed at stopping what Tehran describes as US and Israeli aggression during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Rosatom says situation at Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant keeps deteriorating
stories.summary: Rosatom head warned that the situation at Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant continues to deteriorate following another strike near the facility. Russia's state nuclear corporation said the attacks pose a direct threat to nuclear safety.

stories.title: Hundreds of Israelis protest against war, clash with police
stories.summary: Hundreds of Israeli protesters gathered in several cities on Saturday to demonstrate against their country's war with Iran. Clashes between demonstrators and police were reported during the rallies.

stories.title: Strike kills three fighters in northern Iraq
stories.summary: An air strike on a police station in Mosul, northern Iraq, killed three fighters and two police officers on Saturday. Five others were wounded in the attack.

stories.title: Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London on Saturday to protest against the rise of far-right movements in the United Kingdom. The demonstration took place weeks before local elections.

stories.title: AI infrastructure on the front line: Lessons for Asean from the Iran war
stories.summary: On March 1, Amazon Web Services reported drone strikes on its data center facilities in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain following Israeli and U.S. attacks on Iran. The strikes caused structural damage and disrupted cloud services. Iran warned that U.S. tech companies with Israeli ties, including Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia, were considered legitimate targets for retaliation.

stories.title: Man killed in Sumy region after Russian drone explosion
stories.summary: A 75-year-old man was killed in the Znob-Novhorod community of Ukraine's Sumy Oblast after a Russian drone exploded. The strike targeted the region, which borders Russia.

stories.title: Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi to CPAC: A free Iran is within reach right now
stories.summary: Iranian opposition figure and Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi addressed the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC), urging support for a free and democratic Iran. He rejected partial settlements with Iran's current government and positioned Iran as a potential future partner of the US and Israel.

stories.title: Israeli strike on south Lebanon kills seven, wounds eight
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on Deir al-Zahrani in the Nabatieh district of southern Lebanon killed seven people and wounded eight others. Lebanon's National News Agency and the Health Emergency Operations Centre at the Ministry of Public Health confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: ‘No Kings’ anti-Trump rallies take place across US amid anger over Iran war
stories.summary: Anti-Trump protests branded 'No Kings' took place across the United States, driven in part by opposition to the ongoing war with Iran. Organizers reported a nearly 40% increase in protest events outside major cities since the demonstrations began in June.

stories.title: Sweet heist? Nestle says 12 tonnes of KitKat stolen in Europe
stories.summary: Nestlé confirmed that a truck carrying approximately 12 tonnes — 413,793 units — of KitKat chocolate bars was stolen during transit between production and distribution sites in Europe. The company warned the theft could cause store shortages ahead of Easter.

stories.title: Son of exiled shah rejects Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the son of Iran's last shah, rejected the possibility of peace negotiations with Iran's current leadership at the Conservative Political Action Conference in Texas. The 65-year-old argued Tehran would use diplomacy to stall while continuing hostile behavior.

stories.title: 21 arrested in Tel Aviv, Haifa during mounting protests against Iran war
stories.summary: Police arrested 21 people during anti-war protests in Tel Aviv and Haifa as demonstrations against Israel's involvement in the Iran conflict grew. Mainstream Israeli protest groups offered tentative support to the anti-war movement for the first time since fighting began.

stories.title: Nighttime attack on Odesa: two dead, number of injured rises to 14
stories.summary: A Russian overnight attack on the Ukrainian city of Odesa killed two people and injured at least 14 others. The number of total casualties rose to 16 as rescue operations continued.

stories.title: Kuwait airport hit by Iranian drone strikes
stories.summary: Kuwait International Airport was struck by suspected Iranian drones on Saturday, sending thick black smoke rising from the facility. The attack caused damage to the airport, though full casualty details were not immediately available.

stories.title: Poland and Estonia are building Shahed killer Mark I at sustainable cost. Lesson came from Ukraine
stories.summary: Poland and Estonia are jointly developing the Shahed Killer Mark I, a cost-effective system designed to counter Iranian-made Shahed drones. The project draws on lessons from Ukraine, where shooting down cheap drones with expensive missiles proved unsustainable.

stories.title: Russia declares emergency in Dagestan's capital as floods cut power to more than 327,000 people
stories.summary: Authorities in Makhachkala, the capital of Russia's Dagestan region, declared a state of emergency on Saturday after heavy rainfall caused widespread flooding. Power was cut to more than 327,000 people across the southern Russian region.

stories.title: Settlers attack several Palestinian villages, 2 reported injured; no arrests made
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, injuring at least two people including a Palestinian teenager and a foreign volunteer. Medics reported victims were beaten and pepper-sprayed. No arrests were made, with residents saying Israeli forces arrived too late.

stories.title: Iran-backed Houthis join war with attack against Israel
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement, an Iran-backed group, launched an attack against Israel, marking its entry into the wider conflict. Concerns have risen that the Houthis may also target commercial shipping in the Red Sea, which could disrupt global trade and compound existing economic pressures.

stories.title: Could Ukraine’s drone expertise serve Gulf countries?
stories.summary: Gulf nations are exploring new defense partnerships as the Iran conflict escalates, with Ukraine's expertise in drone warfare drawing particular interest. The potential cooperation could see Ukrainian drone technology and tactics adopted by Gulf states.

stories.title: Urging US to ‘stay the course’ in Iran, exiled prince wins ovation from conservatives
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last shah, received a standing ovation at CPAC after urging the United States to continue its campaign against Iran. He argued that only the fall of the Islamic Republic could bring lasting regional stability.

stories.title: Qatar elder statesman warns Israel’s war on Iran risks spiralling out of control
stories.summary: Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani, a former Qatari prime minister and foreign minister, warned that the Israeli-US military campaign against Iran risks triggering a prolonged regional escalation. He described the coming days as decisive for determining whether the conflict can be resolved.

stories.title: War Diary Day 29: Industrial strikes against Iran trigger wider retaliation
stories.summary: On day 29 of the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted major steel production facilities in Ahvaz and Isfahan as well as nuclear infrastructure. Iran and its proxies responded with coordinated retaliatory attacks across multiple Gulf states, widening the conflict's regional scope.

stories.title: Indonesia says it is in ‘positive’ talks with Iran to let tankers pass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Indonesia reported it is in "positive" negotiations with Iran to secure safe passage for its tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels are carrying crude oil for domestic use and fuel oil intended for external consumers.

stories.title: Russian forces strike two districts in Dnipropetrovsk region 45 times, causing damage
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 45 artillery and drone attacks on two districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region on March 28. The strikes damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure and caused fires.

stories.title: WTO talks eye fresh extension of e-commerce duties moratorium
stories.summary: World Trade Organization members are discussing a fresh extension of the moratorium on customs duties for electronic commerce transmissions, which is set to expire at the end of March. India has publicly voiced disagreement with renewing the moratorium.

stories.title: Russian drones kill four in Ukraine, damage key infrastructure and maternity hospital
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 273 drones targeting Ukrainian territory, with the southern Odesa region bearing the brunt of the attacks. The strikes killed four people and damaged key infrastructure, including a maternity hospital.

stories.title: Houthis say they launched second attack on Israel, vow more strikes
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi group announced it carried out a second attack on Israel on Saturday using missiles and drones. The group pledged to continue military operations against Israel in the coming days.

stories.title: Israel hits Iran naval research site, fresh blasts rattle Tehran
stories.summary: The Israeli military said it struck a naval weapons research facility in Tehran on Saturday. The attack is part of Israel's ongoing campaign of strikes across Iran.

stories.title: Press group slams Israeli forces' 'violent assault' on CNN crew
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned what it called a violent assault by Israeli soldiers on a CNN crew in the occupied West Bank. The journalists were covering an attack by extremist settlers on local Palestinians at the time of the incident.

stories.title: Egypt to slow some state projects amid Iran war
stories.summary: Egypt announced it will slow large state projects involving fuel consumption for at least two months. The decision is a response to energy disruptions caused by the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine denies Iran destroyed anti-drone system depot in UAE
stories.summary: Ukraine denied Iranian claims that Tehran destroyed a facility in the United Arab Emirates allegedly used to support the US military. Iran had earlier said it struck the depot, which it described as housing anti-drone systems.

stories.title: Missiles hit southern Israeli city of Eilat
stories.summary: Social media footage shows a missile strike hitting the southern Israeli city of Eilat. Details on casualties and the origin of the strike have not been independently confirmed.

stories.title: UAVs strike diesel locomotive transporting cargo for Russian military
stories.summary: Soldiers from Ukraine's "Reid" regiment used unmanned aerial vehicles to identify and strike a diesel locomotive transporting cargo for Russian military forces. The attack targeted key logistics assets on a critical front-line sector.

stories.title: Cop martyred in terrorist attack on police vehicle in Bannu
stories.summary: Head Constable Dilnawaz Khan was killed and three other officers were injured when militants attacked a police vehicle in the Sheikhan Mama Khel area of Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Police said two attackers were killed in the ensuing exchange of fire.

stories.title: Iran war: US amphibious assault ship arrives in Mideast amid talk of ground operation
stories.summary: The USS Tripoli, a US amphibious assault ship carrying approximately 3,500 Marines and sailors, arrived in the Middle East amid growing speculation about a possible US ground operation in Iran. The vessel's contingent includes transport and strike fighter aircraft as well as amphibious assault assets.

stories.title: Iran allows Pakistani ships through Hormuz in ‘harbinger of peace’ move
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced that Iran has approved the passage of 20 Pakistani-flagged ships through the Strait of Hormuz, with two vessels crossing daily. Dar described the arrangement as a step toward regional peace and stability.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three journalists in south Lebanon, authorities denounce 'war crime'
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon on Saturday killed three journalists covering the war between Israel and Hezbollah. The Israeli military claimed one journalist was a Hezbollah intelligence operative but provided no evidence. Lebanese authorities condemned the attack as a war crime.

stories.title: Ukrainian experts already develop solutions to protect Qatar’s airspace, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukrainian air defense experts have conducted a comprehensive assessment of Qatar's capabilities against aerial threats. The experts have developed specific solutions to strengthen Qatar's air defense systems.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky agrees to air defence cooperation with UAE, Qatar on Gulf tour
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed defence cooperation agreements with Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia during an unannounced tour of Gulf nations. The deals focus on countering aerial threats from missiles and drones amid the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: Questions over Israel’s interceptor stockpiles as Mid-East war drags on
stories.summary: Questions are mounting over whether Israel can maintain its interceptor stockpiles as the Middle East conflict continues. The Israeli military has dismissed reports that it is running low on interceptors used to counter missile and rocket attacks.

stories.title: Houthi missile attack on Israel stokes fears of renewed strikes on Red Sea shipping
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces launched a missile attack on Israel, raising fears they could resume strikes on Red Sea shipping. Analysts warn the effects would be devastating if the Iran-backed group disrupts the waterway, which some vessels use as an alternative to the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Qatar elder statesman warns Israel’s war on Iran risks spiralling out of control
stories.summary: Qatar's former Premier and Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassem al-Thani warned that Israel's war against Iran risks spiralling out of control. He suggested the escalation offers little benefit to the United States, while Israel stands to gain from a prolonged conflict.

stories.title: World’s largest aircraft carrier USS Gerald Ford arrives in Croatia for repairs
stories.summary: The USS Gerald Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, arrived in Croatia for repairs. A non-combat fire had broken out in the ship's main laundry room on March 12, injuring three sailors.

stories.title: Several hurt as Iranian missile hits Jerusalem-area town; Hezbollah continues to strike north
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck the town of Eshtaol near Jerusalem, lightly wounding about 19 people. Separately, two impacts were detected near Eilat with no injuries. The IDF reported Hezbollah fired approximately 250 rockets at Israeli targets over the past day.

stories.title: Russia to impose temporary gasoline export ban amid Iran war
stories.summary: Russia announced a temporary ban on gasoline exports effective April 1 through July 31, 2026. The measure aims to stabilize domestic fuel supply and control prices amid market volatility linked to the ongoing crisis in West Asia.

stories.title: Over 400,000 KitKat bars stolen, as thieves ‘make a break’ with 12 tonne shipment
stories.summary: A truck carrying approximately 413,793 KitKat bars weighing around 12 tonnes was stolen during transit in Europe. Nestlé confirmed the theft of the shipment, which disappeared last week between production and distribution locations, warning it could cause store shortages before Easter.

stories.title: Missing Cuba-bound boats carrying aid arrive safely in Havana
stories.summary: Two sailboats had gone missing while sailing from Mexico to Havana to alleviate the humanitarian crisis in Cuba. The Mexican Navy located the vessels and escorted them to port.

stories.title: Mexico finds 2 boats lost while carrying aid to Cuba
stories.summary: Mexican officials located two sailboats that had gone missing while carrying humanitarian aid from Mexico to Havana, Cuba. Both vessels were found and all crew members were reported safe.

stories.title: US-Israeli strikes kill at least 12 in multiple residential, civilian areas: Iran media
stories.summary: US and Israeli overnight airstrikes hit multiple residential and civilian areas in cities across northern and northwestern Iran, killing at least 12 people, according to Iranian media reports.

stories.title: Air defense systems activated in Kyiv region
stories.summary: Air defense systems were activated in the Kyiv region after Russian drones were detected overhead. Ukrainian Air Defense Forces engaged and shot down the incoming targets.

stories.title: 'The Road to October 7': The long centuries of hatred that led to Hamas’s attack - review
stories.summary: A review examines the book 'The Road to October 7,' which traces centuries of antisemitism and hostility leading to Hamas's October 7 attack. The review follows a previously published interview with the author.

stories.title: Potential Houthi threat to Red Sea shipping could further damage global economy
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the Iran-backed Houthi group could disrupt shipping through the Red Sea, potentially bringing a second major waterway to a standstill alongside the Strait of Hormuz. The threat poses significant risks to global supply chains and energy markets.

stories.title: IDF detains CNN journalists in the West Bank, one crew member injured, cameras damaged
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers detained a CNN crew covering settler violence in the West Bank for approximately two hours. One photographer was injured during the incident and his camera was damaged.

stories.title: Zelenskyy visits UAE for talks on security situation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the United Arab Emirates for talks on the broader security situation. Zelenskyy emphasized that countering terrorism is a matter of principle for Ukraine globally.

stories.title: Tears and defiance as Lebanese family bury child, 11, killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: Eleven-year-old Jawad Younes and his uncle Ragheb were buried on Saturday in Lebanon after an Israeli strike hit their family compound the previous day. Mourners expressed both grief and defiance at the funeral.

stories.title: Mexico's navy locates two missing sailboats carrying aid to Cuba, crew safe
stories.summary: Two sailboats carrying humanitarian aid from Mexico to Cuba that had gone missing were located by the Mexican Navy. A spokesman for the Nuestra America Convoy confirmed on Saturday that all crew members are safe.

stories.title: Foreign Ministers of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkiye to visit  Pakistan for talks on West Asia
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Türkiye are set to visit Pakistan for discussions on the situation in West Asia. Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister stated the country is working with "honesty and sincerity" to help resolve ongoing disputes in the region.

stories.title: Zelensky: Europe must be stronger than single leader with anti-European views
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy called on Europe to demonstrate strength independent of any single leader with anti-European views. He also expressed hope that the EU would find a way to unblock a €90 billion loan for Ukraine.

stories.title: Murder inquiry launched after death of young woman in Leeds
stories.summary: West Yorkshire Police in Leeds launched a murder investigation after a young woman was found unconscious with serious injuries on Kennerleigh Avenue in Austhorpe early Saturday morning. She was taken to hospital but pronounced dead shortly after. Four people have been arrested.

stories.title: US and Iraq to ‘intensify cooperation’ against attacks
stories.summary: The United States and Iraq agreed to intensify cooperation to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks against U.S. facilities. The announcement signals a renewed joint security commitment between Baghdad and Washington.

stories.title: Zelensky: U.S. ready to provide security guarantees only after Ukrainian army withdraws from Donbas
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that the United States has conditioned the provision of security guarantees to Ukraine on the withdrawal of Ukrainian armed forces from the Donbas region.

stories.title: ‘Blatant crime’: Israeli strike kills at least 2 journalists in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike struck a clearly marked press vehicle in Jezzine, southern Lebanon, killing Al Manar TV correspondent Ali Shoaib and Al Mayadeen TV correspondent Fatima Ftouni. Al Mayadeen reported that additional journalists were in the vehicle at the time of the strike.

stories.title: FIA director general says agency has compiled data of human smugglers, facilitators
stories.summary: FIA Director General Dr Usman Anwar briefed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi at FIA headquarters in Islamabad, disclosing that the agency has compiled comprehensive data on individuals involved in human smuggling. The FIA is establishing coordination committees with other agencies and deploying modern technology to strengthen enforcement.

stories.title: Urkaine’s Zelensky agrees air defence cooperation with UAE, Qatar on Gulf tour
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to air defense cooperation deals with the UAE and Qatar during a Gulf tour. Ukraine has promoted its anti-drone defense capabilities, which it describes as the most advanced in the world.

stories.title: Ukraine, UAE agree to cooperate on defence, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine and the United Arab Emirates have agreed to cooperate on defence matters. Zelensky said on Telegram that their respective teams would finalize the details of the arrangement.

stories.title: Media association condemns ‘violent assault’ on CNN crew by Israeli soldiers
stories.summary: The Foreign Press Association condemned what it called a violent assault by Israeli soldiers who detained a CNN crew near the Palestinian village of Tayasir in the occupied West Bank. The team had been reporting on the aftermath of an Israeli settler attack and the establishment of an illegal outpost.

stories.title: Who says Israeli attacks in Lebanon kill nine paramedics, wound seven
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported that Israeli strikes on healthcare workers in southern Lebanon killed nine paramedics and wounded seven others across five separate attacks. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said four hospitals and 51 primary healthcare centres have been forced to shut down.

stories.title: Anti-Trump rallies pop up in thousands of US cities for 'No Kings' protest
stories.summary: Demonstrators gathered in thousands of U.S. cities on Saturday, March 28, for the third round of "No Kings" rallies opposing President Donald Trump's policies. Protesters in St. Paul, Dallas, Washington, and New York voiced opposition to aggressive deportation efforts and the war in Iran.

stories.title: At CPAC, a generational divide over Republican support for Israel
stories.summary: At the Conservative Political Action Conference, a generational divide emerged over Republican support for Israel. Attendees aged 45 and younger were more likely to question the party's longstanding pro-Israel stance compared to older participants.

stories.title: Sweet heist? Nestle says 12,000kg of KitKat stolen
stories.summary: Nestlé reported that approximately 12,000 kilograms of KitKat chocolate bars were stolen. The company warned the theft could lead to a shortage of KitKats on store shelves ahead of the Easter holiday.

stories.title: Victorians get free public transport for a month in bid to ease surge in fuel demand
stories.summary: The Victorian state government in Australia announced free public transport on all metro and regional V/Line services from March 31 through the end of April. The temporary measure aims to reduce fuel demand as petrol prices surge due to the Middle East conflict's impact on energy markets.

stories.title: Army is 100% supplied with fuel, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy confirmed that the Armed Forces of Ukraine are currently 100% supplied with fuel. He added that he is negotiating additional fuel supply agreements with Middle Eastern countries.

stories.title: 17 people killed, five missing in flooding in western Yemen
stories.summary: Flooding in western Yemen killed at least 17 people, with authorities searching for five others who remain missing. Officials warned residents to exercise caution as further rainfall is expected.

stories.title: As war rages, Iranian politicians push for exit from nuclear weapons treaty
stories.summary: Amid ongoing US-Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure, hardline Iranian politicians are calling for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, escalating tensions over the country's nuclear posture.

stories.title: France opens probe into suspected attack on Bank of America in Paris
stories.summary: French police in Paris arrested a suspect who was reportedly attempting to detonate an explosive device outside the Bank of America headquarters. A second suspect remains at large.

stories.title: Iran kills 'militants', arrests dozens in security crackdown
stories.summary: Iranian authorities said they killed suspected militants and arrested dozens of people linked to Israel and the United States. The operations are part of a widening wartime security crackdown across multiple Iranian provinces.

stories.title: Ukraine, UAE agree to cooperate on defence, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Saturday and announced an agreement to cooperate on security and defence matters.

stories.title: US-Israeli strike kills Iraqi government-linked fighters in Kirkuk: Report
stories.summary: A strike in Kirkuk, northern Iraq, killed three members of the Popular Mobilisation Forces and wounded four others. The PMF, which is formally integrated into Iraq's armed forces, blamed the United States and Israel for the attack.

stories.title: Israel assesses damage after missile strike near Jerusalem
stories.summary: An Iranian ballistic missile struck the town of Eshtaol near Jerusalem, injuring residents and damaging homes, vehicles, and nearby structures. The strike occurred as the regional war between Israel and Iran entered its second month.

stories.title: War update: Russian forces launch 143 attacks, fiercest clashes are in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 143 attacks on Ukrainian defensive positions in a single day, with the heaviest fighting occurring in the Pokrovsk sector. Increased Russian activity was also reported in the Huliaipole, Kostiantynivka, and Oleksandrivka sectors.

stories.title: Paris: Suspected bomb attack outside Bank of America foiled
stories.summary: French police arrested a suspect reportedly attempting to activate an explosive device outside the Bank of America office in Paris. A second individual involved in the suspected bomb attack remains at large.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP says Lebanon will be part of Iran war truce talks
stories.summary: A Hezbollah member of parliament stated that Lebanon will be included in any ceasefire negotiations related to the Iran conflict. The lawmaker rejected certain proposals as amounting to surrender, as fighting along Lebanon's front continues to intensify.

stories.title: 'Down with the king': Death of Bahraini in custody sparks angry dissent
stories.summary: The death of 32-year-old Mohamed al-Mosawi in Bahraini custody has triggered public dissent in the Gulf state. Al-Mosawi was reportedly detained at a checkpoint during Ramadan, and rights group BIRD alleges he was subjected to enforced disappearance and torture.

stories.title: Zelensky explains why Ukraine has no fuel reserves
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy explained that Ukraine's diesel fuel reserves were depleted because Russia targeted fuel storage facilities at the start of the war. Current reserves are committed to existing supply contracts.

stories.title: Strike kills Iraqi government-linked fighter, wounds six
stories.summary: A missile strike on a base near Kirkuk airport in northern Iraq killed one Popular Mobilisation Forces fighter and wounded six others, according to Iraqi security and medical sources. Responsibility for the strike has not been confirmed, though US or Israeli forces have been blamed for recent attacks in the area.

stories.title: Why Israelis living through this moment may be the lucky ones - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on the hardships faced by Israelis during the current period of conflict. The author argues that those enduring difficult times that lead to improvement may ultimately be considered fortunate in historical retrospect.

stories.title: Our refuge: War, loss, and faith are shaping Israel’s shared story - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses how ongoing wars are shaping a collective Israeli national narrative. The author argues that shared experiences of conflict and loss forge a sense of communal resilience and faith among citizens.

stories.title: Iran footballers pay tribute to victims of school strike
stories.summary: Iranian football players paid tribute to victims of an Israeli airstrike on a school in the southern Iranian city of Minab. The strike, which occurred on 28 February, killed at least 170 people, including students.

stories.title: Ukraine struck Russian explosives factory 1,000 kilometers from front with Flamingo cruise missile it built itself
stories.summary: Ukraine struck a Russian explosives factory in Chapayevsk, approximately 1,000 kilometers from the front lines, using a domestically built Flamingo cruise missile. The plant supplied explosive fill for Russian munitions.

stories.title: Stray drones put Baltic states in crossfire of Ukraine conflict
stories.summary: Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia have requested European Union assistance to strengthen their air defenses amid concerns over stray drones linked to the Ukraine conflict entering Baltic airspace.

stories.title: Questions over Israel’s interceptor stockpiles as Mideast war drags on
stories.summary: Analysts are questioning whether Israel's multi-layered air defense system can sustain its interceptor stockpiles as the Middle East war continues into its second month. The Israeli military has denied reports of shortages, but some assessments suggest long-range interceptors have been significantly depleted by ongoing Iranian missile and Hezbollah rocket attacks.

stories.title: Michigan student disciplined for protesting against war on Gaza reaches settlement with school
stories.summary: A Palestinian and Arab middle school student in Canton, Michigan, reached a settlement with her school district after filing a lawsuit over her first amendment rights. The teenager alleged she faced racism from a teacher for refusing to stand for the pledge of allegiance as a protest against the war on Gaza.

stories.title: BBC Arabic defended as lone voice in region for giving ‘Israeli perspective’
stories.summary: BBC World Service director Fiona Crack defended BBC Arabic as a unique voice in the region for covering the Israeli perspective on stories overlooked by Gulf state-owned media. The Arabic service has faced sustained criticism over its coverage choices and calls for its closure.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine does not receive any indications from partners regarding redirection of weapons to Middle East
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has received no indications from US or allied partners that weapons designated for Ukraine are being redirected to the conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Two Sudanese men face court in Greece after at least 22 people die off Crete coast
stories.summary: Two Sudanese men appeared before a court in Crete, Greece, accused of smuggling migrants from Libya. At least 22 people died after being thrown overboard during six days adrift at sea without food or water. The suspects were given 48 hours to prepare testimony before an investigating magistrate.

stories.title: Paris cops thwart suspected terrorist bombing near Bank of America
stories.summary: French police in Paris foiled a suspected terrorist bombing plot near a Bank of America location. France's interior minister announced heightened security measures for Jewish, American, and Iranian opposition targets amid the ongoing regional war.

stories.title: Why diverging US-Israel goals complicate how the Iran war ends
stories.summary: The United States and Israel have diverging objectives in the war with Iran, complicating prospects for ending the conflict. Washington seeks to contain Iran and protect energy markets, while Israel pursues a more aggressive strategy aimed at collapsing the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis strike at Israel as attacks on Iran continue
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement launched strikes targeting Israel amid the ongoing attacks on Iran. Analysts warn that if the Houthis escalate further, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a critical global shipping choke point, could become a target.

stories.title: No Kings protests live updates: millions of people across the US expected to rally against Trump administration
stories.summary: Millions of people across all 50 US states participated in the third round of "No Kings" protests against the Trump administration, with more than 3,000 events scheduled. The protests are part of a coalition opposing what organizers describe as a slide toward authoritarianism.

stories.title: CNN crew say troops assaulted them, detained them, then trumpeted far-right ideology
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers at an illegal outpost in the West Bank detained a CNN crew, assaulted members, and damaged equipment. One soldier told the reporter he was carrying out "revenge" for a settler's death. The IDF condemned the incident and said it would investigate.

stories.title: Bahrain probes death of jailed activist, denies Shia crackdown
stories.summary: Bahraini authorities are investigating the death of a jailed activist while denying accusations of a crackdown on the Shia community. The Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy said the activist's family was contacted to collect his body from a military hospital.

stories.title: France hosts ‘No Kings’ march as anti-Trump protests spread
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators rallied at the Place de la Bastille in Paris for a "No Kings" march protesting against US President Donald Trump. The protest, part of a wider wave of anti-Trump demonstrations, denounced authoritarianism and "endless wars."

stories.title: Lebanon condemns ‘blatant war crime’ after Israel kills three journalists
stories.summary: Lebanon's government condemned the killing of three journalists in an Israeli missile strike in southern Lebanon as a "blatant war crime." The victims were Ali Shoeib of Al Manar TV and Fatima and Mohammed Ftouni of Al Mayadeen, killed in a strike on their car far from the frontlines.

stories.title: Russian forces launch airstrike on Komyshuvakha; one person injured
stories.summary: Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. One woman was injured in the airstrike.

stories.title: Russian satellites imaged US Diego Garcia, Prince Sultan Air Base, Al-Udeid, and Incirlik — days before Iranian strikes, says Zelenskyy
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy, speaking in Qatar, shared intelligence indicating that Russian satellites imaged several key Western military installations — including Diego Garcia, Prince Sultan Air Base, Al-Udeid, and Incirlik — days before Iranian strikes were carried out.

stories.title: German city wary as Volkswagen weighs shifting car plant to Iron Dome production
stories.summary: Volkswagen is reportedly considering converting its car manufacturing plant in Osnabrück, Germany, to produce Iron Dome missile defence components, potentially saving 2,300 jobs. Some residents fear the shift could make the city a military target, while others question the system's relevance for Europe.

stories.title: Senegal celebrate AFCON win at Stade de France after being stripped of title
stories.summary: Senegal paraded the Africa Cup of Nations trophy at the Stade de France in Paris ahead of a friendly against Peru, despite being ordered to return it. CAF had reversed Senegal's 1-0 final victory over Morocco in Rabat and awarded a 3-0 win to the hosts.

stories.title: 'Down with the king': Death of Bahraini in custody sparks angry dissent
stories.summary: The death in custody of Mohamed al-Mosawi in Bahrain has sparked public protests, with mourners gathering at his funeral in Muharraq. Bahrainis allege the man, accused of aiding Iran, was tortured, and say his death was intended to silence dissent.

stories.title: Iranian strike on Saudi base wounds several US troops, damages aircraft
stories.summary: An Iranian attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia wounded a dozen US troops, with two suffering serious injuries and ten sustaining concussions. The strike, involving at least one missile and several drones, also damaged multiple US refuelling aircraft.

stories.title: Ukraine and Qatar signed defense partnership agreement for at least 10 years, says Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukraine and Qatar signed a defence partnership agreement for at least 10 years during President Zelenskyy's visit to Doha. The agreement was reached with Qatar's Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani.

stories.title: Houthi forces enter Iran conflict with missile attacks on Israeli military sites
stories.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen entered the US-Israeli war on Iran by launching missiles at Israeli military sites, with Israel saying it intercepted the projectiles. Pakistan announced it would host a meeting of Middle Eastern powers to seek a regional approach to ending the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy signs air defence deals with UAE, Qatar on Gulf tour
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed air defence cooperation agreements with the UAE and Qatar during a Gulf tour. Kyiv aims to leverage its experience intercepting Russian drones to assist Gulf states in countering aerial threats.

stories.title: A tide in the affairs of Nepal
stories.summary: An analysis argues that India and Nepal need to reimagine their bilateral relationship to address a geopolitical and geo-economic landscape that has fundamentally changed since 1947. The piece calls for repurposing longstanding ties so both nations can fulfill the relationship's potential.

stories.title: Situating Nepal’s current  political moment in the long history of feudalism to republican democracy
stories.summary: Nepal's political trajectory since 1950 has included feudal rule, absolute monarchy, civil war, and a transition to a republic. The Rastriya Swatantra Party won a landslide in the 2026 elections following a large but violent Gen Z-led movement. Analysts question whether this victory will overcome the country's deep structural constraints.

stories.title: Political metamorphosis of contemporary Nepal
stories.summary: Nepal's traditional parties, including the Nepali Congress and various communist factions, were sidelined in the March elections by a younger generation organized through social media and rap music. This horizontally structured movement prioritized individual aspiration over collective ideology and propelled a relatively new political force to power.

stories.title: Houthis enter war and say attacks on Iran, Hezbollah must stop
stories.summary: The Yemen-based Houthi militant group formally entered the war involving Iran, demanding that attacks on Iran and Hezbollah cease. The move marked a significant escalation of the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Palestinian teenager dies after being shot by Israeli forces
stories.summary: A 15-year-old Palestinian, Adham Dahman, died after being shot by Israeli forces at the Dheisheh refugee camp south of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: US and Iraq to 'intensify cooperation' against attacks
stories.summary: The United States and Iraq agreed to intensify cooperation against attacks targeting Iraqi forces. The announcement follows Iraq's decision to authorize the Hashed al-Shaabi militia to respond to strikes after 15 of its fighters were killed in an airstrike.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on factory in Samara region with Flamingo missiles
stories.summary: Ukraine's Armed Forces struck the Promsintez factory in Chapaevsk, Samara Region, Russia, using FP-5 Flamingo missiles. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the attack on the facility.

stories.title: Senegal parade AFCON trophy, despite title being awarded to Morocco
stories.summary: Senegal's national football team paraded the Africa Cup of Nations trophy at the Stade de France in Paris ahead of a friendly match against Peru. The display came despite the tournament title having been officially awarded to Morocco.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 5
stories.summary: Russia launched over 270 drones at Ukraine overnight, killing at least five people. In Odesa, two people were killed and 11 injured, with a maternity hospital and private homes damaged in the Black Sea port city.

stories.title: What could Houthi involvement in the Iran war mean?
stories.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile launch against Israel on Saturday, which Israel said it intercepted. Analysts warned the Houthis' entry into the month-old war could further disrupt global shipping if they resume targeting vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
