stories.title: 12 US troops wounded, 2 seriously, in Iranian attack on Saudi base — report
stories.summary: Twelve US troops were wounded, two seriously, in an Iranian attack on a Saudi Arabian base involving ballistic missiles and drones. Several aerial refueling planes were reportedly damaged. Approximately 300 American soldiers have been injured since the start of the war, with most casualties described as minor.

stories.title: Pakistan says holding 'detailed discussions' with leaders in Iran and Gulf
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said Islamabad has held detailed discussions with leaders in Iran and Gulf countries to de-escalate Middle East tensions. In a televised address, Sharif said Pakistan is pursuing diplomatic mediation while also taking measures to shield its economy from rising global oil prices.

stories.title: First MSF medical aid shipment reaches Iran via Turkey, local media reports
stories.summary: Iran's Press TV reported that the first shipment of medical aid from Doctors Without Borders (MSF) arrived in Iran via Turkey and was handed over to the Iranian Red Crescent Society. The shipment included essential pharmaceutical supplies amid disrupted humanitarian supply chains caused by the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Trump plan proposes to disarm Hamas in eight months, destroy tunnels
stories.summary: A disarmament plan presented by US President Donald Trump's "Board of Peace" would require Hamas to surrender weapons in stages over eight months and allow destruction of its Gaza tunnel network. The plan envisions a US-backed committee of Palestinian technocrats taking security control before Israeli forces withdraw.

stories.title: Pakistani ports emerge as safe trade hub
stories.summary: Global shipping lines are diverting container vessels to Karachi ports as risks increase in the Strait of Hormuz due to the Middle East conflict. Pakistan's government has reduced port charges, expedited cargo clearance, and established sub-committees to recommend structural reforms in maritime and logistics sectors.

stories.title: Gulf countries warn of rising threat from Iran-backed militias and proxies
stories.summary: Six Gulf states—Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan—issued a joint statement condemning Iranian attacks on their soil and warning of a rising threat from Iran-backed militias and proxy groups. They expressed concern that Tehran could activate sleeper cells across the Middle East amid its war with the U.S. and Israel.

stories.title: Israel’s unending attacks in Lebanon push country’s population to the brink
stories.summary: Israeli military operations in Lebanon have continued for four weeks, coinciding with a broader US-Israeli campaign against Iran. Many Lebanese civilians are suffering under the sustained bombardment and aggression.

stories.title: FBI confirms Director Kash Patel's email hack claimed by Iran-linked group
stories.summary: The FBI confirmed that Director Kash Patel's personal email account was hacked by an Iran-linked group calling itself the Handala Hack Team. The bureau said the accessed data was historical and contained no government information.

stories.title: Uproar in Bahrain after detainee dies in police custody
stories.summary: A 32-year-old detainee in Bahrain died in police custody after being arrested for opposing the war on Iran. Human rights groups say the man was killed while detained, prompting widespread outrage in the country.

stories.title: Violence in Syria's Druze heartland may be war crimes: UN
stories.summary: UN investigators warned that war crimes and crimes against humanity may have been committed during deadly violence in Syria's Suweida province, a Druze-majority area. The findings highlight ongoing instability and targeted violence in the region.

stories.title: Bank of America settles Epstein case for $72.5 million
stories.summary: Bank of America agreed to pay $72.5 million to settle a lawsuit alleging the bank ignored red flags tied to convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein's operations. The bank denied wrongdoing but chose to settle the case.

stories.title: As Vietnam leads on AI rules, Southeast Asia risks ‘economic own goal’
stories.summary: Vietnam became the first Southeast Asian nation to enact a comprehensive artificial intelligence regulatory law on March 1. Analysts warn that while such data-control measures may offer domestic benefits, the broader regional push risks undermining innovation and deterring foreign investment.

stories.title: Missile debris injures five Indian nationals in Abu Dhabi, officials say
stories.summary: Five Indian nationals were injured in Abu Dhabi by falling debris from intercepted ballistic missiles, with injuries ranging from minor to moderate. Authorities also worked to extinguish two fires caused by missile debris in the Khalifa Economic Zones.

stories.title: Ukraine plans to increase rapeseed oil exports
stories.summary: Ukraine projects rapeseed oil exports of 576,000 tons in the 2025/2026 marketing year, a 2.7-fold increase compared to the previous season.

stories.title: Morocco draw under new coach as Algeria, Egypt win big
stories.summary: Morocco drew in Mohamed Ouahbi's first match as head coach, while Algeria and Egypt both secured dominant victories in World Cup warm-up fixtures.

stories.title: UN warns of humanitarian crisis as Hormuz disruptions risk agriculture
stories.summary: The United Nations established a task force to ensure fertiliser shipments can transit the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing conflict-related disruptions. UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva warned that continued maritime trade interruptions could trigger a massive humanitarian crisis affecting global agricultural production.

stories.title: How the US-Israel war on Iran unfolded in its first four weeks
stories.summary: Al Jazeera published a review of the first four weeks of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, covering major military operations, political developments, and economic impacts during the opening month of the conflict.

stories.title: Trump says ‘Cuba is next’ target of US military
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly threatened Cuba with military action while speaking at a Saudi investment conference. The remarks raised concerns about a potential expansion of US military operations beyond the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Can ‘reliable friend’ China fill the gap as US pressures allies to snub South Africa?
stories.summary: China pledged continued support for South Africa after President Cyril Ramaphosa was disinvited from the G7 summit in France following US threats to boycott the event. The withdrawal of the invitation, originally issued by French President Macron, raised questions about whether Beijing could fill the diplomatic gap.

stories.title: US envoy predicts Iran talks as war enters second month
stories.summary: US envoy Steve Witkoff said talks with Iran could begin this week as the conflict enters its second month. The diplomatic push comes as US-Israeli strikes continue to target Iranian nuclear sites amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis threaten to join war: ‘Our fingers are on the trigger’
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels threatened to militarily intervene in the US-Israeli war on Iran if other countries join the fighting or if the Red Sea is used to attack Iran. The Iran-backed group warned their forces are ready to act.

stories.title: Israel plans 'security zone' in Lebanon as one million face permanent displacement
stories.summary: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs overnight and expanded evacuation orders across large parts of southern Lebanon up to the Zahrani River. Israeli ground forces are operating at multiple locations inside Lebanon, and approximately one million people face potential permanent displacement due to a planned Israeli security zone.

stories.title: EU and CPTPP agree to progress with ‘historic’ digital trade deal, Canada’s international trade minister says
stories.summary: The European Union and the parties to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) agreed in Yaoundé to move forward on a digital trade agreement. Canada's international trade minister described the prospective deal as historic.

stories.title: How mothers raise newborn babies during Israel’s offensive in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes on Lebanon forced civilians, including pregnant women, to flee their homes. Hawraa Houmani, 29, was nine months pregnant when she was displaced from her village by the bombing campaign.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent coordinating strikes against AFU artillery in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine's counterintelligence unit detained a Russian GRU agent in the Donetsk region. The agent was coordinating Russian airstrikes targeting Ukrainian artillery positions in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: ‘That’s a lie’: US’ Rubio attacks Zelensky, ready to divert Ukraine arms to Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly attacked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, calling his claims false. Zelensky had said in an interview that Washington was pressuring Ukraine to cede its Donbas region to Russia. Rubio also indicated willingness to redirect arms from Ukraine to the Iran campaign.

stories.title: Merz says he will fight for future of Franco-German fighter jet project
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he is working to salvage the troubled Franco-German-Spanish Future Combat Air System (FCAS) fighter jet program. Merz emphasized the need for greater cooperation within Europe's defense industry.

stories.title: UAE says interception debris caused fires in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi authorities responded to two fires caused by debris from the interception of ballistic missiles in the Khalifa Economic Zones area. Iran's IRGC separately claimed a kamikaze drone struck a hotel in Dubai targeting what it described as US elements in the region.

stories.title: 'If Lebanon won't disarm Hezbollah, the IDF will': Effie Defrin warns against Hezbollah’s rearmamen
stories.summary: Israeli official Effie Defrin warned that the IDF will disarm Hezbollah if the Lebanese government does not act. He stated that Israel will not allow Hezbollah to rearm and will continue operations to protect civilians along the northern border.

stories.title: IAF intercepts over 90% of drones launched by Iran, Hezbollah during Operation Roaring Lion
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force reported intercepting over 90% of drones launched by Iran and Hezbollah during Operation Roaring Lion. The IDF uses multiple interception systems, though the Iron Beam laser has not yet significantly reduced drone intrusions.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli advance toward Litani River
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it attacked Israeli forces that had crossed into Lebanese territory and were advancing toward the Litani River. The operations included rocket, artillery, and drone strikes near the town of Taybeh and targeted two Israeli Merkava tanks near al-Qantara in the Marjayoun district.

stories.title: Cyclone Narelle downgraded to tropical low but severe weather warnings remain for storm-ravaged WA
stories.summary: Cyclone Narelle was downgraded to a tropical low on Saturday after making landfall in Western Australia on Friday. Severe weather warnings remain in effect, with flash flooding threatening the wheatbelt region and Perth as the system moves south-east from Geraldton.

stories.title: Thousands of 'No Kings' protests planned across US in opposition to Iran war
stories.summary: The 'No Kings' protest movement organized more than 3,000 gatherings across the United States for Saturday, with opposition to the Iran war among key grievances. Major demonstrations were expected in Washington, Minneapolis, Chicago, and San Francisco.

stories.title: US’ Rubio urges world to stop Iran imposing tolls in key Hormuz strait
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on the international community to prevent Iran from imposing tolls on shipping through the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Displaced mothers in Lebanon welcome babies' new lives with hope and fear
stories.summary: Hawraa Houmani, a 29-year-old woman nearly nine months pregnant, fled Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon near Nabatieh to a school shelter in Beirut. Displaced mothers in Lebanon are giving birth in difficult conditions, cut off from their regular medical care.

stories.title: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters killed in new war with Israel so far, sources say
stories.summary: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters have been killed since the Lebanese armed group launched a new war with Israel on March 2, according to two sources familiar with Hezbollah's internal count in Beirut.

stories.title: Video shows US missile likely used in deadly strike on Iranian town, experts say
stories.summary: Weapons experts identified a U.S.-made Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) in video footage of a deadly strike on the southern Iranian town of Lamerd. Analysts say the finding points to American munitions being used in the attack.

stories.title: Nepal’s ex-PM K.P. Sharma Oli arrested over alleged role in crackdown on protesters
stories.summary: Former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli and ex-Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak were arrested in Kathmandu over their alleged involvement in a deadly crackdown on protesters in September 2025. The arrests came one day after newly elected Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his cabinet were sworn in.

stories.title: US can only confirm about a third of Iran’s missile arsenal destroyed, sources say
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence indicates that only about one-third of Iran's missile arsenal has been confirmed destroyed nearly one month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign. The status of another third remains uncertain, though bombings may have damaged or buried those missiles in underground facilities. Similar assessments apply to Iran's drone capabilities.

stories.title: UN chief launches task force to aid passage of fertiliser through Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: The United Nations Secretary-General established a task force to facilitate the passage of fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative warns that war-related disruptions could worsen global food shortages and humanitarian crises.

stories.title: German Chancellor Merz says he has doubts over Iran war aims
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed doubt that the United States and Israel have a clear strategy for ending the war in Iran. However, Merz said Germany would in principle be prepared to help stabilize the region after hostilities conclude.

stories.title: Northern residents concerned IDF won’t be allowed to ‘finish the job’ against Hezbollah
stories.summary: Evacuated residents of northern Israel expressed concern that the IDF may not be permitted to complete its military campaign against Hezbollah. Residents who remained during the conflict reported struggling to maintain their businesses amid ongoing sirens and limited shelter access.

stories.title: Russia lags in naval drone development and large-scale deployment, says Pletenchuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Pletenchuk stated that Russia lags behind in the development and large-scale deployment of unmanned naval drone systems, despite having available resources and ongoing development efforts.

stories.title: Rubio says war on Iran to last ‘weeks not months’, no US ground troops needed
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated after a G7 meeting in France that the war against Iran is expected to last weeks, not months. Rubio said Washington could achieve its objectives without ground troops but acknowledged deploying some forces to the region to preserve flexibility for President Trump.

stories.title: Intense bombing in Tehran, Isfahan
stories.summary: US-Israeli airstrikes struck Tehran and Isfahan in early morning raids, sending black smoke rising over both Iranian cities. The strikes are part of the ongoing military campaign targeting sites across Iran.

stories.title: US special envoy Witkoff predicts Iran talks as war enters second month
stories.summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff predicted Iran would hold talks with Washington as the US-Israeli war entered its second month. The conflict began on February 28 with air strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and has since expanded to target Iranian nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Trump pushes Saudi Arabia to join Abraham Accords
stories.summary: President Donald Trump urged Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords at an investment forum in Miami. He said the Middle East is being transformed by the war involving Iran and called the region's future bright.

stories.title: Canada eyes Mercosur pact by autumn
stories.summary: Canada's international trade minister announced on Friday in Yaounde that he aims to finalize a free-trade agreement with the South American Mercosur bloc by autumn. The deal would strengthen trade ties between Canada and Mercosur member states.

stories.title: Iranian media report strike on Tehran university amid attacks
stories.summary: Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency reported that a US-Israeli airstrike targeted a university in Tehran. The capital has been hit by repeated air strikes in recent weeks as part of the ongoing military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Belgian ex-diplomat appeals order to stand trial in Congo's Lumumba murder
stories.summary: A former senior Belgian diplomat has appealed a court decision ordering him to stand trial over the 1961 assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the Democratic Republic of Congo's first prime minister. The appeal was confirmed by the ex-diplomat's lawyer in Brussels on Friday.

stories.title: How China’s EV makers think they can outrun disastrous price wars
stories.summary: Chinese EV manufacturers are shifting from price competition to a technology-driven contest. BYD unveiled a battery capable of charging from 10 to 70 percent in five minutes, to be deployed in models priced as low as 155,000 yuan, while announcing plans to build 20,000 charging stations.

stories.title: KP Sharma Oli: Nepal’s former prime minister arrested over alleged role in deadly protest crackdown
stories.summary: Nepalese police arrested former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli at his residence near Kathmandu on Saturday over his alleged role in the deadly crackdown on anti-corruption protests in September that killed at least 77 people. Former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak, accused of ordering forces to fire on protesters, was also arrested.

stories.title: US operations in Iran ‘on or ahead of schedule’, says Rubio
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said military operations in Iran are on or ahead of schedule. Washington has deployed two contingents of thousands of Marines to the region to support the campaign.

stories.title: Rubio says US can achieve Iran objectives without ground troops
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States can achieve its objectives regarding Iran without deploying ground troops. Rubio indicated he expects U.S. operations in Iran to conclude within a matter of weeks.

stories.title: These pro-Palestine PACs are trying to beat AIPAC at its own game
stories.summary: Several pro-Palestine political action committees are working to elect pro-Palestinian candidates in US elections, seeking to counter AIPAC's influence. The groups are capitalizing on shifting American public sentiment toward Israel, though their electoral results remain mixed so far.

stories.title: From jammed broadcasts to a blocked website: BBC Russian's 80 years of defiance
stories.summary: BBC Russian is marking 80 years of broadcasting, having spent decades fending off signal jammers during the Soviet era. Its website is currently blocked in Russia, but millions of readers continue to access it through other means.

stories.title: Lubinets explains why he continues humanitarian dialogue with Moskalkova
stories.summary: Ukraine's Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets explained that his continued humanitarian dialogue with Russian counterpart Tatyana Moskalkova enables the delivery of letters and parcels to prisoners of war held by both sides.

stories.title: IRGC threatens 'beyond eye for eye' retaliatory strikes on US-Israeli sites in region
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened retaliatory strikes on industrial facilities linked to the US and Israel across the region. The IRGC warned that Tehran's response to attacks on its nuclear and infrastructure sites would exceed proportional retaliation and urged workers at targeted sites to evacuate.

stories.title: Death of South Korean ‘torture expert’ reopens authoritarian era wounds
stories.summary: Lee Geun-an, a former South Korean police officer notorious for torturing political prisoners during the country's authoritarian era, died at age 88 from multiple organ failure. His death revived painful memories as he had never expressed remorse, calling himself a "patriot" and his interrogation methods "art."

stories.title: How to win friends and influence people in ancient China
stories.summary: The article discusses the ancient Chinese text Guiguzi, a work on persuasion and political strategy, drawing parallels to Dale Carnegie's self-help classic on interpersonal influence.

stories.title: Trump demands Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz, slams NATO and warns: “Cuba is next”
stories.summary: President Trump declared at the FII Priority forum in Miami that the Iran military operation is two weeks ahead of schedule and demanded Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He also sharply criticized European NATO allies for not joining the campaign and warned that Cuba could be a future target.

stories.title: Iranian missile, drones strike US airbase Prince Sultan in Saudi Arabia, aircraft damaged - report
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Iranian missiles and drones struck Prince Sultan Air Base, a US facility in Saudi Arabia, damaging aircraft. The attack was confirmed through open-source imagery and data circulating online.

stories.title: Trade deal with India not far-off, but there are still gaps: U.S. official
stories.summary: A US official indicated that a trade deal between the United States and India is close but gaps remain, particularly around pulses. India seeks to protect its domestic market for the agricultural commodity, while the US is pushing for greater access.

stories.title: Trump suggests renaming Hormuz - 'Strait of Trump' during speech confirming negotiations with Iran
stories.summary: During a speech at the FII Priority Summit in Miami, US President Donald Trump suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Strait of Trump' and confirmed that negotiations with Iran are underway, urging Tehran to open the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Beirut again amid Hezbollah clashes
stories.summary: Fresh Israeli airstrikes hit southern Beirut while Hezbollah claimed ground clashes with Israeli forces. Lebanon faces mounting civilian casualties and displacement from the sustained military operations.

stories.title: US to deploy another aircraft carrier near Iran, reports say
stories.summary: The United States is expected to deploy the aircraft carrier USS George H.W. Bush to the Middle East near the ongoing conflict with Iran, according to CBS News and CNN. It is unclear whether the carrier will join or replace two American carriers already operating in the region.

stories.title: 'The gravest crime against humanity': What does the UN vote on slavery mean?
stories.summary: African and Caribbean nations are pushing at the United Nations for countries that historically benefited from the transatlantic slave trade to pay reparations. The vote highlights ongoing disagreements over compensation mechanisms.

stories.title: Iranian attack on Saudi base wounds at least 10 US troops
stories.summary: Twelve US troops were wounded, two seriously, in an Iranian military strike on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. The attack is part of the broader US-Iran conflict that has resulted in hundreds of American military casualties.

stories.title: Myanmar travellers take to the trains as fuel prices rise
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices driven by the Middle East war are pushing commuters in Myanmar to use the country's aging railway system instead of planes and cars. First-class train tickets from Yangon to Naypyidaw cost about $9, offering a significantly cheaper alternative.

stories.title: Malaysian politicians slam Philippine senator: ‘Sabah not a commodity’ to ease oil woes
stories.summary: Malaysian politicians from Sabah rejected a Philippine senator's suggestion linking the territory to oil and gas disputes. Azrul Ibrahim of Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah Youth stated that Sabah is part of a sovereign nation and outdated territorial claims should not be revived to address another country's internal crisis.

stories.title: MTR Corp’s use of CRRC technology can act as ‘showcase’ for rest of the world
stories.summary: CRRC's chief engineer said Hong Kong's MTR Corporation's use of mainland Chinese-made rail equipment can serve as a showcase for deploying the technology internationally. The partnership between MTR Corp and CRRC extends beyond equipment to broader research and development collaboration.

stories.title: China puts Ma Xingrui protege Guo Yonghang under investigation for corruption
stories.summary: Guo Yonghang, former Communist Party secretary of Guangzhou and a protégé of ex-Xinjiang party secretary Ma Xingrui, is under investigation for corruption. Ma was abruptly removed from his post in July and has since vanished from public life, deepening uncertainties about his fate.

stories.title: Chinese man rescued from ‘zip tie escape challenge’ after delivery man alerts police
stories.summary: A man in Guangzhou, China, became trapped while attempting a viral "zip tie escape challenge" at home. A passing delivery man heard his calls for help and alerted police. Firefighters forced open the gate and freed the man, who was found tightly bound.

stories.title: Israeli strikes target Nabatieh district, Bekaa Valley towns in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit multiple towns in Lebanon's Nabatieh district and the Bekaa Valley. Strikes were reported on Haboush, Kfar Tebnit, Yahmar, the Zifta Valley, and Arab Salim in southern and eastern Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump says US may reconsider role with Nato allies
stories.summary: President Trump criticized NATO allies for their lack of support during the war with Iran, suggesting the US may reconsider its commitments to the alliance. Speaking at an investment forum in Miami, he questioned why Washington should support allies who did not reciprocate.

stories.title: Trump says US is 'crushing Iran currently, as we speak'
stories.summary: President Trump claimed the United States is currently crushing Iran and that the military campaign is forcing Tehran toward negotiations. Speaking in Miami, he alleged Iranian officials were denying ongoing talks with Washington but provided no evidence.

stories.title: More than 300 US troops injured since start of Iran war
stories.summary: More than 300 U.S. troops have been injured since the start of military operations against Iran. Of those, 273 have returned to duty, while 10 soldiers remain seriously wounded.

stories.title: Court sentences woman to 18 years in prison for 'passing data to Ukraine' in Crimea
stories.summary: A court in Russian-occupied Crimea sentenced a woman from Russia's Moscow region to 18 years in prison on charges of state treason for allegedly passing information about Russian military equipment to Ukraine.

stories.title: One killed, several wounded in Iranian ballistic missile attack on central Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian ballistic missile attack struck central Israel, killing one person and wounding several others. Cluster munition bomblets hit six separate sites, damaging buildings, while two additional people were lightly hurt in southern Israel by interception debris.

stories.title: Trump says US-Israeli war on Iran creating a new Middle East
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told a Saudi investment conference that the US-Israeli war on Iran is creating a new Middle East. He claimed the region would soon be free from what he called Iranian nuclear blackmail.

stories.title: Twelve US troops wounded in Iran strike on base in Saudi Arabia, US official says
stories.summary: Twelve US troops were wounded, two seriously, in an Iranian military strike on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. The casualties add to over 300 US service members wounded since the war against Iran began on February 28.

stories.title: Three more suspects arrested for antisemitic attacks in Netherlands
stories.summary: Dutch prosecutors announced on Friday that three men were arrested in Amsterdam on suspicion of involvement in an antisemitic attack on a synagogue or helping to prepare a similar attack. The arrests are part of ongoing investigations into targeted violence against Jewish sites in the Netherlands.

stories.title: Iranian football players hold schoolbags in solidarity with girls killed in strike on Minab school
stories.summary: Iran's men's national football team wore black armbands and held schoolbags during their anthem before a friendly match against Nigeria in Belek, Turkey. The gesture honored schoolgirls killed in a strike on a school in Minab, Iran, at the start of the war. Iran's participation in the upcoming World Cup is uncertain due to the conflict.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump again slams NATO’s lack of support for war on Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's Red Crescent reported that more than 92,600 civilian housing units have been damaged across the country due to US-Israeli military strikes. President Trump again criticized NATO allies for not supporting the war on Tehran.

stories.title: Iran war energy shock revives Asean’s power grid plans: ‘it’s the way to go’
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war on Iran has pushed oil prices above $100 per barrel, causing fuel shortages and long queues across Southeast Asia. The energy shock has revived long-stalled plans for an integrated ASEAN regional power grid, with officials calling cross-border electricity sharing an urgent priority.

stories.title: Enemy strikes industrial and energy infrastructure in Kryvyi Rih, hits residential areas
stories.summary: Russian strike drones hit industrial and energy infrastructure in the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, with impacts also reported in residential areas.

stories.title: Iran-linked group claims hack of US FBI director personal email
stories.summary: An Iran-linked hacking group called the Handala Hack Team claimed responsibility for breaching FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email. The hackers leaked photos and documents in what appeared to be an effort to embarrass US officials.

stories.title: One killed, several injured in Iran missile barrage on southern, central Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile barrage triggered alarms across southern and central Israel, killing one person and injuring several others. Police are investigating possible shrapnel damage from the attack.

stories.title: Iran’s response to US peace proposal expected Friday, source says
stories.summary: Iran's response to a U.S. peace proposal aimed at ending the Middle East war was expected on Friday, according to a source briefed on the matter in Washington. The proposal seeks to bring an end to the ongoing conflict between the U.S. and Iran.

stories.title: Slovenia's PM launches coalition talks after cliffhanger election
stories.summary: Slovenian Prime Minister Robert Golob initiated coalition talks with political party leaders on Friday following an inconclusive election. Golob pledged urgent economic measures to help the Alpine country cope with soaring energy costs through a broad coalition government.

stories.title: PCB issues show-cause notice to Naseem Shah for ‘violating terms of central contract, media policy’
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board issued a show-cause notice to fast bowler Naseem Shah for violating the terms of his central contract and the board's media policy. Naseem, who also plays for PSL team Rawalpindiz, has been given a deadline to respond.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill one, injure 17 in south Lebanon: Report
stories.summary: An Israeli attack on the town of Sarafand in Lebanon's Sidon district killed one person and injured 17, according to Lebanon's National News Agency citing the Public Health Ministry.

stories.title: NYC Council’s approval of synagogue protection bill marks a welcome win for centrist Jews
stories.summary: The New York City Council approved a bill aimed at enhancing protection for synagogues, drawing overwhelming support from council members. The measure signals limits on the far left's influence in the city legislature, though its practical impact is expected to be limited.

stories.title: Labor to use new fuel security powers to underwrite extra shipments to Australia
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the government will use new fuel security powers to financially underwrite additional imports of petrol, diesel, and fertiliser affected by the Middle East war. He did not rule out future fuel rationing or work-from-home measures but expressed preference for voluntary arrangements.

stories.title: Rescue workers rush to save lives after south Tehran missile strike
stories.summary: Iranian rescue workers in south Tehran pulled survivors and bodies from a building struck by a missile. The incident is part of ongoing US-Israeli military strikes targeting the Iranian capital.

stories.title: Former minister: Canada should step up support for Ukraine as U.S. role weakens
stories.summary: A former Canadian minister urged Canada to increase its support for Ukraine's defense capabilities as the United States' role in backing Kyiv diminishes.

stories.title: Iran strike wounds US troops and damages planes at Saudi airbase
stories.summary: An Iranian missile struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday, wounding at least 10 US service members—two of them seriously—and damaging several US refueling aircraft. Satellite imagery appeared to show damage at the facility.

stories.title: 'Memory of a generation': China mourns the sudden death of a controversial education influencer
stories.summary: A prominent and controversial Chinese education influencer died suddenly at the age of 41, prompting widespread mourning across the country. The figure was described as a defining voice for a generation despite being a divisive public personality.

stories.title: Iran targets Israeli and U.S.  bases in new missile strike
stories.summary: Iran launched a new missile strike targeting Israeli and U.S. military bases in the region, marking a further escalation in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Uruguay raises fuel prices 7% over Middle East war and shifts to monthly price-setting
stories.summary: Uruguay's government announced a 7% fuel price increase effective April 1, citing rising oil costs caused by the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which handles roughly 20% of global crude oil transit.

stories.title: Milwaukee rabbi and son ordered to pay $1,000 for destroying anti-Israel mural
stories.summary: Rabbi Peter Mehler and his son Zechariah were ordered to pay $1,000 after destroying an anti-Israel mural in Milwaukee. Zechariah pleaded guilty and his father no contest; they said they felt vindicated after the Palestinian muralist reportedly praised Hamas during a court outburst.

stories.title: Zelensky: Main global challenge today is countering “Shahed” drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that countering Iranian-made Shahed drones is currently the main global security challenge. He noted the threat is well understood in the Middle East as well.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1493: Ukraine batters Russia’s Baltic oil lifeline as Estonian intelligence confirms 40–50% of exports halted
stories.summary: On day 1,493 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian drone strikes targeted Russia's Baltic oil export infrastructure. Estonian intelligence confirmed that 40 to 50 percent of Russian oil exports through the Baltic have been disrupted by the campaign.

stories.title: G-7 foreign ministers demand an end to attacks on civilians in Iran war
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers called for an end to attacks on civilians in the ongoing Iran war. The group also reiterated the need to restore safe, toll-free freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Houthis warn ‘fingers on the trigger’ as US-Israel war on Iran continues
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement warned that its forces are ready to act as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues. The Iran-aligned group has the capability to target key shipping lanes around the Arabian Peninsula.

stories.title: Israeli air force strikes Hezbollah targets in Beirut for second time on Friday
stories.summary: The Israeli air force carried out a second round of strikes on Friday targeting Hezbollah positions in Beirut. The attacks focused on the southern suburb of Dahiyeh, a known Hezbollah stronghold.

stories.title: Rubio: US can achieve Iran war aims without ground troops, campaign to end in coming weeks
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington can achieve its military objectives in Iran without deploying ground troops and expects the campaign to conclude within weeks. He noted that thousands of additional troops are being sent to the region to provide President Trump with maximum operational flexibility.

stories.title: Missile targeting Riyadh region intercepted, Saudi Arabia says
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's defence ministry announced Saturday that it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile targeting the Riyadh region. The ministry confirmed the interception via a post on the social media platform X.

stories.title: ‘Fingers on the trigger’ for military intervention, Houthis warn
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement warned it is prepared for direct military intervention if the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran escalates further, signaling the potential for a wider regional conflict.

stories.title: DM Fedorov: Electronic points can now be exchanged for drone parts and technology
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry announced that military units can now exchange electronic points on the Brave1 Market platform for drone components and technology, in addition to complete drones, electronic warfare systems, and non-lethal weapons.

stories.title: US burns through 850 Tomahawk missiles in Iran, alarming Pentagon officials, WaPo reports
stories.summary: The U.S. military has expended approximately 850 Tomahawk cruise missiles in its operations against Iran, according to a Washington Post report. The high rate of consumption has alarmed Pentagon officials and prompted internal discussions about replenishing stockpiles.

stories.title: US uses hundreds of Tomahawk missiles on Iran, alarming some at Pentagon, WaPo reports
stories.summary: The US military has fired over 850 Tomahawk cruise missiles in four weeks of war with Iran, according to a Washington Post report. The rapid consumption rate has alarmed some Pentagon officials and prompted internal discussions about replenishing precision weapons stockpiles.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers breach FBI director’s personal e-mail, publish excerpts online
stories.summary: An Iran-linked hacker group breached the personal email account of FBI Director Kash Patel and published excerpts online. The hackers publicly claimed Patel as a successfully targeted victim.

stories.title: European police targets violent Scottish crime gang behind drug trafficking
stories.summary: Europol announced that European police targeted a violent Scottish crime gang allegedly behind drug trafficking operations. The operation resulted in 13 arrests across Europe.

stories.title: Myanmar military signals leadership changes as parade begins
stories.summary: Myanmar's military junta signaled potential leadership changes as its annual Armed Forces Day parade commenced.

stories.title: Trump pitches China trade ‘win’ to US farmers ahead of Xi meeting, midterms
stories.summary: Ahead of a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, US President Trump promoted past trade agreements with China as a win for American farmers, citing over $40 billion in soybean exports. The meeting comes amid economic pressures from tariffs and the Iran war.

stories.title: French TV under fire over ‘disgraceful’ interview with Russian minister
stories.summary: French television faced criticism over an interview with a Russian minister who claimed Russian forces never targeted exclusively civilian sites. The interview was widely described as disgraceful for its handling of the minister's assertions.

stories.title: Iran-linked hackers breach FBI Director Kash Patel’s personal email, publish excerpts online
stories.summary: Iran-linked hacker group Handala Hack Team claimed to have breached FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email account, publishing personal photographs and documents online. The Justice Department confirmed that Patel's email had been compromised.

stories.title: Breonna Taylor shooting: charges dismissed against ex-police officers for falsifying warrant
stories.summary: A US district judge in Louisville dismissed federal charges against former police officers Joshua Jaynes and Kyle Meany, who were accused of falsifying the search warrant used in the 2020 raid that resulted in Breonna Taylor's death.

stories.title: Connecticut officer fired after shooting man in mental health crisis as others tried to de-escalate
stories.summary: Hartford, Connecticut Mayor Arunan Arulampalam fired police Officer Joseph Magnano for fatally shooting Steven Jones, a Black man experiencing a mental health crisis, approximately 30 seconds after arriving on scene where three other officers had been attempting to de-escalate.

stories.title: The German army protecting Western Europe's eastern edge
stories.summary: Germany is working to expand its military role as a leading European defence power, with the German army taking on responsibilities for protecting Western Europe's eastern flank.

stories.title: Oyarzabal double seals Spain win against Serbia in World Cup warm-up
stories.summary: Spain defeated Serbia 3-0 in a warm-up match ahead of the 2026 World Cup, with forward Mikel Oyarzabal scoring twice to secure a comfortable victory.

stories.title: What is the TACO trade and are investors profiting amid war on Iran?
stories.summary: Amid the ongoing conflict with Iran, global energy markets are experiencing heightened volatility. Traders using the so-called 'TACO' strategy are attempting to profit from the widening energy crisis driven by the war.

stories.title: I escaped North Korea with my mum. Now I'm terrified she might be sent back
stories.summary: A North Korean defector named Geumseong, who escaped to South Korea with his mother, fears she may be forcibly repatriated to North Korea after being detained in a Chinese prison.

stories.title: Zelensky explains why no date set for next trilateral meeting
stories.summary: President Zelensky explained that no date has been set for the next trilateral meeting because the US negotiating team can only meet within the United States due to security restrictions, while Russia refuses to negotiate on US soil.

stories.title: Gulf states tell US ending the war is not enough, Iran’s capabilities must be degraded
stories.summary: Gulf state policymakers told the United States that merely ending the war with Iran is insufficient and that Iran's military capabilities must be degraded. The Gulf states expressed concern about what kind of regional order would follow the US-Israel campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Iranian players hold schoolbags in solidarity with slain girls
stories.summary: Iran's men's national soccer team wore black armbands and held schoolbags before a match in Belek, Turkey, on March 27. A team official said the gesture was a protest over the killing of schoolgirls on the first day of the Iran war.

stories.title: Iran says projectile hit near Bushehr nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Iran's Atomic Energy Organisation reported that a projectile struck near the Bushehr nuclear power plant, marking what it described as the third attack by US and Israeli forces on the site. The organisation said there were no casualties or damage and condemned the targeting of peaceful nuclear facilities as a violation of international regulations.

stories.title: Why China’s demand that Japan return an ancient tablet could mark a ‘historical reckoning’
stories.summary: China is demanding that Japan return a 1,300-year-old stone tablet currently housed in Japan's Imperial Palace, positioning the case as part of a broader campaign to reclaim cultural artifacts lost during wartime looting.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis say 'fingers on the trigger' as Iran war widens
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement declared its readiness to intervene militarily should the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran expand, warning that its forces have their 'fingers on the trigger.' The statement raised concerns about the conflict widening across the region.

stories.title: Kuwait says main port damaged in drone attack
stories.summary: Kuwait's Shuwaikh port was struck by enemy drones at dawn, causing material damage but no reported casualties, according to the Kuwait port authority.

stories.title: Rubio says Iran war to last weeks, no US ground troops needed
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington expects its military campaign against Iran to conclude within weeks without ground troops. G7 nations simultaneously adopted a declaration calling for an immediate halt to attacks on civilian populations and infrastructure in Iran.

stories.title: Chinese ships halt attempt to exit Strait of Hormuz despite Iran safe passage assurances
stories.summary: Two Chinese-owned vessels halted their attempt to exit the Strait of Hormuz despite Iran's assurances of safe passage. The ships had broadcast their Chinese ownership and crew details on ship-tracking systems.

stories.title: Water production plant, industrial facility hit in Iran, IAEA says
stories.summary: Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency that a heavy water production plant at Khondab and the Khuzestan steel production factory were struck on Friday. The IAEA reported no radiation risk from either site, noting no declared nuclear material was present and no off-site radiation was released.

stories.title: U.S. weighs sending up to 10,000 troops to West Asia: reports
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering deploying up to 10,000 troops to West Asia. An Iranian official warned that Tehran would respond to a ground invasion by activating Houthi rebels in Yemen to attack Red Sea shipping.

stories.title: Egypt imposes business curfew to counter soaring fuel costs
stories.summary: Egypt imposed a nighttime business curfew starting Saturday, ordering shops, restaurants, and malls to close by 9:00 PM to reduce energy consumption as fuel costs have more than doubled due to the Iran war.

stories.title: Former US soldiers argue Israeli policy is now guiding US interests
stories.summary: Former US military personnel, including ex-CIA briefer Ray McGovern, former Green Beret Anthony Aguilar, and former Army Intelligence Captain Josephine Guilbeau, have argued that Israeli policy is increasingly guiding US foreign policy interests. Veterans across the political spectrum have questioned why Israel remains a favored ally.

stories.title: Lubinets calls for humanitarian corridor to evacuate civilians from Oleshky
stories.summary: Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets called on the International Committee of the Red Cross and Russia to establish a humanitarian corridor for evacuating civilians from Oleshky and surrounding settlements in the Kherson region.

stories.title: FBI director’s personal email, photos and documents leaked by Iran-linked hackers
stories.summary: The Iran-linked hacker group Handala Hack Team breached FBI Director Kash Patel's personal email account, publishing over 300 emails dating from 2010 to 2019 along with personal photographs and documents. Both the hackers and the FBI confirmed the breach.

stories.title: 'My daughter is under the rubble': Inside Tehran as civilian toll of strikes rises
stories.summary: One month after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, residents of Tehran described devastating effects on civilian life. Survivors recounted searching for family members trapped under rubble as the civilian toll from the strikes continued to rise.

stories.title: Why China’s space-based solar power is the next frontier of green energy
stories.summary: China is advancing its Zhuri space-based solar power project amid disruptions to global energy supplies caused by the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Middle East war. Chinese rocket scientist Long Lehao compared the program's scale to placing the Three Gorges Dam into geostationary orbit.

stories.title: Rubio sees G7 building 'coalition' against Iran strait control
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at the G7 that European allies are ready to join a coalition opposing Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative comes amid growing global energy security concerns.

stories.title: 'Shooting gallery': How a US invasion of Iranian islands might unfold
stories.summary: Military analysts are examining how a potential US invasion of Iranian islands might unfold, involving paratroopers and Marines establishing a beachhead. The analysis draws on historical cautionary tales of amphibious and airborne assaults to highlight significant risks.

stories.title: Live from the mamad: Laughter is the best medicine amid war
stories.summary: Comedians in Israel are performing during wartime, with shows occasionally interrupted by air raid sirens. Performers and audiences are using humor as a coping mechanism amid ongoing conflict.

stories.title: How to get by in Dubai: What to do when your cruise is stranded by war
stories.summary: Cruise ship passengers stranded in Dubai due to the regional conflict are navigating challenges in the city, which is largely inaccessible on foot. Reports note that Google Maps often indicates walking between locations is not feasible.

stories.title: Trump provides new aid for farmers and food suppliers amid Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced new federal aid measures for American farmers and food suppliers facing challenges from the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. The package includes federal loan guarantees and updated renewable fuel standards aimed at supporting the agricultural sector during the conflict.

stories.title: Guns in the streets as US, Israel intensify month-long attacks across Iran
stories.summary: A senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps official in Tehran announced on state television that children over the age of 12 are permitted to join armed patrols and checkpoints as US and Israeli attacks on Iran continue into their second month.

stories.title: Rubio says US can achieve Iran objectives without ground troops
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the United States is achieving its war objectives in Iran without deploying ground troops. He said those objectives include destroying Iran's missile and drone capabilities along with their production facilities.

stories.title: Ukraine destroys Russia’s anti-drone radar system in Crimea, confirms damage of Kirishi refinery
stories.summary: Ukraine's military destroyed a Russian anti-drone radar system in occupied Crimea and confirmed damage to the Kirishi oil refinery. The Ukrainian General Staff also reported additional strikes on targets in Crimea and occupied parts of Donetsk Oblast.

stories.title: One killed, several injured in latest Iranian missile attack on central Israel
stories.summary: An Iranian missile attack struck central and southern Israel, killing one person and injuring several others. Medics reported two people lightly wounded in the south from interception fragments. Yemen's Houthi movement threatened to join the conflict.

stories.title: Two Waves of Bombing: New Videos Reveal Further Details About Iran Girls’ School Strike
stories.summary: Bellingcat geolocated and verified two new videos released by Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs showing multiple missiles striking an IRGC compound and an adjacent girls' school in Minab, Iran. The footage reveals that the deadly attack occurred in two distinct waves of bombing.

stories.title: Rubio: U.S.-Iran War Could Last Another 2 to 4 Weeks
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated the war against Iran could last another two to four weeks. The White House said it remains committed to achieving all military objectives despite a lack of NATO support for the campaign.

stories.title: Hamas considers a proposal to disarm in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas is reportedly considering a US-backed proposal to disarm in the Gaza Strip, which could facilitate reconstruction efforts. However, delays and regional tensions continue to threaten the future of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Social media influencer Clavicular arrested in Florida on battery charges
stories.summary: Social media influencer Braden Eric Peters, known online as Clavicular, was arrested in Florida on battery charges. Peters and his girlfriend are suspected of involvement in an attack on a 19-year-old woman, according to the Osceola County Sheriff's Office.

stories.title: US can only confirm about third of Iran’s missile arsenal destroyed, sources say
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies can only confirm that approximately one-third of Iran's missile arsenal has been destroyed, according to sources. Similar uncertainty surrounds the extent of damage to Iran's drone capabilities.

stories.title: Russia Drops Budget Cut Plans as Oil Price Surge Boosts Revenues – Bloomberg
stories.summary: Russia has dropped planned budget cuts after a surge in oil prices boosted state revenues, according to Bloomberg. Sources indicated that the windfall could be channeled into increased spending on the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Donbas in exchange for security guarantees: Rubio denies Zelensky's statements
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected statements by Ukrainian President Zelensky regarding a deal involving security guarantees in exchange for Ukrainian withdrawal from the Donetsk and Luhansk regions.

stories.title: Israel bombs 2 IRGC-linked steel plants, 2 nuclear facilities as Iran vows revenge
stories.summary: Israel struck two IRGC-linked steel plants and two nuclear facilities in Iran, including a yellowcake facility in Yazd and the Arak heavy water reactor. An Israeli security source said damage to the steel plants is expected to cost billions and could paralyze the industry. Iran vowed revenge.

stories.title: Mexico’s navy searches for two missing boats involved in Cuba aid convoy
stories.summary: Mexico's navy is searching for two sailboats that went missing while participating in the Nuestra America Convoy, an aid mission headed to Cuba. Organizers stated the vessels were crewed by experienced sailors equipped with safety gear.

stories.title: Grieving Iranian mother tells UN about children before school attack
stories.summary: An Iranian mother addressed the UN Human Rights Council, describing the last time she saw her children before they were killed in a school attack in Iran.

stories.title: Warsaw just made it legal to fight for Kyiv. It used to carry five years in Polish prison
stories.summary: Poland enacted a law allowing its citizens to serve in Ukraine's military without prior government authorization. President Karol Nawrocki signed the legislation, removing a previous prohibition that carried a penalty of up to five years in prison.

stories.title: IDF's ‘Operation Roaring Matzah’: Keeping Passover, ensuring security for army and country
stories.summary: The IDF launched 'Operation Roaring Matzah' to ensure soldiers can observe Passover while maintaining security operations. Troops expressed readiness to hold Seder celebrations even inside tanks during active duty.

stories.title: UN rights chief urges US to conclude probe into deadly Iran school strike
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights urged Washington to complete its investigation into a fatal strike on a primary school in Iran, raising the issue at a UN Human Rights Council meeting in Geneva on March 27. Several states expressed outrage over the incident.

stories.title: Russian jailed in Britain for attacking woman after Trump’s son alerted police
stories.summary: Matvei Rumiantsev, a Russian national, was sentenced to four years in prison by a British court on March 27 for attacking a woman in London. The incident was reportedly witnessed by Donald Trump's son Barron Trump, who alerted police.

stories.title: Israel launches strikes on nuclear sites as Iran warns of retaliation
stories.summary: Israel conducted airstrikes targeting multiple sites in Iran, including a uranium facility, steel plants, and a heavy water complex. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned the strikes would lead to escalation and potential retaliation.

stories.title: The huge Iranian missile fragments scattered across Israel, West Bank
stories.summary: At least 270 Iranian missile fragments have fallen across the West Bank, with the majority landing near Ramallah. The debris represents large fragments from missiles fired during the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: Europe should link support for Trump on Iran to arms supplies for Ukraine – NATO expert
stories.summary: A NATO expert argued that European allies should condition any support for President Trump's Iran policy on the provision of US weapons to Ukraine. The recommendation aims to prevent Europe from yielding to US pressure without securing reciprocal commitments.

stories.title: Ukraine closes on Mideast deals to help counter Iranian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister announced the country is close to finalizing security agreements with the UAE and Qatar to counter Iranian drone attacks. Speaking in Vaux-de-Cernay, France, on March 27, he also said he saw potential to involve China in peace efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

stories.title: Russians’ trust in Putin hits wartime low as fatigue grows
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin's public approval rating dropped to 70.1 percent, down 1.9 points from the previous week, marking a wartime low. The decline reflects growing fatigue among Russians over the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: War with Iran to end in few weeks — Rubio
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the war with Iran could conclude within a few weeks, offering a public forecast on the expected duration of the conflict.

stories.title: Iranians suffer from internet blackout as well as US-Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Iranian civilians are enduring both US-Israeli airstrikes on Tehran and a government-imposed internet blackout. Residents report that the inability to contact relatives or learn what is happening has made the situation nearly unbearable.

stories.title: How important are the Gulf economies to the world?
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing the economic risks posed by the US-Israeli war on Iran to Gulf economies, warning that the conflict's impact extends beyond the energy sector to broader global economic stability.

stories.title: US special envoy Witkoff says US hopeful of meetings with Iran soon
stories.summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff said at an investment forum in Miami that the United States is hopeful meetings with Iran will take place soon. He stated that a 15-point deal is on the table and the US is awaiting Iran's response.

stories.title: China denies retaliating against Panama ships, accuses Washington of canal grab
stories.summary: China denied retaliating against Panama-flagged vessels after Panama revoked port concessions held by a Hong Kong-based conglomerate at both ends of the Panama Canal. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian accused Washington of seeking to seize control of the strategic waterway and making false allegations about intensified ship inspections.

stories.title: Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen begins coalition talks, hoping to remain prime minister
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen began coalition talks seeking a third term in office after her centrist cabinet suffered a major defeat in the March 24 election. She hopes to remain prime minister despite the electoral setback.

stories.title: Ukraine closes in on Middle East deals to help counter Iranian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine is pursuing military deals with Middle Eastern partners to counter Iranian drones used by Russia. Kyiv is seeking to bolster regional support as the US-Israeli war on Iran raises concerns about potential reductions in American military aid to Ukraine.

stories.title: Long-sought Red Army Faction suspect charged in Germany for 1990s attacks
stories.summary: BERLIN, March 27 - German prosecutors have charged one of the last surviving alleged militants of the Red Army Faction with attempted murder and a string of violent attacks carried out more than three

stories.title: Afghan jailed for 15 years in the UK for raping 12-year-old girl
stories.summary: Ahmad Mulakhil, an Afghan national and asylum seeker, was sentenced to 15 years in a British prison on March 27 for raping a 12-year-old girl. The case sparked local protests and political controversy after police initially did not disclose his asylum-seeker status.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region about 50 times in one day, leaving five injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 50 attacks using drones and artillery on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day. Five people were injured, including a child.

stories.title: Cholera aid for African countries stalled by Iran conflict
stories.summary: GENEVA, March 27 - Emergency cholera medical supplies for several African countries have become stuck in a logistical quagmire caused by the Iran war, aid officials told Reuters, raising concerns abou

stories.title: Israel attacks major industrial and nuclear sites in Iran
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit major industrial and nuclear infrastructure in Iran, including the Arak heavy-water plant. Smoke was observed rising from the facility following the attack.

stories.title: Uruguay considers with “interest” British offer of three Royal Navy offshore patrol vessels
stories.summary: Uruguay's government is considering a British offer to acquire three Royal Navy River-class offshore patrol vessels — HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey, and HMS Severn. The ships have been operational since 2003 and are scheduled for decommissioning in 2028 as part of Britain's fleet renewal under NATO defense spending commitments.

stories.title: ‘I’ll never be the same’: Iranians recount one month of war
stories.summary: Iranians tell about how life has changed and about watching missiles fall.

stories.title: Rubio says US ‘concerned’ by settler attacks, insists Israel will ‘do something’
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed concern over settler attacks in the West Bank, stating Israel would take action. His comments came hours after another Palestinian family was targeted near Hebron, and he recalled Trump's opposition to status quo changes in the territory.

stories.title: Molotov cocktails thrown at Russian cultural centre in Prague
stories.summary: PRAGUE, March 27 - An unknown attacker threw several Molotov cocktails at the building of a Russian cultural centre in Prague on Thursday night and police are searching for the suspect, Czech police s

stories.title: WTO reform talks face US-India wall in Cameroon, diplomats say
stories.summary: WTO reform talks in Cameroon face significant obstacles from both the United States and India, according to diplomats. An African diplomat noted that India has so far shown no signs of changing its negotiating position.

stories.title: Drone reveals extent of Iranian missile damage in Israeli city of Arad
stories.summary: Drone footage captured the extent of damage in the Israeli city of Arad caused by a recent Iranian ballistic missile attack. The images revealed significant destruction across the area days after the strike.

stories.title: Syria: Wives of the missing push for legal reform
stories.summary: In Syria, wives of missing persons are pushing for legal reforms to address decades-old family laws that restrict women's custody, inheritance, and remarriage rights. The issue affects hundreds of thousands of women and children whose cases remain tied to absent male relatives.

stories.title: Tehran accuses US of ‘calculated’ assault on school
stories.summary: Iran said the US' strike on a school was a war crime and a crime against humanity.

stories.title: War in Lebanon 'was imposed upon us', PM Nawaf Salam says
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told FRANCE 24 in Beirut that the Israeli offensive on Lebanon "was imposed upon us." Salam stated Lebanon could have avoided the conflict had Hezbollah not launched rockets in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli assassination of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

stories.title: PM says expanding scope of Roshan Digital Account to strengthen Pakistan as ‘attractive investment destination’
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced plans to expand the Roshan Digital Account scheme to foreign investors, aiming to strengthen Pakistan as an investment destination. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb had first announced the expansion on March 16.

stories.title: US Space Command provides update on phased headquarters relocation to Alabama
stories.summary: U.S. Space Command announced plans to break ground on a new headquarters facility on a roughly 60-acre site near the center of Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama, in 2027. The command provided an update on the phased relocation process.

stories.title: Landslips triggered by heavy rainfall kill at least 20 people in Tanzania
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall triggered landslips in Tanzania, killing at least 20 people. In neighboring Kenya, seasonal flooding has killed at least 88 people and affected 21 counties, with at least two rivers bursting their banks.

stories.title: Smoke rises over Beirut suburbs after massive Israeli airstrike
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck Beirut's southern suburbs, sending smoke rising over the city's skyline. The strikes were part of Israel's ongoing military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Europe should reduce its dependence on US through 'Europeanization' of NATO – expert
stories.summary: A security expert argued that Europe should pursue a comprehensive "Europeanization" of NATO to reduce its dependence on the United States and strengthen its own defense capabilities.

stories.title: 'New phenomenon of dangerous rhetoric': World leaders embrace proud disregard for international law
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch Executive Director Philippe Bolopion described what he called a seismic shift in the conduct of war, noting that world leaders are openly embracing violations of international humanitarian law. He warned of a normalization of dismissing international legal norms and lacking empathy for civilian suffering.

stories.title: Iran: Rolling Ultimatums, Moscow "at the EU table"?
stories.summary: President Trump issued rolling ultimatums threatening to destroy Iran's power plants, initially setting a Monday midnight deadline. The deadline was extended first by five days and then to ten days, with Trump claiming productive conversations and ongoing negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: US expects Iran operation to end in ‘weeks, not months’, says Marco Rubio
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said after meeting G7 foreign ministers in France that Washington expects its military operation against Iran to conclude in weeks, not months. Israel has simultaneously threatened to escalate and expand its attacks against Iran, even as Tehran continues firing missiles at Israel.

stories.title: US-Israeli attack kills two in Firouzabad, Iran
stories.summary: Two people were killed and two others injured when US-Israeli strikes hit a cement factory in Firouzabad, Iran, according to the Iranian Students' News Agency.

stories.title: G7 ministers call for end to attacks on civilians amid war in Middle East – Reuters
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of the G7 nations issued a joint statement following their meeting in France, calling for an immediate halt to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Leading NYC anti-Israel activist targeted in firebombing plot, feds say
stories.summary: Federal authorities charged a suspect with planning a firebombing attack on Nerdeen Kiswani, head of the group Within Our Lifetime, in New York City. The suspect was identified as a member of the extremist Jewish Defense League.

stories.title: US Palestinian activist says FBI foiled assassination plot against her
stories.summary: US law enforcement arrested a man for allegedly plotting a Molotov cocktail attack against Palestinian-American activist Nerdeen Kiswani. The FBI said it foiled the assassination attempt before it could be carried out.

stories.title: Role reversal: Ukraine moves training home and exports the lessons abroad
stories.summary: Ukraine has shifted military training operations back to its own territory after years of Western-led instruction abroad. Ukrainian forces are now exporting battlefield lessons learned during the war to train Western allied militaries.

stories.title: ‘Total chaos’: The Kremlin knows Russians are angry about new Internet restrictions. It’s struggling to respond.
stories.summary: Mobile internet blackouts have spread from Russia's regions to Moscow, and Kremlin polling shows 83% of teenagers reacted negatively to the restrictions. Authorities continue throttling Telegram while pro-government pollsters avoid publishing adult discontent data.

stories.title: Lloyds bank faces £66m court battle with car loan customers
stories.summary: Law firm Courmacs Legal is preparing a £66 million claim against Lloyds Banking Group on behalf of 30,000 car loan customers. The borrowers allege they were financially harmed by contracts arranged through Lloyds' motor finance arm, Black Horse, and fear the Financial Conduct Authority's official redress scheme will favor lenders.

stories.title: Canada’s Bill C-12 an ‘attack on refugee, migrant rights’: Advocates
stories.summary: Canadian rights groups are criticizing Bill C-12, a new law restricting asylum access. Advocates say the legislation threatens refugee and migrant rights and could expose thousands of people to persecution, violence, and precarity.

stories.title: A look at the giant Iranian missile hulls scattered across Israel and the West Bank
stories.summary: Large fragments of intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles have been found scattered across Israel and the West Bank. The debris, meters long and potentially toxic, has landed in residential areas affecting both Israeli and Palestinian communities.

stories.title: 1 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strike on Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a vehicle in the border village of Malomikhaylovka in Russia's Belgorod region, killing the driver. Regional Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov confirmed the fatality.

stories.title: Iran Guards warn civilians after Trump pushes Hormuz deadline
stories.summary: The Guards warned civilians in the Middle East to stay away from areas near US bases.

stories.title: Sybiha: South Korea's technology and experience open new opportunities for Ukraine's recovery
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha highlighted South Korea's expertise in technology, infrastructure, and post-war development as offering significant potential for joint projects in Ukraine's recovery and reconstruction.

stories.title: Diaspora Jews targeted over a dozen times in March, as Iran war fuels tensions
stories.summary: Jewish communities in the diaspora were targeted in over a dozen incidents during March, including shootings, bombings, arson, and a car-ramming. The increase in attacks is apparently linked to rising tensions from the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Russian Government Aims to Reopen Black Sea Beaches by June After Oil Spill Cleanup
stories.summary: Russian authorities aim to reopen Black Sea beaches near the resort city of Anapa in Krasnodar region by June. Swimming has been banned since thousands of metric tons of heavy fuel oil washed ashore in December 2024.

stories.title: Donbas-for-peace offer raises fears of more war, nuclear spread
stories.summary: A proposed peace deal involving Ukraine's withdrawal from the Donbas region in exchange for U.S. security guarantees has raised alarms among critics. Opponents warn the arrangement could reward Russian aggression and incentivize nuclear proliferation by other states.

stories.title: Iran's response to US peace proposal expected Friday, source says
stories.summary: Iran is expected to deliver a counter-proposal to a US peace plan on Friday, according to a Reuters source. US President Trump and senior White House officials were informed of the timeline through intermediaries.

stories.title: Norway floats additional $11.8B in defense spending through 2035, cancels drone program
stories.summary: Norway announced an additional $11.8 billion in defense spending through 2035, earmarked for F-35 fighter jet munitions including AARGM-ER missiles, as well as submarine and frigate procurement. The government simultaneously canceled a drone acquisition program.

stories.title: Rubio: US expects Iran war to end in ‘weeks, not months’
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States expects its military operation in Iran to conclude within weeks rather than months.

stories.title: Israel strikes Iranian nuclear development facilities, Tehran vows retaliation
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck Iranian nuclear development facilities, including a heavy-water reactor near Arak, after the IDF called on nearby residents to evacuate. Tehran vowed retaliation for the attacks on its nuclear infrastructure.

stories.title: ‘I’m not shocked’: Palestinian activist’s home targeted in foiled firebombing plot
stories.summary: Palestinian-American activist Nerdeen Kiswani, founder of Within Our Lifetime, was the target of a foiled firebombing plot against her home. Kiswani said she was informed her life was in danger and described how such incidents deeply affected her.

stories.title: Ukraine offers Gulf allies drone defense in bid for scarce Patriot missiles
stories.summary: Ukraine is offering Gulf allies its expertise in drone defense systems in exchange for scarce Patriot missile batteries. Kyiv seeks to leverage its large-scale drone warfare experience to secure air defense systems it cannot manufacture domestically.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky offers air defence for Gulf funds in Saudi Arabia deal
stories.summary: Ukraine is leveraging its anti-drone warfare expertise to attract foreign support and funding.

stories.title: Lithuania expresses protest with Russia over strikes on Ukraine, including attacks on central Lviv
stories.summary: Lithuania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally protested to Russia over new strikes on Ukrainian territory, including attacks that damaged a UNESCO World Heritage site in central Lviv.

stories.title: In tense call, Vance knocked PM for overselling Iran regime change likelihood — report
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance reportedly had a tense call with Israel's prime minister, criticizing him for overselling the likelihood of regime change in Iran. US officials suspected an Israeli effort to influence Vance, who is set to lead ceasefire talks with Iran.

stories.title: The Iran War’s Economic Winners and Losers
stories.summary: Analysts are examining the economic consequences of the war in the Persian Gulf, assessing which countries and sectors stand to gain or lose from the conflict. Questions have been raised about whether the Gulf region's longstanding economic model is now in jeopardy.

stories.title: War Diary Day 28: Pressure builds as pause on strikes on Iran extended
stories.summary: On day 28 of the U.S.-Israel war against Iran, President Trump extended a pause on strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure until April 6. Tehran rejected the move as psychological signaling, denying that any diplomatic request had been made, while Washington framed it as a response to ongoing talks.

stories.title: Huge Iranian missile fragments, intercepted by air defenses, lay scattered across Israel, West Bank
stories.summary: Large fragments of Iranian missiles intercepted by air defenses have been found scattered across Israel and the occupied West Bank. Iran has launched hundreds of missiles since the war began, with debris measuring four to five meters landing in areas including school playgrounds.

stories.title: France rebukes Lavrov, says Russia does not defend international law
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Russia of flouting international law in both Ukraine and Iran on Friday. The rebuke came in response to remarks made by Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov during a French television interview defending Moscow's positions.

stories.title: War between Hezbollah and Israel deepens fractures in Lebanon
stories.summary: The conflict is pushing Lebanon’s fragile state and society towards breaking point.

stories.title: Gulf states tell US ending the war is not enough, Iran’s capabilities must be degraded - analysis
stories.summary: Gulf states have communicated to the United States that simply ending the war in Iran is insufficient and that Iran's military capabilities must be significantly degraded. Regional policymakers are focused on what kind of security order will emerge after the conflict.

stories.title: War update: 66 combat clashes on front line since morning, fighting continues in six sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 66 combat clashes along the front line since morning, with the heaviest Russian activity concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors. Fighting was ongoing across six fronts.

stories.title: At least thirteen killed in US-Israeli attacks on residential areas in Iran's Kermanshah
