stories.summary: Oil prices rose while stock markets showed mixed results as investors expressed concern over the trajectory of the U.S.-Iran war. Market uncertainty was driven by inconsistent White House messaging, with President Trump alternating between threats and peace rhetoric.

stories.title: Spanish woman who died through euthanasia failed by state, say critics
stories.summary: Noelia Castillo, a Spanish woman, died by euthanasia on Thursday evening at a Barcelona hospital following a prolonged legal battle with her father. Critics say the state failed her throughout the process.

stories.title: Nigeria: Army Intensifies Offensives, Records Gains Against Iswap, Boko Haram in Northast
stories.summary: The Nigerian Army, under Operation Hadin Kai, has intensified offensives against ISWAP and Boko Haram in the North-East. The military reported major gains targeting key leaders and insurgent strongholds.

stories.title: Rubio, G7 diplomats duel over wars in Iran and Ukraine
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clashed with G7 counterparts over the wars in Iran and Ukraine at a gathering outside Paris. Rubio criticized European allies for not supporting US military efforts in the Gulf, while European nations rebuffed President Trump's request for military assistance in the region.

stories.title: Africa: Can the Iran War Shift the Dial On Climate Action?
stories.summary: An analysis from the Institute for Security Studies examines how the Iran war's impact on Africa could be profound, while suggesting that lessons from the conflict might accelerate the continent's energy transition.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Escalating Violence and Influx of Returnees in DR Congo Fuel Regional Instability
stories.summary: The humanitarian crisis in the Democratic Republic of Congo has worsened following the reopening of the Burundi-DRC border, with returning Congolese refugees facing overcrowded conditions. Escalating clashes between AFC, M23 rebels, and government-affiliated forces, including drone strikes, are fueling regional instability.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: See Shabbat times for your area.

stories.title: Opinion: Iran's way of warfare is being tested to its limits
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Iran's layered warfare strategy of forward defense through allied non-state partners and long-range missiles is being tested under current hostilities. The piece notes that Iranian military commander Hossein Salami, who had vowed overwhelming defensive power, was killed in an Israeli air strike.

stories.title: Africa: Africa Is Forging Its Own Green Future
stories.summary: African institutions are developing their own frameworks for a green energy transition, aiming to advance both economic development and climate resilience. The push comes despite long-standing shortfalls in international climate financing for the continent.

stories.title: Latin American Countries Boost Ties to Africa
stories.summary: Latin American countries are strengthening ties with African nations in a new era of south-south cooperation. The article questions whether these partnerships can outlast the current leftist leadership in the region.

stories.title: China’s economy big enough to absorb Iran war shocks, says Justin Lin
stories.summary: Economist Justin Lin Yifu, dean of Peking University's Institute of New Structural Economics, stated that China's economy has sufficient capacity to absorb shocks from the Iran war and still meet its growth targets. He also noted China is preparing for the possibility that Washington might renege on trade deals.

stories.title: The end of ‘win-lose’? China-backed mediation body makes pitch at Boao Forum
stories.summary: Teresa Cheng Yeuk-wah, secretary general of the newly launched International Organisation for Mediation, promoted the China-backed body at the Boao Forum for Asia. She described mediation as a flexible alternative to arbitration and litigation for resolving commercial and state-level disputes involving long-term investment.

stories.title: Protection against Iranian attacks: Zelensky meets with Ukrainian military experts in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Ukrainian military experts currently in Saudi Arabia to discuss key requirements for strengthening air defense in the region.

stories.title: West Africa: Ecowas Marks 50 Years With Academic Quiz Competition for Liberian Students
stories.summary: ECOWAS marked its 50th anniversary by hosting an academic quiz competition for senior high school students in Kakata, Liberia. The event aimed to promote regional awareness and academic excellence among West African youth.

stories.title: Nigeria: Sanwo-Olu Inaugurates Irele Tower By Lagos Free Zone
stories.summary: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu inaugurated Irele Tower, the first commercial building within the Lagos Free Zone. He described the project as a milestone in the development of the Lekki economic corridor in Nigeria.

stories.title: Nigeria: LCCI - Bank Recapitalisation'll Improve Access to Credit, Make Lending Conditions Competitive
stories.summary: Nigeria's Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry said the ongoing bank recapitalization exercise, with its deadline days away, should improve access to credit. Private sector operators and MSMEs hope the increased capital requirements will lead to more affordable lending rates.

stories.title: Nigeria: Customs Officers' Wives Promote Environmental Sustainability At Lagos Port
stories.summary: The Customs Officers' Wives Association organized an environmental awareness campaign at the PTML chapter in Lagos port, Nigeria. The initiative aimed to sensitize members, officers, and stakeholders about environmental sustainability.

stories.title: China says talks would help restore Hormuz transit, supports Pakistan as mediator

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Poultry Farmers Kick Against Proposed $900m China Partnership
stories.summary: Nigerian poultry farmers voiced strong opposition to a proposed $900 million investment deal between the federal government and China, warning it could harm the domestic poultry industry if not carefully managed.

stories.title: War on Iran sparks global fertilizer shortage, threatens food prices
stories.summary: The war has almost halted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow passage off Iran that handles about a fifth of the world's oil and nearly a third of global fertilizer trade

stories.title: Nigeria: APC Suspends Dagogo Over Alleged Anti-Party Activities
stories.summary: Nigeria's All Progressives Congress (APC) suspended party chieftain Fubara Dagogo over allegations of gross misconduct and anti-party activities.

stories.title: West Africa: BRVM Awards 2026: AllAfrica Global Media Once Again Nominated for "Financial Media of the Year"
stories.summary: [allAfrica] The Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières (BRVM) has officially announced the nominees for the seventh edition of the BRVM Awards. For the third consecutive year, AllAfrica Glo

stories.title: Mass cancellations as Arkia changes course, says long-haul flights to depart from Israel, not Jordan
stories.summary: Israeli airline Arkia reversed its decision to operate long-haul flights from Jordan and Egypt, announcing that flights to New York, Bangkok, and Hanoi would depart from Israel instead. The change triggered mass cancellations, as flights from Israel are capped at 50 passengers each.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Army Probes Alleged Extrajudicial Killing in Maiduguri
stories.summary: [Premium Times] Social media posts alleged that Mr Mustapha, also known as Abchin, was unarmed and returning from a Sallah visit when he was killed.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Arrest Suspects in Benue, Recover Ak-47 Rifle, Ammunition
stories.summary: Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke conducted clearance operations in Benue state, Nigeria, against criminal elements targeting farmers in the North Central zone. Several suspects were arrested and one AK-47 rifle with ammunition was recovered.

stories.title: Fighting in Iran: Is another 1970s‑style oil crisis looming?
stories.summary: The ongoing war in the Middle East has raised concerns about potential oil supply disruptions reminiscent of the 1970s energy crises. Topics spanned the Strait of Hormuz uncertainty and various issues across Hong Kong, mainland China, and broader Asia.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Violence Intensifies As UN Mission Pledges Continued Support
stories.summary: A senior UN official told the Security Council that the security and political situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains extremely tense. The UN mission pledged continued support as violence intensifies in the DRC.

stories.title: Five more children returned from temporarily occupied Kherson region
stories.summary: Five more children have been returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory from the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region. Four of the five children are without parental care.

stories.title: As Philippines battles fuel crisis, will Marcos postpone Asean summit?
stories.summary: Philippine lawmakers urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to postpone the 2025 ASEAN summit as the country struggles with soaring fuel prices amid the global energy crisis. Analysts cautioned that postponement could undermine Manila's chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

stories.title: Malaysia’s ships allowed to pass Strait of Hormuz, PM Anwar says
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Iran has granted clearance for Malaysian oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The Malaysian government is also introducing domestic fuel conservation measures.

stories.title: First responders rescue man from Tehran building hit by air strike
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent Society released footage showing first responders in Tehran rescuing a man trapped in a building damaged by an air strike.

stories.title: Trump says he was told Mojtaba Khamenei may be gay, spotlighting Iran’s brutal anti-gay persecution
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly claimed he was told that Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's supreme leader, may be gay. Same-sex relations are criminalized in Iran and can carry the death penalty under the Islamic regime's systematic persecution of LGBTQ+ individuals.

stories.title: US considers sending additional 10,000 ground troops to Middle East amid Iran talks - report
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly considering deploying an additional 10,000 ground troops to the Middle East during ongoing Iran talks. The force would likely include infantry and armored vehicles, supplementing the 82nd Airborne Division already in the region, according to the Wall Street Journal.

stories.title: Palestinians flee tear gas as Israeli settlers arrive in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: The Israeli army fired tear gas at Palestinian residents of Beit Imrin village in the occupied West Bank as Israeli settlers arrived in the area.

stories.title: Envoy to Britain warns against cancelling king’s US visit
stories.summary: A diplomatic envoy to Britain has warned against cancelling the king's planned visit to the United States. Buckingham Palace has not yet officially confirmed the trip.

stories.title: Hong Kong home prices surge to near 2-year high, but Iran war clouds outlook
stories.summary: Hong Kong's second-hand home prices rose 1.6 percent in February, marking 11 consecutive months of growth and pushing the official index to a 22-month high. Since reversing a downward trend in April, prices have climbed nearly 8 percent, though the ongoing Iran conflict clouds the market outlook.

stories.title: A way out for the US and Iran? The diplomatic path that could prove China right
stories.summary: Chinese Middle East expert Niu Xinchun of Ningxia University suggested nuclear containment and regional ceasefires as the most viable starting points for U.S.-Iran negotiations. He argued the escalating conflict has validated China's longstanding insistence on diplomatic and political solutions to the crisis.

stories.title: Albanese government says fuel supply ‘same, if not higher’ in coming weeks as Coalition calls for halving of excise
stories.summary: The Australian government sought to reassure the public that fuel supply levels would remain normal or increase in coming weeks amid rising prices. The ACCC reported diesel and unleaded petrol prices rose roughly 10% and 8% respectively across Australia's five largest cities. The Coalition called for the fuel excise to be halved.

stories.title: Iran bars its sports teams from traveling to ‘hostile’ countries
stories.summary: Iran announced a ban on its sports teams traveling to countries deemed "hostile," citing security concerns. The decision affects an upcoming club soccer match in Saudi Arabia and prompted efforts to relocate Iran's World Cup matches from the U.S. to Mexico.

stories.title: Australia will be left with no submarines if it abandons Aukus, senior defence official warns
stories.summary: A senior Australian defence official warned that Australia would have no submarines if it abandons the Aukus partnership with the US and UK. The official declined to outline an alternative plan if the promised Virginia-class and Aukus-class nuclear-powered submarines do not arrive under Australian command.

stories.title: Red Crescent video shows aftermath of strike on homes in Iran’s Urmia
stories.summary: The Iranian Red Crescent released video showing damage to a residential area in Urmia, the capital of West Azerbaijan province, following a strike.

stories.title: Albanese says Australia playing “constructive” role in the war on Iran
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that his government has played a "constructive" role in the war on Iran, though he did not specify the nature of Australia's contribution.

stories.title: Ukraine says ‘no indication’ US weapons to be diverted to Middle East
stories.summary: Ukraine stated there is no indication that US-supplied weapons will be diverted to the Middle East. The PURL programme enables Ukraine to receive US military equipment financed by European countries.

stories.title: Google’s Gemini AI app debuts in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Google launched its Gemini AI chatbot mobile app in Hong Kong, where it quickly topped Apple's app store chart. The rollout followed Google's announcement of a gradual introduction of generative AI services to the city, beginning with web-based access before the mobile version.

stories.title: Cheap and elusive, drones put incessant pressure on Israel’s evolving air defenses
stories.summary: Iran and Hezbollah are deploying waves of low-cost drones that challenge Israel's air defenses. Israel is responding with layered defense systems and emerging technologies, drawing on lessons from Ukraine's experience with drone warfare.

stories.title: Wild autumn weather delivers snow, storms and power cuts to eastern Australia
stories.summary: Severe autumn storms struck eastern Australia on Thursday night, leaving thousands without power across multiple states and delivering the first major snowfall of 2026 to highland areas. Tropical Cyclone Narelle was also expected to make landfall near Perth, bringing potential flash flooding to Western Australia.

stories.title: At least six killed in Iran's Qom, as Tehran announces hits across region
stories.summary: A U.S.-Israeli strike on a residential area in Qom, Iran, killed at least six people, with the number of wounded still unknown. The Red Crescent said rescue operations continue in both Tehran and Qom to find people trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Who is Hasan Piker, the US left-wing streamer critics say the Democrats should reject?
stories.summary: U.S. left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has drawn scrutiny as Democratic politicians appear on his show. Critics accuse him of antisemitism and warn that engagement with him risks centering bigotry within the party.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to sell defense systems in surplus to partners – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to sell surplus defense systems to partner nations. The Ukrainian defense industry is currently operating at half capacity due to insufficient funding, and proceeds would help increase domestic drone production.

stories.title: Hong Kong slams UK for undermining city’s rule of law with calls to release Jimmy Lai
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government condemned the United Kingdom for undermining the city's rule of law after British authorities pledged to press for the release of Jimmy Lai, the former media executive sentenced to 20 years for national security offences. Hong Kong dismissed London's comments as misleading and irresponsible.

stories.title: Over 1,000 Diaspora leaders urge action against ‘Jewish-extremist terror in West Bank’
stories.summary: Over 1,000 Diaspora Jewish leaders sent a letter to Israeli President Herzog condemning settler violence in the West Bank as morally and strategically damaging. They called on the president to intervene given the government's lack of action.

stories.title: Iran recruiting teenagers for Tehran checkpoints amid war
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly recruiting children as young as 12 to staff checkpoints in Tehran amid the ongoing war. The minors are being tasked with collecting security data and conducting operational patrols.

stories.title: Hezbollah attacks Israeli forces attempting to advance into southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced multiple attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, including detonating explosive devices and launching missiles, claiming confirmed casualties. The assaults came as Israel attempted to advance deeper into Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Two aid boats go missing en route to Cuba, says Mexico
stories.summary: Two humanitarian aid boats carrying nine people went missing after departing Mexico bound for Havana, Cuba. The Mexican navy has launched a search and rescue operation.

stories.title: Middle East live: Iran launches strikes on Israel and Gulf sites
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced they carried out missile and drone strikes against targets in Israel and US-linked military facilities across the Gulf on Thursday. Strikes reportedly hit sites in the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain, including a Patriot air-defence maintenance facility.

stories.title: Russia says Britain's decision to detain its vessels is hostile, vows response
stories.summary: Russia's embassy in the United Kingdom called Britain's plan to detain Russian vessels a hostile act, as reported by the TASS news agency. Moscow vowed to respond with political, legal, and asymmetric measures against the decision.

stories.title: Belarus leader gifts rifle to North Korea's Kim as they sign friendship treaty
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko visited Pyongyang and gifted a rifle to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as the two signed a friendship treaty. Both leaders are key supporters of Russia's war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Two Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon combat, military says
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that two of its soldiers were killed during combat operations in southern Lebanon on Thursday. The clashes occurred amid ongoing fighting with Hezbollah along the Israeli-Lebanese border.

stories.title: Trump suggests that Iran let ten oil tankers through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump suggested during a White House Cabinet meeting that Iran allow ten oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing blockade.

stories.title: As haze returns to Singapore, is crisis ‘quietly accepted’ by Asean as inevitable?
stories.summary: Recurring transboundary haze has returned to Singapore, with residents reporting worsening air quality during evening hours. The article examines whether ASEAN member states have quietly accepted the annual haze crisis—driven largely by land-clearing fires in the region—as an inevitable occurrence.

stories.title: China’s top chip foundry SMIC unveils action plan for seizing new growth opportunities
stories.summary: China's largest contract chipmaker, SMIC, released an action plan alongside its 2025 annual report aimed at enhancing existing operations and pursuing new growth opportunities through 2026. The strategy focuses on optimizing current capabilities while supporting China's semiconductor self-sufficiency drive.

stories.title: Iran’s harder-to-hunt long-range missiles are taking greater toll
stories.summary: Despite nearly four weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes that have significantly degraded Iran's military capability, Tehran continues to deploy long-range missiles from hard-to-reach bases in eastern Iran. Recent strikes against Israel, likely involving Khorramshahr missiles, hit targets near Dimona's nuclear research facility and injured over 100 people.

stories.title: Ukraine using strikes to pressure Russia after oil sanctions eased, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is using strikes to pressure Russia after the US issued a 30-day waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products.

stories.title: Mexico launches search for two missing aid boats bound for Cuba
stories.summary: Mexico's navy launched a search operation after two boats carrying humanitarian aid to Cuba went missing en route from Mexican waters.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent who attempted to cut off power to Kropyvnytskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) counterintelligence officers detained a Russian FSB agent in Kropyvnytskyi. The agent was allegedly attempting to sabotage power supply infrastructure in the central Ukrainian city.

stories.title: US judge temporarily halts Trump-era sanctions on AI firm Anthropic
stories.summary: A US federal judge temporarily blocked Trump administration sanctions imposed on AI company Anthropic, finding the measures likely violated the law. The ruling freezes a Pentagon designation of the firm as a national security risk while the government considers an emergency appeal.

stories.title: War Diary Day 27: Multifront escalation in US-Israeli war on Iran appears imminent
stories.summary: On day 27 of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, strikes intensified inside Iran with multiple explosions reported across Tehran and Khorramabad. Air defence systems were activated in the capital, and the conflict showed no signs of de-escalation as President Trump's five-day pause expired.

stories.title: Iran launches assault on US-Israeli infrastructure
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced it carried out missile and drone attacks targeting Israeli and U.S. military bases across the Middle East region.

stories.title: Two humanitarian aid boats heading to Cuba have gone missing, Mexico says
stories.summary: Mexico's navy launched a Caribbean search-and-rescue operation for two sailboats carrying humanitarian aid to Cuba with nine crew members of various nationalities. The boats departed Isla Mujeres in Quintana Roo last week bound for Havana but failed to arrive or make contact as scheduled.

stories.title: Who is fighting in Myanmar’s multi-front civil war?
stories.summary: Myanmar's civil war involves multiple factions including the ruling military regime, various ethnic armed organizations, and pro-democracy forces, with alliances among the groups frequently shifting.

stories.title: Iran forbids sports teams from traveling to 'hostile' countries
stories.summary: Iran announced that its sports teams will not travel to countries unable to guarantee Iranian athletes' safety amid ongoing hostilities, effectively banning travel to nations deemed hostile.

stories.title: North Korea and Belarus sign friendship treaty on Lukashenko’s first visit
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko signed a friendship and cooperation treaty during Lukashenko's first visit to Pyongyang. Both nations face Western sanctions and support Russia's war in Ukraine, with approximately 2,000 North Korean soldiers reportedly killed in the conflict.

stories.title: Iran says it is receptive to any request from Spain, alluding to Hormuz transit
stories.summary: Iran signaled it is open to requests from Spain regarding transit through the Strait of Hormuz. This marks the first such concession Tehran has offered to a European Union member state.

stories.title: Japanese combat troops to return to Philippines in ‘significant’ Indo-Pacific defence shift
stories.summary: Approximately 1,000 Japanese armed combat troops will deploy to the Philippines next month for joint Balikatan military exercises alongside U.S. forces, marking the first time Japanese combat troops have been on Philippine soil in 81 years since World War II. Experts describe the move as a significant shift in Indo-Pacific security architecture toward overlapping multilateral arrangements.

stories.title: Analysts say Trump doesn’t understand Iran reality has changed
stories.summary: Analysts Ross Harrison and Hassan Ahmadian discussed U.S. strategy regarding Iran, arguing that President Trump fails to recognize how conditions inside Iran have changed.

stories.title: China’s airlines add 2,900 flights to Europe as Russia access pays dividends
stories.summary: Chinese airlines are adding nearly 2,900 more China-Europe flights to summer schedules compared to last year, benefiting from access to Russian airspace that allows shorter, more fuel-efficient routes. Western carriers face detours around the Middle East conflict zone, giving Chinese airlines a growing competitive advantage on Europe-bound routes.

stories.title: Swastika found scratched into window of Jewish bagel shop in Sydney
stories.summary: A swastika was found scratched into the window of Lox in a Box, a Jewish bagel shop on Oxford Street in Paddington, Sydney, weeks before its planned opening. New South Wales police are investigating the incident as malicious damage, amid a string of reported antisemitic acts since the October 2023 Hamas attack and Israel's war in Gaza.

stories.title: ‘National security threat’: Pro-Israel US Democrats condemn West Bank settler violence
stories.summary: Pro-Israel U.S. Democratic lawmakers, including Representative Ritchie Torres, publicly condemned Israeli settler violence in the West Bank, calling it a national security threat that is undermining Israel's standing in the United States.

stories.title: US-Israeli attacks target residential buildings in Iran
stories.summary: U.S.-Israeli strikes completely destroyed four residential buildings in Urmia, the capital of Iran's West Azerbaijan province. The provincial crisis management director confirmed the attacks killed and injured a number of civilians.

stories.title: Trump says Iran’s ‘present’ to US was allowing 10 oil tankers through Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump characterized Iran's decision to allow 10 oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz as a "present" to the United States. Trump continues to press Tehran to agree to a broader deal to fully reopen the maritime chokepoint.

stories.title: Mexico’s navy searches for 2 Cuba-bound aid boats that are missing
stories.summary: Mexico's navy launched a search-and-rescue operation for two boats transporting humanitarian aid to Cuba that departed Isla Mujeres in Quintana Roo last Friday. The vessels, carrying nine crew members of various nationalities, were expected to arrive in Havana by midweek but no communication or arrival confirmation was received.

stories.title: Ukraine deploys unified drone command system in just two months – Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukraine deployed a unified digital drone command system called Mission Control within the DELTA ecosystem in two months, according to official Mykhailo Fedorov. The system is now operational across all corps and troop groupings, enabling faster battlefield decision-making.

stories.title: What my madcap journey across the Middle East and to NYC taught me about the war
stories.summary: A traveler recounts a complicated journey from Tel Aviv through Amman and Abu Dhabi to New York after flight cancellations caused by the Middle East war, illustrating the conflict's disruption to civilian travel across the region.

stories.title: What ancient Chinese wisdom can offer a divided world – and the US
stories.summary: The article discusses how ancient Chinese philosophical traditions might offer insights for navigating current global divisions, including U.S.-China tensions. It notes uncertainty over the timing of a summit between President Xi Jinping and President Trump amid cascading international crises including wars and economic instability.

stories.title: Beyond oil: The crucial exports blocked by Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The price of a wide range of goods - from food, to smartphones, to medicines - could be affected by the US-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: Reports of explosions in Tehran, as Israeli army announces attacks on Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it completed a large-scale wave of attacks in Iran after explosions were reported in central and eastern Tehran.

stories.title: Zamir said to warn cabinet that IDF will ‘collapse in on itself’ amid manpower shortage
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir reportedly warned the Israeli cabinet that the military risks collapsing due to manpower shortages. He called for laws to enlist ultra-Orthodox men and extend military service, while the Central Command head said West Bank policies are further straining forces.

stories.title: Hungary government accuses journalist of spying for Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungarian authorities launched an investigation accusing a journalist of spying for Ukraine during an increasingly contentious election campaign. The journalist has dismissed the espionage allegations.

stories.title: At CPAC, Republicans close ranks behind Trump on Iran war
stories.summary: At the Conservative Political Action Conference in Texas, Republican supporters rallied behind President Trump and expressed support for the U.S. military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: UK police to reopen Andrew Tate rape probe
stories.summary: Hertfordshire Constabulary in the UK announced it would reopen an investigation into rape and sexual assault allegations made against influencer Andrew Tate by multiple women between 2014 and 2015. The British-American citizen, who promotes controversial views to millions of social media followers, faces multiple investigations across jurisdictions.

stories.title: Chinese woman uses teeth to carve intricate sculptures, including Great Wall of China model
stories.summary: Chen Qin, a 25-year-old woman from China's Hubei province, has gained over one million online followers for creating intricate sculptures using only her teeth. Her works range from small animal carvings to large replicas of the Great Wall and the Yellow Crane Tower, all crafted from carrots.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister defends Hormuz Strait curb
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres that blocking vessels in the Strait of Hormuz is Iran's legal right as a coastal state. Araghchi attributed the waterway's insecurity to U.S. and Israeli aggression.

stories.title: Israel targets Beirut's southern suburbs
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit Beirut's southern suburbs early Friday, with AFP correspondents reporting several explosions. Security sources told Reuters that three missiles targeted a building in the area.

stories.title: Report: Trump deliberates sending 10,000 more ground troops to Middle East
stories.summary: The Pentagon is deliberating sending up to 10,000 additional ground troops to the Middle East, according to the Wall Street Journal. The deployment would give President Trump more military options while he weighs peace talks with Iran.

stories.title: Should Hong Kong be using ‘war chest’ firepower for Northern Metropolis?
stories.summary: The article examines whether Hong Kong should deploy its substantial fiscal reserves to fund the Northern Metropolis development project. It draws parallels to the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when the Hong Kong Monetary Authority used its reserves to defend the currency against speculators.

stories.title: UAE, Kuwait responding to attacks
stories.summary: Kuwait's army said it shot down two drones in secured areas, while Sharjah in the UAE reported that its air defense systems were responding to a missile threat.

stories.title: ‘Accountability has arrived’: dual US court losses show shifting tide against Meta and co
stories.summary: Juries in California and New Mexico delivered back-to-back verdicts finding Meta liable for harm its products caused to young people, marking the first such trial defeats for the company. The rulings represent an escalation in legal accountability for social media firms over child safety concerns.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli army gathering in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it targeted Israeli soldiers and vehicles with missiles for a second time in Khallat al-Ain, located in the southern Lebanese municipality of Qantara.

stories.title: US judge questions block on Maduro’s use of Venezuelan funds for defence
stories.summary: A US federal judge in Manhattan questioned whether blocking Venezuelan government funds for Nicolás Maduro's legal defense violates his constitutional rights but did not dismiss drug-trafficking charges against him. Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, captured in a US raid on Caracas, appeared in court in prison garb and have pleaded not guilty.

stories.title: Israel war on Iran fought 'without strategy', opposition leader says
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid criticized the government for fighting a multi-front war "without strategy" and with insufficient troops. Lapid, head of the Yesh Atid party, warned that the government could not claim ignorance of the situation.

stories.title: Projectile from Lebanon kills at least one in north Israel
stories.summary: A projectile launched from Lebanon struck northern Israel, killing at least one person. Video from the scene showed flames and black smoke at the impact site.

stories.title: US said weighing deployment of another 10,000 ground troops to Mideast; IDF strikes in Tehran
stories.summary: The U.S. is reportedly weighing deployment of 10,000 additional ground troops to the Middle East as the Israeli military conducted extensive strikes on targets in Tehran. Separately, a senior Hamas official criticized a peace envoy for linking reconstruction to disarmament.

stories.title: Japan’s cherry blossom parties could wilt as inflation strains wallets
stories.summary: Japan's traditional cherry blossom viewing season faces dampened enthusiasm due to persistent inflation, economic fallout from the Iran conflict, and unsettled weather forecasts. A survey by Intage found that 38 percent of Japanese planned to attend hanami events, reflecting muted excitement compared to previous years.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump delays attacks on Iranian energy sector by 10 days
stories.summary: Iran's military launched missiles and drones targeting Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan. President Trump announced a 10-day pause on planned strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure, saying Iran has a "chance to make a deal."

stories.title: How Pakistan positioned itself at the centre of global crisis management
stories.summary: Pakistan has positioned itself as a diplomatic mediator in the Middle East conflict, leveraging its nuclear-armed status despite its own economic and security challenges along the Afghan border.

stories.title: Iran war complicates WHO's emergency medical supply routes
stories.summary: The World Health Organization is rerouting emergency medical supply deliveries from its Dubai hub due to the ongoing Iran war, using longer overland journeys to reach crisis zones such as Lebanon. Rising fuel costs threaten to further hamper shipments if the conflict continues.

stories.title: Trump says he’ll sign order to pay TSA during shutdown
stories.summary: President Trump announced he would sign an executive order to pay Transportation Security Administration officers during a partial government shutdown caused by a congressional deadlock. The move aims to alleviate disruptions at U.S. airports as lawmakers remain unable to agree on ending the shutdown.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky arrives in Saudi Arabia for ‘important meetings’
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Saudi Arabia for what he described as important meetings. Kyiv is offering its air-defense expertise to countries in the region amid ongoing drone strikes by Iran.

stories.title: In meeting with MQM-P delegation, PM Shehbaz lauds services of ex-Sindh governor Kamran Tessori
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met an MQM-P delegation in Karachi and praised former Sindh Governor Kamran Tessori, who was recently replaced by PML-N's Nehal Hashmi. Both Tessori and Hashmi attended the meeting, during which Pakistan's political situation and regional diplomatic efforts were also discussed.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in Balakliia house after enemy attack, one injured
stories.summary: A fire erupted in a private home in Balakliia, Ukraine, following an enemy drone attack, injuring one person.

stories.title: ‘Return hubs’ for migrants clear EU Parliament hurdle
stories.summary: The European Parliament advanced proposals to establish offshore "return hubs" for migrants who have been refused asylum. The vote reflects growing pressure across the 27-nation EU bloc to curb migration.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed, 4 wounded in southern Lebanon by Hezbollah anti-tank missile
stories.summary: Sergeant Aviaad Elchanan Volansky was killed and four other Israeli soldiers were wounded in southern Lebanon by a Hezbollah anti-tank missile. He is the fourth IDF soldier killed in the current Lebanon operation. Lebanon plans to appeal to the UN Security Council over Israeli attacks.

stories.title: United Airlines jet has close call with US Army helicopter, prompting investigation
stories.summary: The FAA is investigating a close call between a United Airlines Boeing 737-800 and a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter near John Wayne Airport in Orange County, California on Tuesday evening. The aircraft came within close proximity during the jet's final approach, marking another incident between commercial and military aircraft.

stories.title: Under fives should have at most hour a day of screen time, under new UK advice
stories.summary: The UK government issued new guidance advising parents to limit screen time for children under five to no more than one hour per day. For children under two, screen use should be avoided except for shared interactive activities. Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged government support for parents managing children's online exposure.

stories.title: Indian among two killed in UAE by debris of intercepted missiles
stories.summary: An Indian national and a Pakistani national were killed in Abu Dhabi by debris from intercepted missiles. The Indian Embassy offered condolences and assistance to the victim's family.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran war tests MAGA ‘America First’ creed
stories.summary: Polling indicates that US public approval of military action against Iran is declining into negative territory. The trend is testing the "America First" foreign policy principles central to the MAGA movement under President Trump.

stories.title: Federal judge sides with Anthropic in first round of standoff with Pentagon
stories.summary: A federal judge in California's northern district granted Anthropic a temporary injunction blocking the Pentagon's punitive measures against the AI company. The dispute centers on Anthropic's refusal to allow the Department of Defense to use its Claude AI model in autonomous weapons systems. Judge Rita Lin ruled while the full case proceeds.

stories.title: Trump urges Iran to make a deal or US will ‘keep blowing them away’
stories.summary: President Trump urged Iran to negotiate a deal, warning that the US would otherwise continue military strikes. Trump described Iranian officials as desperate to reach an agreement and claimed they were already in communication with Washington.

stories.title: Zelensky to ink air security deal with Saudi Arabia on surprise visit, says source
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made an unannounced visit to Saudi Arabia to sign a security cooperation agreement focused on air defense. The visit reflects growing Gulf interest in Ukrainian arms technology, particularly Kyiv's expertise in countering drone attacks, amid the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Trump ‘pausing’ plan to destroy Iranian power plants for 10 days
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he is pausing his plan to strike Iranian power plants for 10 days, signaling an opening for potential negotiations with Tehran.

stories.title: EU’s top diplomat urges US to pressure Russia to stop aiding Iran
stories.summary: EU Foreign Policy Chief Kaja Kallas urged the United States to pressure Russia to stop providing assistance to Iran amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Lebanon to complain to Security Council over Israeli assault
stories.summary: Lebanon announced it will file a complaint with the UN Security Council over ongoing Israeli bombardment. Parts of Lebanon have been under constant attack since early March after the country was drawn into the wider Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Russian court bans Oscar-winning documentary ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’
stories.summary: A Russian court banned the Oscar-winning documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" after the Kremlin-appointed human rights council complained that images of minors were used without parental consent.

stories.title: Zelensky thanks Canada for new sanctions on Russia’s shadow fleet
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Canada for imposing new sanctions targeting approximately 100 tankers belonging to Russia's shadow fleet used to circumvent existing energy export restrictions.

stories.title: Greater Bay Area trails peers in basic research despite strong tech potential: Deloitte
stories.summary: The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area spent approximately 28.9 billion yuan on basic research in 2024, accounting for just 5.67 percent of total R&D spending, below China's national average according to Deloitte. Despite this gap, the region shows strong potential in semiconductors and smart manufacturing sectors.

stories.title: US deploys uncrewed drone boats in conflict with Iran
stories.summary: The United States confirmed the deployment of uncrewed drone boats in its active conflict with Iran, marking the first acknowledged use of such autonomous naval vessels in combat operations by Washington, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran ‘begging to make a deal’ but teases new aid for farmers amid war fallout
stories.summary: President Trump denied being desperate for a deal with Iran, claiming Tehran was eager to negotiate while presenting oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz as an Iranian concession. The US-Israeli war on Iran is nearing its one-month mark, driving up global oil prices.

stories.title: Bennett says Netanyahu ‘tearing the State of Israel apart,’ vows to replace him
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett accused Prime Minister Netanyahu of "tearing the State of Israel apart" and vowed to replace him. Bennett said he had offered former general Eisenkot a partnership and criticized the government's handling of the ultra-Orthodox draft issue.

stories.title: Why is Pakistan involved in efforts to stop the war in Iran?
stories.summary: Pakistan has positioned itself as a mediator in efforts to end the Iran war. Islamabad has avoided taking sides, instead seeking to maintain stable relations with all parties involved in the conflict.

stories.title: Iranian regime hardliners ramp up calls for a nuclear bomb, sources claim
stories.summary: Hardline elements within Iran's regime are reportedly intensifying calls for developing a nuclear weapon. However, sources claim no formal decision has been made to change Iran's nuclear doctrine, despite ongoing uranium enrichment activities.

stories.title: Mediators say Iran has not requested pause on energy-site strikes: Report
stories.summary: Mediators involved in US-Iran peace talks told the Wall Street Journal that Iran has not requested a 10-day pause on strikes against its energy facilities and has not yet delivered a final response to a 15-point peace plan. This contradicts President Trump's earlier claim that the pause came at Tehran's request.

stories.title: Australia news live: Kyle Sandilands in court for hearing over radio sacking; Coalition calls for cut to fuel excise
stories.summary: Severe overnight storms in Sydney, Australia, caused widespread power outages across the city. Separately, Australia's Coalition has called for a cut to fuel excise amid rising energy costs.

stories.title: NYC Council passes bill to protect houses of worship by veto-proof majority
stories.summary: The New York City Council passed legislation to protect houses of worship by a veto-proof majority as part of a broader plan to combat antisemitism. Critics have raised concerns the bill could harm free speech rights, and Mayor Mamdani has not confirmed whether he will sign or veto it.

stories.title: Eurovision Song Contest oddsmakers predict Israel will win televoting again this year
stories.summary: Oddsmakers tracked by the Eurovision World website give Israel a 26% chance of winning the televoting portion of this year's Eurovision Song Contest, following its televoting success in previous editions.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill five as Hezbollah claims new attacks
stories.summary: Lebanon reported that Israeli strikes killed five people as Hezbollah claimed new attacks. Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem stated that negotiations with Israel under fire would constitute "surrender" and urged Lebanese authorities to reconsider criminalizing the group's military activities.

stories.title: Mbappe nets for 10-man France in win against Brazil in World Cup warm-up
stories.summary: France defeated Brazil 2-1 in a friendly match held in the United States, with Kylian Mbappe scoring for a ten-man French side. The match served as a potential warm-up ahead of the 2026 World Cup final.

stories.title: Deputy PM Kuleba on end of heating season: Where to begin shutting off heat
stories.summary: Despite constant enemy attacks, 98.9% of residential buildings and 99.9% of social facilities were provided with heat during the 2025/2026 heating season.

stories.title: Deputy PM Kuleba on end of heating season: Where to begin shutting off heat
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Kuleba reported that 98.9% of residential buildings and 99.9% of social facilities received heat during the 2025/2026 heating season despite continuous enemy attacks. Officials are now planning the transition to end the heating season.

stories.title: Olivia Dean leads the way with three wins at 2026 Mobo awards
stories.summary: British singer Olivia Dean won three awards at the 2026 Mobo awards, including best female act, album of the year, and song of the year. Other winners included Raye for video of the year, Central Cee for best hip-hop act, and Ezra Collective in the jazz category.

stories.title: Manila’s streets empty as fuel prices surge amid Strait of Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: Streets in Manila have emptied as fuel prices surge in the Philippines amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis. Filipinos are contending with soaring oil costs, shrinking incomes, and a stagnating economy.

stories.title: As world seeks war’s end, Israelis hold out for full victory
stories.summary: Israeli public opinion strongly favors continuing the war against Iran until Tehran's regime is sufficiently weakened to no longer pose a threat. This stance contrasts with growing international calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict.

stories.title: China warns U.S. against building arms facility in Philippines
stories.summary: China warned the United States against building an arms facility in the Philippines. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that Beijing would "firmly safeguard its territorial sovereignty and security interests."

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran to make a deal or the U.S. will “keep blowing them away”
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran to reach a deal or the United States would "keep blowing them away." The statement came amid the ongoing US military campaign against Iran, raising fears of further escalation in West Asia.

stories.title: Why Iraq is the most fragile front in the US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Iraq faces escalating instability as militias and foreign powers clash on its territory amid the broader US-Israel conflict with Iran. Analysts describe the country as one of the most fragile fronts in the regional war.

stories.title: US proposal to end war is 'one-sided', door to diplomacy still open, Iranian official says
stories.summary: Iran described a US proposal to end the war, conveyed through Pakistan, as "one-sided and unfair," according to a senior Iranian official speaking to Reuters. The official added that a diplomatic path could still be found if Washington adopted a more realistic approach.

stories.title: Iran war is starting to disrupt global value chains
stories.summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development warned that the ongoing Iran conflict risks pushing the global economy toward stagflation. EBRD chief economist Beata Javorcik said the outcome depends on the duration of hostilities, as sustained high energy prices would drive inflation and undermine economic growth.

stories.title: Venezuelans deported by US detail fresh claims of torture and abuse at El Salvador mega-prison
stories.summary: Eighteen Venezuelan men deported by the US to El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Centre (Cecot) have filed a petition before the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights alleging torture, sexual assault, and medical neglect by Salvadoran authorities.

stories.title: Israel says new wave of missiles launched from Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that a new wave of missiles was launched from Iran toward Israel. Israeli air defense systems were activated to intercept the incoming projectiles.

stories.title: US Army seeks sled-mounted air defense for light infantry
stories.summary: The US Army is soliciting proposals for sled- or pallet-mounted air defense weapon systems designed for light infantry units. The systems would be transportable by light manned and unmanned vehicles during joint forced entry operations.

stories.title: ECC approves Rs100bn supplementary grant for PM’s austerity fund
stories.summary: Pakistan's Economic Coordination Committee approved a Rs100 billion supplementary grant for the prime minister's austerity fund, intended to finance petroleum pricing subsidies. The decision was made amid concerns about the impact of Gulf region developments on energy prices.

stories.title: Will Trump Put Boots on the Ground in Iran?
stories.summary: The US military is deploying thousands of additional troops to the Middle East amid the escalating conflict with Iran, raising questions about the possibility of a ground operation in the region.

stories.title: Argentina declares Jalisco New Generation Cartel a ‘terrorist’ group
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei's government designated Mexico's Jalisco New Generation Cartel as a terrorist organization. Officials said the move is intended to strengthen international cooperation against organized crime.

stories.title: What are the red lines for Iran and the US in the war?
stories.summary: Iran stated that a list of 15 demands presented by the United States does not reflect reality, as both sides negotiate potential red lines in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: War in the Mideast: are the UK, Australia and Taiwan about to run out of fuel?
stories.summary: Social media posts claiming the UK, Australia, and Taiwan are on the verge of fuel crises amid Iran's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz have gone viral. France 24 examined the claims against available data to assess whether the alarming warnings about dwindling reserves and imminent blackouts are accurate.

stories.title: Trump postpones US strikes on Iranian power grid to April 6 amid talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump postponed planned US strikes on Iran's power grid to April 6, 2026, amid ongoing negotiations. Trump has threatened the attacks to pressure Iran into reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping waterway.

stories.title: Is Russia really shaping up as the biggest winner from the Iran war?
stories.summary: Russia is emerging as a potential major beneficiary of the Iran war, as Asian nations scramble to secure Russian energy supplies amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption. President Putin encouraged oil and gas suppliers to leverage additional revenues generated by the spike in energy prices.

stories.title: New York Post: Ukraine kills over 6,000 Russian troops in four days, shifts course of war
stories.summary: Ukraine repelled massive Russian assaults and eliminated more than 6,000 Russian troops over four days, according to the New York Post. Ukrainian military innovations were credited with shifting the course of the conflict.

stories.title: Two killed, 8 injured in Israeli air strike in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike targeted the town of Kfar Reman in the Nabatieh district of southern Lebanon, killing two people and injuring eight others, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: WTO holds crunch meeting amid growing uncertainty over multilateral system
stories.summary: The World Trade Organization held a critical meeting as tariff wars have disrupted the existing multilateral trade system. Members warned that failure to agree on reforms could lead some parties to draft an entirely new set of trade rules.

stories.title: Trump pushes back Iran strikes deadline to 6 April
stories.summary: President Trump announced he was pausing US attacks on Iranian power infrastructure by at least 10 days, pushing the deadline to April 6, 2026. He claimed talks with Tehran were going well.

stories.title: Trump says talks with Iran ‘going very well,’ delays strikes on power plants by 10 days
stories.summary: President Trump announced a 10-day delay to planned US strikes on Iranian power plants, saying talks with Tehran are going well. Israel expects limited influence over Trump's decision, while the IDF continues striking Iranian targets.

stories.title: One killed in Tehran following an attack on a telecommunications building
stories.summary: A telecommunications building in southwest Tehran was hit in an attack, and shrapnel from the projectile struck a passing car, killing one person, according to Iran's Mehr news agency.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1492: Bombs on Baltic pipelines, boots on shadow tankers — and then Washington’s ultimatum
stories.summary: On day 1,492 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine struck the KINEF refinery in Russia's northwestern energy corridor for a third consecutive time. Britain's navy gained authority to board sanctioned shadow fleet vessels, and President Zelenskyy revealed Washington is conditioning security guarantees on Ukraine surrendering all of Donbas.

stories.title: Israeli naval intelligence reduces Iranian threat to Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Israeli naval intelligence directed precision strikes on specific targets in the Strait of Hormuz area as part of Operation Roaring Lion, aiming to reduce Iran's threat to maritime traffic in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Budanov: World War III has been underway for some time already
stories.summary: Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Ukrainian President's Office, stated that World War III has already been underway for some time, suggesting the current global conflicts constitute a broader war.

stories.title: Improvised explosive found at CENTCOM, USSOCOM HQ in Florida, FBI’s Patel says
stories.summary: An improvised explosive device was discovered at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, Florida, which houses both US Central Command and US Special Operations Command. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the finding.

stories.title: Amid war, Iranian hardliners ramp up once-taboo calls to seek nuclear bomb
stories.summary: Following the killing of Iranian security chief Ali Larijani, hardliners within Iran's IRGC have intensified once-taboo calls to develop a nuclear weapon and withdraw from the Non-Proliferation Treaty. Sources say the killing has weakened less hawkish figures who previously pushed back against such proposals.

stories.title: Trump takes swipe at ‘not great’ Australia among complaints about global lack of support for US in Iran conflict
stories.summary: President Trump criticised Australia, NATO, the UK, and other nations for insufficient involvement in the US-Israeli war against Iran. He expressed surprise at Australia's lack of support during a White House press conference alongside comments about UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

stories.title: Germany won’t send Taurus missiles to Ukraine – and now Merz says Ukraine doesn’t need them anyway
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that Berlin will not send Taurus cruise missiles to Ukraine, arguing Kyiv no longer needs them. Germany pointed to Ukraine's domestically produced long-range weapons systems as justification.

stories.title: Chief of Staff Zamir warns IDF will collapse due to lack of manpower, raises 'ten red flags'
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir warned that the Israeli military faces a manpower crisis and could collapse, raising 'ten red flags.' He noted that Israel lacks legislation to significantly increase ultra-Orthodox conscription even during peacetime.

stories.title: Al Jazeera visits Iran’s UNESCO-listed palace damaged by war
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reporters visited Tehran's Golestan Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that Iran says was damaged by US-Israeli military strikes. The visit documented the extent of damage to the historic landmark.

stories.title: Trump urges Republicans to end filibuster to ease airport delays
stories.summary: President Trump urged Republican senators to eliminate the filibuster to address growing airport delays linked to DHS staffing shortages. Senate Majority Leader John Thune has repeatedly stated that Republicans lack the votes to bypass or weaken the filibuster rule.

stories.title: On Taiwan, Trump reimagines strategic ambiguity to suit his own ends
stories.summary: President Trump postponed a planned visit to China, initially having pressured Beijing to join a naval escort campaign in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump's shifting stance on Taiwan and China policy has frustrated Beijing over the lack of strategic clarity from Washington.

stories.title: South Africa disinvited from G7 in France
stories.summary: South Africa stated that France rescinded President Cyril Ramaphosa's invitation to the G7 Leaders Summit scheduled for June, alleging Paris acted under US pressure. Separately, Ethiopia is intensifying its bid to join the World Trade Organization more than two decades after applying.

stories.title: Gulf nations take lead on Iran at UN while Europe weakens stance, Danon tells 'Post' - interview
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador Danny Danon told the Jerusalem Post that Gulf nations have taken the lead on addressing Iran at the United Nations while European countries have weakened their stance. He noted regional rivals set aside differences to confront a common threat.

stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis ready to join Iran war if needed, raising new shipping risk
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels have signaled readiness to join the Iran war if called upon, raising new risks for international shipping. Diplomats and analysts say the Iran-aligned movement is waiting for the right moment to intervene.

stories.title: At least nine people dead, dozens missing as boat sinks off Djibouti coast
stories.summary: At least nine people died and dozens remain missing after a boat sank off the coast of Djibouti. Rescue operations recovered 266 survivors, and the UN warned that the deadliest season on the migration route is just beginning.

stories.title: Russian farmers complain of mobile internet shutdowns amid spring planting
stories.summary: Russian farmers are reporting that government-ordered mobile internet shutdowns, imposed to counter Ukrainian drone attacks, are disrupting fieldwork during the spring planting season. A major farming lobby raised the concerns publicly.

stories.title: An Iran Exit Plan
stories.summary: Analysts suggest there remains an opportunity for a diplomatic compromise between Washington and Tehran to end the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Trump says Iran had ‘better get serious soon’ in US talks
stories.summary: President Trump warned Iran to "get serious soon" in negotiations with the United States. The warning coincided with Israel's announcement that it had killed the commander of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards' navy.

stories.title: Request for preferential energy cargoes will be ‘considered favourably’, Oman envoy assures petroleum minister
stories.summary: Oman's ambassador to Pakistan assured Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik that Islamabad's request for preferential energy cargoes would be "considered favourably." The envoy expressed Oman's readiness to support Pakistan's energy diversification and security efforts.

stories.title: War on Iran could be 'catalyst' for erosion of US petrodollar, Deutsche Bank says
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank warned that the ongoing war on Iran could serve as a catalyst for the erosion of the US petrodollar system. The petrodollar arrangement helps keep borrowing costs low for American consumers and the US government.

stories.title: G-7 Aims to Balance Addressing Russia-Ukraine, Iran Wars
stories.summary: G-7 allies are seeking to balance attention between the Russia-Ukraine war and the Iran conflict, with concerns that Washington may deprioritize support for Kyiv as the Iran war continues.

stories.title: Iran may believe it has the upper hand as Trump seeks talks
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Iran believes it holds the upper hand in negotiations with the US after nearly four weeks of war. Tehran's growing confidence in its bargaining position reflects its assessment of strategic resilience despite American military superiority.

stories.title: Spanish woman Noelia, 25, dies by euthanasia after father loses legal bid to stop her
stories.summary: A 25-year-old Spanish woman named Noelia, who was paraplegic following a failed suicide attempt, died by euthanasia at a hospital in Sant Pere de Ribes. Her father had unsuccessfully pursued a legal challenge to prevent the procedure, making it the first such case to reach a Spanish court since euthanasia was legalised in 2021.

stories.title: 'Return hubs' for migrants clear EU parliament hurdle
stories.summary: The European Parliament approved measures enabling tougher penalties for irregular migrants and their potential deportation to "return hubs" outside the EU. Human rights groups have criticised the legislation as part of a broader tightening of immigration rules across the 27-nation bloc.

stories.title: US markets see biggest slump since start of US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: US stock markets suffered their largest decline since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, with the Dow falling 450 points, the S&P 500 dropping 1.7%, and the Nasdaq declining 2.3% into correction territory.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in southern Lebanon by Hezbollah anti-tank missile
stories.summary: An IDF soldier from the Golani Brigade was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank missile near the Litani River in southern Lebanon on Thursday. Four other soldiers were injured in the same attack.

stories.title: Iran placing messages on missiles as war of narratives intensifies
stories.summary: Iran's military released a video showing personnel placing a written message on a missile prior to launch. The act is part of an intensifying war of narratives between Iran and its adversaries.

stories.title: Leaked Nepal report into deadly uprising calls for prosecuting ex-PM KP Sharma Oli
stories.summary: A leaked report from a Nepali commission has recommended prosecuting former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli in connection with the September 2025 uprising that killed at least 77 people and led to his ouster. Oli was subsequently defeated in elections by rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Chernihiv's transport infrastructure, one person injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck transport infrastructure in the northern Ukrainian city of Chernihiv, injuring at least one person.

stories.title: Iranian security forces accused of using civilians as cover to avoid strikes
stories.summary: Iranian security forces are accused of using civilians as human shields to avoid strikes, according to witness testimonies. Forces have reportedly assembled in schools and universities and created deliberate traffic congestion near checkpoints.

stories.title: How Pakistan positioned itself at the centre of global crisis management
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a key mediator between the United States and Iran amid the ongoing conflict. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir as part of de-escalation efforts.

stories.title: Russia's spring offensive in Ukraine expected to focus on 'Fortress Belt' in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Russia's anticipated spring offensive in Ukraine is expected to target the heavily fortified "Fortress Belt" of cities in the eastern Donetsk region. Moscow has repeatedly demanded Ukraine relinquish the area as a condition for peace. A retired US Navy vice admiral described the region as a strategic corridor for further military operations.

stories.title: Pakistan resumes military operations against Afghanistan
stories.summary: Pakistan resumed military operations inside Afghanistan after an Eid al-Fitr pause. The operation, ongoing since October, has reportedly killed hundreds.

stories.title: Italy police warn reptiles used as weapons after snakes found behind wall in secret room
stories.summary: Italian police discovered snakes hidden behind a wall in a secret room and warned that reptiles are being used as weapons. Authorities said the animals served as tools of intimidation and displays of criminal power in the area.

stories.title: What does each side in the Iran war say it would accept for a deal?
stories.summary: The United States, Israel, and Iran have each laid out maximalist positions for ending the ongoing war. The conflict has disrupted Gulf energy supplies and threatened the global economy as all sides seek favorable terms.

stories.title: Trump extends deadline to strike Iran's energy sites
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced on his Truth Social platform that he would pause threatened US strikes on Iranian power plants for 10 days, extending the deadline to April 6, 2026. Trump claimed the pause came at Iran's request and said talks were going well.

stories.title: Algeria and Spain discuss increasing gas supplies to the European nation
stories.summary: Spain's top diplomat visited Algeria to discuss increasing natural gas supplies to Spain. The discussions come as the Iran conflict disrupts global energy markets.

stories.title: Iran’s Parliament working on bill to impose fees on ships in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's parliament is drafting legislation to impose fees on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The measure would likely face strong opposition from Gulf Arab states, the United States, and other maritime nations.

stories.title: Flatterers out in force to fill Trump’s head with Venezuelan statue dreams
stories.summary: At a White House cabinet meeting, US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum claimed Venezuela intends to honor President Trump with a statue. The session drew criticism for its displays of flattery, with observers comparing the atmosphere to that of North Korea.

stories.title: Russia Eyes New Windfall as Iran War Chokes Fertilizer Supplies
stories.summary: Russia, the world's second-largest fertilizer producer, stands to benefit financially from global fertilizer supply disruptions caused by the ongoing war with Iran affecting shipping and trade routes.

stories.title: Defense forces destroy Russian fuel train in temporarily occupied Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Security Service and Armed Forces personnel jointly destroyed a Russian fuel train in the temporarily occupied Luhansk region of eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump again berates NATO for inaction in securing Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump criticised NATO allies during a Cabinet meeting for refusing to help secure the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas typically passes. Trump called the situation a failed test for the alliance.

stories.title: US secretary of state says ‘growing amount of energy’ flowing through Hormuz
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said intermediary countries are passing messages between Washington and Tehran and that progress has been made. He noted a growing amount of energy is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, though not yet at full capacity.

stories.title: One month on, Iran has the upper hand as war risks rise for Trump and the world
stories.summary: One month into the Iran war, analysts assess that Iran holds the upper hand as the conflict has become a grinding, destructive military campaign for regional superiority. Risks are rising for both the Trump administration and the broader international community.

stories.title: Russia is now sending its own drones back to Iran – the weapons it learned to make from Tehran
stories.summary: Western intelligence reports indicate Russia began delivering drones to Iran in early March 2026, marking the first known transfer of Russian lethal aid to Tehran since the war started. The drones are based on technology Russia originally acquired from Iran.

stories.title: Companies to enter negotiations to build commercial data centers on Army installations
stories.summary: The US Army plans to use its Enhanced Use Lease authority to allow private companies to finance and operate commercial data centers on underused land at Fort Bliss, Texas, and Dugway Proving Ground, Utah.

stories.title: Is Pakistan hosting US-Iran talks? Here’s what we know so far
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a potential venue for indirect US-Iran talks amid the ongoing conflict. Islamabad has been engaging with regional leaders and calling for de-escalation since hostilities began on February 28.

stories.title: Enemy attacks Dnipropetrovsk region over 70 times in one day, eight wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces launched more than 70 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day using drones, artillery, and aerial bombs across four districts, wounding eight people.

stories.title: NHS bosses say resident doctors’ strike will cause ‘maximum harm’
stories.summary: The British Medical Association's decision to withdraw from pay negotiations has led NHS bosses to accuse resident doctors of planning strikes intended to cause maximum harm to patients. Health Secretary Wes Streeting gave doctors until April 2 to reconsider their rejection of a £700 million pay offer.

stories.title: Iran war: Houthi restraint driven by local priorities
stories.summary: Despite threats to intervene in the Iran war, Yemen's Houthi militia has remained largely passive. Analysts suggest local priorities and internal considerations are driving the Iran-backed group's restraint.

stories.title: Trump has called Middle East wars 'crazy', but the US-Israel war on Iran may be the craziest yet
stories.summary: An analysis argues the US-Israel war on Iran has hardened Tehran's stance, fueled global instability, and divided President Trump's MAGA political base. The conflict is seen as contradicting Trump's stated America First foreign policy agenda.

stories.title: Republican Support for Trump’s Iran War Is Wobbling
stories.summary: Republican lawmakers are showing growing unease with President Trump's war on Iran, raising concerns about the conflict's costs, the possibility of deploying ground troops, and the lack of clearly defined objectives.

stories.title: Israel sends more troops into southern Lebanon as ground invasion expands
stories.summary: Israel deployed additional troops into southern Lebanon as its ground invasion expanded. Lebanese Prime Minister warned that Israeli actions and statements threaten Lebanese sovereignty and violate international law.

stories.title: Israeli entrepreneurs raise $11 million to fight vulnerabilities exploited by Iranian hackers
stories.summary: Israeli startup Onit Security raised $11 million to combat cybersecurity vulnerabilities exploited by Iranian hacker groups. The company developed an AI-driven platform to detect and remediate these exploits.

stories.title: Temporary pause in Operation Ghazab lil-Haq has concluded, FO says
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced that the temporary pause in Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, a military campaign against the Afghan Taliban launched on February 26 following cross-border firing, has concluded. Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said the operation would continue until its objectives are achieved.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves urged to raise taxes on companies profiting from war on Iran
stories.summary: UK charities and trade unions are urging Chancellor Rachel Reeves to impose windfall taxes on banks, defence firms, and energy companies profiting from the US-Israel war on Iran. The proposed revenue would fund emergency cost-of-living support for British households.

stories.title: Gulf states have a right to defend themselves against attacks
stories.summary: Analyst Fadel Abdulghany argued that Gulf states have a right to collective self-defense and to request military assistance following recent Iranian attacks on the region.

stories.title: Iran's stolen futures: The arrested Iranians at risk of execution by the regime
stories.summary: Since protests began on December 28, thousands of Iranians have been arrested on charges of 'crimes against the state.' Many detainees face lengthy prison sentences or execution by the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Iran's navy commander Alireza Tangsiri
stories.summary: Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz announced that an air strike killed Alireza Tangsiri, commander of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards' navy. The US military confirmed the operation and stated that Tangsiri's death makes the region safer.

stories.title: Trump comments on possibility of redirecting weapons for Ukraine to Middle East
stories.summary: President Trump acknowledged reports that the US Department of Defense is considering diverting weapons originally earmarked for Ukraine to the Middle East, stating that American military forces routinely redirect resources.

stories.title: Explosions heard across Tehran after IDF announces wave of strikes on regime terror targets
stories.summary: The IDF announced a wave of strikes on targets across Iran, with explosions heard in Tehran. Targets included missile launching sites, weapons manufacturing facilities in Isfahan and Parchin, and a Quds Force site in central Iran.

stories.title: Siblings who fled to China charged over bomb planted outside US Air Force base
stories.summary: Alen Zheng, 20, and Ann Mary Zheng, 27, both US citizens, were charged in federal indictments after an explosive device was left outside a gate at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, Florida. Both siblings fled to China after the incident; the sister was arrested upon her return. Their mother was detained for deportation after overstaying her visa.

stories.title: 4th Pakistani national killed in UAE due to ‘falling debris’ from missile interception
stories.summary: A fourth Pakistani national was killed in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, by falling debris from the interception of a ballistic missile amid the US-Israeli war on Iran. The Abu Dhabi Media Office also reported additional deaths and injuries from a separate interception incident.

stories.title: Explainer-Israeli plan for Lebanon 'buffer zone' follows long past of invasions, occupation
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to seize a portion of southern Lebanon to create a buffer zone against Hezbollah militants. The move has raised fears among Lebanese of prolonged Israeli military occupation, potential deepening of instability, and further civilian displacement in the region.

stories.title: EU probes Snapchat over suspected child protection failings
stories.summary: The European Union has opened an investigation into Snapchat over suspected failures in child protection measures. The US-based messaging app has approximately 97 million monthly active users across the 27-nation EU bloc.

stories.title: Finland’s top court fines ex-minister for remarks on gays
stories.summary: Finland's top court fined former minister Päivi Räsänen over remarks about homosexuality. In a text exceeding 20 pages, Räsänen had described homosexuality as a "psychosexual developmental disorder" and an "abnormality."

stories.title: Spanish woman dies by euthanasia after long legal battle with father
stories.summary: A Spanish woman named Noelia Castillo died by euthanasia after a prolonged legal dispute with her father over the procedure. The European Court of Human Rights ruled in her favor earlier in the week.

stories.title: How High Could Energy Prices Go?
stories.summary: Energy policy expert Jason Bordoff discussed how the ongoing Middle East conflict could drive energy prices higher, analyzing the potential winners and losers of sustained disruption in the region.

stories.title: Trump urges Iran to negotiate end to war or face further assassinations
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump urged Iran to negotiate an end to the nearly month-long war, threatening further assassinations of senior officials. On the same day, Israel announced it had killed Iranian Revolutionary Guards naval commander Alireza Tangsiri in a strike on the port of Bandar Abbas.

stories.title: Join Us for a Special Live Webinar - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish People Policy Institute is hosting a live webinar in which experts will discuss whether the war's objectives have been achieved and assess future challenges and opportunities.
