stories.summary: Heavy rainfall struck several parts of Egypt, including New Cairo, flooding roads across the country. Local authorities warned of two days of continued heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms, strong winds, and lower temperatures.

stories.title: Trump eyes China deal, but dragging out talks risks backlash, warns former diplomat
stories.summary: Former US Deputy Secretary of State Stephen Biegun said President Trump is seeking an economic deal with China during a planned Beijing visit. Biegun warned that if Beijing drags out trade negotiations too long, Trump could adopt a much tougher stance against China.

stories.title: DJI unveils its first 360-degree drone amid patent dispute with crosstown rival Insta360
stories.summary: Chinese drone manufacturer DJI launched its first 360-degree drone, the DJI Avata 360, featuring an 8K omnidirectional camera. The product directly challenges domestic rival Insta360 amid an escalating patent dispute between the two Shenzhen-based companies.

stories.title: Trump: Iran ‘begging’ for deal as pressure mounts on Tehran
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on Truth Social that Iran is "begging" for a deal as pressure mounts on Tehran. He described the Iranian delegation as "strange" and asserted that Iran has been "militarily obliterated" with no chance of recovery.

stories.title: Sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker struck by drone near Istanbul, 140,000 tons of oil on board
stories.summary: A drone struck the sanctioned Russian shadow-fleet tanker ALTURA near Istanbul while it was carrying approximately 140,000 tons of oil. The vessel had previously transported millions of barrels of Russian crude to India and China.

stories.title: Is Europe heading to an energy crisis?
stories.summary: Europe is bracing for an energy supply crunch and price shock as the ongoing Iran conflict disrupts global energy markets.

stories.title: Zelensky: EU will resolve issue of granting Ukraine loan
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is awaiting the release of a €90 billion EU loan or an alternative financing mechanism. The funds are intended to support Ukraine's military operations.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz highlights Pakistan’s role in Middle East de-escalation in meeting with Chinese envoy
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif discussed Middle East de-escalation efforts with Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zedong. Pakistan, alongside Türkiye and Egypt, played a key role in securing a five-day pause on US plans to strike Iranian energy infrastructure, officials said.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia stoic amid Iran war, but attacks on Red Sea ports could change that
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has maintained a restrained stance during the Iran war, but experts warn that any Iranian attack on the Bab al-Mandeb Strait — Riyadh's remaining oil export shipping route — would likely trigger an immediate Saudi retaliation.

stories.title: Social media platform X faces global outage not linked to country-level disruption: NetBlocks
stories.summary: Social media platform X experienced a global outage, with internet monitor NetBlocks confirming the disruption was not linked to country-level filtering. Pakistani users reported a sharp spike in issues after 12pm, with problems affecting the timeline and app functionality.

stories.title: 2 men released on bail after arson attack on London Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: Two men were released on bail in London after being arrested for an arson attack on Jewish community ambulances. Police said the suspects face strict conditions and the incident is being investigated as an antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Volkswagen in talks to make Iron Dome parts at struggling German auto plant: report
stories.summary: Volkswagen is reportedly in discussions to manufacture components for Israel's Iron Dome air-defense system at an underperforming German automotive plant. The move reflects a broader trend of European automakers pivoting toward defense production as the German auto industry faces significant economic challenges.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires over 600 times at Israel, IDF troops over last 24 hours
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched over 600 attacks on Israel and IDF forces within a 24-hour period. Analysts suggest the surge in attacks may be aimed at pressuring Israel and the US into agreeing to a ceasefire on all fronts.

stories.title: Domestic helper held over death of baby found in rubbish bin at Hong Kong plaza
stories.summary: A 34-year-old Indonesian domestic helper was arrested in Hong Kong on suspicion of concealing a child's birth. A newborn boy with his umbilical cord still attached was found by a cleaner in a rubbish bin at Lee Theatre Plaza in Causeway Bay and was later declared dead at hospital.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 26 – Premature ceasefire will not neutralize Iran’s potent threat
stories.summary: Times of Israel editor David Horovitz discussed U.S. efforts to initiate high-level negotiations with Iran, warning that a premature ceasefire could fail to neutralize Iran's threat to the region and the world.

stories.title: US war in Iran: China casts itself as savior of SE Asia
stories.summary: Beijing is positioning itself as a more reliable partner for Southeast Asian nations as the US-Israeli war with Iran drives fuel prices higher across the region. China is leveraging the crisis to contrast its stability with Washington's military engagements.

stories.title: The limits of military might: Thoughts on the wars in Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that military force in the conflicts involving Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza can weaken adversaries but cannot eliminate them or resolve the underlying disputes driving the violence.

stories.title: Iranian press review: Reports of US backchannel to Ghalibaf cause backlash in Tehran
stories.summary: Reports of a U.S. backchannel to Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf sparked a political backlash in Tehran. Meanwhile, Iranian cancer patients face treatment difficulties and opposition figures have condemned attacks on national infrastructure.

stories.title: Video: GCC chief says Iran charging for ships to pass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: GCC Secretary-General Jasem al-Budaiwi accused Iran of charging fees for ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively imposing a toll on maritime traffic.

stories.title: Defense forces halt major Russian offensive in Pokrovsk area
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported halting a major Russian offensive near the city of Pokrovsk in eastern Ukraine. No further details on casualties or territorial changes were provided.

stories.title: PSX loses over 2,000 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan Stock Exchange's KSE-100 index fell over 2,600 points, or 1.67%, during intraday trading on Thursday, dropping to around 155,670 points. The decline followed a significant recovery the previous day, when value-hunting and cautious optimism over easing Middle East tensions had lifted the index above 158,000.

stories.title: China’s CNOOC to boost oil and gas output amid Middle East strife
stories.summary: China National Offshore Oil Corporation announced plans to further boost oil and gas production in 2025 amid geopolitical tensions. The state-backed company reported an 11.5 percent drop in net profit to 122.08 billion yuan despite record-high production volumes, owing to low oil prices.

stories.title: Palestinian prisoners' families fear Israel's death penalty law
stories.summary: Families of Palestinian prisoners have expressed fear over Israel's proposed death penalty legislation. One mother told reporters she now worries her imprisoned son could face execution.

stories.title: Trump stays popular in Philippines despite Iran war fuel crisis
stories.summary: Despite an energy crisis in the Philippines driven by the US-Israel war on Iran, Filipino public opinion remains largely favorable toward President Trump. Public anger has instead focused on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s administration for failing to control soaring fuel prices across the archipelago.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in Hezbollah gunfight; terror group fires rockets, drones at north
stories.summary: An IDF soldier was killed in a gunfight with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, while the group fired rockets and drones at northern Israel. Separately, an 11-year-old girl was in serious condition after suffering heart failure during a rocket attack, and 15 troops were hospitalized with suspected hypothermia.

stories.title: ‘We’ll go 40%’: Army wants good-enough tech it can reshape for battle
stories.summary: The commander of the U.S. Army's 4th Infantry Division stated the service prefers fielding technology at roughly 40 percent maturity that can be adapted and refined during operations. The approach prioritizes speed of deployment over perfection, embracing good-enough solutions that can be reshaped for battlefield conditions.

stories.title: Israel says IRGC Navy’s commander, other chiefs killed; Qalibaf said removed from hit list
stories.summary: Israel confirmed it killed IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri and other senior Iranian military officials. Israeli authorities reportedly removed Iranian FM Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf from their target list at Pakistan's request to facilitate ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: As oil-shocked world turns to renewables, China will reap the rewards
stories.summary: The oil shock from the Iran war is accelerating global investment in renewable energy, with analysts predicting China will be the largest beneficiary. China's renewable energy exports are expected to perform strongly, offsetting costs from higher-priced oil imports.

stories.title: India sees spike in social media censorship amid Iran war
stories.summary: Activists in India are raising concerns about increased social media censorship, particularly targeting posts critical of the Indian government and its stance on the Iran war. Content removals have reportedly spiked amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: “You think of only one thing: is your person’s name there” — the Mariupol marine who came home after 1,400 days
stories.summary: Ukrainian marine Ruslan Kurtmallaiev, who defended Mariupol with the 36th Separate Brigade, was released after approximately 1,400 days in Russian captivity, including over two years in solitary confinement. He received only one letter and one phone call from family during his detention.

stories.title: Israel ramps up attacks on Iran, fearing US 'truce' deal
stories.summary: Israel has intensified strikes against Iran, with reports suggesting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is acting pre-emptively ahead of a potential US announcement of a temporary truce with Tehran.

stories.title: As a Palestinian, I stand in solidarity with the Iranian people. Here’s why
stories.summary: A Palestinian writer expressed solidarity with the Iranian people, arguing that Western promises of freedom are undermined by imperialism's pursuit of control.

stories.title: A phone-free childhood? One Irish village is making it happen
stories.summary: A village in Ireland is pursuing a phone-free childhood initiative for local children. A local school principal said the goal is to give kids time to gradually adapt to the digital world rather than being immersed in it from an early age.

stories.title: Iran to allow Malaysian vessels to pass in Strait of Hormuz: Anwar
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Iran has agreed to allow Malaysian vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Anwar said he spoke with Iranian and other regional leaders, and efforts are underway to release detained Malaysian oil tankers and their crews.

stories.title: Samsung, SK urge employees to cut car use as energy risks rise over Iran crisis
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Group asked employees to reduce private car use and adopt fuel-saving measures as energy supply risks mount due to the Iran crisis. The South Korean conglomerates are responding to rising fuel costs and potential disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim meets Lukashenko, slams ‘pressure ​on Belarus from West’
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un met Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko in Pyongyang, where the two allies of Russia signed a friendship treaty and criticized Western pressure on Belarus.

stories.title: Netanyahu vows to seize more of Lebanon amid annexation fears
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has pledged to seize additional territory in southern Lebanon, amid calls from far-right government ministers to annex areas largely depopulated by Israel's military campaign.

stories.title: At least 15 IDF soldiers evacuated from Lebanon with hypothermia symptoms
stories.summary: At least 15 IDF soldiers operating in Lebanon were evacuated after developing hypothermia symptoms. One soldier was in moderate condition, while 14 others, including an officer, sustained light injuries.

stories.title: China says ‘glimmer of hope’ on Iran war talks
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi expressed seeing a "glimmer of hope" for Iran war talks during separate phone calls with his Turkish and Egyptian counterparts. Wang urged dialogue as a path toward resolving the conflict.

stories.title: Meet Karin Prien, who could become Germany’s first president of Jewish descent
stories.summary: German federal minister Karin Prien, a granddaughter of Holocaust survivors, is being considered as a candidate for Germany's presidency. If selected, she would become the country's first president of Jewish descent.

stories.title: Oil prices jump 5 percent on Iran-US talks uncertainty
stories.summary: Oil prices surged approximately 5 percent amid uncertainty surrounding ongoing US-Iran negotiations, raising concerns about potential supply disruptions. Brent crude reached $107 per barrel.

stories.title: India among five nations granted passage through Strait of Hormuz by Tehran
stories.summary: Iran has granted passage through the Strait of Hormuz to five nations, including India, after effectively blocking the critical waterway. The strait handles roughly 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments, and its near-closure has driven a surge in global energy prices.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Teachers Issue Ultimatum Over Pay and Conditions
stories.summary: Teachers represented by the Amalgamated Rural Teachers Union of Zimbabwe (ARTUZ) issued a petition to the government threatening industrial action. The union cited long-standing grievances over pay and working conditions.

stories.title: Namibia: Nandi-Ndaitwah Assesses Zambezi Floods As School Close, Communities Refuse to Relocate
stories.summary: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah assessed flood conditions in the Zambezi region, where rising waters have forced school closures. Some affected communities have reportedly refused to relocate despite the flooding.

stories.title: NATO 2025 Annual Report warns energy infrastructure is primary target in any Russian attack on the Alliance
stories.summary: NATO's 2025 annual report, presented by Secretary General Mark Rutte on 26 March, identified energy infrastructure as the primary target in any potential Russian attack on the Alliance. The report noted that Russia's strikes on Ukrainian power grids informed NATO's defensive training priorities.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz floats EU-China trade deal as capitals soften on Beijing
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in parliament he could envision a future EU trade deal with China, signaling a softening European stance toward Beijing. The remarks reflect how rising trade and geopolitical tensions with Washington are prompting European capitals to reconsider their relationship with China.

stories.title: Pro-Israel Democrats decry settler violence in West Bank amid attacks on Palestinians
stories.summary: Several pro-Israel Democratic lawmakers in the US have publicly denounced escalating settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Dozens of Israeli settlers have conducted apparently coordinated attacks, torching homes and vehicles, with at least 10 Palestinian civilians killed by settlers and police since the start of the month.

stories.title: AI rift widens as China urges boycott of top US conference over sanctions ban
stories.summary: The China Computer Federation urged Chinese researchers to boycott a major AI conference after organizers barred submissions from US-sanctioned institutions, including Huawei Technologies. The move marks a new flashpoint in deepening US-China tensions over artificial intelligence development.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine and US assess Putin's intentions to end war differently
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv and Washington differ in their assessments of Russian President Vladimir Putin's willingness to end the war. Zelenskyy argued that only additional international pressure can compel Putin to pursue peace.

stories.title: In mixed Haifa, weary residents face near-constant Iranian and Hezbollah missile fire
stories.summary: Residents of the mixed Jewish, Christian, and Muslim city of Haifa are enduring near-constant missile fire from Iran and Hezbollah. Local businesses across all communities are suffering as customers stay away.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Maduro set to again appear in US court: How strong is the case?
stories.summary: Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is scheduled to appear in a U.S. court on March 26 for a second hearing since his abduction by U.S. military forces on January 3.

stories.title: Egypt's Cairo businesses hit with energy crunch amid Iran war
stories.summary: Egypt announced energy-saving measures to reduce natural gas consumption as its ongoing energy crisis worsens due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Businesses in Cairo are being affected by the energy crunch.

stories.title: Octopus reports sharp rise in solar panel sales since start of Iran war
stories.summary: UK energy company Octopus Energy reported a 54 per cent increase in solar panel sales this month compared to the same period last month, driven by the Iran war's impact on oil prices. Good Energy also reported a doubling of consumer interest in solar installations following the latest energy price shock.

stories.title: EU advances trade deal with US with safeguards - Europe live
stories.summary: The European Union advanced a trade deal with the United States that includes safeguards, following months of delays over tariff legality concerns. Separately, President Trump criticized NATO allies on social media for doing "absolutely nothing" to support the US campaign in Iran.

stories.title: Libya tows damaged Russian LNG tanker from its coast
stories.summary: Libya's coast guard towed a damaged Russian LNG tanker away from the shores near Zuwara after a drone attack. Mediterranean nations have raised concerns about potential environmental risks from the incident.

stories.title: Ukraine struggles to find more NATO donors to pay for US weapons, Bloombeg reports
stories.summary: Ukraine is struggling to secure additional NATO allies willing to fund purchases of U.S. weapons. Only a few countries currently contribute, with the UK being the latest donor. Kyiv estimates it needs $15 billion in 2026 but received just $4.3 billion for 2025, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: Jaishankar in France for G7 meet; West Asia crisis tops agenda
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister Jaishankar traveled to France for a G7 foreign ministers' meeting focused on the West Asia crisis. Ministers are expected to discuss negotiation channels for de-escalation and reopening maritime routes disrupted by the conflict.

stories.title: Israel strikes Iran as Trump says Tehran wants deal to end war
stories.summary: Israel launched a wide-scale wave of strikes targeting Iranian infrastructure, including in central Iran, as the conflict that began on February 28 continued. The war has drawn in multiple Middle Eastern nations, disrupted energy markets, and raised fears of broader global economic damage.

stories.title: Libya, Iran, and the Limits of Airpower
stories.summary: An analysis examines the 2011 NATO air campaign in Libya as a lens for understanding the constraints of airpower in the current Middle East situation. The piece highlights the difficult strategic choices facing U.S. President Donald Trump regarding military options involving Iran.

stories.title: Malaysia says its tankers allowed through Hormuz
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister announced that Iranian authorities have permitted Malaysian oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz, signaling a limited easing of passage restrictions for selected vessels.

stories.title: G-7 meets in France to narrow transatlantic Iran split
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in France to address a transatlantic split over the Iran conflict. France has also invited additional foreign ministers beyond the G7 membership in an effort to broaden the scope of the discussions.

stories.title: Britain moves from sanctions lists to tanker seizures – navy can now board Russia’s shadow fleet
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has expanded its enforcement against Russia's shadow fleet beyond sanctions to include naval authority to board tankers. Approximately 75% of Russian crude exports are transported via the shadow fleet, and the UK and allies have sanctioned more than 500 vessels.

stories.title: Drone attacks sanctioned Russian oil tanker in Black Sea – media
stories.summary: A drone struck the oil tanker Altura in the Black Sea approximately 14 miles from the Bosporus strait. The Altura is subject to sanctions by the EU, Switzerland, Ukraine, and the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Iran to Lebanon: Four million people displaced by US-Israeli war
stories.summary: According to reports, approximately three million Iranians and at least one million Lebanese have been displaced from their homes as a result of US-Israeli military attacks on both countries.

stories.title: Finland’s president says Ukraine talks may be at ‘end of the road’
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said he fears US-led Ukraine peace talks may have reached a dead end. Stubb, who has close ties with both President Trump and President Zelensky, suggested the Iran war may be diverting attention from Ukraine negotiations, or that talks have simply stalled.

stories.title: Cape Town mayor campaigns for leadership of Democratic Alliance
stories.summary: Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis announced his campaign for the leadership of South Africa's Democratic Alliance, the second-largest party in the ruling coalition. He said he aims to build voter trust and expand the party's support base.

stories.title: Royal Navy leads NATO maritime force from German flagship; HMS Dragon in Cyprus
stories.summary: Royal Navy personnel will command one of NATO's maritime immediate response forces from a German flagship vessel. HMS Dragon, originally slated to lead the force, is no longer available and is currently deployed near Cyprus.

stories.title: At least 28 civilians killed in Sudan drone strikes
stories.summary: Drone strikes in Sudan killed at least 28 civilians in the Darfur and Kordofan regions amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces. The attacks have worsened the country's displacement crisis.

stories.title: Trump plans May visit to China for talks with Xi after Iran war delay
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced plans to visit Beijing on May 14–15 to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping, rescheduled from an earlier date due to the ongoing Iran war. Trump also said he would host Xi for a reciprocal visit, as both leaders seek to manage tensions between the world's two largest economies.

stories.title: China’s Pony AI to launch robotaxi service in Europe with Uber, local start-up
stories.summary: Chinese self-driving firm Pony AI announced plans to launch robotaxi services in Zagreb, Croatia, in partnership with Uber and local start-up Verne. The companies aim to operate thousands of autonomous taxis across multiple European cities in the coming years.

stories.title: Turkey, Pakistan emerge as key brokers, shaping post-war order amid Iran conflict- analysis
stories.summary: Turkey and Pakistan are positioning themselves as key mediators in the Iran conflict, seeking to ease tensions and influence the post-war regional order. Both countries are working to establish diplomatic roles amid the broader crisis.

stories.title: Russians strike Dnipro, high-rise building damaged, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Dnipro in central Ukraine, damaging a multi-story residential building. Casualties were reported, though specific numbers were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Iran rejects US ceasefire plan and submits its own | First Thing
stories.summary: Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal and submitted its own negotiation plan, with Foreign Minister stating Tehran has no intention of negotiating for now. Intermediaries are working to keep diplomatic channels open. The conflict has killed over 1,000 people in Lebanon, more than 1,500 in Iran, and 16 in Israel, according to respective authorities.

stories.title: Ukraine drafts its first Africa strategy — targeting Maghreb and sub-Saharan states as geopolitical rivals
stories.summary: Ukraine is drafting its first comprehensive Africa strategy, targeting Maghreb and sub-Saharan states. Lieutenant General Kyrylo Budanov chaired an interagency meeting that produced a draft plan, which is now headed to the Cabinet of Ministers for approval.

stories.title: Germany warns of world economic ‘catastrophe’; OECD cuts UK growth forecast
stories.summary: European officials and the OECD have issued warnings of severe economic fallout as the war on Iran approaches its one-month mark. The OECD has cut its growth forecast for the United Kingdom amid broader concerns about global economic stability.

stories.title: Russian troops regroup and prepare for larger-scale offensive actions – Trehubov
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Trehubov reported that Russian troops are regrouping and preparing for larger-scale offensive operations. The anticipated intensification may coincide with spring vegetation growth, which provides concealment for infiltration groups.

stories.title: G7 allies meet in France to narrow transatlantic Iran split
stories.summary: G7 allies convened in France to address divisions over the war on Iran. British Foreign Minister Yvette Cooper expressed concern that the conflict had diverted attention from the Gaza peace plan and ongoing violence in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Fuel crisis LIVE: LPG supply to be cut off if households refuse PNG switch where available, says Centre
stories.summary: India's central government warned that LPG supply would be cut to households that refuse to switch to piped natural gas where available. The Central Consumer Protection Authority also directed hotels and restaurants not to levy additional fuel-related surcharges on consumers.

stories.title: Iranian naval commander Alireza Tangsiri killed in attack, Israel says
stories.summary: Israel's defence minister announced that Alireza Tangsiri, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy, was killed in an Israeli strike. Israel cited Tangsiri's role in blocking the Strait of Hormuz as justification for the attack.

stories.title: Prominent scholar Tariq Ramadan sentenced to 18 years for rape
stories.summary: Swiss scholar Tariq Ramadan, a former Oxford University lecturer, was sentenced in absentia to 18 years in prison for the sexual assault of three women. The sentencing took place in a French court.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israel military says it has carried out 'wide-scale' strikes in Iran
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it carried out "wide-scale" strikes in Iran. US President Trump claimed Iran was participating in peace talks, while Tehran denied direct negotiations and set its own ceasefire conditions, including compensation for war damages.

stories.title: WTO members gather in Yaounde amid deep divisions and calls for reform
stories.summary: The World Trade Organization's 166 members convened a ministerial conference in Yaoundé, Cameroon, amid sharp divisions over institutional reform. Geopolitical tensions, rising protectionism, and the Middle East conflict overshadowed the trade discussions.

stories.title: SpaceX reportedly set to launch IPO valuing firm at $1.75 trillion
stories.summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, is reportedly preparing an IPO that would value the rocket and satellite internet company at approximately $1.75 trillion, seeking to raise $75 billion on public equity markets. The move comes as its subsidiary xAI continues to consume significant cash.

stories.title: Travelers flock to Clear security app to bypass TSA lines amid US airport chaos
stories.summary: Clear Secure, a biometric security company, has seen a surge in new sign-ups as travelers seek to bypass long TSA lines at more than 60 US airports. The increased demand comes amid a partial Department of Homeland Security shutdown that has left TSA workers unpaid.

stories.title: Nepal’s probe into deadly uprising finds ex-prime minister, officials ‘reckless’
stories.summary: A high-level probe in Nepal found former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli and senior officials criminally negligent over shootings during last year's youth uprising that killed 76 people. The committee, led by former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki, recommended investigation and prosecution of Oli and other officials.

stories.title: Taiwanese court jails former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je for 17 years for corruption
stories.summary: A Taiwanese court sentenced former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je to 17 years in prison for taking bribes and misusing political donations. Ko founded the Taiwan People's Party in 2019 and finished third in the 2024 presidential election. He did not plead guilty.

stories.title: UN adopts Ghana slavery resolution despite Israel, US opposition
stories.summary: UN adopts Ghana-led resolution recognising transatlantic slavery as a crime against humanity and calls for reparations despite US and EU opposition.

stories.title: Zimbabwe says 15 nationals killed after being lured to fight for Russia
stories.summary: Zimbabwe confirmed that 15 of its nationals were killed after being recruited to fight for Russia under false pretenses. The Zimbabwean government said it is engaging Moscow to repatriate remains and bring surviving citizens home.

stories.title: Adopt a Bomb Shelter. Give Israelis a Safer Passover. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jewish Joint Distribution Committee is soliciting donations to equip bomb shelters in Israel with Wi-Fi and resilience kits ahead of Passover, aimed at communities facing ongoing attacks.

stories.title: Russia's largest oil refineries in Leningrad region under drone attack
stories.summary: The Kirishinefteorgsintez (KINEF) oil refinery in Kirishi, Leningrad region, was attacked by drones. KINEF is one of Russia's largest refining facilities.

stories.title: German army eyes AI tools to expedite wartime decision-making
stories.summary: The German army is exploring artificial intelligence tools to speed up wartime decision-making. Lieutenant General Christian Freuding, Germany's army chief, shared insights gained from visits to Ukrainian command posts about integrating AI into military operations.

stories.title: Anger mounts in northern communities as Netanyahu urges residents stay put
stories.summary: Municipal leaders in northern Israel have criticized the government's response to relentless Hezbollah rocket attacks that are driving residents to flee. Prime Minister Netanyahu has urged local officials to discourage outward migration from the affected communities.

stories.title: Israelis set to lose even more sleep as clocks to move forward for daylight saving
stories.summary: Israel is set to move clocks forward one hour for daylight saving time, with 2 a.m. becoming 3 a.m. in the early hours of Friday. Daylight saving time is scheduled to end on October 25.

stories.title: Pakistan navigates shifting US-Iran dynamics amid ongoing war
stories.summary: Pakistan is emerging as a potential venue for US-Iran de-escalation talks amid the ongoing war, with CNN reporting Washington is actively exploring Islamabad as a meeting site. A 15-point US plan to end the war was reportedly delivered to Iran through Pakistani channels.

stories.title: Co-op boss Shirine Khoury-Haq to step down after difficult year for group
stories.summary: Co-op Group chief executive Shirine Khoury-Haq will step down on 29 March following a year marked by a cyber-security attack that contributed to a £125 million loss and allegations of a toxic workplace culture. Board member Kate Allum will serve as interim CEO while a permanent successor is sought.

stories.title: Tamtam: The Saudi pop star nurturing Saudi Arabia's music scene
stories.summary: Saudi pop singer Tamtam discussed her music career, identity, and return to Riyadh in an interview, reflecting on feminism, diaspora experiences, and creative freedom in Saudi Arabia's growing music scene.

stories.title: Video: Storms wash away vehicles and flood homes across Middle East
stories.summary: Severe storms swept across parts of the Middle East, washing away vehicles in Oman and flooding homes in Syria. The extreme weather caused widespread disruption across the region.

stories.title: Yale report ties Russian energy giants to kidnapping and military training of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: A Yale School of Public Health Humanitarian Research Lab report found that Russian energy companies Gazprom and Rosneft transported and indoctrinated at least 2,158 Ukrainian children at camps in Russia and occupied territories between 2022 and 2025.

stories.title: Pakistan says it is relaying messages between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar confirmed that Islamabad is relaying messages between the United States and Iran as part of indirect mediation efforts. Dar said Washington has presented 15 points that Iran is currently reviewing, with Turkey and Egypt also supporting the initiative.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Grants Speedy Hearing As Terror Suspects Admit Spying On U.S., Israeli Embassies
stories.summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria, granted an accelerated hearing in the trial of three terror suspects. The accused are charged with spying on U.S. and Israeli embassies in Nigeria on behalf of individuals linked to Iran.

stories.title: Trump to visit China in May after rescheduling trip due to Iran war
stories.summary: US President Trump confirmed a rescheduled visit to China in May to meet President Xi Jinping, delayed due to the Iran war. The White House Press Secretary indicated the administration estimated the war would last approximately four to six weeks.

stories.title: At least 24 killed as bus plunges into Padma river in Bangladesh; search on for missing
stories.summary: At least 24 people were killed when a bus plunged into the Padma River in Bangladesh's Rajbari district. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called local officials for updates and ordered an investigation into the accident, with search operations continuing for missing passengers.

stories.title: US activists work to connect Iranians via Elon Musk’s Starlink amid internet blackout
stories.summary: US digital activists are working to provide Iranians with internet access via Elon Musk's Starlink satellite service amid a government-imposed blackout. The activists' efforts date back to 2022, when mass protests erupted in Iran following the death of Mahsa Amini in custody.

stories.title: Niger: Boa Niger Suspends Dividend After Profit Collapse in 2025
stories.summary: Bank of Africa Niger (BOAN) announced it will not pay a dividend for the 2025 financial year following a sharp decline in earnings. The decision breaks several years of regular dividend distributions by the bank.

stories.title: Oil prices could hit $120 as war risks escalate, analyst warns
stories.summary: An analyst has warned that oil prices could reach $120 per barrel as risks from the ongoing Middle East conflict escalate. Prices are expected to remain elevated amid continued uncertainty over supply disruptions.

stories.title: Muzychuk explains how National Guard fire groups protect critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Approximately one thousand mobile and stationary fire groups of Ukraine's National Guard are tasked with protecting critical infrastructure. A National Guard official explained how these units respond to aerial threats across the country.

stories.title: 9 injured as Iran fires 6 missile salvos at Israel within hours, many with cluster warheads
stories.summary: Iran launched six missile salvos at Israel within a 24-hour period, some carrying cluster warheads, injuring at least nine people. Two people were killed by an intercepted missile in Abu Dhabi, and the Israeli Air Force conducted extensive retaliatory strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump lashes out at Nato, says it has done ‘nothing’ on Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized NATO allies on Truth Social, accusing them of doing "absolutely nothing" to assist with the situation involving Iran. He stated that the US needs nothing from the alliance.

stories.title: VW pulls Skoda brand from China after years of falling sales
stories.summary: Volkswagen announced it will withdraw its Skoda brand from mainland China following years of declining sales. The Czech automaker is realigning its global strategy to focus on growth markets including India and the ASEAN region, as international car brands continue losing ground in China's automotive market.

stories.title: Moldova court cases reveal Russia’s transnational network to recruit, train and deploy spies and saboteurs
stories.summary: Moldovan court cases have revealed a Russian-linked transnational network that recruited Moldovan citizens for drone training camps in the Balkans. The same recruiter also organized the painting of Stars of David on buildings in Paris following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks.

stories.title: Four injured in Tel Aviv by missile debris
stories.summary: Four people were wounded in Tel Aviv after shrapnel from an Iranian missile fell across the city, landing in at least six locations. Israeli media reported injuries and property damage from the debris.

stories.title: Italy's Meloni says to boost cooperation with Algeria on gas deliveries
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited Algeria on Wednesday and announced plans to boost cooperation on gas deliveries to Italy. Meloni and Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune agreed to collaborate on projects including shale gas extraction and offshore exploration.

stories.title: Dozens dead in Bangladesh as passenger bus plunges into Padma River
stories.summary: A passenger bus carrying approximately 40 people plunged into the Padma River in Bangladesh while attempting to board a ferry. Dozens were killed, including children.

stories.title: Two drone strikes on civilian targets kill 28 people in Sudan
stories.summary: At least 28 civilians were killed in two drone strikes in Sudan as the civil war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces nears its fourth year. One strike hit a market in Saraf Omra, North Darfur, killing 22 people including an infant, while another struck a truck carrying civilians in North Kordofan.

stories.title: France pays national tribute to former Prime Minister Lionel Jospin
stories.summary: France held a national tribute on Thursday for former Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who died on Sunday. President Emmanuel Macron led the ceremony honoring Jospin, who headed the "plural left" coalition government from 1997 to 2002.

stories.title: Iran says it is reviewing a U.S. ceasefire plan but no talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran is reviewing a US ceasefire plan but denied that any direct talks or negotiations with the United States have taken place. He confirmed that various messages had been exchanged through intermediaries.

stories.title: Israel, US diverging timelines on possible negotiation for end of war
stories.summary: A US plan to end the Middle East war was conveyed to Tehran through Pakistani mediators, but Iran rejected the proposal and put forward its own conditions. Despite these indirect diplomatic exchanges, Israel has continued large-scale military strikes against Iran.

stories.title: Colombia Hercules crash aftermath: political clash over causes intensifies days after tragedy
stories.summary: The crash of a Hercules C-130 military aircraft in Putumayo, Colombia, on March 23 killed 70 people and has triggered a political confrontation between President Gustavo Petro, military leadership, and the opposition. The dispute centers on the causes of the disaster and the state of Colombia's defence capabilities ahead of May 31 presidential elections.

stories.title: Hungary moves to restrict gas supplies to Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary has banned its gas transmission system operator from holding auctions for shipments to Ukraine in the third quarter, moving to wind down gas supplies. Hungary and Slovakia blame Kyiv for an outage on the Druzhba pipeline that carries Russian crude through Ukraine to their refineries.

stories.title: ‘Missile hit’ flips car in Israel
stories.summary: Surveillance footage from central Israel captured a car being flipped over by debris from an incoming rocket or missile strike. The incident highlighted the ongoing threat from projectile attacks on Israeli territory.

stories.title: WHO alarmed by health turmoil in Cuba
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Wednesday that Cuba's health situation is "deeply concerning" as a US fuel blockade worsens the island's energy crisis. He called for health to be protected from geopolitics, energy blockades, and power outages.

stories.title: South Africa: Mantashe Tells South Africans Not to Panic Over Fuel Shortages
stories.summary: South African Mineral Resources and Energy Minister Gwede Mantashe urged citizens not to panic over fuel shortages linked to the US-Israel-Iran war. Petrol and diesel prices are expected to rise sharply on April 1, with diesel set to increase by R9.50 per litre.

stories.title: Russians attack railway and port infrastructure at night
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukrainian railway and port infrastructure during the night. No casualties were reported in the strikes.

stories.title: Five weapons, 57 days: how Budapest escalated against Ukraine after one Russian drone strike
stories.summary: Tensions between Budapest and Kyiv escalated over 57 days following a Russian drone strike, with Hungary deploying five diplomatic or economic measures against Ukraine. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry noted that Hungarian gas imports have not stopped and that Kyiv has contingency plans prepared.

stories.title: UN adopts Ghana's slavery resolution, defying resistance from US, Israel
stories.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted a Ghana-proposed resolution recognizing transatlantic slavery as the "gravest crime against humanity" and calling for reparations. The non-binding resolution passed with 123 votes in favor, three opposed—including the US and Israel—and 52 abstentions, including EU members and Britain.

stories.title: Europe can’t rely on US for air-defense missiles, top EU official says
stories.summary: A top EU official, Kubilius, is conducting a "missile tour" across Europe to discuss air-defense missile production with manufacturers. The effort underscores concerns that Europe cannot rely on the United States for air-defense missile supplies and that the European Commission must support domestic production.

stories.title: Israeli judge closes case of Palestinian teen's death in prison
stories.summary: An Israeli judge closed the investigation into the death of a Palestinian teenager in Israeli prison, despite evidence suggesting starvation and an unclear cause of death. The decision has raised concerns about the treatment of Palestinian detainees.

stories.title: Strike kills IRGC Navy chief Tangsiri in Strait of Hormuz, Israeli official tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli sources confirmed the IDF carried out a strike that killed IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri in the Strait of Hormuz. Several of Tangsiri's top naval aides were also reported killed in the same attack.

stories.title: Residents injured after blast in Israeli home amid new Iranian barrage
stories.summary: Five people were injured after a blast struck a residential area in Kafr Qasim, central Israel, during a new Iranian missile and projectile barrage. Medics responded to the scene as fears of further Iranian strikes intensified.

stories.title: Ex-Taiwan presidential hopeful sentenced to 17 years for corruption
stories.summary: Former Taiwan presidential candidate Ko Wen-je was sentenced to 17 years in prison on corruption charges. His supporters had previously described the prosecution as politically motivated.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Broadband Demand May Spike By 2030
stories.summary: Nigeria's broadband demand is projected to grow significantly as the country's population is expected to reach 245 million by 2030. The forecast highlights increasing pressure on the country's telecommunications infrastructure.

stories.title: Australian growth forecasts slashed as global economy faces inflation spike
stories.summary: The OECD warned that the US-Israel war on Iran threatens a major global inflationary spike as soaring fuel prices endanger growth in European and Asian nations. Australian growth forecasts have been slashed, with economists expecting higher interest rates and inflation driven by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: G7 allies meet against backdrop of wars in Ukraine and Iran, with unpredictable US
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers are convening in Vaux-de-Cernay, France, amid ongoing wars in both Iran and Ukraine and growing unease over unpredictable US foreign policy. The meeting addresses economic uncertainty and the challenges of coordinating Western democratic responses to multiple simultaneous crises.

stories.title: OECD cuts eurozone growth outlook as war drives inflation
stories.summary: The OECD downgraded its eurozone growth forecast by 0.4 percentage points to 0.8 percent, citing rising energy prices and inflation driven by the Middle East war. Growth projections for Germany and France were each cut by 0.2 points.

stories.title: US links security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a Reuters interview that the United States is conditioning security guarantees on Ukraine relinquishing all of Donbas. The disclosure highlights a key point of contention in ongoing negotiations over Ukraine's future security framework.

stories.title: Middle East conflict will damage UK’s economy ‘more than any other’
stories.summary: The OECD warned that the Middle East conflict will hurt the UK economy more than any other industrialised nation, cutting its 2026 growth forecast from 1.2% to 0.7%. The organisation also cautioned about rising inflation linked to the regional instability.

stories.title: What can the Iran war tell China about missile interception?
stories.summary: A Chinese military magazine urged Beijing to develop an air-based missile interceptor system, citing lessons from the Iran war. The analysis highlighted how Iran's ballistic missiles posed severe challenges to Israel's existing midcourse and terminal-phase missile defence systems.

stories.title: Once a poor village boy, famous China educational guru Zhang Xuefeng dies at 41 after a run
stories.summary: Zhang Xuefeng, a prominent Chinese education influencer with over 30 million online followers, died on March 24 at age 41 after suffering cardiac arrest following a run. CCTV News reported he felt unwell after exercising and was rushed to the hospital, where doctors were unable to revive him.

stories.title: Help us reach our goal of 4,500 Seder boxes for Tel Aviv-Yafo families in need - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The Jaffa Institute is seeking support to provide 4,500 Seder boxes to underprivileged families in Tel Aviv-Yafo ahead of Passover.

stories.title: Bangladesh recovers 24 bodies after bus plunges into river
stories.summary: Rescue teams including navy divers recovered 24 bodies, including five children, from a bus that plunged into the Padma River at Goalanda, Bangladesh, about 65 km west of Dhaka. The bus sank on Wednesday with approximately 50 passengers on board; many managed to escape.

stories.title: Watch: Iran wants to make a deal ‘so badly, but they’re afraid to say it’: Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed Iran wants to reach a deal but is "afraid to say it," suggesting Iranian negotiators fear repercussions from their own government for engaging in talks.

stories.title: Ukraine terminates 116 agreements with Russia, Belarus, and CIS
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers terminated 116 international agreements previously concluded with Russia, Belarus, and within the Commonwealth of Independent States framework.

stories.title: Israel hinders repair of damaged water infra deepening Gaza’s health crisis
stories.summary: Palestinian engineers in Gaza are struggling to repair water infrastructure damaged by Israeli military operations. Contamination of the water system is deepening the health crisis facing Gaza's population.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso Leads the Way in Culturally Inspired Ai
stories.summary: Burkina Faso is integrating local languages into its artificial intelligence development as part of a push for digital sovereignty. The initiative positions the country as a leader in culturally inspired AI on the continent.

stories.title: Nigeria: Maiduguri Bombings Show New Threat to Civilians
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch called on Nigerian authorities to ensure civilian protection and investigate bombings in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno state. The attacks highlighted a new threat to civilians in the region.

stories.title: Two-nation theory
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses the severe poverty facing Pakistanis, noting the country's dependence on successive IMF programs and describing charitable food distribution as a national spectacle amid a bleak job market and rising costs.

stories.title: Amid US-Israel war, Iran football team trains in Turkiye before World Cup
stories.summary: Iran's national football team has traveled to Turkey for training and two friendly matches ahead of the FIFA World Cup, scheduled to be held in the US, Canada, and Mexico.

stories.title: Iran drafts law to impose tolls for transiting Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran is drafting legislation to impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes. The waterway has been largely closed to tanker traffic amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: ECOWAS appoints veteran diplomat to mediate with Sahel States
stories.summary: ECOWAS appointed former Guinean Prime Minister Lansana Kouyaté to mediate with Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso. The three Sahel states withdrew from the regional bloc last year, and Kouyaté is tasked with re-establishing dialogue.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in gunfight with Hezbollah terrorists in southern Lebanon, IDF says
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that 21-year-old Staff Sergeant Ori Greenberg of the Golani Brigade was killed in a gunfight with Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon. Another Israeli soldier was injured in the same engagement.

stories.title: Drone hits Russian oil tanker in Black Sea near Turkey
stories.summary: A drone struck a Russian oil tanker carrying crude in the Black Sea near the Bosphorus strait close to Turkey. The crew was reported safe after the explosion damaged the vessel, amid rising tensions in the region.

stories.title: Russia maintains high air activity over waters of Black Sea and Sea of Azov – Pletenschuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Pletenschuk reported that Russian forces continue high air activity over the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, maintaining persistent aerial operations in the region.

stories.title: Rising stakes
stories.summary: An editorial warns of the global economic impact of the ongoing Middle East war, particularly on Asia and Pakistan, highlighting surging fuel prices across benchmarks including Dubai crude and Murban and calling for an immediate end to hostilities.

stories.title: Ex-NSA leaders say Americans are becoming ‘numb’ to cyber threats
stories.summary: Former National Security Agency leaders warned that Americans are becoming desensitized to cybersecurity threats. One former NSA director said that serious cyberattacks have not prompted sufficiently strong policy responses or public awareness.

stories.title: Cathay to increase fuel surcharge for all flights by 34% from April
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways announced a 34 per cent increase in fuel surcharges for all flights starting in April, its second increase in two weeks. The airline cited rising jet fuel prices driven by the Middle East war, noting its fuel hedging measures were insufficient to offset costs.

stories.title: How much junk is in South China Sea? Beijing flexes surveillance muscle with survey
stories.summary: A Chinese survey estimated approximately 93 million pieces of debris are floating on the surface of the South China Sea. Using fixed-ship monitoring, underway surveys, and satellite remote sensing, marine scientists audited 26 locations in the central and southern portions of the disputed waters.

stories.title: Russian Lawmakers Headed to Washington for Meetings, State Department Says
stories.summary: A previously unreported “federal government delegation” will visit the U.S. Institute of Peace on Friday.

stories.title: Russian Lawmakers, Federal Officials Headed to Washington for Meetings, State Department Says
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department confirmed that a group of Russian lawmakers and federal officials is headed to Washington for meetings. The delegation plans to visit the U.S. Institute of Peace, in a previously unreported engagement.

stories.title: Gaza: Strike near Deir al‑Balāḥ tents kills at least one
stories.summary: An airstrike near tents in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, killed at least one person. Video from the scene showed an explosion triggering a fire as residents and medics rushed to assist the wounded.

stories.title: Turkey-operated tanker carrying Russian oil struck by naval drone in Black Sea
stories.summary: A crude oil tanker traveling from Russia's Novorossiysk port to Istanbul was struck by a naval drone near the Bosphorus strait on Thursday morning, according to Turkish Transportation Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu. The attack targeted the ship's engine room, but no injuries were reported.

stories.title: Pakistan steps in as Iran mediator while India watches from the wings
stories.summary: Pakistan has emerged as a backchannel mediator between Tehran and Washington as the Iran war reshapes West Asian geopolitics. India, despite growing partnerships with the US, Israel, and Gulf states, has been absent from meaningful conflict-resolution efforts regarding Iran.

stories.title: Iran says 87,000 civilian sites damaged in war
stories.summary: Iran's Red Crescent reported that more than 87,000 non-military sites have been damaged or destroyed across the country since the start of Israeli-US strikes. The organization described widespread harm to civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks Slobidskyi district of Kharkiv, injuries reported
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed-type drone struck the Slobidskyi district of Kharkiv on the morning of March 26, injuring one person. The attack is part of ongoing Russian drone strikes targeting Ukrainian urban areas.

stories.title: At the crossroads
stories.summary: An editorial examines two possible trajectories for the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran: either nascent ceasefire efforts, in which Pakistan is playing a key mediating role, succeed, or the conflict escalates further if the US moves additional troops into the region.

stories.title: China’s lidar giants pivot to robotics as Jensen Huang praises Chinese supply chain
stories.summary: Chinese lidar sensor manufacturers Hesai Group and RoboSense Technology are expanding into robotics products. Shanghai-based Hesai plans to invest 200 million yuan this year to design and manufacture sensor and actuator components for robots, seeking new growth as China strengthens its global robotics supply chain.

stories.title: Israel medics say Iranian missile attack leaves six wounded
stories.summary: Iranian missile attacks on Israel wounded six people and caused damage to homes, according to Israeli medics. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon has also escalated, with one Israeli soldier killed.

stories.title: Cuban president says Raul Castro involved in US talks amid oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel stated that former leader Raúl Castro is involved in ongoing talks with the United States. The discussions come amid rising tensions, including a US oil blockade and remarks by President Trump about taking over Cuba.

stories.title: New India bill to amend transgender rights sparks protests
stories.summary: India's government has introduced a bill that would amend the existing Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, altering how transgender individuals are legally recognised and their right to self-identify, prompting public protests.

stories.title: Singapore leader sees China helping small groups realise big results for Asia
stories.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said at the Boao Forum for Asia that China could lead plurilateral cooperation among smaller groups of like-minded Asian countries. He also suggested Beijing could spearhead AI governance efforts and play a larger role in promoting regional economic prosperity.

stories.title: Trump sets new China visit date as Iran war stokes economic risks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he would visit China on May 14–15 for a meeting with President Xi Jinping, after delaying the trip by about six weeks due to the Iran war. The revised schedule is one day shorter than the originally planned three-day visit starting March 31.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Joins Ghana, 121 Others Urging Reparations for Slavery's Historical Wrongs
stories.summary: Nigeria joined Ghana and 121 other UN member states in adopting a resolution declaring the transatlantic slave trade the gravest crime against humanity. The resolution calls for reparations for slavery's historical wrongs.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda to Withdraw Troops From Some Positions in Eastern DR Congo, Says Gen Muhoozi
stories.summary: Uganda announced plans to withdraw some of its troops deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Chief of Defence Forces General Muhoozi Kainerugaba confirmed the planned partial drawdown.

stories.title: War update: 158 clashes on front lines in past day
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 158 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines on Wednesday, March 25, reflecting continued high-intensity fighting across multiple sectors.

stories.title: ‘He will call me Mama’: The Gaza ‘grandmother’ raising an orphaned baby
stories.summary: A woman named Maha in Gaza adopted an infant named Hamza after an Israeli air strike killed his parents on the day he was born. She had previously been known as 'Grandmother' within her family.

stories.title: G7 meets in France to narrow transatlantic Iran split
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers convened near Paris to discuss Middle East tensions, the Ukraine war, and other global crises. The meeting aimed to bridge differences between European allies and the United States on Iran policy.

stories.title: Helium hitch: Why US-Israel war on Iran could cause MRI scan delays
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran is disrupting global helium supplies, which could lead to delays in MRI scans and affect other medical and industrial applications that depend on the gas.

stories.title: US embassy urges citizens to leave Iraq over attacks
stories.summary: The US embassy in Iraq issued a security alert warning of escalating attacks by Iran-aligned armed groups targeting American citizens and interests. The embassy urged US nationals to leave Iraq immediately, recommending overland travel via Jordan.

stories.title: US seeks Hamas ‘political surrender’ in new Gaza plan
stories.summary: The United States has proposed a new plan for Gaza that analysts describe as seeking Hamas's political surrender and disarmament. Critics say the proposal exploits the broader regional war to impose inequitable terms on Gaza.

stories.title: Ukraine intercepts 130 of 153 Russian drones in overnight attack – Air Force
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 130 of 153 drones launched by Russian forces in an overnight attack beginning the evening of March 25, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.

stories.title: Russian attacks kill two in Ukraine's Kharkiv, damage infrastructure on the Danube
stories.summary: Russian attacks killed two people in Ukraine's northeastern city of Kharkiv and its surrounding region. A separate strike on the Danube port of Izmail damaged port facilities and energy infrastructure, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war highlights: Israel strikes Tehran as Trump says U.S. negotiating to end war
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a new wave of attacks against locations in Israel, including Tel Aviv and Kiryat Shmona, as well as US military bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain. Meanwhile, Israel struck Tehran as President Trump said the US was negotiating to end the war.

stories.title: Israeli media claim IRGC naval commander killed
stories.summary: Israeli media outlets, including Channel 12 and Channel 14, reported that a senior commander in Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy was killed in Bandar Abbas. The commander was reportedly responsible for operations to close the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials have not confirmed the claim.

stories.title: Iran war: Why a Trump climbdown won’t save Asia’s economies
stories.summary: An analysis examines why a potential US de-escalation in the Iran war may not shield Asian economies from significant damage. The region's heavy dependence on energy imports and exports has left leading Asian economies highly vulnerable to the conflict's disruptions for a second consecutive year.

stories.title: Election Commission of Pakistan ‘fails’ to clarify anomaly in party-based LG poll mechanism in Punjab
stories.summary: Pakistan's Election Commission has not clarified how party-based local government elections will be conducted at the union council level in Punjab. PTI MPA Imtiaz Mahmood Sheikh sought clarification on the mechanism given that nine councillors must be elected from each constituency.

stories.title: Iraqi Kurdish commander says there are no plans to invade Iran
stories.summary: Peshmerga Major-General Sirwan Barzani stated that Iraqi Kurdish forces have no plans to invade Iran but expressed frustration over approximately 430 drone and missile attacks on the Kurdistan region of Iraq since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28.

stories.title: Man who opened fire on police in Odesa killed during arrest – National Police
stories.summary: A man who opened fire on patrol police officers in Odesa on March 25 was killed during a subsequent special operation to apprehend him, according to Ukraine's National Police.

stories.title: German minister calls Iran war an ‘economic catastrophe’
stories.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius described the ongoing war involving Iran as an "economic catastrophe," stating that its economic impact is "absolutely evident."

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in south Lebanon fighting
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that one of its soldiers was killed during operations in southern Lebanon. The death brings the total number of Israeli soldiers killed in southern Lebanon to three since Israel restarted its war on Lebanon on March 2.

stories.title: Next says Middle East conflict could add £15m to costs and push up prices
stories.summary: UK retailer Next warned that the Middle East conflict could add £15 million to its costs, assuming the war lasts three months. The company said it is currently offsetting higher fuel and air freight costs with savings elsewhere, but prices may rise if the conflict extends further.

stories.title: Oil slides 4pc amid fragile diplomacy signals
stories.summary: Oil prices fell approximately 4 percent after reports that the US sent Iran a 15-point ceasefire proposal, with Brent crude dropping to $100.53 and WTI to $88.78. Pakistan delivered the proposal, and either Pakistan or Turkey could host de-escalation discussions.

stories.title: Russia strikes injury 13 people in four oblasts of Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces wounded 13 people across Sumy, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, and Donetsk oblasts on March 25. Overnight, Russia launched 153 strike drones against Ukraine, of which 130 were destroyed by Ukrainian air defenses.

stories.title: Bondi terror attack took place amid global spike in foiled IS-inspired plots, researchers find
stories.summary: Research by the West Point Combating Terrorism Center found that the December 2024 Bondi beach shooting in Australia occurred amid a global spike in foiled Islamic State-inspired plots. Many of the plots targeted Western holiday events such as Christmas markets, following years of IS messaging urging followers to act independently.

stories.title: Men bailed over suspected arson attack on Jewish ambulance service in London
stories.summary: Two UK men, aged 47 and 45, were arrested and released on bail in connection with a suspected arson attack on four ambulances operated by a Jewish charity in Golders Green, north London. The Metropolitan Police said the pair were bailed until April while the investigation continues.

stories.title: Netanyahu knows what Tehran doesn’t: Trump is 'all in' on the war - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis suggests Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu believes President Trump is fully committed to the military campaign against Iran, a shift from past dynamics in which Israel largely confronted Iran alone and sought limited U.S. and European support mainly on the nuclear issue.

stories.title: Mexico races to clean crude from Veracruz coastline
stories.summary: Cleanup crews and Mexican navy personnel remained deployed along the Gulf coast in Veracruz and Tabasco on 26 March after crude oil polluted beaches. Authorities said 128 tonnes of contaminated waste had been removed, while the source of the spill remains under investigation.

stories.title: What is 'Saraya Awliya al-Dam' in Iraq?
stories.summary: Saraya Awliya al-Dam, an Iraqi militia group, has expanded its regional attacks amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran. The group operates within the broader network of Iran-aligned armed factions in Iraq.

stories.title: Pakistan Insti­tute of Legislative Development for regular civil-military consultations at National Security Committee level
stories.summary: Pakistan's Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency (Pildat) has called for institutionalizing the National Security Committee as a regular forum for civil-military consultation, recommending monthly meetings to review domestic and international security developments.

stories.title: As India and US seek to reset defence ties, Iran war threatens to be the wild card
stories.summary: A visit by US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby to New Delhi has raised expectations of strengthened US-India defence ties. However, analysts caution that the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran could complicate bilateral relations, particularly around India's energy and security concerns.

stories.title: Egypt curbs 'sedition' as debates on Iran war threatens GCC ties
stories.summary: Egyptian media regulatory authorities have issued rules for state-controlled and private media covering the Iran war, aiming to curb what officials describe as content that could provoke sedition and threaten ties with Gulf Cooperation Council member states.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it struck Israeli settlement
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced that it struck the northern Israeli town of Kiryat Shmona with missiles, marking a continuation of cross-border hostilities between the group and the Israeli military.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,210 troops, air defense system over past 24 hours – Ukraine's General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported that Russia lost approximately 1,210 troops killed or wounded in the past 24 hours, along with an air defense system. Total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022 have reached approximately 1,292,170 personnel.

stories.title: Fears net zero is ‘next Brexit’ as oil crisis fuels political climate divide
stories.summary: Rising energy costs from the Iran war are fueling a political divide over the UK's net zero emissions target. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, the Conservative party, and right-wing media are intensifying attacks on the 2050 net zero goal, while climate advocates fear the issue could become as politically divisive as Brexit.

stories.title: ‘Demand shock’: China cannot escape the impact of a long Iran war, analyst warns
stories.summary: An analyst at consultancy Roland Berger warned that China cannot fully escape the economic impact of a prolonged US-Israel war on Iran. While China may be more resilient than other countries, a demand shock from slowing economies in Southeast Asia and among regional partners would still pressure China's economy.

stories.title: Israeli push for more force ‘not working out very well’
stories.summary: Israeli public opinion reportedly favors increased use of military force against Iran, but observers note that the strategy of escalating force has not yielded the desired results so far.

stories.title: Israeli girl suffers cardiac arrest during sirens in Safed, hospitalized in serious condition
stories.summary: A young girl in the northern Israeli city of Safed suffered cardiac arrest after falling out of bed while trying to reach a shelter during sirens. United Hatzalah paramedics performed CPR using a defibrillator, and she was hospitalized in serious condition.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘afraid’ to admit it wants a deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said Iran is "afraid" to publicly admit it wants a deal, responding to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's statement that Tehran does not intend to negotiate with Washington.

stories.title: Trump pauses attacks on energy plants, says talks going 'well'
stories.summary: President Trump said he paused strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, claiming Iran had requested the halt. He described ongoing negotiations as going "well."

stories.title: Iran responding to proposal to end war as IRGC commander killed
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is reviewing a US proposal to end the conflict, while Israel announced it had assassinated a commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' navy.

stories.title: Trump warns will 'unleash hell' on Iran if it doesn't surrender
stories.summary: President Trump warned he would "unleash hell" on Iran if it does not surrender, accusing Tehran of being afraid to admit it is engaged in talks with the United States. The threats came as U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran continued.

stories.title: Nigeria: Women's Groups Ask 36 States Assemblies to Pass Reserve Seat Bill
stories.summary: Women's organisations across Nigeria have delivered formal letters to lawmakers in all 36 state assemblies demanding swift passage of the Special Seats for Women Bill. The bill would reserve legislative seats for women, and advocacy groups have intensified their campaign nationwide.

stories.title: Nigeria: CBN Bans Foreign Currency Payments for Diaspora Remittances From May 1
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has banned foreign currency payments for diaspora remittances effective May 1, 2026. International Money Transfer Operators must now route all transactions exclusively through designated naira settlement accounts held at Authorised Dealer Banks.

stories.title: Iraqi Kurdish commander says there are no plans to invade Iran
stories.summary: Peshmerga commander Sirwan Barzani, a senior Iraqi Kurdish military figure, stated there are no plans to invade Iran from the Kurdistan region of Iraq. He said Iran should not be targeting Kurdish bases in the area.

stories.title: Two teenagers killed in Shiraz, two dead in Abu Dhabi as Iran war expands
stories.summary: Two teenagers were killed in an attack in Shiraz, Iran, and two people died in Abu Dhabi as the conflict between Israel, the U.S., and Iran continues to expand. Israel announced strikes on Isfahan while Trump and Tehran debated ceasefire terms.

stories.title: OpenAI axes Sora video app in pivot to business tools
stories.summary: OpenAI announced it is shutting down Sora, its AI video generator, barely six months after launch, ending a potential $1 billion deal with Walt Disney Co. The company is pivoting toward business-focused AI tools ahead of a possible stock market debut.

stories.title: Israeli soldier killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army confirmed that 21-year-old Sergeant Uri Greenberg of the Golani Brigade was killed and two other soldiers were wounded during operations in southern Lebanon. Additional soldiers were evacuated from southern Lebanon for medical treatment.

stories.title: Gulf airspace closures leave Asia-to-Europe travellers stranded and bleeding cash
stories.summary: Airspace closures over the Persian Gulf due to the Iran conflict have left Asia-to-Europe travelers stranded and facing mounting costs. Most travel insurance policies exclude war-related disruptions, offering little relief to affected passengers.

stories.title: Drone targets Turkish-owned crude oil tanker in Black Sea
stories.summary: A crude oil tanker with 27 Turkish crew members was struck by a drone in the Black Sea after departing a Russian port carrying approximately one million barrels of oil. The Sierra Leone-flagged vessel is owned by Turkish firm Besiktas. No casualties were reported, according to Anadolu Agency.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kryvyi Rih, infrastructure site damaged
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih early on Thursday, March 26, damaging an infrastructure facility in the attack.

stories.title: Lebanon must not become next Gaza, says UN chief
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that Lebanon must not suffer the same devastation as Gaza, stating the wider Middle East war is "out of control." Israeli strikes killed nine more people in Beirut and southern Lebanon. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez condemned US-Israeli actions.

stories.title: Heritage sites at risk of landing on Unesco ‘danger list’
stories.summary: Two World Heritage sites at Mohra Moradu and Sirkap in Taxila, Pakistan, risk being placed on UNESCO's "danger list" after restoration work by Punjab's archaeology department allegedly compromised their authenticity. Officials from Pakistan's Department of Archaeology and Museums called the use of cement a serious violation.

stories.title: France is 'more and more keen' on Australia critical minerals investment, minister says
stories.summary: Australia's Resources Minister Madeleine King said France is increasingly interested in investing in Australian critical minerals projects. The announcement comes as countries worldwide compete to secure access to rare earths and other critical minerals essential for technology and energy transitions.

stories.title: Why it’s so hard to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Reopening the Strait of Hormuz remains a complex challenge due to Iran's geography, mobile weapons systems, and the risk of American military losses. The strategic waterway's closure continues to affect global energy markets.

stories.title: 10 Ukrainians Humbled Two NATO Battalions. When Will NATO Wake Up?
stories.summary: During NATO's Hedgehog 2025 exercise in the Baltics, 10 Ukrainian soldiers acting as an opposing force simulated the destruction of 17 armored vehicles and conducted 30 strikes in half a day, effectively neutralizing two NATO battalions. The exercise, conducted without US forces, highlighted significant gaps in NATO readiness.

stories.title: Israel removes two Iranian officials from hit-list, Pakistani officials says
stories.summary: Israel removed Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf from its target list at Pakistan's request, according to a Pakistani official. The U.S. reportedly urged Israel to stand down after Pakistan argued the two officials were essential for potential negotiations.

stories.title: No headway as Iran, US remain entrenched
stories.summary: Iran and the United States remain at an impasse over ceasefire efforts, with Washington claiming productive backchannel talks and Tehran insisting that exchanging messages through mediators does not constitute negotiation. Pakistan delivered a 15-point US proposal to Iran, which Tehran received coolly while setting five conditions for ending the war.

stories.title: Four Russian State Duma deputies charged over support for seizure of Ukrainian territories
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement charged four additional Russian State Duma deputies with encroaching on Ukraine's territorial integrity for their support of the seizure of Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims attack on Israel's Northern Command headquarter
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it targeted the Israeli army's Northern Command headquarters in the city of Safed with a missile barrage. Separately, several Israeli soldiers were evacuated from southern Lebanon for medical treatment.

stories.title: Hezbollah says negotiating with Israel would be surrender, amid strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah declared that negotiating with Israel would constitute surrender, as Israeli strikes continue on Lebanon. The group became involved in the broader Middle East conflict after firing rockets into Israel.

stories.title: Iran’s Civilizational Rhetoric Is Hollow
