stories.summary: An analysis argues that Iran's claims of pursuing a long-term civilizational strategy are contradicted by its actual policy decisions. The Islamic Republic's rhetoric about thinking in terms of centuries is characterized as hollow given its short-term actions.

stories.title: Fortnite tops ADL’s ‘leaderboard’ ranking video games on efforts to curb antisemitism
stories.summary: The Anti-Defamation League released a ranking of ten popular online video games based on their efforts to combat antisemitism. Fortnite received the top score, followed by Grand Theft Auto Online, Call of Duty, and Minecraft, with games evaluated on safety features, moderation, and hate-speech policies.

stories.title: A Torpedo in the Trade Lanes: Naval Warfare Returns to the Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: A US submarine sank the Iranian warship IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean approximately 40 nautical miles off Sri Lanka's southern coast. Sri Lankan Navy personnel rescued survivors, and the incident sparked debate over the legality of the strike and the nature of naval combat in busy maritime corridors.

stories.title: US comedian Seth Herzog apologises over ‘offensive’ BTS joke
stories.summary: Comedian Seth Herzog apologized after making a joke during a Tonight Show taping that was perceived as offensive to BTS and its fanbase. The remark, made while warming up the audience, drew backlash as the K-pop group prepared for a high-profile return to American television.

stories.title: Crude oil theft network busted in Tando Allahyar
stories.summary: Pakistan's Oil and Gas Development Company uncovered a major crude oil theft operation in Sindh's Tando Allahyar district, involving illegal tapping of the Kunnar Pasakhi Deep oil field pipeline near Tando Jam and an unlawful refinery processing stolen crude for local sale.

stories.title: PSL 11 set to start with Lahore-Hyderabad clash
stories.summary: The 11th edition of the HBL Pakistan Super League is set to open with defending champions Lahore Qalandars facing debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. The match will be held behind closed doors.

stories.title: 35 Pakistani institutions feature in QS university rankings
stories.summary: Thirty-five Pakistani universities were included in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026, with 31 public-sector and four private institutions represented. NUST and Quaid-i-Azam University led among public universities, while LUMS topped business schools and AKU led in medicine.

stories.title: Sirens blare across Israel as fourth Iranian barrage in two hours detected
stories.summary: A fourth salvo of Iranian missiles was detected heading toward central Israel within a two-hour period. Sirens were activated across multiple areas including central Israel, Jerusalem, and the coastal city of Ashdod.

stories.title: As Trump pushes for talks, US troop moves signal potential Iran war escalation
stories.summary: The US has ordered thousands of additional troops to the Middle East even as President Trump publicly pushes for negotiations to end the Iran war. Iran has rejected Trump's diplomatic outreach and threatened massive retaliation if US ground forces are deployed.

stories.title: Starmer authorizes military to interdict Russian shadow fleet vessels in UK waters
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer authorized British military personnel to interdict vessels belonging to Russia's shadow fleet operating in UK waters, as part of broader efforts to increase pressure on the Putin regime.

stories.title: Two killed in Abu Dhabi, UAE media office says
stories.summary: The UAE media office confirmed that two people were killed in Abu Dhabi as a result of missile interception operations during recent Iranian attacks on the region.

stories.title: How South Korea Can Bring Iron to the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States has begun redeploying THAAD missile defense systems and Patriot batteries from South Korea to the Middle East amid the Iran conflict. The redeployment raises concerns about South Korea's defense posture and the need for Seoul to strengthen its own capabilities to fill the gap.

stories.title: Pepys ‘curated’ letters to conceal being offered enslaved boy as bribe – research
stories.summary: New research by Cambridge University historian Dr. Michael Edwards reveals that 17th-century diarist Samuel Pepys deliberately curated and erased correspondence to conceal that he had been offered an enslaved boy as a bribe. Pepys served as a naval official in the 1670s.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran: What’s happening on day 27 of attacks?
stories.summary: On day 27 of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, attacks have intensified. President Trump reiterated claims that Iranian leaders want to negotiate a deal, though Tehran has publicly denied any ongoing talks.

stories.title: Kharkiv region deputy sentenced to seven years for deporting Ukrainians to Russia
stories.summary: A deputy of the Kupiansk District Council in Ukraine's Kharkiv region was sentenced to seven years in prison with property confiscation for collaborating with Russian occupiers and organizing the deportation of Ukrainian civilians to Russia.

stories.title: Auction clearance rate slumps to 57% nationwide as interest rate hikes prompt Australians to sell
stories.summary: Australia's national auction clearance rate fell to about 57%, the lowest in 2025, as interest rate hikes and Iran war-linked price rises weigh on homebuyer confidence. Sydney's clearance rate dropped to 55%, with the number of properties for sale reaching levels not seen since 2021.

stories.title: India's fertiliser supplies under strain as war disrupts shipments
stories.summary: India's fertiliser supply chain is under pressure as the ongoing war disrupts shipping routes. Analysts indicate that current stocks should cover the upcoming sowing season but warn of potential shortages if the conflict continues.

stories.title: Thursday briefing: Why ​most Israelis ​back the ​conflict​ with Iran, even as international support wanes
stories.summary: Polling shows more than 90% of Jewish Israelis support the ongoing conflict with Iran, even as at least 15 people have been killed and hundreds injured by Iranian missiles since the war began in February. International support for Israel's actions has waned, exposing widening fractures between Israel and its allies.

stories.title: As Iran war rages, China links peace to economic growth at Boao Forum
stories.summary: At the Boao Forum for Asia, China's top legislator Zhao Leji called for rejecting power politics in favor of economic development and resolving conflicts through negotiation. The statement came as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to destabilize the region.

stories.title: Hezbollah targets seven Israeli army tanks in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it targeted a total of seven Israeli army tanks in the Qantara area of southern Lebanon, including a Merkava tank. The strikes are part of ongoing retaliation as the Israeli military conducts a ground invasion pushing deeper into Lebanese territory.

stories.title: UK authorises military to board Russian shadow fleet tankers
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer authorized the UK military to board and detain Russian ships suspected of belonging to Moscow's shadow fleet. The vessels are alleged to enable Russian oil exports in violation of Western sanctions.

stories.title: Third Iranian attack detected in Israel
stories.summary: Sirens sounded across Israel as a third wave of Iranian attacks was detected within approximately ninety minutes, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Football : France and Brazil face off in a World Cup-style friendly
stories.summary: France and Brazil are set to play a World Cup-style friendly as a final warm-up before the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the US, Mexico, and Canada. Brazil faces several squad absences, while France, the World Cup runners-up, topped their qualifying group, and Kylian Mbappé could become France's all-time leading scorer.

stories.title: Deaths and debts: Missiles in Gulf shake millions of South Asian families
stories.summary: South Asian nationals make up the majority of those killed in Iranian attacks targeting Gulf states. The violence has rattled economies in South Asian countries that depend heavily on remittances from workers in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Russian attack damages port and energy infrastructure in Izmail district
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Izmail district in Ukraine's Odesa region, damaging port and energy infrastructure at two locations.

stories.title: 50 years after the Dirty War, Argentinians remember the Jews who ‘disappeared’
stories.summary: Fifty years after Argentina's Dirty War, communities are remembering the estimated 1,900 Jewish victims who were abducted, tortured, and murdered by the military junta. As many as 30,000 people total are believed to have disappeared during the conflict.

stories.title: Iran's Foreign Minister says no talks have taken place with US
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated on state television that no negotiations have taken place with the United States and that Iran's policy remains one of continued resistance. His remarks came after President Trump claimed Washington had proposed a peace plan.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Expands Security Ties Amid Insurgency
stories.summary: Nigeria is broadening its security partnerships in response to rising extremist threats. The country has strengthened cooperation with France, continued receiving US military support, and renewed engagement with European Union leaders to address its ongoing insurgency challenges.

stories.title: Iran war deflects attention from Ukraine as Russia starts spring offensive
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran has diverted global attention from Russia's invasion of Ukraine, now in its fifth year. Russia launched nearly 1,000 drones and 34 missiles at Ukraine in one of the war's largest bombardments, while Ukraine responded with almost 400 drones targeting Russian territory.

stories.title: In one of country's poorest states, Venezuelans hope for post-Maduro boom
stories.summary: In Venezuela's Sucre state, one of the country's poorest regions, residents are hoping for an economic recovery following the potential end of the Maduro era. A lack of long-term investment has severely hampered local livelihoods and development prospects.

stories.title: Egypt ready to host meetings related to de-escalating Iran war, says FM
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty announced that Egypt is prepared to host meetings aimed at de-escalating the Iran war. He said Egyptian mediation between Iran and the U.S. continues in cooperation with Pakistan and Turkey, advocating for a resolution based on mutual benefit.

stories.title: Iran fortifying Kharg Island in preparation for potential US attack - report
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly fortifying Kharg Island, its primary oil export hub, in preparation for a potential US attack. US officials and military experts have warned of significant risks associated with a ground invasion of the island.

stories.title: 50 years after the Dirty War, Argentine Jews remember the ‘disappeared’ from their community
stories.summary: Fifty years after Argentina's Dirty War, educational initiatives are highlighting the disproportionate number of Jewish victims who were abducted, tortured, and murdered by the military junta. Government forces were accused of antisemitic targeting during the repression.

stories.title: Charity Commission warns Alan Turing Institute of its legal duties after complaints
stories.summary: The UK Charity Commission issued formal regulatory guidance to the Alan Turing Institute's board of trustees after receiving whistleblower complaints from staff. The watchdog reminded trustees of their legal duties regarding financial oversight and management of organisational change at the leading AI research institute.

stories.title: China woman lives in nursing home, pays US$30 rent by providing companionship to residents
stories.summary: A 25-year-old Chinese woman named Zhang Jin lives in a nursing home in Suzhou, Jiangsu province, paying just 200 yuan (US$30) per month in rent by providing companionship to elderly residents. The arrangement reflects a growing trend among young Chinese seeking affordable living while addressing the country's aging population challenge.

stories.title: US-Israeli attack targets residential area in Bandar Abbas
stories.summary: The governor of Hormozgan province in southern Iran said a U.S.-Israeli attack struck a residential area in Bandar Abbas. Earlier, two teenage boys were reportedly killed in a similar strike in Shiraz.

stories.title: ‘No negotiations’ says Iran FM as US touts peace plan
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister stated that no negotiations with the United States are taking place, even as Washington promoted a peace plan. Violence on the ground continued unabated after nearly four weeks of conflict.

stories.title: West Bank extremist violence is eroding Israel's national security from within - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial addressed extremist settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, arguing that such acts undermine Israel's national security from within.

stories.title: Trump defends Iran war amid economic fallout, backlash from Republican lawmakers
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump defended the war on Iran amid growing economic concerns and pushback from Republican lawmakers, some of whom expressed opposition during a briefing on a potential ground invasion.

stories.title: Australia bans Iranian tourists with valid visas for six months
stories.summary: Australia has banned Iranian tourists holding valid visas from entering the country for six months. The move followed Iranian footballers being granted asylum, and critics have called it a "moral failure."

stories.title: Netanyahu boasts about ‘breaking boundaries in every sense of the word’
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel is working to expand its buffer zone along its border with Lebanon.

stories.title: UN designates African slave trade as ‘gravest crime against humanity’
stories.summary: The UN General Assembly voted 123 to 3, with 52 abstentions, to designate the transatlantic African slave trade as "the gravest crime against humanity." The US, Israel, and Argentina opposed the resolution, while Britain and EU member states abstained. Ghana's president supported the measure.

stories.title: South Africa: Cape Town Gang Violence Intensifies - South African News Briefs - March 26, 2026
stories.summary: Gang violence has intensified in Cape Town, South Africa, according to reports from March 2026. Specific details on casualties or operational responses were not provided in the available source material.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump insists Iran wants a deal despite initial rejection; China sees ‘glimmer of hope’ for talks
stories.summary: Donald Trump insisted Iran wants a deal despite Tehran's initial rejection of a US ceasefire plan, while China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said he sees a "glimmer of hope" for negotiations. Qatar publicly distanced itself from alleged mediation efforts, and Iran submitted its own counter-proposal amid ongoing diplomatic push.

stories.title: Reports of injuries in Israel as second Iranian salvo detected in past 20 minutes
stories.summary: Israel's military detected a second salvo of Iranian missiles within approximately 20 minutes. Sirens sounded across central Israel and Jerusalem, and search-and-rescue teams responded to reports of injuries and infrastructure damage in the Petah Tikva and Kfar Qasim areas.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan Calls for Exceptional Support to Conflict-Affected Countries Within 2026-2029 International Cooperation Strategy
stories.summary: At a Geneva meeting on March 25, 2026, Sudan called for flexible and exceptional approaches within the 2026–2029 international development cooperation strategy. Sudanese representatives urged that conflict- and disaster-affected countries receive tailored support for recovery, reconstruction, and labor market stimulation.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Cabinet Fires Prisons Chief Amid Political Fall-Out With Southwest State
stories.summary: Somalia's cabinet met in Mogadishu and dismissed the country's prisons chief amid a political dispute with Southwest State. The session also focused on security matters and intensifying operations against Al-Shabaab.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: 15 Zimbabweans Killed in Russia-Ukraine War After Being Duped Into Foreign Military Recruitment
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's Information Minister Soda Zhemu revealed that at least 15 Zimbabwean citizens have died fighting in the Russia-Ukraine war after being lured into foreign military service through suspected human trafficking networks.

stories.title: Sirens sound in central Israel and Jerusalem after Iranian attacks detected
stories.summary: The Israeli military said its air defenses were responding to missiles launched from Iran, with sirens activated across central Israel, parts of Jerusalem, and the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Two people killed in Abu Dhabi in latest Iranian attack
stories.summary: Two people were killed in Abu Dhabi in the latest Iranian attack on the UAE. The strikes followed Iran's refusal to accept a ceasefire proposal put forward by U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Oil prices rise higher as Iran denies US talks, dimming deescalation hopes
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices rose above $104 per barrel after Iran denied participating in talks with the United States, reducing hopes for a diplomatic de-escalation in the conflict.

stories.title: US airport wait times longest in history after hundreds of unpaid officers leave
stories.summary: The US Transportation Security Administration reported the longest airport wait times in its history, with some exceeding 4.5 hours, after more than 480 officers left due to a Department of Homeland Security funding shutdown causing severe staffing shortages nationwide.

stories.title: Gulf states’ scepticism over alleged US-Iran talks signals a distrust of Trump
stories.summary: Qatar publicly distanced itself from alleged US-Iran ceasefire talks shortly after President Trump claimed "strong talks" were underway to end the war. Gulf states' reluctance to endorse the reported negotiations reflects broader suspicion that US peace rhetoric may serve as cover for further military escalation.

stories.title: EU healthcare workers say they ‘refuse to be instruments’ in deportation plans
stories.summary: More than 1,100 healthcare professionals across Europe have urged MEPs to reject proposed measures aimed at increasing deportation of undocumented people. The workers warn the plans could transform hospitals into immigration enforcement sites, creating a "climate of fear" that deters people from seeking medical care.

stories.title: WHO warns of health crisis ‘unfolding in real time’ across Middle East
stories.summary: The WHO's regional director for the Eastern Mediterranean, Dr. Hanan Balkhy, called for a total stop to hostilities in the Middle East to halt what she described as a "health crisis unfolding in real time." She urged that hospitals and healthcare facilities be treated as safe havens throughout the conflict.

stories.title: Explosion at Hong Kong recycling yard injures 2
stories.summary: An explosion at a recycling yard at the intersection of Ting Kok Road and Fung Yuen Road in Tai Po, northern Hong Kong, injured two people. Online footage showed large flames and black smoke following the blast.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Woman Arrested for Child Brutality After Forcing Minor to Touch Burning Gas Stove in Viral Video
stories.summary: Police in Harare, Zimbabwe, arrested a woman after a viral video showed her forcing her son to touch a burning gas stove. The child was allegedly punished for stealing from a local tuck shop.

stories.title: Ousted Homeland Security chief Noem begins new envoy role with tour
stories.summary: Former U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem began a tour of Western Hemisphere nations in her new role as envoy to an anti-drug-cartel coalition. She was fired by President Trump earlier in March.

stories.title: UAE responding to attacks from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Defence said it was responding to incoming missile and drone threats from Iran, stating that sounds heard across the country resulted from air defense systems intercepting the attacks.

stories.title: Philippines suspends electricity market due to war on Iran
stories.summary: The Philippines' energy market regulator suspended the wholesale electricity spot market across all three national grids until further notice, citing fuel supply risks and price volatility caused by the war on Iran.

stories.title: Malaysia’s prime minister says Iran talks should end war
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim stated that any negotiations with Iran should be aimed at ending the ongoing war.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires missiles at central Israel; 2 soldiers seriously hurt in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired missiles at central Israel, with the Israeli military saying the projectiles were intercepted. Two Israeli soldiers were seriously wounded in Lebanon, and a woman was moderately injured while seeking shelter during the attack.

stories.title: Nigeria: U.S. Troops in Nigeria to Help Fight Terrorism Could End Up Making It Worse - Analyst
stories.summary: An analyst warns that the recent deployment of US troops in Nigeria to assist with counterterrorism efforts could worsen the country's security situation rather than improve it.

stories.title: Man dies after getting electric shock from lamp post near Lantau beach
stories.summary: A 57-year-old man surnamed Chan died after receiving an electric shock from a lamp post near a beach on Lantau Island, Hong Kong. Staff at a nearby resort said the lamp post had not been inspected for 10 years.

stories.title: 'We are being choked': Philippines transport workers strike over fuel costs
stories.summary: Transport workers in the Philippines have gone on strike over rising fuel costs, saying they can no longer cope financially. The Philippine government has declared a national energy emergency in response to the crisis.

stories.title: Kuleba outlines elements of Ukraine’s energy resilience plans
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba outlined plans to strengthen the country's energy resilience by making critical infrastructure protection measures systemic, noting that significant investment will be required.

stories.title: Iran wants Lebanon included in any ceasefire, sources say
stories.summary: Iran has communicated through intermediaries that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement with the United States and Israel, linking a halt to the broader conflict to an end of Israel's offensive against Hezbollah.

stories.title: War on Iran 'catastrophe' for global economy, German defence minster says
stories.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called the war on Iran a "catastrophe for the world's economies" during remarks at Australia's Parliament House in Canberra. He stated that European countries were not consulted before the conflict began and expressed opposition to being drawn into it.

stories.title: China opens world’s largest ship data set that could be used to train drones
stories.summary: A Chinese military research team released the DMSD data set, described as the world's largest publicly available visible light-infrared ship detection data set. It contains over 2,000 paired images and nearly 20,000 annotated instances that could be used to train drones and maritime surveillance systems.

stories.title: The Age of Asymmetric Warfare Is Here, and the West Is Not Ready
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the era of asymmetric warfare has arrived, with Ukraine's experience offering key lessons for the United States on drone defense. The assessment suggests Western militaries are not adequately prepared for the evolving nature of modern conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy says US has linked security guarantees to ceding of Donbas
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters that the US is conditioning security guarantees on Ukraine ceding the entire eastern Donbas region to Russia. Zelenskyy said the Middle East conflict has diverted President Trump's attention, leading to increased US pressure on Kyiv to accept a quick resolution to the war.

stories.title: Videos show wave of missiles fired from Lebanon to Israel
stories.summary: Videos circulating online showed rocket interceptions over central Israel, depicting missiles fired from Lebanon being engaged by air defenses.

stories.title: 'Why is this war different from all other wars?': Eretz Nehederet celebrates Passover amid Iran war
stories.summary: The Israeli satirical show Eretz Nehederet aired a Passover-themed episode referencing the Iran war, featuring a parody of the Dayenu song with Prime Minister Netanyahu singing about toppling the government and removing the nuclear threat.

stories.title: The Army wants to use bullets, mortars, and artillery rounds to take out small drones
stories.summary: The US Army is exploring ways to use existing kinetic munitions — including bullets, mortars, and artillery rounds — to counter small drone threats. The effort focuses on adapting current weapons systems to engage tiny, hard-to-target unmanned aerial vehicles on the battlefield.

stories.title: Support for Ukraine to be one of key topics at G7 foreign ministers meeting in France
stories.summary: G7 foreign ministers are set to meet in France on March 26–27, with support for Ukraine expected to be a central topic of discussion among the seven nations.

stories.title: Russia slams second US-Israeli strike at Iran’s Bushehr nuclear reactor
stories.summary: Russia's foreign ministry condemned a second US-Israeli strike on Iran's Bushehr nuclear reactor, accusing the two countries of risking a nuclear disaster at the site.

stories.title: Australia bans visitors from Iran amid war in the Middle East
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs Department announced a ban on visitors from Iran, citing the ongoing war in the Middle East and describing the measure as being in the national interest.

stories.title: UAE oil company CEO says Iran curbs on Strait Hormuz 'economic terrorism'
stories.summary: ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber described Iran's restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz as "economic terrorism" during a speech in the United States, warning that the curbs were destabilizing the global economy.

stories.title: Trump, fearing slaughter, said to reject Netanyahu’s proposal to jointly call for Iranian uprising
stories.summary: Reports indicate that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu asked President Trump to jointly call for an Iranian uprising after Israel killed senior Iranian officials. Trump reportedly declined out of concern that Iranian protesters would face a violent crackdown; Netanyahu later issued the call independently.

stories.title: Report: Trump wants to avoid prolonged war in Iran
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that US President Donald Trump told associates he wants to avoid a prolonged war in Iran and hopes to bring the conflict to an end within weeks, privately telling advisors he believes the war is in its final stages.

stories.title: 16 dead after bus plunges into river in Bangladesh, search on for missing
stories.summary: At least 16 people died after a bus plunged into a river in Bangladesh. Fire service and coastguard divers, assisted by military and police, continued searching for missing passengers.

stories.title: Live: Israel carries out fresh wave of strikes across Iran
stories.summary: Israel's military announced it carried out a fresh wave of strikes across Iran on Thursday as Tehran continues to reject negotiations on a peace deal. US President Donald Trump warned he is ready to "unleash hell" if Iran does not accept terms to end the nearly four-week-old Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Kuwait intercepts drones as authorities struggle to put out fire at airport
stories.summary: Kuwait's National Guard shot down two drones after alarms sounded across the country. Authorities continued to battle a fire at Kuwait International Airport caused by two drones that struck a fuel tank at the site roughly 24 hours earlier.

stories.title: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell to stand trial after allegedly leading attack on Melbourne Indigenous camp
stories.summary: Neo-Nazi figure Thomas Sewell, 33, has been committed to stand trial in Melbourne after pleading not guilty to five charges related to an alleged group assault on Camp Sovereignty, an Indigenous protest site. Sewell appeared via video link at Melbourne magistrates court on Thursday.

stories.title: China’s weight-loss drug makers take on global giants as Novo Nordisk patent expires
stories.summary: At least ten weight-loss drugs are seeking regulatory approval in China after Novo Nordisk's semaglutide lost patent protection there on March 20. The Chinese market for such therapies is projected to reach roughly US$14 billion by 2030, intensifying competition among domestic drugmakers and global pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Contractor failed to supervise smoking workers, residents say in Tai Po fire hearing
stories.summary: A public evidential hearing into a fire that killed 168 people at Wang Fuk Court estate in Tai Po, Hong Kong, has entered its fourth day. Residents testified that rubbish was piled outside the building where the blaze started, and alleged that the contractor failed to supervise workers who were smoking on site.

stories.title: Israeli military says it carried out 'wide-scale' strikes in Iran
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced on Thursday that it had completed a "wide-scale wave of strikes" across Iran.

stories.title: Malaysia moves to tighten rules for expats, raising fears of talent flight
stories.summary: Malaysia's government announced plans to reduce the number of foreign workers in the country to promote local hiring and raise domestic incomes, sparking concerns about a potential exodus of skilled expatriates.

stories.title: Lubinets: Russia holds 26 Ukrainian media workers in captivity, Red Cross confirms detention of only one
stories.summary: Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets reported that Russia is unlawfully holding 26 Ukrainian journalists and media workers. The International Committee of the Red Cross has officially confirmed the detention of only one of them.

stories.title: Russia sought to blackmail US using intelligence to Iran, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia attempted to blackmail the United States by offering to stop sharing military intelligence with Iran in exchange for Washington cutting off intelligence support to Ukraine.

stories.title: Australia bans visitors from Iran for 6 months amid war
stories.summary: Australia has imposed a six-month ban on visitors from Iran, citing concerns that Iranian nationals may overstay their visas due to the ongoing war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Euro, Chinese yuan to end US dollar dominance, top economist says
stories.summary: Harvard economist Kenneth Rogoff, a former IMF chief economist, argues that the US dollar faces a growing crisis of legitimacy. He suggests the euro and Chinese yuan could eventually challenge dollar dominance, a thesis elaborated in his book Our Dollar, Your Problem, published in May last year.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz says Ukraine no longer needs its Taurus missiles
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that Ukraine no longer needs Germany's Taurus cruise missiles. He cited Ukraine's progress in developing its own domestic weapons as rendering the long-running Taurus debate moot.

stories.title: Iran announces launch of 82nd wave of attacks
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it launched new assaults under Operation "True Promise 4," targeting US facilities and equipment in the region, marking the 82nd wave of attacks in the campaign.

stories.title: US links security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters that the United States has conditioned its offer of security guarantees for a peace deal on Kyiv ceding the entire eastern Donbas region to Russia.

stories.title: Trump reschedules Iran-delayed China visit for May 14-15
stories.summary: President Donald Trump rescheduled his postponed visit to China for May 14–15 in Beijing, after delays caused by the Iran conflict. Trump also said he would host Chinese President Xi Jinping for a reciprocal visit in Washington.

stories.title: Trump to hit Iran harder if Tehran does not accept defeat, White House says
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said President Trump would intensify strikes on Iran if Tehran does not accept that it has been "defeated militarily."

stories.title: Enact special law to send Japan’s warships to secure Hormuz, ex-adviser tells Takaichi
stories.summary: Former Japanese national security adviser Akihisa Nagashima has urged Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to enact a special measures law enabling Japan to send warships to help secure the Strait of Hormuz jointly with other nations. The proposal would go beyond Japan's previous military contributions in geopolitical conflicts, even before a ceasefire is reached.

stories.title: Iraqi groups claims 23 operations over the past day
stories.summary: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed its fighters carried out 23 operations over the past 24 hours, targeting what it described as enemy bases throughout Iraq and the broader region.

stories.title: Netanyahu's political advisor doubtful of Iran's willingness to negotiate
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political advisor Ophir Falk questioned Iran's willingness to negotiate in a CNN interview, calling Tehran's statements unreliable and outlining regime removal as a potential path to eliminating what Israel views as an existential threat.

stories.title: ABC boss’s ‘utterly offensive’ comments condemned as broadcaster comes back online after strike
stories.summary: ABC staff and union representatives in Australia have condemned managing director Hugh Marks's description of a 24-hour strike as staff "playing games," calling the comments "utterly offensive." More than 2,000 ABC employees walked off the job on Wednesday before the broadcaster resumed operations.

stories.title: Is Trump any closer to an Iran exit strategy?
stories.summary: The White House maintains President Trump is leading U.S. policy on Iran, but some Republican lawmakers have expressed frustration over inconsistent messaging regarding the administration's war aims and exit strategy.

stories.title: Maduro faces New York court in key hearing over legal defense
stories.summary: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores appeared before the Southern District Court of New York on March 26 for a second hearing in their criminal case. Maduro was captured in January during a US military operation and faces multiple charges including drug trafficking.

stories.title: Uganda 'on the side of Israel' amid Iran war, defense chief says
stories.summary: Uganda's Chief of Defense Forces General Muhoozi Kainerugaba expressed support for Israel amid the war with Iran, stating in social media posts that Israel has a right to exist and that attacks against it must stop.

stories.title: In Lebanon, paramedics mourn their own killed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: In the southern Lebanese town of Nabatieh, paramedics gathered to mourn and bury two colleagues killed in an Israeli strike. The emotional ceremony highlighted the toll the conflict is taking on emergency medical responders in Lebanon.

stories.title: Rodríguez promises "legal certainty" to investors while Machado competes for attention from Texas
stories.summary: Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodríguez addressed American, Saudi, and Latin American investors via videoconference at the FII Priority investment forum in Miami. She assured attendees that her government is advancing reforms to guarantee legal certainty for investments in the country.

stories.title: Harrison: ‘There is going to be some kind of a military escalation.’
stories.summary: Analyst Ross Harrison argued that public diplomatic rhetoric between the United States and Iran is masking hardline positions on both sides, and predicted some form of military escalation ahead.

stories.title: Iran’s ‘Tehran toll booth’: Legally risky route for shippers through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran is charging vessels for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, with at least one vetted ship reportedly paying $2 million to use the corridor. The arrangement poses legal risks for shippers navigating the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Ousted Venezuelan president Maduro to appear in New York court
stories.summary: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in a New York court on Thursday for the second time since his capture by US forces in January. He faces multiple charges including drug trafficking and weapons offences, while his legal team challenges procedural obstacles related to US sanctions.

stories.title: Trump: Iran wants deal ‘so badly’; White House says campaign ‘very close’ to meeting goals
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran wants a deal "so badly," while the White House indicated the military campaign was close to meeting its goals. Tehran reportedly told mediators that any ceasefire must include an end to Israel-Hezbollah hostilities, and two senior Iranian officials were temporarily removed from a US-Israeli target list.

stories.title: Trump confirms May meeting with Xi Jinping as Iran war forces postponement
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump confirmed a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping scheduled for May, which was postponed due to the ongoing Iran war. It would be the first US presidential visit to China since 2017.

stories.title: Ukraine-US fund approves first investment, in navigation tech producer
stories.summary: The Ukraine-U.S. investment fund, established under the minerals deal signed in April 2025, approved its first investment in a navigation technology producer.

stories.title: NATO commander says allies must urgently rethink defence
stories.summary: A senior NATO commander urged allied nations to urgently rethink their defense strategies. He specifically highlighted the need to counter the mass production of drones by Russia and Iran.

stories.title: Chinese satellite performs landmark refuelling test in low Earth orbit
stories.summary: A Chinese commercial satellite, Hukeda-2 (also called Yuxing-3 06), completed a refuelling test in low Earth orbit using a flexible robotic arm described as resembling an octopus tentacle. The demonstration satellite launched from Jiuquan in Gansu province and conducted compliance control and refuelling experiments, advancing in-orbit servicing capabilities.

stories.title: Life in Iran illustrates shifting realities amid US-Israel war
stories.summary: A resident of eastern Tehran describes the immediate impact of the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, including an explosion that shattered windows in their home. Despite the proximity of strikes and the sound of jets overhead, daily life in the Iranian capital has continued with a degree of normalcy amid the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine shares experience on energy infrastructure resilience with EU – Kuleba
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba stated that Ukraine is prepared to share its experience in protecting energy infrastructure with the European Union, citing new security challenges from hybrid and military threats facing Europe's energy systems.

stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln operations ongoing following Iranian targeting
stories.summary: The US Central Command said the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln continued operations against military targets in Iran while sailing in regional waters. Iran's military had earlier claimed it targeted the carrier with naval cruise missiles.

stories.title: Tehran issues warning to regional neighbour if Iranian island occupied
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker issued a warning to a regional neighbor over the potential occupation of an Iranian island, as the US administration continued deploying additional troops to the region.

stories.title: UN needs more funds to help people displaced by Mideast war, refugee chief says
stories.summary: UN refugee chief Filippo Grandi urged donors in Brussels to increase funding for humanitarian operations related to the widening Middle East war. He said the agency had received less than 10% of the funds needed to assist displaced populations.

stories.title: Why China’s humanoid robots are still waiting for their ‘ChatGPT moment’
stories.summary: Experts at the Boao Forum for Asia in Hainan said China's humanoid robots remain years away from a breakthrough "ChatGPT moment" of widespread usability. Persistent challenges in task adaptability, training efficiency, and unresolved hardware and software limitations continue to prevent large-scale deployment of the technology.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts more drones east of the country
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's defence ministry announced it intercepted and destroyed eight drones in the kingdom's eastern region.

stories.title: ‘Worst industrial crisis in living memory’: Commerce chamber chief’s warning over Iran war
stories.summary: International Chamber of Commerce chief John Denton warned of the worst industrial crisis in living memory as the Iran conflict's economic effects spread to businesses globally.

stories.title: Singapore’s green fuel levy on air travellers delayed over Iran war
stories.summary: Singapore's Civil Aviation Authority announced it is delaying a sustainable aviation fuel levy from its original start date to October 1, citing rising fuel costs caused by the Iran war. The levy, to be paid by airline customers, will vary based on travel class or flight length and is part of Singapore's green fuel initiatives.

stories.title: 2 injured as Iran fires missile salvos at central Israel after 14-hour lull
stories.summary: Iran fired two missile salvos at central Israel after a 14-hour lull, injuring at least two people. Separately, Hezbollah mortar fire wounded four Israeli soldiers in Lebanon, Russia was reportedly delivering drones to Iran, and Australia imposed a six-month ban on Iranian visitors.

stories.title: Andrew Hastie open to 25% tax on gas profits and says multinationals have ‘had a really good run’ on Australian wealth
stories.summary: Australian Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie said he is open to a 25% tax on gas profits to fund a Scandinavian-style sovereign wealth fund. The Albanese government is reportedly modelling the effects of such a tax amid a global energy crisis, as Hastie argued multinational companies have "had a really good run" exploiting Australian resources.

stories.title: Boy, 7, is youngest professional rally car driver in China, starting race journey at age 1
stories.summary: Seven-year-old Shao Ziyan from Wenzhou in Zhejiang province has become China's youngest professional rally car driver after receiving certification at age five. His father says the boy became fascinated with car racing as a toddler and began using a racing simulator at home when he was just one year old.

stories.title: Trump says Iranian leaders want deal ‘so badly’ but fear retaliation
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed that Iranian leaders want to reach a deal with Washington but are reluctant to publicly acknowledge negotiations out of fear of domestic retaliation.

stories.title: Petroleum dealers postpone strike in light of Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Pakistan's Petroleum Dealers Association postponed a planned strike set for March 26, citing the Middle East conflict's impact on global fuel supplies. PPDA Chairperson Abdul Sami Khan cited potential consumer hardships from a supply chain crisis.

stories.title: Trump housing chief requests new criminal investigation into Letitia James
stories.summary: Federal housing director Bill Pulte has requested criminal investigations into New York Attorney General Letitia James for alleged insurance fraud, according to reported referrals to prosecutors in Florida and Illinois. James's lawyer characterized the move as a vendetta by the Trump administration.

stories.title: Trump’s trip to meet Xi Jinping in China rescheduled for May due to Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's planned visit to China has been rescheduled from late March to May 14–15 due to the Iran war. Trump announced on Truth Social that he will meet President Xi Jinping in Beijing and later host Xi for a reciprocal visit in Washington, marking his first trip to China in eight years.

stories.title: US, Israel temporarily remove two Iranian officials from target list - report
stories.summary: The United States and Israel temporarily removed Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi from their target list as President Trump seeks to create an opening for peace negotiations with Tehran.

stories.title: Kremlin mouthpieces: Data on five more Russians justifying war against Ukraine released
stories.summary: Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate and Center for Countering Disinformation published data on five additional Russian individuals involved in disinformation campaigns justifying Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Warning over mould and infections as Hong Kong set for more damp days
stories.summary: Health experts in Hong Kong are warning elderly residents and those with chronic illnesses to take precautions against mould and infections as high humidity is expected to persist through the end of the week. They recommend using dehumidifiers and removing mould, noting that damp conditions can cause breathing difficulties for asthmatics.

stories.title: Hezbollah announces the targeting of Israeli military HQ in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Lebanon's Hezbollah said it targeted the Israeli Ministry of Defense headquarters in central Tel Aviv and Military Intelligence Directorate barracks with advanced missiles. The group also claimed it destroyed 10 tanks and two D9 bulldozers during an Israeli advance attempt in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump claims Iranian negotiators fear being 'killed by their own people'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed at a dinner for Republican members of Congress that Iran is participating in peace talks but publicly denying it, suggesting Iranian negotiators fear being killed by their own people if the discussions become known.

stories.title: ‘Someone asked if my book was influenced by Dhurandhar’: author Sarnath Banerjee
stories.summary: Author Sarnath Banerjee discussed his new book, Absolute Jafar, an India-Pakistan love story set across Delhi, Chicago, Karachi, and Berlin. He addressed questions about potential influences on the work.

stories.title: IDF accelerating strikes as possibility of US-Iran ceasefire looms - report
stories.summary: Reports indicate the Israeli military is accelerating strikes on Iran amid the possibility of a US-Iran ceasefire. Officials claimed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the destruction of as much of Iran's arms industry as possible within 48 hours.

stories.title: One Palestinian killed in Israeli settler attack in Masafer Yatta
stories.summary: A Palestinian worker was killed and eight others were injured in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, after Israeli forces and settlers reportedly chased vehicles carrying local residents and opened fire, causing several vehicles to overturn.

stories.title: British suppliers to be prioritised for contracts in sectors vital to national security
stories.summary: The British government announced new guidance prioritising domestic suppliers for public contracts in shipbuilding, steel, AI, and energy infrastructure, designating them as sectors vital to national security. The policy was accelerated as the Middle East war highlighted the fragility of global supply chains.

stories.title: Iran war could boost China’s ‘petroyuan’ and weaken US dollar dominance, analysts say
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank analysts say the US-Israeli war in Iran could undermine the US dollar's dominance in the oil-rich Middle East and strengthen China's "petroyuan" alternative. The nearly month-long conflict is testing the foundations of the petrodollar regime, and damage to Gulf economies may prompt those states to shift their foreign asset holdings.

stories.title: What Japan’s missile plan for remote Pacific island reveals about its defence goals
stories.summary: Japan is reportedly planning to deploy advanced anti-ship missiles on Minamitorishima, its easternmost Pacific island, to counter perceived rising Chinese military activity. The defence ministry also aims to station a launcher, surveillance drones, and radar systems on the island as early as June, according to NHK.

stories.title: Iran war live: US demands Tehran accept defeat; Israel pounds Lebanon
stories.summary: An Iranian official described the United States' 15-point proposal as "maximalist," while Iranian state television outlined five conditions Tehran requires for a peace agreement.

stories.title: War update: 140 clashes on frontline, Pokrovsk sector remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 140 combat engagements along the front lines, with the Pokrovsk sector remaining the most active. Russian troops launched 39 attacks on Ukrainian positions in that sector alone, losing over 150 personnel.

stories.title: Israel says over 5,000 injured since start of war on Iran
stories.summary: Israel's health ministry reported that 5,165 people have been hospitalized since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Of those, 106 remain under treatment, including 13 in serious condition.

stories.title: Chinese nationals, companies charged in US with smuggling AI chips and drug trafficking
stories.summary: US authorities indicted Chinese nationals in two separate cases involving alleged smuggling of advanced AI chips to China and drug trafficking with money laundering. The charges came as President Trump announced new dates for a summit with China.

stories.title: U.S. to deploy 1,000 elite troops to West Asia
stories.summary: The United States announced plans to deploy 1,000 elite troops along with Marines and rapid-response naval vessels to West Asia as part of the Iran war effort. Iran and Israel have exchanged strikes, with Gulf neighbors Kuwait and Saudi Arabia also coming under fire. Iran's military claimed it also targeted a U.S. aircraft carrier.

stories.title: Russia says it shot down almost 400 Ukrainian drones as Moscow, Kyiv escalate aerial barrages
stories.summary: Russia said it intercepted nearly 400 Ukrainian drones in a major aerial escalation. Leningrad region Governor Alexander Drozdenko reported 56 drones shot down in his region, with a fire breaking out at the Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga.

stories.title: US offers $3 million reward, possible relocation, for information on finances of Haiti gangs
stories.summary: The United States offered a reward of up to $3 million and possible relocation for information on the financial activities of Haiti's Viv Ansanm and Gran Grif criminal groups. The announcement was made on Wednesday in Port-au-Prince.

stories.title: Egypt says it is ready to host Iran de-escalation talks
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty stated that Cairo is prepared to host de-escalation talks regarding Iran, signaling Egypt's willingness to play a diplomatic role in reducing tensions.

stories.title: Right-wing candidates Fujimori, Lopez Aliaga top crowded Peru field ahead of presidential vote, poll shows
stories.summary: A new poll shows right-wing candidates Keiko Fujimori and Rafael Lopez Aliaga leading voter preferences ahead of Peru's April presidential election. The results indicate a rightward shift in a crowded field of 35 contenders.

stories.title: Lukashenko greeted by Kim Jong-un on Belarus leader’s first visit to North Korea
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko made his first visit to North Korea, where he was greeted by leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang. Lukashenko visited the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun and was welcomed at a ceremony on Kim Il-sung Square.

stories.title: Kim vows North Korea's 'unshakable' support for Russia
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pledged his country's "unshakable" support for Russia. Analysts assess that North Korea's assistance is provided in exchange for Russian food supplies and weapons technology.

stories.title: ‘Out of control’: UN chief names personal envoy for Middle East war
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres appointed French diplomat Jean Arnault as his personal envoy for the Middle East war, describing the situation as out of control. Arnault brings over 30 years of international diplomacy experience to the role.

stories.title: U.N. chief names Arnault as personal envoy for Middle East war
stories.summary: U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres named veteran French diplomat Jean Arnault as his personal envoy on the Middle East conflict, warning the situation is out of control and the world risks a wider war.

stories.title: Luxury Paris hotel near Elysee reopens after fire forces brief closure
stories.summary: A five-star hotel near the Élysée presidential palace in Paris reopened on Wednesday after a fire earlier forced the evacuation of approximately 400 people. Paris firefighters and the hotel confirmed there were no reported casualties.

stories.title: Hopes for diplomatic end to Iran war give boost to shares, ease price of oil
stories.summary: Global stock markets rose after the United States floated a truce proposal to Iran. The S&P 500 gained 0.5%, the Dow Jones added 0.7%, and markets in London, Paris, and Shanghai climbed more than 1%, while oil prices eased.

stories.title: Ukraine to scale up drone production with European partners – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is working with European partners to expand joint weapons production, with a primary focus on drones. New agreements are being prepared to scale up manufacturing.

stories.title: US Army Special Operations Command takes home top prize in sniper competition
stories.summary: Seventeen elite sniper teams representing multiple U.S. military branches and partner nations competed in a sniper competition at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The U.S. Army Special Operations Command won the top prize in the event.

stories.title: Rights group warns of 'dystopian' Hong Kong after bookstore arrests
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch warned that Hong Kong is becoming increasingly repressive after authorities arrested individuals linked to a bookstore selling publications about jailed newspaper publisher Jimmy Lai. HRW Asia director Elaine Pearson questioned who might be targeted next.

stories.title: Lukashenko greeted by Kim Jong Un on first visit to North Korea
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko visited North Korea for the first time, receiving a warm welcome from Kim Jong-un. The visit underscores deepening ties between the two Moscow-aligned nations, both of which have supported Russia's war in Ukraine.

stories.title: What is at stake at the WTO’s MC14? | Explained
stories.summary: The World Trade Organization's 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) is taking place amid a weakened dispute settlement system. Key issues include the contentious e-commerce moratorium and India's role in the negotiations.

stories.title: Spanish PM says West Asia war 'far worse' than Iraq in 2003
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the current war in West Asia as far worse than the 2003 Iraq conflict. Sánchez has refused U.S. requests to use Spanish military bases for operations against Iran, despite President Donald Trump's threat to cut trade ties with Spain.

stories.title: Iranian foreign minister rejects talks with US
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied that any negotiations with the United States have taken place, stating that Tehran is not engaged in talks with Washington.

stories.title: Justice Department settles lawsuit from Trump ally Michael Flynn for US$1.2 million
stories.summary: The US Justice Department settled a lawsuit brought by Michael Flynn, former national security adviser to President Trump, for approximately $1.2 million. Flynn had previously pleaded guilty to lying to the FBI about conversations with a Russian diplomat before receiving a presidential pardon.

stories.title: British forces will be able to board Russian shadow fleet ships in UK waters
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced that UK forces will be authorized to board Russian shadow fleet ships operating in British waters. Starmer said the measure aims to cut off funding for Russia's war effort, making the announcement while arriving in Finland for a military summit.

stories.title: Supporters of Jewish charter school file lawsuit challenging ban in Oklahoma
stories.summary: Supporters of the proposed Ben Gamla School, a Jewish charter school, filed a lawsuit in Oklahoma challenging the state's ban on publicly funded religious charter schools. The case could set a precedent as the nation's first such institution.

stories.title: Airstrike in western Anbar kills 7 Iraqi soldiers, wounds 13
stories.summary: An airstrike in western Anbar province, Iraq, killed seven Iraqi soldiers and wounded 13 others. Iraq's Ministry of Defense condemned the attack as a serious violation of international law, noting it targeted areas near medical facilities and personnel.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill three in southern Lebanon, injure several
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed three people and wounded four in Qounine, in the Bint Jbeil district of southern Lebanon. Additional Israeli raids on Toulene in the Marjayoun district injured seven people. Heavy air strikes were also reported across the Nabatieh governorate.

stories.title: Strike on alleged drug vessel kills four in the Caribbean, US military says
stories.summary: The US military struck a vessel in the Caribbean, killing four people who were allegedly operating on behalf of designated terrorist organizations. The strike brings the total deaths to at least 163 since US attacks on alleged narco-terrorist vessels began in September.

stories.title: Tusk clashes with Nawrocki over his visit to Hungary
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk criticized President Karol Nawrocki's visit to Budapest, arguing it led Hungary to halt gas supplies to Ukraine, a move Tusk said benefits Russian President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: US ties Ukraine security guarantees to Donbas withdrawal, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States is conditioning post-war security guarantees on Kyiv ceding the Russian-occupied Donbas region. Zelensky warned such terms would weaken Ukraine's defenses and embolden Moscow.

stories.title: 11 Palestinian families evicted after court found Jews owned their East Jerusalem homes before 1948
stories.summary: An Israeli court ordered the eviction of 11 Palestinian families from homes in the Silwan neighborhood of East Jerusalem. The ruling was based on a 1970 law allowing Jews to reclaim properties owned before Israel's establishment in 1948.

stories.title: Jordan says expelling Iranian diplomats sends clear message to Tehran
stories.summary: Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman al-Safadi announced the expulsion of Iranian diplomats, saying it sends a clear message that attacks on neighboring states are unacceptable. He stated that Iran has launched dozens of missiles and drones toward Jordan during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iran's rejection of US talks reflects deep mistrust
stories.summary: Iran has publicly rejected direct talks with the United States, reflecting deep-seated mistrust. However, analysts suggest Tehran's hardline stance may be aimed at setting preconditions rather than permanently closing the door to diplomacy.

stories.title: Sikorski: Ukraine targets military sites in Russia, while Putin attacks Ukrainian churches
stories.summary: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski stated that Ukraine strikes military targets in Russia, whereas Russia attacks civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, including churches, highlighting the asymmetry between the two sides' conduct.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu seeks to avoid snap vote as Iran war gives no boost in polls
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to avoid snap elections, which he has consistently rejected during wartime. Polls indicate that the ongoing war with Iran has not boosted his political standing domestically.

stories.title: US wants Ukraine to withdraw from Donbas in exchange for security guarantees – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States has proposed that Kyiv withdraw its forces from unoccupied parts of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions in exchange for security guarantees.

stories.title: Houthis reiterate support for Iran but will stay on the sidelines
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement reiterated its political and religious support for Iran but said it is not currently participating in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Houthi officials told the Associated Press that any decision to join the fighting would be made independently by Yemen.

stories.title: Trump to skip major annual conservative gathering for first time in decade
stories.summary: President Donald Trump will skip the Conservative Political Action Conference for the first time in a decade, citing a busy schedule amid the ongoing Iran conflict. Trump had been a regular fixture at CPAC since 2016.

stories.title: Video shows Israeli strike hitting displacement camp in Gaza
stories.summary: Video footage captured an Israeli strike hitting a tent camp for displaced Palestinians in Deir el-Balah, in central Gaza. The camp was sheltering people who had been displaced by ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: Death penalty bill expected for final vote next week after Knesset panel approves outline
stories.summary: An Israeli Knesset committee approved the outline of a death penalty bill, which is expected to receive a final vote next week. The legislation would impose a death sentence on terrorists who intentionally kill as part of an act of terrorism, without requiring a unanimous verdict.

stories.title: France confirms oil crisis, says 30-40% Gulf energy infrastructure destroyed
stories.summary: France confirmed that 30–40% of Gulf energy infrastructure has been destroyed, contributing to a global oil crisis. The announcement came as part of an update on the economic impact of the ongoing Iran conflict.

stories.title: ‘Like oil’: Kyiv gripped by drone rush amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Gulf states are approaching Ukrainian drone manufacturers amid the Middle East war, driving a surge in demand in Kyiv. However, analysts note these states are unlikely to abandon their existing expensive conventional arms procurement programs.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1491:  For first time since World War II, bombs have fallen on Russia’s Leningrad Oblast
stories.summary: For the first time since World War II, bombs struck Russia's Leningrad Oblast as part of Ukraine's long-range campaign against Russian territory. The strikes are part of a broader offensive that has reportedly shut down 40% of Russian oil exports.

stories.title: Iran rejects U.S. proposal, sets out conditions to end war
stories.summary: Iran rejected a U.S. ceasefire proposal that offered sanctions relief in exchange for Tehran dismantling its nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian officials set out their own conditions for ending the conflict.

stories.title: Hungary's Orban faces pivotal battle against ally-turned-foe
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán faces the most serious electoral challenge of his 16-year rule ahead of an April 12 national vote. His opponent is a former political ally who is now seeking to unseat him.

stories.title: Cyprus opens discussion with UK over its military bases, amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Cyprus has opened discussions with the United Kingdom regarding the future of British military bases on the island, including RAF Akrotiri. The talks follow a March 2 drone strike at RAF Akrotiri that heightened concerns about security risks linked to the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: US Postal Service to introduce 8% fuel surcharge on packages
stories.summary: The US Postal Service announced an 8% fuel surcharge on packages, its first ever, driven by oil price spikes linked to the Iran war. The surcharge is set to take effect on April 26 and remain in place until January 2027.

stories.title: Why China’s strategy to stay out of Iran war is working – and crisis may spur opportunity
stories.summary: Analysts say China's strategy of avoiding military entanglement in the Iran war while issuing diplomatic statements may allow Beijing to emerge favorably from the conflict. China's approach follows its long-standing playbook of non-intervention and economic positioning.

stories.title: Sweden joins agreement on special tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression
stories.summary: Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard announced that Sweden has confirmed its intention to join the agreement establishing a Special Tribunal to investigate Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Low chance for US-Iran deal, but Trump 'can always surprise us,' Israeli officials tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli officials told the Jerusalem Post that a US-Iran deal remains unlikely but expressed concern that President Trump could declare a temporary ceasefire as indirect communications between Washington and Tehran continue.

stories.title: What is IDF's view on pontential long-term occupation of southern Lebanon? - analysis
stories.summary: Israeli military analysts are debating whether Israel is prepared for a long-term occupation of southern Lebanon up to the Litani River or whether its current posture is a temporary measure to pressure Hezbollah.

stories.title: Oil, stock trading spikes before Trump's Iran remarks spark insider trading suspicions
stories.summary: Unusually high volumes of oil futures were traded roughly 15 minutes before President Trump announced a halt to strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, prompting insider trading suspicions. Traders who bet on falling prices ahead of the announcement would have profited from the subsequent drop.

stories.title: Explainer-Can the US government be held liable for the LaGuardia Airport collision?
stories.summary: Investigators are examining the causes of a collision on March 23 between an Air Canada Express aircraft and a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport in New York. The two pilots were killed, and 39 of the 76 passengers and crew were hospitalized. The incident has renewed concerns about air traffic control staffing shortages.

stories.title: German foreign minister hopes Iran peace talks given chance to work
stories.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on March 25 welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump's pursuit of negotiations to end the war with Iran. Wadephul expressed hope that the diplomatic talks would be given a genuine chance to succeed.

stories.title: Will too much AI weaken troops' judgement?
stories.summary: As the Pentagon accelerates deployment of large language model-based AI tools, research raises concerns that over-reliance on such systems could undermine human judgment and communication among military personnel.

stories.title: Tracy Kidder, Pulitzer-winning author who turned unlikely subjects into bestsellers, dies aged 80
stories.summary: Pulitzer Prize-winning author Tracy Kidder died at age 80. Known for narrative nonfiction, Kidder turned subjects such as computer engineering and nursing home life into bestsellers, earning acclaim for his deeply researched storytelling.

stories.title: Gaza death toll rises as Israeli attacks continue amid ceasefire
stories.summary: At least 689 people have been killed and 1,860 injured in Israeli attacks on Gaza since a ceasefire took effect on October 11. The overall death toll in Gaza has reached 72,265 since October 2023.

stories.title: UAE ambassador to US warns against ending Iran war too soon
stories.summary: UAE Ambassador to the US Yousef Al Otaiba wrote in a Wall Street Journal op-ed that the war against Iran requires a decisive outcome addressing the full scope of the Islamic Republic's threat, warning against ending the conflict prematurely.

stories.title: Australia politics live: opposition calls on Labor to activate emergency powers to tackle fuel crisis
stories.summary: Australia's opposition called on the Labor government to activate emergency powers under the liquid fuel emergency act to address a growing fuel crisis. One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce also called for food rationing, warning of cascading supply disruptions.

stories.title: Zelensky: We propose mutually beneficial partnership, Middle East and Gulf offer opportunities to strengthen Ukraine
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine's diplomatic team is pursuing cooperation with Middle Eastern and Gulf countries, which are interested in Ukraine's experience in defending against modern drone warfare.

stories.title: Lacking 'morals, values, or principles': Georgia government 'guided by Kremlin'
stories.summary: Former Georgian Defense Minister Tina Khidasheli said Georgia's government is guided by the Kremlin and lacks morals and principles. She argued that despite Georgia's EU candidate status, laws such as the foreign agents law are suppressing dissent and deterring civic activity.

stories.title: UN names African slave trade 'gravest crime against humanity'
stories.summary: The UN General Assembly designated the transatlantic African slave trade as "the gravest crime against humanity," a decision seen by advocates as a step toward healing and potential reparations. Separately, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited Algeria to discuss increasing Algerian gas deliveries. The ongoing Middle East conflict is also reportedly threatening Kenya's flower export industry.

stories.title: US Justice Department’s Oct. 7 task force said to be unraveling
stories.summary: The US Justice Department's task force established to prosecute Hamas members over the October 7 attack is reportedly losing resources amid broader upheaval in the federal judiciary, according to the Washington Post.

stories.title: White House doubles down on Iran threats as Republican lawmakers retreat
stories.summary: The White House intensified threats against Iran, stating US objectives would be met within two weeks, while Republican lawmakers expressed frustration at being kept uninformed about the administration's plans.

stories.title: Gov’t approves millions for border cities in North under Hezbollah fire
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved millions in funding for border communities in northern Israel that are under Hezbollah fire, aiming to strengthen resilience and support relief efforts for residents in the area.

stories.title: Czech Senate discusses European EUR 90B loan to Ukraine
stories.summary: The Czech Senate discussed a proposed European Union loan of 90 billion euros to Ukraine. The Czech government expressed full support for Ukraine and urged the fastest possible unblocking of the funds, though it will not financially guarantee the loan.

stories.title: 'No talks': Tehran doesn't want to negotiate with US, Iranian FM Aragchi says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Iran has not engaged in negotiations with the United States and that message exchanges through mediators do not constitute formal talks. Iran is seeking a permanent end to the conflict.

stories.title: FM Sa’ar urges UN to designate Hezbollah as terror group, calls Iran global threat
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar called on the United Nations to designate Hezbollah as a terrorist organization, stating that Iran has transferred $1.2 billion to Hezbollah since the ceasefire and plays a direct role in training militants.

stories.title: Pakistan Could Be a U.S.-Iran Peace Broker
stories.summary: An analysis argues Pakistan could serve as a credible peace broker between the United States and Iran, given Islamabad's relationships with both countries and its strategic position in the region.

stories.title: Iran ‘present’ touted by Trump was passage of several fuel tankers through Hormuz
stories.summary: The "present" from Iran that President Trump publicly touted was the passage of several fuel tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Officials said the US sought a signal from Iran to gauge whether a diplomatic off-ramp was worth pursuing.

stories.title: COGAT discovers motor oil hidden inside UN's humanitarian aid to Gaza in smuggling attempt
stories.summary: Israel's Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) said it discovered motor oil concealed inside UN humanitarian aid shipments bound for Gaza, calling it a serious violation of aid mechanisms exploited by Hamas.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: West Bank attacks surge, Israel restricts Gaza aid
stories.summary: Israeli settler attacks surged across the West Bank, while Israel imposed further restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza and carried out additional land seizures during the week.

stories.title: Congolese rapper, Gims, arrested in Paris over alleged money laundering
stories.summary: Congolese-born rapper Gims, whose real name is Gandhi Djuna, was arrested at Paris's Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport on allegations of money laundering, according to Africa Intelligence.

stories.title: Israel issues notice: Ben-Gurion Airport flights likely restricted until at least April 16 - report
stories.summary: Israel issued a NOTAM indicating that flights at Ben-Gurion Airport are likely to remain restricted until at least April 16 due to ongoing attacks from Iran and Hezbollah, according to Channel 13.

stories.title: Russia planning operation against Ukraine's water supply systems in coming months – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia is planning an operation targeting Ukraine's water supply systems in the coming months. He stressed the need to bolster protection of critical infrastructure and air defense capabilities.

stories.title: Philippines farmers feeling the pinch of the war on Iran
stories.summary: Cabbage farmers in the Philippines are harvesting crops at a loss as the war on Iran drives fuel costs higher and causes produce prices to plunge domestically.

stories.title: An Iranian to negotiate with: Who is Mohammad Qalibaf?
stories.summary: Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf is a prominent Iranian politician with close ties to the military establishment. He has been associated with corruption allegations and played a role in the suppression of protests, but he is considered a potential interlocutor in negotiations.

stories.title: An Iranian to negotiate with: Who is Mohammad Ghalibaf?
stories.summary: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is a prominent Iranian politician with close ties to the military establishment. He has also been associated with corruption allegations and involvement in the suppression of domestic protests.

stories.title: Pentagon announces major surge in missile production
stories.summary: The Pentagon has announced a major surge in production of missile systems and related components. The accelerated manufacturing effort focuses on systems deemed critical to U.S. capabilities for defeating aerial threats, including one-way attack drones.

stories.title: Netanyahu spokesman quits, admits to racist remarks on Mizrahi Jews, attacks on PM
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's spokesperson Ziv Agmon resigned after leaked comments surfaced in which he made racist remarks about Mizrahi Jews and criticized the prime minister. Agmon said the comments predated his role and were taken out of context.

stories.title: US investors bet big on Indian cricket with record billion-dollar IPL deals
stories.summary: US investors purchased Indian Premier League cricket teams Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals in separate billion-dollar deals, both setting new records for IPL franchise sales.

stories.title: Map: Military Strikes Target Complex Criminal Landscape on Colombia-Ecuador Border
stories.summary: InSight Crime mapped the complex criminal dynamics along the Colombia-Ecuador border, one of the world's most significant cocaine transit corridors, where military strikes have targeted multiple armed and criminal groups.

stories.title: Four killed in latest US attack on alleged drug-smuggling boat in Caribbean
stories.summary: The US military struck an alleged drug-smuggling boat in the Caribbean, killing four people. The Trump administration characterized those targeted as members of a designated terrorist organisation.

stories.title: Spain's Sanchez says global citizens shouldn't pay for fallout of Iran war
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on March 25 criticized what he called illegal U.S. and Israeli actions in Iran, saying it was unjust for global citizens to bear the economic costs. He warned that Spanish firms alone had lost approximately 100 billion euros in under a month due to the conflict.

stories.title: A mysterious group is calling on Russians to protest the Kremlin’s Internet restrictions. Is it a trap?
stories.summary: A movement calling itself "Scarlet Swan" has appeared on TikTok and Telegram in Russia, urging protests on March 29 against the Kremlin's internet restrictions. Opposition activists and journalists have warned the movement may be a trap orchestrated by Russian security services.

stories.title: Pakistan Medical and Dental Council says 10 universities offering unrecognised postgraduate programmes
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council identified 10 universities offering unrecognised postgraduate medical and dental programmes. The council directed these institutions to discontinue the programmes, which lacked mandatory recognition under the PMDC Act of 2022.

stories.title: Iran releases video claiming to show downing of US jet
stories.summary: Iran released video footage it claims shows the downing of a US F-18 fighter jet during the ongoing conflict between the two countries.

stories.title: Jordan says expelling Iranian diplomats sends clear message to Tehran
