He is expected to play a central role in upcoming coalition negotiations. Rasmussen is also credited with easing tensions between Denmark and the U.S. over Greenland.

stories.title: Volkswagen in talks to make Iron Dome parts for Israel
stories.summary: German automaker Volkswagen is in talks to manufacture components for Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system. The potential move would mark a return to military-related manufacturing for the company, which has a controversial wartime history.

stories.title: Pack a Seder: How one box is reaching Israel's most isolated survivors
stories.summary: An initiative called Pack a Seder is delivering Passover supplies to isolated Holocaust survivors in Israel. Organizer Zalman Duchman said the program serves elderly survivors the organization supports throughout the year.

stories.title: Iran calls US proposal to end war ‘maximalist, unreasonable’
stories.summary: Iran has publicly rejected a US proposal to end the ongoing war, describing the terms as "maximalist" and "unreasonable." Details of the proposal and Iran's specific objections have not yet been fully disclosed.

stories.title: Nigeria: Three Killed, Many Injured As Violence Erupts in Nasarawa Community
stories.summary: Three people were killed and many injured in Nasarawa State, Nigeria, after violence erupted in the Aso A area of a community on Wednesday morning, reportedly sparked by a dispute between a mobile police officer and a herder.

stories.title: Dagenham leaseholders left homeless by fire could be forced to pay for cladding works
stories.summary: Former leaseholders of the Spectrum Building in Dagenham, east London, say they face bills for fire safety works on the tower block that was demolished after a major fire in August 2024. The Greater London Authority is seeking to reclaim £6 million allocated for uncompleted cladding remediation on the destroyed building.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria Unveils HIV Prevention Plan, Shifts Focus Beyond Treatment
stories.summary: Nigeria launched a new HIV prevention plan shifting its focus beyond treatment to address evolving infection patterns. The initiative aims to close gaps in the country's overall HIV response.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gov Speaks As Terrorists Gun Down Soldiers in Kebbi
stories.summary: Governor Nasir Idris of Kebbi State, Nigeria, expressed shock after terrorists killed several soldiers in the state. The attack highlights ongoing security challenges in northwestern Nigeria.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Backs Revival of Muslims' Morning Call to Prayer
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame reassured Muslims that the morning call to prayer will be restored. The practice had been disrupted as local government institutions implemented noise pollution regulations in Kigali and other areas.

stories.title: Iran’s Peace Negotiator Is His Country’s Trump
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Ghalibaf has emerged as a key peace negotiator for Iran. His political rise has been characterized by populist imagery, allegations of real estate corruption, and a reputation for ruthlessness.

stories.title: War will end 'when Iran decides it', Iranian official tells state TV
stories.summary: Iranian state television reported that a senior official rejected the US-proposed ceasefire plan to end the war. The official stated that the conflict will end when Iran decides, not according to President Trump's timeline.

stories.title: Canada Faces Its Finland Moment
stories.summary: An analysis compares Canada's current geopolitical position to Finland's situation during the Cold War, arguing that Ottawa faces threats from a powerful and confrontational neighbor in the United States.

stories.title: Seeking a deal with different faces of the same regime, Trump risks subverting his own vital war goals
stories.summary: President Trump promised Iranians that after the war their government would be theirs to reclaim, but analysts question whether negotiations with the existing regime can achieve that goal. Critics warn his approach may undermine stated US war objectives, including guaranteed security for Israel.

stories.title: US demands of 15-point peace plan likely 'unacceptable' for Iran
stories.summary: The United States has sent a 15-point peace plan to Iran, which Tehran has publicly dismissed as excessive. Reported demands include sanctions relief, rollback of Iran's nuclear programme, IAEA monitoring, freedom of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and an end to Iranian support for proxy groups.

stories.title: UN migration agency says 2025 was deadliest year on Red Sea migrant route
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that 2025 has been the deadliest year on record for the Red Sea migrant route. The number of people who died or went missing on the route doubled to 922.

stories.title: Airbus wins Chinese airline’s 101-plane order in victory over Boeing in key market
stories.summary: China Eastern Airlines placed a multibillion-dollar order for 101 Airbus A320neo aircraft, marking another win for the French manufacturer over rival Boeing in the Chinese market. While the list price would be approximately $15.8 billion, China Eastern said Airbus granted a significant discount.

stories.title: Should China be worried about Japan’s maritime force overhaul?
stories.summary: Japan's Maritime Self-Defence Force restructured its organizational framework on Monday to accelerate decision-making and improve ship operations, including preparations for quasi-carrier capabilities. Chinese analysts view the overhaul as reflecting Japan's shift toward preparations for a potential conflict with Beijing.

stories.title: Fifty years on, Israel repeats previous mistakes leading to the October 7 massacre - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel has repeated the intelligence failures that preceded the 1973 Yom Kippur War, contributing to the October 7, 2023 attack. The analysis highlights persistent blind spots over five decades and calls for urgent intelligence reform.

stories.title: Ukraine needs about two thousand anti-ballistic missiles per year – Kubilius
stories.summary: EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius stated that Ukraine requires approximately 2,000 anti-ballistic missiles per year. He noted that improvements in Russian ballistic missile capabilities have reduced interception effectiveness, increasing Ukraine's need for interceptors.

stories.title: In Nairobi, residents blame flood devastation on inadequate infrastructure
stories.summary: Flooding across at least 21 Kenyan counties since March has displaced over 34,000 people, with the capital Nairobi particularly hard hit. Residents blame the severity of the devastation on inadequate infrastructure and rapid urban growth. Nairobi's governor has launched emergency operations to clear drainage systems.

stories.title: Ghana and EU sign defence partnership to counter west Africa insecurity
stories.summary: Ghana and the European Union signed their first formal defence partnership on March 25 in Accra. Ghana also signed similar agreements with Iceland and Australia. The partnerships aim to counter growing insecurity in West Africa from groups linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

stories.title: Iran appears to target Israeli power plant in missile attack, but misses
stories.summary: Iran apparently targeted an Israeli power plant with a missile attack but missed. Separately, a senior Iranian official confirmed receiving the US peace proposal, and the Israeli Air Force struck Iran's sole submarine development facility.

stories.title: Saudi Pro League, the US or Europe - what are Salah's options?
stories.summary: Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah announced he will leave the club this summer. Analysts are examining his potential destinations, including the Saudi Pro League, the United States, or other European clubs.

stories.title: US defense giant taps Israeli drone navigation tech built for jammed battlefields
stories.summary: A US defense company has partnered with Israeli firm ASIO to use its drone navigation technology. The system is designed to keep unmanned aircraft operational in combat environments where GPS signals are jammed or denied.

stories.title: Pro-Iran Iraqi militias expand attacks into Syria
stories.summary: Pro-Iran Iraqi militias expanded their attacks into Syria, targeting the Kharab al-Jir base in Hasakah province on 23 March. Damascus says US forces had already withdrawn from the base in February 2026.

stories.title: GOP moving forward with new reconciliation bill, with money for defense: Graham
stories.summary: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Lindsey Graham announced that Republicans are advancing a second reconciliation bill that includes increased defense funding. Graham said the bill aims to ensure adequate resources for homeland security and to support U.S. military personnel engaged in combat operations.

stories.title: Missiles overhead, silence below: Israel’s home front holds firm
stories.summary: Israel's home front is holding together amid ongoing Iranian missile attacks, with a combination of military censorship and public unity suppressing dissent. The prolonged conflict with Iran has tested civilian resilience across the country.

stories.title: Anthropic’s case against the Pentagon could open space for AI regulation
stories.summary: A California judge has suggested the US Department of Defense may be attempting to undermine Anthropic, the AI company, for advocating restrictions on AI weapons systems. The case could set precedents for AI regulation in the defense sector.

stories.title: Iran struggles to assert control in Iraq amid strikes, militia attacks, tensions - analysis
stories.summary: Iran is struggling to maintain influence in Iraq following strikes and militia activity. Kurdish leaders in the autonomous region have expressed outrage over an Iranian attack, prompting Tehran to appear to walk back the incident, though it continues asserting control elsewhere in the country.

stories.title: Fedorov holds discussions with representatives of 13 assault and infantry units
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov held a closed meeting with representatives of 13 assault and infantry units to discuss front-line conditions. Topics included service term policies and financial support for soldiers.

stories.title: Russia pulls more staff from Iran nuclear plant after reported strike
stories.summary: Russia evacuated an additional 163 staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant following a reported overnight strike on the compound. Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev said approximately 300 Russian personnel remain at the facility, which Russia partially constructed.

stories.title: Ukraine: Massive wave of daytime Russian strikes hits sites nationwide
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 1,000 drones at targets across Ukraine on March 24 in one of the largest daytime air strikes since the war began. The attacks killed several people and caused damage in multiple cities, some located hundreds of kilometres from the front lines.

stories.title: Danish election signals shift toward Dutch and Belgian-style of coalition building
stories.summary: Following Denmark's general election, analysts observe a shift toward fragmented, negotiation-heavy coalition politics resembling models seen in the Netherlands and Belgium. Traditional parties experienced electoral erosion, though not uniformly. External crises influenced public perception but did not singularly determine voting outcomes.

stories.title: Musketeer d'Artagnan's remains believed found under Dutch church
stories.summary: Archaeologists believe they have discovered the remains of Charles de Batz-Castelmore d'Artagnan, the historical figure who inspired Alexandre Dumas's famous musketeer character, beneath a church in the Netherlands. D'Artagnan was killed during the 1673 Siege of Maastricht.

stories.title: State Duma Members to Travel to U.S. in Coming Days for Congressional Talks
stories.summary: A delegation of four or five Russian State Duma members is expected to travel to Washington, D.C. in the coming days for talks with members of the U.S. Congress.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief urges unity, no talks with Israel amid Lebanon attacks
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem called for unity against Israel and rejected any negotiations while Lebanon is under attack. He stated that negotiating under fire would amount to imposing surrender on Lebanon.

stories.title: Ukrainian grain was stolen, relabeled Russian, and sold to a UN food program supplier—the paperwork said nothing about Mariupol
stories.summary: An investigation found that grain stolen from Ukrainian territories, including Mariupol, was relabeled as Russian and sold to a UN World Food Programme supplier in Turkey. The same Russian family involved reportedly also manufactures attack drones for Russia's military.

stories.title: Russian drone makers sell stolen Ukrainian grain—part reaching a UN food supplier
stories.summary: An investigation found that a Russian family involved in manufacturing attack drones for Russia's war in Ukraine also exports stolen Ukrainian grain. Some of the wheat reportedly reached a supplier for a UN food program operating in Turkey.

stories.title: Israeli court closes case into Palestinian teen’s death despite evidence of starvation
stories.summary: An Israeli court closed an investigation into the death of 17-year-old Palestinian Walid Ahmad, who died in Israeli custody in March 2025 amid evidence of starvation. Human rights experts condemned the ruling, citing ongoing impunity as prisoner deaths continue to mount.

stories.title: Israeli attacks hit Gaza shelters and aid site despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit shelters and an aid distribution site in Gaza despite a ceasefire being in place, killing and wounding Palestinians. UN officials warned of deepening humanitarian crisis and ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Are Middle East attacks pushing Asia towards an energy crisis?
stories.summary: Attacks on energy facilities across the Middle East, including Qatar's LNG infrastructure, are driving global energy prices higher. Asian economies that depend heavily on Middle Eastern energy imports face growing concerns about a potential energy crisis.

stories.title: Latvia and Estonia confirm crash of Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics confirmed that a Ukrainian drone crashed in Latvia's Kraslava region on March 25 while en route to strike targets in Russia. Estonia also confirmed a similar incident on its territory the same night.

stories.title: Semicon China: AI, advanced packaging set to drive country’s chip industry growth
stories.summary: China's chip industry is expected to account for approximately 42 percent of global wafer fabrication capacity by 2028, according to data presented at Semicon China. Agentic artificial intelligence and advanced packaging technology were identified as key growth drivers for the sector.

stories.title: Pentagon, Lockheed sign plan to boost PrSM missile production
stories.summary: The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin have signed a plan to boost production of the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM). BAE Systems and Honeywell Aerospace have also signed new framework agreements to increase munitions production over the coming years.

stories.title: Russia building satellite network to replace Starlink, launches first 16 into orbit
stories.summary: Russia launched the first 16 satellites for a new network called Rassvet, meaning 'Dawn,' intended as a domestic alternative to SpaceX's Starlink constellation. The project aims to provide independent satellite communication capability.

stories.title: Lebanese court issues arrest warrants against Hezbollah terrorists for weapons smuggling
stories.summary: A Lebanese court issued arrest warrants for Hezbollah operatives accused of smuggling weapons into southern Lebanon. Two suspects reportedly admitted to transporting arms intended for attacks against Israeli military forces, claiming such actions were justified under international law.

stories.title: 14-year-old boy indicted for spying for Iran in exchange for money
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors indicted a 14-year-old boy for allegedly spying for Iran in exchange for payment. The minor reportedly contacted an Iranian agent via Telegram and filmed footage of a hospital and residential areas, and was asked to surveil Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar.

stories.title: UN confirms Gaza security force to include Kazakhstan, Indonesia and Morocco
stories.summary: The United Nations confirmed that Kazakhstan, Indonesia, and Morocco will participate in a security force for Gaza. Discussions over the composition of the stabilization force have been ongoing since September 2025.

stories.title: Australians can expect high fuel costs to linger for far longer than the war in Iran
stories.summary: Diesel prices in Australia have surpassed $3 per litre in nearly every capital city amid disruptions linked to the Iran war. Trucking operators and farmers warn they may go out of business, with potential knock-on effects for food prices. Economists caution the inflationary impact could outlast the conflict itself.

stories.title: Long-promised animal cruelty prevention laws quietly shelved by Victorian government
stories.summary: The Victorian state government in Australia has quietly shelved long-promised animal cruelty prevention legislation that would have recognized all animals as sentient. The Labor bill, which aimed to raise care requirements, will not be introduced before the next state election despite being pledged nearly a decade ago.

stories.title: China still on track to supplant US as world’s No 1 economy in 10 years: academic
stories.summary: A University of Hong Kong academic said China remains on track to surpass the United States as the world's largest economy within the next decade. Li Cheng argued that while China faces a structural economic transition, current U.S. challenges—including what he called self-defeating policies—are more severe.

stories.title: Small petrol stations urge Albanese government to crack down on fuel wholesalers as operators run dry
stories.summary: Independent petrol station operators and miners in Australia are urging the Albanese government to crack down on major fuel wholesalers accused of hoarding supply. Smaller operators, particularly in rural and regional areas, report running out of fuel amid disruptions caused by the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel using white phosphorus to scorch earth in south Lebanon, researcher says
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch says it has verified and geolocated images showing Israel using white phosphorus munitions over southern Lebanon. Researchers identified the weapon by its distinctive airburst plume from M825-series artillery projectiles. The use of white phosphorus in civilian areas has drawn accusations of violations of the laws of war.

stories.title: ‘Makes Covid look like a tea party’: Australian food prices could rise for the next year, farmers warn
stories.summary: Australian farmers warn that food prices could rise for at least the next year due to the Iran conflict's impact on fuel, fertiliser, and petrochemical supply chains. Norco dairy cooperative CEO Michael Hampson said a six-to-twelve-month disruption is a best-case scenario, contingent on the Strait of Hormuz reopening.

stories.title: Philippines says it is working with US to obtain oil from US-sanctioned nations
stories.summary: The Philippines declared a national energy emergency on Tuesday due to oil supply disruptions from the Middle East war. Its ambassador to the U.S. said Manila is working with Washington to obtain waivers allowing it to purchase oil from U.S.-sanctioned countries.

stories.title: Suspicious bets placed on US-Iran strikes trigger insider trading concerns
stories.summary: Suspicious trading activity involving thousands of oil contracts occurred approximately 15 minutes before U.S. President Trump announced on March 25 that he would step back from threatening Iranian energy sites. The trades, which would have profited from falling crude prices, have raised concerns about potential insider trading.

stories.title: US and Czech citizens placed in pretrial detention over arson at plant supplying Ukraine — Czech intelligence asks if Russia used pro-Palestinian group as cover
stories.summary: Czech authorities placed US and Czech citizens in pretrial detention over an arson attack on a plant supplying materials to Ukraine. Czech intelligence is investigating whether Russia used a pro-Palestinian group as cover for the operation; one suspect shouted 'Free Palestine' upon arrest.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strike on Novatek-Ust-Luga plant in Russia's Leningrad region
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a strike on the Novatek-Ust-Luga plant in Russia's Leningrad region, verifying earlier reports of the attack on the energy facility.

stories.title: UK to host talks on mission to reopen Hormuz, says official
stories.summary: Britain and France will chair military talks involving approximately 30 nations to form a coalition aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The UK-hosted discussions follow a joint statement by six countries expressing readiness to ensure safe passage through the strait, subsequently endorsed by 24 additional nations.

stories.title: Lebanon state media says Israeli strikes kill 9 in south
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed nine people in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanese state media. Hezbollah said its fighters launched multiple attacks targeting Israeli troops in south Lebanon and inside Israel.

stories.title: Israel talks up Iranian threats to European cities to justify war
stories.summary: Israel has been framing Iran as a threat to European cities in an effort to build international support for its war against Tehran. The campaign aims to persuade European governments that the conflict serves broader Western security interests.

stories.title: Nigeria moves to broaden security alliances amid ongoing insurgency threats
stories.summary: Nigeria is broadening its security alliances to counter ongoing extremist insurgency threats. The country is strengthening cooperation with France, maintaining US military support, and renewing engagement with European Union leaders.

stories.title: Pentagon inks deal with BAE, Lockheed to quadruple THAAD seeker production
stories.summary: The Pentagon has signed deals with BAE Systems and Lockheed Martin to quadruple production of seekers for the THAAD missile defense system. The agreement complements a January deal between the Pentagon and Lockheed to increase annual THAAD interceptor production from 96 to 400 units.

stories.title: PMD forecasts rain in Karachi tomorrow, more showers across Sindh this week
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department has forecast rain in Karachi on Thursday and additional showers across Sindh throughout the week. A westerly wave is affecting southern parts of the country, with Karachi expected to see partly cloudy weather and temperatures between 24.5°C and 34°C.

stories.title: 'A heinous crime': Strikes kill seven fighters in Iraq's Anbar
stories.summary: US strikes killed seven fighters in Iraq's Anbar province, escalating tensions between Washington and Baghdad. Iraq's government asserted its right to respond and warned it risks being drawn deeper into the widening regional war.

stories.title: Blaze at Russia's Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga after major Ukrainian drone attack
stories.summary: A fire broke out at Russia's Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, a major oil export hub, following a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack, Russian officials reported on Wednesday.

stories.title: US worried by rise in ‘foreigner butchering’ scams from China
stories.summary: US officials have expressed concern over the rise of "foreigner butchering" scams originating from China, in which criminal gangs deliberately target non-Chinese victims to avoid attracting scrutiny from Beijing.

stories.title: ‘They can reach me wherever’: China using financial tactics to coerce people who flee, says report
stories.summary: A new report highlights China's use of financial tactics, including tax bills from Hong Kong authorities, to coerce dissidents who have fled abroad. Christopher Mung Siu-tat, head of the UK-based Hong Kong Labour Rights Monitor, described receiving such demands. The report urges the UK to address Beijing's transnational repression.

stories.title: US army raises upper age for recruits to 42 and scraps marijuana restrictions
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has raised its maximum enlistment age from 35 to 42 for the army, army national guard, and army reserves. The new regulation also removes barriers for potential recruits with legal convictions for marijuana or drug paraphernalia possession.

stories.title: Russians attack rescuers who extinguished fire caused by previous strike in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: In Velykyi Burluk, Kupiansk district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region, Russian forces struck State Emergency Service rescuers as they were extinguishing a fire in a non-residential building caused by a prior Russian drone attack.

stories.title: Iran wiped 50 Israeli firms’ data, hacked cameras, official says
stories.summary: An Iranian official claimed that Iran wiped data from 50 Israeli firms and hacked security cameras as part of cyber operations. However, Iran had not penetrated or disrupted critical Israeli infrastructure such as energy grids, banks, or hospitals.

stories.title: Ukraine is developing first-ever Africa strategy, Budanov announces. Russia already has fighters from 36 African countries fighting in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov announced that Ukraine is developing its first-ever strategy for Africa to expand its relations and presence on the continent. Russia has already recruited fighters from 36 African countries to serve in the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Former head of UK's MI6 says Iran has 'upper hand' in war
stories.summary: Former MI6 chief Sir Alex Younger stated that Iran currently has the upper hand in its war with Israel and the US. Speaking to the Economist, Younger said the US underestimated the task and lost the initiative to Iran approximately two weeks ago.

stories.title: Iran conflict disrupts economies, but experts predict rise in defense spending
stories.summary: The Iran conflict is disrupting economies across the Middle East and beyond, but defense analysts predict a rise in military spending among Gulf states. Experts say countries in the region are accelerating military modernization, prioritizing advanced air defense systems such as Patriot and THAAD upgrades to counter asymmetric threats.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief rejects talks with Israel while under bombardment
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem declared in a televised address that negotiating with Israel under bombardment amounts to imposed surrender. He called for unity against Israel and said Hezbollah fighters are prepared to continue operations without limits.

stories.title: CULTURE: KARACHI’S MEMORY MAP
stories.summary: An exploration of Karachi's place names reveals the city's layered history, from its origins as the fishing settlement of Kolachi to naming conventions from pre-colonial and post-Partition eras. Neighborhoods such as Mithadar reflect specific historical episodes in the port city's evolution.

stories.title: Iran military spokesperson says US is negotiating with itself
stories.summary: An Iranian military spokesperson dismissed a 15-point US peace plan, saying Washington is "negotiating with itself." The plan was drafted by the US and sent to Tehran as part of efforts to end the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Oil supply shock hardens energy transition resolve – for some
stories.summary: The Iran war's disruption to energy supplies has prompted divergent responses globally, with some countries accelerating renewable energy transitions while others are increasing reliance on fossil fuels. Meanwhile, oil prices fell on hopes for de-escalation, and suspicions of insider trading related to U.S. policy announcements have emerged.

stories.title: Iranian military mocks Trump's claim of U.S.-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: An Iranian military spokesperson mocked President Trump's claims that the US and Iran are engaged in negotiations, characterizing the US as unable to resolve the conflict and warning Washington not to portray its setbacks as an agreement.

stories.title: Federal Anti-Monopoly Service Grants Grace Period on Telegram, YouTube Ad Ban After Backlash
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Anti-Monopoly Service granted a grace period on its ban of advertising on Telegram and YouTube following public backlash. Advertisers still face fines for placing ads on Instagram and Facebook, which Russia banned in 2022.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty bill for Palestinian prisoners moves to final vote
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset has advanced a bill to impose the death penalty on Palestinians convicted of terrorism to a final vote. The legislation was initiated by the far-right Otzma Yehudit party, led by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The measure has drawn sharp criticism from opponents and human rights groups.

stories.title: Security body’s ‘chaotic’ Ukraine evacuation after invasion put staff at risk: Leaked report
stories.summary: A leaked report reveals that the OSCE's evacuation of staff from Ukraine following Russia's 2022 invasion was described as "chaotic" and put personnel at risk. The findings come as the security body considers sending a mission back to Ukraine to monitor a potential ceasefire.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike Russian icebreaker in Leningrad region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a Russian combat icebreaker at the Vyborg Shipyard in Russia's Leningrad region, according to Ukrainian military officials.

stories.title: Fuel crisis LIVE: PM's 'like Covid period' statement has panicked people, says M.K. Stalin slams Union Government over gas shortage
stories.summary: Global oil prices fell more than 5% amid President Trump's statements about negotiations with Iran. In India, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin criticized the Union Government, saying the prime minister's comparison of the fuel crisis to the Covid period had caused public panic.

stories.title: Pakistan delivers US proposal to Iran as venue for talks remains undecided
stories.summary: Pakistan has delivered a U.S. proposal to Iran regarding potential negotiations, while Turkey and Pakistan are both under consideration as possible venues for talks aimed at ending the conflict.

stories.title: Lebanese army 'lied to the IDF,' didn't disarm Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, Israeli officers say
stories.summary: Israeli military officers accused the Lebanese army of deceiving Israel by falsely claiming it had enforced the demilitarization of southern Lebanon. Officers said the Lebanese army failed to disarm Hezbollah in the area as agreed.

stories.title: New platform matches stranded travelers with families for Pesach in Israel
stories.summary: A new website, IsraelForPesach.com, has been launched to connect travelers stranded in Israel over Passover with local families offering holiday meals and accommodations.

stories.title: Russian-Iranian arms smuggling route said cut off by Israel’s Caspian Sea strikes
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on the Caspian Sea have reportedly severed a Russian-Iranian arms smuggling route used to transfer weapons and supplies. The route was critical for transporting components for Shahed drones used by both heavily sanctioned countries in their respective conflicts.

stories.title: Iranian strikes pose ‘existential threat,’ Gulf states tell UN rights council
stories.summary: Gulf states told the UN Human Rights Council that Iranian strikes on neighboring countries pose an existential threat. The council considered a draft resolution condemning Tehran's attacks, while Iran called for regional unity against Israel.

stories.title: Most Americans say US war on Iran has gone too far
stories.summary: Polling indicates most Americans believe the US war on Iran has gone too far, with rising gas prices a major concern. President Trump's foreign policy is facing increasing domestic criticism as the conflict continues.

stories.title: Defense Minister Katz, IDF Chief of Staff Zamir confirm IDF dropped 15,000 bombs on Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz and IDF Chief of Staff Zamir confirmed the Israeli military has dropped 15,000 bombs on Iran. A statement noted that the overall pace of IDF and US attacks has been cooling off.

stories.title: Iranian attacks amount to violation of sovereignty, Gulf states tell UN
stories.summary: Gulf states brought a resolution before the UN Human Rights Council demanding an end to what they called Iran's "unprovoked attacks" on neighboring countries. The resolution characterizes the Iranian strikes as violations of sovereignty.

stories.title: China says Mexico’s tariff hikes constitute ‘trade barriers’ after probe
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce accused Mexico of imposing trade barriers through tariff hikes on Chinese goods, saying the measures breach trade rules. The friction between the two trading partners has been fuelled by escalating pressure from Washington under President Trump.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Pentagon equity stakes FTW?; Hill & Valley Forum takeaways; plus a bit more
stories.summary: The Pentagon is exploring equity stakes in defense companies, among other defense business developments discussed at the Hill & Valley Forum.

stories.title: Hungary halts gas supplies to Ukraine until oil transit via Druzhba pipeline gets restored — Orban
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán announced that Hungary is halting gas supplies to Ukraine until transit of Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline is restored. The pipeline had previously been damaged by Russian attacks on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Former head of UK's MI6 says Iran has 'upper hand' in war with US and Israel
stories.summary: Former MI6 chief Sir Alex Younger said in a podcast interview with the Economist that the US has lost the initiative to Iran in the ongoing war. He assessed that the Iranian regime has proven more resilient than anticipated by the US and Israel.

stories.title: Kenya finalises trade deal with China as they deepen bilateral ties
stories.summary: Kenya and China finalized a trade agreement that grants Kenya duty-free and quota-free access to the Chinese market beginning in May. The deal was part of a broader effort to deepen bilateral ties between the two countries.

stories.title: UN council condemns Iran attacks, demands reparations
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Council unanimously adopted a resolution condemning Iran's attacks on Gulf neighbors and calling for full reparations for victims. The motion, put forward by Gulf Cooperation Council states and Jordan, also criticized Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and demanded an immediate halt to attacks.

stories.title: Comedy legend John Cleese attacks Muslims and Islam in online posts
stories.summary: British comedian John Cleese posted online statements attacking Muslims and Islam, claiming Muslims seek to impose their will and would kill non-Muslims to achieve it. The remarks drew widespread criticism.

stories.title: Pakistan’s mediation offer reflects growing diplomatic confidence, Capitol Hill symposium told
stories.summary: At a Capitol Hill symposium in Washington, speakers noted that Pakistan's offer to mediate between the United States and Iran reflects Islamabad's growing diplomatic confidence. Participants discussed Pakistan's desire to play a stabilizing role amid the US-Iran military confrontation in the Gulf region.

stories.title: Pinduoduo operator’s profit slides as Chinese firm cites higher reinvestment
stories.summary: PDD Holdings, the Chinese e-commerce company behind Pinduoduo and Temu, reported an 11 percent drop in quarterly profit to 24.5 billion yuan, missing analyst estimates. Revenue rose 12 percent year-over-year to 123.9 billion yuan as the company increased reinvestment spending.

stories.title: Estonia and Latvia say territories hit by stray Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Estonia and Latvia reported that stray Ukrainian drones struck their territories. The incidents occurred on the same night Ukraine launched a large-scale attack on Russia's port of Ust-Luga, located near the Estonian border.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ Gaza envoy urges Hamas to disarm ‘without delay’
stories.summary: A U.S. envoy serving on President Trump's "Board of Peace" urged Hamas to disarm without delay as part of efforts related to the Gaza conflict.

stories.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon amid Litani annexation threat
stories.summary: Israeli forces have intensified strikes on southern Lebanon and Beirut, where fighting has escalated since 2 March. The renewed violence has killed over 1,000 people amid threats related to the Litani River area.

stories.title: Indian singer's drowning was accidental - Singapore coroner
stories.summary: A Singapore coroner ruled that the drowning death of iconic Indian singer Zubeen Garg was accidental, finding no evidence of foul play.

stories.title: Bombs fall on Russia’s Leningrad Oblast for first time since WWII. Ukrainian military says they could be launched not from jet but A-22 civilian ultralight
stories.summary: Ukraine struck Russia's Leningrad Oblast with bombs for the first time since World War II. The Ukrainian military indicated the munitions may have been launched from A-22 civilian ultralight aircraft, with systems capable of hitting targets up to 1,600 km away.

stories.title: 'Make cheese not war': How France's Larzac protests inspired demos around the world
stories.summary: A new book examines how protests on the Larzac plateau in France, beginning in 1971 against a military base expansion, became a template for demonstrations worldwide. Local farmers swore oaths never to leave their land after the government dismissed them as mere peasants, pioneering a model of sustained regional resistance.

stories.title: Israeli teen indicted for working with Iranian operatives, charged with espionage
stories.summary: A 14-year-old Israeli has been indicted for espionage after working with Iranian operatives. The teenager allegedly carried out sabotage and surveillance tasks in exchange for cryptocurrency.

stories.title: Drone attack on Vinnytsia region: Injury toll rises to 20, one killed
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on Ukraine's Vinnytsia region on March 24 killed one person and injured 20 others. Damage to 71 households was recorded in the area.

stories.title: Trump’s war on Iran, in his own words
stories.summary: President Trump has made numerous public statements about the US war with Iran over the course of the conflict. A compilation of his remarks traces the evolution of his rhetoric and justifications since hostilities began.

stories.title: ‘Prolonged conflict wouldn’t make sense for US midterms’
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that a prolonged US conflict with Iran could negatively affect Republican prospects in the upcoming US midterm elections. The political calculus may push the administration toward seeking a resolution before the vote.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz hails Saudi Arabia’s ‘restraint’, stresses urgent need for de-escalation of ongoing Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised Saudi Arabia's "remarkable restraint" during the ongoing Middle East conflict in a phone call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The leaders discussed de-escalation following US-Israeli military actions against Iran that began on February 28.

stories.title: Middle powers are taking up the mantle of multilateral leadership
stories.summary: The article argues that middle powers are increasingly assuming leadership roles in multilateral governance as the United States retreats from the international systems it helped create. The shift is underscored by the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russia sells its oil while arming the enemy Washington is bombing
stories.summary: An analysis highlights that Russian oil continues to flow on global markets while Iranian oil exports remain blocked amid the ongoing conflict. The disparity in energy trade is reportedly affecting the dynamics of the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: 'There's no safety anymore': Palestinians warn of expanding West Bank settler violence
stories.summary: Palestinian communities across the occupied West Bank report a surge in attacks by Israeli settlers on their villages. The escalation in settler violence has coincided with the onset of the Iran war, raising fears among Palestinians about worsening security conditions.

stories.title: Thai tanker safely transits Strait of Hormuz after Iran talks
stories.summary: A Thai oil tanker safely passed through the Strait of Hormuz following diplomatic negotiations with Iran. The transit highlighted cooperation efforts as the ongoing conflict continues to disrupt global oil supply routes.

stories.title: US conservatives gather for CPAC with the right openly divided over Iran war
stories.summary: US conservatives gathered at CPAC amid open divisions within the Republican Party over the Iran war. While Trump retains broad base support, "America First" activists are questioning a conflict with no clear end in sight.

stories.title: Is Iran cashing in millions from Strait of Hormuz blockade?
stories.summary: An Iranian lawmaker claimed that Tehran is quietly charging oil tankers up to $2 million each for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The alleged practice could effectively turn the critical global waterway into a toll-collecting chokepoint.

stories.title: Microsoft president says building data centres requires trust of U.S. communities
stories.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith stated at the CERAWeek conference in Houston that building data centers requires winning and sustaining the trust of local communities where facilities are to be constructed.

stories.title: Russians strike Kharkiv with drones, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kholodnohirskyi and Novobavarskyi districts of Kharkiv using unmanned aerial vehicles, causing casualties among civilians.

stories.title: Asian Champions League quarterfinal sends Iran’s Tractor FC to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The AFC Asian Champions League Elite quarterfinal draw has placed Iran's Tractor FC against Dubai-based Shabab Al-Ahli. The match is scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Iraq summons US envoy over attacks on military units
stories.summary: Iraq's Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani ordered the foreign ministry to summon the US chargé d'affaires in Baghdad following American attacks on Iraqi military units. The move reflects mounting pressure on the Iraqi government to respond to the strikes.

stories.title: Zhang Dongmei named new deputy director of office overseeing Hong Kong affairs
stories.summary: Beijing appointed Zhang Dongmei, a former vice-president of the All-China Women's Federation, as a new deputy director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office. She is the first woman to hold the role since the office's status was elevated in 2023, filling a vacancy left by Xiang Bin's departure.

stories.title: Kenya: Wandayi Warns Oil Firms Against Hoarding, Cites Licence Risk
stories.summary: Kenyan Energy Cabinet Secretary Opiyo Wandayi warned oil marketing companies in Nairobi against hoarding fuel. He stated that companies found hoarding risk losing their operating licences.

stories.title: Namibia: Swakopmund's Ruach Elohim Foundation Rescues 49 Babies, Urges National Safe Haven Awareness
stories.summary: The Ruach Elohim Foundation in Swakopmund, Namibia, has rescued 49 babies since 2020 through its baby saver box program. The organization is urging greater national awareness of safe alternatives for mothers unable to care for their newborns.

stories.title: Kenya: Death Toll From Ongoing Floods Climb to 88, Police Say
stories.summary: Kenya's National Police Service reported on Wednesday that the death toll from ongoing floods across the country has risen to 88, as torrential rains continue to affect multiple regions.

stories.title: Top WTO official sounds fertiliser warning over Middle East war
stories.summary: A senior World Trade Organization official warned that the Middle East war has effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-third of global fertiliser shipments normally transit. The disruption poses risks to agricultural supply chains worldwide.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Mar. 25 – Are Gulf states poised to enter Iran war?
stories.summary: Mideast expert Ksenia Svetlova analyzed Iran's relationships with its Arab neighbors and assessed the likelihood of Gulf states entering the Iran war. The briefing also examined whether the Islamic Republic is near regime change.

stories.title: Video: Trump’s Board of Peace pushes Gaza disarmament plan at UN
stories.summary: An envoy from President Trump's Board of Peace presented a plan at the United Nations to disarm armed groups in Gaza. The proposal is part of broader US efforts to shape post-ceasefire security arrangements in the territory.

stories.title: US reportedly sends peace plan as Iran opens Strait of Hormuz to ‘non-hostile’ oil vessels
stories.summary: Washington reportedly sent a 15-point peace plan to Tehran as the US and Iran seek to end nearly a month of warfare. Iran announced it would allow "non-hostile" oil vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, while President Trump said negotiations were underway.

stories.title: German army eyes AI tools to expedite wartime decision-making
stories.summary: The German army is exploring artificial intelligence tools to speed up wartime decision-making, drawing lessons from combat operations in Ukraine. The initiative aims to exploit battlefield data to better predict the dynamics of future conflicts.

stories.title: China names AI tokens after the yuan. Should the US worry for the dollar?
stories.summary: China officially designated "ciyuan" as the Chinese translation for "token," the computational units used by AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude. The term combines "ci" (word) and "yuan" (currency), and observers see it as an effort to shape AI-related terminology with economic connotations.

stories.title: Former defence exec Tan Ruisong given death sentence for ‘exceptional’ corruption
stories.summary: Tan Ruisong, former chairman of China's state-owned Aviation Industry Corp of China (AVIC), has been given a suspended death sentence for accepting over 613 million yuan in bribes and engaging in insider trading. Tan led China's leading military aircraft maker from 2018 until his retirement in March 2023.

stories.title: SBU highlights most notable special operations in 2025
stories.summary: The Security Service of Ukraine highlighted its most notable special operations in 2025, including the widely publicized operation codenamed "Spiderweb," among dozens of unique missions carried out during the year.

stories.title: Ukraine Hits Ust-Luga Oil Terminal in Largest Overnight Drone Attack of the Year
stories.summary: Ukraine carried out its largest overnight drone attack of the year on Russia's Ust-Luga oil terminal on the Baltic Sea. The port, capable of handling around 700,000 barrels of oil exports daily, was reported ablaze as firefighters responded.

stories.title: Iran says 'non-hostile vessels' can transit Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced it will permit vessels it deems 'non-hostile' to transit the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions. Tehran attributed the restrictive shipping measures to actions by the United States and Israel, as tensions continue to affect global energy markets and shipping lanes.

stories.title: The Iran War Is Pushing Europe Back to Nuclear Energy
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving Iran is prompting European nations to reconsider nuclear energy as a power source. The continent faces a renewed energy crisis, leading governments to revisit a form of energy that many had largely moved away from.

stories.title: Spain says Israel seeks to repeat ‘Gaza destruction’ in Lebanon
stories.summary: Spain's prime minister warned that Israel is replicating in Lebanon the same destructive military tactics it used in Gaza. The statement reflects growing European criticism of Israeli military operations in the region.

stories.title: Danish PM hands in government resignation after defeat in general election
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen submitted her government's resignation to the king on March 25 after her three-party coalition suffered a significant defeat in the general election. She may secure a third term but must negotiate with centrist Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen, who has emerged as kingmaker.

stories.title: Unclear 'how much of a negotiation is taking place' between US and Iran
stories.summary: Iran has received a U.S. plan to pause the Middle East war, officials said on March 25, though Tehran has not confirmed receipt and publicly dismissed Washington's diplomatic efforts. The U.S. is simultaneously deploying paratroopers and additional Marines to the region, raising questions about the sincerity of negotiations.

stories.title: Israel strikes Tehran as Trump says US negotiating to end war
stories.summary: Israel carried out strikes on Tehran while President Trump stated the U.S. was negotiating to end the broader Middle East conflict. Kuwait and Saudi Arabia separately reported repelling fresh drone attacks without identifying their origin.

stories.title: FO condemns harsh sentences awarded to Kashmiri leader Asiya Andrabi, associates by Delhi court
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office condemned a Delhi court's sentencing of Kashmiri leader Asiya Andrabi to life imprisonment and her associates Fehmeeda Sofi and Nahida Nasreen to 30-year prison terms. The convictions were under India's Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act for alleged militant conspiracy.

stories.title: US 'negotiating with itself', Iran says, as Trump pushes talks
stories.summary: Iran's leadership said the US is "negotiating with itself" as President Trump claimed diplomatic progress. Both sides have issued maximalist demands, and Iran's new hardline leadership appears far from reaching any agreement to settle the regional war.

stories.title: Iran ready to seize Bahrain and UAE coastlines if US 'makes a mistake', Iranian expert warns
stories.summary: An Iranian security analyst warned on state broadcaster IRIB that Tehran is prepared to seize the coastlines of Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates if the US "makes a mistake" in the region. Analyst Morteza Simiari said Iran's armed forces are ready to take action.

stories.title: US-Iran mediation: What are each side’s demands – and is a deal possible?
stories.summary: US envoys have transmitted a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran through Pakistan as a mediator. Tehran has responded with its own set of conditions, and significant gaps remain between the two sides' demands.

stories.title: White House says Donald Trump ‘did nothing wrong’ amid reports he showed classified map on plane in 2022 – US politics live
stories.summary: The White House stated that President Trump "did nothing wrong" following reports he displayed a classified map on a 2022 flight to his New Jersey golf club. Separately, a leading Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee revealed Trump retained a highly sensitive record from his first term accessible to only six people.

stories.title: Danish PM Frederiksen resigns and coalition talks begin following close election – Europe live
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen confirmed her government's resignation after the outgoing three-party coalition failed to secure enough mandates to continue. She stressed the urgency of forming a new government, citing global instability, and indicated she is prepared to serve another four-year term.

stories.title: Drones crash in Estonia and Latvia overnight — stray Ukrainian or deliberate Russian, origin unclear
stories.summary: A drone struck the chimney of Estonia's Auvere power plant after entering from Russian airspace, while another exploded in Latvia's Krāslava district. No injuries were reported in either incident, and Estonia's government convened an emergency meeting as investigations continue.

stories.title: Turkey urges Gulf states to avoid joining Israeli-US war
stories.summary: Turkey has intensified diplomatic efforts to prevent Gulf Arab states from joining the Israeli-US war on Iran. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan traveled to Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, urging restraint amid growing regional escalation fears.

stories.title: Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance calls for Russia's expulsion from UNESCO
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance has called on the international community to sign an open appeal demanding Russia's expulsion from UNESCO, citing systematic Russian attacks on cultural heritage sites in Ukraine.

stories.title: Estonia, Latvia report drone incursions from Russian airspace
stories.summary: Estonia and Latvia reported drone incursions from Russian airspace. Latvian officials in Riga said the drone that entered Latvian territory may have been of Ukrainian origin.

stories.title: Floods in Kenya worsen as 2 rivers burst banks, with death toll climbing
stories.summary: Flooding in Kenya has worsened after two rivers burst their banks, with at least 21 counties affected. The rising death toll has raised concerns over public safety, infrastructure damage, and growing humanitarian needs.

stories.title: China Mobile bets on Hong Kong as gateway for global computing flows
stories.summary: China Mobile has invested nearly HK$10 billion over five years to develop Hong Kong as a global computing hub. The state-owned telecom operator opened a new data center in northern Hong Kong and announced plans to expand investment in next-generation submarine cables, integrating the city into China's national computing network.

stories.title: Global outrage mounts as Israel threatens to annex south Lebanon
stories.summary: Global backlash is growing as Israel pushes to seize territory up to Lebanon's Litani River. Many governments and observers warn Israel is using the ongoing war to redraw borders by force, with threats of annexing southern Lebanon drawing widespread condemnation.

stories.title: Qatar condemns Iran attacks, warns it will defend sovereignty
stories.summary: Qatar's cabinet condemned Iranian attacks on its territory and neighboring countries, demanding they stop immediately. Qatar warned it reserves the right to respond and will take measures to protect its sovereignty and security.

stories.title: In midst of Iran war, Trump administration keeps an eye on China rivalry
stories.summary: The Trump administration is maintaining focus on its strategic rivalry with China even as the U.S. remains engaged in the conflict with Iran. Congressional hearings and proposed legislation continue to target China, which is emerging as a major issue ahead of upcoming U.S. elections.

stories.title: What do we know of the US's 15-point peace plan sent to Iran?
stories.summary: The Trump administration reportedly sent a 15-point peace plan to Iran, with Pakistan hosting facilitation efforts. Tehran has dismissed claims of progress in negotiations. Meanwhile, the U.S. is reinforcing its military posture in the region, with reports of at least 3,000 airborne troops set to deploy in the coming days.

stories.title: Israel says struck two naval missile production sites in Tehran
stories.summary: Israel said it struck two naval missile production sites in Tehran as the conflict with Iran escalates. Regional tensions continue to rise while diplomatic efforts intensify to prevent the war from widening further.

stories.title: US is 'negotiating with itself' says Iranian military following Trump comments
stories.summary: Iran's military dismissed President Trump's claim that Tehran desperately wants a deal, stating the US is effectively negotiating with itself. The remarks followed Trump's assertion that Iran sought an agreement urgently.

stories.title: Danish PM secures third term despite party's historic setback
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen secured a third term after her left-wing bloc won the most votes in the March 25 parliamentary elections, though it fell short of a majority. Her Social Democrats received 21.9% of the vote, their lowest share since 1903, down from 27.5% in 2022.

stories.title: Russian attack damages residential and critical infrastructure in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a large-scale drone attack on Ukraine's Chernihiv region on March 24, damaging residential areas and critical infrastructure across the region.

stories.title: Fire at Kuwait airport after drones hit fuel tank: Aviation agency
stories.summary: A fire erupted at Kuwait's airport after drones struck a fuel tank, according to the country's aviation agency. Authorities reported only limited damage and no casualties from the attack.

stories.title: Zelensky slams 'absolute depravity' after massive Russian drone attack
stories.summary: Russia launched a massive drone attack on Ukraine on March 25, following a 24-hour barrage of nearly 1,000 drones that killed eight people across the country. President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the strikes, which hit Lviv's historic center and residential areas in western Ukraine.

stories.title: Large Polymarket, Wall Street bets on Trump’s war news under scrutiny
stories.summary: Large, well-timed trades on Polymarket and Wall Street tied to Trump administration announcements about Iran war developments have drawn scrutiny. Critics allege the White House may be engaged in insider trading based on the timing of the bets.

stories.title: Sirens sound from Jerusalem to northern Israel as Iran fires waves of ballistic missiles
stories.summary: Air-raid sirens sounded across Israel from Jerusalem to the north as Iran launched waves of ballistic missiles. The Israel Electric Corporation reported no damage to its infrastructure near Hadera despite reports of shrapnel impact.

stories.title: 'Mind-blowing corruption': Alleged insider trading over US-Israeli strikes in Iran
stories.summary: Media outlets are examining allegations of insider trading linked to U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, questioning whether diplomatic moves may have been exploited for financial gain. Reports also cover Trump's 15-point peace plan and its implications for global markets.

stories.title: Denmark’s PM resigns after failing to secure majority in general election
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has resigned after failing to secure a parliamentary majority in the general election. She may still return for a third term as prime minister following coalition negotiations.

stories.title: Portugal cuts growth forecast as Israeli-US war drives energy prices higher
stories.summary: Portugal's central bank lowered its 2026 economic growth forecast from 2.3 percent to 1.8 percent. The Bank of Portugal cited rising energy commodity prices linked to the Israeli-US war on Iran and recent storm damage as key factors.

stories.title: Immigrating to Israel during war ‘closes a circle,’ Iranian-American Jew says
stories.summary: Sami Rahamim, an Iranian-American Jew whose parents left Shiraz in 1949, is among 30 new citizens immigrating to Israel despite travel restrictions during the war. He described the move as "closing a circle."

stories.title: Taiwan skips WTO meeting after Cameroon labels it ‘Province of China’
stories.summary: Taiwan announced it will skip a World Trade Organization ministerial meeting for the first time after host nation Cameroon listed it as a "Province of China" on official documents.

stories.title: First flotilla boat arrives in Cuba to deliver aid amid crisis
stories.summary: The first of three humanitarian aid boats carrying activists and essential supplies arrived in Cuba from Mexico. The delivery responds to widespread blackouts and infrastructure collapse on the island caused by dwindling fuel supplies under a U.S.-imposed blockade.

stories.title: US interceptor stockpiles being depleted by Iran war, could take years to replenish
stories.summary: The Payne Institute estimates that the war with Iran has consumed roughly one-third of the US THAAD missile interceptor stockpile. Annual production of THAAD missiles does not exceed about 100, meaning replenishment could take years.

stories.title: Dozens of bodies, mostly infants, discovered in Kenya mass grave
stories.summary: A mass grave containing 32 bodies, including 25 children—mostly infants—was discovered in Kenya. Authorities believe some of the remains came from local hospitals and mortuaries.

stories.title: Ahead of Passover, Israelis warned of increased threats worldwide amid war with Iran
stories.summary: Israel's National Security Council warned Israeli citizens abroad of increased threats ahead of Passover amid the war with Iran. Jewish events and gatherings outside Israel are considered heightened risks, with assessments that Iran will work to carry out attacks against Israeli and Jewish targets.

stories.title: Estate of Mike Lynch ordered to pay £920m to Hewlett Packard Enterprise
stories.summary: A London high court ordered the estate of late British tech entrepreneur Mike Lynch to pay £920 million to Hewlett Packard Enterprise. The ruling relates to HP's 2011 acquisition of Lynch's software firm Autonomy, after a 2022 legal finding that Lynch misrepresented the company's value.

stories.title: Watch: Trump should end the war and ask Israel to leave Iran alone | The Hindu Editorial
stories.summary: A Hindu Editorial analysis argues that President Trump should end the war with Iran and pressure Israel to cease its military operations there. The piece notes Trump's administration has eased some sanctions on Iranian oil, suggesting a potential opening for diplomacy.

stories.title: Drone enters Estonia from Russia, hits power plant chimney
stories.summary: A drone entered Estonian airspace from Russia overnight and struck the chimney of the Auvere power plant. Estonian authorities are investigating the incident and its origin.

stories.title: Spain’s PM says Israel to inflict on Lebanon same destruction as in Gaza
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez accused Israel of seeking to inflict the same level of destruction on Lebanon as it carried out in Gaza. Sanchez has been one of the few European leaders to openly condemn Israel's war in Lebanon and the US-Israeli campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Watch: ‘Hey Trump, you’re fired!’: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard mocks U.S President
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard publicly mocked US President Donald Trump in a propaganda message amid the ongoing military conflict between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: Iran ready to seize Bahrain and UAE coastlines if US 'makes a mistake', Iranian expert warns
stories.summary: Iranian national security analyst Morteza Simiari warned on state broadcaster IRIB that Iran is prepared to seize Bahraini and UAE coastlines if the US "makes a mistake." He said Iran could fundamentally alter the regional landscape in response to further escalation.

stories.title: Ukraine built the ground drone playbook. Russia copied it. Now Ukraine is destroying the copies near Vovchansk
stories.summary: Near Vovchansk in northeastern Ukraine, Ukrainian forces are destroying Russian unmanned ground vehicles that were modeled on Ukraine's own ground drone designs. The sector has become a technology duel as both sides deploy and counter robotic combat systems.

stories.title: Inside the Palestinian camp in Beirut where residents are staying put, for now
stories.summary: A FRANCE 24 team visited Bourj el-Barajneh, a Palestinian refugee camp in Beirut's southern suburbs, an area frequently targeted by Israeli airstrikes. Many residents say they have no choice but to remain. The camp was established in 1948 following the displacement of Palestinians during the Nakba.

stories.title: African producers may have energy edge during Iran war, if they can overcome hurdles
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has disrupted roughly a fifth of global oil and LNG supply, potentially giving African producers in Nigeria, Angola, Gabon, Algeria, and Libya a structural advantage. Analysts note these West and North African exports are viewed as lower-risk alternatives, though capacity constraints limit their ability to fully fill the gap.

stories.title: Trump’s war in Iran exposes US’s shift from a global guardian to an arbiter of chaos
stories.summary: The U.S.-backed war in Iran has caused widespread economic disruption across Asia. India redirected liquefied gas supplies to households, Nepal rationed gas, the Philippines trimmed the government workweek to four days, and Bangladesh closed universities and rationed fuel, all due to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Professor sues Texas university that terminated contract after Palestine talk
stories.summary: Philosophy professor Idris Robinson has sued Texas State University officials, alleging they violated his constitutional rights by terminating his contract after he gave an off-campus talk on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Pro-Israel social media accounts identified Robinson roughly a year after the event, which took place in another state.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders and AOC introduce bill to pause building of new datacenters
stories.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced legislation to impose a moratorium on the construction of new AI datacenters in the United States. The bill aims to allow time for establishing federal environmental and labor protections amid rising energy demands from artificial intelligence infrastructure.

stories.title: Ukraine gains access to 14 new food export markets since January – Tkachuk
stories.summary: As of March 2026, Ukraine's food products have gained access to 14 new export markets since January, according to Ukrainian official Tkachuk, expanding the country's agricultural trade reach.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine escalate drone attacks as Moscow starts spring offensive
stories.summary: Russia launched nearly 1,000 drones at Ukraine in 24 hours as part of a spring offensive, damaging an energy facility in the Chernihiv region and leaving approximately 150,000 consumers without power. Ukraine responded with its largest reported overnight drone attack on Russian regions and Crimea, with Russia claiming to have downed nearly 400 incoming drones.

stories.title: In Lebanon, some schools choose to stay open despite the war
stories.summary: Some schools in Lebanon have chosen to remain open despite ongoing conflict and airstrikes. In Beirut, a school near the frequently targeted southern suburbs continues in-person classes, while other students attend remotely.

stories.title: Ex-Tory minister Crispin Blunt pleads guilty to possession of crystal meth
stories.summary: Former Conservative MP and ex-prisons minister Crispin Blunt pleaded guilty at Westminster magistrates court to four drug possession charges, including crystal meth and cannabis. The charges stem from a raid on his home in Horley, Surrey, in October 2023.

stories.title: Fresh strike on base in western Iraq kills seven
stories.summary: A fresh air strike on a military base in Iraq's western Anbar province killed seven security forces and medics. The attack comes amid rising US-Iran tensions and escalating regional violence.

stories.title: UN experts demands release of Gaza doctor Abu Safiya after 'severe torture'
stories.summary: Two UN special rapporteurs demanded the release of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza, who has been detained by Israel since December 27, 2024. The experts said Israeli prison conditions have "gravely endangered" him through severe torture.

stories.title: Pakistan delivers US proposal to Iran as talks venue debated
stories.summary: Pakistan has delivered a US proposal to Iran as diplomatic efforts to end the war intensify, according to a senior Iranian source. Turkey and Pakistan are both under consideration as possible venues for negotiations between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: US ramps up military presence in the Middle East amid reported talks
stories.summary: The United States is expanding its military presence in the Middle East despite reportedly sending a 15-point peace plan to Tehran. Soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division are planned for deployment to support operations related to Iran, joining thousands of Marines arriving in the region by March 25.

stories.title: Nigeria: A Festival or a Culture of Rape?
stories.summary: An article highlights ongoing concerns about sexual violence at festivals in Nigeria, referencing the Ozoro incident and warning that conditions enabling such crimes remain unaddressed.

stories.title: Europe could face Iran war fuel rationing by April, says Shell boss
stories.summary: Shell CEO Wael Sawan warned that Europe could face energy shortages and fuel rationing as soon as April if the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen to oil and gas shipping. Shell said it is working with governments to address the supply crisis, which has already led to energy rationing in parts of Asia.

stories.title: National Guard downs over 500 Shahed drones since start of year – spokesperson
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Guard has shot down more than 500 Iranian-designed Shahed drones in the first three months of 2026, using mobile fire groups and interceptor drone crews to protect critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Nigeria: Old Video of Nigerian President's Son Thanking Nigerians for Supporting His Father's Administration Resurfaces
stories.summary: An old video of Nigerian President Bola Tinubu's son thanking Nigerians for supporting his father's administration has resurfaced on social media, according to fact-checking outlet Africa Check.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: An opportunity for Iran's minorities?
stories.summary: Iran's ethnic minorities — including Azeris, Kurds, Balochs, and Arabs — collectively make up nearly half the country's population and have historically faced marginalization under successive regimes. Analysts suggest these communities could play a significant role amid the current Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Qatar says it will not join regional escalation, condemns attacks
stories.summary: Qatar declared it will not be drawn into the escalating Israeli-US war on Iran. Speaking at the UN in Geneva, Qatar's representative condemned attacks on countries not party to the conflict, calling them violations of international law.

stories.title: Former Hong Kong exchange executive Ba Shusong reported out of public sight
stories.summary: Ba Shusong, former managing director and chief China economist at Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX), has not appeared in public recently and could not be contacted. Ba was a prominent academic who frequently spoke at major conferences about Hong Kong's role connecting mainland China with global markets.

stories.title: Iranians feel 'deceived, abandoned' as Trump weighs striking deal with Iran's old guard
stories.summary: Reports suggest the US may be exploring a deal involving former Iranian political figures, including Ghalibaf. A resident of Isfahan said many Iranians would feel "deceived and abandoned" if such a deal materialized, fearing a transition from one authoritarian system to another.

stories.title: US sends 15-point peace plan to Iran while deploying troops in the region
stories.summary: The Trump administration sent a 15-point peace plan to Iran via Pakistani officials, but Tehran has rejected the prospect of negotiations with Washington. Simultaneously, at least 1,000 additional U.S. troops are being deployed to the Middle East, with Iran reportedly preparing for the possibility of American ground forces.

stories.title: Anduril, Palantir developing Golden Dome anti-missile shield's software - report
stories.summary: U.S. defense technology firms Anduril and Palantir are reportedly developing the software for the Golden Dome anti-missile shield. The software would integrate radars and sensors to detect and track airborne threats.

stories.title: Slavutych in Kyiv region left without power after morning Russian attack
stories.summary: Approximately 21,000 residents of Slavutych in Ukraine's Kyiv region lost centralized electricity supply following a Russian attack on the city's power infrastructure.

stories.title: Stocks rise and oil dips on hopes of 15-point Iran peace plan
stories.summary: Global stock markets rose and oil prices dipped following reports that President Trump sent a 15-point peace framework to Iran. Positive sentiment was also boosted by Iran's announcement that it would permit "non-hostile" ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Why a prolonged war with Iran will constrain the U.S. | Data
stories.summary: The article reports that the United States has expended a significant share of its previously procured weapons in operations against Iran, raising concerns about strained military stockpiles. Analysts suggest a prolonged conflict would constrain U.S. military capacity.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran Guards have fired missiles at Israel, Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain, state TV reports
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles at Israel, Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, according to Iranian state television. President Trump sent a peace plan to Tehran, and Iran announced it would allow passage through the Strait of Hormuz for oil vessels it deems "non-hostile."

stories.title: Israel’s US envoy says settler violence a ‘stain’ costing the nation friends
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, called settler violence a "stain" that is costing the country international support. He expressed anger at the failure to stop growing extremist attacks while insisting efforts are being made to address the issue.

stories.title: Anduril, Palantir developing Golden Dome missile shield's software, source says
stories.summary: Defense technology firms Anduril and Palantir have been selected to develop software for the Golden Dome missile shield program. Lockheed Martin, RTX, and Northrop Grumman had previously joined the project as prime contractors.

stories.title: Trump sends peace plan as Iran opens Strait of Hormuz to ‘non-hostile’ oil vessels
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump sent a peace plan to Iran amid nearly a month of warfare, while Tehran announced it would allow "non-hostile" oil vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Trump stated the U.S. was actively negotiating with Iran.

stories.title: Two arrested over antisemitic arson attack on London Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: London police arrested two men in connection with an antisemitic arson attack on Jewish community ambulances. A third suspect is believed to be at large, and police are examining a claim of responsibility by a group with possible links to Iran.

stories.title: Air Canada pilots killed in LaGuardia crash were early in flying careers
stories.summary: The two Air Canada pilots killed in the LaGuardia Airport crash were identified as Antoine Forest and Mackenzie Gunther on March 24. Both were reported to have been early in their flying careers.

stories.title: Two years after al-Shifa siege, I am glad my mother did not live to witness it
stories.summary: A personal essay reflects on the destruction of Gaza's al-Shifa Hospital two years after an Israeli siege. The author describes stepping over severed limbs and rubble at what was once Gaza's largest medical facility.

stories.title: UN human rights chief warns war on Iran is spreading
stories.summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk warned that the war on Iran is spreading across the region. He said civilians are bearing the brunt of the escalating conflict.

stories.title: Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz is an international crisis
stories.summary: Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, creating an international crisis. The closure of the critical shipping lane is being described as requiring urgent action from the international community.

stories.title: Hitler posters appear in Iran as warning to foreign collaborators
stories.summary: Banners quoting Adolf Hitler in Persian have appeared on streets in Iran as the government continues arresting and executing individuals accused of collaborating with Israel.

stories.title: Affordable housing
stories.summary: Pakistan faces an estimated housing shortfall of 10 million units, with only about 350,000 units added annually. The deficit is driven by demographic pressures and rapid urbanisation. The article frames affordable housing access as a fundamental socioeconomic necessity rather than merely a policy goal.

stories.title: Estonia and Latvia say they were hit by drones as Ukraine unleashes massive attack on Russia
stories.summary: A drone originating from Russian airspace struck a power plant in Estonia on Wednesday, while another drone — likely a stray Ukrainian one — crashed into Latvian territory. The incidents occurred as Ukraine launched a massive drone barrage against Russia, igniting a fire at a major petroleum export hub near the Estonian border.

stories.title: Drones strike Russia's Ust-Luga port, fire reported
stories.summary: A drone attack caused a fire at the port of Ust-Luga in Russia's Leningrad region, a major Baltic Sea energy export terminal.

stories.title: Are US and China looking for ‘minimum stability’ after going through a ‘rough patch’?
stories.summary: Academics and former officials at a Tsinghua University forum in Beijing discussed the need for minimum stability in U.S.-China relations and the prevention of open confrontation. President Trump's planned visit to China has been postponed by several weeks as the U.S. focuses on its war with Iran.

stories.title: How climate change led to demise of once-thriving Chinese civilisation 4,500 years ago
stories.summary: Scientists have linked the collapse of a thriving civilisation in what is now Hubei province, central China, approximately 4,500 years ago to climate change. The civilisation, which featured palaces, advanced engineering, and jade luxury goods, gradually declined as its population dispersed across the region.

stories.title: Trump’s new gimmick
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump extended his 48-hour ultimatum to Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by another five days after Tehran did not comply. Trump claimed negotiations were underway, but Iran denied that any direct talks were taking place. Iran has endured over three weeks of U.S.-Israeli strikes.
